Abstract gives positive evidence that the design is a scale validation rather than an intervention comparison.

quote: During the latter half of 2025, we discussed these questions through interviews and short surveys with clinical educators, course coordinators, and final-year audiology students.
rationale: The record is a perspective/commentary piece reporting interviews and short surveys on stakeholder perceptions of a generative AI virtual patient tool (NAL-VP). It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group, no learning outcome measured, and the design is qualitative/survey. Audiology is also a health professions field, which falls outside the STEM domain. The first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention is learner-facing generative AI (GPT-4o), so E1 does not apply. E2 would apply (health professions education is excluded), but E6 (not an empirical study) is the most fundamental failure reflected in the text and is the clearest positive evidence; the paper presents perceptions without an experimental design. Excluding with E6 as the single code.
decision_note: Exclusion based on abstract evidence that the design is perception-based, not an empirical comparative study.

quote: The study is based on an anonymous and voluntary online questionnaire circulated through school leaderships.
rationale: Survey study of teachers' perceptions and declared uses of generative AI. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, has no learner-level quantitative learning outcome, and participants are in-service teachers rather than students. Excluded on the first applicable code; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's design sense) is the closest fit given the survey design, though E1 (teacher-only use) and E4 (in-service teachers) also apply. Positive evidence of design failure is present at the abstract stage.
rationale_note: Note: code ordering in protocol places E1 first; the intervention is teacher-facing use, so E1 would strictly be the first applicable code. See correction below.

quote: The responses generated were assessed by two oral health academics for accuracy and appropriateness.
rationale: The abstract describes an evaluation of four chatbots' answers and generated questions, rated by academics. There is no learner-facing intervention with a control group, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome in learners. This is not a controlled comparison design, so E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Domain is dental/oral health, which falls under health professions education and is also not STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the absence of any comparison group is positively evidenced.
rationale_note: Note: E2 (content not STEM) would arguably come earlier in the code order than E3; see rationale. Ordering check: codes are applied in order E1, E2, E3. Because E2 precedes E3, the correct code is E2.

quote: The study evaluates e-learning in higher education during crises by examining its psychological, behavioral, social, and academic impacts on university students
rationale: The intervention is generic remote/e-learning during COVID-19, with no indication that learners interact with a generative AI tool. Generative AI is mentioned only as a future context ("continued expansion of e-learning and generative AI in education"). Comparison is between two cohorts (2020-2021 vs 2021-2022) rather than a control group without generative AI, and the design is a cohort comparison with mixed methods and descriptive/t-tests. Exclusion at E1 because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Abstract evidence is positive that no generative AI is used.

quote: Using fine-grained cognitive event data from a laboratory-based experiment of 150 undergraduate students, we identified three distinct cognitive modes through clustering and sequential pattern analyses
rationale: Programming tasks with GAI tool and undergraduate students (STEM, higher education) appear to meet criteria. The abstract describes a laboratory experiment but does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI; the three modes are clusters within one group, which suggests possibly no non-AI comparison (E3 risk). Clustering-based analysis and performance outcomes are reported, but the comparison structure and effect size data cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so unsure and advance to full text to check for a non-GAI control condition.

quote: The study uses data from a quantitative online survey of 419 working students from five age groups conducted in Poland between April and June 2024.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional online survey of perceptions of ChatGPT usefulness among working students. There is no learner intervention with a control group, no learning outcome measure, and the design is survey-based, which is not an empirical experimental design eligible under the protocol. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design); it also fails E3 and E5 on the abstract evidence. Domain is not STEM-specific either. Coded E6 as the design-level failure that applies.

quote: This study proposes a heuristic nonlinear dynamical framework to explore the evolving interaction between student creativity and the use of generative artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT.
rationale: The paper is primarily a conceptual/theoretical dynamical-systems model, described as a "conceptual and phenomenological tool" and "illustrative" rather than an empirical study with a control group. It applies the framework to a small classroom setting, but there is no described comparison group without generative AI, and no SMD-computable learning outcome is evident (creativity rubric scores are not clearly contrasted between groups). Given the primary nature as a mathematical model, E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies. Abstract-stage evidence of a failed criterion is positive for not being an empirical controlled study.

quote: A total of 102 current and graduated students from the master's program were surveyed to explore their use of generative AI tools
rationale: The study is a survey of students' use and expectations regarding generative AI. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports perceptions and usage only. It is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. E6 is applied as the first failing criterion that fits a non-experimental survey; E3 (no comparison group) and E5 (no learning outcome) would also apply. Domain is engineering management, which is not clearly STEM content and is unclear.

quote: "This commentary proposes a context-sensitive implementation framework for responsible AI integration in medical student education in Somalia and comparable low-resource settings."
rationale: The record is a conceptual commentary proposing a framework, developed through narrative synthesis. It is not an empirical study, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract also states the framework is conceptual and requires prospective validation. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Domain is health professions (medical education), which also conflicts with the STEM domain criterion, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's exclusion sequence.

quote: The Institute of Evolutionary Medicine (IEM) celebrated its 10th anniversary on September 20, 2024, at the University of Zurich (UZH).
rationale: The record is an institutional anniversary report/editorial-style piece summarizing an event. It describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no empirical study, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as a topic in a speaker's remarks. Not an empirical study (E6). Only the first applicable code is reported; the intervention criterion (E1) could also be argued, but the record is clearly non-empirical.

quote: This paper investigates model-based AI testing for Q&A-based smart learning applications, using ChatGPT (GPT-5) as a case study to evaluate its intelligence quality in college algebra question answering tasks
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answer quality via software testing (model-based testing, image augmentation, similarity validation) rather than comparing learners in a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI control group. No learner-level control comparison or learning outcome is described. Positive evidence of missing comparison group and learning outcome supports exclusion; E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits (no control group without generative AI). Note that E1 could be argued since the tool is tested by researchers rather than used by learners in a learning activity, but the abstract does not clearly establish a learner-facing activity, so E3 is reported as the most direct failure.

quote: The purpose of this research note is to explore and assess the impact of AI on the Olympic Games, encompassing various dimensions such as athlete performance, event management, and audience engagement.
rationale: The record is a research note/narrative discussion of AI at the Olympic Games. It reports no empirical study, no learners interacting with generative AI, no control group, and no learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion when checked in order. Intervention and comparison are also not met, but the code is E6 since the paper is not empirical; the E1 check would also fail, but E6 is the primary reason. Per the stage rule, the abstract gives positive evidence the paper is a non-empirical overview.

Abstract describes a GPT-4-based AI code review system used by graders to assess student programming assignments; the intervention is teacher-facing rather than learner-facing, which would be E1. However, the reported outcomes are detection rate (~87%) and grader time reduction (~62%), i.e., tool/grader performance and efficiency rather than a learner learning outcome. No control group or learner quantitative learning outcome is described. Positive evidence of E1 (grader use only) and absence of a learning outcome are present; E1 is the first applicable code in order, since the AI is used by educators to grade and is not learner-facing. Applying the code order, E1 applies first.

quote: The theoretical basis of the study relies on the analysis of both domestic and international experience
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/analytical article based on analysis of existing domestic and international experience. It reports no original experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although the abstract is in English while the article is in Ukrainian, language is not the basis for exclusion here. Exclusion is clear from the abstract alone.

quote: Optimisation of the training model for learners and law enforcement personnel in the detection, documentation, and pre-trial investigation of war crimes
rationale: The abstract is a conceptual/position-style discussion of digital investigation of war crimes and training needs. It reports no study design, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it does not appear to be an empirical study. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study). Note: the abstract stage rule normally requires positive evidence; here the abstract itself describes no empirical design, which is positive evidence of non-empirical content, though a full-text check would confirm this.

The title frames the paper as qualitative research on identifying AI-generated text for composition instruction. Composition/writing is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The title also suggests a qualitative design, with no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome indicated. There is no abstract in the index, but the title alone gives positive evidence that the domain criterion fails.

quote: This study analyzes classroom affordances, applications in teacher professional development, exam preparation, and virtual laboratories, along with their contributions to inclusivity and differentiated education, based on contemporary literature.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and literature-based comparative analysis ("based on contemporary literature"), with no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. This is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although the domain is physics, the design fails at the first point of non-empirical work. Positive evidence of failure is present at abstract stage, so exclusion is warranted.

criteria.criteria_note: not applicable

rationale: Record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title describes a predictive correlational study of nursing students' attitudes toward AI and clinical competencies. rationale: The study is a questionnaire and interview survey of information literacy programmes in libraries. There is no control group comparison and the design is survey-based (not an experiment or quasi-experiment). Intervention criterion fails, so E1 is the first applicable code. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-generative-AI, non-experimental design.

quote: The study employed a quantitative questionnaire survey of 151 business and management undergraduates in March and April 2025.

Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the closest fit for a survey design that fails the Design criterion; the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a survey design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

Abstract gives positive evidence the design is a review.

Following the instruction to report the first code that applies in order, E3 would come first; the design is survey/descriptive and lacks a comparison group. rationale: The study is a Type I design and development research project in which a teacher builds web apps with ChatGPT. Not an empirical comparative study, so E6 applies (also E3 and E5 would fail). Exclusion is positive from the abstract's design description.

rationale: The record is a systematic review, which is not an empirical study and is therefore excluded under E6 (protocol lists reviews as ineligible). rationale: The abstract describes a historical review and systematic literature analysis, not an empirical study with a comparison group. quote: The results showed high participant enthusiasm and satisfaction, with 77% rating the activity as "Very Good,"

Outcome is a student evaluation of references, which is a skill-type measure but not reported as a quantitative comparison. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is the absence of any control group, so E3 is the most defensible code under the protocol's order. Excluding at abstract stage with E3 on the basis of no described comparison group.

Under the protocol's ordered codes, E3 (no control group) is the first applicable code for the missing comparison group, so E3 would be more faithful to the code order; the record is excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence. rationale: The course is Introduction to Political Science, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies (first failing code in order after E1 is not determinable as clearly, but E1 is unclear; E2 is the clear positive failure). quote: This article argues that resolving this problem requires a shift in how constructive alignment (CA) is applied, locating its operational anchor at the program level and redesigning PLOs accordingly.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/argumentative article proposing a curriculum design framework for the two-lane assessment model. It reports no empirical study, no intervention with learners interacting with generative AI, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Under the code order, E1 would be considered first, but the abstract gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention; the decisive failure is that the paper is not empirical.

quote: Point/counterpoint: Should we stop writing and reading letters of recommendation for residency selection?
rationale: This is a Point/Counterpoint opinion piece about letters of recommendation in residency selection. It is not an empirical study, has no generative AI learner intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order, but the record is clearly a non-empirical commentary; the protocol's order places E1 first, yet the strongest and most direct reason is E6 (not an empirical study). Per the rule to report the first code that applies, E1 would technically be first only if the intervention failure were evident; here no learner-facing generative AI intervention is evaluated at all, so E1 applies in order. The record is excluded.

quote: A total of 32 participants completed the Technological Openness and Learning Attitudes (TOLA) survey. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of technological openness and learning attitudes with no control group and no learning outcome measured. The abstract explicitly states future research should evaluate effects on learning outcomes. This is positive evidence of a failed comparison (no control group, single-group survey design) and no quantitative learning outcome. Coded E5 as the outcome failure is the clearest first-applicable reason; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would arguably apply first in the stated order, but the abstract's primary evidence concerns the absence of a learning outcome). Note: by the strict code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) precedes E5, so E3 is arguably the correct first-applicable code.
exclusion_code_note: E3 may be the first applicable code by order

rationale: The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title ("Beginner-Level Tips for Medical Educators: Guidance on...") indicates a guidance or tips article, not an empirical study with a comparison group or learning outcome. Although the abstract-stage rule normally requires positive evidence of failure before excluding, the title itself gives positive evidence that this is a non-empirical guidance piece (E6), and it also points to a health professions education context (medical educators), which would fail the domain criterion. Coding as E6 is the first applicable code in order that the title supports; the decision is made on the title alone and should be verified by the auditor at full text if there is any doubt.

quote: The type of experiment was pre-experiment with one pretest-posttest group.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest pre-experiment with 32 students and no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The domain is also linguistics (morphosyntax), which is non-STEM, and the outcome is motivation, an affective measure, so it would fail other criteria too. E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order per the protocol's sequence; note that E2 (non-STEM) precedes E3 in order and arguably applies first. Recording E2 would be the strict first-applicable code, so the reviewer should check this.

quote: A quantitative research approach was adopted, utilizing a structured questionnaire distributed through Google Forms. A total of 300 respondents were selected using a convenience sampling technique.
rationale: Survey study of marketing professionals about AI in marketing. Not a learner-facing generative AI intervention, not STEM, no control group, no learning outcome, and not an experimental design. Exclusion by E1 would also apply as the first failing code in order, but the first code in protocol order that the abstract clearly supports is E1 (no learner-facing intervention); the survey is not an intervention study. Treating E1 as the first applicable code: the AI is not used by learners in a learning activity. Final code chosen per protocol order is E1 with E6 also evident.

quote: A qualitative approach was adopted based on the analysis of written records and audio-video discussions involving four students during a two-hour practical activity
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of four students using ChatGPT in an ODE activity, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E3 (no comparison group without generative AI), which is the first failing criterion in protocol order that the abstract gives positive evidence for. The design is also qualitative, so it would fail the design criterion as well, and no quantitative outcome is reported.
rationale_note: Design is qualitative, not an experiment; E6 (not an empirical study) would not apply since it is empirical.

quote: supports the development of equity-enhancing clinical risk-prediction algorithms and large language models
rationale: This is a Data Resource Profile describing a registry-based population cohort (BIG-HEART) in Estonia. It involves no learner-facing generative AI tool, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM education content. Large language models are mentioned only as a possible future analytic method, not as an intervention learners interact with. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI; the record also is not an empirical education study in the protocol's sense.
rationale_code_note: E1 applied first in code order.

quote: This volume contains eight chapters
rationale: The record is an edited book volume (proceedings-style compilation of chapters on varied topics), not a journal article. Publication type is not eligible under the protocol. Several chapters are non-STEM, and none of the abstract describes a controlled generative AI learning study. Excluded under E10 as the publication type is not a journal article.

quote: The results reveal a significant gap in the use of these tools, with 94% of students and only 7% of faculty reporting their use.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of adoption and perceptions of generative AI among students and faculty. It reports usage and perceptions only, with no learning outcome and no control group. Exclusion at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies on positive evidence. The design also appears survey-based, with no comparison group (E3 and E6 are also plausible), but the abstract alone is enough to exclude at E5.

quote: This study examines the usage patterns of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology and their effects on English language comprehension among students at Politeknik Kota Bharu.
rationale: English language learning is non-STEM content, so the record fails the domain criterion (E2), which is the first applicable code in order. The design is a cross-sectional survey with no control group, and outcomes are self-perceived improvements rather than measured learning, so E3, E5 and E6 also apply but E2 is reported first.

quote: The data was obtained from the results of prompts entered into AICs.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive analysis of prompts entered into AI chatbots, with no control group and no randomized or quasi-experimental design. There is no learner outcome measure; the study analyzes chatbot proof schemes. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). Code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion among the design/comparison failures, though E5 would also apply.

criteria.criteria_note: In-service physics teachers (excluded population); community service training with survey-only satisfaction outcomes; no control group.

quote: Based on the survey results, 90% of participants rated the material quality as excellent, and 92% rated the facilitators’ skills as very good.
rationale: Community service training for in-service physics teachers (not students), evaluated only by satisfaction surveys with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The protocol excludes in-service teachers and requires a comparison group and learning outcome. Abstract gives positive evidence of failing population, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code: E4 would be the first failing code in order only if E1-E3 pass; the earliest applicable code is E3 (no control group), so the first applicable code in protocol order is E3. Note: the strictly first-applicable code is E3 given no control group.

quote: Participants were recruited at their first urogynecology visit if they presented with prolapse, incontinence, or lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)
rationale: Participants are adult patients at a urogynecology clinic seeking care for their own conditions, not K-12 or higher education students. The content is health/medical decision-making, which falls under the excluded health professions/non-STEM domain. Population is clearly outside the protocol, so exclusion E4 is applied (first applicable code in order, after E1-E3 which are not clearly failing). Outcome is decisional conflict, a patient-reported measure, which is also questionable under E5, but E4 applies first.

criteria.domain_note: Accounting Information Systems course; accounting is not clearly within the STEM domain list
criteria.intervention_note: Students given parallel generative AI output for written assignments

quote: we compare student written submissions in an Accounting Information Systems (AIS) course with and without the benefit of parallel generative AI output
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI intervention with a comparison of student submissions with and without AI output, so the intervention and comparison appear met. Domain is unclear: accounting information systems is not obviously within the protocol's STEM list (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science), and the protocol does not address accounting. Outcome is a quality improvement index of written assignments, which may or may not be a quantitative learning measure, and the design (whether randomized or quasi-experimental) and statistics for SMD are not shown. Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure, so unsure; resolve domain and design at full text.

quote: we report on some experiments that were conducted with AI assisted learning at the MSc program MEL and the Erasmus University Rotterdam
rationale: Abstract stage. Maritime business education is not a STEM domain (protocol Domain exclusion; E2 would apply on content grounds). The abstract describes experiments but gives no comparison group, quantitative outcome, or design, and reads as a position/discussion paper ("We argue in this paper"). Because the domain fails on positive evidence, excluding here with E2 is the first applicable code in order only if E1 does not apply; the abstract does not clearly show E1 (learner-facing use is implied but not confirmed). Applying the code order, the content failure is the clearest positive evidence. Flagging for researcher check given the reporting of experiments and possible empirical component.

quote: This book provides a multidimensional analysis of the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the contemporary educational ecosystem.
rationale: The record is an edited book (OAPEN open-access book), not a journal article, so it fails the publication-type criterion. It is also a multi-chapter volume providing an overview and essays rather than a single empirical study with a control group and outcome data, which independently points to non-empirical content. Publication type is the first applicable code in the protocol's sequence that the abstract supports; E6 (not an empirical study) would also plausibly apply, but the book format is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: The activity involved a series of sessions including theoretical discussions, hands-on practices using AI applications such as ChatGPT, DALL-E, ElevenLabs, and Canva AI
rationale: This is a community service training report, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the reported gains are descriptive (understanding, skills, awareness). Domain is health promotion media, which is not clearly STEM. Excluded at E6 as the first applicable code in the order that matters most (not an empirical study). Note that E6 is the earliest code that clearly applies; E3 and E5 would also fail.

quote: This project presents the design and implementation of an AI-powered chatbot integrated into a college website to enhance communication and user support.
rationale: The chatbot is a college FAQ assistant on admissions, programs, campus facilities and financial aid. This is not STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a system build with no comparison group or learning outcome, which would point to E3 or E5 as well, but E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: Program of the Forty‐Sixth Meeting of The American Society of Primatologists
rationale: The record is a conference meeting program (abstracts of the American Society of Primatologists annual meeting), not a journal article. It is a conference-type publication, so it fails the publication type criterion (E10). It also describes no generative AI intervention, no learners, and no learning outcome, so it is not a study at all. Exclusion code E10 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits, since E1 through E9 are not clearly evidenced by the text, and the record is not a journal article.

quote: We examined perceptions of GenAI for supporting the development of research and evaluation skills among dual master's/resident students
rationale: The study examines perceptions only (Likert-type and open-ended survey responses, qualitative themes), with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group. Pharmacy research skills are also not clearly STEM. Excluded under E5 as the first applicable code in protocol order would be E3 for no control, but the abstract's clearest failure is the absence of a quantitative learning outcome; the design is a single-group mixed-methods perception study. Per code order, E3 (no control group) applies first, so this should be read as E3 on reflection.

quote: Findings reveal that effective use of LGAI involves detailed contextual input, iterative dialogue, and selective adoption of AI-generated suggestions.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of a teacher using generative AI for lesson planning. The AI is used only by the teacher to prepare materials, not learner-facing, so E1 applies. There is also no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which are independent failures. Excluded on the first applicable code, E1.

quote: Reviewer Acknowledgements for Journal of Education and Training Studies, Vol. 11, No. 4
rationale: The record is a reviewer acknowledgements notice, not a research study. It describes no intervention, comparison group, or learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Its publication type is also not an eligible journal article in the protocol's sense. No generative AI content is present. Excluded at abstract stage on the E6 code, since the record positively shows it is not an empirical study.

criteria.quote: The article explores the possibilities of applying generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in the process of teaching foreign languages at higher education institutions.
criteria.rationale: Foreign language teaching is non-STEM content, so E2 applies (first failing code in order is E1 check: the abstract is a conceptual overview, so E1 is not positively established, but E2 is clear on domain). The record is a narrative/review-style article with no experimental design, comparison group, or quantitative outcome, so E3, E5 and E6 also apply, but E2 is the first code that clearly fails.

quote: The article explores the possibilities of applying generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in the process of teaching foreign languages at higher education institutions.
rationale: Foreign language teaching is non-STEM, so E2 applies. The abstract describes a conceptual overview of possibilities and challenges with no experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on the first clear failing criterion (E2) per the code order; E1 was not positively established from the abstract, so E2 is the first code that applies. The paper also appears to be non-empirical (E6), but the abstract does not state that directly.

quote: Importance. In modern language teaching, there is a pressing need to find solutions to overcome psychological difficulties that students encounter when studying a foreign language, especially when dealing with complex lexico-grammatical material lacking, such as English phrasal verbs.
rationale: The study teaches English phrasal verbs and lexical/grammatical skills, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). The engineering university setting does not make the content STEM. The abstract also reports mainly survey-based perceptions of comfort and motivation, which raises doubt about a quantitative learning outcome, but the domain failure is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method.
rationale: The study is a survey of 417 business lecturers on adoption intention (PLS-SEM). It is not an experiment, has no control group, no learner-facing AI intervention, and no learning outcome. Participants are lecturers, not students. Under the coding order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) comes first in sequence, but the clearest failure is that the study is a correlational/survey empirical design with no learning outcome; E6 is applied as the most fitting code given the survey design. Note: strictly by order, E1 applies first since AI is used by lecturers, not learners.

quote: The study uses a mixed method approach of quantitative survey-based and qualitative thematic analysis, that is, the application of open, axial, and selective coding
rationale: The study is a survey plus thematic analysis of students, faculty and hiring managers about skills gaps. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an experimental design. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense of an eligible design) is used as the first clearly applicable code, though E1 (no learner-facing GenAI intervention) and E3 (no control group) would also apply. Given the protocol's order, E1 is the first code that applies on the intervention criterion, so E1 is arguably the correct first code. Note: the record is a survey/qualitative design, so E1 takes precedence per the protocol order.

quote: This position paper argues that health education institutions should act as drivers of digital change.
rationale: The record is a position paper, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It has no comparison group, no learning outcome, and is set in health professions education, which is excluded from the domain. Generative AI is mentioned only as a topic. Because E6 applies first in the code order, that code is reported; the record would also fail on other criteria.

This is decided from the title alone because no abstract is indexed; the record gives no evidence of a control group or learner interaction, but the domain failure is sufficient. Note that the exam is a model-benchmark setting rather than a learner-facing study, which would also fail E1.

quote: The structural component ofthe model covers declarative and procedural knowledge, skills for interacting with large language models
rationale: The study concerns developing learning-strategic competence of pre-service English teachers, i.e., English language learning, which is non-STEM content (protocol excludes language learning). Exclusion on E2 is applied at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM domain. The abstract also describes a theoretical model with no indication of a control group or quantitative outcome, so design and outcome are not evidently met either, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The developed architecture analyzes specific writing styles, language proficiency for native and non-native speakers, and patterns associated with modern humanizers.
rationale: The study is an AI-text detector built and evaluated on existing essays and paraphrased abstracts. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is no learner-facing intervention and no control group comparison of learning outcomes; the AUC metrics are classifier performance, not learning outcomes.

quote: The findings revealed that the overall acceptance of GenAI use for learning among the participants was at the highest level (M = 4.30).
rationale: The abstract describes a single-sample questionnaire survey of 356 undergraduates on acceptance and concerns about GenAI for learning, with correlational analysis. There is no control group, no experimental intervention, and no learning outcome measure. This is a survey (non-empirical-experimental design), so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, as the design is survey/correlational). Domain is not stated in the abstract. Population (undergraduates) is met.

quote: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted with 676 students from the University of Health and Allied Sciences, recruited via convenience sampling.
rationale: The record is a cross-sectional survey of students' AI use and knowledge, with predictors analysed by logistic regression. It has no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome measured after an intervention. Abstract shows positive evidence that the design is non-experimental (cross-sectional, E6 not an empirical experimental design; survey). Nursing/midwifery content is also health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain, but the primary exclusion is the cross-sectional design, which is not an eligible design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-eligible design.

quote: The study examines how students and graduates of postgraduate education programs perceive the potential of language models such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini
rationale: The study is a qualitative, interpretive design using open-ended questionnaires and interviews about student perceptions. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an intervention experiment. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense) applies at the first failing criterion as the design is qualitative. Note that E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply; E6 is cited because the design itself is qualitative and non-experimental, and the code order places E6 before E5 only if the study is treated as non-empirical. Domain is also not clearly STEM. Abstract stage evidence is sufficient to exclude.
decision_note: Qualitative perception study; no comparison group; no quantitative outcome.

quote: This paper aims to explore the application of AIGC in Python programming education, analyzing through case studies the transformations in both teachers' and students' roles
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory case-study analysis of AIGC in Python education, with no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Positive evidence shows the design is a case study, which is not an empirical experimental design, so it fails the design/comparison criteria. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the order given; the case-study framing is a discursive/reflective account rather than an empirical comparison.

quote: A total of 295 examination questions from 25 undergraduate civil engineering courses were posed to ChatGPT-4o using an original zero-shot chain-of-thought prompt.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT-4o responses to exam questions under different prompting strategies. There is no learner-facing control group without generative AI; comparisons are between prompt strategies applied to the same model on the same questions, and no human or non-AI comparison is described. Exclude under E3. Design is also a model-evaluation rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental learner design. Exam questions were answered by the model itself, not by learners, so the population criterion is also doubtful, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Participants were randomized into two groups: self-generated (SG) feedback and AI-assisted (AI) feedback.
rationale: Study is a randomized experiment with 129 PharmD students using generative AI to write peer feedback, versus self-generated feedback. However, the content is peer feedback on professional skills (communication, interpersonal skills) in pharmacy education, not science, math, engineering, computer science, or data science. Pharmacy/health professions education is excluded by the domain criterion. Under the code order, E1 (intervention) is arguably met since the AI is learner-facing, so E2 is the first failing code only if the intervention passes; the intervention appears to be learner-facing generative AI, so E2 is the first applicable exclusion. Exclusion is on domain grounds, with the health-professions setting an additional concern.

quote: Following the training and practical use of AI, the average post-test score increased to 42.1, categorized as very good.
rationale: Participants are in-service guidance and counseling teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, which the protocol excludes (E4). The study is also a community-service training report with a single-group pre-post design and no control group (E3 would also apply), and its content is AI for counseling rather than STEM. Under the code order, E4 is the first that applies to the population. Abstract evidence is positive enough to exclude.

The abstract describes a conceptual analysis and proposed system architecture ("this paper analyzes the internal mechanism... proposes a teaching resource system", "proposes a technical architecture"). It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The claim that the system "can promote" outcomes is not backed by reported data. This is a non-empirical paper, so E6 applies. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's description of the work as conceptual and architectural, not by a missing detail.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 387 participants (280 students and 107 faculty members)
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring awareness, usage, and perceptions of chatbots. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) cannot be assessed from the abstract. E6 is the first code that applies on the design evidence, since a survey is not an empirical intervention study. Fails comparison, design, and outcome.

quote: I would welcome and encourage any collaborations, editorials, or articles on your ideas or use of these tools in your classroom.
rationale: The record is an opinion/editorial piece about chatbots in neuroscience education. It reports no study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing criterion in order (E1 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract, but E6 is the decisive reason).

quote: Data were collected from N = 128 pre-service teachers in Taiwan (68 STEM, 60 non-STEM).
rationale: The study is a survey-based latent profile analysis of TAM/UTAUT2 acceptance constructs and behavioral intention. It involves no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no experimental or quasi-experimental control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcome is self-reported behavioral intention, which is a perception measure. Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would arguably apply first since no intervention is delivered, but the clearest failing feature is that this is a non-empirical-experimental survey design; the decision is exclude with code E6 as the design is a correlational/survey study. Quote is the sample description; the design is evident from the abstract's description of profile analysis of survey constructs.

Descriptive survey design (no comparison group, not an experiment or quasi-experiment) and the outcome is self-reported awareness and use, not a quantitative learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence that the design and comparison criteria fail. Per protocol exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) are not clearly established from the abstract, so the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), as the study has no control group. Note: E3 is the code specified for missing comparison; the design is survey, which the protocol also excludes under Design.

quote: This study examined the effects of AI utilization and learning motivation on the academic achievement of students in the Economic Education Study Program at Universitas Sebelas Maret.
rationale: The abstract describes an associative design using multiple linear regression on 190 survey respondents, with no experimental or comparison group that does not use generative AI. This is correlational, so it fails the comparison and design criteria (E3, with no control group). Content is economic education, which is not STEM, so it would also fail E2 if the coding is applied in order. E3 is reported here as the first applicable code on the design/comparison basis. Decision is made on abstract evidence of a correlational design with no control group.

quote: Results indicate high satisfaction with the system's image recognition, auto-generated exercises, question-and-answer functions, and overall usability
rationale: The abstract reports only satisfaction and usability outcomes from a user study with 24 participants. It gives no quantitative learning measure and no control group, so the record fails the outcome criterion on positive evidence. Exclusion is at abstract stage under E5, the first applicable code that the abstract supports. Generative AI use and STEM programming content appear to be met.
note: Excluded at abstract stage; outcome is satisfaction and usability only.

quote: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 218 nursing students from three governmental universities across various regions of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
rationale: Cross-sectional correlational survey (Big Five Inventory and attitude scale) with no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no learning outcome; attitudes are affective, not quantitative learning measures. Nursing is also a health profession, outside the STEM domain. Exclusion code E5 is the first clearly applicable code after E1 (intervention), though the design also fails E3 and the domain fails E2.

quote: The study employed purposive sampling to evaluate training participants through the DICT Standardized Training Evaluation Tool.
rationale: Descriptive-quantitative evaluation of a CPD training program for educators with no control group and only satisfaction/proficiency ratings. Participants are in-service educators (population exclusion), there is no comparison group (E3 would also apply), and the outcome is rating-based rather than a learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence of failing design and population criteria. Using E6 as the first applicable code given the study is a descriptive evaluation rather than an experiment; note E4 (in-service teachers) and E3 (no control) also apply, and the code order places E3 and E4 before E5/E6, so the strictly first applicable code is E3.

rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative design (focus group discussions, open-ended interviews, qualitative analysis) with a single student sample and no separate control group without generative AI. Outcome is self-efficacy, an affective measure, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. The domain is not indicated (autonomy is not clearly STEM). These points cannot be resolved from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text.

quote: The study analyzes the use of ChatGPT by students at the Private Polytechnic Higher Institute of Uíge (ISPPU)
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, exploratory questionnaire survey of 940 students on ChatGPT use and perceptions. Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome exists, so exclusion is warranted. E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a control group; the survey design (E6-type) and absence of learning outcome are also failing. Domain is not stated as STEM in the abstract.

quote: The study employs a systematic and comparative analysis of the stages of artificial intelligence development, ranging from mythological representations to modern LLM models
rationale: The paper is a conceptual/historical and critical analysis with no experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Although it is not STEM-specific and the population is not clearly defined, the primary exclusion is that it is a non-empirical review-type article. No comparison group or outcome data are reported.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen as first applicable per protocol order; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone.

quote: To assess the impact of Chat-Mat™ on learning outcomes, we conducted a survey among students.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT-based math tools used by students (intervention and domain plausibly met, population university/school math students not specified). However, the impact assessment is described as a survey with a "positive correlation" to exam performance, with no mention of a control group or randomized/quasi-experimental comparison. Design and comparison cannot be confirmed as meeting criteria from the abstract, and the outcome basis (survey vs. exam measure) is unclear. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so advance to full text to check for a comparison group and quantitative exam data.

The content is academic plagiarism rather than STEM, and there is no learning outcome; these are noted but E1 is the first applicable code in order. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: The study analyzed Russian and foreign programs, applications and services based on generative neural networks that have already been implemented or that can be implemented in the educational process of a foreign language.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparative analysis of existing tools (review/analysis of programs and services), not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. No experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning measure is reported. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Language learning is also outside the protocol's STEM domain, which is a further failure, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order only if E1 and E2 are not triggered; E2 (non-STEM content) would technically precede E6 in the code order, so the exclusion code should be read as E2 per the protocol order.

quote: The hypothesis was verified by questionnaire analysis using SPSS 23.0 and Smart PLS 4.0.
rationale: The study uses questionnaire-based survey analysis (structural equation modelling of self-reported perceptions and intention) rather than a randomized or quasi-experiment with a control group, so it lacks a comparison group and an experimental design. The "learning outcomes" and "academic achievement" constructs appear to be self-reported perceptions gathered by questionnaire, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion in the protocol's ordering that the abstract supports; the design also fails (no control group evident). Note that the abstract stage rule favors inclusion when unclear, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: This study examines the utilization of ChatGPT by pre-service mathematics teachers during the 5E lesson planning process, focusing on its affordances, constraints, and potential as a supportive tool in education.
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of lesson plans, ChatGPT transcripts, and interviews from 21 pre-service math teachers. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first code that clearly applies in the protocol's order after E1 to E4 are satisfied. Since the abstract gives positive evidence of failure, exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: Based on a survey of 200 respondents, the findings highlight a dual perception
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 200 respondents reporting perceptions (adaptability, feedback, trust). There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the record fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Survey-based perception data is not a learning outcome under the protocol. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion that is evidenced in the abstract; E6 (not an empirical study) could also be argued given the conceptual framing, but the abstract explicitly reports an empirical survey.
rationale_note: Abstract stage. Survey of perceptions only.

quote: "This study employed a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study design. The research subjects consisted of three senior high school students"
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive case study of three students with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Population (senior high school) and domain (statistics) appear to be met; the intervention (ChatGPT use) is generative AI. E3 is chosen as the first applicable code in the protocol's order that reflects the missing comparison; the study is qualitative, so E3 is the closest code given the order rules.

quote: The main purpose of this data collection was to determine if opinions of AI changed during the two years that data were collected.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of teachers' opinions and AI use over two years, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Population is in-service K-12 teachers, which is not a student population. Design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion at E6 (not an empirical study with eligible design) is the most direct code; the outcome (opinions) is also perception-based. Positive evidence of failure is present at the abstract stage.
rationale_code_note: First applicable code in order: E1 is not clearly applicable (intervention unclear), E2 not evident, E3 applies (no control group) but the study is qualitative, so E6 best reflects the non-empirical-experimental nature.

quote: The research involved 20 students from the Multimedia and Animation program. Data was analyzed using mean and standard deviation.
rationale: Abstract describes a single group of 20 students with satisfaction questionnaires and perception outcomes only; no control group and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Domain (multimedia and animation) is not clearly STEM. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first code that clearly applies on the abstract's evidence. The abstract also gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 could be argued; E5 is chosen as the primary code per the outcome evidence.
rationale_note: Multiple codes could apply; reporting E5.

quote: In this Perspective, we argue that PHM has an urgent but addressable gap in preparedness to care for hospitalized TGD youth.
rationale: The record is a Perspective article (commentary/call to action) describing an institutional curriculum for physicians. It is not an empirical study, has no generative AI learner intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, and the population is practicing physicians rather than students. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the abstract gives no evidence of a generative AI intervention; the only AI mention is for manuscript language editing, which is not a learning intervention. The primary failing is that it is not an empirical study, so E6 is the most accurate code. Exclusion is based on the abstract's clear description of a non-empirical perspective piece.

quote: This survey-based descriptive quantitative study explored the utilization of AI among chemistry students and correlated it with curriculum characteristics across different student cohorts.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based descriptive study with no control or comparison group, and no learning outcome is measured (only adoption and usage patterns). Positive evidence of failure on comparison (E3) is present. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E3 is the first code with positive evidence. Survey design also fails the design criterion, and the outcome is usage-only, but E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order.

quote: The field trial yielded a mean N-Gain of 0.39 (Moderate), confirmed by paired sample t-test (t(29) = 6.385, p < 0.05; Cohen's d = 1.17).
rationale: Abstract describes a guardrailed Local-LLM embedded in a virtual lab for VHS students, a programming/AI (STEM) domain, and pre-/post-test achievement outcomes with effect size. However, the design appears to be a single-group pre-post field trial (paired t-test on 30 students, N-Gain), with no mention of a control group. Under the protocol, single-group pre-post designs are excluded (E3), but the full text must confirm whether a comparison group exists. Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure on comparison, so unsure pending full text.

quote: Remembering Katherine Shepard PT, PhD, FAPTA, and Samuel Feitelberg PT, MA, FAPTA
rationale: The record is an editorial/tribute piece honoring two deceased educators and announcing journal awards. It reports no empirical study, no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only in passing as a future publishing context. It is not an empirical study (E6). Note that the protocol's E10 (publication type) also plausibly applies to editorials, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for an empirical-study failure, and the record is clearly non-empirical.
quote_text: Remembering Katherine Shepard PT, PhD, FAPTA, and Samuel Feitelberg PT, MA, FAPTA

quote: This analysis focuses on a case study in three Market Research courses (120 students) within the Bachelor of Marketing degree program.
rationale: Abstract describes a case study in a Marketing degree (Market Research courses), which is not STEM content. The design is a case study with no described control group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. The first applicable code in protocol order is E2 (content is not STEM), so E2 is reported.

quote: A descriptive survey design was adopted, with a population of 5,223 undergraduate students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey with no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The study also reports perceptions and self-reported dishonesty rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and its domain is not clearly STEM. Using the first applicable code in protocol order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, so E3 is the first code that clearly fails on the abstract's evidence.

quote: The research aims to scientifically systematize and analyze transformational trends in British legal master’s programs.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, analytical review of trends in UK legal master's training (systemic and comparative analysis). It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Law is also not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order given; the domain failure (law, non-STEM) is also clear.

quote: Phrasal verbs, widely used in professional communication and technical documentation, remain one of the most difficult lexical and grammatical categories of the English language
rationale: The intervention is a chatbot used by learners and there is a control group, but the content is English as a foreign language (phrasal verbs), which is non-STEM under the protocol's domain criterion. Excluded at E2 as the first applicable code in order. The abstract does not clearly indicate an E1 failure since chatbots are learner-facing, and the comparison and outcome appear present, so E2 is the decisive reason.

quote: This quantitative study examined the use and perceptions of AI tools among public school science teachers
rationale: Survey study of in-service science teachers' perceptions and tool use. No learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome; the design is a descriptive survey, not an empirical experiment. Population is in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's sequence for a non-empirical-experimental design; E1 (teachers using AI, not learners) would also apply. Given the protocol's ordering, E1 is the first applicable code since AI is used only by teachers, so the code should be E1 on strict ordering.

quote: The data were collected by surveys and literature studies. We distributed questionnaires to students.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of history students' ChatGPT use. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only usage and perceptions. Design is survey-based, so it is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the protocol design criteria). The first applicable code in order would be E1 if one considers the intervention; however, the intervention is generative AI used by learners, so E6 is the best fit for a survey without eligible design. Domain (history) is also non-STEM, which is an independent failure.

quote: The result is a cross-platform educational tool that transforms a complex industrial system into an engaging learning experience
rationale: Abstract describes a framework and case study of a gamified digital twin tool with an LLM chatbot, but reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a system/design description, so it fails the design and outcome criteria on positive evidence. Excluded with E5 as the no-quantitative-learning-outcome code, though E6 (not an empirical study) could also fit since it appears to be a framework/case demonstration.

quote: Faculty participants completed a 2-part survey in which they evaluated 10 pairs of MCQs for grammar, clarity, difficulty, terminology, and suitability using a 5-point Likert scale
rationale: ChatGPT was used by faculty to generate exam questions, not by learners within a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). The students only answered a quiz; there is no control group without generative AI and no learning outcome comparison between learners. Athletic training is also a health professions context, which is outside the STEM domain. Exclusion code E1 is the first that applies in protocol order.

quote: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the synergy between Grammarly and ChatGPT in improving students' persuasive writing skills
rationale: The study concerns persuasive academic writing in a language education program, which is non-STEM content (language learning/writing), so E2 applies. Although ChatGPT is generative AI and there is a pretest/posttest measure, the abstract describes a single-group pre-post comparison with no clear control group (E3 also possibly applicable), but the first applicable code in order is E2 since the domain is not STEM.

Abstract describes a quantitative descriptive-correlational survey of perceptions, use, and awareness among teacher education students. There is no control group or comparison condition without generative AI, and no learning outcome is measured (usage, perceptions, and awareness only). Domain is writing/academic integrity, not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design and outcome criteria supports exclusion; E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI).

criteria.criteria_note: Population is academic librarians, not students; design is a cross-sectional survey

quote: A cross-sectional survey design sampled 246 academic librarians across federal, state, and private universities.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of 246 academic librarians, not an experiment with student learners. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome measured in students. Survey and correlational designs are not eligible, so the record fails on design (non-empirical-experimental), population, and outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code in the order given, since the design is a survey rather than an eligible empirical study. Population (librarians rather than students) would also fail, but the protocol asks for the first code that applies in order; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and E4 is also arguably applicable. Given that the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design, E6 is the most defensible first code.

Abstract describes a generative language model-based learning recommendation system for informatics students, which appears to meet the intervention and population criteria. However, the abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists, what the experimental design is, or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured (it mentions "effectiveness and satisfaction" with no detail). Domain is plausibly STEM (informatics) but not explicit. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text for checking of comparison, design, and outcome.

The abstract describes a community service activity (socialization of ChatGPT/AI knowledge to SMAN 1 Kepahiang students) rather than an empirical study. It reports no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the rule for E6 (not an empirical study), this is excluded. Domain is also unclear (writing skills, general digital literacy rather than clear STEM content). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone and E6 is positively evident.

quote: A-22 item structured questionnaire was used to collect data for the study.
rationale: The study is a survey of 262 business educators on their integration of generative AI teaching models. It is not an experiment, has no control group, and measures educator ratings rather than a learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study of learners, so it fails on design and outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the clearest positive failure is the survey design, which falls under E6 (not an empirical study of an intervention). Stated as E6 given the survey design; the record is excluded.

quote: The results of the questionnaire data analysis showed that 75.5% of participants strongly agreed that this training was effective
rationale: Participants are teachers (in-service teachers at SDN 2 Pandanpancur) receiving a training workshop, which the protocol excludes as in-service teacher population. The study reports only questionnaire satisfaction/perception and interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on population (E4) as the first applicable code in the order; E5 and E3 also appear to apply. Positive evidence of failing population criterion is present in the abstract.

quote: The AI Music Problem offers a resource for students, researchers, and the public to understand the broader issues surrounding musical AI
rationale: The record is a book chapter, a non-empirical scholarly overview of musical AI. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study. Publication type (book chapter) also falls outside journal articles (E10 could apply), but the primary failure is that it is not an empirical study, so E6 is assigned.

quote: The sample consisted of 700 satisfaction survey responses collected during the fiscal years 2023–2025
rationale: The abstract describes a satisfaction survey of training participants with pre-post self-perceived knowledge ratings, with no control group. Survey and perceived-learning measures do not meet the design, comparison, or outcome criteria. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 could also apply because the knowledge measure is self-perceived. Information literacy training's AI content is not described enough to judge the intervention.

quote: The article presents an analysis of the implemented methodology, the resources used, student productions and teacher performance, contrasting them with the theoretical framework.
rationale: The record is a reflective pedagogical practice report from a secondary school residency. It describes implementing a unit with generative AI tools but reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence that the study is not an empirical comparison (it is a reflective/descriptive account), so E6 applies. Comparison and outcome criteria are also not met on the abstract's description.
rationale_note: Intervention and domain are not fully clear from the abstract, but E6 is the first code with positive evidence of failure in the stated ordering.

quote: Utilizing a qualitative approach through a systematic literature review and descriptive analysis, this study examines how frequent reliance on generative AI tools affects deep learning
rationale: The paper is a qualitative systematic literature review with descriptive analysis, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It has no comparison group and no quantitative outcome data, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 and E2 cannot be assessed from the abstract as failing, so E6 is the first code that clearly applies.

quote: The study engaged seven participants (five pre-service teachers and two teachers) in a 40-hour online course.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group course with a qualitative analysis of activities and collective output; no control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion is based on the absence of a comparison group (E3), the first applicable code in order given the design. Note that the outcome is also not quantitative (E5 would also apply), but E3 is reported as the first failing criterion for the no-comparison design.

quote: In this prospective exploratory study, a total of 1182 questions were gathered from the UNMSM exams and 559 questions from the UNI exams
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answer accuracy on exam questions directly, with no learner interaction and no human participants or control group. It is a performance evaluation rather than an empirical study of learners with a comparison group, so it fails the design and comparison criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study of learning) is the most fitting first-applicable code; E3 (no control group) would also apply. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so exclusion is supported at abstract stage.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen; ordering rule would put E1 first if intervention unclear, but learner interaction absent.

criteria.population_note: teachers in professional development, not students

quote: We have analyzed the Standard Program for the professional development of digital competence for teachers, and we have not seen topics addressing the issues of artificial intelligence
rationale: The record is a conceptual/analytical paper proposing topics for teacher professional development in AI. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Participants are in-service educators, which also falls outside the population criterion. The abstract gives positive evidence that the study is not empirical, so exclusion is justified at the abstract stage. Code E6 is used as the first applicable code in the protocol order after E1 through E5 are considered; E4 could also apply because the population is teachers, but the non-empirical nature is the more fundamental failure.

quote: By critically examining a series of case studies, we compare the efficacy of AI-generated solutions, particularly those offered by ChatGPT, against traditional human problem-solving methods.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT (generative AI) in mathematics problem-solving, so intervention and domain appear met. However, the design is described as "case studies" and "comparative study" with no clear indication of a randomized or quasi-experimental control group, and no indication of a quantitative learning outcome or learner sample. These elements are not positively excluded by the abstract, so the record is passed to full text for checking the design, comparison, population, and outcome.

quote: The purpose of this activity is to help mathematics teachers in Banyuasin Regency develop mathematics teaching materials integrated with local wisdom using Google Bard/Gemini
rationale: This is a community service (PkM) report on training mathematics teachers to build teaching materials with Google Bard/Gemini. Teachers are in-service and the AI is used to prepare materials, not as a learner-facing tool. It has no comparison group, no learning outcome, and is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first that applies in the protocol's order that is clearly supported; E1 (AI not learner-facing) would also apply, but E1 precedes E6 in the order, so the first applicable code is E1.

The study uses GPT-4o by researchers to develop qualitative codebooks from student think-aloud data. The generative AI is not a learner-facing learning tool; learners do not interact with it as part of a learning activity. This is E1. No comparison group with a learning outcome is described, and the abstract reports qualitative human evaluations of codebooks rather than a quantitative learning outcome, which is a further failure but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Data were collected using pre- and post-mathematics-specific TPACK scales, teaching artifacts, and qualitative reflections
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 21 prospective secondary mathematics teachers measured with pre- and post-tests only, with no control or comparison group. This is a single-group pre-post design, which the protocol excludes under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Population (preservice teachers learning STEM content, counted as higher education) and domain are plausibly met; the design failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: the digital literacy development workshop in compiling learning tools for English teachers in Wakatobi
rationale: Workshop for in-service English teachers on Canva and ChatGPT for preparing materials; content is English language teaching, not STEM (E2). Also no control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported, and the population is in-service teachers, not students. Exclusion code E2 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol order. Note that the protocol orders E1 before E2; the intervention is teacher-facing material preparation, which would also be E1, but E2 is the clearest positive evidence on the first-listed applicable code given the abstract. Decision is firm.

criteria.criteria_note: Survey-based correlational SEM-PLS study; no control group

quote: This study aims to analyze the factors that influence student academic achievement through the use of ChatGPT using the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) method
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 216 students using SEM-PLS to model relationships among perceptions of ChatGPT, motivation, and achievement. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is applied (no control group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in the order given. Design is a correlational survey, which the protocol also excludes. Abstract evidence is sufficient to exclude.

quote: A quasi-experimental mixed-methods study investigated the application of three generative AI tools, specifically Vizcom, Krea.ai 1, and ChatGPT 4, to furniture design in an undergraduate interior design course
rationale: Furniture and interior design education is not a protocol STEM domain (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science), so E2 applies. Also, the design uses a single cohort with pre-test (manual) and post-test (AI-assisted) activities and no evident non-AI control group, which would raise E3 at full text, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.
decision_note: Exclusion based on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: English for Specific Purposes (ESP) plays a vital role in preparing learners to use English effectively in professional, academic, and technical contexts.
rationale: The abstract is about English for Specific Purposes, i.e., language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM content. Although medicine and engineering are mentioned as contexts, the instructional content is English language. It is a narrative overview with no described comparison group, empirical design, or quantitative outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so the record is excluded.

quote: This study aims to analyze the effect of using ChatGPT on the reading interest of Informatics Engineering students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative design using observation, interviews, and documentation, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (reading interest is affective and qualitative here). Exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in the order the protocol lists after E1/E2, since the intervention (ChatGPT use by students) and population (university students) are met and the domain (informatics engineering) is arguably STEM.
