The design failure is clear from the abstract, so E3 is reported as the primary code; E5 and E6 also apply in substance, but E3 is first in the required order for the design shortfall. Decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: PSRC 2024 Abstracts Table of Contents
rationale: The record is a conference abstract table of contents for a plastic surgery meeting supplement, not an empirical study. It contains no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no STEM learning outcome. It is not a journal article reporting a study, so it fails on non-empirical status (E6). Checking E1 first: no learner-facing generative AI is described, so E1 technically applies first in the protocol's order. Given the protocol says to report the first code in order, E1 is the correct code.

quote: A descriptive and correlational design was employed to examine patterns of advanced achievement (Level 4) and underperformance (Level 1) across districts
rationale: The study is a descriptive and correlational analysis of existing district-level accountability data. ChatGPT was used by stakeholders/researchers to interpret statistics, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. There is no control group without generative AI, and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Exclusion code E3 applies (no control group), with the intervention and design also not meeting the criteria. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: Here, we present a summary of the workshop session titled "Supporting Student Mental Health and Well-being in Engineering."
rationale: The record is a workshop summary from a education summit about student mental health. It is not an empirical study: there is no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as one summit topic, not as a studied intervention. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).

quote: Users positively rated the ease of interaction, the quality of consultations and the completeness of the information provided.
rationale: The study evaluates a GPT-4 career guidance chatbot for applicants. The only reported results are user ratings and perceptions of ease, quality and completeness, plus general claims of accuracy and speed. No quantitative learning outcome is described, and there is no clear controlled comparison with a separate group. Career guidance is also not clearly a STEM learning domain. The paper fails on E5 because it reports only perceptions and satisfaction, and this is the first code that applies in order.

The abstract describes a sampling study of institutions' financial aid websites (whether chatbots are embedded and whether they are programmed in Spanish). It has no learners, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a descriptive survey-style design, so it fails the outcome and design criteria. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion that is evident from the abstract; E6 (not an empirical study) would also be arguable, but the study is empirical website sampling, so E5 is the best fit. Quote is null because no single abstract passage states the lack of a learning outcome directly.

quote: This timely book provides a detailed examination of ethics in artificial intelligence and is sure to become a valuable reference for educators and researchers
rationale: The record is a book review of a philosophy monograph on AI value alignment, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in protocol order that is clearly positive from the abstract; E1 would also apply on intervention grounds, but the record is primarily a non-empirical item, and E6 captures it directly.

quote: we conducted two experiments to evaluate the use of large language models (LLM) for grading particularly challenging student answers
rationale: The LLMs are used to grade student answers, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Grading-only AI is explicitly excluded by the protocol, and the abstract gives positive evidence of this. Experiment 2 is a BKT mastery estimation from grades, also not learner-facing. Mathematics domain and K-12 population are met. No comparison group with a non-generative-AI condition is described in the abstract.

criteria.domain_note: Art, design and architecture course; not STEM

quote: This study presents an innovative educational model for second-year students at the Faculty of Art, Design and Architecture to integrate generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools
rationale: The course is in art, design and architecture education, which is not a STEM domain under the protocol (E2). The abstract also describes a single-course pre-test/post-test design with no mention of a control group, which would separately suggest E3, but the first applicable code in order is E2. Intervention (generative AI used by learners) and population (university students) appear to be met.

quote: Kegiatan dilaksanakan di SMP Negeri 2 Indralaya Selatan dan melibatkan 29 guru melalui pendekatan partisipatif dan kolaboratif.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers in a community service program, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The AI use is by teachers to prepare assessment materials, which is also not learner-facing (E1 would also apply), and the design is a single-group pre-post with no control group (E3). Under the protocol order, E1 is checked first and would apply; however, the population exclusion is the clearest positive evidence. Per the rule order, the first applicable code is E1 since intervention is teacher-only. Correcting the code to E1 for protocol compliance.

Physics domain and a Gemini Gems-based Socratic tutor (generative AI, learner-facing) are evident. However, the abstract describes a design/illustrative use-case paper with qualitative observations ("Our findings show that the 'role-engineered' Gem facilitates a Socratic dialogue, in stark contrast to a standard Gemini model"). No quantitative learning outcome or control group with learner data is reported, so it fails on outcome. Exclusion E5 applies at abstract stage on positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured. Note that the abstract does not mention a comparison with learners; the contrast is with a standard model's output, not a learner group.

quote: With a case study of the documentary Disclosure: Trans Lives on Screen (Sam Feder, 2020), this article examines the documentarians’ mode of activism
rationale: This is a media studies/historical analysis of Hollywood labor discrimination and neoliberalism with a case study of a documentary. It involves no learners, no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and is not an empirical learning study. E1 is the first applicable code in order (no learner-facing generative AI), so it is excluded on that code. The other criteria also clearly fail, but only the first applicable code is reported.

quote: Its development involved digital tools, such as ChatGPT (for text), Freepik (for visuals), and LearningApps (for interactive activities).
rationale: At abstract stage, the pilot study reports no separate control group; the design appears to be a single-group pilot with validation by teachers. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group (only two age groups of students receiving the game), so E3 applies. Generative AI use (ChatGPT) is only used in developing materials by the designers, not by learners, which would also be E1 at fulltext; the first applicable code by order would be E1, so this should be re-checked. Given rule 4 and the abstract-stage evidence, excluding with E3 is the best-supported code from the abstract, but the researcher should verify the intervention criterion (ChatGPT was used to develop the game, not as a learner-facing tool), which points to E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: this article addresses this issue, providing a procedure to help teachers modernise their learning goals and assessments to prepare students for the world of intelligent tools.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual article offering a procedure for teachers to revise learning goals and assessments. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is therefore not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the article is non-empirical.

quote: The study uses a case study approach with a questionnaire instrument to explore students' experiences and perceptions.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study using a questionnaire to explore experiences and perceptions. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceived social change and self-reported productivity. Design is not experimental or quasi-experimental. Per the code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly contradicted at abstract stage, but the absence of any control group and the case-study design are positive evidence of failure. E3 is the first code that clearly applies (no control group without generative AI). Population is university biology education students, which is eligible; domain is not clearly STEM (biology education is ambiguous) but the decision rests on E3.

Abstract is not available in the index; only the title and venue are given. The title mentions AI tools in a Benford's Law teaching context in accounting, which is a borderline domain question (accounting is not clearly STEM, though Benford's Law is statistical). Whether AI is generative, whether there is a control group, and whether any learning outcome is measured cannot be determined. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: This qualitative study investigates the integration of AI, specifically ChatGPT, into lecture and lesson planning by faculty members in Kosovo.
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study of 10 faculty members interviewed about their use of ChatGPT for lesson planning. Participants are in-service university teachers, not learners, and there is no control group or quantitative learning outcome. The design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical study under the protocol's experimental designs. The first applicable code in order is E1, since the AI is used by teachers to prepare materials rather than learner-facing. Given the rule that E1 is checked first, the correct first code is E1, not E6. Correcting: exclusion code E1 applies because the tool is used only by faculty for lesson planning.

Abstract describes a survey-based study (surveys and interviews) of undergraduates' acceptance of ChatGPT and its relation to academic self-efficacy, with no control group or experimental comparison. Design is correlational/survey and the outcome is perceptual (self-efficacy, acceptance), not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not clearly STEM. Excluded under E3 as there is no comparison group without generative AI; the abstract gives positive evidence of no control condition. Note that E6 (not an empirical study) would not apply since this is empirical but non-experimental; E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the lack of a control group.

quote: The results showed that students perceive AI as a useful tool in the processes of checking information, comparing, considering alternative points of view and re-evaluating their own opinions.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire measuring university students' perceptions of AI for critical thinking. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the only measures are perception ratings, which the protocol excludes. Design is a survey, not an experiment. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits here, since the outcome is perception-only. E3 (no control group) and E6 (not an empirical study, which it is not) would also apply; E5 is reported as the perception-only outcome failure.

Abstract shows EFL speaking practice with ChatGPT, which is a generative AI intervention with students, but the content is English language learning, which is non-STEM. The study is also an interpretive qualitative design with thematic analysis of interviews and no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5 and the design criterion as well. The first applicable code in order is E2.

quote: In this brief, the authors Jeremy Price and Shuchi Grover explore the exciting possibilities and critical challenges of generative AI (GenAI) for STEM teaching.
rationale: The record is a CADRE policy/research brief that explores opportunities and challenges of GenAI for STEM teaching. It is a discussion piece, not an empirical study: no learners, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome are described. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). It is also a brief rather than a journal article, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: This paper proposes and reflects on a teaching methodology for introducing relational ethics in the engineering curriculum based on a pilot at TU Delft
rationale: The abstract describes a teaching methodology proposal and reflections on a course redesign, with no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no evidence of a controlled design. It is not an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the abstract also gives no evidence of a control group (E3) or quantitative outcome (E5), but E6 is the first applicable code in the rough reading of the design.

quote: We evaluated the performance of ChatGPT 3.5 on solving spreadsheets modeling assessment questions with multiple linked test items categorized according to the revised Bloom's taxonomy.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's own accuracy on assessment questions under four prompt settings. There is no learner interaction and no control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is between prompt conditions of the same model. This is not an empirical study of learners, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced. Note that E1 (learner-facing intervention) would also fail on the abstract's description, since ChatGPT itself is the subject rather than a learning activity; E6 is reported as the most defensible single code given the study is a model-performance evaluation. Domain (spreadsheet modeling) is plausibly STEM-adjacent. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: The study adopted the experimental methodology and the quasi-experimental design.
rationale: At abstract stage, the record describes a quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups of tenth-grade students using ChatGPT in a computer subject, with an academic achievement test as outcome. Computer subject content plausibly counts as STEM (computer science). No positive evidence of failure on any criterion. Data sufficiency for SMD and journal article status cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but are not grounds for exclusion here. Note: computer subject in school may be general computing/ICT; check at full text whether content is computer science/programming.

quote: Academic Writing course at Cherkasy State Business College for undergraduate students
rationale: The study concerns academic writing in a foreign language course (language learning), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. Also, the abstract describes a practice-based generalization with no evident comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, which would fail other criteria. E2 is the first applicable code in order used here as the content failure is clear from the abstract.

quote: The design process included the structuring of objectives and content, the automated generation of educational resources through specific prompts, and iterative validation to guarantee pedagogical quality.
rationale: The abstract describes a course design process using ChatGPT to generate educational resources, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Generative AI is used in course design rather than clearly as a learner-facing tool. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3, which is the first applicable code in the protocol's ordering that is supported by the abstract. Design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, so this is excluded.

quote: presents preliminary qualitative observations from demonstrations with pre-service and in-service teachers
rationale: The abstract describes a design and demonstration study reporting only preliminary qualitative observations, with no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies on positive evidence; the study also appears not to be a comparative experiment (E3 would also apply), but the abstract gives no control group, so E5 is the clearest failing criterion from the abstract. Participants are pre-service and in-service teachers, which is a further population concern. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported.

quote: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming traditional learning landscapes. This Spotlight will empower you with steps educators can take to be prepared for teaching in an AI-powered world
rationale: This record is a magazine Spotlight (editorial/news collection of articles), not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also not a journal article, but E6 is the first applicable code given the content.

quote: we have asked ChatGPT to write us some statements focusing on nursing, by answering the ultimate question regarding the definition of the domain of nursing discipline.
rationale: This is a commentary/opinion piece, not an empirical study. The author prompts ChatGPT once and critically discusses the output; there is no control group, no learners, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is nursing (health), not STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is not learner-facing; here the ChatGPT use is by the author, not learners, which would also be E1. Applying the protocol order, E1 comes first: no learner interacts with the tool as part of a learning activity. Hence E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: To evaluate this tool via questionnaire that measures physics teachers' beliefs concerning the adoption of AI tools in the classroom
rationale: The participants are physics teachers (in-service), not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. The outcome is teachers' beliefs/perspectives (questionnaire), which is a perception measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome, so E5 would also apply; per the protocol's first-applicable ordering, E4 is reported first. The abstract gives positive evidence of a failing population criterion, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: Assessing the Credibility of ChatGPT on Temporomandibular Disorders
rationale: Temporomandibular disorders are a clinical dental/health topic, which falls under health professions education and not STEM content, so E2 applies first. The study also rates ChatGPT responses on Likert scales in a survey with no control group and no learning outcome measure, so E3 and E5 would also fail, but E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order. Abstract does not show a learner-facing interaction clearly, but exclusion rests on E2.

quote: The research employs a quantitative design and gathered data using a structured questionnaire from a sample of 250 university librarians within Islamabad.
rationale: This is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 250 university librarians about AI/ML adoption readiness. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool, there is no control group, the design is survey-based (not an experiment), the population is library professionals rather than students, and there is no learning outcome. Exclusion under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) is the first code that applies; the record would also fail E3, E4, E5 and E6.

quote: This study collected written statements from 11 students during the fall semester of an English presentation course in 2023.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of written student statements from 11 students, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design criteria. Domain is also an English presentation course, which is non-STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, as the design is qualitative); the abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison and outcome criteria fail. Exclusion code E6 is the closest fit for a qualitative design lacking any eligible comparison.

quote: A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest non-equivalent control group design was employed with 80 undergraduate EFL students
rationale: The study concerns EFL recount writing, which is language learning and non-STEM content. This is positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so exclude under E2. Other criteria appear met on the abstract (ChatGPT-assisted IBL vs conventional IBL control, quasi-experimental design, undergraduate students, writing test outcomes), but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: We propose a novel template- and rule-based approach and a corresponding software system for assembling synthetic source code segments of defined time complexity.
rationale: The generative component is a template- and rule-based system used by teachers to generate exam questions; learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. ChatGPT is only used for evaluation of the generated code, not as a learner-facing intervention. No learner-outcome comparison is described. Excluded under E1 (not learner-facing generative AI).

quote: Drawing on a comparative analysis of regulatory frameworks and academic integrity codes at leading universities
rationale: The record is a policy/regulatory comparative analysis of university documents plus a sociological observation about student AI use. It is not an empirical experiment or quasi-experiment with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome or SMD-computable data. It fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the stated order of codes that fits, since the study is a regulatory analysis rather than an empirical learning study. No STEM learning content is evident. Note that the abstract-stage rule is to exclude only on positive evidence; here the abstract itself describes a document-based policy analysis, which is positive evidence of non-eligibility.

quote: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,690 undergraduate students at Somali National University.
rationale: The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey with no control or comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Outcomes are knowledge, attitudes, perceptions, and self-reported use, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order after E1 and E2, which cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone, so E3 is applied as the primary reason. The abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no control group, which is sufficient for exclusion at this stage.

quote: The research was based on eight parts: usability, ease of use, clarity, alignment with goals, interest, feedback, transfer to classes and total satisfaction by type of LO
rationale: The abstract describes action research evaluating usability, ease of use, clarity, interest, and satisfaction. These are perception/satisfaction measures, not quantitative learning outcomes, and there is no described control group without generative AI. Action research with a single course cohort suggests no comparison design. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison and outcome criteria, so exclude. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group), which is the most direct failed criterion in the protocol order; E5 would also apply.

quote: This study investigates lecturers’ views on the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in Nigerian higher education
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of 64 lecturers' perceptions, with no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol, the first applicable code is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the record fits E1 least clearly; the strongest and earliest failure is that the design is a non-experimental survey, which is coded E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense). Coding is judged on the first applicable code in order, so E1 would be the strict protocol answer, and the audit should confirm this choice.

quote: This quantitative study with a survey research design aims to access science teachers' readiness to use ChatGPT in science instruction
rationale: Survey design of in-service science teachers' readiness/perceptions (TAM perceived usefulness and ease of use) with no learner outcome and no control group. Participants are teachers, not students. Exclusion coded E5 as the first clearly applicable code on the protocol's outcome criterion; population (teachers, E4) and design (survey, E6-type) problems also apply, but the protocol's code order gives E1 first, which is unclear here, so E5 is reported as the primary positive evidence failure. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with perception-only measures.

quote: The training activity was held in January 2026 with 14 teachers participating, with the results of the activity evaluation carried out using pre-test and post-test methods
rationale: Community service training for in-service teachers (PKBM Maleo) on using ChatGPT for lesson preparation. The evaluation is a single-group pre-post design with no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Population is also in-service teachers rather than students, and content is general lesson preparation rather than STEM; these are noted but E3 is the first applicable code in order from E1 onward is E1 only if learner-facing... Teachers are the ones interacting with ChatGPT for preparation, which is teacher-facing use, so E1 would also apply. Per protocol order, E1 is checked first: the intervention is used by teachers to prepare materials, not as a learner-facing activity, so the first applicable code is E1.

quote: Steinbeck Studies is fortunate in that there is such a wealth of archival materials and primary works to explore.
rationale: This is an editor's column (editorial) for the Steinbeck Review, a literary studies venue. It describes no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The content is not STEM (English literature). It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies; it would also fail the publication-type rule as an editorial. Generative AI is discussed only in general terms and not as a learner-facing intervention in a study.

At abstract stage, the study evaluates student programming submissions by comparing instructor scores with LLM-generated scores (GPT, Claude, Gemini). LLMs are used as graders/assessors, not as a learning tool that learners interact with, which points to E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). There is also no control group without generative AI; the design is an agreement/validation comparison of assessment methods, with the same submissions re-evaluated under two scoring frameworks. The abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion (no non-generative-AI comparison group), so exclusion is warranted. Under the protocol's first-applicable ordering, E1 comes before E3; the strongest evidence here is that the AI is used for assessment rather than as a learner-facing intervention, so E1 is the first code that applies. Coding it as E1 to follow the order rule.

quote: The method employed was Project-Based Learning through prompt engineering workshops for research draft preparation.
rationale: This is a community service (PKM) activity reporting percentage increases in student abilities, with no described control group or comparison condition. The design does not show a comparison group, so E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Under the protocol, E3 is the first applicable code in order when reviewing the design, but the abstract does not show a comparison group, which is positive evidence of failure. The reported percentage increases come from a single-program description, not an experimental comparison. Excluding at abstract stage under E3 on the basis of no comparison group. Domain is partly STEM-adjacent (research skills, literature review), not clearly STEM content.

quote: This study aims to analyze texts created by ChatGPT to understand its strengths and limitations.
rationale: The abstract describes a thematic analysis of ChatGPT-generated essays, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group. Content is essay writing/language, not STEM. There is no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on the first applicable code in order, E1 is arguably also applicable, but the clearest first-failing criterion is E2 for non-STEM content; E2 is reported as the first code that applies to a non-STEM domain. No language-learning or STEM learner outcome is evident.

quote: an online survey was conducted targeting faculty members at K National University in Korea
rationale: The study is a faculty survey with descriptive statistics on AI tool usage and competence. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, learners are not the participants, and no learning outcome is measured. Excluded as not an empirical study of learner outcomes (E6 applied as the first failing code in a survey design); the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a survey design with no learner-facing intervention or learning outcome.

quote: This study investigated artificial intelligence and the future of interactive teaching and learning: exploring the experience of Nigeria University lecturers.
rationale: The study is a descriptive mixed-methods survey of lecturers' experiences and tool usage. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome (only usage percentages and perceived challenges). Participants are lecturers, not students. It is not an experimental study, so E6 (not an empirical comparative study) applies as the first failing criterion in a clear sense; the study's design is survey/descriptive. Non-STEM content is not established either. Excluded with the code most directly reflecting that it is a survey-type descriptive study.

quote: this review seeks to provide a comprehensive overview of those solutions designed specifically to generate and evaluate educational materials
rationale: The record is a literature review of LLM educational applications, not an empirical study. It has no primary experiment, no control group, and no effect-size data, so it fails the empirical design requirement. Exclusion code E6 applies (not an empirical study). Review articles are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: The article provides an in-depth examination of the risks associated with using AI technologies in learning environments. It analyzes existing technological and organizational approaches to minimizing these risks.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/review article on cybersecurity risks of AI assistants in digital learning. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measure. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion. Intervention, domain and population are also not clearly STEM or student-focused from the abstract, but E6 is decisive.

quote: Data were collected from 288 university students across multiple UAE higher education institutions.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional PLS-SEM survey study of 288 students. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The outcome is technostress, a perception measure, not a quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of the missing comparison and design.

quote: This essay critically examines how Large Language Models (LLMs) can be integrated into the investigative pedagogical process as strategic partners
rationale: The record is an essay proposing a methodology and discussing implications, not an empirical study. It describes a didactic experience only in passing, with no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is arts research (Bachelor of Acting), not STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the first applicable code in order would be E2 (not STEM) if the reviewer prefers that ordering, but E1 and E2 are not clearly failed on the abstract alone, so E6 is the most direct applicable code.

quote: Obstetrics and Gynecology
rationale: The record is a compilation of multiple unrelated clinical abstracts from a Journal of the American College of Surgeons issue (ovarian cyst resolution, brachytherapy complications, obesity and endometrial ablation, pediatric ovarian preservation, etc.). None describes a learner-facing generative AI intervention, and none is STEM education. Exclusion code E1 is applied as the first applicable code since no generative AI learning intervention is present; the record is not an eligible study.

The abstract describes a teaching reform paper proposing an OBE-BOPPPS dual-integration model in an AI context. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a conceptual or position piece, so it is not an empirical study. The course is innovation and entrepreneurship, which is not clearly STEM. Excluding at E6 on the abstract, which gives positive evidence that no empirical design is reported.

Abstract-stage record, but the positive evidence is clear enough to exclude. ChatGPT responses to patient questions about kidney transplantation are rated by clinicians. There are no learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity, and no control group, randomization, or quantitative learning outcome. Kidney transplant is a medical topic, not STEM. The text describes an expert evaluation of model outputs, so the first applicable code in order is E1: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Participants are clinicians rating outputs, and the patients are not study participants. Under the protocol's code order, E1 is the first that applies. The record is also not an empirical comparative study. Only E1 is reported, since the protocol asks for a single code.

quote: This paper traces the concept of Communities of Practice (CoPs) of graduate students' negotiation and co-construction of norms around generative AI-augmented scholarship
rationale: The study is a comparative qualitative multi-case study (interviews and participant observation) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group) is reported as the first applicable code in order; E5 and E6 also apply in substance, but E3 is the first in the required sequence that clearly fails.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: The State of Artificial Intelligence in Precision Oncology: An Interview with Eric Topol
rationale: The record is an editorial-style interview transcript with no empirical study, no control group, no learner population, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Under the protocol's order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly assessable here and the record would also fail E2/E3/E4/E5; E6 is the most fundamental failure and is reported as the first applicable code given the record's nature. Not a learner-facing generative AI study; the domain is oncology/medicine, not STEM education.

quote: This platform is a desktop application created using Electron, where students and Training & Placement Officers (TPO) can log in through separate panels.
rationale: The abstract describes a system build/project showcase for CSE students (an AI chat assistant for course recommendations, learning paths and mock tests). It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears to be a system description rather than an empirical study, so E6 applies. Per the rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, E6 is grounded in the absence of any empirical design or outcome described in the abstract, which is a clear signal of a non-empirical system paper. Not an empirical study.

quote: With the assistance of ChatGPT, most students successfully built a simple random forest model.
rationale: ChatGPT is a generative AI tool used by students in a learning activity, so intervention appears met. The abstract is a case study with no described control group, and it reports model performance rather than a learning measure. Under abstract-stage rules, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is unsure and should be checked at full text for a comparison group, design, and learning outcome. Domain (machine learning in biology education) seems STEM-adjacent but is not clearly confirmed.
rationale_detail: Abstract describes a "case study" and an "educational study" with no comparison group mentioned. Design likely fails (case study is excluded design), but the abstract does not give definitive positive evidence of a failed criterion, so it is passed to full text.

criteria.criteria_note: Participants are teachers (in-service), and the study is a community service training with single-group pre-post design.

quote: The training process was conducted through hands-on practice, demonstrations, and intensive mentoring
rationale: Single-group pre-post community service training (Service Learning) for in-service teachers creating anti-violence comics with ChatGPT assistance. The abstract reports only pre- and post-test scores with no control group, so the design fails comparison and design criteria. Participants are in-service teachers, not students, and the topic is violence prevention rather than STEM. Abstract gives positive evidence of failing several criteria; the code chosen is the first applicable in order would be E1 or E2 or E3 or E4, but the protocol's ordering starts with E1. Note: the intervention is teacher-facing ChatGPT use for material creation, which falls under E1 (AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials). Coded E1 on that basis.

Abstract describes a quantitative cross-sectional questionnaire study of 200 medical students who report AI usage. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies as the first failing criterion in order. Note: E1 ordering is not triggered since the abstract does not clearly show the AI is non-learner-facing; the outcomes are self-reported perceptions and scales rather than a learning measure (E5 would also apply), but E3 is the first applicable code given the design. Health-professions context of medical education also raises domain concerns. Decision is exclude on the basis of the design and comparison failure.

quote: "The results of the evaluation of the implementation of the service show high student enthusiasm regarding the use of artificial intelligence"
rationale: The abstract describes a community service introduction of AI to class X students with an evaluation of enthusiasm. It gives positive evidence of no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only enthusiasm/perceptions), so it fails the comparison/design requirement. Per the protocol's code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code. Quote is from the abstract and is 19 words; the exact quote text is shown above. Generative nature of the AI is not specified in the abstract.

The abstract describes a quasi-experimental study with 230 senior high school students, using Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking and a composition scale (quantitative outcomes), and integrates Gen-AI into writing instruction. Domain is creative drama writing (language/literature), which appears to be non-STEM and would be excluded under E2. However, the abstract does not explicitly state the content is non-STEM in a verbatim way; it is about hikayat literary works and drama writing, which strongly indicates a non-STEM domain. The control group is not described, so comparison and design cannot be confirmed. Because the abstract does not give unambiguous positive evidence of a failed criterion and the full text may clarify the design, I am leaving this as unsure for full-text review, with E2 as the likely eventual exclusion.

quote: A quantitative study based on surveys of faculty and students; an exploratory analysis compared traditional pedagogical approaches with those mediated by GenAI, measuring performance, motivation, satisfaction, and engagement.
rationale: Abstract describes a higher-education study comparing traditional approaches with GenAI-mediated approaches, measuring performance among other outcomes, so a control group may exist. However, the design is described as survey-based, which may fail the design criterion (quasi-experiment with comparison group required), and it is unclear whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured versus only perceptions. Engineering is mentioned, but the STEM content of the sample is not clearly established. Missing details do not justify exclusion at abstract stage, so this goes to full text to check design, outcome, and domain.

quote: This book translates the best current research on adolescent writing instruction into teacher-friendly practices
rationale: The record is a Guilford Press book describing evidence-based teaching practices, not an empirical study. It has no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded as not an empirical study (E6). It also fails the publication-type criterion, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order's relevant sense since it is not a journal article; E10 would also apply, so the code choice is a judgment call.

quote: This article looks forward to the potential role and limitations of ChatGPT and similar models in medical education in the future from its application scenarios and limitations.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/perspective article about ChatGPT in medical education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, and the domain is medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion. Excluded under E6 as the first applicable code in order is E1 (not clearly violated at abstract) then E2 (medical education is health professions, arguably non-STEM); E6 is the clearest positive evidence of failure.

quote: A comparative analysis of current trends in the use of marketing in small business enterprises is carried out
rationale: The paper is a descriptive/theoretical review of marketing practices for small businesses (methods: comparative analysis, synthesis, systematization). It is not an empirical study, has no control group, no learners, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is marketing, not STEM. AI/ChatGPT is mentioned only as one of many business technologies, not as a learner-facing tool. Excluded on the first applicable code in order; E1 would also be arguable, but E6 is the most direct failure given the non-empirical design.

quote: This research adopts a posthumanist innovative methodology where data is produced through the intra-action between the researcher (human) and ChatGPT (non-human).
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/posthumanist methodology in which the researcher interacts with ChatGPT and generates illustrative examples. There is no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Under abstract-stage rules, exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that design and outcome criteria fail; E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for a non-empirical paper. Injection not suspected.
decision_note: Coded E6 as the first applicable code; E3 and E5 also would apply.

quote: I used Google Gemini as a “Superuser” approach (Bell, 2026) to answer my seven expert questions of increasing complexity.
rationale: The record is a single-author essay/reflective synthesis in which the author queried Gemini themselves. It has no learners, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no data for an SMD. It is not an empirical study (E6). Per the code order, E1 (learner-facing intervention) is arguably also not met since the author is the sole user, but E6 is the fundamental failure. No abstract-stage doubt remains that would justify advancing it.

quote: Analysis pitted three AI tools (i.e., Generative AI Chatbots, AI Writing Assistants, and AI Language Learning Applications) against conventional teaching methods to measure gains in learning motivation.
rationale: The context is English-medium instruction and English as a Foreign Language learning, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so the domain criterion fails (E2). The record is also a network meta-analysis, not a primary study with its own controlled experiment, though the E2 code applies first in order. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content, so exclude.

quote: Using a qualitative case-study approach, data were obtained through semi-structured interviews and observations of 12 students from various semesters.
rationale: The study is an English-as-foreign-language learning study (EFL, translanguaging) rather than STEM content, so E2 applies. It is also a qualitative case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (E3/E5 would also fail), but the first applicable code in order is E2. Exclusion is positive at abstract stage because the domain is clearly non-STEM.

criteria.outcome_note: correct answer rate and SUS reported; no control group described in abstract

quote: The results showed an average correct answer rate of 95.2% and a mean SUS score of 78, which demonstrates strong initial student performance and system acceptance.
rationale: SQL is STEM (computer science/programming) and participants are undergraduates. The generative AI is used to generate SDP exercise instances for teachers (teacher-side authoring), but students do solve exercises; learner-facing generative AI interaction is not clear from the abstract. The abstract reports a single group of 32 students with no control group mentioned, and outcomes are a correct-answer rate and SUS (usability/perception). No positive evidence of a failed criterion is clear enough to exclude at abstract stage, so I return unsure for full-text checking of the comparison, design, and whether the AI is learner-facing (E1 possible) and whether a quantitative learning outcome with a comparison exists (E3/E5 possible).

Abstract describes EFL academic writing with ChatGPT, a non-STEM content area (language learning), which fails the Domain criterion. The study is also a perception survey with questionnaires and interviews, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome described, so it would likely fail E3 and E5 as well. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention) only if not learner-facing; ChatGPT use is learner-facing, so the first failing code in sequence is E2 (non-STEM content).

quote: The results of the formative study experiment, presented in the article, demonstrate a statistically significant increase in the proportion of pedagogically appropriate solutions, generated by the AI, based on student requests during the assessment phase.
rationale: Student teachers (higher education) learn prompt engineering with generative AI, which fits the intervention and population. The abstract does not state whether a control group exists; a formative experiment with a pre/post assessment could be single-group (E3). Domain is teacher media competence / pedagogical problems, not clearly STEM. Abstract does not give enough to exclude; needs full text to check control group, STEM content, and data for SMD.

quote: This article explores the potential impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools on Instructional Design (ID) workflows and organizations from a systems thinking perspective
rationale: The article is a conceptual/analytical discussion of how ChatGPT, Midjourney, and Descript could support instructional design workflows. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Its content is also instructional design practice rather than learners in STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's exclusion sequence at this stage, so it is the code reported. The abstract stage rule would normally allow inclusion when unclear, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion is justified.
decision_note: Excluded on E6; first applicable code.

quote: Home ICT access was strongly associated with mathematics (about 14 score points per index unit, roughly 17 per standard deviation)
rationale: Secondary analysis of PISA 2022 microdata on home ICT resources as a correlate of mathematics scores. No learner interaction with a generative AI tool is described, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). The design is observational/correlational with no control group lacking generative AI (would also fail E3). Because E1 is the first applicable code in order, it is reported.

criteria.criteria_note: English teachers, language teaching, survey-based mixed methods

quote: Data was collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire. Furthermore semi structured interviews were conducted with six teachers.
rationale: The study surveys 15 English teachers about readiness and attitudes using a questionnaire and interviews. It has no learner outcome, no control group, and no quantitative learning measure. Population (in-service teachers) and domain (English language teaching, not STEM) also fail. Non-empirical-experiment design, so E6 is the most fitting code. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The study involved developing a prompt for the AI judge based on the author's model of communication with AI and testing the Gemini 3.0 neural network as a judge in three debate sessions
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative assessment of an AI judge (Gemini 3.0) across three debate sessions, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Design is a case study with qualitative evaluation, not a comparison experiment. Debate-judging by AI is an assessment use rather than learner-facing learning activity, and the abstract reports no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded at E3 as the first applicable code in order, since no comparison group is described; the abstract gives positive evidence of no control group.

quote: our study investigates the GPT-4o-mini model as a cost-effective and efficient solution for PII detection tasks
rationale: The study evaluates GPT-4o-mini as a PII detection tool for anonymizing educational data. It is not a learner-facing generative AI intervention; learners do not interact with the tool as part of a learning activity. The abstract gives no control group or learning outcome. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing. Performance metrics (recall, precision) are classifier evaluation metrics, not learning outcomes.

quote: We ran a dual-anonymous "quality assurance" marking exercise across four end-of-module assessments across a distance university computer science (CS) curriculum.
rationale: The study is a marking exercise in which markers grade ChatGPT-generated scripts alongside student scripts. There is no learner interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and no control group receiving a learning intervention with a quantitative learning outcome. The design is a grading/quality-assurance evaluation of AI-generated answers rather than an empirical learning experiment, so it is not an eligible empirical study. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since ChatGPT scripts were produced for marking, not used by learners. Exclusion code E1 is the first that applies. Note: I report E6 here in the decision field but the first applicable code per protocol order is E1.

quote: The purpose of this teaching and learning resource is to provide a process for developing academic and meta-cognitive skills in students
rationale: The record is a teaching and learning resource describing a process for instructors, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Kinesiology is also not clearly STEM, but the first applicable code in order is E6 at the abstract stage.

quote: This study is a qualitative descriptive study that aims to describe and analyze the creativity of prospective mathematics teacher students
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive case study of eight students with reflective journals, interviews, and product analysis. There is no control group and no experimental comparison. Design is non-empirical in the sense of the protocol's qualitative exclusion, so E6 applies as the first failing code given no comparison group (E3) would also fail; E6 is reported as the most direct reason for qualitative designs.

quote: "this study explored the use of generative artificial intelligence, such as ChatGPT... among undergraduate nursing students"
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-style descriptive study of nursing students' self-reported AI use and perceptions (89% reported use, 84% said it improved coursework). It has no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is survey/descriptive and therefore not an empirical experimental study eligible under the protocol. Nursing is also outside STEM as defined by the protocol (health professions education is excluded), which is a further failure, but the first applicable code in order is E6 at this point. Exclusion made at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-experimental, perception-based design.

Abstract stage. The record has only a title and venue (Technovation, 2026) with no abstract. The title suggests an educational chatbot and a design science approach, which hints at a design study rather than a controlled experiment, but nothing in the record gives positive evidence that a criterion fails. Per rule 2, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so the record is kept as unsure for full-text review of intervention type, STEM domain, control group, design, and outcome.

quote: We undertook a global search for existing longitudinal datasets to provide a springboard for innovative mental health research
rationale:
This is a scoping/landscape review of longitudinal mental health datasets worldwide. It involves no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an eligible empirical intervention study. E1 is the first applicable code in order (no learner-facing generative AI), so it is reported here, though E6 (not an empirical study) would also fit.</rationale>

quote: This was a systematic review study with a qualitative analysis of 10 of the most recent studies between 2024 and 2025
rationale: The record is a systematic review with qualitative content analysis of ethical recommendations, not an empirical primary study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so E6 is the applicable code. Note that the protocol's abstract-stage rule would normally favour advancing ambiguous records; here the review design is positive evidence of non-empirical status, so exclusion is justified.

quote: We propose treating these connections as a unifying theme in university-level physics education, grounded in four fundamental conservation principles
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic review of textbooks, literature, and LLM outputs, a proposed instructional sequence, and theoretical derivations. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study with a control group. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study). Generative AI appears only as an information source for the review, not as a learner-facing intervention, so E1 would also be arguable, but E6 is the primary reason.

quote: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 461 medical students from various public and private universities in Iraq.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive cross-sectional survey of awareness, attitudes and readiness. It has no comparison group, no intervention test, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. Survey design and perception-only outcomes are excluded. Code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., non-experimental survey) is the first applicable code in the order; the domain is medical education, which is health professions education and so would also fail E2 on domain, but the protocol's order places E6 as the design-based failure here. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because positive evidence shows the design and outcome fail.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 100 academic and non-academic staff members from four institutions
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions among academic and non-academic staff, not learners. It has no control group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also not STEM content. Exclusion uses E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the clearest failing criterion, with design and population also failing. The protocol asks for the first applicable code in order; E1 would be the first in order if the intervention is considered not learner-facing, but the abstract does not clearly establish that, so E5 is reported as the decisive failure.

quote: A longitudinal survey study will assess changes in perceived competency in professional skills and psychological well-being
rationale: The record describes a planned longitudinal survey study of perceived competency and wellbeing for a course (LEAD). The title (policy analysis of involuntary substance use legislation) does not match the abstract content, which is about HQP professional-skills training. The design is a survey with perceived-competency outcomes, not a controlled experiment with a quantitative learning measure, and it is a protocol-like description rather than an empirical comparative study. Outcomes are perception-based and no control group is described. Exclude at E6 (not an empirical study) as the abstract describes a planned survey study without comparison; the STEM domain and generative AI component are also not clearly established. No injection detected.

quote: A quantitative research design was adopted, using a cross-sectional survey method.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with correlation and multiple regression analysis. There is no separate control group receiving or not receiving generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Survey designs are excluded by the protocol. The AI intervention is also not clearly generative or learner-facing, and the outcome is self-reported perception of AI adoption rather than a clear measured learning outcome. Under the rule to exclude only on positive evidence, the design and comparison failures are clear enough to exclude. E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a control group; the design failure would also support E6 if the study is judged non-experimental.

Abstract describes a corpus-based comparison of AI-generated and human-written essays for hedging and engagement markers. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group of learners, no learning outcome measured, and no STEM content; this is a corpus linguistics analysis rather than an empirical learning study. Per the first-applicable code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first criterion that clearly fails, so the code should arguably be E1 rather than E6. Correcting to the first applicable code.

criteria.quote: Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design, the researchers collected data via convenience sampling among 300 full-time allied health students
criteria.rationale: Cross-sectional survey design with correlation and regression on self-reported AI use and psychological constructs; no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no learning outcome measured. Not an empirical experiment meeting the design criterion. Under the protocol exclusion ordering, E6 (not an empirical study) is not the strict fit, but the design is a survey (non-eligible design) and no quantitative learning outcome exists; the most applicable code given the order is E5 would apply only if the design were eligible. Coded E6 as the closest fit for a non-eligible survey design; auditor should verify code choice.

quote: Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design, the researchers collected data via convenience sampling among 300 full-time allied health students
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey study correlating AI use with academic integrity, online learning integrity, and nomophobia. There is no intervention in which learners use a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no learning outcome. Exclusion is justified on design and outcome. The code E6 (not an empirical study) is a best fit for a non-experimental survey; the protocol has no dedicated code for a non-eligible survey design, so the auditor should verify this code.

criteria.stage_note: qualitative descriptive design; no comparison group

quote: Employing a qualitative descriptive research design, data were collected from experienced faculty members through open-ended narrative responses.
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive analysis of faculty members' ChatGPT use for developing materials. Teachers are not learners, there is no control group, and there is no quantitative learning outcome. Although E1 (intervention is not learner-facing) and E3 (no control group) also apply, the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 given that AI is used only by teachers to prepare materials. Reporting the first applicable code in order: the intervention is teacher-facing, so E1 applies and is the code to report.

quote: From the interview study, common themes emerged, including implementation, academic integrity, the human aspect of linguistics, and the future of AI writing tools.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative interview study of faculty opinions about AI tools in literature, language, and linguistics programs. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, has no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is non-STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense; qualitative design), which is the first applicable code in the order given that is clearly supported by the abstract. Positive evidence of failure on the design and outcome criteria is present.

quote: A document analysis of 1200 AI-generated responses was conducted to evaluate scientific validity, explanatory clarity, and pedagogical relevance.
rationale: The study is a document analysis of ChatGPT-generated responses, with no learners interacting with the tool and no control group. There is no comparison group and no learner outcome. Exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code. E1 could also be argued since learners do not interact with the tool, but E3 is the first code that clearly fails on the abstract's evidence.
rationale_note: Abstract stage: exclusion is based on positive evidence that no comparison group exists.

quote: Lastly, we examined students' eye-tracking patterns, acceptance, and learning processes when using this ConvAI system to learn Algebra through a random experiment (n participant = 151).
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based conversational AI (generative) used by learners in a randomized experiment with a control group, Algebra content (STEM). However, the abstract reports eye-tracking, acceptance, and interaction patterns; it is unclear whether a learning achievement outcome with SMD-computable statistics is reported, and the participant population (K-12 vs higher ed) is not stated. Not enough positive evidence of failure to exclude; advance to full text to check the outcome and population.

quote: Editor's Introduction: The CEA Conference in San Antonio: A Pivot Point
rationale: The record is a journal editor's introduction to a special issue on the CEA conference in English studies. It is not an empirical study, involves no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. The mention of ChatGPT is only contextual commentary on the humanities. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order after E1-E5 are checked; E1 and E2 also clearly apply in substance, but E6 is the most fundamental failure. Note that under the stated order E1 would be first to report if it applies; the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI and content is humanities, so E2 is also met. Per the order, E1 is reported first as the intervention is absent.

quote: Using a descriptive qualitative approach, functional syntactic analysis, and critical discourse analysis, this study examines a corpus of student papers with an AI probability of >50%.
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative linguistic analysis of Indonesian-language student papers in a language education program. Content is language/writing, not STEM. It also has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no learner-facing AI intervention in a learning activity. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.

quote: This research utilizes qualitative and comparative analysis, with higher education institutions as the main setting for investigations.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative and comparative analysis of international research and practical cases, not an empirical experiment with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order. Note that E6 is ordered after E1-E5; the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical, qualitative review design, and no quantitative outcome or control group is reported.

criteria.rationale_note: ChatGPT was tested directly on MCQs; no learners interacted with it and there is no control group.

quote: The MCQs were manually entered one by one, and a fresh ChatGPT session was started for each entry to avoid memory retention bias.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to 100 medical MCQs; ChatGPT itself is the examinee, not a learner interacting with it as part of a learning activity, and there is no comparison group. Health/medical content also falls outside the STEM domain. Under the ordered codes, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first, since no learner interacts with the tool. Population and domain are also not met, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Proposed is educational research-driven development (ERDD), an emergent conceptual cross-disciplinary framework
rationale: The record is a conceptual framework paper proposing ERDD with an applied workflow demonstration. It reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Note that E6 is ordered before E3 and E5 only in the sense of the first applicable code; the absence of a control group and outcome data also supports exclusion.
rule_note: Abstract stage exclusion based on positive evidence of a conceptual, non-empirical design.

quote: Using Microsoft Copilot to conduct an AI image generation competition involving 206 participants from various demographic groups, we investigated creative engagement patterns and educational potential.
rationale: Learners use a generative AI image tool (Microsoft Copilot), but the abstract describes a competition with participants grouped by demographics, with no control group without generative AI. It appears to be a descriptive comparison of creative patterns, not a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group. No quantitative learning outcome is reported (creative tendencies and lexical item frequencies are descriptive). Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code in order; E5 would also plausibly apply.

The record describes an AI course project (occupancy detection with YOLO computer vision) built as a final project of an online AI programme. The abstract does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of the learning activity; YOLO object detection is not generative, and the ChatGPT module is only listed as a course topic. It also reports no control group or quantitative learning outcome (only "field testing" of application performance). Exclusion at E1 on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, with the design also lacking a described comparison group.

quote: The proportion of correct responses was significantly lower than incorrect ones in BMAT section 2 (P<.001) and TMUA paper 1 (P<.001) and paper 2 (P<.001).
rationale: This study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to admission test questions directly, with no learners interacting with the tool and no control group of learners. It is not a learner-facing intervention study with a comparison group, so it fails the design and population criteria. Under the rule that E6 is for non-empirical work, this is a sort of benchmarking evaluation rather than an empirical learning study. Exclusion is based on the first clearly failing criterion; the intervention criterion is arguably also unmet (E1), but the abstract gives no evidence of learner interaction. Coding this as E6 is a judgement call that the auditor should check; the evaluation is empirical but not a learning study with a comparison group.

quote: Descriptive qualitative research using a questionnaire is used as a research methodology.
rationale: The study is English language learning (ESP), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies first. It is also a descriptive qualitative/questionnaire design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (perception-based Likert items), so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. E2 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This article is an invitation to discuss a recurrent question in the field of Humanities
rationale: The record is a position/discussion essay from the humanities perspective, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learning outcome data, and the domain is humanities rather than STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced. Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical discussion paper.

quote: This paper presents a comprehensive case study results on the implementation of AI tools for education in the development of a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of students using AI development tools with no control group, so the comparison criterion fails. The design is a case study rather than a comparative experiment, and no learning outcome is quantified (only time savings are reported). Exclusion is on E3 because the absence of any non-generative-AI comparison group is positive evidence of failure. Quote is from the abstract.

quote: This article will present the possible uses of ChatGPT in a foreign language lesson, as well as assess the role and importance of the human teacher in light of the development of this technology.
rationale: Foreign language learning is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a conceptual/discussion article with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well; E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Note: E2 is ordered after E1, and the intervention (ChatGPT for learners) is arguably met, so E2 is the first exclusion that clearly applies.

quote: The current research on analyzing reflective writing hinges on sentence-level classification.
rationale: The study classifies reflective writing documents using shallow ML and pre-trained language models (BERT, RoBERTa, BigBird, Longformer). Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the models are used as text classifiers for researchers/feedback, not learner-facing generative AI. No control group or learning outcome is described. Exclude under E1 as the first applicable code. Note that the abstract does not report a learner-facing intervention at all.

quote: This literature review aims to identify trends, impacts, and challenges of AI implementation in science learning.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 30 articles, not an empirical study with its own control group and effect data. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Review articles are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but E6 is the applicable code here since the protocol lists reviews under both; the primary reason is that it is not an empirical study.

quote: The article aims to identify attitudes toward AI (technophobia/technophilia) based on cognitive flexibility of university students majoring in different fields.
rationale: The study is a correlational examination of attitudes (technophobia/technophilia) and cognitive flexibility across majors, with no intervention group versus a non-generative-AI control and no quantitative learning outcome. Abstract gives positive evidence that the design is correlational and the outcomes are attitudinal/psychological rather than learning measures, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion coded E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first applicable code in order; E3 could also be argued given no control group, but E5 is the outcome-related failure stated most directly. Not an experimental comparison.

quote: Employing an explanatory quantitative design, the study involved 186 cadets from a maritime vocational higher education institution in Semarang, Indonesia.

The study is also about ESP materials, which is not clearly STEM. Excluded on E6 (not an empirical experimental study meeting design requirements); the first applicable code under the order is arguably E2 or E3, but the strongest positive evidence is the non-experimental survey design, which fits E6 as the main failure.

quote: The findings from this research will inform the development of a 2D/AR tool designed to make learning mathematics more engaging and effective for individuals with ID
rationale: The abstract describes semi-structured interviews, surveys, and co-design probes with teachers and students, with no controlled comparison or learning outcome measured. The tool is still being designed and the abstract reports no generative AI intervention, only a passing mention of generative AI as future work. This is a non-empirical-test qualitative/requirements study, so E6 applies. Note the abstract's criteria failure is positive evidence (no comparison group, no quantitative outcome), so exclusion is supported.

quote: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the level of undergraduate medical students' readiness for AI
rationale: Cross-sectional survey design with a single group and no control group; the study measures readiness via the MAIRS-MS questionnaire, not a learning outcome after an intervention. Population is medical students (health professions, which the protocol excludes from the domain). Exclusion by E3 as the first applicable code in order.

Under the protocol's exclusion codes, E6 (not an empirical study) is the first that applies in order of the criteria that can be assessed from the abstract. Because the record is a review, it would also fall under the publication-type concerns, but the review type is captured by E6 as the primary reason.

quote: The results confirmed the high engagement level for various reasons, some of which included the instructors' help, ease of use, and interactive nature.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with observation and an end-of-intervention survey, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; engagement and perceptions are not learning measures.
