rationale: The course is on translating specialized texts into English, which is language learning/translation studies, not STEM. Per the protocol, language learning and other non-STEM content is excluded (E2). Design, comparison, and outcome are not clearly established in the abstract (it mentions survey data and satisfaction), but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion. No injection detected.

quote: Surveys conducted with over 300 students over this time reveal the growing use of GenAI in their educational practices.
rationale: The study is a longitudinal survey of usage and ethical perceptions across four semesters, with no control group lacking generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome (usage rates and perceptions only). Exclusion code E3 is the first code that applies on positive evidence: there is no comparison group, and the design is survey-based (which would also fall under E5/E6 on closer reading). Exclusion is justified on the abstract alone because the design and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence. Note that the first-applicable-code order would place E1 or E2 first only if the abstract gave positive evidence of those failures, which it does not; E3 is the earliest clearly supported code.

quote: Original statements identified as using FML were entered into the Google Chrome "Help me write" tool, a writing aid using Generative AI.
rationale: The study is a qualitative analysis of AI-rewritten faculty feedback statements. The population is surgical clerkship students and residents rated by reviewers, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1 concerns the intervention, but the AI is used by faculty). Population is also not clearly K-12 or higher education learners; residents are postgraduate trainees, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (reviewer classification agreement only). No control group without generative AI exists. Per protocol order, E1 would apply first because AI is used only by faculty to prepare feedback, which is the first applicable code.

quote: The results show a high recognition of AI in both groups, with a significant increase in the adoption of advanced tools
rationale: The study is a comparative survey of AI knowledge and use across two student cohorts (Dec 2024 vs Dec 2025), measured by structured questionnaires. Outcomes are self-reported knowledge, adoption and perceived improvements rather than a quantitative learning measure, and there is no control group without generative AI; the design is survey-based, not an experiment. Under the abstract-stage rule the exclusion rests on positive evidence: the outcome is perception/usage-based. Primary code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies first in the code order before E3 and E6 considerations.

quote: In a recent Perspective, Cooper et al. (2024) highlight a set of benefits and challenges for the use of LLMs in ecology
rationale: This is a commentary/opinion piece (a response to a Perspective) in Methods in Ecology and Evolution, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded as E6 (not an empirical study). Domain is ecology research, not a STEM learning context in the protocol sense, but E6 applies first in the code order given the lack of any empirical design.

quote: Using a qualitative single-case design, the study draws on a semi-structured interview to explore how the participant interpreted her role in practice.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative single-case study based on a semi-structured interview, which is not an empirical quantitative study with a control group. It is not an eligible design (E6 not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of comparative/quantitative evaluation). The topic is English language teaching assistantship, which is non-STEM, and there is no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion on the first applicable code in order would be E1 or E2 or E3; the most fundamental failure is the qualitative design, so E6 is assigned as the primary reason. Note: the protocol's code order would place E2 (non-STEM content) before E6 if applied strictly; the non-STEM domain is clear from the abstract (English language teaching), so E2 is arguably the first applicable code.

quote: The rapid transition towards Society 5.0 exposes adolescents to significant cyber risks, necessitating comprehensive digital literacy education.
rationale: Content is digital literacy and social media ethics, not STEM. The abstract also describes a participatory action research community service with a single workshop group and no control group, and reports behavioral shifts rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order and is supported by the abstract's framing of digital literacy and cyber resilience.

The record has only a title, venue, and year, with no abstract. The title suggests a framework paper about prompt engineering for information literacy, which may be a conceptual paper rather than an empirical study, and it does not indicate a STEM domain, a control group, or a quantitative outcome. Positive evidence of failure is absent, so the record cannot be excluded at the abstract stage and should advance to full text for checking.

quote: Semi-structured interviews with eight instructors from various universities provided detailed insights into their decisions about adopting and discontinuing certain technologies.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of eight instructors about technology adoption. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It also samples teachers rather than students. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the clearest applicable code given the abstract; design and population also fail, but the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, and E1 (intervention not learner-facing) is not clearly established from the abstract alone.

quote: this presentation reflects on the current practices of animation artists, and the latest applications in the field of machine learning
rationale: The record is a conference presentation offering a philosophical and theoretical reflection on generative AI and animation artistic practice. It reports no empirical study, no control group, no learner population, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the non-empirical/design requirement (E6). It is also not STEM content and has no comparison group, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), which cannot be confirmed from the abstract; the clearest failure is that this is a non-empirical reflection, so E6 is applied. Publication type (presentation, Lirias repository) may also fall under E10, but the nature of the work is primarily non-empirical.

quote: As an initial phase of design-based research, this study employed a combination of literature review and implementation research.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual proposal of an instructional model, validated by expert content validity review and "implementation scenarios" rather than an empirical comparative study. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. This is not an empirical study with a comparison group, so E6 applies (E3 and E5 would also apply, but E6 is the first code in order that fits the design). Exclusion is supported on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: The Latest News Notre Dame Law School celebrates 35 years of Father Mike Show
rationale: Record is a law school newsletter ("NDLS Communicator") with news items and event listings, not an empirical study. It has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. E6 is the first applicable code in order (E1 would also apply, but E6 is the most fundamental failure; under strict order E1 is first, so this is noted for audit: the intervention is absent, which also fails E1).

quote: Zero-shot prompting with GenAI for EFL cloze text generation: a mixed-methods evaluation for language assessment in China
rationale: The title shows the content is EFL (English as a foreign language) cloze text generation for language assessment, which is language learning and non-STEM content. This is positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so exclude under E2. No abstract is available, but the title alone is sufficient for this exclusion.

quote: "applied the M/I (Muddiest/Interesting Point) feedback technique in a university liberal arts philosophy course"
rationale: The study is a classroom action research project in a university philosophy course, which is not STEM content. The M/I technique is a paper-based muddiest-point reflection with instructor feedback, and no generative AI tool is learner-facing in the described intervention. The design is single-group action research with survey-based perceptions and no control group. E2 is the first applicable code in order, since the content is not STEM. Abstract evidence is sufficient to exclude on domain.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on domain.

rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT-supported teacher feedback on EFL writing. EFL writing is language learning, not STEM content, so the domain criterion fails (E2). The first failing code in order is E1 check: ChatGPT here generates feedback that the teacher adapts, so it is not clearly learner-facing, but the content-domain failure is clear and is the reason given. Population (university EFL students) is not in question. No control group is described in the abstract, but the domain failure alone is sufficient.

quote: Analysis of four large-scale datasets—OULAD (n=32,593), MIT Open Learning, Stanford AI Index, and UCLA UCUES—using OLS regression (R²=0.542, p<0.001)
rationale: The abstract describes a secondary analysis of existing large-scale datasets (OULAD, MIT Open Learning, Stanford AI Index, UCLA UCUES) with OLS regression and a simulated 15% error rate, rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental study with a control group that does not use generative AI. It is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria, and no generative AI learner intervention with a control comparison is evident. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study of the eligible design). The abstract also does not indicate a STEM focus, and the OULAD dataset is not clearly a generative AI intervention. Design criterion is judged not met on the abstract's positive evidence.

quote: Through a survey of 140 respondents in Coimbatore, key findings indicate widespread adoption of AI tools
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 140 respondents with chi-square tests of associations. There is no control group and no experimental comparison, so the design is survey/correlational and fails the comparison and design criteria. Outcomes are self-perceived improvements rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code per order: E1 is unclear (ChatGPT use is generative, but learner-facing use is not clearly established), E2 is not applicable, and E3 is the first clear failure (no control group without generative AI). Positive evidence of no comparison group is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This qualitative study explored AI adoption, perceived benefits and risks, and needs for professional development among lecturers and administrators
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an experimental design, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Participants are lecturers and administrators, not learners. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible quantitative design); the primary failure is the non-experimental qualitative design.

quote: Generative AI can now solve the vast majority of physics problems a typical student will encounter until the end of a master’s course.
rationale: The record is a short opinion/commentary piece in Europhysics News with no empirical design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Physics is STEM, but the abstract gives positive evidence that the paper is non-empirical.

quote: "we surveyed 1,041 full-time undergraduate students through Savanta about their use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools"
rationale: The record is a policy note reporting a cross-sectional survey of students' use and perceptions of GenAI. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, and it reports no quantitative learning outcome, only usage and perceptions. It fails on design (survey), comparison (no control group), and outcome (perceptions/usage only). Per the exclusion order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design) is the first applicable code given the survey/policy-note nature.

quote: Having assessed 35 peer-reviewed articles published during 2023 through 2025 employing qualitative metasynthesis methodology and guided by grounded theory
rationale: The record is a qualitative metasynthesis of 35 articles, not an empirical primary study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is also about English language teaching (ELT), which is non-STEM content. Exclusion uses E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in protocol order, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone, but the domain failure (E2) is also clear; E6 is the first code that applies on the protocol's ordering of checks.

quote: This paper presents real-world cases identified by a team of authors
rationale: The abstract describes an interprofessional reflection paper presenting use cases and ethical discussion. It is not an empirical study: there is no control group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Domain is nursing, which is not STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for this record's evident design.

quote: A cross-sectional, correlational, quantitative study was conducted with a representative sample of 580 students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional correlational survey of students' knowledge, use, and perceptions of generative AI in writing. It has no intervention and no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The writing domain is also non-STEM, and the outcomes are perceptions and self-reported use rather than a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not the first applicable code since AI use by students is described; E3 is the first clear failure in order for a correlational design lacking a comparison group. Given the non-STEM domain (E2) is also present, the strict ordering would prioritize E2 only if E1 is not triggered; here E1 is not clearly triggered, so E2 would precede E3. Re-checking the order: E2 (content not STEM) applies before E3, so the first applicable code is E2.

criteria.quote: This study employed a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study design.
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative descriptive case study with observations, open-ended questionnaires, and interviews. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome (only observation scores and perceptions). Not an empirical comparison design; the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails, but the clearest failure is design/outcome. Under the code order, E1 is not positively shown (AI use by students is unclear from abstract), E2 does not apply (mathematics), E3 is the no-control failure, which is positively evidenced by the qualitative design. Coding E6 as the non-empirical-in-protocol-sense design failure is the closest match to a qualitative case study; flagged for auditor review since E3 may be the strictly first applicable code.

quote: The study employed a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study design.
rationale: Qualitative case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on design grounds. Code choice is debatable: strictly by the protocol's code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) would come before E5, and a qualitative case study may fit E6 (not an empirical study) only loosely. Flagging for auditor review on the code. Note the abstract reports an observation score percentage, which is not a learning outcome measure.
exclusion_code_note: E3 vs E6 for auditor review

criteria.rationale_note: AI outputs were graded by markers; no learner-facing comparison group evident

quote: Each AI tool was prompted with an essay question from undergraduate (UG) level 4 (year 1), level 5 (year 2), level 6 (year 3) and postgraduate (PG) level 7 biomedical sciences courses.
rationale: The study evaluates outputs of ChatGPT, Bing and Bard, which were prompted by researchers and graded by four independent markers. No learners interact with the AI tools and there is no control group without generative AI; the only comparison is among generative AI tools. This fails the comparison criterion (two generative AI variants only) and the design criterion (no comparison group of learners). Excluded at E3 as the first applicable code. Domain is biomedical sciences, which is not clearly within the protocol's STEM list, but the comparison failure is decisive.

Record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title suggests a language model used for student performance prediction, which points to predictive analytics (an exclusion in the protocol), but the title alone does not give positive evidence that a criterion fails. Per rule 2, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review. Year 2024 satisfies the date criterion; journal venue suggests a journal article.

quote: This research paper delves deeply into the multifaceted positive and negative educational affordances of the use of GenAI while also exploring future possibilities
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/discussion paper exploring UNESCO competency domains and future possibilities. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a non-empirical paper, so E6 applies. Positive evidence of failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This poster showcases a case study of an Australian higher education institution’s artificial intelligence (AI) literacy staff development program.
rationale: The record is a poster describing a case study of a staff AI literacy program. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome, and participants are staff rather than students. Poster format also falls under E10, but the primary reason is that it is not an empirical study (E6), which is the first applicable code in the stated order given the design. Note that E4 (staff, not students) would also apply; under the protocol's order, E1 and E2 are not clearly positive from the abstract. Excluding on E6 as the design is a non-empirical case-study showcase.
rationale_note: Cross-check: E4 also applies because participants are academic and professional staff.

quote: The International Conference on Academic Studies in Technology and Education (ICASTE) is set to take place at Amara Premier Palace Hotel in Antalya, Turkey, from November 16-19, 2023.
rationale: The record is a conference proceedings volume (ICASTE2023 proceedings), not a journal article. Protocol excludes conference proceedings under E10. It is also a collection of unrelated presentations with no single empirical study of a generative AI intervention with a control group, so it fails design and other criteria as well, but the publication-type exclusion applies first in the code order given the record's nature.

quote: The study results showed that the t value for measuring creative and critical abilities was 6.691 and 7.151. It was found that there was a significant difference between the test scores obtained before and after the treatment.
rationale: Abstract describes high school students using ChatGPT as a virtual tutor for mathematics, with quantitative test outcomes. However, the reported comparison is before vs after treatment within one sample of 20 students, which suggests a single-group pre-post design (E3). No control group is mentioned in the abstract. Abstract does not positively confirm a comparison group, so per the abstract-stage rule this is not excluded outright; it is sent to full text to verify whether a separate non-GenAI control group exists.

quote: The study outlines the development of a frictionless HTML5 web browser application, without prior coding expertise.
rationale: GenAI was used by the educator/designer to create a simulation via natural language prompting (human-AI collaboration for design of teaching resources). Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies. No control group or learning outcome is described; the study is a design/development report. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: SECURE-A2RC, a rubric-constrained, Arabic-aware large language model framework designed to deliver scalable, interpretable, and culturally relevant cybersecurity education.
rationale: The study concerns cybersecurity literacy and phishing detection with Arabic translation fidelity. Cybersecurity awareness and language/translation content is not among the protocol's STEM domains (science, math, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so it fails the domain criterion. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract. Exclude under E2 as the first applicable code is content not STEM; note that E1 ordering would require checking learner-facing use, which the abstract does not clearly establish, but the domain failure is clear.

Abstract describes a system architecture and design methodology with implementation experience in courses. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a system/design description, not an empirical study. Exclusion is on positive evidence: the abstract lacks any control group or outcome data. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable first failing code; E3 and E5 would also apply on the abstract's content. Population (advanced training courses for teachers/learners) and domain (prompt engineering, AI literacy, not clearly STEM) are also unclear.

quote: In this laboratory reflection, the goal is to provide some practical advice for one of the most critical aspects of the process
rationale: The record is a narrative laboratory reflection giving advice on writing fellowship personal statements. It is not an empirical study: there is no intervention, control group, or learning outcome. It also does not involve generative AI as a learner-facing intervention, and its subject is not STEM learning. E6 is the first code that applies in the protocol's order, since E1 (intervention) would be the first code checked. Strictly, E1 might be argued because no learner interacts with a generative AI tool in an activity; the paper only mentions LLMs in advice tables. Excluding under E6 as the primary failure because the paper is a non-empirical reflection/commentary.
rationale_note: Note for auditor: Under the strict order, E1 precedes E6. The paper does not describe a learner-facing generative AI intervention (LLMs appear only as advice to applicants), so E1 could also be argued. I chose E6 as the more fundamental failure, but the auditor may prefer E1 per the ordering rule.

quote: Participants were randomized into two groups: self-generated (SG) feedback and AI-assisted (AI) feedback.
rationale: Randomized study of generative AI-assisted peer feedback among third-year Doctor of Pharmacy students. The content is pharmacy professional/clinical education on peer feedback (communication, interpersonal skills), which is health professions education and not STEM content, so E2 applies. Per the protocol, health professions education is excluded from the Domain criterion. Other criteria appear plausibly met at abstract stage, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

Abstract describes a design-and-development study (ADDIE) with interviews, Likert questionnaires, and observations analysed descriptively. No control group or comparison condition is mentioned, and the study reports perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports exclusion at E3; the abstract does not report a quantitative learning outcome either (E5), but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

criteria.quote: The study employed a descriptive quantitative approach with purposive sampling. The data were collected through an online questionnaire
criteria.rationale: Study uses a single-sample descriptive questionnaire of perceptions of ChatGPT (means and SDs of perceived benefits and challenges). No control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which applies given perception-only measurement; the absence of a comparison group (E3) would also fail the criteria, but E5 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced by the abstract's description of perceptions.

quote: The data were collected through an online questionnaire, and the study sample comprised 166 preservice SETs.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive survey of perceptions with no control group and no learning outcome. Per the code order, E1 (intervention) is arguably met since ChatGPT use is learner-facing, E2 is not clearly violated (special education content, not STEM, which is actually a domain concern). Among codes applied in order, E2 (content not STEM) could be argued since special education standards are not STEM content, but the abstract is ambiguous on domain. I've selected E5 because the outcome is clearly perception-only. Abstract-stage exclusion is warranted on positive evidence of a perception-only design with no comparison group.

quote: This paper constructs a dynamic path model of "AI -ideological and political educationwriting" tripartite integration tailored to general education contexts.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework and model construction for AI-empowered ideological and political education in a scientific paper writing course. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This indicates a non-empirical (conceptual/design) paper, so E6 applies. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion needs positive evidence; here the abstract itself presents a conceptual model without any data collection, which is positive evidence that the study is not empirical. The writing-course domain is also not clearly STEM, but that is not needed as the basis for the code.

The abstract states the study "utilized a survey research methodology" with descriptive statistics only, and no control group. This is a survey design with no comparison group, and the outcomes are perceptions and attitudes rather than a quantitative learning measure. Excluded on E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in order; the survey design also fails the design criterion and the outcome is perception-only.

quote: The support will be provided through a three-session sleep management program. Each session will include an individual meeting between a PROMESS-Sleep expert and a medical student
rationale: The intervention is a human-delivered sleep management program with no indication of any generative AI tool. Learners do not interact with generative AI. Also not STEM content (sleep/fatigue health education), and it is a trial protocol rather than a results study. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, the first applicable code.

quote: Our findings reveal that students’ trust in AI, familiarity with algorithms, and lower anxiety about AI are key predictors of positive perceptions and adoption of LLMs in learning.
rationale: The study is a cross-national survey of 1906 university students on perceptions and adoption of LLMs. It reports perceptions and usage, not a quantitative learning outcome, and has no control group or comparison design. This is a survey design with no learning outcome, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. The exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's exclusion list that is clearly evidenced; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply). Following the rule that codes are reported in order from E1, E1 is not clearly met (intervention is use of LLMs, not explicitly described as learner-facing in a learning activity), so E5 is reported here at abstract stage with the caveat that the design is a survey.

quote: The article examines the possibilities of integrating visualization and media analysis into the IT training of future bachelor's students in secondary education.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical generalization and literature analysis ("methodological basis... analysis of scholarly sources, comparison, generalization"). No empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome are reported. This is not an empirical study (E6). Generative AI appears only as a topic among several practices, not as a tested intervention.

quote: Following each debate, participants completed a questionnaire assessing moderation effectiveness, hedonic motivation, satisfaction, perceived utility and usage intention
rationale: The abstract's outcomes are perception-based (moderation effectiveness as perceived, enjoyment, satisfaction, perceived utility, usage intention). No quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or skill performance is reported, and the protocol excludes perception-only outcomes. Domain is also unclear (general debate, not clearly STEM). Excluded at abstract stage on E5 because positive evidence shows no learning outcome.

quote: Exhibit - A Showcase of Scholarship, Creativity and Preservation Provided by Xavier University Library (Xavier University)
rationale: The venue is a library exhibit showcase, not a journal article, so it falls under publication type E10. The abstract also describes a qualitative discussion analysis of narrative cases with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, which points to E3/E5/E6 as well. E10 is reported first as the publication-type failure is the clearest. Only the venue indicates publication type; the other criteria are not assessed further at this stage.

quote: Drawing on 40 reflexive diaries produced by 186 students enrolled in a journalism course, the study employs thematic coding
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative thematic analysis of reflexive diaries from journalism students, with no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failing comparison, design, and outcome criteria is present, so exclusion is warranted. Under the code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code at this stage; the design and outcome failures would also apply (E5/E6). Journalism is also not clearly STEM. The record is a qualitative, non-experimental study.

quote: An exploratory qualitative interview-based design with supplementary background information was used.
rationale: The study is an exploratory qualitative interview-based design with thematic analysis, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) cannot be assessed from the abstract, and E3 (no comparison group) is also met, but the first applicable code in order is E5 only if E1-E4 are not clearly failing. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative outcome and no comparison, E5 is the clearest code applied here; the design failure (qualitative, no control) is also evident. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract. Note that E3 is arguably the first failing criterion in order (no control group) and a reviewer may prefer E3 at fulltext; the abstract does not describe any control group.

quote: The AI-generated annotations critique how the assessments align with the three dimensions of the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) and suggest ideas to elicit students' science sense-making.
rationale: The GenAI (MLLM) is used to annotate and critique science assessments, with teachers/researchers as users; learners do not interact with the tool. No learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measure. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (first applicable code in order).

quote: this article describes the design iterations, and presents a case study with five in-depth interviews with pre-service teachers on evidence-use
rationale: The abstract describes a design-based research study with a case study of five in-depth interviews. It reports no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is qualitative and not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible design) at abstract stage, since the evidence positively shows a qualitative case study design with no comparison group. The generative AI element appears only as a redesign proposal, not as a studied intervention.
rationale_note: Note: the strongest code is arguably E3 (no comparison group without generative AI) or E5 (no quantitative outcome); the protocol says report the first that applies in order, and E3 precedes E5 and E6 in the list, so E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: This study employed a qualitative research method using interviews, observations, and documentation techniques.
rationale: The study is qualitative (interviews, observations, documentation) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical design meeting the protocol's comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 is used because the study is qualitative, which falls under non-empirical-study-type exclusion for this protocol's design requirements; the abstract also gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no quantitative outcome. Note the abstract also mentions ChatGPT use within the internship, but the design failure is decisive.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen for qualitative design; protocol lists qualitative designs under Design exclusions.

quote: The study employed a comprehensive research methodology that included designing practical experiments and field tests to assess the accuracy of the commands formulated by computer science students
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Claude) used by computer science students at Faculty of Education, Zawilah, with computer science content (programming projects), which fits population, domain and intervention. However, the abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists; it mentions experiments and an intervention of prompt-formulation training, with no clear comparison group. Design and comparison cannot be confirmed, and no quantitative outcome statistics are described (quality assessment is implied but unmeasured). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so I return unsure for full-text review. Publication type and language (Arabic title, English abstract) also need checking at full text.

quote: The results showed a high mean score for the accuracy of the responses (M = 4.10, SD = 1.32)
rationale: The study is a feasibility evaluation of a customized GPT for graduate students' access to university regulations. It has no control group and no comparison condition, and its only measure is accuracy of GPT responses rated by a reviewer panel, not a learning outcome. The domain is administrative regulations, not STEM. Exclusion is at the abstract stage on the basis of the absence of a learning outcome (E5), which is the most direct failed criterion; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3) and the content is non-STEM (E2), so the record would fail further criteria even if E5 were disputed.
exclusion_note: First applicable code in protocol order: intervention is generative AI, so E1 does not apply; content is administrative regulations, so E2 (not STEM) applies before E5 in the protocol's order. Code E2 is the first that applies.

quote: "The research used primary data obtained from surveys."
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using PLS-SEM on perceptions (usefulness, ease of use, motivation, value, intention to use). It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it measures attitudes and intentions only. Survey design and perception-only outcomes fail the protocol. Under the exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract, so the first clear failure is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would apply as well), but the abstract-stage code is reported as E5 because the outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-powered training platform in oral medicine and pathology education
rationale: The intervention is a GPT-4-powered chatbot platform (learner-facing generative AI) with a traditional tutorial control group and pre/post knowledge scores, but the content is oral medicine and pathology, a health professions topic rather than STEM. Excluded under E2 (content not STEM). Although the abstract is sufficient to exclude, the domain failure is clear from the title and abstract.
rationale_note: Medical/dental education falls under health professions, which the protocol excludes from the Domain criterion.

quote: In a capstone cybersecurity course, the instructor encouraged students to use ChatGPT 3.5 on a self-directed learning assignment to select topics, find learning resources, and carry out their learning plans.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT (generative AI) used by learners in a higher-education cybersecurity course. Cybersecurity is plausibly STEM (computing), but the abstract does not clearly establish that it is a computing/STEM domain outcome. The abstract mentions students who did not use ChatGPT, which hints at a comparison, but it does not state a comparison group design or any quantitative learning outcome; it reports perceptions ("found it to be a helpful learning aid", plans to use). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is unsure and should be checked at full text for a control group, learning measures, and effect-size data.

quote: The results of the application of each activity were evaluated on the basis of group interviews where students and teachers analyzed the results achieved.
rationale: The abstract describes three teaching activities evaluated through group interviews, with no control group or comparison condition and no quantitative learning measure. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison group (E3), and the design appears to be descriptive rather than an experiment. Exclusion is based on the abstract's own description of evaluation method.

quote: The editors hope that this issue of the European Heart Journal will be of interest to its readers.
rationale: This record is a journal front-matter editorial/focus-issue summary covering several cardiovascular reviews and commentaries. It does not describe any generative AI intervention, learners, control group, or learning outcome. It fails the intervention (E1) criterion, but the record is not an empirical study at all, so the first applicable code in the stated sense is E6 (not an empirical study). No eligible study is described.

quote: Исследование рассматривает эффективность чат-ботов на базе ИИ в языковом обучении по сравнению с традиционными методами
rationale: The study concerns language learning (non-STEM content), which the protocol excludes under Domain. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-STEM domain, so E2 applies. Other elements (randomized design with control group, LLM chatbot, quantitative outcomes) appear to be met, but the domain failure alone is sufficient. Note that the record is in Russian with an English abstract; language was not used as a basis for exclusion.

quote: Quantitative analysis revealed that a “Planning–Verification” pattern where the AI outputs are actively cross-validated had significantly higher learning than passive reliance
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI (GAI) use by engineering students (Information Theory and Coding, a STEM domain) with a quantitative learning comparison. However, the abstract compares two AI-use patterns (Planning–Verification vs passive reliance), which may be two generative AI variants without a non-AI control group, a possible E3 failure. The abstract does not state whether a non-AI control group exists, so this cannot be resolved at abstract stage. Advancing to full text to check the comparison and design.

This is a community service (pengabdian masyarakat) training program. The abstract describes interactive training, hands-on practice and mentoring with no separate control group; improvement is reported only descriptively, with no comparison group or quantitative design. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports E3. Topic is research skills/academic writing, not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on the absent comparison group, which is positive evidence from the design description.

quote: this paper proposes a novel large-model-driven virtual simulation experiment paradigm tailored for power battery courses
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework ("we systematically review", "a comprehensive methodological framework is proposed", "we discuss") with no experimental design, control group, or learning outcome data. It reads as a position/framework paper rather than an empirical study, so it fails the empirical-study requirement. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical design; the abstract gives no evidence of a comparison group or outcome measure. Venue "Transactions on Comparative Education" is not a typical journal name, but that was not used as a basis for the decision.

quote: Tribute to Mary Katherine Tillman (1940–2022) Phillip R. Sloan
rationale: The record is a tribute/obituary for a Newman scholar, not an empirical study. It describes no generative AI intervention, no comparison group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are not applicable to this record.

quote: For many, the thought of copying numbers from a telephone book seems like an astonishingly mind-numbing and fruitless endeavor.
rationale: This is a magazine-style opinion/review piece in Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery about boredom and creativity, not an empirical study. It describes a telephone-book boredom study only as secondhand commentary, with no generative AI intervention, no STEM content, and no learner population. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) would also apply since no generative AI learning intervention is described; the earliest-applicable order places E1 first, so the code should be re-checked by the auditor. Ordering rule: E1 is checked before E6, so the strictly correct code is E1.

quote: We randomly assigned seventy-four medical students to two groups.
rationale: The study is set in an evidence-based medicine training program with clinical vignettes and MCQs for medical education. Clinical medicine is a health professions context, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain (health professions education is excluded). The abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content, so E2 applies. Other criteria are unclear from the abstract (the ChatGPT-generated cases are used by learners, but the control also receives human-written cases, and the outcome is evaluation ratings plus MCQ psychometrics). Excluding on the first applicable code, E2.

quote: The study is conducted on the expert assessment method basis.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/expert-assessment development of a matrix of AI tools for law training. No learner-facing intervention is tested, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Domain is law, which is non-STEM (E2 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails; the clearest failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Law content is also not STEM, but E6 is the primary reason at abstract stage.

quote: Scientific writing and publication are teamwork, where the joint efforts and collaboration of researchers, editors, reviewers, as well as publishers are required.
rationale: The record is a narrative commentary on ChatGPT in scholarly communication. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). The quote is a generic passage from the text, not evidence of a design.

quote: This study employs a qualitative research approach featuring unstructured interviews with BS and MS students, as well as university educators
rationale: The study is an ESL (English as a second language) study, which is non-STEM content and therefore fails the domain criterion (E2). It is also a qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail design, comparison, and outcome criteria as well. E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order, since the intervention check (E1) is arguably met by ChatGPT/Grammarly use and the domain check precedes the others.

quote: These reflections are intended as conceptual insights and practical proposals rather than a comprehensive literature review.
rationale: The paper is a personal reflection offering conceptual insights and proposals, not an empirical study. It states that formal assessment remains in abeyance, so there is no quantitative learning outcome or control group. Exclude under E6, which applies before the other codes.

quote: Using precision, recall, F1-score, false positive and false negative rates, and inter-rater agreement metrics such as Fleiss' Kappa and Krippendorff's Alpha, we systematically analyzed the performance of eleven state-of-the-art models
rationale: The generative models are used to grade student responses (automated grading), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. The protocol excludes AI used only for grading (E1). Also no control group without generative AI; the comparison is model vs human graders, not a learner-facing control. Excluded at E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: This longitudinal multiple-case qualitative study investigates how non-native pre-service English teachers
rationale: The study is a longitudinal multiple-case qualitative design with interviews and artifacts. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The domain is English language teaching, not STEM. Under the stage-ordering rule the first applicable code is E2 (content is not STEM), but the clearest and most fundamental failure is the qualitative design with no comparison group, so E3 is applied as the primary code. Note: strict ordering would list E2 first; the design failure is also decisive.

quote: Employing a qualitative approach, the study captures students' experiences and perspectives
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of students' perceptions of AI tools (ChatGPT, Grammarly). It has no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not a controlled experimental design. Positive evidence of a failed design and outcome criterion supports exclusion as not an empirical study in the protocol's sense (E6 is the closest code given the qualitative, perception-based design; E3 and E5 would also apply, but E6 is not the first-listed code that clearly fits, so this is a judgement call). Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract.

quote: This approach makes it possible to solve the following tasks: reducing the time and effort required for manual checking of programming tasks completed by students
rationale: GitHub Copilot is used by the instructor/researchers to generate tests for checking student programming tasks; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This is teacher-side/assessment use, so E1 applies. No control group, no learning outcome, and no empirical comparison is described in the abstract either; the abstract describes a methodological proposal.

quote: A qualitative research study was adopted, employing semi-structured interviews with ten students selected through purposive sampling.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of ten students about syllabus preferences. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the design criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first applicable code among those that fit; E3 and E5 would also apply, but the design is qualitative and the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a non-eligible design. Note: under strict code ordering E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is unclear because the study concerns perceptions of AI tools rather than an intervention, so the exclusion relies on the qualitative design.

quote: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is revolutionizing education, echoing historic shifts such as the emergence of the codex and the printing press.
rationale: The abstract is a narrative/position overview with no described empirical design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a non-empirical review or commentary, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). No STEM-specific content or control group is described either, but those are not needed to exclude at this code.

quote: The results show that the use of generative AI significantly strengthens key skills for effective requirements elicitation, overcoming the limitations of traditional methods.
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI interview simulation used by Master's students in a requirements elicitation course (software engineering, plausibly STEM). It reports a significant improvement versus traditional methods, which suggests a comparison group, but the abstract does not state the control design, the study design, or the statistics needed for an SMD. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text.

quote: In this study, we conducted a preliminary literature review to identify motivators and demotivators for using LLMs in software engineering education.
rationale: The record is a preliminary literature review that maps motivators and demotivators. It is not an empirical study with a comparison group or a quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the design and outcome requirements. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies.

quote: A cohort of 52 undergraduate students majoring in pharmacy and biochemistry participated in a semester-long intervention involving AI-generated narrative preclass readings
rationale: The abstract describes a single cohort of 52 students receiving the AI-generated stories intervention, with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. Comparison is framed as student self-perceptions versus "traditional instructional explanations" within the same cohort, and outcomes are largely self-reports and surveys. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3 at the abstract stage. Organic chemistry is STEM, and the population is undergraduate, so those criteria are met. Outcome quantitative status is unclear, but the exclusion rests on the comparison failure.

criteria.comparison_note: no control group described in abstract

quote: This report presents the developments of a didactic sequence carried out within the framework of an intervention research project linked to the Professional Master's Program in Arts (ProfArtes)
rationale: The study is an art education intervention (Debret reinterpretations via Triangular Approach), which is not STEM, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. The abstract also describes observation and interviews with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, but E2 is the first applicable code. Design is not an experiment with comparison; outcomes are qualitative and perception-based.

quote: A qualitative-interpretative approach was adopted, using an integrated case study design, in which each of the 22 written responses from trainee history teachers
rationale: The study is a qualitative-interpretative integrated case study of written responses. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. Generative AI use is mentioned only as an exploratory, uncontrolled, hypothesis-generating finding. Under E6 (not an empirical study), it is not an eligible design; the empirical nature is qualitative, so the closest fit is design-based exclusion. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), which applies before E5/E6. Given the protocol's order, E3 is the first failing code, so E3 is the correct code.

quote: Pre/post survey data revealed higher reported AI familiarity, comfort, and perceived usefulness in lesson planning.
rationale: The abstract describes only pre/post survey data on perceptions (familiarity, comfort, perceived usefulness) and qualitative responses, with no quantitative learning outcome. There is also no described control group, and the design appears to be a single-group pre-post survey. Excluded under E5 as the outcome is perception-only; the comparison criterion also appears unmet. Preservice teachers count as higher education, and the STEM domain (science lesson planning) is met.

quote: In this case study, we present practical tools around the experiment that let students get hand-on with science
rationale: The record is a conceptual/position piece with a case-study presentation of teaching tools (workshop/session description). It reports no comparison group, no controlled design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion at E6 (not an empirical study). It also does not describe a generative AI learner-facing intervention in an evaluated form; AI is discussed only as a general topic.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is a case study/position paper without a control group or outcome data.

quote: The experimental group learned the same content using GeoGebra within a smart classroom environment.
rationale: The abstract describes GeoGebra software, which is dynamic geometry software, not a generative AI tool. Nothing in the abstract indicates a large language model, generative model, or other generative AI component, so the intervention criterion appears not met (E1). Other criteria appear met: quasi-experimental control group, secondary students, mathematics (geometry), and a conceptual understanding outcome. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that the tool is not generative AI.

quote: The data were collected from library professionals in Saudi Arabia via Google Forms.
rationale: The study is a self-developed questionnaire survey of library professionals (not students), with no generative AI intervention, no control group, and only perception-type self-rated literacy scores. It fails several criteria. Under the stated code order, the first applicable code is E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention), but the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no learners, so E4 (population not K-12 or higher education students) is the clearest single code I can justify from the abstract. Note that E1 could also be argued; the abstract alone does not show any AI tool used in a learning activity, so this is a judgement call that the auditor should review.

quote: A piloted, cross-sectional survey was administered via email.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of usage and perceptions of LLM tools among faculty and students. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome (perceptions and usage only), and is a survey design rather than an experiment. Domain is dental education, which is health professions education and so falls outside STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study is inaccurate, but the design is a survey with no eligible comparison) is not the first applicable code by strict order; however, the first applicable code in order is E2 (dental/health professions education is not STEM content). Applying the protocol's code order, E1 is not clearly met since the intervention is not established as learner-facing use in a learning activity, so the first clear failure is E2.

quote: Evaluation results obtained through post-training questionnaires revealed that 66.7% of participants responded very positively to the training.
rationale: Community service training for science teachers (in-service, which is excluded from the population) to develop practicum modules with ChatGPT. Evaluation is by post-training questionnaire only, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention, but the teacher-only use of AI to prepare materials maps to E1 by the borderline rule. Coding E1 would be the first applicable code: AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: Empirical data indicate that the targeted use of AI significantly enhances student performance in academic writing and oral communication
rationale: Abstract-stage screen. Population is higher education (Computer Science students at non-linguistic universities), and the abstract reports performance gains in academic writing and oral communication. Domain is ambiguous: this is an English for Specific Purposes course for CS students, which may be non-STEM language learning under the protocol. Intervention includes Generative AI as one of several technologies, but the abstract does not establish a control group or design. No positive evidence of a failed criterion, so unsure; resolve at full text for comparison, design, and whether the domain counts as STEM.

quote: The system accepts scanned handwritten student PDFs, rasterises each page at 3× scale, produces three preprocessing variants per page
rationale: The system is an automated answer-sheet grading tool used for evaluation, not a learner-facing generative AI learning activity. Gemini is used for OCR text refinement and embeddings for scoring, not as a tool learners interact with. There is also no described control group or learning outcome comparison; the validation compares against teacher marks (agreement, not learning). Excluded at E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: The Colin Ferguson Oration is the address given to attendees at the annual Australia Accounting Hall of Fame dinner and presentation evening.
rationale: The record is an invited oration (commentary/essay) on AI and accounting, not an empirical study. It has no comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, no learning outcome, and is not STEM education content. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits; the record is clearly a non-empirical essay on the profession rather than an education study.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the abstract positively describes a non-empirical oration.

quote: This qualitative study, informed by grounded theory, involved six discussion groups with 16-year-old students from three schools
rationale: The study is a qualitative grounded-theory design using discussion groups, with no control group, no experimental intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study that meets the design criterion. Under the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established since generative AI is only mentioned as a preferred resource, and E3 would also apply, but the qualitative design fails the Design criterion; E6 is chosen as the primary reason since the study is qualitative and not an experimental empirical study. Note the ordering rule may point to E3 or E5 instead; the core failure is the qualitative design.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a qualitative design.

quote: This research aims to develop and evaluate an automated English paragraph scoring system using the Gemini API aligned with the Thai upper secondary curriculum's writing indicators
rationale: The study concerns automated scoring of English (EFL) paragraphs, which is language learning and not STEM content, so E2 applies. The study is also an AI scoring/agreement study (Gemini used for grading, not learner-facing learning activity with a control group), and it reports QWK agreement rather than a learning outcome with a control group. E2 is the first applicable code in order from the protocol's perspective of content domain, so it is reported. Abstract gives clear positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: we used an observational study design with a single condition
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes an observational study with a single condition and no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Students annotated a ChatGPT-produced code trace; the programming domain and higher-education population fit, and the design fails the comparison requirement. Excluded on E3, the first applicable code in order that the abstract gives positive evidence for.

quote: Dr. Mary Blair Bowers is a pioneer in the use of biological electron microscopy (EM) for the study of cell cytoskeleton and motility.
rationale: This is a biographical tribute/historical essay about a microscopist, not an empirical study. It describes no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that E1 (no learner-facing generative AI) would also apply on the face of it; E6 is the first applicable code given the nature of the document, so it is reported as the primary code.

quote: The experiment has shown that artificial intelligence ChatGPT-4 generally gives an adequate idea of the current issues in this area of engineering pedagogy.
rationale: The abstract is a theoretical/conceptual article on humanitarian engineering thinking. It describes an informal "experiment" in which ChatGPT-4 was queried, with no description of learners, a control group, or a quantitative learning outcome. The article's stated purpose is to substantiate a regularity and refine ontological ideas, so it does not appear to be an empirical study with comparison data. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is positive evidence from the abstract. No quantitative outcome or control group is reported, so E3 and E5 would also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: A total of 85 students participated — 45 experimental and 40 control — from a rural educational institution in the province of Imbabura.
rationale: Abstract shows a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with a non-equivalent control group, students in middle basic education, mathematics content, and a learning outcome (rating scale). Gamification with AI and feedback via generative AI suggests a generative AI intervention. Published 2026. Effect sizes are reported (d = 2.48), so data sufficiency appears plausible. Journal venue is listed as a revista; publication type and full-text language are not verifiable at abstract stage, so no exclusion is made. Include at abstract stage per rule 2.

quote: The sample group consisted of 48 fourth-year students from the Digital Technology for Business program at Silpakorn University.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group study of 48 students with no control group. Outcomes are opinions, perceptions, feasibility ratings, and usage frequency, not a quantitative learning measure. The domain (business/digital technology across education, software, art, business) is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion on E3 (no comparison group without generative AI) is the first code that applies with positive evidence; E5 would also apply.

The record is a retraction notice for a special issue, not an empirical study of a generative AI learning intervention. The abstract describes no intervention, comparison group, learning outcome, or STEM content. The title refers to rural digital governance, which is outside STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), since the record itself is a retraction notice. Note that the title does match a retracted article in the list, but the abstract gives no design details to assess further.

quote: This research employs a quantitative method with a correlational approach.
rationale: The study is a correlational survey design with no control or comparison group receiving or not receiving generative AI; it relates self-reported AI use to critical thinking. This fails the comparison and design criteria (E3 applies as no control group without generative AI exists). Population (university students) is fine; the domain is mathematics education, and AI tools named include Photomath and ChatGPT, but the correlational design is the decisive positive evidence of failure.

quote: The methodology relies on a mixed approach combining quantitative and qualitative methods: analysis of teachers’ activity in LMS Moodle, content analysis of forums and reflections, surveys, observations, and thematic coding of discussions.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical analysis of connectivism with an illustrative course (E-learning 2023) evaluated through activity analysis, content analysis, surveys, and observations. No separate control group, no generative AI learner intervention evaluated against a comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome are described. Participants are teachers (in-service, which falls outside the population), and the content is pedagogy rather than STEM. Judged as a non-empirical/descriptive study, E6, with the design failing to show a comparison group. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design, so exclusion is supported.

quote: This conceptual paper examines how honesty and integrity, as foundational values in science, are being tested in an AI-mediated educational environment.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper that proposes a model based on literature. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6), which is the first applicable code in order after E1 to E5 are considered; E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the earliest code with positive evidence of failure.

quote: The paper has analyzed the correlation between the use of digital tools and perceived acquisition of 21st-century skills among university students
rationale: The study is a correlational survey of digital tool use and self-perceived skill development, with no control group and no experimental manipulation. The outcome is perceived skill development, not a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol, the design (correlational/survey) and the lack of a non-generative-AI comparison group both fail. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that E1 could also be argued, since the digital tools are not clearly learner-facing generative AI, but E3 is the clearest positive evidence. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclude.

quote: this study proposes combining state-of-the-art machine translations (i.e., Google Translate & ChatGPT) and artificial neural networks (ANNs) to mitigate two key concerns of human scoring
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT translation) is used for automated scoring of student responses, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Learners do not interact with generative AI, so E1 applies. The study also has no control group without generative AI, and it is a psychometric scoring study rather than a learning intervention, so other criteria are doubtful. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical article on forming academic integrity in pedagogical training (specialty 011). ChatGPT appears only as an illustrative prompt example, not as a learner-facing intervention. No controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome is described; the "results of checking the integrity" are not reported quantitatively. Not an empirical comparative study. Domain (pedagogical sciences) is also not STEM. Exclusion code E1 would be the first applicable code in order, since the generative AI is not a learner-facing intervention; however, the primary failure is that the paper is not an empirical study. Following the code order strictly, E1 applies first because the intervention criterion is not met by learner-facing generative AI.

quote: The study surveyed nursing faculty from Jordan and the United States using a self-reported questionnaire.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of nursing faculty perceptions. No learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, participants are faculty rather than students, the domain is health professions nursing, and the outcome is perceptions only. The design is a survey, so it is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol; E6 is the most applicable code. Note that E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would arguably apply first in code order since faculty are the users, so E1 is the first code that applies by the stated ordering.

quote: The year 2021 marked the fiftieth anniversary of Keith Thomas's Religion and the Decline of Magic (1971), a book that set the agenda for decades of scholarship on the history of supernatural beliefs.
rationale: The record is a historiographical essay on Keith Thomas's 1971 book in Past & Present. It is not an empirical study: there is no intervention, comparison group, learner population, or learning outcome. It is not a STEM learning study. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits; E1 and E2 would also apply in spirit, but E6 is the most fundamental failure. The abstract is clearly positive evidence of non-empirical scholarship, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

This is a conference meeting report summarizing sessions. It is not an empirical study: it reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome. It contains no generative AI learner intervention; AI appears only as a discussion topic. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 would also plausibly apply, but the record is primarily a non-empirical report.

quote: The results indicate that the chatbot provided accurate responses aligned with the curriculum content, with significantly higher average scores than students.
rationale: Abstract describes a ChatGPT-based chatbot for Electromagnetic Engineering (STEM), but it is unclear whether learners interact with the chatbot, whether there is a control group without generative AI, or the study design. The comparison is chatbot versus students' scores, which is not clearly a control group of learners without generative AI. Not enough positive evidence of failure at abstract stage; advance to full text to check design, comparison, and outcome data.
rationale_note: Possible E3 issue at full text if no non-AI control group exists.

quote: The article analyses and systematizes the influence of AI technologies on the content and methods of training future professionals in the field of digital technologies.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/analytical review of AI's influence on training digital technology specialists. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing criterion in order (E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so E6 is the first clear failure only after the study-type judgement; E6 is the earliest code with positive evidence). Design and comparison criteria are also not met.

quote: The results indicate a significant improvement in students’ understanding of generative AI concepts and their ability to apply the technology in a simple learning context.
rationale: The abstract describes a community service training program (PKM) with no separate control group; the reported improvement implies a single-group pre-post comparison, which the protocol excludes under E3. Domain (generative AI literacy) is also not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion is present, so exclude at abstract stage. Publication venue is not a journal article indication either, but this is not the basis for exclusion.

quote: In this study, a correlational survey design within the scope of quantitative methods was employed.
rationale: The study is a correlational survey of AI literacy among preschool administrators, with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an experimental study. Coding E6 (not an empirical study is inaccurate strictly, but the design is a survey, which the protocol excludes as a design); the first applicable code in order is E1, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Applying the order strictly, E1 applies first.

quote: An observational pilot analysed logs for 205 students and an anonymous questionnaire (N = 100).
rationale: The abstract describes an observational pilot with log analysis and a questionnaire only, with no separate control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group and a non-experimental design fails the comparison and design criteria, so the record is excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain and population are not clearly stated in the abstract, but the exclusion rests on the comparison failure alone.

The record has only a title, venue, and year (2026, so the date criterion is met). The title suggests ChatGPT use in proof validation, which is mathematics, but there is no abstract. The title's Habermas framing hints at a qualitative or theoretical design, which would fail the design criterion, but this cannot be confirmed. No comparison group, learning outcome, or population details are visible. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: Based on a systematic analysis of scholarly sources, the essence of mobile learning is clarified as a form of organizing the educational process
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and conceptual paper: literature analysis, theoretical generalization, and proposed didactic models, with no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the one-code rule, E6 is reported as the first applicable code in order over later codes such as E3 and E5. The paper is a 2026 Ukrainian-language article, so the date criterion is met, but the language of the full text was not verified at this stage.
exclusion_code_note: E6 is listed in the protocol as the code for non-empirical studies.

quote: A prospective, single arm, pre-post design, which incorporates both quantitative and qualitative measures.
rationale: The study is a single-arm pre-post design with no control group, which fails the comparison and design criteria (E3 would be the code for a single-group pre-post design). Under the protocol's ordering rule, E2 is checked before E3, though, and the topic is breaking bad news in medical education, which is health professions education and therefore not STEM. The domain failure is the first applicable code in order, so E2 is reported. The outcomes are self-efficacy, willingness, and intention, which are self-reported perceptions rather than learning measures, so E5 would also apply later in sequence. The population is senior medical students, which is higher education.

The study is a community service program on ChatGPT training to improve university students' writing skills. Writing is not STEM content, so E2 applies first in the code order. Also, the design is a before-after evaluation of a single group with no control group described (E3 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E2. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's described focus on writing, not STEM.

The quote is in Indonesian; the English translation reads "This study employs a literature review method by examining academic publications".

quote: This article provides a systematic and comprehensive review of this deepening fusion
rationale: The record is a review article on electromagnetic metamaterials and AI, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 would be checked first, but the review is not a learner-facing study, so E6 is the substantive reason. Exclusion at the abstract stage is justified because the abstract positively states it is a review.

Design, comparison, and quantitative learning outcome are unclear from the abstract, so the record advances to full text for checking.

No learner interacts with generative AI and there is no control group. Excluded at E1 as the first applicable code. Design is a retrospective comparison of predicted versus observed item indices, not a controlled experiment.

Following rule order, E1 is not clearly applicable since generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini) are mentioned as used by students, so E3 is the first clear failure at abstract stage.

Descriptive quantitative survey (questionnaire of 39 students, Likert averages) with no control group, so no comparison without generative AI. Outcome is perceived benefit/usage rather than a learning measure, and the design is not experimental. Domain is also not clearly STEM (general assignments in digital communication). Excluded at abstract stage on E3 as the first clear failure per protocol order; the design is survey-based and would also fail E5 and E6 at full text.
