quote: This research employed a qualitative case study design.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study with three purposively sampled students and no control group. This fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code; the qualitative design would also fail the design criterion. Intervention (ChatGPT as learner support), STEM content (mathematics), and population (senior high school) appear to be met.

quote: the course instructor and seven AI models using five different prompts with varying levels of detail
rationale: The generative AI models are used to grade student responses, not as learner-facing tools in a learning activity; the protocol excludes AI used only for grading (and the abstract shows AI as assessor). Also history content is not STEM, and the design is an exploratory case study with no control group without generative AI. E1 is the first applicable code in order. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: This study used a quasi-experimental method with a single-group pretest-posttest design.
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a single-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that does not use generative AI, which is a positive indication of E3 (one group measured before and after). Domain is also not clearly STEM from the abstract, but E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is positively evidenced. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: involving fifteen teachers from various disciplines
rationale: Participants are in-service secondary school teachers in a community-engagement workshop, which the protocol excludes (in-service teachers are not K-12 or higher education students). The abstract also gives no control group, no quantitative learning outcome with statistics, and reports a workshop with qualitative-style improvement claims. The population failure is the first applicable code in order that is positively evidenced; E4 is reported as the first failing criterion that is clearly stated.
rationale_note: Also noted: no control group described (E3) and no quantitative outcome (E5) in the abstract; E4 chosen as the first code in protocol order that applies on positive evidence.

rationale: Abstract stage. The content is naloxone/opioid overdose prevention and treatment in nursing education, which is health professions education and not STEM under the protocol's domain rule. The abstract also reports only a single-cohort descriptive design with perceptions and a quiz mean, with no control group described, so E3 and E5 are not clearly established from the abstract alone. Excluding on E2 is sufficient.

quote: News in Astronomy & Geophysics – December 2023
rationale: The record is a news magazine column (a round-up of astronomy and geophysics news items), not an empirical study. It describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not a journal research article eligible for the review. Excluded on E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits; E10 (publication type) could also apply, but the content is a news item rather than a research paper.

quote: Participants were blinded to question source.
rationale: ChatGPT was used by educators to author MCQs (teacher-side material preparation), and learners did not interact with the generative tool. Raters are international nurse educators evaluating item quality, not learners. This fails E1 (not learner-facing generative AI). Also the outcome is perceived item quality ratings by educators rather than a learning outcome in students (E5 would also apply), and the population is educators, not students (E4). E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Implications for research and teaching, including a consideration of ChatGPT, are also presented.
rationale: Abstract describes an analysis of general chemistry students' experimental design outputs in an activity. No learner-facing generative AI intervention is described; ChatGPT appears only as a consideration in implications. No control group or quantitative comparison is evident, and the design appears to be qualitative/descriptive analysis of student work. Positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI supports E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: Online Career Mentorship Platform Using AI-Powered Recommendations
rationale: The abstract describes a career mentorship platform matching students and professionals with mentors and giving career guidance. This is not STEM content, so E2 applies. The outcomes reported (matching accuracy, response relevance, satisfaction) are system metrics and satisfaction, not learning outcomes, and no control group without generative AI is described. Exclusion rests on the domain criterion, which is clearly not met.

E6 is the first code that applies in order.

quote: generative AI-based vocational high school apparel class
rationale: Content is handkerchief/life-accessory fashion design, which is not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science, so E2 applies. The study also appears to lack a comparison group: it classifies prompts into levels and compares design scores across them within one class, with a mixed-methods exploratory design, which would likely be E3 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported.

quote: Item analyses revealed no statistically significant differences between the two AI models regarding item difficulty, discrimination, variance, or reliability.
rationale: The study compares two generative AI tools (ChatGPT and DeepSeek) generating multiple-choice items; there is no non-generative-AI control group, so E3 applies. Students sat a test built from AI-generated items, and the study is about item generation by AI rather than learner-facing learning, and the outcome is item psychometrics rather than learner learning, so other codes could also be argued, but E3 is the clear first failing criterion per the comparison row as the study only compares two generative AI variants. Abstract-stage evidence supports exclusion.

quote: This reflective, collaborative autoethnographic study investigates the experiences of a doctoral student and her supervisor.
rationale: The study is a reflective collaborative autoethnography of one doctoral student and supervisor. It has no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. E6 is the first applicable code in order: the paper is a qualitative reflective account rather than an empirical study meeting the design requirements. Domain is also unclear (sexuality studies research topic, not clearly STEM). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: We collected pre- and post-surveys from 191 students in the genetics class. We used a mixed method analysis (quantitative and qualitative) to analyze students' ratings and explanations.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-class pre/post survey study with no control group, and outcomes are self-reported perceptions and usage (less likely to use AI for essays, more positive attitudes). No quantitative learning outcome is reported, so E5 applies. Also a single-group pre-post design (would be E3 under the comparison rule), but the first applicable code in order is E5 only if E3 is not checked first; per protocol order E3 precedes E5, so the strictly first applicable code is E3. Note the design lacks a comparison group, which is the earlier-ordered failure.

quote: We gathered reports from UN agencies, NGOs, news, social media, and interviews with Yemenis abroad. We used both manual review and AI (LLMs) to analyze themes.
rationale: This is a descriptive analysis of secondary reports about education disruption in Yemen. Generative AI (LLMs) is used by researchers to analyze themes, not by learners in a learning activity (E1 would apply under the intervention rule, but E1 is for learner-facing AI and the first applicable code in order is E1). Strictly in code order, the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 is the first applicable code. No control group, no learner quantitative outcome, and the design is not an empirical experiment; E6 also fits. Reporting the first applicable code in order gives E1.

quote: This review proposes a structured framework for educators and learners to develop critical thinking while engaging with AI in medical contexts.
rationale:
The record is a narrative review (Obstetrical & Gynecological Survey, abstracted from an NEJM review article) that proposes a framework. It is not an empirical study with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. It is also medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study, the first applicable code in order.</rationale>

It also involves no generative AI intervention learners interact with (the only AI mention is a summary of another team's study of chatbot answers to legal questions), and the domain is education law, not STEM. E6 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly met, so it is reported. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the article's own stated purpose. rationale: The study is a survey of 61 educators (in-service teachers, not students) with no control group and no learner-facing intervention. Under the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study is a stretch, but the design is a descriptive survey). Note that the survey design is itself a non-eligible design; the code applied here is the closest match in the order of checks, since E1 (learner-facing intervention) and E3 (no control group) would also apply. rationale: The record is a document-based case study of a national policy program. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares ChatGPT-4o's performance on a two-tier test against students' scores. This is positive evidence from the abstract: the comparison is AI performance versus human test scores, not an intervention-control design. Excluding at abstract stage on E3 is reasonable, though the intervention criterion is also doubtful (E1 could apply since the AI was prompted by researchers, not learners).

Under the rules, E6 is the first code that applies after checking E1 through E5, which are not clearly established from the abstract alone. There is no comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists on comparison/design (no control group, correlational) and population (in-service teachers, not students), so the record is excluded. Per the code order, E1 is not clearly applicable, E2 is unclear, and E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first clear failure reached after E1/E2, so E3 is assigned.
decision_note: Exclusion code chosen per protocol order; population (E4) would also fail.

quote: Se realiza una revisión bibliográfica y un estudio de caso instrumental con enfoque cualitativo en un instituto de Barcelona
rationale: Qualitative instrumental case study with interviews and a focus group; no control group, no comparison, no quantitative learning outcome, and no generative AI intervention that learners use in a learning activity (ChatGPT is only mentioned as a tool students depend on). Excluded on E3 as no control group without generative AI is reported, which is the first applicable code in the stated order given the design is non-experimental. Domain (library/information literacy) is also not clearly STEM.

quote: Quantitative data came from Likert scale responses, while the researchers drew qualitative insights from coded action verbs and thematic analysis of open-ended responses.
rationale: The study is a survey-based pilot of student perceptions (Likert self-report) of AI-guided assignments, with no described control group and no measured learning outcome. Outcomes are perceived effectiveness and self-reported cognitive engagement, which the protocol excludes as perception-only. The exclusion code is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The abstract also gives positive evidence of a single-group, survey-based design. Although the rule says to exclude only on positive evidence at abstract stage, the abstract clearly describes perception-only outcomes, so E5 is justified. Comparison and design criteria also appear not met, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order the protocol specifies for this stage.

quote: A quantitative approach using a survey method was conducted with 170 students
rationale: The study is a survey-based correlational design (coefficient of determination analysis) with 170 students, not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a control group. There is no comparison group described. Coded E6 as not an empirical experimental study per protocol design criteria; the design is survey/correlational, which the protocol excludes. Domain (writing scientific papers in an IT education program) is also not clearly STEM content. The first applicable code in order is arguably E3 (no control group without generative AI), but the abstract's positive evidence is a survey design, so E6 was used as the closest fit. Note for audit: E3 could be argued instead, since no control group is reported.
decision_note: Audit flag: criteria object contained a duplicate key; design/outcome statuses above reflect the intended values.

quote: The findings revealed growing reliance and acceptance of AI tools among doctoral students.
rationale: The study investigates PhD students' perceptions of AI tools for academic writing using a mixed-methods survey and six interviews. It reports perceptions and attitudes, not a quantitative learning outcome, and there is no control group or comparison design. Not STEM content either (English department), but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention were clearly not learner-facing; the abstract does not establish that, so E5 is applied as the clearest positive failure: no quantitative learning outcome, only perceptions.

quote: First, we compared and analyzed the documents of the general intellectual property curriculum of the 2015 and 2022 curricula
rationale: The abstract describes a document analysis of curricula, textbooks, and laws, plus a feasibility check of generative AI on a patent specification. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a non-empirical policy and curriculum analysis, so E6 applies. Generative AI use is mentioned only as an assistant-teacher proposal, and the record does not show learners interacting with it.

quote: The DTA dataset did not measure AI use and was used only to test whether recovery-related programming traces added predictive information.
rationale: The study is a survey structural equation model plus text coding and observational behavioral-trace prediction. It has no separate control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition; the survey is correlational, and the DTA dataset did not measure AI use at all. The design fails the comparison and design criteria (E3 applies as the first failing code, since no control group without generative AI exists). Correlational/survey designs would also fail E6-style design criteria, but E3 is the first applicable code in order given the comparison failure. Abstract provides positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Speaking anxiety is still a major obstacle to effective learning of English language among Pakistani ESL learners
rationale: The study concerns English language learning (conversational English practice), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies as the first failing criterion in code order. The abstract also describes a correlational/questionnaire design with no control group and perception-based outcomes (anxiety, confidence), which would fail E3, E5 and design criteria as well. Given the E2 applies first, it is the code reported.

quote: The Gemini AI Technical Training Program is part of a Community Service initiative aimed at enhancing teachers' capacity to use AI technology in a practical and ethical manner within educational environments.
rationale: The record describes a community service training program for in-service teachers (Ciayumajakuning region), not a controlled study with a comparison group or a quantitative learning outcome for students. It is a community service report, not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Population also fails (in-service teachers are excluded by protocol), and there is no comparison group or learning outcome reported in the abstract.

quote: This emerging technology report examines the design, development, and implementation of an artificial intelligence (AI)d chatbot to support inquiry-based learning within a K–12 capstone context.
rationale: The record is an emerging technology report describing the design and development of a chatbot. It reports no comparison group, no controlled design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion. Domain is also unclear (capstone internships, not obviously STEM). Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical design report.

Abstract describes a correlational mixed-methods study (Pearson correlation) of students' GenAI acceptance, anxiety, and self-regulation. There is no intervention with a control group and no learning outcome measured; the design is correlational and the outcomes are perceptions/affective constructs. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI), which is the most direct failed criterion at abstract stage. Note that the design failure (correlational, not an experiment) and the outcome failure (no quantitative learning measure) would also apply.

quote: The community service activity was successful, with indicators showing 100% teacher attendance over the two-day activity, 97% participation in discussions and questions, and 81% teacher understanding
rationale: Community service (pengabdian masyarakat) report of a teacher training activity, not an empirical study. No control group, no learner-facing generative AI intervention (teachers only), in-service teachers rather than students, and outcomes are attendance/participation/understanding percentages rather than a quantitative learning outcome. E6 is the first applicable code in the order given; E1 (teacher-only AI use) and E4 (in-service teachers) would also apply.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: Several chatbots scored significantly worse on hypothetical problems than on realistic problems, with scores declining by an average of 13%.
rationale: The study uses chatbots as models of biology students and compares chatbot scores on hypothetical versus realistic questions within the same chatbots. There is no separate control group of learners without generative AI, and no learner-facing intervention is described. This is a within-model comparison of question types, so E3 applies. Domain is biology, which is not STEM under the protocol's list (science is listed, so biology could count as science; the exclusion rests on the missing comparison group).

quote: we explore how generative AI provides Chinese Heritage Language (CHL) learners with tailored real-time feedback
rationale: Abstract stage. The study concerns Chinese heritage language literacy (reading materials generated by ChatGPT), which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies. Also the abstract describes surveys, progress assessments and EEG with no clear control group described, but the domain failure alone is sufficient for exclusion. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the domain criterion fails.

quote: GenWise is a cross-platform intelligent mobile suite designed to unify diverse AI-driven utilities into a single, cohesive application experience.
rationale: This is a software architecture and system description paper (toolkit design, implementation, architecture). It reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failing the outcome and design criteria is present, so it is excluded at abstract stage under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). It is also not an empirical study (E6), but the abstract describes a system presentation with no evaluation data; E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the outcome failure.

quote: This systematic review provides unique findings with an up-to-date examination of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education (HE) from 2016 to 2022.
rationale: This is a systematic review of 138 articles, not an empirical study. It has no control-versus-generative-AI comparison or learning outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Reviews are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but E6 is the first applicable code in the ordering that fits best.

quote: The course was designed to promote active learning while avoiding emerging AI threats of cognitive off-loading or reduced critical thinking.
rationale: The course is about generative AI in public service education for MPA students, which is not a STEM domain, so E2 applies. The abstract also reports no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome (only student data and qualitative-sounding observations), so E3 and E5 are likely too, but E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

criteria.population_note: human evaluators are computer science students

quote: Results showed an average MRR@10 of 0.72, compared to 0.48 for keyword search and 0.61 for non-agentic RAG
rationale: The system is a generative LLM-based tool, but the evaluation centers on retrieval metrics (MRR, Precision@5), system latency, and Likert/SUS perception ratings. No clear quantitative learning outcome (achievement, conceptual knowledge, problem solving, or skill performance) is reported, and the study is a system development paper comparing retrieval baselines rather than a learner-facing learning intervention with a control group. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 based on positive evidence that the outcomes are system-performance and perception measures. Note the comparison is against non-agentic RAG and keyword search, so comparison-group status is also ambiguous.

quote: Through the technology determinism theory, technology-mediated learning, and unified theory of acceptance and use of technology the researcher engaged a qualitative research to examine the experiences of 10 lecturers and 40 students
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study examining experiences of lecturers and students, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a non-empirical-quantitative design that fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering, though the study is qualitative rather than non-empirical; the design failure is the substantive reason. Music study is also not clearly STEM.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of qualitative design without a control group or quantitative outcome.

quote: In order to apply LLMs to the task, detailed scoring guidelines were provided for the language models.
rationale: The LLMs are used by teachers to evaluate student code, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). The study is a correlation between LLM and manual scores, with no control group and no learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

Abstract describes an analysis of bad programming practices in code produced by ChatGPT and in handwritten C/C++ examples, with execution-time measurements of functions. It reports no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control/comparison group of learners, and no learning outcome. It appears to be a position/analytical paper rather than an empirical controlled study. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study); E1 could also apply since GenAI is used to generate code for comparison, not as a learner-facing tool.

quote: we conducted a systematic review of 55 studies through the lens of the five-dimensional technology-based learning framework
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 55 studies, not an empirical study with a control group. Under the protocol's Publication type and Design rules, reviews are ineligible and this is not an empirical comparison design. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies.
rubric_note: Review article; E6 used as the closest code for non-empirical records.
rationale_short: Systematic review, not an empirical study.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on clear positive evidence of a review.

quote: Methods: A qualitative design was used based on a systematic literature review (SLR) following PRISMA protocols and the SALSA framework.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review with qualitative design, not an empirical experimental study. It has no control group comparison or quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order after the intervention and domain checks, which cannot be assessed from the abstract.

quote: the feedback generated by the GPT-4 was generally high in quality, with 90% rated as coherent, 82% as relevant, 92% as clear, and 85% as personalized.
rationale: Generative AI (GPT-4) is used to produce feedback on Arabic short-answer responses, but the abstract reports only evaluator ratings of feedback quality (coherence, relevance, clarity, personalization). No quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or skill performance is reported, and there is no indication of a control group. Exclusion at E5 because no learning outcome is evident; the study appears to be a feedback-quality evaluation. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails.

quote: Despite limitations, including a small sample size and lack of a control group, AI-generated podcasts were positively received
rationale: The abstract explicitly states the study lacked a control group, and participants were assigned to listen to one of three AI-generated podcasts with no non-generative-AI comparison. This is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (E3). Wilderness medicine is also not clearly STEM, but E3 is the applicable first-failing code in the protocol's order only where E1/E2 do not apply; the intervention is learner-facing generative AI, and domain is unclear, so E3 is the reported code.

quote: the use of PBL supported by Wordwall and ChatGPT had a significant effect on students' cognitive learning outcomes (Sig. < 0,001)
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a quasi-experiment with a nonequivalent control group (class X.2) comparing PBL with ChatGPT and Wordwall against a control, with a cognitive outcome (essay test) and Cohen's d reported (1.00), year 2026, high-school physics (global warming). ChatGPT use by learners is implied by the PBL syntax but the abstract does not detail the learner's direct interaction; this is consistent with inclusion. The title and abstract are in Indonesian/English; the abstract is English, so language is not excluded at this stage. Full-text check needed for language and the exact learner-facing ChatGPT use. Note: physics global warming is treated as science content.

quote: Utilizing a quasi-experimental design, we applied AI-empowered PBL to the experimental group and traditional PBL to the control group
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experiment with a traditional PBL control group, generative AI (AI code auto-completion and dialogue Q&A) used by learners, undergraduate data science students (population/domain met), and quantitative pre-post scale and project outcome measures. Publication year 2025 meets date criterion. Data sufficiency for SMD and journal status cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure, so include for full-text check.

quote: Using a mixed-methods design, quantitative data from pre- and post-tests were evaluated using a comprehensive prompt-writing rubric
rationale: Content is EFL academic writing / prompt engineering as a writing genre, not STEM (E2). The abstract also describes a single-group pre-post design with no control group, which would independently fail E3. Domain failure is the first applicable code in order, so E2 is reported.

quote: The 14th National Colloquium on Distance Higher Secondary Education organized by the Red de Bachilleratos Universitarios Públicos a Distancia del Espacio Común de Educación Superior a Distancia (ECOESAD) was held October 6-13, 2023.
rationale: The record is a conference review (reseña) of a colloquium, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also a review/editorial-style piece, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given.
rationale_detail: Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical event review.

quote: integrating artificial intelligence in English speaking practice
rationale: Content is English language speaking practice, which the protocol explicitly excludes as non-STEM (E2). The study is also a survey-based mixed-methods design reporting perceptions, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would also apply; E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: Data were collected from 540 university students, whose responses to open‐ended and scale‐based questions were systematically analysed to capture the nuances of their perceptions
rationale: The study is a survey/perception study with sentiment analysis of student responses. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention with a control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and attitudes, which are excluded. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) could also be argued, but the abstract does not describe a learning activity involving generative AI tool use by learners, so E5 is the clearest failure given the perception-only outcomes. No comparison group is described, and the design is a survey, so E3/E6 also apply in part. Abstract-stage exclusion is warranted because positive evidence shows no learning outcome and no control group.

quote: The framework has been verified through two years of teaching practice in the course Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Technology at Chengdu Technological University.
rationale: The abstract describes a curriculum integration framework (knowledge modules, ideological and political elements, teaching methods, cases) for an AI course. It does not indicate learners interacting with a generative AI tool; the framework is about course content design, and "generative AI" appears only as context. No control group, comparison design, or quantitative learning outcome is described; outcomes are self-reported literacy and attitudes. Exclusion is on E1 as the first applicable code, since no learner-facing generative AI intervention is evident. Could alternatively be E3 or E5 at fulltext, but the abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is not a generative AI tool.

quote: The methods include an analytical review of Russian scientific and applied literature, a scenario description of LLM application, and a risk analysis using the “effect-risk-control measure” scheme.
rationale: The abstract describes an analytical literature review, a scenario description, and a risk analysis rather than an empirical comparative study. There is no control group or quantitative learning outcome described. Positive evidence that the study is not empirical, so E6 applies (first applicable code in the order given; E3 and E5 are also likely but the design is non-empirical).
rationale_note: Exclusion made at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-empirical design.

quote: we adopted a qualitative case study to examine how GenAI operated as both a pedagogical resource and a site of ideological tension
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study of one focal participant with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordering, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group), but the study is primarily a non-empirical-type qualitative design; the clearest positive evidence is the qualitative case study design, which fails the Design criterion. Code E6 (not an empirical study) is not exactly right either, since it is empirical qualitative research; on the strict first-applicable ordering, E3 (no comparison group) is the earliest code with positive evidence of failure. Note: the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group only indirectly, so the most defensible code is E3 given the single-participant qualitative case design with no comparison condition.

quote: involving 25 science teachers as participants
rationale: Participants are in-service junior high school science teachers in a community service training program, not K-12 or higher education students (population excluded by protocol). The study also reports a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group, so comparison and design criteria are not met. Population failure is the first applicable code in order (E4 precedes E3 only in the sense of listing; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone). Exclusion is based on the in-service teacher population, which is an explicit exclusion.

quote: This research is a qualitative systematic review.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative systematic review of 12 articles analyzed with NVivo open coding. It is not an empirical intervention study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Under the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study). The record is not in the Persian-language title's scope for exclusion; language is not the basis here.

quote: The findings indicated that participants experienced a high level of immersion through unexpectedly natural interactions, engaged in reflective self-assessment of their interaction skills
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative-style study (weekly evaluation records, interaction reports, researcher journals, iterative categorization) with 30 students and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Design is not an experiment with a comparison group, and outcomes are perceptions and reflections. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense; the design is qualitative, which the protocol excludes). Note that E6 is the closest code; the substantive failures are no comparison group (E3) and no quantitative outcome (E5). Under the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E3 comes before E5 and E6, so the code should arguably be E3 given no control group is described. Abstract gives positive evidence of a single-group qualitative design.

quote: Our study implemented ChatGPT3.5 to generate feedback and evaluative scores on short assignments in a broad range of disciplines.
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative coding study of ChatGPT-generated feedback on student writing, plus a correlation between response length and AI score. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Design is descriptive/correlational rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment, and no learner-facing quantitative learning outcome is reported. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the absence of any comparison group; E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced.
rationale_note: Exclusion uses E3 since no control group is described; design also appears non-experimental.

quote: all written assignments of a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) course of the general education curriculum were either carried out at home (control condition) or in class (experimental condition)
rationale: The experimental manipulation is writing assignments in class without technological aids versus at home. No learner-facing generative AI tool is part of the intervention; the study is about removing AI use. Intervention criterion is not met (E1). The course is Introduction to Psychology, which is not clearly STEM, so domain is also doubtful, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

criteria.exclusion_code_note: E5 applied at abstract stage; design also appears non-experimental

quote: This analysis reveals that the chat's responses and the teachers' reactions to them made several key contributions to improving mathematical problems
rationale: The abstract states the study is a qualitative analysis of prompts, ChatGPT responses, and teacher reflections with 15 pre-service teachers. No control group and no quantitative learning outcome are reported; the TPACK and problem-posing claims are not supported by any measured statistics. Positive evidence of failing criteria (qualitative design, no quantitative outcome) is present, so exclusion is warranted. Primary code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is given as the first applicable code in the order, though E3 (no control group) and E6 (qualitative, not an empirical quantitative study) would also apply.

Title indicates a latent profile analysis of problematic ChatGPT use and psychosocial factors among adults. This is a correlational/profile design with no learner-facing learning intervention and no control group, and the topic is mental health rather than STEM learning. No abstract is available, so the exclusion rests on the title alone. Coded E1 as the first applicable code in order, since ChatGPT use is not a learning intervention in a study of this kind. Note that the title alone is limited evidence; a researcher may wish to confirm at full text if desired, though the design (latent profiles, psychosocial correlates) is clearly non-experimental.

quote: The analysis is based on two case studies.
rationale: The abstract describes two case studies using a conceptual framework on agency, which is a qualitative/case design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Case studies are excluded by the design criterion, and the protocol's E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order only if considered non-empirical; the closest fit given the case-study design with no comparison group is E3 for no control group. Applying codes in order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at abstract stage, E2 (content) is unclear since algebra didactics is STEM, E3 applies because there is no comparison group described. Excluding under E3 on positive evidence that no control group exists.
quote_check: The analysis is based on two case studies.

quote: By integrating AI into classroom instruction, learners are guided through the process of decoding waveforms, identifying physical properties, and making predictions based on graphical data.
rationale: Physics (electromagnetic waves) is STEM, so the domain criterion is met. The abstract mentions large language models and graph-interpreting algorithms, which may be generative, but it does not say whether learners interact with a generative tool. It does not describe a control group or a comparison design, and "improved comprehension" gives no evidence of a quantitative outcome. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so this is unsure and should be checked at full text.

quote: the teaching of one of the most complex sections of the Kazakh literature school curriculum – "Zar Zaman" poetry
rationale: The study uses generative AI (ChatGPT GPT-4o) in a quasi-experimental design with a control group, 8th-grade students, and a quantitative rubric outcome. However, the content is Kazakh literature (poetry of the Zar Zaman period), which is not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science. Fails the domain criterion (E2), which precedes E3-E5 in the code order. Abstract provides positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: Our study evaluated ChatGPT-3.5's capability to generate pharmacology multiple-choice questions adhering to the NBME guidelines for USMLE Step exams.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT-generated exam questions reviewed by experts; learners do not interact with the AI, and there is no control group or learning outcome. Pharmacology is also a health-professions content area rather than STEM as defined by the protocol. Abstract shows no comparison group, so E3 is the first applicable code given the absence of a control group without generative AI. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of missing comparison.

quote: Post-course results indicated increased confidence in analyzing primary data and deeper engagement with the literature
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods survey and usage-log design with pre/post self-reported perceptions and confidence, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are perceptions and usage only, which the protocol excludes. Design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order? Order is E1 then E2, E3 precedes E5). Applying the order strictly: E3 applies first because there is no control group without generative AI, so the code should be E3.

quote: Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering five dimensions
rationale: Abstract describes a single-sample survey of student perceptions and usage of AI applications. There is no control group and no comparison condition, so the study lacks a comparison group (E3). It also reports only perceptions and usage, with no quantitative learning outcome (E5 would also apply). E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported. Design is a survey, which is excluded by the protocol.

quote: This study adopts a quantitative, non-experimental, and correlational approach to analyze the impact of academic AI tool usage on the development of computational thinking among Systems Engineering students.
rationale: The abstract describes a non-experimental, correlational design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Positive evidence of a failed comparison and design criterion is present, so exclusion is warranted at the abstract stage. Design is correlational, which is also excluded by the Design criterion; E3 is the first applicable code in order given the lack of a comparison group.

quote: Asking large-language models about the best learning environments for creative thought produces a list of suggestions for renovating lecture and studio spaces in architecture schools.
rationale: The abstract is a conceptual/essay-style piece on "living geometry" and architecture. It describes no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The only AI use is asking LLMs for suggestions, which is not a learner-facing intervention with a comparison. The domain (architecture design) is not clearly STEM under the protocol. Positive evidence shows the study is not an empirical comparative study, so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).

quote: This study investigates how master's students engage with ChatGPT in group-based academic tasks
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory case study with group discussions, logs, reflections and focus groups. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the design is qualitative and not an eligible comparative design. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the best fit, since it is an empirical case study; the decisive failures are E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome). Per the first-applicable order, E3 comes before E5 and E6, so the code should be E3. Final code given as E3 below.

quote: The study design used was a descriptive survey.
rationale: Descriptive survey of lecturers' awareness of AI technologies; no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Population is in-service lecturers, not students. Design is survey, so it is not an empirical experimental study; E6 applies (not an empirical study eligible under the design criteria). The first-applicable code by order would be E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design. Exclusion reported as E6 for the non-experimental design.

quote: We are very grateful for the numerous, insightful, thought-provoking, and helpful contributions to this discussion.
rationale: The record is an authors' reply to a discussion of a statistical methodology paper on the Manifold Hypothesis and latent metric space models. It involves no learner-facing generative AI tool, no control group, no learning outcome, and no empirical study. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would technically be the first code that applies, since the record describes no learner-facing AI at all. I have reported E6 because the record is a discussion reply and not an empirical study of any kind; the researcher should check whether E1 is the preferred code under the first-applicable rule.

quote: Разработан прототип инструмента оркестрации разнородных моделей с доступом в закрытый контур компании через VPN-каналы.
rationale: The abstract describes design and development of a prototype LLM/RAG system for analyzing nuclear-industry documentation and a qualitative-style comparison of cloud vs in-loop modes. It reports no controlled comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no learner population; it reads as a system-description paper rather than an empirical learning study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the strongest positive evidence; the domain (nuclear engineering documentation review, not a STEM learning setting) and population are also unclear or not met. Note the abstract gives positive evidence of no learning outcome, so E5 could also apply; E6 is cited as first applicable per the strongest reading of the abstract.

The record is a commentary (title: "A Student-Informed Commentary on Risks, Benefits, and Hybrid Use") about AI in medical admissions screening. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also concerns admissions screening rather than learner-facing generative AI in STEM learning, and there is no quantitative learning outcome or control group. No abstract is available. The title alone is positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion is supported.

quote: A qualitative approach with an exploratory case study design was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative exploratory case study using observation, document analysis, and thematic analysis. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative sense, so E6 applies. Under the rules, E6 is the first code that applies given the qualitative design; the earlier codes (E1, E2) cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone, and E3 and E5 also fail but E6 reflects the study design most directly.

quote: This special issue of Neurobiology of Language focuses on the role of the cerebellum in spoken and written language comprehension and production.
rationale: Record is an editorial/position piece ("Ten Myths and Misunderstandings") introducing a special issue on the cerebellum and language. It is not an empirical study, involves no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the first applicable code in order is E1 for the AI intervention, but the record's non-empirical nature is the core failure, and no generative AI is mentioned in the abstract beyond a passing reference to LLM training, not a learner-facing tool. There is no control group without generative AI; the study compares LLM ratings with human ratings of the same recordings, which is an assessment reliability design, not an intervention comparison. Primary exclusion is E2 (non-STEM, health professions). Design is also not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison.

quote: integrating 45 effect sizes from 25 empirical studies published between 2022 and 2025

Publication type (journal article) does not by itself remove it, so E6 is the applicable code.

However, the abstract also describes a pre-post design with a second group, and the control arm may be considered a generative AI-only group; the protocol's comparison requirement needs fulltext confirmation. Additionally, the domain is ambiguous: "dark web site production" is a web-development topic that may or may not count as STEM (computer science), and the abstract does not make this clear. Abstract does not give clear positive evidence of exclusion, so it is advanced for full-text review. Note: the record's title and abstract also use the term "dark web" in a way that could refer to web development (likely a translation of the Arabic term for web design/production), which needs checking.

Qualitative case study analysis of 36 written reflections from nine preservice teachers, coded with the SAMR framework. It reports perceptions and attitudes, with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, but E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly met on the abstract's evidence. Domain is not clearly STEM (general technology course). Abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative outcome.

rationale: Fashion design education is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). The abstract reports satisfaction scores, not a quantitative learning outcome, and gives no sign of a control group, so E2 applies as the first failing criterion in code order. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that content is non-STEM.

quote: Artificial intelligence in healthcare – the other side of the coin!
rationale: The record is an opinion/commentary piece (editorial-style essay on AI in ophthalmology and medicine) with no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). No quantitative learning outcome or comparison group is reported, and it is not a learner-facing STEM intervention study.
rationale_note: Criteria map: comparison not met (no control group); design not met (no empirical design); outcome not met (no quantitative learning outcome); intervention, population, and domain unclear/not applicable as the paper does not describe a learning study.

quote: this paper presents a thorough investigation of ten representative classical machine learning algorithms
rationale: The record is a survey/review of classical machine learning algorithms. It is not an empirical study, has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6), which is the first applicable code after the intervention check; the abstract gives positive evidence of a review design. Intervention and comparison criteria also fail on the abstract text, but E1 (learner-facing generative AI) is a non-empirical-review case better captured by E6 given the protocol's ordering only applies to the first code; E1 would technically apply first, so note this ambiguity for the auditor.

The title ("A Reddit Perspective") indicates analysis of Reddit discussion about banning ChatGPT in educational spaces, not an experimental study with a control group and learning outcome. No abstract is available. Design appears to be a non-experimental text/discourse analysis, so it is not an empirical intervention study. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on title only; no abstract content was available to confirm. Note that the record has no abstract, so the decision rests on the title and venue alone.

quote: This study investigates high school students' preferences for English writing feedback from three sources
rationale: The content is English writing feedback (EFL), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies as the first failing criterion in code order. The outcome is also preference/perception based rather than a quantitative learning measure, and there is no clear generative-AI-free control with learning outcomes. Exclusion is positive evidence based on the abstract content.

quote: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from March 1 to July 15, 2026.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of attitudes and use of AI among physicians, residents, and medical students. It has no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a survey design, not an empirical experiment. Health/medical content also falls outside the STEM domain (E2) and the population is medical professionals, but the first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention, which is unclear. Given the survey design, E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible empirical design) is the most accurate code. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the design is clearly a survey.

Abstract describes a mixed-method study with a survey of 524 students, focus groups, and pre/post surveys on academic integrity awareness. There is no described control group, and the designs are descriptive or single-group pre-post, which fails the comparison and design criteria. Nothing in the abstract indicates a learner-facing generative AI intervention with a comparison group or a quantitative learning outcome in STEM. Per the rule, I'm excluding on the first code that clearly applies. The protocol's E3 (no control group) is arguably the stronger fit; however, the paper is primarily a non-empirical-style conceptual/descriptive article, and the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and descriptive analysis only. Coding E6 is a judgment call; the auditor should review. Also note that the Study 2 single-group pre-post design alone would be E3 under the protocol.

quote: A quantitative design was employed using a structured questionnaire completed by 506 students from several higher education institutions in the UAE.
rationale: Survey-based cross-sectional study of ChatGPT usage patterns by demographic group. No experimental or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI control group is described, and no quantitative learning outcome is measured (usage and perceived improvement only). Per protocol the design and comparison fail on the abstract. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by positive evidence; the design criterion also fails (survey). The domain is not clearly STEM (general university students, writing support), which is also unclear.

quote: The article substantiates a criterion-based diagnostic framework for assessing digital literacy among undergraduate students in non-IT fields.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical framework (criteria, indicators, levels) and diagnostic tools, not an empirical study with a generative AI intervention or a control group. Generative AI appears only as a future expansion topic. Not an empirical study (E6). Note that E1 (no learner-facing generative AI) would also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order only if ordered first; per the protocol order E1 comes first, so the intervention criterion is also not met given no generative AI tool is used by learners.

quote: Survey data were evaluated using descriptive analysis, while the recorded verbal and non-verbal responses were analyzed thematically.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey with descriptive and thematic analysis of responses from 63 lecturers and students. It reports no controlled comparison group and no quantitative learning measure, only survey-based perceptions of memory and retrieval. The design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Under the code order, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but the study is not an empirical experimental study; E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the best fit for a survey without a comparison group. Note that E6 is strictly a "not an empirical study" code; this is a judgment call that a researcher should check at full text if needed.

quote: The study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational research design.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational design using questionnaires and multiple regression, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Correlational designs fail the Design criterion and lack the required comparison group. Exclusion code E3 is used for the absence of a control group; the design criterion also fails (correlational), but the first applicable code in protocol order is taken as E3 since no comparison group exists. Students' ChatGPT use is self-reported and measured as a predictor, not as a randomized or quasi-experimental manipulation.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a correlational design with no control group.

quote: this study utilizes the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to analyze the impact of 'mAIntenance'-an interactive AI chatbot
rationale: The record is a single-sample perception survey (TAM, one-sample t-test, ANOVA across academic years) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the abstract explicitly says results are subjective perceptions rather than objective academic performance. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply, but E5 is not later in the order than E3 so E3 would be the first code in the protocol order; however the protocol orders E3 before E5). Note: under the protocol order, E3 (no control group) applies first because the study has no comparison group. Corrected below.

quote: Here, we summarise the key points from iAIM keynote presentations.
rationale: This is a conference report summarising keynote talks, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the domain is medicine/health care rather than STEM education. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study; this is the first applicable code in order that fits, since E1 cannot be confirmed as a learner-facing intervention evaluation and the record is not a research study at all.

quote: The study involved 312 students from various academic programs who used ChatGPT in learning activities.
rationale: The study is a descriptive correlational survey design (ChatGPT dependency vs. self-regulated learning questionnaires) with no control group that lacks generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Outcome is self-reported self-regulated learning/dependency rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's rule to report the first that applies; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Central to this approach is the use of Google Notebook LM, a dynamic tool that not only enhances the teaching and learning experience but also prioritizes the cultivation of a genuine passion for complex texts among P-12 students.
rationale: The study concerns literacy/reading instruction in a graduate reading practicum, which is non-STEM content (language/literacy), so it fails the domain criterion (E2). The abstract also gives no indication of a control group, a quantitative learning outcome, or a comparative design, but the E2 failure is sufficient as the first applicable code. Exclusion at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: This study presents a web-based Automatic Question Generation (AQG) system that generates Physics questions for Malaysian upper secondary levels
rationale: The T5-based system generates physics questions for teachers' assessment writing; learners do not interact with the generative tool as part of a learning activity. Evaluation is by ROUGE-L and expert educator ratings, with no control group and no learner learning outcome. Excluded under E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Other criteria also appear unmet (no control group, no learning outcome, not an experimental design).

quote: The study follows a qualitative-analytical design: it re-analyses the aggregated results of a published online survey of 300 school teachers
rationale: The paper is a theoretical/qualitative-analytical study that re-analyses survey results from teachers and proposes an algorithm. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome for students. Population is teachers (in-service), not students. Not an empirical experiment; exclude under E6 as not an empirical study meeting the design requirement. Note that E1 (teacher-only use of AI for planning) could also apply; E6 is the earliest applicable code given the design, but the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 since AI is used only by teachers for lesson planning. Reporting per protocol order: E1 applies first.

quote: This resource is written in Rmarkdown, with knitted .html files included for viewing.
rationale: The record is an educational tutorial/teaching resource (QUBES) on forecasting phenology with R packages, not an empirical study. It describes no experimental or comparison-group design and no learner outcome measure. Generative AI appears only as an example for improving a ggplot output for presentations, not as a learner-facing intervention in a comparison study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E1 could also arguably apply, but E6 is the primary failure and is first in the reporting logic for a non-empirical resource.

quote: "Natural language processing (NLP) is well positioned to revolutionize clinical and health services research."
rationale: This record is a editorial commentary (Hospital Pediatrics "In this issue" piece) about NLP for pediatric chart review research. It is not an empirical study of learners, has no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note the first applicable code in order would be E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since no learner-facing intervention is described; E6 is the more fundamental reason given the record is an editorial, so E6 is reported as the primary code.

quote: A Web of Science Core Collection search conducted in April 2025 yielded 729 peer-reviewed English-language journal articles.
rationale: This is a bibliometric review (co-citation, keyword co-occurrence, BERT-based clustering) of 729 articles, not an empirical study. It has no control-group experiment or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract.
rationale_note: Note: the schema field 'onset' is not in the protocol; ignored.

quote: Accounting and Financial Institution Program

decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that content is accounting, not STEM.

quote: Opinion Piece Grounded in a qualitative review of existing literature, this paper employs a conceptual and interpretive approach
rationale: The record is an opinion piece and conceptual literature review that explicitly reports no primary empirical data. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Under the code order, E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed from the abstract as the paper has no intervention study at all, so E6 is the first applicable code that is clearly supported.

quote: Student feedback indicates increased satisfaction and feedback uptake, while the educator reports enhanced clarity and fairness in assessment.
rationale: Labelled a practice report describing a feedback model implemented in an engineering course. The abstract reports only satisfaction, perceived uptake, and educator views, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion on positive evidence: no comparison group and no learning outcome are described. E6 is the most fitting first-applicable code; E3 and E5 would also apply, but the record is a practice report rather than an empirical study.

quote: This study compared two versions of ChatGPT, Model 3.5 and reasoning o1, on their capacity to provide pedagogically sound and personalized trigonometry tutoring.
rationale: The study compares two generative AI variants (ChatGPT 3.5 vs o1) using comparative content analysis of responses, with no non-generative-AI control group, so E3 applies. It also appears to lack a learning outcome measure (responses were coded, not learner outcomes) and is not an experimental design. E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: A quasi-experimental study was conducted involving 60 undergraduate physics students split equally into an experimental group (AI supported OMO framework) and a control group (traditional lecturing).
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: ChatGPT (generative AI) used by learners for self-study, a control group receiving traditional lecturing, a quasi-experimental design, undergraduate physics (STEM), and a post-test performance outcome. Year 2026 meets the date criterion. Data sufficiency for SMD (means and SDs given but no control pre-test or n per group beyond total), publication type (CyberLeninka record, journal status not stated), and language are not resolvable from the abstract; these are checked at full text. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so include.

quote: A qualitative analysis was conducted on reflective essays written by students who participated in AI-related curriculum and extracurricular programs at a university in Daejeon in 2025.
rationale: The study is a qualitative analysis of reflective essays with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a conceptual/qualitative design, so it is not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative evaluation. Domain is unclear (AI literacy, reading and writing, not clearly STEM). Excluded on E6 as the first applicable code given the qualitative, non-comparative design; E3 and E5 would also apply.

quote: In this article, we present physician perspectives from our pilot experience implementing an ambient AI clinical documentation system
rationale: The article is a perspective/commentary describing a pilot implementation with six attending physicians. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is clinical documentation in pediatric inpatient care (not a student learning activity), with no STEM learning context. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that clearly applies to this non-empirical perspective piece. Other codes (E1 for learner-facing use, E3 for no control, E4 for population, E5 for outcome) would also fail, but the record's nature as a perspective article makes E6 the primary reason.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen per first-applicable ordering; note E1 (not learner-facing) also clearly fails.

quote: This research uses survey techniques with 107 respondents and in-depth interviews with Faculty Leaders for data triangulation.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey and interviews, with no separate control group receiving a comparison condition and no experimental design. Arabic writing is not a STEM domain. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in order of the protocol's code list, since the study has no comparison group without generative AI. The design also reads as a survey, which would fail the design criterion. The domain (Arabic language writing) is clearly non-STEM, which is an independent failure. Under rule 2, exclusion at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence of a failing criterion (survey design, no control group, non-STEM content).

quote: Through semi-structured interviews, focus groups, and documentary analysis, an intensive and growing use of GAI by students for academic activities was evidenced

It is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design, comparison, or outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first code that clearly applies; the study is in fact empirical but qualitative, so E3/E5 would also apply. Its design fails the protocol's design criterion (qualitative designs excluded). Domain is also not clearly STEM. The quote is from the abstract.

Positive evidence of failing comparison, design (qualitative), and outcome (no quantitative measure) is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Primary code: E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative sense) is the most fitting; the qualitative nature points to E6 as the first applicable code given the design is qualitative rather than a comparative experiment. quote: Pre- and postcourse surveys revealed significant increases in students' frequency of AI use, academic confidence in using AI, and perceived utility of AI
rationale: Intervention is a learner-facing LLM chatbot (ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini) in a STEM course (general chemistry) with students in higher education. However, the abstract reports only survey outcomes (frequency of use, confidence, perceptions, anxiety) and states academic performance was not compromised without giving a quantitative learning measure. Perception and usage outcomes do not satisfy the quantitative learning outcome requirement, so the record fails E5. No control group is described in the abstract, but since E5 applies on the outcome evidence, it is the first clear failure in order given the abstract. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the outcome is perception/usage only.

quote: Survey data from 100 secondary school teachers revealed no statistically significant gender differences in general AI use, content creation, lesson clarification, and problem-solving.
rationale: The study is a survey of secondary school teachers examining gender differences in AI use and confidence. It has no learner-facing AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a survey design. Population is in-service teachers, which is excluded. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since AI use here is by teachers and not learners. Coding E1 as the first failing criterion per the order rule would be more accurate than E5; the abstract shows teachers only use AI tools in a survey with no learner-facing intervention. Final code is E1.

quote: Shaping AI in Pelvic Floor Physiotherapy: The Impact of Role-Play Prompting on ChatGPT Response Quality

The study also appears to evaluate ChatGPT response quality under role-play prompting, not learner-facing use with a learning outcome, so no learner-facing intervention or quantitative learning outcome is evident. No abstract was available. The domain failure is positive evidence, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

Exclusion code E10 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported; E1 is unclear because the study tests ChatGPT directly rather than learners, so E10 is reported as the primary code.

quote: The study adopted a sequential explanatory research design to evaluate the effects of CPD training on the pedagogical knowledge of lower secondary school teachers of mathematics and science.
rationale: The intervention is continuous professional development training for in-service teachers, not learner-facing generative AI. No generative AI tool is mentioned, and the population is in-service teachers rather than students, so the record fails E1 (and would also fail E4). No control group without generative AI is described. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not generative AI.

Title indicates a study of teachers' AI literacy and their teaching innovation behaviors (survey-style mediation analysis) in Chinese K-12 education. The population is in-service teachers, not students, and the outcome concerns teacher behavior rather than a learner quantitative outcome. No abstract is available. Excluding on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clearly applicable failure; the population failure (E4) is also evident, but the protocol requires reporting the first code in order, and E4 precedes E5 in the list, so the correct code is E4. No intervention with learner-facing generative AI is described either, which would be E1 and comes first in order.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. That would point toward E1, but the title does not show that clearly. It also gives no evidence of a control group, a STEM domain, a student population, or a quantitative learning outcome. Nothing in the record is positive evidence of a failed criterion, so under the abstract-stage rule it advances to full text for review.

Abstract is absent from the index; only the title and venue are available. rationale: The record is a systematic literature review (thematic analysis of 20 articles, PRISMA). It is not an empirical primary study with a control group, so it is not an empirical study (E6). quote: Data were collected from N = 93 university students at a Hungarian university; analyses were conducted on the subsample of n = 73 AI users.
rationale: Abstract describes a correlational/regression survey of students' perceived AI role and cognitive independence, with no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group without generative AI. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code given the abstract; the design failure would also support E6 arguably, but the abstract gives no evidence of an experiment. Positive evidence of failure is present for comparison, so exclude.

quote: Using a qualitative research methodology, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 17 pre-service English language teachers
rationale: Qualitative interview study of perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical comparative study eligible under the protocol. Content is also language teaching (non-STEM), so E2 could apply too, but the first applicable code in order is E6 only if no earlier code applies; E1 and E2 are arguably met here since the study concerns perceptions of EFL teaching, which is non-STEM. Coded E2 would be the first applicable code in protocol order, but the study's design (qualitative, no outcome) is the more fundamental failure. Decision: exclude at abstract stage on clear positive evidence of qualitative design.

quote: This study examines the use of ChatGPT as a translation-support tool for Arabic texts among seventh-semester students of the Arabic Language Education Program
rationale: Arabic translation is language learning, not STEM (E2). The study is descriptive qualitative with interviews and observation, with no control group (E3 would also apply), and no quantitative learning outcome (E5). Per the code-ordering rule, the first applicable code is E2.

quote: The first step in the integration of ChatGPT developed by OpenAI is the thorough identification of the goals of the education process followed by the allocation of the appropriate API
rationale: The abstract describes a development/architecture proposal for ChatGPT-integrated intelligent tutoring systems. It reports no controlled experiment, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data, so it does not appear to be an empirical study evaluating learning. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is supported by positive evidence in the abstract that the work is a design/development paper. Language teaching is mentioned, but STEM content is not clearly established.

quote: "each AI model was prompted to generate 50 MCQs across five key hematology topics"
rationale: At abstract stage, the AI models generate MCQs as content creators; learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity. The study compares AI models against expert ratings of their outputs, with no control group of learners and no learning outcome. This is positive evidence of E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), which is the first applicable code in order. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives clear evidence the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: Experiments with multilingual encoders and a controlled MiniLM setup show that morphology-aware normalization produces measurable improvements under fixed evaluation conditions
rationale: The study is a controlled evaluation of QA model pipelines (NLP metrics such as answer selection and contextual overlap) rather than a learner-facing intervention with a control group of learners and a learning outcome. No learner outcome or learner-comparison design is described, so no quantitative learning outcome is met. Exclude on E5 at abstract stage given positive evidence that the outcome is model performance, not learning.

quote: A qualitative approach with a phenomenological design was employed to capture the lived experiences of students who actively use ChatGPT in their learning process.

Under the protocol, E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies. Design is also not eligible (E3 / qualitative design), but the protocol's ordered codes put E5 for a no-quantitative-outcome study; the abstract clearly reports only perceptions and experiences. Domain is also unclear (not explicitly STEM). Exclusion is certain on the basis of design and outcome.

Community service training report for in-service vocational teachers, not an empirical study. No control group, no learner-facing generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome. Recording E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: This paper investigates the systematic integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI) in teacher education
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative systematic review synthesizing literature, which is not an empirical primary study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Mixed teacher population (pre-service and in-service) and STEM focus are not clearly established, but the E6 exclusion is sufficient.

quote: This perspective article is grounded in professional experience and classroom observation, and its aim is to raise an issue and open it for discussion rather than to settle it.
