Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense). Abstract gives positive evidence of qualitative design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Note that E2 (content not STEM) could also apply; E6 is cited as the first applicable code in the given order only if E1 and earlier codes do not apply. E1 does not apply because the intervention is student-facing generative AI use (ChatGPT, Gemini). E2 precedes E6 in order, so the correct first applicable code is E2.

Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion requires positive evidence; the closest code is E3 (no control group), though E6 (not an empirical study) may also apply. Note that the generative AI component is used to generate questions, which may be teacher/system-side rather than learner-facing, so E1 is also possible at fulltext. Marking exclude with E3 as the most supported code given no comparison is described; a researcher should verify at fulltext if needed.

rationale: The abstract describes two generative AI variants (GPT-only vs GPT with RAG) compared on accuracy of answers to university queries. Learners are not clearly the ones interacting with the tool (queries appear to be benchmarked by the researchers), and the outcome is answer accuracy rated by experts rather than learning. These points cannot be fully resolved from the abstract, so I return unsure for full-text review rather than excluding on missing information.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage rule: exclude only on positive evidence.

rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive design using semi-structured interviews on student perceptions. quote: In this research, the case study method, which is one of the qualitative research approaches, was used.
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study based on semi-structured interviews with 10 academicians, analyzed by content analysis. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental study with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are academics giving opinions, not students. It is therefore not an empirical study meeting the design requirements (E6). Under the code order, E1 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but E6 is the decisive failure.

quote: The results indicate that the experimental group experienced a significant improvement in stoichiometric understanding, with an N-Gain score of 0.84
rationale: At the abstract stage, all criteria appear met: generative AI integrated into learner activity, a pretest-posttest control group design (quasi-experimental with control), high school students (Grade XI), chemistry stoichiometry (STEM), and quantitative outcomes (N-gain, CCTST/CTMS/CTS). Publication year 2025 meets the date rule. Venue is a journal (AS-SABIQUN); article type not fully confirmed but no exclusion is evident. Include for fulltext verification of SMD data and control-group content.

quote: A posttest-only control group experimental design compared novice Arduino programmers who developed their own programs (self-programming group, n = 17) with novice Arduino programmers who used ChatGPT 3.5 to write their programs
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear met: learners use ChatGPT 3.5 (generative LLM) to write Arduino programs; a self-programming control group without generative AI exists; the design is an experimental posttest-only control group; undergraduates in an introductory agricultural systems technology course (programming is computer science/engineering content); outcomes include programming rubric scores and posttest scores (quantitative learning measures); published 2024. Means/SDs are not in the abstract, but Cohen's d is reported for some outcomes and missing information is not evidence for exclusion. Full-text check still needed for SMD computability and journal-article status.

quote: The empirical basis is the program "Neural Networks in Foreign Language Teaching," where AI tools were applied for needs assessment, content adjustment, and development of differentiated tasks.
rationale: Abstract indicates the population is adult in-service professional development (continuing professional education for teachers), which falls outside K-12 or higher education students. The content is foreign language teaching, which is non-STEM. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is mentioned. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of population failure (in-service teachers/adult CPE learners), with E4 as the first applicable code in order before E2 is considered; note the domain also appears non-STEM.

criteria.intervention_note: AI used by teachers to grade essays, not learner-facing

quote: An AI Agent named "Essay Grading Assistant" ... used to assess intermediate-level Chinese writing
rationale: The AI agent is used for automated scoring of essays; learners do not interact with it as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). Also the design is an agreement/correlation study between AI and human raters with no control group without generative AI (E3 would also apply), and the domain is Chinese language learning, which is non-STEM (E2). Under the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 is given.

quote: The program was conducted at SD Islam Plus YLPI Pekanbaru and involved 32 teachers over a three-day period.
rationale: Participants are in-service elementary school teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. The record is also a community service program with no described control group or quantitative learning outcome; these would be additional failures, but the first applicable code in order is E1 check (AI is used by teachers for media design, not learner-facing) — however, the population failure is the clearest and the protocol excludes in-service teachers. Excluded on population.

quote: Survey data were collected from 193 high school students and analyzed using SEM to validate the proposed model.
rationale: The study is a survey-based SEM analysis of correlations among reading factors, not an experiment with a generative AI intervention or control group. Generative AI is mentioned only as a suggestion in the discussion, not as an intervention learners used. Not an empirical experimental study meeting the protocol; E6 applies as the first failing code in order (E1 would also apply since no learner-facing generative AI intervention is evaluated, but the design is correlational/survey). Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design.

quote: Through usability testing with high school students to evaluate technical feasibility, user experience, and pedagogical value
rationale: The abstract describes a prototype development with usability testing and Likert-based satisfaction measures (EUCS). There is no control group or comparison condition, and the outcomes are perceptions/satisfaction rather than a quantitative learning measure. Per the protocol, this fails comparison (E3) and the outcome criterion. E3 is applied as the first failing code in order, since the design has no comparison group without generative AI. Record is clearly positive evidence of no control group in the abstract.

quote: The study evaluated the perceptions of medical students regarding a didactic intervention with ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group quasi-experimental pre-post design measuring only perceptions (confidence, general impact, willingness to recommend). The protocol excludes single-group pre-post designs (E3) and outcomes limited to perceptions (E5). Reporting only perceptions with no quantitative learning outcome is the clearest positive failure. Domain is physiology, which is health professions education and so also falls outside the protocol's domain scope. The first applicable code in the order is E1 only if intervention fails; ChatGPT as a learner-facing tool is met, so E3 comes before E5 in the sequence. Because the rule asks for the first code in order, the design failure (no separate control group, E3) is the code that applies first here. Note the domain issue (medical physiology, health professions) is also a fail, but the protocol's code list puts E2 (non-STEM) earlier than E3; physiology in medicine is health sciences, which the protocol excludes under Domain.

quote: An intensive statistics and data science training short course was developed to ensure that in-country researchers could implement the necessary statistical methods for COVID-19 surveillance.
rationale: The abstract describes a short statistics course with participant feedback and course overview. No learner-facing generative AI tool is mentioned, so E1 applies. The design is a course description with feedback, with no control group or learning outcome reported, so the record also fails E3 and E5. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: We are at the cusp of a new technological era as artificial intelligence (AI) has a growing potential to transform our educational landscape and social work practice.
rationale: The abstract is a position/commentary piece on AI in education and social work, discussing ethical concerns and forecasts. It describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. No STEM content or learner intervention is described.

quote: The study is based on an integrative literature review of 31 peer-reviewed publications from 2021-2025.
rationale: The record is an integrative literature review, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract.

quote: Effectiveness of a Mobile Application with an AI-Powered Chatbot to Enhance Nursing Students' Awareness of Substance Abuse Prevention
rationale: The content is substance abuse prevention education for nursing students, which is health education and not STEM content. This is a clear positive failure of the domain criterion, so it is excluded under E2 at abstract stage. The other criteria (quasi-experimental control group, AI chatbot, KAP and SURPS outcomes, 2026 publication) appear to be met, but the domain failure is sufficient on its own.

quote: We show positive feedback from the design methodology we discuss as well as the overall process of providing automated tutoring in a gamified virtual environment.
rationale: Abstract describes student observations, feedback surveys and focus group interviews, i.e., perceptions and qualitative data, with no quantitative learning outcome or control group. Outcome criterion appears not met on positive evidence. Multi-agent reinforcement learning tutor is not clearly generative AI, but the exclusion rests on the absence of a quantitative learning outcome and a comparison group.

quote: Participant characteristics and satisfaction were assessed through standardized pre- and postbootcamp surveys, and qualitative feedback was analyzed thematically by independent coders.
rationale: This is a descriptive program report of a bootcamp with no control group. Outcomes are satisfaction and qualitative feedback only, with no quantitative learning measure. The design is not a comparison study, so E3 is the first applicable code. The record is also a tutorial/program description, which would likely fail E6 as well, but E3 applies first in the protocol's order of codes.

quote: we compared expert-defined KPs with data-driven clusters generated from LLM embeddings of student responses in biology
rationale: The study analyzes LLM embeddings of existing student responses to open-ended questions for clustering and automated scoring. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is no experimental control group or learning outcome; it is a computational analysis of embeddings. Domain is biology, which is not STEM under the protocol's list (science is listed, so this is arguably met, but E1 applies first). No injection detected.

quote: Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the system performs efficiently in terms of AI generation speed, API response time, security resilience, and overall user satisfaction achieving an average UAT score of 4.5/5.0.
rationale: The abstract describes a system build with evaluation focused on generation speed, response time, security, and user satisfaction (UAT). No control group without generative AI is described, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Satisfaction and performance metrics are not learning outcomes. Exclude at abstract stage on E3 (no comparison group) based on positive evidence in the abstract; E5 would also apply.
rationale_note: Primary code E3 chosen because the evaluation has no described comparison group; the record also lacks a learning outcome (E5).

quote: this study examines the effects of AI-facilitated dialogic practice with ChatGPT on the speaking proficiency of pre-service English teachers
rationale: The study targets English-language speaking skills of pre-service English teachers, which is language learning and not STEM. This fails the Domain criterion, so E2 applies. Other criteria (quasi-experimental design with control group, quantitative pre/post tests) appear to be met at abstract level, but the domain failure is decisive.

quote: In the conversation between Dr. Hagan and ChatGPT regarding the potential role of AI in medicine, ChatGPT exhibits remarkable intellect and provides a comprehensive discussion
rationale: This is a commentary/dialogue piece about ChatGPT's views on AI in medicine. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study. It is also medical rather than STEM-education focused. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order given the record shows no empirical design.

quote: Spark, one of the products offered by MyQ (formerly Plethora), is a game-based platform meticulously designed to introduce students to the foundational concepts of computer science.
rationale: The abstract describes a product overview and examination of the Spark platform, with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Spark is a game-based platform and the abstract does not indicate any generative AI learner-facing intervention; the mention of GAI only concerns students being less likely to use it. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. This is an abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence that the record is a descriptive overview rather than an empirical study.

ChatGPT is used to generate quantitative aptitude questions and human specialists rate their accuracy and creativity. Learners do not interact with the tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). There is no control group without generative AI and no learning outcome in students. The study evaluates AI output quality, not learning. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1.

quote: Case studies of three academic libraries
rationale: The title describes a case study design of academic libraries in Thailand addressing AI literacy. Case studies are not controlled comparison designs, and there is no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome indicated. The topic is library AI literacy rather than STEM learning content. No abstract is available. Excluded as not an empirical comparative study (E6), though the record's design is described only by its title, so the exclusion rests on the case-study design signal.
rationale_note: Exclusion code is E6 as the first applicable code. Domain is also not STEM, but E2 would apply later in order; under the protocol order, E1 (intervention) was not clearly established, so E2 might arguably be the first applicable code. Auditor should check.
quote_text: Case studies of three academic libraries

quote: Following seven iterative refinements, ChatGPT produced 100 MCQs targeting clinical-year medical students.
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods evaluation of ChatGPT-generated MCQs. Generative AI is used by the item writer, not by learners in a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (this would be E1 at full text). The abstract also has no control group, no learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. Per the protocol's code order, E1 is the first applicable code. Note that the record's own abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is teacher/researcher-facing, so I am recording E4 only as a placeholder is not correct; the code should be E1 under the protocol's order.

quote: An anonymous web-based cross-sectional survey of medical students aged ≥18 years in Georgia and India was conducted
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey correlating AI-use dependency with psychological distress. It has no control group without generative AI and no experimental comparison, so the comparison and design criteria fail. The outcome is DASS-21 distress and self-perception, not a quantitative learning outcome, and the record is a survey rather than an experiment. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code in the protocol's ordering, although E5 and E6 also apply. Since E3 is listed before E5 and E6, it is reported here.

quote: Results showed that the AI-based FS significantly improved the students' ability to pose statistical inquiry questions compared to the control group.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study uses an AI-based feedback system built on GPT-4 with sixth-grade students, an experimental vs. control group (teacher feedback), pre/post tests on statistical inquiry question posing (statistics domain, quantitative outcome), and published 2024. No positive evidence of failure of any criterion is present. Data sufficiency for SMD, language, and publication type cannot be judged from the abstract, so the record advances to full text.

quote: This study investigates Caribbean EAP lecturers' perceptions of academic integrity in the GenAI era
rationale: The study surveys 18 EAP lecturers about their perceptions of academic integrity and AI-detection software. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome in students. It is a qualitative/descriptive questionnaire study of teachers, so it is not an eligible empirical intervention study. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an intervention/comparison design); E1 would also apply because the AI is not used by learners in a learning activity. Under the code order, E1 is the first applicable code, so this should be reviewed by the auditor.
decision_note: Coded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: ChatGPT for academic writing: A game changer or a disruptive tool?
rationale: This is a narrative editorial/commentary on ChatGPT. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, no experiment and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Other criteria (STEM content, population) are not addressed by the abstract.

Community service activity with a single group evaluated by pre-test and post-test before and after training, with no separate control group. The protocol excludes single-group pre-post designs (E3). Population (senior high school students) and the generative AI focus appear compatible, and domain is unclear as the content is digital literacy and ethics rather than STEM. The E3 code applies on the design/comparison failure, which is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: Purposive sampling method was administered in order to select 20 respondents.
rationale: Participants are farmers receiving extension training on rice blast disease management, not K-12 or higher education students. Content is agricultural pest management, not STEM as defined by the protocol. Study uses an exploratory design with 20 respondents and no described control group in the abstract. Exclusion coded to E4 as the first applicable code in order; the abstract gives positive evidence that the population is not students.

quote: This design case describes how Los Angeles Pacific University (LAPU), a fully online, student-centered institution, implemented Spark, an AI course assistant, across all courses within four weeks.
rationale: The record is a design case describing an institutional rollout. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome data. Its own self-description is a design case, not an empirical comparative study, so E6 applies. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design criterion and the outcome criterion fail, so exclusion is justified even under the abstract-stage rule.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice covering a special issue, not an empirical study of learners using generative AI. The titled article (Xiao et al., social media and adolescent conformity) is listed as retracted and its text here contains no empirical design, comparison group, or learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Its topic (social media and conformity) is also not STEM and involves no generative AI learner intervention, but the first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention; I judged E6 as the most defensible single code because the record itself is a retraction notice and no study content is present. Exclusion is based on the record as given; the retraction notice itself is not an eligible study.

quote: The National Education Policy 2020 has given importance to Artificial Intelligence for latest Education System by implementing Coding, AI, CHATGPT in Curriculum, Teaching and Learning.
rationale: The abstract is a policy-oriented discussion of NEP 2020 and library practices. It describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of failure, not missing information.
rationale_note: Criteria marked 'not_met' on comparison, design, and outcome are supported by the absence of any described experiment or measured outcome in the abstract.

quote: A systematic review was conducted following a search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and ERIC (November 2022–April 2026).
rationale: The record is a systematic review, which is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also addresses medical education (clinical reasoning), which is health professions education and outside the STEM domain, but E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Included studies are synthesized, not a primary study with a control group. The review is also dated 2026 and so passes the date criterion, but that does not change the exclusion.

quote: Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews supported by audio recordings.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of Grade 11 students' experiences and perceptions with AI. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome measure; the motivation findings are perception-based. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, and E2 (STEM content) is not clearly established either. The first code that clearly applies is E3, since there is no comparison group without generative AI. The record is excluded on positive evidence of missing controls and qualitative design.

The abstract describes a systematic literature review plus a survey of university students about attitudes and ethical perceptions toward ChatGPT. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Not an empirical learning study, so E6 applies at the first failing point in order is actually E3 (no control group) for design-level reasons; however, the survey-only, perception-based design is most directly non-empirical-for-learning. Coded E6 as the best fit; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome, so exclusion is supported.

quote: The study emphasizes the need for responsible AI integration in higher education through AI literacy training, clear academic integrity guidelines, validation protocols, and human-centered teaching strategies.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-sample perceptual questionnaire study (descriptive statistics, thematic analysis) of students who already use AI tools. There is no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are perceived usefulness and self-reported autonomy/engagement. Positive evidence of failing design, comparison, and outcome criteria is present, so exclusion is warranted. E3 is the first applicable code in the order of checks used here for the missing comparison group; the design (survey) and outcome (perceptions only) failures also apply. Domain is not stated in the abstract (general university students), so it is not assessed as a failure.

quote: Using an online questionnaire administered in weeks two and three of a mandatory managerial analytics course, data were collected from 45 respondents at a Canadian university.
rationale: The study is a survey of MBA students' perceptions, intentions, and concerns about AI and communication tools. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Only perceptions and intended use are reported, which the protocol excludes. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 is not used because the abstract does not clearly establish whether the tools are generative (ChatGPT is named, but the intervention itself is not described as a learning activity). E5 applies because no learning outcome is measured. The design also fails, which is consistent with exclusion, but E5 is the cleanest code given the protocol's ordering and the abstract's content.

quote: Teaching learners how to use generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots to code can enhance independent learning via real-time assistance and debugging support.
rationale: Abstract describes a library workshop teaching Python with generative AI chatbots (intervention and programming domain appear met). It does not state whether there is a control group, the study design, or a quantitative learning outcome; the "assessment" is mentioned but not described. Population is library participants, which may or may not be students. No positive evidence of an exclusion, so unsure at abstract stage for full-text review.

quote: We collect quantitative Likert ratings and qualitative comments from 1211 students on their awareness and perceptions of AI
rationale: The study surveys students' perceptions and awareness of GenAI. Outcomes are perceptions only, not a quantitative learning measure, so E5 applies. No control group or experimental design is described; the study is a survey-based perception study. Abstract gives positive evidence of perception-only outcomes, so exclusion is warranted at abstract stage.

quote: The dataset comprises 6716 utterances collected from conversations between a Socratic chatbot and 34 undergraduate statistics students
rationale: The study is a pseudo-labeling / classification pipeline for Bloom levels of chatbot utterances. It has no experimental or comparison group and no learner quantitative learning outcome; the reported metrics (micro-F1, macro-F1) are classifier performance, not student learning. Excluded under E5 as no quantitative learning outcome is measured. Comparison and design criteria also appear unmet (no control group), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given for this stage.
rationale_note: Order note: the protocol lists E1 to E10 in order; E3 (no control group) and E5 may also apply. Given the task's ordering rule, E3 precedes E5 and would be the first code that applies. Correcting: the first applicable code is E3.

quote: This article aims to analyze sentiment analysis whose data is taken from Twitter using the keyword "CahtGPT OpenAI".
rationale: The study is a sentiment analysis of Twitter posts about ChatGPT using Naive Bayes with PSO optimization. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is no learning intervention, control group, or learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1.

quote: We evaluate the retrieval core—the component that determines whether generated answers can be grounded—on an original corpus of 20 synthetic Indonesian academic-regulation passages and 30 labeled questions.
rationale: The study is a system architecture paper evaluating retrieval performance (Recall@k, MRR, nDCG, latency) on a synthetic corpus. It has no learners, no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition, and no learning outcome measured in students. Domain is academic regulations, not STEM. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported; E1 (not learner-facing) could also apply since the RAG tool is not shown to be used by learners, but the abstract does not clearly establish that. Abstract-stage evidence shows no learning outcome, so excluded.

quote: IEEE Intelligent Systems is promoting young and aspiring artificial intelligence (AI) scientists and recognizing the rising stars as "AI's 10 Watch."
rationale: The record is an editorial-style announcement recognizing AI researchers. It is not an empirical study and describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention, control group, or learning outcome. E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order that fits; E1 (no learner-facing intervention) would also apply, but the record is fundamentally a non-empirical editorial, so E6 is the best single code. Also, the publication type appears to be an editorial/feature rather than a journal research article.

quote: This study analyses the use of ChatGPT by 133 PSTss solving FPs and examines how this use is shaped by problem complexity and prior experience.
rationale: Abstract describes profiling of ChatGPT use by 133 pre-service teachers across problem complexity and prior experience; no separate control group without generative AI is described, and the analysis appears to be observational/descriptive profiling. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3. Population (pre-service teachers, STEM-adjacent mathematics modelling) and intervention are plausibly met.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on E3 based on absence of any control condition described.

rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative-dominant two-phase mixed-methods study with no control or comparison group; outcomes are transcript-coded dialogue moves, revision counts, and survey perceptions, with no quantitative learning outcome or comparison. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain is business/AI course, which is not clearly STEM, but the comparison failure is the primary basis. Exclusion is based on the abstract's design description.

quote: Findings revealed that students in the control group had limited informal exposure to AI and lacked ethical guidance, whereas students participating in the structured AI-supported intervention demonstrated higher levels of academic writing performance
rationale: Abstract describes an AI (ChatGPT) writing intervention with a control group and performance outcomes compared via Mann-Whitney and Wilcoxon tests, so intervention, comparison, population and outcome appear met or unclear. Domain is EFL academic writing, which is a non-STEM content area under the protocol (language learning excluded), which would point to E2. However, the abstract does not fully settle whether the content is STEM-adjacent, and the design (case study mixed methods, quasi-experimental status) is unclear. Given the abstract-stage rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, I am not excluding; flagging for full-text check of domain (E2 likely).

quote: Employing a correlational-predictive design, data were collected from 35 seventh-semester students who had completed a teaching practicum.
rationale: The study is a correlational-predictive survey of attitudes toward CRT-GenAI integration, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (the 4-point Likert attitude measure is affective). It also concerns EFL teaching (language learning, non-STEM domain). Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the outcome failure; E3 (no control group) and domain issues would also apply, but the primary failure is the absence of a learning outcome. Abstract stage: positive evidence of design and outcome failure is present.

quote: Now artificial intelligence aims to use technology, especially computer systems, to simulate human intelligence processes; it draws conclusions from data, understands content, learns independently, and even interacts with people.
rationale: The abstract is a general discussion of learning beyond textbooks, data analysis, AI, and constructivism. It describes no study, no design, no participants, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It gives positive evidence that the record is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Note that E6 is applied here as the first applicable code under the protocol order, but the code order runs E1 to E5 first; the abstract gives no positive evidence for E1 through E5 failing, so E6 is the earliest code with positive support.
rationale_note: Abstract lacks any empirical design; no study described.

rationale: Title indicates AI-based grading in language education. Language learning is explicitly excluded from the STEM domain criterion, so E2 applies. Also, AI used only for grading would fail the intervention criterion (E1), but E2 is the first applicable code in the stated order only if ordered earlier; E1 precedes E2 in the protocol. Note: under strict code order, AI used only for grading is not learner-facing generative AI (E1) and should be considered first. The record is excluded on the basis of the evident non-STEM content with no abstract available to confirm other criteria. The abstract is not available, so this decision rests on the title alone and should be verified at full text if the reviewer disagrees.

quote: Matteo Pasquinelli distinguishes The Eye of the Master from other recent monographs on automation and labor by offering a “social history of artificial intelligence.”
rationale: This record is a book review of Pasquinelli's monograph The Eye of the Master, not an empirical study. It describes no learners, no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The E1 check is not applicable as no learner-facing intervention is described. The record text is garbled in places but contains no instructions addressed to a reviewer or AI system.

quote: Using a qualitative descriptive methodology, structured interviews were applied to 76 students from six educational programs of the Faculty of Law and Social Sciences
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive interview study of student perceptions, with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no domain that is STEM (Law and Social Sciences). It is not an empirical experimental design meeting the protocol, so it is excluded. E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense) is the best-fitting code for a qualitative perception study; the earlier-ordered codes E1-E5 are not clearly established from the abstract alone, but E2 (non-STEM content) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 is not positively shown, E2 is the first clear failure since the content is Law and Social Sciences, so the code should be E2 instead.

quote: Dear Editor, A recent issue entitled 'Chat generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) educates college students about sexual violence and its impact on their mental health: a proposal'
rationale: This is an editorial/letter (Dear Editor) that discusses sexual violence and mental health in college students. It reports no empirical study, no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Not STEM content either. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order; E1 would also apply on intervention grounds, but the record is a commentary with no intervention evaluated, so E6 is the primary reason.

quote: Hasil dari pelatihan menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan ChatGPT memberikan manfaat yang signifikan bagi siswa/i.
rationale: Community service training for vocational high school students on ChatGPT use. The abstract reports only questionnaire responses (satisfaction/perceptions) from 22 trainees, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design (no control group, pre-post or descriptive only) and outcome (perceptions only), so excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in order per the protocol's listing (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply. Reporting the first code in protocol order as E3 is the nearest match given the absence of any comparison group.

quote: We conducted 63 individual interviews with fifth- and sixth-graders (between 10 and 12 years old) living in the inner city of Montréal
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of a contextualised outdoor science curriculum. Nothing in the abstract indicates any generative AI tool, a control group, or a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E1 applies first because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. The design is also qualitative (would fail E3/E5/E6 as well), but E1 is reported as the first applicable code.

criteria.quote: Using a cross-sectional survey, the proposed model was tested with SmartPLS (PLS-SEM)
criteria.rationale: Cross-sectional survey measuring acceptance/behavioral intention (perceptions), with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. E5 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is clearly positive from the abstract; E3 (no control group) and E6 (not empirical) would also be arguable, but the survey is clearly empirical, so the outcome failure is the primary reason stated here. Population (pre-service teachers, higher education) is met.

quote: Thirteen teachers from SMK Permas Jaya 2 and ten from SIJB participated in this community service program
rationale: Community service mentoring program with pretest and post-test of a single group of in-service teachers (no control group, single-group pre-post design). Fails comparison and design criteria; participants are in-service teachers, not students (population not met). Also the content is digital literacy rather than clearly STEM. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in the order, since there is no control group without generative AI. The population exclusion (E4) also applies, but E3 is listed first.

The study concerns Japanese language teaching materials generated by LLM-based GAI, with topics of pop culture (idols, fashion, manga). Japanese language learning is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also reports evaluation of text quality (difficulty, accuracy) rather than a learning outcome in a controlled comparison, and no control group is described. Only the first applicable code is reported, which is E2.

quote: Sixty-two graduate students at Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah University (Fez) completed an online qualitative survey (Oct 2024-Feb 2025) comprising seven open-ended questions
rationale: The study is a qualitative survey of student accounts about generative AI feedback for English learning. English language learning is non-STEM (E2 would apply), but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is absent; the stronger positive evidence is that there is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, and the design is qualitative. Per protocol order, E1 is not clearly established (generative AI use is described), E2 applies to content (English language learning is explicitly non-STEM). Given the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E2 is the earliest clear failure among the listed codes that applies to the content; however, E2 precedes E3 and E5 in the order, so the decision is coded E2 as the first clearly failed criterion. Stated as exclude with the single code E2 applied.

quote: The program evaluation shows that the majority of students found the application engaging and easy to use, and that it significantly assisted them in determining suitable majors for their higher education.
rationale: Community service program describing implementation of a web-based AI recommendation system for choosing majors and universities; not a STEM learning activity and no control group is described. The evaluation reports perceptions (engaging, easy to use) rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and it is a community service report rather than a controlled empirical study. Excluded at the first applicable code in order; E6 (not an empirical study) is the most defensible code given the program-implementation design with no comparison group. Domain (E2) also clearly fails, so the exclusion is supported on multiple grounds.

quote: A complementary student pilot study provided preliminary evidence of positive learning gains and user receptivity.
rationale: The main evaluation is educator-rated quality of AI-generated materials, where the AI is used by educators to prepare content, which would fall under E1 if that were the only use. A student pilot with learning gains is mentioned, but the abstract does not describe its design, control group, or statistics. The STEM component (Numerical Methods) is present alongside a non-STEM course. Because the abstract does not clearly show a failed criterion and the student pilot may meet the criteria, the record is unsure and should be checked at full text, mainly for whether students interacted with the generative AI and whether a control group exists.

quote: The author proposes a conditional periodization of the academic workplace evolution - from version 1.0 (1950s) to version 5.0 (since 2020)
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/essay-style paper: a proposed periodization of the instructor workplace, drawing on literature and personal experience, with a case description of automated grading by an LLM. There is no comparison group, no controlled design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails the protocol's empirical design requirement (E6). Note that the record is in Russian and the paper's own abstract does not show a learner-facing comparison.

quote: An artefact-based qualitative analysis was conducted on eight de-identified group submissions
rationale: The study is a qualitative artefact-based analysis of eight group submissions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the exclusion order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code at the abstract stage; the absence of a quantitative outcome (E5) also applies but E3 is reported first. Note that E3 is coded here on the basis of the abstract's described qualitative design, which gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: We also include expanded benchmarking experiments, including human expert evaluations and ablation studies, to assess model performance and learning outcomes.
rationale: LLM-based virtual AI teacher used by students to analyze their math draft errors and hold multi-round dialogues, so the intervention appears learner-facing generative AI and the domain is mathematics. The abstract mentions learning outcomes and "improves student learning efficiency" but does not show a control group, a comparison design, or the statistics needed for an SMD. Also, "expanded benchmarking" and "model accuracy" suggest technical evaluation, which may not be an empirical learning study with a control group. Missing information is not evidence of exclusion, so this is unsure pending full text, where the comparison design and whether a learning outcome with a control group exists should be checked.

quote: Conference Code: OP-158: Perception and experiences of undergraduate medical students on new CBME curriculum
rationale: This record is a compilation of many conference abstracts (National Journal of Pharmacology and Therapeutics conference proceedings, NAPTICON-2025), not a single journal article. Most entries are perception surveys or non-generative interventions, and none report a control-group comparison with generative AI. The only AI-related entry (OP-304 flip class with AI tool) is unclear on design and outcome and is mostly unreadable. Under the protocol, conference abstracts are not eligible publication types (E10), and the record also fails E1/E3/E5 on the entries that are readable. Coded E6 as the record is not an empirical journal article reporting a single eligible study; the ordering rule makes E1 the first applicable code only where intervention is clearly non-generative, which is not established for every entry. Note for auditor: E10 may be the more accurate code given the conference-abstract publication type; I selected E6 because the record is a multi-abstract compilation rather than a single publication.

quote: Through qualitative analysis, findings reaffirm relevance of the three original strategies
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative analysis of digital curation on Wikimedia platforms, not an experiment with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design requirements. GenAI is mentioned only as context for the framework, not as a learner-facing intervention. Exclusion at the first applicable code: E1 is arguably applicable too (no learner-facing GenAI tool evident), but the clearest positive evidence is the qualitative, non-experimental design, which falls under E6 as not an empirical study meeting the protocol's design criteria.

quote: The case study examined PSTs in a South Korean university course who were tasked with creating lesson plans using generative AI
rationale: The study is a case study with thematic analysis of qualitative data. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is EFL (non-STEM). It is not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design. Coded E6 as the first clearly applicable code for a non-experimental case study; E2 (non-STEM) and E3 (no control) would also apply. Under the code ordering, E1 does not apply because learners did use generative AI. Note that E2 precedes E6 in the protocol ordering, so the first applicable code by strict order is E2 (EFL content is not STEM), and the decision should be corrected to E2 if the auditor applies the order strictly.

quote: Integrating prompt engineering into the transversal skills for language education: a case study
rationale: The study is about academic writing in language education (Italian language learning), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also does not describe a control group or a quantitative learning outcome, but the domain failure is the first applicable code in protocol order and is sufficient on its own.

quote: A quantitative relational survey model was used. The sample consisted of 220 teachers from public high schools.
rationale: Correlational survey of teachers' digital literacy and subjective well-being. No generative AI intervention, no control group, and participants are in-service teachers rather than students. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since no generative AI tool is involved at all. Note that the code order in the protocol places E1 first, so E1 is the correct code rather than E6; the design is also not an experiment. Excluded on the basis of the abstract.

criteria.criteria_note: fields are assessed on abstract evidence

quote: The primary results suggested that the prompts could be used for vocabulary-in-context learning and have potential for use in language teaching.
rationale: Content is Vietnamese language learning, which is non-STEM (E2). The study is also action research with five learners and reflections-based thematic analysis, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are in-service teachers. Any of these would exclude; E2 is reported first in the protocol order.

quote: This study aims to examine the quality assurance (QA) landscape of Vietnam's legal education through a content analysis of institutional and program-level accreditation reports
rationale: The study is a document content analysis of accreditation reports, not an empirical learning intervention with a control group. It has no generative AI intervention learners interact with (AI such as NotebookLM and ChatGPT was used by researchers for data extraction), no comparison group, no learning outcome, and the domain is legal education, not STEM. Per the protocol's order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first applicable code; however, the core failure is that it is not an experimental empirical study. Applying the code order, E1 applies first since generative AI is used only by researchers for analysis, not by learners.

quote: A qualitative case-study design drew on classroom observation, field notes, reflective notes, semi-structured interviews, students’ writing activities, and coded interview data.
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study of nine EFL students using DeepSeek AI. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the content is English language writing, not STEM. The design is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the protocol, so E6 (not an empirical study per protocol design) is the applicable code; the first applicable code in order is E2 (non-STEM content). Under the protocol order, E2 applies first because the domain is English language learning, which is not STEM.

quote: Participants were not randomly assigned to conditions, and the absence of a control group makes it difficult to isolate the specific effects of AI tools.
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a one-group pretest/posttest design with no control group, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion (E3). Academic writing tasks are also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on E3 based on the explicit statement of no control group and one-group pre-post design.
outcome_note: Performance measured via pre/post tests but not clearly quantitative learning outcome

rationale: The study evaluates AIGC detection tools' accuracy on student work; learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). It also has no control group with a learning outcome and no SMD-type data, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well, but E1 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract evidence is sufficient for exclusion.

Survey-based study (questionnaire of 235 research scholars, regression of behavioral intention). No experimental or comparison-group design, and the outcome is behavioral intention/adoption perception rather than a quantitative learning measure. Excluded at the first applicable code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also fails the comparison and design criteria, but the rule is to report the first code that applies in order. Note: the rule order places E3 before E5 for comparison failure; however, the outcome failure is clear from the abstract. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no learning outcome.

quote: The article is dedicated to researching the role of creativity and digital technologies in the development of language education in higher education institutions
rationale: Abstract describes a language and literature teaching context (language learning is explicitly excluded from the STEM domain), and it reads as a conceptual/pedagogical article with a scenario "pedagogically analyzed" rather than a controlled experiment with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of non-STEM content is present, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order; design and outcome evidence also appear absent.

quote: Artificial intelligence tools for the development of writing skills in English language learning
rationale: The study concerns English as a Foreign Language writing, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies. It is also a pre-experimental single-group design with no control group (E3 would also apply), but E2 is the first applicable code in order. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.
rationale_note: Ordering rule: E1 not applicable (ChatGPT is generative and learner-used); E2 applies first.

quote: Pedagogical conversational agents (PCAs)—generative AI-powered virtual characters trained to converse with students like a teacher—offer promising solutions that could extend to SEL.
rationale: The content is social-emotional learning (SEL), which is not science, math, statistics, engineering, computer science, or data science, so it fails the STEM domain criterion (E2). The study also compares a PCA with human educators facilitating SEL with a static AI child, and the outcomes are coded dialogue quality rather than clearly a learning measure, so further criteria are uncertain. The domain failure is sufficient for exclusion at the first applicable code. Note that the first-applicable code rule applies at fulltext; at abstract stage the exclusion rests on positive evidence that the content is not STEM.

quote: The Editorial Process A manuscript will be reviewed for possible publication with the understanding that it is being submitted to Journal of the Anatomical Society of India alone at that point in time
rationale: The record is the journal's "Instructions to Author" page, not a research article. It describes no intervention, comparison, population, or outcome. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Its text contains no instruction directed at an AI system, so no injection is suspected.

quote: The findings demonstrate that Moodle API integration facilitates the real-time automation of grade retrieval per sub-CLO.
rationale: The abstract describes a design-science development of an OBE monitoring system (Moodle API and OpenAI API for faculty documentation drafting). The generative AI is used by faculty to draft RPS documents, not by learners in a learning activity (E1 would apply). No control group, no learning outcome measure, and no empirical comparison is described. Under the rule of the protocol's code order, E1 is the first applicable code: the AI is not learner-facing. Excluding on E1 is the correct first code.

quote: This practice-oriented applied literature review addresses this challenge by synthesizing two established frameworks
rationale: The record is an applied literature review that synthesizes frameworks (deep work, self-regulated learning) and develops strategies. It is not an empirical study: there is no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in protocol order that is clearly evidenced; E1 and E3 are not positively established from the abstract alone, but the review design itself is decisive.

quote: This year's Perspectives column delves into these pressing concerns.
rationale: The record is a journal Perspectives column introducing a set of commentaries on generative AI and language education. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Language learning is also non-STEM content, which would independently fail the domain criterion. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention were learner-facing AI, which the abstract does not establish; the editorial nature of the piece makes E6 the clearest first failing code, though E2 would also apply.

quote: The results are fascinating: the provisioning time including all VCL background tasks is always less than a minute and utilizes fewer computing resources while providing a better user experience.
rationale: Abstract reports system performance benchmarks (provisioning time, resource use, HTTP load tests) with 30 users, not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or skill performance. No control group with a comparison is described. The generative component (GPT-3.5 terminal tool) is present but its role is secondary to the infrastructure evaluation. Excluded under E5 as no quantitative learning outcome is reported; design (no comparison group, performance evaluation) also appears not to meet criteria.

quote: we also examined how 55 students' holistic reading of socio-scientific texts on climate change in a ChatGPT scenario changes after a reading-science intervention
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory study of students' reading performance on ChatGPT-generated texts, with a pre/post change after a reading-science intervention in one group. No separate control group without generative AI is described, and the design appears to be a single-group pre-post comparison, which is E3 per the protocol. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that no comparison group exists; the abstract does not mention any control condition. Although the study is in junior secondary STEM-adjacent science education (climate science), the population and domain criteria are met.

quote: Through the verification of the development case of junior high school physics intelligence three-dimensional textbook, the study found that
rationale: The abstract describes a framework and a development case of an AI textbook, with no control group, comparison, or quantitative learning outcome reported. It reads as a conceptual/design paper rather than an empirical comparative study. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the best fit on the abstract's positive evidence; the design-and-framework nature is clear. Note that the "verification" is a development case, not a controlled experiment, so no comparison group is evident.

quote: Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using t-tests, ANOVA, Pearson's correlation coefficients, and hierarchical regression analysis
rationale: The study is a survey-based correlational design (questionnaires, regression) with no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition, and the outcome is intention to use AI (a perception/affective measure), not a learning outcome. No intervention comparison is described. Excluded at abstract stage on E3 as the lack of a comparison group is positively evidenced; the design is also not experimental. Nursing is a health profession, and the domain is not clearly STEM, so this is a further concern.

quote: Descriptive correlation research design was adopted.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive correlational design among 200 nursing students with no control group receiving or not receiving generative AI. Correlational designs are excluded by the Design criterion, and the absence of a comparison group yields E3. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design, so exclusion at the abstract stage is justified. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) was not the first applicable code because it was not clearly established from the abstract; E3 is the most direct failure of the comparison criterion.

quote: This digital poster provides insights into the project, covering its development process, trial outcomes, challenges encountered, and future directions
rationale: The record is a digital poster (ASCILITE Publications, conference-type output), which is an ineligible publication type under the protocol (posters, work in progress excluded). It also describes a project/tool evaluation with staff as reviewers, and the abstract gives no clear controlled comparison of learners with versus without generative AI. Exclusion is on publication type, the first applicable code in order that is evident from the abstract.

quote: Through conceptual analysis and theoretical synthesis methods, the study has translated the ethical knowledge domain from abstract principles into mandatory ethical checkpoints
rationale: The paper is a conceptual/theoretical proposal of an instructional design process (EE-AID) for lecturers, built through conceptual analysis and theoretical synthesis. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Population is university lecturers (in-service teachers), which also falls outside the protocol. Exclusion at E6 is the first applicable code in the order that fits the abstract's positive evidence.
rationale_note: Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical design.

quote: This article reviews the current status of relevant education at home and abroad, analyzes major problems, and proposes suggestions for curriculum and training reform
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative review/position article on medical education and clinical research training. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome measure. This is not an empirical study (E6). Generative AI is mentioned only as background context, and the domain is clinical research training rather than STEM learning with a generative AI intervention.

quote: Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery holds the position that the use of ChatGPT and other AI models should not be encouraged, nor should they be included as an author on scientific articles.
rationale: This is an editorial/commentary on ChatGPT in plastic surgery research. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Its domain (plastic surgery research) is also not STEM-learning related and it has no learner-facing intervention. E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits the record's nature.

quote: This practice-based study proposes a Human-AI Co-Creation Model for visual communication education and reports its classroom implementation
rationale: Abstract describes a practice-based framework and classroom implementation with instructor field notes, critique artifacts, rubrics and reflections. No separate control group without generative AI is described, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Visual communication/graphic design is not clearly STEM either, but E3 is the first applicable code in the order given.

quote: the impact of pre-service teachers' development of performance tasks utilizing differentiated generative artificial intelligence tools
rationale: The study measures only attitudes toward generative AI and acceptance levels, which are affective/perception outcomes not extracted under the protocol; no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Excluded on E5. Domain (STEM content of performance tasks) is not evident from the abstract but is not needed for the decision.

quote: This paper focuses on the in-depth exploration and practice of innovation programs for college students in the context of new engineering disciplines, combined with the current development trend of generative AI technology.
rationale: Abstract mentions generative AI in the context of college students' innovation and entrepreneurship projects, but does not say learners interact with a generative AI tool, nor describes a control group, a research design, a quantitative learning outcome, or effect sizes. The study's discipline (innovation and entrepreneurship, new engineering) is not clearly STEM content. Abstract gives no positive evidence of a failed criterion, so it is advanced to full text for checking the intervention, comparison, design, and outcome.

The record is an opinion/editorial-style piece on AI in scientific publishing and ChatGPT's societal implications. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Under the abstract rule, the exclusion rests on the abstract describing a discussion piece rather than an empirical design. No passage gives a verbatim quote for the non-empirical nature beyond the general framing, so quote is null.

quote: Using a sample of 26 master's-level students in a course on AI's societal aspects, this study examines the impact of (1) prior knowledge and attitudes toward technology and learning, and (2) personal value orientations.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/regression study of 26 master's students using GenAI for game design, with no separate control group that avoids GenAI. Analyses examine associations between individual attributes and outcomes, not a comparison between groups. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3. Design also appears correlational, which the protocol excludes. Note the abstract stage rule would normally favor unsure, but the abstract clearly describes a single-sample correlational design with no control condition.

quote: Drawing on classroom experience and student feedback, we argue that grounded inquiry sharpens judgement in Earth science teaching
rationale: The abstract describes an argumentative/opinion piece drawing on classroom experience and student feedback, with no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study with a controlled design, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Earth science is STEM, but the empirical criteria clearly fail.

The record has only a title and venue; no abstract is available. The title suggests a conceptual framework for designed AI withdrawal in higher education, which may not be an empirical study (E6), but this cannot be confirmed from the record. Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: This conceptual paper presents a design framework for developing pre-service Physics teachers' TSPCK through the strategic integration of AI tools within a methodology course.
rationale: The abstract describes itself as a conceptual paper that presents a design framework and synthesizes existing evidence. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Domain (physics) and population (pre-service teachers, higher education) would fit, but the paper fails on design and outcome.

quote: The research is structured into two parts: a questionnaire-based investigation and interviews.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire and interview investigation of educators' perspectives, with no experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome in learners. It is not an empirical controlled study meeting the design criteria. Participants are teachers (not students), and the outcome is perception-based. Coded E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design); the first applicable code in order would be E1 or E3 at most, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey/interview design with no learner outcome, so E6 is the best fit at abstract stage.

quote: Errol, I know that I am like many, many online instructors when it comes to artificial intelligence (AI): somewhat lost, a bit confused and with a ton of questions.
rationale: The record is an advice-column piece ("Ask Errol") answering an instructor's questions about ChatGPT and holiday recognition in an online Criminal Justice/Economics course. It is not an empirical study: no experiment, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The E6 code is applied on the basis of the abstract text alone, which describes a column rather than a study.

quote: The purpose of this quantitative research was to identify the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool and its influences on the self-esteem and academic performance
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based quantitative study using questionnaires with no described experimental or quasi-experimental design and no separate control group without AI; it compares users by university type and program rather than assigning an intervention. Design is survey/correlational, which fails the Design criterion. Exclusion code assigned is E6 (not an empirical experimental study) per the protocol's design-based exclusion; the AI tool is not specified as generative, and STEM content is not clear. Given the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental survey design, exclusion is appropriate.

quote: Using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) methodology, 21 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2022 and 2025 were identified and analyzed through qualitative thematic synthesis.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review (PRISMA, qualitative thematic synthesis of 21 studies), not an empirical primary study. It has no control group or quantitative outcome of its own. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Its own text is the basis for the decision; it was not treated as an included primary study.

quote: EFL undergraduate students in the Hospital Administration program
rationale: The intervention is ChatGPT used as a conversational partner (generative AI, learner-facing), with a control group and pre/post oral tests. However, the content is English as a foreign language speaking skills, which is language learning and not STEM. The protocol excludes language learning and other non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The Hospital Administration program is only the student's major, not the learning content.

quote: Participants were 37 PSTs enrolled in a technology integration in instruction course in the Spring 2025 semester.
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 37 preservice teachers measured with pre- and post-intervention surveys and lesson plan rubric scores, with no control group that lacks generative AI. This matches the E3 pattern (single-group pre-post design). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a single-group design. Note: the record's Venue and Year (2026) are noted; the publication-type and date criteria are not evaluated further since E3 applies first in the code order (E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing; the domain is lesson planning for preservice teachers, which is not clearly STEM).

quote: The method used is a quantitative approach by collecting data through questionnaires distributed to 54 students class of 2022.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of students' behavior with ChatGPT, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is survey-only, so it is not an empirical experimental study eligible under the protocol. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense); the survey design also fails the comparison and outcome criteria. Domain is library and information science, which is not clearly STEM. Exclusion at the abstract stage is supported by positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group and no learning outcome.

quote: The research was carried out using the methods of scientific cognition commonly accepted in Russia: general scientific (dialectical) method and specific scientific methods
rationale: Theoretical/legal-analysis article on ChatGPT use in juridical science. No experimental or comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and not an empirical study. Domain is law, which is not STEM. Exclusion code E6 is the first code that applies on the protocol's ordering, because the record is a non-empirical analysis. Under the rule order, E2 (non-STEM) could also be argued; E6 is reported as the primary reason since the design is non-empirical.

Abstract describes a methodology and architecture for GPT-4-based competency matching and gap analysis over academic programs, job vacancies, and 286 students' documents. It reports no control group or comparison condition without generative AI, and no learning outcome measured in learners. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion at E3. The intervention is also not clearly learner-facing (GPT-4 processes documents for analysis), but the comparison failure is the clearest ground. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the abstract lacks any control arm.

quote: Qualitative findings further highlighted the value of artificial intelligence applications, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google Translate
rationale: Content is English language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study is also a descriptive-correlational survey with perception-based measures and no control group, which would fail E3, E5, and design criteria. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the domain criterion fails.

quote: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of artificial intelligence-powered automated grading systems (AI AGSs) in STEM education
rationale: Review article, not an empirical study.

quote: To assess current state of artificial intelligence (AI) within occupational therapy (OT) practice, education, and research
rationale: Project description of a needs assessment and student resource development in occupational therapy, a health professions field, with no controlled comparison, no learning outcome, and no experimental design described. Health professions education is outside the STEM domain. The record is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of design, domain, and outcome failure. Coding E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the order given is a judgment call, since E2 (not STEM) is listed earlier and arguably applies first. Auditor should check: the protocol's order places E2 before E6, so E2 may be the more correct code.

quote: A total of 1186 articles published between 1977 and 2025 and indexed in the Scopus database were analyzed using machine learning‐based semantic topic modeling and descriptive analysis.
rationale: This is a bibliometric topic-modeling review of 1186 Scopus articles, not an empirical study of learners interacting with generative AI. It has no control group, no learning outcome, and is not an eligible empirical design. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Per the protocol's order, E1 is not applied because the record does not describe a learner-facing intervention to assess.

quote: The overall suitability of the curriculum was rated at the highest level with a mean of M = 4.91 and a standard deviation of SD = 0.19.
rationale: Development and expert-validation study (R&D) of a prototype course curriculum. Abstract reports needs survey and expert suitability ratings only; there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the study cannot meet the comparison, design, or outcome criteria. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order, since there is no control group without generative AI. Also, the record's stage is abstract, so exclusion is supported by positive evidence of missing comparator. No injection detected.

quote: Our study was conducted in the province of Québec, Canada, which resulted in 116 students experiencing the same educational intervention from home.
rationale: The abstract describes an outdoor place-based educational intervention with no indication of any generative AI tool. Students were interviewed by telephone; no AI is mentioned. Intervention criterion positively fails, so E1 applies. Comparison is between two delay groups (one week vs two months) with no non-AI control described, but E1 takes precedence as the first applicable code.

quote: over 150 language teachers co-developed AI-empowered TPACK for corpus technology (AI-TPACK-CT) during online professional development
rationale: Participants are in-service language teachers in professional development, not K-12 or higher education students. Content is language teaching, not STEM. The design is a mixed-methods study with CoI/SNA and case studies, with no control group described. Exclusion is on population (E4), the first applicable code in order would be E1 for intervention, but the abstract does not clearly establish whether the AI is learner-facing; the population and domain failures are clear positive evidence, so E4 is reported as the primary code.
rationale_note: Code order: E1 was not clearly failed at abstract stage; E2 (non-STEM) and E4 (in-service teachers) are clearly failed.

quote: The proposed solution successfully improved teachers' digital skills, with average scores increasing from 62 to 85, and students' digital literacy from 65 to 85.
rationale: This is a community service program reporting pre-post changes in scores with no control group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. It is a community service report rather than a controlled empirical study. Domain is not clearly STEM (general digital literacy at an elementary madrasah). Excluded at abstract stage on E6 as not an empirical comparative study; a single-group pre-post design also meets E3 per the borderline rules, but E6 is the earliest applicable code in the protocol's ordering only if the study is not empirical, so this is a judgment call that the auditor should check.
rationale_note: Note: the first applicable code under the protocol order is arguably E2 (domain unclear, not STEM) or E3 (single-group pre-post). Auditor should verify.

quote: A total of 48 students majoring in English education completed a FIT-Choice-based survey.
rationale: The study is a survey of career motivations among pre-service English teachers, with regression on perceptions. It has no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome; it is also non-STEM (English education). Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first code that clearly applies in the required order, with the survey design and English-language content also failing other criteria. Note that the order rule would have E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) checked first; the abstract does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool, so E1 is arguably the first applicable code. Reporting E1 would be more faithful to the order.

quote: The case studies underscore common themes, such as the democratization of creative tools through AI, the necessity for critical AI literacy
rationale: The study concerns Communication Design courses (Digital Culture and Sociology of Media), which are not STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a comparative analysis of case studies with no indication of a control group or quantitative learning outcome, so the design and comparison criteria appear unmet as well, but E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.
