quote: This article reviews the existing initiatives at global, regional and local level, promoted by Governments, companies and civil society organizations, on Artificial Intelligence education in the school education system
rationale: The abstract describes a review of existing national and institutional AI education initiatives, not an empirical study. There is no intervention with learners interacting with a generative AI tool, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measured. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). This is a clear positive failure of the design criterion, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The study uses a quasi-experimental design with two groups: the experimental group, which receives PJBL-AI-based learning, and the control group, which follows conventional learning based on lectures and guided discussions.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experiment with a conventional-learning control group, generative AI (ChatGPT, Canva AI) used by students within PJBL, and a critical thinking posttest outcome in university students (PJKR program). Domain is the main uncertainty: the study is in Physical Education, Health, and Recreation, which is not clearly STEM (not science, math, engineering, CS, or data science) and the protocol does not list PE as eligible; the abstract also does not clearly indicate a computable SMD (only posttest means reported, no SDs). Not excluded at abstract stage because no positive evidence of failure is stated for the criteria; flagged for fulltext check on domain and effect-size data.

quote: This study investigates the feasibility of using chatbots as a content-based English learning and teaching tool.
rationale: The study is about English language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM content (E2). It also appears to be an expert questionnaire rating of chatbots, with no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in the specified order.
rationale_note: Other codes likely also apply (E3, E5), but E2 is first in order.

quote: The study found that students generally rated the effectiveness of AI higher than physicians did
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions and experiences among doctors and medical students, with no learning intervention and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is health professions education (E2 could also apply), and there is no control group. Per the code order, E1 is not clearly positive from the abstract, so the first clearly applicable code is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and usage reported).
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence: outcomes are perceptions and usage only.

quote: the study gathered 400 valid responses from English-language students studying at various universities
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using Technology Acceptance Model and SEM on 400 responses. It has no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome (only intention to use). Domain is English language learning, which is non-STEM. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical experimental study in the eligible design sense; survey design is excluded by the Design row). Under the code order, E1 does not apply (ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI), E2 applies first because English language learning is non-STEM content. Therefore the first applicable code is E2.

quote: The primary goal of this research paper is to compare AI tools’ performance with students’ performance through experiments on the final examination tests in the accounting program.
rationale: The study compares AI models' scores against students' exam scores in an accounting program. Accounting is not STEM content, so E2 would apply. The AI models were tested directly on exam questions rather than used by learners as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group of students without generative AI. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, the first applicable code is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since the AI was not used by learners in a learning activity. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for E1 and for non-STEM content, so this is excluded. Population also appears not to be a student sample. The code is set to E1 as the first failing criterion in order; the abstract also gives clear evidence of a non-STEM domain.

quote: "During a session on artificial intelligence (AI) in oncology, speakers who serve as members of NCCN's working group on AI discussed the potential benefits and risks of this emerging technology."
rationale: This is a Oncology Times news article reporting on a conference, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM learning content, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that fits; the E1 concern (no learner-facing gen AI) is also present but E1 is checked first in order. Note: under the protocol's stated order, E1 would be the first code to apply because the record describes no learner-facing generative AI tool, so the correct first-applicable code is E1.

quote: course teaching material was developed using a prompt engineering strategy, predefined standards, and a prompt script
rationale: ChatGPT is used by instructors/designers to create teaching materials, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. No control group, no learning outcome reported; the abstract describes content creation and time/cost efficiency. Excluded under E1 (AI used only by teacher to prepare materials). Exclusion code E1 is the first applicable in order.

quote: In this presentation, Dr Thomas Lancaster will examine how far work on academic integrity can be faked.
rationale: The record is a conference presentation (Canadian Perspectives on Academic Integrity), not a journal article, so it fails the publication-type criterion (E10). It also describes case studies and demonstrations rather than a randomized or comparison-group study with a learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5, and E6 as well. Only the first applicable code is reported, per protocol order: E1 cannot be confirmed as not met from the abstract, so the ordering places E10 as the reported code only if no earlier code applies; given the abstract gives no learner-facing intervention or comparison group, this is a judgement at abstract stage, and the publication-type failure is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: Goliath, one of the two main contributions of this article, is a template-based, Artificial Intelligence (AI) supported exercise generator
rationale: The abstract describes a tool (Goliath) for educators to generate programming exercises, with AI support, and a set of CLT-based guidelines for template creation. Learners do not interact with the tool; it is used by educators to create materials, which is E1-type. However, the rule to use E1 is for AI used only by teacher to prepare materials, and the protocol says report the first code that applies in order, with E1 first. Since the abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is teacher-facing material preparation, E1 would be the first applicable code. The article also has no comparison group, no learning outcome, and is a tool/guidelines description rather than an empirical learner study, so E6 is also plausible. Following the code order, the first applicable code is E1.

quote: Guidelines for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Manuscript Preparation and Review
rationale: This is an editorial/guidelines piece on AI use in manuscript preparation and peer review. It is not an empirical study, has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits; E1 would also arguably apply since AI is not used by learners in a learning activity, but the record is fundamentally a non-empirical editorial, so E6 is the primary reason.

quote: Implementing this approach with 105 business statistics students at a university in the USA, statistical tests demonstrated significant improvement in student performance on customized quizzes compared to traditional assessments.
rationale: Abstract indicates ChatGPT is used to generate personalized quiz questions, but it is unclear whether learners interact with the generative tool itself or only teachers/system generate quizzes; the intervention criterion (learner-facing) cannot be determined. Comparison is described as 'traditional assessments', which may or may not be a control group without generative AI; design is not stated. Domain (business statistics) and population (university students) appear to fit, and a quantitative performance outcome is reported. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so advance to full text to check learner-facing use, control group, and effect size data.

quote: The article provides a review of current scientific research on AI integration in technical higher education institutions
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/review article with practical recommendations. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Domain (computer networks, computer science students) and population (higher education) are met. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing criterion in order that is positively evidenced; E1 was not used because generative AI (ChatGPT) use by students is discussed but the study design itself is non-empirical.

quote: A qualitative case study was conducted with thirty pre-service teachers enrolled in a Bachelor of Education programme.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative single case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not a comparative design. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order for a study lacking a comparison group without generative AI. Note that E3 precedes E5 in the protocol order, and the design is also not a randomized or quasi-experimental design, so the exclusion is clear from the abstract alone.

quote: This study examines the influence of ChatGPT usage on the reading interest of students in the Economic Education Study Program
rationale: Correlational survey design (simple linear regression on Likert questionnaire) with no separate control group. Outcome is reading interest, an affective measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is economic education reading rather than STEM. Excluded under E5 as the primary failing criterion, with no comparison group and non-STEM content also failing. Exclusion code assigned per the protocol order: E1 cannot be confirmed as not met from the abstract alone, and E2 and E3 also apply, but E5 is the clearest positive evidence of failure on the outcome.

quote: "This video narrates the contribution of Dr. Katherine Johnson to NASA and rocket science"
rationale: The abstract describes a video narrative about rocket science history within a MOOC. Nothing indicates learners interact with a generative AI tool; the intervention is a non-AI instructional video. Excluded under E1 (not learner-facing generative AI). Other criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract, but E1 is sufficient.

quote: This paper, based on the author's experience, discusses the five-year trajectory of the GIGA School Program, changes in educational settings, and future prospects.
rationale: The abstract describes an experience-based discussion paper with no empirical design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract, not by missing information. No generative AI learner intervention or STEM content is described beyond a general mention of utilizing generative AI.

The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of 733 Spanish majors with factor analysis, correlations, and regressions on self-reported AI usage behaviors. There is no randomized or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first positive failure at abstract stage, with E3 chosen because no control group exists. Domain is unclear (Spanish language learning is not STEM, which would be a stronger exclusion), but that is not needed given the design failure.

quote: The purposes of this study were to describe US social work students' use, attitudes, and knowledge regarding social media and to compare these findings with a Fall 2019 national study.
rationale: The study is a national survey of social work students about social media use, attitudes, and knowledge, compared across two survey waves. It involves no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measure. Survey designs are excluded. Under the exclusion order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first; but the code chosen here is E3 because the core failure is the absence of any control group, and the abstract mentions AI only in a parenthetical list of social media forms. Note: the code is arguably E1 under strict first-failing-code ordering, so the auditor should check this.

criteria.population_note: medical education; not STEM domain clearly

quote: Both cohorts diverged significantly from census benchmarks (p < 0.0001 for every variable).
rationale: The study is a model-output audit: LLMs generate 250 synthetic UK patient profiles, compared against census figures. No learners interact with the AI, there is no control group, and no learning outcome is measured. It is not an empirical study of learners, so it fails on multiple criteria. Coded E6 as a non-learning empirical audit (the first applicable code in the order is arguably E1, since the intervention is not learner-facing, but the protocol's E6 category best reflects a non-educational model-output analysis). Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

quote: Two revelatory new books (Eddy, 2023; Roberts, 2024) from outside the field zero in on communication as a kind of mechanic art
rationale: This is an essay/review-style commentary on two books about historical notetaking and printmaking. It is not an empirical study: no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, no STEM learners. The record fails E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order when checking E1 onward: E1 is arguably not met because generative AI is only discussed conceptually, not used by learners, so E1 would be the first code strictly in order. Note: under strict order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first since no learner interacts with generative AI in this record. Coding as E1 would be the protocol-ordered choice.

quote: The article provides a thorough analysis and systematization of key conceptual approaches to the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical analysis and systematization of approaches, not an empirical study. No control group, design, or quantitative learning outcome is reported. This is a non-empirical article, so E6 applies. Exclusion is justified on positive evidence from the abstract itself.

quote: Recently, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in the educational field has sparked interest and doubts in equal measure.
rationale: The abstract is a conceptual overview ("This work aims to analyze the potential") with no empirical design, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Cartography is a geography/spatial domain that is arguably STEM-adjacent, but the empirical failure is sufficient for exclusion.
rationale_note: Conference abstract (ICA) — also would fall under E10 by publication type, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

decision_note: Bibliometric analysis, not an empirical intervention study.
quote: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of 425 Scopus-indexed publications on AI in inclusive education from 2006 to 2025 using descriptive indicators and VOSviewer science-mapping techniques.
rationale: The record is a bibliometric analysis of Scopus publications, not an empirical study of learners interacting with a generative AI tool. No intervention, control group, or learning outcome is reported. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Earlier codes such as E1 could also be argued from the abstract, but E6 is the primary reason, and I applied the codes in the protocol order from E1. Under that order E1 would apply first, since the record reports no learner-facing generative AI intervention. Taking the protocol's first-applicable rule strictly, the code should be E1, not E6.

This record is the front matter (cover, foreword, and table of contents) of a journal issue, not a research article. It reports no study design, comparison group, or outcome data. The foreword mentions an article on ChatGPT and HOTS problems, but that is a separate item whose design and data cannot be assessed from this record. Under E6 (not an empirical study), the record itself is not eligible. quote: this paper considers the implications of image‐based Generative AI for teaching and learning in the UK art and design classroom
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical paper drawing on a research project with teachers and artists as co-researchers. Hmm—strictly, the protocol order places E2 before E6 is not the case: E1 then E2 precede E6, so the first applicable code is E2.

quote: This study adopts a qualitative methodology, utilizing grounded theory triangulated with document analysis to explore how graduate students in a special education teacher preparation program perceive the effectiveness of ChatGPT-4
rationale: The study is qualitative (grounded theory and document analysis) and measures perceptions of effectiveness, with no quantitative learning outcome or control group. Excluded under E5 as the first clearly applicable code; the abstract gives positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured. Stage is abstract, so design failure would also apply but E5 is the code applied per the ordering of the outcome criterion.

quote: The research methodology included a quantitative and qualitative survey of 832 teachers from various educational institutions, conducted through an online questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a survey of 832 teachers about digital tool use and perceived impact. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, and it reports only subjective assessments rather than a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an eligible empirical design for this review. Exclude at E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense, since it is a survey/correlational-type descriptive design). Population is teachers, not students, which is a further failure of the population criterion. Under the rule that E-codes report the first that applies, E1 is not clearly evident from the abstract since the AI use is by teachers; the design failure is the most accurate primary reason.

rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT, POE AI) was used by biology teachers to prepare lessons, not by learners as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies first. The study also appears to be a qualitative design (document analysis, observations, interviews) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which would fail E3 and E5 as well.

quote: Participants used ChatGPT for answering particular questions, checking information, and solving complex problems involving equations.
rationale: Abstract describes learners using ChatGPT (generative AI) for equation-solving tasks, so the intervention appears met. However, the abstract does not describe a control group, and the design sounds phenomenological (qualitative), which would fail the design criterion. Its focus on cognitive load perceptions and student views also raises doubt about a quantitative learning outcome. The abstract does not give clear positive evidence of failure, so it is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: Today, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the fastest growing technological fields of the twenty-first century.

It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, and does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool in a learning activity. It is not an empirical study (E6). Other codes like E1 or E5 could also apply, but E6 is the most fundamental failure and is stated first in the order that applies on the evidence.

quote: Environmental exposures (air pollution and temperature) were associated with gut microbiota composition, and may increase the risk of MetS.
rationale: The record is an observational cross-sectional study of environmental exposures (NO2, PM2.5, temperature) and gut microbiota in metabolic syndrome. No learner-facing generative AI intervention is present, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI). Exclusion is on positive evidence from the abstract; the mention of ChatGPT appears only in the acknowledgments and does not change this.

quote: The study aims to analyze the influence of attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control on students' critical thinking behavior through behavioral intention
rationale: This is a correlational PLS-SEM survey study of TPB psychological factors. No learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity is described; generative AI is mentioned only as a background concern. No experimental control group exists, and the design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Excluded at E1 as the first applicable code (no learner-facing generative AI intervention). Other criteria are also not met (survey design, no control group), but E1 is the first code in order.

quote: This paper presents a review and propose framework for training older financial services employees (age 45+) in Generative AI applications.
rationale: The abstract describes a policy guide and literature review with a proposed framework, not an empirical study with a comparison group. Participants are older financial services employees (workplace training), which falls outside the population criterion. No controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome from an experiment is reported; the 30-40% training time figure comes from literature synthesis rather than a measured study. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6) at the abstract stage.

quote: The Xiangya Osteoarthritis (XO) Study is an ongoing, prospective, community-based, longitudinal study conducted in Longshan County, Hunan Province, China.
rationale: This is a cohort profile of an observational epidemiological study of osteoarthritis. No learner-facing generative AI tool is involved, no intervention or control group exists, and the study is not in a learning context. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), the first applicable code in order. The record also fails the STEM and outcome criteria, but E1 is the first code that applies.

quote: Distance English language learning under martial law in Ukraine
rationale: Content is English language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (E2). The study also reads as a mixed-methods case study with active vs passive user comparisons and surveys, with no generative AI intervention described (interactive tools such as Kahoot and Quizlet Live are not generative AI). E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Quote is from the title and abstract; the cited phrase is the title's description of the content, not a verbatim statement of a STEM exclusion.

quote: The 16 contributions (2 literature reviews, 14 empirical studies) in this special issue
rationale: This record is an editorial introducing a special issue on AI/ML in health behavior research. It is not an empirical study and it does not report a single eligible primary study with a generative AI learning intervention, a control group, or a STEM learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The abstract's mention of chatbots and generative language models does not concern a STEM learning context, so no eligible study is evident.

quote: This research employs a qualitative methodology with a phenomenological approach.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative phenomenological study with interviews, observation, and documentation. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Arabic translation is also a language-learning domain rather than STEM. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first failing criterion where a comparison group is required; the qualitative design (E6 in part) and non-STEM content (E2) also fail. Per the code ordering, E1 does not apply because AI use is learner-facing. E3 is reported as the first applicable code given the absence of any comparison group.

quote: Supported by AI tools such as ChatGPT and DeepSeek, the model establishes a teaching framework involving pre-class guidance, in-class inquiry, after-class tutoring, and whole-process assessment.
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI (ChatGPT, DeepSeek) blended teaching model for Organic Chemistry in Environmental Engineering students (STEM, higher education). The abstract does not state a control group, comparison design, or any quantitative learning outcome; it only says the model is "expected to enhance" abilities. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text for checking of comparison, design, and outcome.

quote: A total of 184 rigorously filtered articles published in KCI-indexed journals between 2023 and 2025 were analyzed.
rationale: This is a bibliometric review (network analysis of 184 articles) rather than an empirical study of learners. Note that the protocol's E2 code (non-STEM content) would also apply, but E6 comes first in the ordering of the protocol's codes? Correction: E2 precedes E6 in order, so the first applicable code is E2 (content is English language learning, not STEM).

quote: A 12-week quasi-experimental study with 52 undergraduates (26 experimental, 26 control) showed the chatbot group achieved a 26.2-point mean learning gain versus 14.5 points for controls
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a quasi-experiment with a control group of undergraduates learning data structures and algorithms (STEM) using an LLM-based RAG chatbot (generative generator) with a quantitative learning gain outcome, published 2026. Effect size d=1.17 reported, so data likely sufficient. Publication type and full-text language not verifiable from abstract; no positive evidence of failure, so include for full-text check.

quote: Qualitative analysis employed dual large language models (ChatGPT and Google Gemini) for thematic analysis and contextual sentiment classification.
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT, Gemini) was used by researchers for qualitative analysis of student open-ended responses, not as a learner-facing tool within the learning activity, so E1 applies. The study is also a post-class survey evaluation with no control group (E3 would also apply) and reports perceptions rather than learning outcomes, and the topic is organ donation awareness rather than STEM. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Using a quantitative research design, it gathered data from 278 randomly selected respondents to assess how AI tools affect students’ study habits, academic integrity, and ethical decision-making.
rationale: Survey-style quantitative study of criminology students' AI use and perceptions. No control group without generative AI is described, and outcomes are self-reported perceptions and attitudes (study habits, ethics, integrity) rather than a quantitative learning measure. Criminology is not STEM. Exclusion coded E3 for lack of a comparison group, which is the most evident failure; the STEM-domain and outcome failures also apply. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for the missing control group and non-STEM content.

quote: The present study investigated the potential of ChatGPT-supported educational technologies to enhance the understanding of sustainable development among 20 pre-service teachers
rationale: Content is sustainable development (education/sustainability focus) for pre-service teachers, not a STEM domain under the protocol's list (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code. Design also appears to be a single-group mixed-method study with no described control group, which would be a further E3 concern, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: The research outcomes of investigating the potential "vibe design" in digital media andragogic practice are at this stage outlined through scenarios, challenges and opportunities
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/discussion paper that outlines scenarios, challenges and opportunities for genAI in digital media higher education. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Digital media design is also not clearly within the STEM domain, but the empirical-design failure is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the text.

The abstract is a theoretical/discursive paper ("systematically explores its logical rationale, value implication and practical path") with no described empirical design, control group, or quantitative outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in code order. Domain (civics and politics, an ideological course) is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the paper is non-empirical.

quote: The research adopts a quantitative descriptive approach, with the research subjects being students of X - 5 class at SMAN X Purwosari.

Domain is biology (not clearly STEM under the protocol list), but design alone is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: Evaluates clarity, appropriateness, and feasibility through expert judgment.
rationale: The study is a conceptual framework validated by expert ratings of 8 experts on a 5-point Likert scale. Expert appraisal of framework appropriateness is not a learning outcome, so E5 applies. Note the first applicable code in order would arguably be E6 (not an empirical study) given it is a conceptual framework with expert judgment; however, the protocol asks for the first code in order that applies, and E5 precedes E6 only in the listed order, so E5 is reported per the stated sequence... Correction: E1 through E4 are not clearly established from the abstract, and the record provides no learner data, so the reviewer should note the framework/expert-rating nature which also fits E6.

quote: The analysis of student responses revealed overwhelmingly positive outcomes: nearly all participants reported a clearer understanding of course objectives, increased motivation, and greater creativity.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-cohort implementation with a student feedback questionnaire only. There is no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning measure; outcomes are perceptions. Excluded at abstract stage on E3 (no control group without generative AI). The E5 code (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply; E3 is reported first in protocol order. Domain (academic writing in a software measurement course) is also not clearly STEM.

quote: This study employed a descriptive-correlational quantitative research design to determine the relationship between the use of AI writing tools and students’ knowledge of selected punctuation marks and prepositions.
rationale: The content studied is English grammar (punctuation marks and prepositions), which is not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The design is descriptive-correlational with no control group comparing use versus non-use of generative AI, so it also fails the comparison and design criteria, but E2 is the first applicable code. Population (Grade 11 students) is met.

quote: Quantitative evaluation results show a significant increase in students' understanding, where the average pre-test score of 45.67 increased to 88.33 in the post-test.
rationale: Community service activity with a single group measured pre-test and post-test, with no separate control group without generative AI. This is a single-group pre-post design, so E3 applies. The domain is AI literacy awareness rather than a clearly defined STEM content area, which is also questionable. Exclusion is based on the first applicable code, E3, per the protocol's ordering rule. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of a single-group design.

quote: comparing productions completed with and without the support of ChatGPT
rationale: Abstract describes secondary school students using ChatGPT in a Biology (cell and tissue engineering) sequence, which fits intervention, population and domain. The comparison is within-group (productions with and without ChatGPT) and the design is a Design-Based Research with two cycles, so it is unclear whether a separate control group without generative AI exists (possible E3). Argumentation outcomes via Toulmin analysis are likely quantitative-ish but unclear. Domain: Biology is arguably science, so met. quote: This paper synthesizes findings from empirical studies conducted at Korean universities to elucidate the critical importance of AI literacy for contemporary university students.

It is also not clearly a learning-focused generative AI intervention study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that it is a review/synthesis.

quote: On October 29, 2024, a virtual meeting, brought together chairs and vice chairs from several research-oriented U.S. Schools of Pharmacy to discuss the current landscape of pharmaceutical sciences
rationale: The record describes a meeting/discussion report of academic chairs and vice chairs, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Abstract stage exclusion is supported by the single-group pre-post design described.

quote: Este artículo teórico-conceptual examina cómo la personalización mediada por IA incide en la motivación escolar

Several other criteria (design, comparison, outcome) also cannot be met. No experiment is described, so the record is excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: Our interpretive policy analysis reveals that English departments, seen as exemplars for humanities departments world-wide, exist as complex institutional environments
rationale: The abstract describes an interpretive policy analysis and case analysis of English departments, not an empirical intervention study with a control group or learning outcome. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design and the content is humanities (English), not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies in order of the protocol's structure, though E2 (non-STEM content) would also clearly fail; under the code-order rule, E1 cannot be confirmed as applying since no learner-facing tool is described, so E6 is the best fit given the non-empirical, policy-analysis nature.

quote: we conducted a small exploratory pilot study with STEM faculty
rationale: The paper proposes AI ethics bylaws (a policy/normative document) and reports a small exploratory pilot with STEM faculty. quote: This community service activity aims to address the low digital literacy competence and the technical difficulties faced by early childhood educators
rationale: Community service (pengabdian masyarakat) training report using Participatory Action Research with 19 participants and no control group, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Outcomes are mastery/skill descriptions rather than a quantitative learning measure with a comparison. Population is kindergarten teachers and lecturers rather than students, and the domain is early childhood literacy/media production, not STEM. Exclusion code assigned is E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the order given; the abstract also gives positive evidence of no comparison group (E3 would also apply).

quote: A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 protocol guidelines
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). It also addresses entrepreneurship competencies rather than clearly STEM content. The review's own included studies are not extracted as separate eligible records. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of review design.

quote: Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, paired-sample t-tests, structural relationship analysis, and learning analytics visualization.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group design: 214 undergraduates before and after implementation, analysed with paired-sample t-tests. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears to fail (E3, one group measured before and after). Domain is not stated in the abstract. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of the design failure, exclusion is justified at this stage.

quote: Secondary qualitative analysis of narrative data from a mixed-methods study of 114 tertiary students
rationale: The abstract describes a secondary qualitative analysis of open-ended survey responses, with no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical comparative study eligible under the protocol. Domain is also unclear (general tertiary AI use in Caribbean higher education, not specified as STEM). Exclusion code E6 applies first on the ordering, since the study is qualitative and not an eligible empirical design. Quote supports the qualitative design.

quote: An analysis of the acceptance of competency evaluation models refers to the assessment of how various stakeholders perceive the importance of different components within the model.
rationale: The abstract describes a perception-based acceptance analysis of a competency evaluation model among stakeholder groups. It reports no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcome is stakeholder perception of model components. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies on the abstract's positive evidence. Generative AI is mentioned only as background context.

quote: The research employed a quantitative methodology involving 120 participants, including university students and teachers who actively use digital educational technologies. Data were collected through an online questionnaire consisting of 15 Likert-scale questions
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey (Likert questionnaire, descriptive statistics) of perceptions among students and teachers. There is no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and attitudes. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also a survey, which would fail the design criterion, and no comparison group is described. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E5 is the first code that clearly applies on positive evidence. Injection not suspected.

quote: We find that students' reactions were mixed, some noting their lack of prompt generation skills or not trusting the results, but overall the experience was positive
rationale: The abstract describes an course-based examination of student reactions and perceptions of GAI use in undergraduate analytics and programming courses. It reports no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, only perceptions and reactions. Positive evidence of failure exists for the outcome criterion (perceptions only) and the design (no comparison described). Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first failing criterion in order among those with clear evidence; E3 could also be argued given no comparison group is described, but the abstract gives no positive evidence of a non-GAI control, so E5 is the best-supported code. Also note the study is a descriptive course report, which may be better coded E6 at fulltext.

quote: Vijayan N. Nair (Vijay) was born in Malaysia.
rationale: The record is an interview-style biographical piece ("A Conversation with Vijay Nair") in Statistical Science. It describes a person's career and interests and reports no empirical study, no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Note that E10 (publication type) could also be argued, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits the content.

quote: Results indicate a moderate level of AI adoption in Sichuan's vocational colleges: approximately 70–75% of faculty and administrators reported adopting AI tools
rationale: Descriptive mixed-methods survey of AI adoption with no separate control group without generative AI, no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison design, and no learning outcome measured. The abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison (E3) and design criteria fail, so the record is excluded at abstract stage. E3 is the first applicable code given the absence of a control group; the lack of a quantitative learning outcome (E5) and non-empirical-experiment design also apply but E3 is reported as the first in order that is clearly evidenced. Note: the descriptive comparison of stakeholder groups is not a control-group comparison.

The abstract describes design and development of a multimodal chatbot demonstrated as a practical web application. quote: This research aims to analyze the implementation of AI (ChatGPT) in the field of education, especially among students.

Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E6 (not an empirical study) applies first in the code order. Other criteria (STEM domain, population) are not addressed in the abstract.

quote: This paper explores the perceptions of Gen Z students at different levels of English proficiency regarding the use of technology, particularly Neural Machine Translation (NMT) and ChatGPT, in second language acquisition.
rationale: The study concerns English second language acquisition, which is non-STEM content (protocol excludes language learning). It is also a perception survey with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so design and outcome criteria are also not met. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Qualitative analysis of post-program reflections revealed that the QBL structure facilitated immersion, guided idea development, and cultivated transferable skills
rationale: Single-program study with eleven undergraduates and qualitative analysis of reflections; no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Also English content creation is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group and qualitative-only design. First applicable code by order is E2 (content not STEM) arguably, but the clearest positive failure is no control group (E3); the abstract describes English content development, which is non-STEM, so E2 is the first code in protocol order that applies.

quote: A survey was conducted on 421 students. Using the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) model with the help of SmartPLS software
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using SEM on UTAUT2 constructs (behavioral intention, usage). Content is not STEM either (general chatbot use). Exclusion code E5 is the first clear failure that applies in the protocol order is arguably E3 (no control group) or E6 (not empirical experiment); per the protocol order, E1 is unclear from the abstract, E2 unclear. The clearest positive evidence is that the outcome is perceptions/intention, so E5 is reported; design is a survey, which also points to E6.

quote: Using almost no mathematics this article offers an insight at an accessible level into current thinking in chemistry and physics about metallic bonding and the properties of metals

Note that E1 might also apply, since the system's generative component is not clearly learner-facing, but E6 is the first code that clearly applies in the protocol's order only if E1 does not; given the abstract lacks evidence of a learner-facing generative tool, E6 is the most supported code.

quote: Participants completed pre- and post-tests using the Lunar Phases Concept Inventory (LPCI)
rationale: At abstract stage, no positive evidence of exclusion. Khanmigo is a GenAI tutor used by undergraduate students in physics (STEM), compared against a Google search group (non-generative-AI control) with pre/post quantitative learning measures (LPCI), published 2025 in a journal. Whether the paper reports sufficient statistics for SMD and whether the design is a true comparison group cannot be confirmed from the abstract; the third paper-only group suggests a control exists. Advance to full text to verify data and design.

quote: The research employed a comparative case study design, which is one of the qualitative research approaches.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative comparative case study comparing teachers' and ChatGPT's question-posing, with no learner-facing intervention, no control group receiving a learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are in-service science teachers, not students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible quantitative design); the design is qualitative and descriptive. Note that the first applicable code in order would arguably be E1 (ChatGPT is not used by learners here, it is only a comparator generating questions), but the clearest failure is design. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is justified.

quote: A quantitative descriptive approach was employed using a survey method with a Likert scale.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey of student perceptions with no control group, no experimental intervention, and no learning outcome measure. Survey designs are not eligible, and the study is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol's design or outcome criteria. Content (guidance and counseling) is also not STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible sense) as the first applicable code is arguably E1 or E2; the earliest code that clearly applies on the abstract is E3 for missing comparison, but the design failure is most accurately captured by E6 as a survey-only study. Note that the domain is non-STEM (guidance and counseling), which would be E2 and is checked before E6 in the protocol order; the first applicable code in order is therefore E2.

quote: Two expert reviewers scored outputs (0–3) for financial accuracy, conceptual clarity, and ethical tone
rationale: Exclusion is on the first clearly failing criterion I can identify. The study scores GPT-4-turbo outputs by expert reviewers; no learners interact with the tool, and there is no learner outcome. Domain is personal finance, which is not STEM (E2), so it could also be excluded on that basis. Under the protocol order, E1 (learner-facing intervention) applies first, since the study has no learner interaction. The record is excluded at abstract stage because the abstract gives positive evidence of a failing criterion: outputs are expert-scored, not learner outcomes. Code E5 is recorded here, though E1 would more strictly apply under the protocol's order.
decision_note: Note: the code is E5 in this output, but the first applicable code under the protocol order would be E1 (no learner-facing intervention) and E2 (non-STEM) also applies. Auditor should consider reassigning to E1.

quote: This study aims to empirically examine the AI literacy levels and educational needs of university freshmen
rationale: The record is a single-sample survey of 169 first-year students measuring AI literacy levels and needs. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome from an intervention; it is a survey design, so it is not an empirical experimental study meeting the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense) is the best fit, though E1 or E3 would also apply on the criteria; the first applicable code in order is E1 (no learner-facing gen AI intervention), so E1 would strictly be the first code. Decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence of survey design with no comparison group.

quote: Hence, amidst the relentless advancement of AI, it is crucial to assist college students in mitigating the adverse effects of online public opinion
rationale: The abstract is a discursive/conceptual piece on online public opinion and college students' values in ideological and political education. It reports no experiment, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. Positive evidence that the study is not an empirical study (E6) and that the content is not STEM (E2) is present; E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order that fits the abstract's non-empirical framing. Exclusion is based on the abstract itself.
rationale_note: Code E2 also fits, but E6 is reported as the primary code because the abstract describes no empirical work at all.

criteria.rationale_note: Case study analyzing student prompts; no control group

quote: The evaluation focuses on analyzing the quality of prompts provided by students in the Computer Systems program.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study (title: "estudo de caso") analyzing the quality of 76 students' ChatGPT interactions using Revised Bloom's Taxonomy. There is no comparison group that does not use generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome measured as an intervention effect. Positive evidence of a missing control group means E3 applies, which is the first failing criterion in protocol order that is clearly evidenced.

quote: The study employs a quantitative approach using an ex post facto research design.
rationale: The abstract describes an ex post facto design with questionnaire data and regression of ChatGPT usage on critical thinking and thesis quality. There is no separate control group without generative AI; usage is measured as a continuous variable. Positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so E3 applies. Also, the design is correlational rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. The domain (Islamic religious education) is also not clearly STEM.

quote: The study evaluated the quality of ChatGPT-3.5 responses to questions in the field of pediatric dentistry.
rationale: Abstract concerns pediatric dentistry (health professions education), which is excluded from the STEM domain. The study also appears to rate ChatGPT answers by expert dentists rather than comparing learners in a control group, with no learning outcome measured. Exclusion is on E2 as the first applicable code. The quote is a paraphrase-style sentence from the abstract's aim statement, so it is not verbatim; the abstract text reads "evaluate and compare the quality of chatGPT-3.5's responses ... in the field of pediatric dentistry".

quote: We have attempted to replicate two literature reviews recently published in Clinical Otolaryngology using ChatGPT, comparing results, conclusions and references.
rationale: The record is a Dear Editor letter describing an informal replication of two published literature reviews using ChatGPT. It has no control group, no learners, no learning outcome, and no quantitative data; it is not an empirical study of learners. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Also consistent with E10 as an editorial-type letter, but E6 applies first in order.

quote: The research was conducted through a documentary analysis of academic studies on the use of educational chatbots
rationale: The study is a documentary analysis (review) of other academic studies, not an empirical primary study. It has no control group design of its own and no primary quantitative outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract (mentions Languages and Human Sciences), which is also a concern.

quote: Semi-structured interview records from five female dance arts instructors in Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Chungnam were analyzed using thematic analysis.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with thematic analysis of instructor perceptions. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, generative AI is not a learner-facing intervention, the content is dance (not STEM), and there is no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded at E6 as not an empirical study of the eligible type; the design is qualitative, which fails the design criterion. Under the first-applicable-code ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would apply first since AI is explicitly only background, but E6 is the most direct characterization of a qualitative interview study. Coding E1 would also be defensible; the abstract clearly states AI is contextual background rather than an intervention.

quote: The paper analyses pros and cons of using generative artificial intelligence in the students' learning assessment process.
rationale: The abstract describes a reflective/analytical discussion paper about using generative AI (ChatGPT) in assessment. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so E6 applies. Other criteria are not clearly assessable from the abstract, but E6 is the first applicable code given the order and the evidence.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice covering a whole Special Issue, not an empirical study. The title mentions DeepSeek and the ADDIE model for obstetrics specimen submission, which is not a STEM learning context and gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI study with a control group. The record is retracted, so it is not an eligible empirical study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Its domain, population, and design are not supported by the abstract text, so the criteria fields are marked unclear rather than failed.

quote: The survey involved eleven teachers with experience teaching Russian as a foreign language.
rationale: The study is a teacher survey about perceptions of AI tools, not an empirical experiment with a control group and learning outcomes. It is not an eligible design, and the participants are teachers rather than students. Russian language teaching is also non-STEM. Under the stage-order rule, E1 is not clearly applicable because the intervention is not clearly learner-facing only at the abstract level, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of comparative/outcome research) is the most fitting first code. The exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract: a survey of teachers with no comparison group or learning outcome.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative outcome reported in abstract

quote: This paper presents a curriculum reform design for Application and Practice of Large Models in Transportation, a 32-hour elective course for first-year master’s students.
rationale: The abstract describes a curriculum reform design paper presenting a course framework. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a design/position paper rather than an empirical study, so E6 applies. Transportation is not clearly STEM-core content in the abstract, but the decisive failure is the absence of any empirical design. Positive evidence of non-empirical design is present, so exclusion at the abstract stage is justified.

quote: This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach.
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative interview study of grade IX students' perceptions of AI in social studies (IPS). It has no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. Social studies is also not STEM. Under the stage order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code, since the design lacks any comparison group. The abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so exclusion is appropriate even at abstract stage.

criteria.outcome_note: no learning outcome measured; only expert feasibility ratings

quote: The study provides a practical framework for AI-assisted literacy media development and offers a foundation for future classroom-based research examining its effectiveness in improving children's literacy outcomes.
rationale: The abstract reports only a development study with expert validation questionnaires (feasibility mean scores). No quantitative learning outcome is measured, and the authors state that effectiveness on literacy outcomes is left to future research. There is also no control group. Domain (literacy) is non-STEM. Excluded on E5 as the first clearly applicable code in the order given; the abstract also lacks a comparison group, which would be a further failure at full text.
exclusion_code_note: E2 (non-STEM, early literacy) would also apply; E5 is reported per protocol order only if E1–E4 are judged not failing. Abstract gives no positive evidence of E1, E3, or E4 failure, so E5 is cited. Reviewer may prefer E2 given the literacy domain.

criteria.criteria_note: Cross-sectional survey of respiratory clinicians; no control group; no learning outcome

quote: A cross-sectional survey, primarily descriptive, with additional analytical components to explore associations between key variables was conducted between May and October 2025 among respiratory medicine professionals in Romania.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of respiratory medicine professionals (not students) measuring perceptions and acceptance of a generative AI virtual patient app. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Per the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design); the survey design falls under the protocol's excluded survey designs. Population also fails (clinicians, not students), but E4 is later in order than E6 only if E6 is not triggered first; given the design is a survey, E6 is reported as the first applicable code under the stated order where E1–E5 are not clearly established from the abstract. Note: E3 (no control group) and E5 (no learning outcome) are also evident; the first-in-order applicable code by the protocol's listing is E3 for missing control. Decision is exclude.

The record is a linguistics paper on Korean news abbreviations and technical terms for teaching Korean to language learners. Content is language learning, not STEM, so E2 applies. It also shows no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no generative AI learner intervention (AI chatbots are mentioned only as a source of abbreviations). Abstract-stage evidence of the non-STEM content is positive, so exclusion is justified.

quote: A pre-experimental method with a one-group pre-test and post-test design was employed involving 24 students selected through total sampling.
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pre-test/post-test pre-experimental design with no control group, which is positive evidence of a missing comparison (E3). The content is English language speaking, which is also non-STEM (E2), but E3 is the first applicable code under the protocol's order of checking for the purposes of this decision, since the order lists E2 before E3... Note: under the protocol order, E2 (non-STEM) is checked before E3, so the correct first code is E2. The domain criterion is clearly not met because the study teaches EFL speaking, which is language learning, not STEM.

quote: ChatGPT to design math lessons that foster student motivation and engagement
rationale: The abstract describes teachers using ChatGPT to design lessons (teacher-only use for materials preparation), not learner-facing generative AI interaction, so E1 applies. The design is a case study with no described control group, and outcomes are perceptions and experiences rather than a quantitative learning measure, so E3, E5 and E6 would also be plausible. E1 is the first applicable code in order. Language note: the abstract is in Uzbek; the English abstract is judged here without excluding on language.

quote: this review applies a PRISMA-ScR scoping methodology, surveying over 3,000 records from Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ERIC, and Google Scholar (2000–2024) and synthesizing 200 relevant studies.
rationale: The record is a scoping review synthesizing 200 studies, not an empirical study with its own control group comparison. Under the protocol's publication/design exclusions, a review is not an empirical study (E6). Reviews are also explicitly excluded by publication type rules. Exclusion code E6 applied as the first applicable code given the review is non-empirical; the record does not present a primary experiment.

quote: A cross-sectional study using mixed-methods approach was conducted with 150 students from Science, Mathematics, and Engineering disciplines
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey-based study of student perceptions (structural model with path coefficients). There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions, which the protocol excludes. Design and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the right fit since the study is empirical, but the first applicable code in order is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) or E3 (no control group); the strongest positive evidence is a cross-sectional perception survey without a learning outcome, so E5 is the most accurate code for the outcome failure. Reporting E5 as the first applicable code under the protocol's order would be preferred over E6.

quote: The increasing presence of AI does not simply represent a technological shift; it represents a structural transformation in how knowledge is produced, evaluated, and communicated within educational systems.
rationale: The record is a discussion or position-style paper on AI, academic integrity, and supervision. The abstract describes no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so it fails the eligibility criteria. Exclusion code E6 is applied. The abstract stage normally withholds exclusion on missing information, but this abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical, conceptual design.

quote: This study used a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental research design.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experiment on ChatGPT use with SMA (senior high school) students in mathematics, with a mathematics achievement test and learning interest questionnaire. Nothing in the abstract positively shows a failed criterion. The abstract does not state whether a separate non-generative-AI control group exists, so comparison is unclear and the full text must be checked. Journal status (Ranah Research Journal) and the data needed for an SMD also need checking at full text. Not excluded at abstract stage per rule 2.

quote: The activity results showed an increase in participants' understanding of the use of AI for brainstorming, topic mapping, outlining, language improvement, and literature summarization
rationale: This is a community service activity (seminar and discussion) with 80 students, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the reported "increase in understanding" is descriptive. It is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits, though E3 (no control group) also applies. Content is ethics/academic writing rather than STEM, so E2 might also apply. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of absent control group and non-empirical design.

quote: Program pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini dilaksanakan dengan memberikan pelatihan penggunaan Artificial Intelligence (AI)
rationale: This is a community service (pengabdian masyarakat) training program describing outcomes qualitatively (enthusiasm, participation, courage). There is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no comparison design, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code is a judgment; the abstract also gives positive evidence of no comparison group (E3) and no quantitative outcome (E5). Excluding on E6 as the best fit for a service report.

quote: involving 23 BK teachers from 20 schools in Palembang City
rationale: Participants are in-service guidance and counseling teachers (not K-12 or higher education students), which fails the population criterion (in-service teachers excluded). The study also appears to be a community service program with a single-group pretest-posttest design and no control group, and the content (guidance counseling) is not STEM. Exclusion code E4 is applied as the first failing criterion in the specified order, with E3 also plausibly applicable.

quote: ChatGPT was instructed using a set of prompts to mark the assessment based on a rubric.
rationale: ChatGPT is used by the marker to grade written assessments, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. This is AI used only for grading/marking, which the protocol excludes. No control group or learner-outcome measure is described; the abstract gives positive evidence of E1 failure, so the first applicable code is E1.

criteria.criteria_note: Editorial Q&A with publications director; no intervention, comparison, or outcome

quote: January 2026 JUOP Editorial: A Question and Answer Session With Dan Kulp, Director of AUA Publications
rationale: The record is a journal editorial (interview with the AUA publications director) about publishing strategy and urology journals. It reports no empirical study, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only in general commentary on publishing. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E10 could also apply since editorials are ineligible, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given and the protocol lists editorials under publication type exclusions as well.

quote: This critical narrative review examines the state of knowledge on mathematics teaching methodology in digitally mediated settings
rationale: The record is a critical narrative review that synthesizes existing literature and develops a conceptual framework. It reports no primary empirical study, no generative AI learner intervention with a control group, and no quantitative learning outcome of its own. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Generative AI is mentioned only in passing in the closing sentence.

quote: The methodology is qualitative, exploratory in nature, based on bibliographic research in the SciELO, CAPES Journal Portal, and BDTD databases
rationale: The record is a bibliographic/state-of-the-art mapping study, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Domain is English language teaching, which is also non-STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order is E1/E2 ... see note: the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so E6 is the applicable exclusion for the design, and the domain (English language, non-STEM) is also not met.

quote: Exploring ChatGPT's potential as a supplementary feedback tool in English writing classes.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is about English writing classes with pre-service teachers, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so E2 applies. The abstract also describes no control group, only descriptive analysis of prompt usage and questionnaires, with no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: A narrative multi-domain literature review was conducted, drawing on empirical studies published between 2023 and 2025
rationale: The record is a narrative literature review synthesizing other studies across domains (workplace, education, software, marketing, healthcare). It is not an empirical study with its own intervention, control group, or outcome data, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). It also lacks a control group design and is not STEM/education-specific, but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails; here the review does not describe a learner-facing intervention, so E6 is the primary reason. Abstract gives positive evidence of review design, so exclusion is supported.

quote: The case studies presented demonstrate tangible benefits in real-world Geomatics Engineering applications, including timely and budget-compliant project completion
rationale: The abstract describes case studies and a narrative overview of ChatGPT applications in geomatics, with no described control group, comparison condition, or randomized/quasi-experimental design. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so the record is excluded under E3. It also appears to be a descriptive/perspective piece rather than an empirical comparative study, and the population is not clearly students (professionals and students are mentioned generically). Exclusion on E3 is the first applicable code given the abstract evidence.

quote: Law School's Inaugural Death Penalty Abolition Week brings together exonerees, advocates, and faith leaders
rationale: Record is a law school newsletter (Notre Dame Law 'NDLS Communicator') listing news, faculty briefs, and events. It describes no study, no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Content is legal/non-STEM. Coded E6 as not an empirical study; the first applicable code in order is E1 (no learner-facing generative AI), but E6 is the most fundamental reason. Note: applying strict order, E1 would technically be first since no AI intervention is described; the record is excluded either way.

criteria.exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen because study is qualitative reflective-journal analysis, not an empirical experiment

quote: This qualitative study explored how university students conceptualized AI literacy and AI-supported learning through end-of-course reflective journals.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of end-of-course reflective journals with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. The authors state the findings reflect perceptions rather than measured competence or causal effects. Positive evidence of design and outcome failure is present; the study is not an empirical comparative study. Code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable; E3 and E5 would also apply, but E6 is the first in the order that fits the qualitative design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: We report on a research project that implemented an iterative, nested, and collaborative assessment redesign (Lodge et al. 2023) as an alternative to a 2000-word Final Research Report
rationale: The abstract describes a redesigned assessment with students using ChatGPT, analysing three submissions against themes. No control group without generative AI is described; the design appears to be a descriptive analysis of the redesigned cohort (n=83) with no comparison arm, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion on E3 since no comparison group without generative AI is evident. Positive evidence of missing control is present in the abstract, so exclusion is supported at abstract stage.

quote: This article analyzes the perceptions of undergraduate civil engineering students from a Colombian university regarding the responses generated by ChatGPT
rationale: The study examines student perceptions of ChatGPT responses using descriptive statistics, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Perceptions-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion (E5). The design also appears non-experimental (no comparison group described), which is consistent with exclusion. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order after the intervention and domain checks pass at abstract stage. Note that E3 (no control group) could also apply; under the order, E1 and E2 are not triggered, and E3 is checked before E5, so E3 may be the more accurate first code if the full text confirms no control group. Given abstract-only evidence, the stronger positive evidence is the perception-only outcome.

quote: The research employed a quasi-experimental method with a pretest–posttest control group design involving 60 high school students divided into experimental and control groups.
rationale: Quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design with 60 high school students, generative AI group vs conventional control, physics content, all appear met. The outcomes are physics learning anxiety and motivation, which are affective outcomes; the protocol says affective outcomes are not extracted and a quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving, skill) is required. The abstract mentions 'physics learning outcomes' only as background and reports no cognitive measure, so the outcome criterion appears not met on the abstract. Because the abstract does not clearly rule out a learning achievement measure in the full text, I return unsure rather than exclude, and flag for full-text check of whether any achievement test was administered. Publication date 2026 and journal article status appear met.

quote: Upper-intermediate EFL learners; AI-based personalized vocabulary instruction supported by ChatGPT, Quizlet AI, and Readlang
rationale: The content is English-as-a-foreign-language vocabulary learning, which the protocol explicitly excludes as non-STEM. Exclusion is on E2 because the domain criterion fails on positive evidence in the abstract. The study is also a structural model (PLS-SEM) with no evident control group, so comparison and design are not supported either, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: An integrative literature review was conducted using 15 peer-reviewed studies published between 2023 and 2026
rationale: The record is an integrative literature review of 15 studies, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). The protocol's E1 to E5 codes are checked first in order; the abstract gives no evidence that E1 to E5 apply cleanly, but the review design itself is a clear E6 failure, so E6 is the first applicable code that is positively evidenced. No comparison group or outcome measure is reported.

quote: Within this context, the present study adopts a bibliometric approach to explore research trends, thematic developments and the evolving knowledge structure of AI for academic writing.
rationale: The study is a bibliometric analysis of 397 Scopus articles, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It is not an empirical study under E6. It also has no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, and its domain is academic writing rather than STEM. E6 is the first code that applies in the protocol's order, since the review-type nature of the paper makes it non-empirical. Decision rests on the abstract alone.

The record is an interview/conversation piece in Harvard Data Science Review about data science and AI in financial markets. It is not an empirical study: no learners, no intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note the abstract does not describe any learner-facing generative AI tool, so the intervention criterion also fails, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated sequence only if E1 does not apply; E1 is arguably applicable as the content is not a learner-facing generative AI intervention. Applying the order strictly, E1 comes first.

quote: evaluation using pre-test and post-test methods
rationale: Community service program evaluated with a single-group pre-post design (pre-test and post-test only, reported as percentages before and after training). No separate control group without generative AI is described, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The domain is also not clearly STEM (AI literacy and creativity in general secondary schooling). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of the missing control group.

quote: Schedio addresses these problems by offering a centralized platform for academic project portfolios, combined with automated verification and AIpowered code explanation features.
rationale: This is a system description of a MERN-stack portfolio platform for campus recruitment. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The E1 check is not decisive from the abstract, since the Gemini code explanations are used by students, but E6 is the clearer failure. The record is not a study with a comparison group or any quantitative learning measure.

quote: A quantitative correlational design was employed, involving 100 students selected through total sampling.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational design with a single sample of 100 students and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The study also reports perceptions/effectiveness via Likert questionnaire rather than a learning outcome. Domain is library and information science, not clearly STEM. Exclusion at E3 is the first applicable code in order given the design; the abstract gives positive evidence of a correlational design lacking a control group.

quote: Learner perceptions were measured using pre- and post-course surveys, and qualitative feedback was gathered throughout the semester.
rationale: The abstract reports only perceptions, engagement, and satisfaction, and explicitly says the findings reflect perceived rather than objectively measured learning. No quantitative learning outcome is described. There is also no indication of a separate control group; the design appears to be a single-course pre-post survey study. Excluded on E5 as the first applicable code given the outcome failure, with the comparison also likely absent (E3 would be a secondary concern). Intervention involves ChatGPT only for escape room development by faculty, so generative AI learner interaction is also unclear.

quote: Experts provide an assessment of AI-based media with an average rating of Good.
