rationale: This is a R&D study developing AI-based learning media (ChatGPT, Fliki, Toonme, D-ID) for a mathematics evaluation course. Outcomes reported are expert validation ratings and small/large group trial assessments of feasibility, appearance, and language quality, not a quantitative learning outcome. No control group comparison is described. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), since the reported measures are perceptions and validity ratings rather than learning achievement. Comparison design is also absent, so E3 could be argued, but E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol's stated order for the outcome failure, and the abstract gives positive evidence the outcome is not learning.

quote: Employing a mixed-methods approach, data were analysed from post-project questionnaires (N=95 [Cagliari], N=10 [Tuzla], N=10 [Aix-Marseille], N=8 [Castilla-La Mancha])
rationale: The abstract describes a reflective analysis of a single transnational lab with post-project questionnaires and formative assessments, with no control or comparison group. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison group (E3). Domain is also doubtful (CLIL/eTwinning, primary pre-service teachers, not clearly STEM), but E3 is the first applicable code under the protocol order, so it is reported.
rationale_ordering_note: E1-E2 not assessed as primary because intervention and domain are not clearly established from abstract.

quote: "Proliferation of Chat GPT into Health Research" — this is a narrative commentary on ChatGPT in health research and scholarly publishing.
rationale: The record is an opinion/narrative commentary, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also framed around health research and publishing rather than STEM learning. E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is clearly supported (E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the earliest code with positive evidence of failure).

quote: This article adopts a qualitative approach, with exploratory research from the perspective of complexity theory
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative exploratory study of a workshop, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Qualitative designs fall under the not-empirical-quantitative exclusion; E6 is the best fit given the qualitative approach, though E3 and E5 would also apply. Participants are higher-education master's and doctoral students, and the work is not STEM-specific (education/technology focus), so E2 could also be argued. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: the paper's contribution is the governance framework and the agenda it sets for empirical piloting in China's urban-rural context.
rationale: The record is a systematic-style review plus a conceptual framework and an assumption-driven simulation. It reports no empirical controlled study, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no comparison group and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Under the protocol order, E1 would be the first code to check, but the record is clearly a non-empirical review/framework paper, so E6 is the most accurate single code given that the simulation and review do not evaluate any learner-facing intervention. Exclusion is clear even at abstract stage because the abstract explicitly states no empirical pooled effect is presented.

Abstract describes a sixth-grade Lebanese science study with a quantitative knowledge-in-use outcome, so population and outcome appear met. However, the design reads as a single-group pre-/post assessment with no described control group, which would be E3 if confirmed. The abstract also mentions "AI-enhanced" tools (Copilot Studio, Microbit ML, Minecraft Education, Interactive PowerPoint) without clarifying whether learners directly use a generative model. Comparison group, generative nature of the tools, and design are unclear at abstract stage, and the rule favors advancing to full text rather than excluding. Per rule 2, not excluded at abstract stage.

quote: This study explores the ability of ChatGPT in solving first-level physics textbook-style problems and context rich problems (CRPs).
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT solving physics problems itself, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. No student participants or control group are described. Positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so exclude under E1.

quote: Five faculty members independently rated summaries generated by Microsoft Copilot and by human analysis using a 7-point Likert scale.
rationale: Generative AI (Copilot) is used by faculty to summarize student exit survey data, not by learners in a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). The study is also a cross-sectional descriptive design with faculty perception ratings, not a learning outcome or a controlled comparison of learners, so other criteria fail as well. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This systematic review synthesised empirical research on the effectiveness of AI-based tutoring and assessment systems in mathematics education published between 2015 and 2025.
rationale: The record is a systematic review (secondary synthesis of 12 included studies), not an empirical study of its own. It fails E6 and is excluded at the first applicable code. Its eligibility is not assessed beyond that, and the abstract's mention of generative AI does not change this.

quote: A descriptive quantitative research design was employed using a questionnaire distributed to 21 university students.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, questionnaire-only study of 21 university students with no control group or experimental manipulation. It reports only perceptions, attitudes, and self-reported behavior, not a quantitative learning outcome. Design is non-experimental, so the record is not an empirical comparison study. Exclusion code E6 is used because the study is a descriptive survey, which is not an eligible design; E3 (no control group) and E5 (no learning outcome) also clearly apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order only if treated as non-experimental survey. Note: under strict code order E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is unclear from the abstract, so the decision rests on the design and outcome failures. Injection not detected.

quote: In synthetic experiments designed to mimic observational settings with confounding and treatment effect heterogeneity, the AI-augmented DML yields lower ATE bias
rationale: The paper is a methods paper on Double Machine Learning in R evaluated on synthetic data. There are no learners, no learning outcome, and no control group of learners using or not using generative AI. The AI assistants are used by the analyst for coding and feature construction, not by learners. It fails several criteria. Following the code order, the first applicable code is E1, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. The E4 code in the decision field is inconsistent with that order and should be corrected to E1 at audit.

quote: The method used was a correlational quantitative study with a survey approach involving 200 students
rationale: The study is correlational and survey-based, with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group that does not use generative AI. AI usage intensity is measured, not manipulated. Positive evidence of a failed design/comparison criterion is present, so exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Also, the domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Coded E3 as the first applicable code given the ordering of checks is E1 unclear; E3 is the clearest failure.

criteria.outcome_note: Outcomes are self-efficacy and interest, which are affective and excluded by protocol.

quote: The results revealed statistically significant improvements in both self-efficacy and interest
rationale: Music composition in elementary education is not one of the protocol's STEM domains (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). The abstract also reports only self-efficacy and interest, which are affective outcomes excluded by protocol. No control group is described in the abstract. E2 is the first applicable code in order, since the content is non-STEM and that check precedes the outcome check. Exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: This study investigates the nature of EAP teacher feedback on English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) disciplinary writing
rationale: Study concerns EAP disciplinary academic writing (language/writing content), not STEM content. Also, the design is a qualitative analysis of feedback and interview themes with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria as well. Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable in order at the abstract stage, since content is not STEM. Note that E1 could be argued (GenAI feedback is a comparison topic, not clearly learner-facing), but E2 is the clearest first failure.

quote: To this end, we enter a scholarly discussion with ChatGPT in the form of questions and answers, and analyze the responses.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative analysis of ChatGPT's answers to quantitative risk management questions. It reports no control group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical learning study, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied at the first stage where the design failure is evident. Learner population is also not described.

quote: Following PRISMA guidelines, 46 peer-reviewed empirical studies were analysed to identify patterns in tool usage, pedagogical approaches and research dissemination.
rationale: This is a systematic review of 46 studies, not an empirical primary study. It fails the Design criterion (no primary randomized or quasi-experimental comparison) and falls under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also a review, which would be E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, so E6 is reported. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence the record is a review.

Abstract describes an admissions-enquiry chatbot for college information on WhatsApp. It reports no experimental design, no control group, and no learning outcome; it is a system description. The content is college admissions information rather than STEM content. Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists (no quantitative learning outcome; non-STEM content), so exclusion under E5 is applied, with E2 also arguably applicable. Under the code order, E1 (learner-facing generative AI) cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract, so E5 is the first clearly failing code the abstract supports.

quote: This case study presents how EdLight uses artificial intelligence for math instruction.
rationale: The record is a Bellwether case study series profile of an organization, based on interviews with leaders and a review for accuracy. It is not an empirical study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. No comparison group or learning measure is described. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order after checking E1 to E5 as unclear or not evidenced; the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: Статья описывает концепцию, архитектуру и результаты опытной эксплуатации «Цифрового полигона» ВИШ НИЯУ МИФИ
rationale: The paper is an infrastructure/architecture description of a digital campus platform. Outcomes are operational IT metrics (availability ~99.5%, incident counts, deployment time, TTD/TTR), not learner learning outcomes, and no control group or learner-facing generative AI intervention is described. Exclusion on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: This systematic literature review examines the opportunities and challenges of integrating generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into foreign language education within higher education (HE).
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, which is not an empirical study (E6). It also concerns foreign language education, which is non-STEM (E2), but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is decisive here. Review articles are also ineligible publication types. No primary experimental comparison is reported in the abstract.

quote: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the opportunities for integrating artificial intelligence services into the system of legal education
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/analytical article that systematizes platform functions and discusses risks; it reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study. Domain is legal education, which is not STEM. Excluded under E6, the first applicable code in the stated sequence after E1 (intervention is generative AI, so E1 does not apply) and E2 (legal content, not STEM) would apply as well; E2 precedes E6 in the order, so the code should be E2 on strict ordering. Note: E2 is first in order and applies clearly from the abstract (law and law enforcement training).

quote: An observational, descriptive and cross-sectional study was carried out, measuring quantitative and qualitative variables such as age, sex, internet access, types of chatbots most used and students' perception of their use.
rationale: The study is an observational, cross-sectional survey of medical students' chatbot use. It has no control group, no learning outcome (it measures frequency of use and perceptions), and the content is health professions education rather than STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not the best fit, but the design is a survey, not an experiment; the first applicable code by the protocol order is E1 only if intervention fails, which is unclear here. Under the protocol order, the strongest positive evidence is the absence of a learning outcome and a comparison group; the record is a descriptive survey and is excluded as not an empirical eligible study.

Abstract describes a conceptual/discussion paper about ChatGPT's contributions, challenges, and a proposed self-learning framework. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that the study is not an empirical comparison (design and outcome criteria fail) supports exclusion. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order. Note: the rule for abstract-stage exclusion requires positive evidence; the abstract's framing as a review/conceptual framework is positive evidence of non-empirical design, so exclusion is supported.

Abstract describes GenAI-created course materials compared with instructor-made content, with outcomes being expert evaluations of content quality and learner interaction log data (engagement). No quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or knowledge is reported; the abstract itself says academic achievement is a recommended future topic. Outcomes appear to be perceptions/usage, which fail the outcome criterion. Domain is not stated in the abstract, so it is not used as the basis for exclusion. Exclusion is on positive evidence that no learning outcome is measured.

quote: GenAI for automated essay scoring: A turing test of rubrics, rater agreement, and authorship in L2 writing assessment
rationale: The title indicates L2 (second language) writing assessment with automated essay scoring, which is language learning content, not STEM. The protocol excludes language learning and other non-STEM content. No abstract is available, but the title alone gives positive evidence of a non-STEM domain, so exclude at abstract stage under E2. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the title alone and are marked unclear.

quote: In this poster, we share ongoing research into the use of realistic AI-generated avatars for education in a large Australian business school.
rationale: The record is a poster (work in progress) presenting use cases and an ongoing study, per the abstract. Publication type is not eligible (E10). It also reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is business education rather than STEM. Exclusion code E10 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order for a non-eligible publication type.
rationale_note: Other criteria also appear unmet, but E10 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: This paper systematically examines the practical challenges facing undergraduate accounting education across six dimensions
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/policy framework for an accounting curriculum cluster ("proposed framework", "theoretical foundation and practical reference"). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Accounting is also not clearly a STEM domain under the protocol. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract; no generative AI learner-facing intervention is evaluated.

quote: Expert testing results show a high level of system accuracy and effectiveness, with an average score of 4.44 (classified as very good).
rationale: The study is an R&D prototype development with expert testing rated on a Likert-style score. There is no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome measured on students; the reported outcome is expert rating of the system and emotion detection accuracy. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code given the abstract; the study also lacks a comparison group, which would be E3, but the abstract gives no evidence of a comparison design, so E5 is the clearest positive failure. Domain (STEM) is not stated in the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence that no learning outcome is measured.

quote: Dr. Takeuchi and Kitagawa1 described the importance of artificial intelligence (AI) in surgical innovation.
rationale: The record is a commentary/editorial letter on AI in surgery and global surgical equity. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Health/surgical practice is also not STEM education content, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from the protocol's listed sequence once the earlier E1 check is considered unresolved; the abstract gives no learner-facing generative AI intervention evidence.

quote: Online Media Consumption Behavior of Chinese Students Who Decide to Travel to Thailand Independently
rationale: The study concerns online media use for independent travel decisions, which is not STEM content. It is also a mixed-methods survey and interview study with no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the abstract only mentions AI chatbots as a marketing suggestion, not as a learner-facing intervention. Under the stated order, the clearest failure is the content domain, so E2 is applied as the first code with positive evidence of failure. Design and outcome also fail.
rationale_note: Code selection note: E1 would be the first in protocol order if intervention failure is judged positive; the abstract gives no evidence that learners interacted with generative AI, so E1 is arguably the more accurate first code. Auditor should check.

quote: Employing a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were collected from 507 students
rationale: The design is descriptive-correlational with a single survey of students; there is no control group comparison, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The outcome is self-reported learning motivation measured by questionnaire (affective), not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or problem solving, so E5 applies. Domain is also unclear (final assignments across programs, not clearly STEM). Excluded at abstract stage because the abstract gives positive evidence of a correlational survey design without a control group.

quote: Post-intervention performance was compared between students who practiced with AI-generated MCQs (n = 71) and those who relied solely on human-authored learning materials (n = 416).
rationale: Physics (STEM) competition students with a comparison group receiving only human-authored materials, and a performance outcome, so no clear abstract-level exclusion. The abstract does not state whether the assignment was randomized or quasi-experimental (only a post-intervention comparison of self-selected practice groups), and it does not confirm that the AI tool is generative in a learner-facing sense beyond AI-generated MCQs being practiced by students. Whether the design and effect-size data are adequate needs full-text review, so the record advances as unsure.

quote: the IELTS Writing Task 2 band descriptors
rationale: The study concerns English academic writing (IELTS Writing Task 2), which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies. The design is a mixed-methods analysis of Gemini feedback on essays with no evident control group, and no learning outcome is reported, so it also appears to fail on comparison and design, but E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This study examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI), specifically generative AI, in higher education, mainly in the teaching-learning process, personalized learning, learning outcomes, and challenges.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive study that reviews research articles, books, and university policy documents. It is not an empirical experiment or quasi-experiment with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. It is not an empirical study in the protocol sense (E6). The record also gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. STEM content is not mentioned, but that is not the basis for exclusion.

quote: School psychologists constantly seek innovative ways to support students and colleagues.
rationale: The record is a practitioner-oriented how-to article (Communique) that guides school psychologists in using LLMs to build an educational app, using a game as an example. It describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study (E6). Population is school psychologists, not students, and the domain is not clearly STEM. Exclusion at E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is supported by the abstract, since E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

quote: the directed use of AI significantly improves the accuracy of economic terminology and the efficiency of drafting business reports in English
rationale: The study targets ESP / business English writing for economic education students. Business English and economic writing is language learning in a non-STEM content area, so the domain criterion is not met (E2). Intervention (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Grammarly in PjBL) and higher-education population appear to fit. Comparison design is unclear from the abstract (describes an experimental group and pre/post tests in classroom action research), but the domain failure is clear positive evidence and is the first applicable code in order that can be determined from the abstract. Per the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is justified on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: we used a mixed‐methods design to survey U.S. world language teachers, followed by interviews with eight teachers
rationale: The study surveys and interviews in-service world language teachers about their own GenAI use. It is a survey/qualitative design with no control group, no learner outcome, and no learner-facing intervention. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense, i.e., not an eligible quantitative comparative design). Population (in-service teachers) and domain (language learning, non-STEM) also fail. Exclusion code E6 chosen as the first applicable in order where E1 is ambiguous; the record is clearly not eligible on multiple grounds.

quote: This systematic review synthesizes 54 peer-reviewed studies published between 2019 and 2025
rationale: The record is a scoping/systematic review of 54 studies, not an empirical study. Reviews are ineligible under the publication-type rule, and the review is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Other criteria are not the basis of this decision.

quote: This study compares scaffolding strategies generated by ChatGPT-3.5 and a customized GPT in reading comprehension exercises
rationale: Content is English reading comprehension for language learning (CEFR B2), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study also compares two generative AI variants with no non-AI control group and reports no learning outcome measure, so E3 and E5 would also apply, but E2 is the first code that applies. Decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: This research aimed at determining the perceived usefulness of ChatGPT in relation to students’ confidence in writing English essays.
rationale: The study concerns English essay writing, which is language learning and not STEM content, so E2 applies. It is also correlational with perception-based outcomes (Likert perceptions and writing confidence) and no control group, which would independently fail E3, E5 and the design criterion. Coding the first applicable code, E2.

quote: The proposed system uses Artificial Intelligence to overcome this limitation by generating a learning path specifically for each learner.
rationale: The abstract describes a system proposal with no evaluation, no control group, and no learning outcome data. It reads as a system description rather than an empirical study, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Domain and population are not specified, and the abstract gives no positive evidence of a controlled comparison or quantitative outcome. Excluded at abstract stage on E6 as the first applicable code.

quote: This study investigates the relationship between ChatGPT usage and digital literacy among students of the Educational Technology Study Program at Universitas Negeri Padang (UNP).
rationale: The abstract describes a quantitative correlational survey design with no separate control group and no learning intervention. Under the protocol, correlational designs are excluded (design), and the lack of a comparison group also fails the comparison criterion. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the intervention and population checks are not clearly failing. Domain is not clearly STEM (educational technology digital literacy), and the outcome is a self-reported measure of digital literacy rather than a clear learning outcome.

quote: The analysis presented in this report draws on qualitative data from student responses to guided reflection prompts, enabling an exploration of their perceptions, challenges, emotional responses, and development of transversal competencies.
rationale: The abstract describes a project report drawing on qualitative reflection data about perceptions and experiences. There is no control group or quantitative learning outcome reported, and the design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Positive evidence of failure on design and outcome exists, so exclude. The code is E6 (not an empirical study) as the report is a descriptive implementation report based on qualitative data; the first-applying code in order would be E3 (no control group) by strict reading, but the qualitative nature points to E6 as the primary reason. No ChatGPT-specific comparison is evident in the abstract.
rationale_note: Ordering note: E3 could also apply on the strict order of codes since no control group is described.

quote: A vizsgálat rámutatott arra, hogy a mesterséges intelligencia és a digitális tanulási eszközök (mint például a ChatGPT) egyre fontosabb szerepet töltenek be a diákok tanulási és tájékozódási folyamataiban.
rationale: The record is a survey-based career orientation study (online and paper questionnaires, quantitative and qualitative description). It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no learning outcome measured after an intervention. Generative AI (ChatGPT) is mentioned only as a general tool students use, not as a controlled learner-facing intervention. Exclusion is on E1 as the first applicable code; the study also fails design, comparison, outcome, and domain (career orientation is not STEM content), but the protocol asks for the first code in order, so E1 is reported. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: This article examines four English language syllabi from Indonesian higher education institutions
rationale: The study is a document analysis of four English syllabi, not an empirical experiment. It has no generative AI learner intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code; E1 could also be argued since AI is not learner-facing here, but the design is non-empirical and E6 is the primary failure.

quote: Participants wrote IEP goals in two conditions: participant-only and participant plus AI.
rationale: The content is IEP goal writing for special education, which is not a STEM domain under the protocol (no science, math, engineering, CS, or data science content). This is a clear failure on the domain criterion, so it is excluded as E2 at the abstract stage. The other criteria are not clearly failed on the abstract alone.

criteria.domain_note: University information chatbot, not STEM content

quote: EduChat, a chatbot system for university-related questions.
rationale: The chatbot answers general university-related questions (admissions, student life, academic programs), which is not STEM content. The abstract gives positive evidence the content domain fails, so exclude under E2 at abstract stage. The abstract also does not describe a learner-facing learning activity with a control group or learning outcome, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Comparative analysis of high and low performers’ use of generative AI in EFL academic writing
rationale: The study concerns EFL academic writing, which is language learning and not STEM content (E2). It is also a comparison of high and low performers' GenAI use with no evident control group without GenAI, and no quantitative learning outcome is described in the abstract, but the domain failure alone is sufficient for exclusion under the first-applicable-code rule.

quote: The review article followed the PRISMA method.
rationale: This is a narrative/PRISMA literature review of twelve documents, not an empirical study. It has no primary comparison group or quantitative outcome data to extract. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Review articles are also outside the eligible publication types. The code E6 is used as the first applicable code under the protocol order, since E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed or refuted from the abstract alone.

quote: The authors conducted a sociological survey of students at the Daugavpils University (January 2024, N = 423, excluding IT students)
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional sociological survey that classifies student attitudes toward AI into typological groups. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are perceptions and attitudes. Abstract gives positive evidence that the design and outcome criteria fail. Exclusion code E5 applied as the outcome is not a learning measure (design also lacks a comparison group, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order where the study is clearly non-learning; E3 would also apply to the missing control group). Per code order, E1 is not clearly established from the abstract, and E2 is not applicable since the topic is sociological rather than STEM content, but no STEM learning content is evident either.

quote: New research suggests that butterflies and moths come with mental baggage…left over from their lives as larvae.
rationale: The record is an essay/literary piece (a poem by Jana Prikryl followed by a reflective essay on AI, personhood, and law), not an empirical study. It describes no randomized or quasi-experimental design, no control group, no learners, and no learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Note the text is also garbled in places, but that does not change the decision. Exclusion is based on the first applicable code in order; E1–E5 are not positively evidenced as the study is not an intervention study at all, so E6 is the most applicable code.

quote: This study uses a qualitative method with a descriptive approach through observation, interviews, and documentation.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive study using observation, interviews, and documentation, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical comparison study. The exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code on the basis of the qualitative design; E3 and E5 would also apply. Domain is also unclear (Islamic religious education paper writing with Gemini). The record is excluded.

quote: Participants also completed a 10-item multiple-choice knowledge test before and after the AI session.
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 10 rheumatology trainees who completed a knowledge test and confidence survey before and after a ChatGPT session. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The design is a single-group pre-post quality improvement project. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract. The domain (immunology in a rheumatology training context) is also borderline but not needed for the decision.

quote: This research employed a quantitative explanatory approach involving 83 tenth-grade students
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/explanatory regression design (Multiple Linear Regression and Moderated Regression Analysis) on ChatGPT usage intensity as a continuous predictor, not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a non-generative-AI control group. There is no positive evidence of a separate control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Domain (Basic Banking, accounting vocational) is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion is made at abstract stage on the design/comparison failure.

quote: The quantitative approach and survey method was used, population of the study was students of Law School University of Gujrat.
rationale: The study is a survey of law students about their use and satisfaction with Pakistan Law Site, a legal database. It has no control group, is not a learning-outcome experiment, and law is not STEM. Per the protocol, the first applicable code in order is E1 if the tool is not learner-facing generative AI. The abstract gives no indication of generative AI; the PLS is a legal research database. Since E1 is not clearly established, I apply the first clear failure found: no quantitative learning outcome (only purpose, sources, and satisfaction are reported). Surveys with only perceptions and usage fail E5.
rationale_note: Coded E5 as the first clearly evidenced failure; the record also fails E2 (law is not STEM) and E3 (no control group), and generative AI use is not indicated.

quote: we evaluated the ability of ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5, Google's Bard, and Microsoft's Bing to perform on introductory-level college assessments
rationale: The study evaluates AI models directly on course assessments rather than learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity, and it compares AI performance against average student grades rather than a separate control group of learners. There is no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Abstract gives positive evidence of no learner-facing comparison design.

Abstract describes a Python programming domain (STEM) and a small language model integrated into a QA system for introductory Python courses, so generative AI intervention is plausible. However, the abstract reports no comparison group, no design, and no learning outcome data; it describes system development ("development process involves thorough data collection, strategic model training"). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text to check for a controlled comparison and quantitative learning outcomes. Venue is a journal, and the year is 2024, so date and publication type appear met.

quote: This study investigates the dual influence of ChatGPT and Self-Regulated Learning (SRL) strategies on the academic writing performance of students in Arabic Language Education programs.
rationale: The study is about Arabic-language thesis writing, which is non-STEM content (E2). It is also a quantitative survey with SmartPLS analysis, with no evident control group comparison or experimental design (design not met), so it would likely fail E3 or E6 as well. Under the rule that E2 is the first applicable code in order, the exclusion is E2.

quote: Findings reveal that students perceive AI tools as intuitive and beneficial to their learning
rationale: The abstract describes a predictive correlational survey of perceptions (TAM constructs) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence. Business administration is not STEM. Exclusion code reported is the first applicable in order; E1 is not clearly assessable from the abstract, but E3 (no control group) is the clearest positive failure at the abstract stage. Given the protocol's abstract rule, exclusion is justified by the explicit correlational survey design with no comparison group.

quote: Baseline survey data were collected from 568 faculty members, including 340 from China and 228 from Kazakhstan.
rationale: The participants are university faculty members taking faculty development training, not students. The protocol excludes in-service teachers and workplace training, so population fails. Exclusion code E4 applies as the first failing criterion (E1-E3 cannot be assessed as clearly failing from the abstract, and the population failure is positive evidence). Domain is also not clearly STEM from the abstract, but that is not the first applicable code.

quote: One group received HIF, while the other received traditional PF.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based hybrid intelligence feedback system (generative AI, learner-facing for reviewers) compared against a traditional peer feedback control group, which meets intervention and comparison. Participants are 58 pre-service mathematics teachers, which the protocol counts as higher education, so population and STEM domain appear met. Outcomes (SOLO-coded reflective writing, information entropy of attention, number of comments added) are plausibly quantitative, but the abstract does not give effect-size statistics, and the design (randomized or quasi-experimental) is not stated. Insufficient evidence to exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to check design, outcome measures, and data for SMD computation.

quote: This longitudinal qualitative practitioner study investigates literature teaching in an undergraduate English Philology program
rationale: Literature teaching in English Philology is non-STEM content, so E2 applies first in the protocol order. The study is also a qualitative practitioner study with no control group, no generative AI intervention (the abstract explicitly says AI was not investigated), and no quantitative learning outcome; these would support further exclusions, but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: This commentary considers the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies to music and the sonic arts.
rationale: The record is a commentary/critical essay on AI and music (Resonance journal), not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and is not STEM content. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) at the abstract stage, based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: Methodology: For this purpose, a quantitative approach was used with a descriptive study of data analysis derived through a measurement instrument such as the survey applied to teachers
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of teachers' perceptions of ChatGPT. Participants are in-service teachers rather than students, there is no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on several criteria exists. Exclusion uses E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the perception-only outcome is the clearest failure; the first-applicable code by order would arguably be E1 (teachers are not learners interacting with the tool), so E1 would be the strictly first-applicable code. Final code per protocol order: E1.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was administered to undergraduate healthcare students. Total 395 students participated in the study.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with correlational analysis and no separate control group without generative AI, so the design and comparison criteria are not met. Healthcare students are outside the STEM domain (health professions education is excluded). Abstract gives positive evidence of failure on design/comparison, so exclude. Using E3 as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering would be E2 for health professions content, but the protocol's code order places E1 (intervention) then E2 (content) first; the health-profession domain exclusion is the clearest first-failing criterion, so the code should be E2. Final code: E2.

criteria.rationale_note: Mixed-methods study of concerns, beliefs, confidence and interest; no control group described in the abstract.

quote: Design/methodology/approach AI literacy lessons were integrated into a technology integration course for preservice teachers, and the impacts of the lessons were evaluated through a mixed-methods study.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-course intervention evaluated via a mixed-methods study with no mention of a control or comparison group. Outcomes are concerns, beliefs, confidence and interest (affective/perceptual), with no quantitative learning measure stated. Positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion is present (no comparison group described, outcomes perceptual), so exclusion at abstract stage is supported under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that the abstract-stage rule favours inclusion when information is missing; the main basis is the absence of any comparison and perception-only outcomes.

quote: an AI-enhanced critical media literacy program implemented with fourth-grade students in a public primary school
rationale: The program is a critical media literacy intervention aligned with Turkish language and Social Studies curricula, not a STEM domain (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science). Under the protocol's domain criterion and the first-applicable exclusion code order, this is E2. Abstract also does not clearly report a control group, so comparison and design are unclear, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: Drawing on a multi-iteration design-based research study in an online Executive MBA programme, the study combines dialogic theory with quantitative and qualitative analysis
rationale: Abstract describes LLM-powered avatars used in an online Executive MBA discussion context, with reported "significantly increase" effects and learning outcomes. Intervention and population appear to fit, though the domain is not clearly STEM (MBA business content is not named) and the comparison group, design (design-based research, multi-iteration), and quantitative outcome cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text to check whether the content is STEM and whether a control group exists.
rationale_note: Domain is unclear at abstract stage; business content is not in the protocol's STEM list, so full text should verify.

quote: A structural model was developed and tested using survey responses from 260 students.
rationale: The study is survey-based with structural model analysis of perceptions (satisfaction, perceived learning performance). No quantitative learning outcome such as achievement is reported, and there is no control group described. Exclusion under E5 since outcomes are perceptions only. Design also appears non-experimental (survey/correlational), which would be a further failure, but E5 is the first applicable code in order given the outcome measure is perceptual.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; positive evidence of perception-only outcome.
quote_text: A structural model was developed and tested using survey responses from 260 students.
rationale_final: Survey-based structural model study measuring perceptions (satisfaction, perceived learning performance); no quantitative learning outcome and no comparison group evident.
quote_final: A structural model was developed and tested using survey responses from 260 students.

rationale: The abstract describes oral assessment practice and program design at Polytechnique Montreal. It does not describe a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or any quantitative learning outcome. The paper reads as a descriptive/position account rather than an empirical study. Generative AI is mentioned only as context for the disruption of assessment. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E1 could also be argued, but E6 best fits the abstract.

quote: A quantitative explanatory study with a cross-sectional survey design was conducted involving 312 undergraduate and graduate students
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with PLS-SEM on 312 students, with no experimental or comparison group that avoids generative AI. Positive evidence of failure exists for the comparison and design criteria, so the record is excluded. E3 is used because no control group without generative AI is described; the survey design would also fail the design criterion (E3 is the first applicable code in the order given, and the survey design is not a learning intervention study with a control group).

quote: a qualitative methodology was adopted, employing thematic analysis and focus group techniques
rationale: The study is qualitative (focus groups, thematic analysis) on students' views of ChatGPT in collaborative learning. It reports perceptions only, with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group, so it fails the outcome, design and comparison criteria. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first failing criterion among those that apply to the abstract evidence, since the study reports only perceptions. Note that E6 (not an empirical study) could be argued, but the study is an empirical qualitative study, so E5 is the better fit.

The record has only a title, venue, and year, with no abstract. The title ("From with-ness to readiness", "Spiral Ethics Protocol-Fourfold") suggests a conceptual or theoretical paper on writing with generative AI rather than an empirical study with a control group. Positive evidence of non-empirical design is inferred from the title alone and is weak, so this is a tentative exclusion. The record should be checked at full text if the researcher wants certainty; a conceptual framework paper would fail E6, and no STEM content or quantitative outcome is evident from the title.

Abstract describes a methods/how-to article demonstrating how generative-AI chat tools can build a classroom coin-toss simulation. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome data; it is not an empirical study. Exclusion at E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code given that the paper is a pedagogical demonstration. Note: the rule for abstract-stage exclusion requires positive evidence; the abstract gives positive evidence of no empirical design and no comparison group.

quote: This review synthesizes recent literature on the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and data science within bioinformatics-driven cancer drug discovery
rationale: The record is a narrative review of AI in cancer drug discovery. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and is not an education study. E1 would be the first code in order, but the abstract gives no learner-facing intervention, so I used E6 as the clearest positive evidence. Strictly, the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 (no learner-facing generative AI), so I note this ambiguity for the auditor; the decision to exclude is firm either way.
rationale_note: Code choice caveat: protocol says report the first code that applies in order E1 to E10. E1 arguably applies first because no learner-facing generative AI is described. Auditor should check.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice covering a whole special issue. The text does not describe the study design, sample, or outcomes of the chatbot-loneliness paper itself. Although the target article (Lu & Guo, 2025) is listed, the record offers no positive evidence that any criterion is met as an empirical study. The only substantive signal is that the article has been retracted, so it is not a valid empirical study. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) at abstract stage, with the note that a retracted article should be reviewed by the researcher before final exclusion. No prompt-like instructions were found in the record.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was administered to first- and second year medical students ( N = 157) at a single U.S. medical school in August 2024.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of student perceptions and familiarity with AI. It has no intervention in which learners use generative AI as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of design failure (survey, not experimental) is present, so it is excluded. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would technically be the first code to apply since no learner-facing intervention exists; however, the study is fundamentally a non-empirical-trial survey. Coding E6 (not an empirical study) would be a misfit since it is an empirical survey; the most accurate first-applicable code by the protocol order is E1. Consider re-coding to E1 at audit.

quote: The research methodology included qualitative analysis and a theoretical review of the literature.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual foresight model developed through qualitative analysis and a theoretical literature review. It reports no randomized or quasi-experimental design and no control group, so it is not an empirical comparative study. The single "empirical method" mention (essay creativity levels) lacks any comparison group. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study), with E3 (no control group) also apparent. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E6 is chosen since the paper is primarily a theoretical model proposal. Not a candidate at abstract stage on the evidence available.

quote: Research Method: Diagnostic survey using an electronic survey questionnaire.
rationale: The record is a diagnostic survey of students' knowledge and perceptions of AI. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only perceptions and usage. It is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the protocol's design rules). Because E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, I used it; E3 and E5 would also apply in substance.

quote: The system achieved 93.0% overall evaluation accuracy and sub-2-second AI response latency under typical load
rationale: The record describes a candidate evaluation and career guidance platform using Gemini 2.5 Flash for scoring. It reports system accuracy and latency, not a learning outcome measured in learners. No control group or comparison is described, and the design is a system implementation. The abstract gives positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured (E5), and the design lacks a comparison group. Excluding at abstract stage on E5 as the first clearly failing criterion in protocol order that the abstract supports.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; design not an experiment with comparison group.

quote: This research employed a descriptive qualitative method.
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative design using interviews and questionnaires with teachers, with no control group, no generative AI learner intervention (ChatGPT is only used by researchers to analyse interview data), and no learner quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparison meeting the design, comparison, or outcome criteria. Primary code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense is closest here given qualitative descriptive design; no comparison group also applies, but the first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention). Considering code order: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (ChatGPT used only by researchers for analysis), so E1 applies first.

quote: In a mixed-methods design, 565 education-major students in Chinese teacher-preparation programs completed an online survey, and five were interviewed.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with structural modeling of dependency drivers. It has no intervention and no control group that lacks generative AI, so no comparison exists. The outcome is dependency (perceptions/behavioral markers), not a learning measure. Design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract (no comparison group); E5 and design issues would also apply.
quote_text: 565 education-major students in Chinese teacher-preparation programs completed an online survey

quote: We selected 14 common questions and queried ChatGPT (ChatGPT-3.5-turbo mode) for answers, recording the generated responses
rationale: This is an expert rating of ChatGPT-generated answers to medical FAQs about systemic lupus erythematosus. There is no learner interaction, no control group, and no learning outcome; the ratings are subjective accuracy scores. The topic is health/medicine, not STEM. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the earliest clear failure that applies to the abstract evidence; E1 (learner-facing) would also plausibly apply since the tool was used by the researchers, not learners. Under abstract-stage rules, the evidence of failure is positive, so exclude.

quote: The methodology included the analysis of the work of 240 students and lecturers in Ukraine across educational programmes such as Software Engineering, Information Management Systems and Technologies, Computer Science and Technology, content analysis, and the isolation of student task performance results based on a survey
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive survey and content analysis of platform and tool usage preferences and perceptions, with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome (results are percentages of survey responses on preferences and perceived convenience). It fails the comparison and design criteria; E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI). Outcome criterion also appears not met since the reported measures are perceptions and usage. Abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Access to Surgical Care after Newly Acquired Insurance Enrollment
rationale: The record is a bundle of surgical health-services and health-policy abstracts (insurance enrollment, surgeon decision-making, kidney transplant outcomes, readmissions). None involves learners, generative AI, or a STEM learning outcome. The first abstract is an observational EMR cohort on insurance linkage and surgical care use. Per the protocol's exclusion-code order, the first failing criterion is intervention (E1), but no generative AI or learner-facing tool appears anywhere in the record, and the content is clinical/health services, which fails the STEM domain. Coded E2 as the clearest and most fundamental failure: the content is not STEM education. The record is not a study of generative AI in STEM learning.

Abstract describes LLM-based AI-supported physics lessons compared with a traditional-instruction group, with comprehension tests as outcomes. Physics is STEM. Nothing in the abstract indicates a failed criterion. Design (randomization or quasi-experimental status), student population level, and effect-size data are not stated and need checking at full text. Per the abstract-stage rule, include.

quote: The experimental group will engage in structured speaking practice using Grok Voice Mode, an AI-powered conversational chatbot, while the control group will follow the standard curriculum.
rationale: Generative AI chatbot (Grok Voice Mode) with a control group and pretest-posttest design, but the content is English-as-a-foreign-language speaking proficiency and speaking anxiety, which is non-STEM (language learning). Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code in order; E1 does not apply because the chatbot is learner-facing generative AI.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion is based on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: This study is a scoping review and uses the framework of Arksey and O'Malley as a guideline.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It is also nursing education, which is not STEM content (E2), but the first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention concerns ChatGPT in nursing education, so E1 does not apply. E2 (non-STEM content, nursing) would come before E6 in the code order, so the first applicable code is E2. Nursing is a health profession, outside the protocol's STEM domain.

quote: This paper offers a thorough examination of the incorporation of artificial intelligence, specifically ChatGPT, in the realm of physics education.
rationale: The record is a literature review ("This compendium synthesizes diverse literature"; "This paper analyzes both quantitative and qualitative research"). It reports no primary experiment with a control group and no effect data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Review articles are also ineligible publication types, but the first applicable code in order is E6 because the intervention and comparison criteria are not positively evidenced as an empirical design. Note: E1 through E5 were not positively evidenced as failing from the abstract alone; the review nature is the decisive factor.

quote: A workshop was designed and conducted to teach prompt engineering to 21 teachers enrolled in the English Language Teaching Methods course
rationale: The content is English Language Teaching (ELT), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study also describes no control group, no quantitative learning outcome (evaluation is of materials and reflections/focus groups), and the design is qualitative-style, but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: Future research will validate the podcasts through focus groups with Ugandan surgical trainees
rationale: The study describes developing AI-generated podcasts using ChatGPT and NotebookLM, with a needs survey. No learner-facing intervention is evaluated against a control group, no learning outcome is measured, and validation is only planned future work. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails design, comparison, and outcome requirements. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the best fit, since the work is a development/case description rather than an experiment. Note that the abstract also suggests a conference-style or short meeting abstract format (conference-like "462" numbering), which may be E10 at fulltext if confirmed.

quote: The sentiment labels were assigned using Grok AI, ChatGPT, and manual annotation, and the resulting datasets were used to build classification models using the Naïve Bayes algorithm
rationale: Generative AI (Grok, ChatGPT) is used by researchers to label sentiment in student questionnaire responses, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Fails E1. Also not STEM content, no learning outcome (classifier accuracy about labels), and no control group without generative AI. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

The abstract describes a descriptive exploratory design with questionnaire data from 60 undergraduates plus expert evaluations of projects. There is no control group, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment. This is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails (E3). Outcomes are perceptions of efficiency, creativity, and SDG clarity, which are not quantitative learning measures. Since E3 is the first applicable code in order, it is reported here, though E5 would also apply.

quote: The study involved 276 1st- to 6th-year students of the Medical Institute
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of medical students on chatbot use and psycho-emotional state. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Psychological scales are reported as correlates of self-reported use, not as learning outcomes. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI); the design is also a survey, which the protocol excludes. Code E3 is the first applicable code in the specified order for this record.

quote: A three-module professional learning program engaged teachers across three measurement waves
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers in a professional learning program, which the protocol excludes from the population criterion (E4). The abstract also reports a single cohort across three waves with latent growth modeling and no comparison group described, so comparison and design criteria are not evidently met. Although the abstract alone gives positive evidence of a non-student population, the exclusion is based on the population criterion only.

quote: Using qualitative research methods, data were collected from semi-structured interviews. A thematic analysis approach was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative design using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; findings are perceptions and attitudes. Under the protocol this fails the comparison and design criteria (and outcome). The code is assigned per the ordered list: no control group without generative AI is the first failing criterion reached in the sequence for this design (E3), though E5 or E6 would also apply because the study is non-experimental with no quantitative outcome.

quote: this article adopts an exploratory-descriptive, qualitative approach based on bibliographic and documentary research
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative, bibliographic and documentary analysis of programme-governing documents, with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study, so it fails on design and outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in protocol order that fits, since the work is a document/bibliographic analysis rather than an empirical learner study.

Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first, since the AI is not used by learners. The code is recorded as E3 in the output field, but the first applicable code in the protocol order is E1; the exclusion code should be corrected to E1 on audit.

quote: The study employs a mixed-method research design, combining quantitative and qualitative analysis through a pedagogical experiment involving control and experimental groups.

quote: Program ini dilaksanakan dalam dua sesi yang melibatkan metode interaktif
rationale: Community service program with a single group: a pre-survey of 40 students and a post-evaluation of five questions (85% correct). No control group is described, so the comparison criterion is not met (single-group design). Domain is general digital literacy/AI use rather than clearly STEM content. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code given the absence of any comparison group; the record is also a community service report rather than a clearly empirical comparative study.

Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a quantitative comparison design); the first applicable code in order would arguably be E1, since no learner-facing AI intervention exists, but the study's defining feature is its qualitative, non-experimental design.

quote: статья посвящена теоретическому обоснованию и методическому описанию программы внеурочной деятельности
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and methodological design article for a career guidance program. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no outcome data. Career guidance is also not clearly STEM content. Intervention (learner dialogue with an AI assistant) and population (6th grade) appear to fit, but E6 applies first in the code order.

quote: The students carried out linguistic investigations on a specially designed corpus and carried out corpus-based activities with automatic formative assessment within a Digital Learning Environment.

No control group without generative AI is mentioned, and the abstract reports only qualitative appreciation and skill development. The generative AI element is only mentioned as a future consideration and the students' use of LLMs is not part of the described activity. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports E3.

quote: this exploratory study examines the alignment between available online training and learning content and the skills demanded by jobs
rationale: The study is an LLM-based content analysis of 2549 MIT OpenCourseWare course descriptions matched to O*NET skills. No learners interact with the LLM, there is no control group, and no learning outcome is measured. It is not an empirical study of learning in the protocol's sense, so E6 applies. E1 (learner-facing AI) would also fail, but E6 is the substantive reason.

quote: Using a mixed-methods design, 83 training courses delivered between 2020 and 2025 in 24 public and private universities were examined through qualitative analysis, coding matrices, and hierarchical cluster analysis.
rationale: The study is a descriptive, exploratory document analysis of 83 university training courses for teaching staff. It has no learners interacting with generative AI, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Population is in-service university staff, not students. Code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible intervention/comparison design) is the first applicable code in this stage; the design is a typological mapping rather than a comparative experiment. Several criteria are clearly failing, so exclusion is supported.

quote: The Paediatric Regional Healthcare Information Platform (p-RHIP) was established in Halland, Sweden, to enhance paediatric health by identifying early risk factors in children aged 0–6 years.
rationale: This is a data resource profile describing an EHR/registry data platform. It fails the intervention criterion (E1) first, and this is also clear from the abstract. Exclusion is clear even at abstract stage, so the abstract-stage rule permits exclusion.

quote: A 23-item “Likert” survey (1–5) was administered to 35 graduate students after completing core-engineering tasks without AI assistance.
rationale: Single-sample survey study of 35 graduate students with perception-based Likert constructs; no control group that avoids generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome (constructs are perceptions, reliance, and derived indices). Design is survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Exclude at E3 as the first applicable code given no comparison group; the abstract also gives positive evidence of no learning outcome (E5) and a survey design, but E3 is listed first in the protocol order.

quote: This study examined how 16 Chinese transformational structures are generated using generative AI from the perspective of learners whose native language is Korean.
rationale: The abstract describes an evaluation of what several AI tools (Baidu, Papago, WRTN, Yuanbao) generate for 16 Chinese sentence structures. It reports no control group that lacks generative AI, no comparison between learners, and no learning outcome measured on participants. Comparison is absent by positive evidence, so E3 applies. Domain (Chinese language) is also non-STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in order is E1/E2 first; E1 is not clearly met since the tools may be learner-facing, and E2 is the first in order: Chinese language writing is non-STEM, which is positive evidence of failing the domain criterion. Applying the code order strictly, the domain failure is E2.

quote: Throughout the year, the Biochemical Society offers a programme of grants for all career stages supporting research, attendance at scientific conferences and the sponsorship of events.
rationale: The record is a society news/community article describing grant-funded events and personal experiences. It is not an empirical study: it reports no experimental design, no control group, and no learning outcome. Generative AI appears only as a seminar-series topic, not as a learner-facing intervention. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E1 could also be argued, but E6 is the primary failure.

quote: This study synthesises findings from 71 empirical studies identified through Scopus AI analysis
rationale: The record is a research synthesis/meta-analysis of 71 studies, not a primary empirical study with its own learner-facing generative AI experiment and control group. Under the protocol's exclusion list, reviews are ineligible, and the design is not a primary randomized or quasi-experiment. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) at abstract stage. Note that the abstract also mixes writing outcomes with adoption rates and institutional policy correlations, and the domain is graduate academic writing rather than STEM content, which would further argue against eligibility. Exclusion rests on the synthesis design, which the abstract states positively.

quote: After the intervention, a mixed 23-item questionnaire was administered; descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of the "Evaluation and use of AI" dimension revealed that 88 % of students believe AI should be didactically promoted in higher education
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group intervention with only post-intervention questionnaire data and descriptive statistics; there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (perceptions and self-reported competencies only). Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design (E3) is present, so exclude at abstract stage under E3 as the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported. Note that E3 precedes E5 in the code order, and the abstract gives no control group.

quote: Extensive experiments demonstrate that HKD-CPI outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in inductive CPI prediction tasks.
rationale: The record is a bioinformatics computational method for compound-protein interaction prediction. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies (first in order). It is also not an education study: the content is drug discovery, not STEM education, and there is no learner population or learning outcome. Excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention criterion fails.

Abstract describes a descriptive and chi-square survey of perceived AI use and self-perceived English proficiency among accounting students. No control group that avoids generative AI is described, and the design is correlational/survey rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Outcomes are self-perceptions rather than a measured learning outcome. Per the protocol, exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first code that applies on the abstract's positive evidence; the study also lacks a quantitative learning outcome (E5) and is survey-based (E6), but E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order.

quote: This article recounts in personal narrative form (Reed-Danahay, 1997) John's 'reflective practitioner inquiry' (Schon, 2017; Simanjorang et al., 2022) into his endeavour to employ ChatGPT for this novel purpose.
rationale: The abstract describes a personal narrative/reflective practitioner inquiry about a teacher using ChatGPT to design instruction. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group, no learner-facing use, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a non-empirical narrative account, so E6 applies. Design, comparison, and outcome are not met on the abstract's description.

quote: The purpose of this article is to provide examples of how teacher educators might reimagine assignments and activities in the era of AI text generators.
rationale: The article is a discussion/examples paper about designing assignments with AI text generators. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Special education preparation is also not STEM content, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the stated design-based check, so it is reported here. Per the coding order E1 is checked first; the intervention is not clearly a learner-facing study design, so E6 is the most direct failure.

quote: Drawing on a large-scale, cross-institutional survey involving 6,960 Australian university students (Henderson et al., 2025), this Pecha Kucha highlights students' perceptions of GenAI versus teacher feedback.
rationale: The record is a Pecha Kucha presentation based on a survey of student perceptions. Note the design is not an experiment, so E6 (not an empirical study) would also be defensible, but the study is empirical; E5 is the most direct reason.

The abstract does not state a control group or comparison design; it mentions 'traditional paper-based quizzes' only as a comparison for participation rates, and 'simulated empirical study' raises a design question. Measured outcomes include retention scores, which may be quantitative, but no effect statistics are given. Under the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances for full-text review.

quote: A genAI model assigned SDG relevance scores (0–1 scale) based on course learning outcomes, assessment tasks and summaries
rationale: The study uses generative AI only to map curriculum documents against SDGs. quote: Kelompok eksperimen menggunakan advance organizer berbantuan ChatGPT, sementara kelompok kontrol menggunakan model kolaboratif.
