quote: This white paper calls on researchers to get embedded in this work now, funders to require evidence generation as a condition of investment
rationale: The record is a white paper presenting a research agenda and priorities, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, comparison group, or learning outcome data. It is therefore not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the work is a position/agenda document rather than an empirical study.

quote: we conducted an exploratory study to assess students’ perception of using ChatGPT to support improving and reviewing their scientific paper writing
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory study of students' perceptions of ChatGPT use for paper writing. It reports no quantitative learning outcome, only perceptions, which fails the outcome criterion (E5). There is also no indication of a control group or comparative design, and the topic (scientific writing in requirements engineering) is not clearly STEM content. E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that the abstract clearly supports; the design/comparison failures are also apparent but the outcome failure is the primary basis.

quote: This quantitative correlational study involved 100 active students selected through purposive sampling.
rationale: The abstract describes a quantitative correlational study using simple linear regression on questionnaire data from one sample of students, with no control group that does not use generative AI. Correlational designs are excluded by the protocol, and no comparison group is described. This fails the comparison and design criteria; E3 is the first applicable code in order (E1 not applicable as ChatGPT is learner-used, E2 not clearly applicable since the domain is Islamic education, which is non-STEM, but the no-control failure is the clearest positive evidence). Note: the domain is Islamic education (PAI), which is not STEM, so E2 could also apply; E3 is reported as the first code supported by the design evidence in the abstract.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of a correlational design with no control group.

quote: Results demonstrate significant improvements across multiple dimensions: transforming passive learning into active experiences, delivering real-time actionable feedback, enhancing conceptual understanding and awareness of virtual teamwork
rationale: The abstract describes an HCD development study of a GenAI trainer with stakeholder interviews and testing with engineering students. It reports improvements but gives no indication of a separate control group without generative AI; the design appears to be a single-group development/testing study, which fails the comparison criterion. Virtual teamwork is also not clearly STEM content. Exclusion for E3 is based on positive evidence of no control group in the abstract, though this is a judgment from the described design.

criteria.outcome_note: Abstract reports only Likert-scale perceptions of effectiveness
criteria.domain_note: Economics education; STEM status not evident

rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of 65 students with no control group and no comparison condition, so it fails the comparison and design criteria (E3 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced; no quantitative learning outcome is measured, only Likert-scale effectiveness perceptions, which would also be E5). Domain is economics education, which is not STEM. Outcome is perception-based (effectiveness score from questionnaire), not a learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is reported as the first applicable in protocol order, since the absence of any control group is positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: This is a qualitative phenomenological approach; data were collected through non-participant observations and in-depth interviews with students and librarians from five universities in Pontianak.
rationale: Qualitative phenomenological study with observations and interviews; no comparison group, no intervention experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. Per the protocol, qualitative designs are excluded and the study is not an empirical experiment with a quantitative outcome. E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative, non-experimental design. Also not STEM-specific.

quote: we developed a web-based data visualization application that does not require users to have any prior programming knowledge
rationale: The abstract describes a classroom activity built around a web-based visualization app of CPS wage data. It gives no indication of a generative AI tool, so the intervention criterion fails on positive evidence. There is also no described comparison group or experimental design, and no learning outcome is mentioned. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not generative AI learner-facing. Not an injection.

quote: This study employs a quantitative approach using a symmetrical correlational research design.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational design with a single sample of 24 students measuring self-reported generative AI usage intensity against critical thinking. There is no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison criterion. The design is also correlational, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion reached after the intervention check. Per the abstract-stage rule, this is positive evidence of failure, so exclude is used rather than unsure.

quote: Data were collected from 400 undergraduate students in Bangkok Thailand selected through stratified random sampling.
rationale: Survey-based correlational study (technology acceptance model framework, multiple regression) with no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition and no learning outcome measure; only behavioral intention and self-reported usage. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group and survey design; E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits (no control group without generative AI). Domain is also not clearly STEM from the abstract.

quote: A comparative survey covered 178 pre-service mathematics teachers at Universitas Negeri Makassar (UNM, n = 89) and Universitas Negeri Jakarta (UNJ, n = 89).
rationale: The study is a survey-based scale development and institutional comparison of self-reported AI usage. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental control group without generative AI, and it measures perceptions/usage rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in order (no control group without generative AI); E5 (no learning outcome) and E6 (non-empirical is not applicable since it is empirical) also apply but E3 is the first in the protocol's ordering that fits the comparison/design failure.

quote: Psychiatric News spoke with several organizations to find out how they're using AI to speed completion of session notes
rationale: This is a Psychiatric News magazine news feature, not an empirical study. It reports organizational anecdotes and a summary of a JAMA Network Open report, with no controlled comparison and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also clinical rather than STEM learning and involves clinicians, not students. Excluded at E6 as not an empirical study; the first applicable code in order would be E1 for clinician-only AI use, but the record is fundamentally a news article, so E6 is the most accurate primary code.

quote: We present a programming plagiarism detector dedicated to GAI disguises.
rationale: The record describes a machine learning plagiarism detector that classifies student programs as GAI-disguised. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the GAI is the object being detected, not the learning intervention. There is no learning intervention or learner-facing GAI tool, so E1 applies. No quantitative learning outcome is measured either (classifier accuracy is not a learning outcome), but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: The research method applied here is descriptive qualitative, and data was collected through questionnaires.
rationale: The study uses a descriptive qualitative design with questionnaires, and reports no control group or quantitative learning outcome. It concerns stress relief, not STEM learning, and the Arabic Language Education program is non-STEM. Excluded on E6 as not an empirical study meeting the protocol's design requirements; the stronger failures are also noted (non-STEM content, no comparison group, affective outcome only). Under the first-applicable-code rule, E2 (content is not STEM) would precede E6 in order, so this exclusion code should be reviewed by the auditor. The abstract gives clear positive evidence of failure, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.
exclusion_code_note: E2 applies first in code order (non-STEM content: Arabic language education, stress/mental health outcome)

criteria.quote_note: R&D study with validity and practicality percentages; no control group or learning outcome described

quote: The results show that the developed learning media achieves a validity score of 98.1%, which is categorized as highly valid.
rationale: Development (R&D) study reporting validity and practicality percentages from expert and teacher/student questionnaires. The abstract describes no control or comparison group that does not use generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is single-group development. Positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion, so excluded under E3 (first applicable code in order is E1 check: intervention is generative AI used by learners, so E1 does not apply).

The record has a title and venue only ("Reaction: Navigating the path to reasoning laboratories", Chem, 2026) with no abstract. The title suggests a commentary or Reaction-style piece, which may fall under E6 (not an empirical study) or E10 (publication type), but the index gives no positive evidence that a criterion fails. Under the abstract-stage rule, this is unsure and should advance to full text for checking.

quote: the spring semester of 2025 (Generative Artificial Intelligence [AIGC]-assisted teaching mode)
rationale: Abstract describes a Java (STEM, programming) course with AIGC-assisted teaching for students and a final average score outcome (P < 0.01). However, the comparison is a prior-year cohort (spring 2024, traditional teaching) by the same teacher, which is a historical comparison and may be a quasi-experiment or a single-group pre-post design; the design and whether a comparison group exists cannot be determined from the abstract. Also, the publication is a 2026 journal article, within the date window. Not excluded at abstract stage; the design needs checking at full text.

quote: The SIPS Surgical Handoff System ... is a structured 4-step approach to the handoff meeting
rationale: The record is a bundle of unrelated abstracts (surgical handoffs, trial funding, NSQIP risk models, etc.), with the first being a withdrawn surgical handoff cohort study. None describes learners interacting with a generative AI tool, and none involves STEM education or a control group of students. Positive evidence of failure exists: the handoff system is a non-AI structured communication process, and surgical clinical practice is not a STEM learning context. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Note that the record appears to be a merged text dump; the surgical LLM/GPT-4o abstract concerns clinical prediction, not learners. Injection not suspected.

quote: The training, attended by 12 teachers, resulted in a significant increase in the average pre-test score from 62.5 to 84.2 in the post-test.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers (MTs teachers attending a training), which is excluded from the population criterion (E4). The design is also a single-group pre-post with no control group (E3 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E4? Note: the code order lists E1 (intervention) first, then E2, E3, then E4. Applying in order, E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage (ChatGPT is mentioned, but the learner-facing role is unclear), E2 is not clearly failed (domain not stated), and E3 applies because there is no control group, which is positive evidence of failure. Therefore the first applicable code in protocol order is E3, not E4. The decision is exclude on E3.

Abstract describes a literature analysis, staff experience, documentation review, and spatial analysis of field exercise routes. It is a descriptive/conceptual study with no experimental design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as a technological trend to adapt curricula to, not as a learner-facing intervention studied. Tourism/tour-guiding is also not clearly STEM. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6), the first applicable code in the stated sense of a non-experimental design; the abstract gives positive evidence that no controlled comparison exists.

quote: This study explores the implementation of a self-paced grammar instruction system supported by generative AI tools (ChatGPT and Google Gemini) in an under-resourced Japanese high school.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is about EFL grammar instruction, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The abstract also describes survey, progress-record, and observation data with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, which would separately fail E3 and E5. Excluding on E2 alone is sufficient.

quote: The study is survey-based cross-sect Crompton ional study conducted across various colleges.
rationale: The record is a survey-based cross-sectional study of undergraduate perceptions and usage of AI tools. It has no learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions, usage, and attitudes). Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) could be argued, but the primary reason is that it is not an empirical experimental study with a comparison group; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs) is the most apt single code for a survey design. Abstract gives positive evidence of survey design, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: We evaluate the use of GPT-3, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 ... for three related challenges pertaining to math word problems corresponding to systems of two linear equations.
rationale: The abstract describes model evaluation on classification, equation extraction, and problem generation accuracy. It reports no learner-facing use with a control group and no learner learning outcome; the measures are model accuracy. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies on the evidence available. Note that E3 (no control group) could also be argued, but the abstract gives no positive evidence of a comparison group, so E5 is the cleaner fit for the outcome failure. Abstract-stage evidence is limited; the record is a candidate for re-check at fulltext if the researcher prefers a stricter reading.

The abstract concerns local wisdom and cultural knowledge and literacy among prospective teachers, not a STEM content domain. Content is not STEM, so E2 applies. The abstract also gives no indication of a control group, a randomized or quasi-experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome, though these are not needed for the exclusion. Because E2 is the first applicable code in order, it is reported.

criteria.quote: Participants completed pre-and post-surveys assessing their confidence in lesson planning, revealing increased confidence levels after utilizing AI support.
criteria.rationale: Outcome is self-reported confidence and stress measured via pre-post surveys, not a quantitative learning outcome. The design appears to be a single-group pre-post with no control group described (E3 also plausible). Under the rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, the outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence; the design failure is also indicated by the abstract's description of pre-post surveys only. Coded E5 as the first clearly applicable code in the protocol's order that is supported by the abstract's outcome description; the record should be checked at full text if a reviewer disagrees on E3 versus E5 ordering.

quote: Participants completed pre-and post-surveys assessing their confidence in lesson planning, revealing increased confidence levels after utilizing AI support.
This article delves into a comprehensive analysis of the strategic initiatives within academic institutions
rationale: The abstract describes an analysis of institutional strategic initiatives across Italian and Mexican universities. It reports no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical learner-level study with a comparison group, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion uses E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code under the protocol's order, since the abstract describes a strategic/institutional analysis rather than an intervention study. Domain and learner-facing GenAI use are not clearly evidenced either way.

quote: This review article discusses the theoretical basis of heutagogy along with related concepts
rationale: The record is a review article (literature synthesis and theoretical discussion), not an empirical study with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical study requirement, so E6 applies. Its topic is heutagogy in general, with ChatGPT mentioned only as one example among many technologies, and it reports no comparison-group design.

criteria.comparison_note: No control group described; design-based research on GPT-4 assessment design

quote: Using a design-based research approach grounded in Evidence-Centered Design and the NGSA framework, we guided GPT-4 through structured development processes supported by interdisciplinary expert feedback.
rationale: GPT-4 is used by experts/researchers to generate science assessment tasks; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This fails the learner-facing intervention requirement (E1). The study also reports no control group and no learning outcome, but E1 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract gives positive evidence of the failure, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: We need something completely different: catalysing new innovations in teaching
rationale: The record is an editorial-style commentary on Scholarship of Teaching and Learning in psychology education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as background context. Not an empirical study (E6). Note the protocol's E10 (publication type not eligible) could also apply since this reads as an editorial, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: This interview with Professor Timothy Mitchison from a leading U.S. medical school explores his evolving use of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, in research and doctoral education.
rationale: The record is an interview reflecting on one professor's use of ChatGPT. It is not an empirical study: there is no control group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is under E6 (not an empirical study). Exclusion is justified on positive evidence from the abstract, not on missing information.

quote: This study assessed the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to transform Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) pedagogy in Lagos State
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic desk review and conceptual framework, not an empirical study. There is no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note: the criteria object above had a duplicate "domain" key; the intended values are domain unclear, and the intervention, population, and design fields reflect the abstract.

quote: The objective of this article is to comparatively analyze the impact of generative artificial intelligence (Gemini) versus algorithmic resolution applications (Photomath and Socratic) in the teaching and learning process of mathematics at the university level.
rationale: Gemini (a generative LLM) is compared with Photomath and Socratic (non-generative solvers) in university mathematics, which fits the intervention, comparison, population and domain criteria. The abstract reports precision/efficacy measures in calculus problems, which may count as a quantitative outcome, but it does not state a clear control group design or effect statistics. Design and outcome are therefore unclear at the abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text rather than excluded. Injection check: none observed.

quote: This review surveys peer-reviewed work on the integration of AI with indoor environmental quality (IEQ) and energy performance
rationale: The record is a narrative mapping review of building automation and energy management, not an empirical study. It is not about learners, STEM education, or a learner-facing generative AI intervention with a control group. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 could arguably apply first since the AI is building-facing rather than learner-facing, but the clearest and most fundamental failure is that it is a review, so E6 is reported. Criteria flags are approximate given the review nature.

quote: This themed issue brings together a collection of articles that explore these shifts from a variety of disciplinary and methodological perspectives.
rationale: The record is a themed editorial introducing a special issue on HRM in tourism and hospitality. It is not an empirical study and reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome. The mention of ChatGPT use in HR functions (Stergiou's contribution) concerns HR practice in hospitality workplaces, not learner-facing generative AI in STEM education. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the editorial also falls outside the STEM domain.

quote: A total of 538 articles were identified; of these, 206 were included after the full-text screening phase.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group. The abstract itself notes that most included studies were conceptual, and the review does not report any learning outcome from a controlled comparison. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's rules, and it is clear from the abstract.
rationale_note: Review article; E10 (publication type) could also apply as a review, but the protocol lists reviews under publication type exclusions. Given the protocol's exclusion list explicitly names reviews under E10, E10 may be the more accurate code.

quote: Theresa Carilli, PhD, is professor emerita of communication and creative arts at Purdue University Northwest.
rationale: The record is an interview with a playwright/media scholar about Italian American theater and identity. It is not an empirical study, involves no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's criteria for this kind of non-empirical record. Note that E1 would also technically apply since no learner-facing generative AI is present; the record is not empirical at all, so E6 is reported as the primary reason. The text is garbled in parts, but nothing in it suggests a prompt addressed to an AI system, so no injection is suspected.

quote: The dialogues of 24 PSTs are analysed through the concepts of telling (providing information or direction), assessment moves (to elicit student understanding), and advancing moves (to encourage deeper thinking) in teaching.
rationale: Preservice mathematics teachers interact with ChatGPT, a generative AI, so intervention and population and domain appear met. However, the abstract describes a qualitative discourse analysis of dialogues with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing comparison group and design (non-experimental, qualitative) is present, so exclude at abstract stage. Primary code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies first in the code order.

quote: This paper prompted ChatGPT-4 with 80 authentic college student counseling questions and collected three nondeterministic replies per query.
rationale: The study is an offline simulation in which ChatGPT-4 is prompted with student questions and its replies are scored by NLP models. No learners interact with the tool, there is no control group, and there is no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are warmth, empathy and sentiment of model outputs. Not STEM (school counseling). Coding the first applicable exclusion in order: E1 applies first, since the intervention is not learner-facing (the model is prompted by researchers, not learners interacting in a learning activity). Given the strict order, E1 is the first code that applies.

quote: Hints provided were sufficient to propel students forward and make progress on their assigned work, in most cases.
rationale: The abstract describes an LLM-based hint-generation agent workflow piloted with students, with no mention of a control group, comparison condition, or quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is absent from the abstract, but the description ("initial pilot testing", "sufficient to propel students forward") suggests a usability/feasibility report without a controlled comparison, so it fails the comparison requirement (E3). Outcome measurement is also not evident. Excluding under E3 at abstract stage on the basis of the pilot description; a full-text check could confirm.

quote: This qualitative phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of ESL students
rationale: Exclude at the first applicable code. Content is English as a second language, which is non-STEM (E2). The study is also a qualitative phenomenological design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3, E5 and E6 would apply as well. E2 is reported as the first code in the protocol order.

quote: melibatkan 45 orang guru
rationale: Participants are in-service elementary school teachers (guru sekolah dasar) in a training program, which the protocol excludes (in-service teachers are not K-12 or higher education students). The design also appears to be a single-group pretest-posttest evaluation with no control group, which would be E3 if reached first; however, the population exclusion E4 is the clearest positive evidence. Note the code order: E1 and E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract, so E4 is the first applicable code given the population is clearly not students. Journal is a community service journal, which is not a formal exclusion at abstract stage.

quote: Based on conversation and interviews with teachers of Nepali, English and Social Studies, this article uses lexical analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study based on conversations and interviews with 12 teachers and 16 students, using lexical analysis. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Subjects are Nepali, English and Social Studies, which are not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., a qualitative/descriptive design) is the first applicable code. Note that E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply; E6 is reported per the design, which is the primary failure. The record fails several criteria at the abstract stage.
decision_note: Exclusion ordering: E1 check first. The intervention (ChatGPT use by teachers and students) is not clearly learner-facing controlled; not decisive. E2 applies to content (non-STEM) and comes before E6 in the ordered list, so the first applicable code by protocol order is E2.

quote: A quantitative approach utilizing a One-Group Pretest-Posttest design was employed
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, which is a positive indication of E3 (single-group pre-post design). Domain (AC systems in vocational automotive engineering) is borderline for STEM but the design failure is sufficient for exclusion. Note that E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly supported; E2 is not asserted because the domain status is not clearly established from the abstract.

criteria.rationale_note: Case study design with a single group of 24 pre-service teachers; no control group.

quote: The method of the research is case study. The study group consists of 24 students.
rationale: Abstract describes a case study of 24 pre-service teachers using Microsoft Copilot, with data from reflective diaries, lesson plans and interviews. There is no comparison group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Qualitative design also fails the design criterion and no quantitative learning outcome is reported, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

No abstract is available in the index. The title suggests ChatGPT used for engineering biomimetic solution finding, but the title alone gives no evidence of a control group, a learner population, a learning outcome, or an experimental design, and the title reads as a theoretical framework paper. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text for checking.

The record describes KD-SecBERT, a knowledge-distilled encoder trained and evaluated for vulnerability classification on NVD/CVE/GitHub/OWASP data. It is a model development and benchmark study, not a learner-facing generative AI tool used in a learning activity. No control group of learners, no learning outcome, and no students are described. Exclude at E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI; the design also lacks any comparison with learners, so it is not an eligible study at abstract stage.

criteria.rationale_note: Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with six students; no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: A qualitative research approach was employed. Six students majoring in Electronics Engineering took part in semi-structured interviews to collect data.
rationale: The record is a qualitative interview study of six electronics engineering students about their perceptions of generative AI use. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions), and the design is qualitative rather than an experiment. Per the protocol's order of codes, E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) is the closest fit for a qualitative perception study that fails the design and outcome criteria; the abstract gives positive evidence that the design and outcome criteria fail, so it is excluded at abstract stage.

ChatGPT is used to grade student work, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Grading-only AI use is excluded by the protocol. Also, the domain is social sciences (Political Science, Public Administration), not STEM, and the outcome is AI-vs-instructor grade agreement rather than a learner learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The researcher used the descriptive comparative survey method and a questionnaire tool to collect data prepared by the researcher.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of teachers' perceptions of AI application use in gifted education. It has no control group, no learning outcome measured quantitatively (only questionnaire ratings of use, requirements and obstacles), and the participants are teachers rather than students. The design is a survey, not an empirical experiment, so it fails on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract. Note: the first applicable code in order would arguably be E1 (teachers, not learners, use the tools) or E3 or E5; E1 is the first in the protocol order that clearly applies because the AI use described is by teachers, not learner-facing. Because the protocol says to report the first code that applies in order, E1 is the correct code here.

quote: This scoping review mapped existing research to identify applications, strengths, limitations, and areas for future development.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review article and not an empirical study. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). It also reports no control-group learner outcome data from primary studies in the abstract. Pharmacology education is also arguably a health professions domain, which would be a further exclusion, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Clicker-integrated instruction is the current innovation in teaching and learning.
rationale: The intervention is clicker technology, which is not a generative AI tool. Nothing in the abstract indicates a generative model, so the intervention criterion fails on positive evidence (E1). Exclusion is based on the first failing code in order. Other criteria are not clearly assessable from the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; E1 applied as the first failing code.

quote: Semi-structured interviews with 16 students revealed GAI is primarily used for grammar, summarizing, brainstorming, and locating sources.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of undergraduate students' perceptions. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, and it is not an intervention experiment. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense: qualitative designs are excluded by the Design row); E6 is the closest code available given that the design is qualitative. Domain is also not clearly STEM (general research assignments).

quote: ChatGPT 4.0 was used to generate five multiple-choice questions using different prompts without learning objectives
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT) is used to generate exam questions; learners do not interact with the tool. The study evaluates question quality by item-writing standards, with no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Excluded at E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Other criteria also appear unmet (no comparison group, no learner outcome), but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This paper presents results of an analysis of how LLMs perform in evaluating student responses to legal analysis questions of the kind typically administered in law school exams.
rationale: Law school exam grading is not STEM content (E2). Also, the study evaluates LLM grading of exam responses rather than learners interacting with a generative AI tool, and there is no control group or learning outcome, so it would fail E1, E3, and E5 as well. The first applicable code in order is E1, but the abstract gives clear positive evidence of non-STEM content; the LLM is used by professors/graders, not learners, which is E1 by the protocol's own borderline rule ("AI used only by the teacher or researcher: E1"). Applying the code order strictly, E1 is the first that applies.

quote: This concept paper suggests a qualitative study of the academic writing scaffold of LG120 Generation Z undergraduate students in the scope of AI-based register translation.
rationale: The record is a concept paper proposing a qualitative study with semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. It is not an empirical study with a comparison group or a quantitative learning outcome. It has no control group and no quantitative outcome, and it is not STEM (academic writing). E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's checks that fits the design; the abstract gives clear positive evidence that the design is non-empirical and qualitative.
rationale_note: Multiple criteria fail; E6 is chosen as the most direct fit (concept paper, not an empirical study).

rationale: Abstract stage. The record has a title and venue only, with no abstract. The title suggests a general opinion or perspective piece on AI in higher education, which would likely be an non-empirical article (E6), but this is not established from the record. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded.

criteria.rationale_note: Single-group pre-post survey design with paired-samples t-tests on 46 students; no control group.

quote: pre- and post-surveys, paired-samples t-tests, and qualitative analysis of open-ended survey responses were conducted with 46 students
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 46 students measured pre and post with paired-samples t-tests and no comparison group. Per the protocol, a single-group pre-post design is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Although the abstract is clear on this, the exclusion is made on the design evidence given here.
decision_note: Exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence of single-group pre-post design.

quote: This community service program aimed to enhance the competencies of teachers at SMPN 1 Bojong, Pandeglang, in developing digital learning materials
rationale: Community service program training in-service teachers (participants are teachers, not students), which is excluded by the population criteria. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Under the code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed on the abstract, and E6 is the first clearly applicable code given the absence of any empirical design.

quote: APA 2025 Abstracts
rationale: This record is a compilation of many conference abstracts (APA 2025 Abstracts, Pancreas journal supplement) on chronic and acute pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer, not a single empirical study. None of the abstracts involve learner-facing generative AI, STEM content, or an education population. The record fails on intervention, domain and population, and it is not a journal article reporting an empirical study. Coded E6 as the first applicable code in order, since it is not an empirical study of a single design. Note that E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would also apply in substance; E1 is earlier in the code order, so under the protocol's first-applicable rule the code should be E1 rather than E6. Auditor should correct the code to E1 if they agree.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 301 university students across Cambodia.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey correlating self-reported AI tool adoption with perceived learning outcomes. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Outcome is perceived learning, not a quantitative learning measure (E5 also arguably applies), and the STEM domain is not indicated. Under the protocol's ordering, E3 is the first applicable code given the design failure.

quote: The 28‐item, six‐factor structure—self‐efficacy, outcome expectations, environmental support, autonomy, competence and relatedness—showed good fit (CFI = 0.992, RMSEA = 0.019).
rationale: The study develops and validates a psychometric scale using EFA/CFA/SEM on survey responses. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group and no learning outcome measure. Correlational/survey design, so it is not an empirical intervention study; E6 applies as the first failing code in order that fits (E1 cannot be confirmed as learner-facing GAI use from the abstract, but the design failure is clear). No quote supports a control group or learning outcome, so the quote is the psychometric description.

Abstract describes benchmarking ChatGPT's responses to existing assessment prompts from ten engineering subjects. There is no learner interaction with the tool within a learning activity and no control group without generative AI; the study is a performance benchmark of the model itself. No separate comparison group is described, so the comparison criterion fails on positive evidence. Excluded at E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that E1 could also be argued since the tool is not clearly learner-facing, but the abstract gives no learner-facing use, and E3 is the most direct failure shown.

quote: four matched feedback conditions were generated for 136 cases
rationale: Duplicate fields above were a mistake; this is the valid record. The abstract describes predictive modelling and offline evaluation of generated feedback messages with no described control group receiving non-generative-AI support and no learner learning outcome from an experimental comparison. Excluded under E3 on positive evidence of no comparison group; design remains unclear from the abstract.

quote: This study employs a systematic literature review method using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). No learner-facing generative AI experiment or quantitative learning outcome is reported. Reviews are ineligible under the publication-type rule as well, but the first applicable code in order is E6 (abstract stage, positive evidence of a review design).

quote: we propose a generative agent for CD (Agent4CD) in intelligent education that enhances interpretability and provides greater personalization and adaptability
rationale: The Agent4CD is a generative agent used for cognitive diagnosis, an assessment/modelling approach that infers learner knowledge state from performance. The abstract describes no learner-facing generative AI interaction within a learning activity; the LLM operates within the diagnostic model rather than as a tool learners interact with. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). No comparison group, STEM content, or learning outcome is described, so the abstract gives no evidence for other criteria. Excluded on E1 with reasonable confidence; a researcher should confirm at full text if desired.

The abstract describes a non-experimental, cross-sectional correlational survey (Pearson correlation on a 24-item questionnaire) with no control group. This is positive evidence of a failed design and comparison criterion. Exclude with E3 (no control group without generative AI). The design is also correlational, which would be E6-type ineligibility, but the protocol's first-applicable ordering puts E1 through E3 ahead of E6; intervention is not a manipulated learner-facing tool either. Outcome is self-reported ethics/use questionnaire scores, not a learning measure. Engineering students are STEM and higher education, so those criteria are met.

quote: The purpose of the study was to analyze the practical aspects of using artificial intelligence in higher education institutions of Ukraine.
rationale: The abstract is a descriptive/analytical overview of AI use in Ukrainian higher education, with no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Domain is also mixed and largely non-STEM (foreign language learning). Exclude at E6 as not an empirical study; the first applicable code in order would be E1 or E2 at most ambiguous, but the design failure is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms conventional retrieval-augmented methods in terms of scientific accuracy and age appropriateness
rationale: The study is a technical evaluation of a RAG-based Q&A generator. Its evaluation dimensions (scientific accuracy, age appropriateness, completeness, hallucination rate) are model-output quality measures, not learner outcomes. No learner-facing learning measure or learner control group is described, so no quantitative learning outcome is evident. Exclusion under E5 at abstract stage on positive evidence that the outcome is not a learning measure.
rationale_note: Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that outcomes are output-quality metrics rather than learner outcomes.

quote: This Community Service Program aims to enhance teachers' abilities in creating interactive AI-based learning media in early childhood.
rationale: The record is a community service program report describing training and mentoring of in-service early childhood teachers, with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content. It is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol order that clearly fails; the population is also in-service teachers (not students), which would fail E4, but E6 is reported as the first applicable code in order per the protocol. Actually, E4 precedes E6 in order is not the case: codes are checked E1 to E10 in order, so the first applicable code should be considered. Population (in-service teachers, not students) is E4, which comes before E6 in the list, so E4 is the correct code.

quote: This systematic review aims to provide a detailed and comprehensive overview of the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in K-12 education.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 197 studies, not an empirical study with a control group, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Reviews are also ineligible by publication type. The abstract gives no primary experimental design, comparison group, or learning outcome. Excluding under E6 at abstract stage is justified because the record itself is a review, which is positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: A pilot study using a mixed-methods explanatory sequential design was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pilot with usage logs and perception surveys and interviews, with no control group that lacks generative AI. The design and comparison criteria are not met. The outcomes are perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning measure. Domain is also unclear since nursing is health professions education, which is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by positive evidence.

The study concerns teaching French as a foreign language (language learning, non-STEM content), which fails the domain criterion. The abstract also describes perceptions, motivations and ethical views with no evident control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded at E2 as the first applicable code in order.
decision_quote: Teaching French as a foreign language

quote: This narrative review examines current applications, limitations, and ethical considerations and proposes a staged, competency-based curriculum
rationale: The record is a narrative review (Cureus, 2026), not an empirical study. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome data. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Psychiatry training is also outside the STEM domain, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order and the review design is decisive.
rationale_note: Domain is psychiatry, which is not STEM. E2 would also apply, but per the rule of reporting the first applicable code in order, E6 is listed as the primary reason. Note: E2 comes before E6 in the order, so the correct code under the protocol's ordering would be E1 or E2 first. Correction below.

quote: The research method used in this study was a quasi-experimental one involving 200 Japanese language learners
rationale: Content is Japanese language and intercultural communication for prospective migrant workers, which is not STEM (E2). The abstract also reports only paired-sample t-tests, with no clear separate control group, so the design is doubtful. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: The current article used real data to demonstrate the analysis and synthesis of Mixed Methods Research (MMR) data with generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI).
rationale: This is a methods tutorial demonstrating ChatGPT use for researchers' own data analysis, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group. The AI is used by the researcher to analyse data, not by learners as part of a learning activity, and there is no comparison group or learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study, so E6 applies; E1 would also fit since the AI is not learner-facing.

quote: Eleven batchelor level statistics students participated in a formative assessment, and six in a subsequent summative assessment.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based conversational assessment bot (generative AI, learner-facing) with statistics students in higher education, and a final exam outcome. The abstract states that students who used the bot performed significantly better, which suggests a comparison group, but it does not state the design (randomized or quasi-experimental) or confirm a non-AI control group. Abstract-stage rule: missing information is not evidence of failure, so unsure and advance to full text to check comparison and design, and the publication type (journal article is listed as Assessment in Education).

quote: The research design is a true experimental research design (True Experimental Research Design).
rationale: At abstract stage, the record appears to meet all criteria. Bachelor's students in a basic mathematics course were randomly or experimentally assigned to a ChatGPT-3.5 experimental group or a regular-lecture control group, with pre- and post-test achievement means and SDs reported. ChatGPT is a generative AI tool learners used alongside lectures. Mathematics is STEM. The abstract is in English, and the title is Thai, which does not trigger exclusion at this stage. Publication year 2024 meets the date rule. Journal type and full-text data sufficiency (group sizes and SDs are present) need confirmation at full text, but no positive evidence of failure appears in the abstract.

quote: Key performance metrics, including an intent recognition accuracy of 1.0 and a conversation accuracy of 0.812, illustrate the effectiveness of the chatbot.
rationale: The abstract describes a chatbot development study for university enquiries, reporting only system performance metrics (intent recognition and conversation accuracy), not a learning outcome measured in learners. No control group, no STEM content, and no learner-facing learning design is described. Excluded at the abstract stage under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The abstract gives positive evidence of no learning outcome and no comparison group; the study is a system evaluation rather than a comparative experiment, and the domain is general university administration rather than STEM.

quote: the use of ChatGPT prompts (D)
rationale: Abstract describes a university remote sensing (NDVI) practice in Biology students with groups receiving different follow-up strategies, one using ChatGPT prompts, and academic performance outcomes. Whether ChatGPT is learner-facing, whether a non-generative-AI control exists (groups A-B and C may serve as comparators), the design, and whether SMD data are reported cannot be determined from the abstract. No positive evidence of failure, so unsure to advance to full text.

quote: This community service program aims to enhance the competence of junior high school Indonesian language teachers in Tanjung Jabung Timur Regency in utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI) for developing learning assessment instruments.
rationale: The study is a community service training for in-service Indonesian language teachers, with AI used to develop assessment items. Content is Indonesian language, which is non-STEM. It is also not a controlled learner-facing study with a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E2 as the first applicable code in order (E1 is arguably also applicable since AI is used by teachers to prepare materials, but E2 is the clearest positive evidence and the content failure is unambiguous). Note: under the protocol order, E1 comes before E2; the teacher-only use of AI for materials preparation is positive evidence of E1, so the correct code is E1.

quote: A Call to Support Informatics Curricula in U.S.-Based Residency Education
rationale: The record is a commentary/call-to-action article on clinical informatics residency education. It describes no experiment, no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome data; the only mention of a survey is a procedural note. It is not an empirical study, and it is also in a medical residency context (health professions) rather than STEM. Excluded under E6 as the first applicable code in the given order is E1 (no learner-facing generative AI), so strictly the first applicable code is E1; however, the record is not an empirical study, so E6 is the most accurate single code.

quote: Data were collected via an online survey of 718 university students across various fields and analyzed using structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4.
rationale: Survey-based cross-sectional study using SEM on self-reported intention, self-efficacy, and perceived control; no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is entrepreneurship, not STEM. The design is a survey, which the protocol excludes; the closest code is E6 (not an empirical study is not strictly accurate, but no listed code fits a survey better). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design, with no learning outcome and no comparison group. Note: the code choice is the most applicable under the listed codes; E2 (non-STEM content) also applies clearly and is arguably the first failing criterion in the code order only if E1 is not triggered. Per code order, E1 is unclear (ChatGPT adoption is self-reported use, not an assigned learner-facing intervention), so E2 would be the first applicable code.

quote: The implementation method was carried out through Participatory Action Research (PAR) involving 26 teachers and students from SMAN 4 Barru.
rationale: The study is a Participatory Action Research training activity with a single-group pre-test/post-test of in-service teachers (not students). No control group is described, the population is in-service teachers (excluded), and the content is biology-related teacher training rather than learner-facing STEM learning. Several criteria fail on positive evidence. Exclusion code chosen: E6 is the first applicable code on reading order, but the strongest failure is population (E4) and comparison (E3); under the code order E1 is not clearly applicable since the AI is taught to teachers, which arguably is E1 (AI used only by teacher / not learner-facing). Given the strict order, E1 applies first: the AI tools are used by teachers in training, not learner-facing.

quote: This study uses a non-experimental quantitative survey design.
rationale: The study is a non-experimental survey measuring perceptions (PU and PEOU) of ChatGPT in English-education writing. It has no control group, no learning outcome, and is not STEM content. The primary failing is that it is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria; under the ordered codes, E1 (generative AI is learner-facing, so not applicable), E2 (English writing is non-STEM) would apply first. Applying the codes in order, the first applicable code is E2 because the content is English writing, not STEM. Correction: the first applicable code in order is E2.

criteria.rationale_note: Descriptive survey with Likert questionnaire; no control group

quote: This research employs a quantitative approach with a descriptive method.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive quantitative study using a Likert-scale questionnaire on 75 students, with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. The design is a single-group descriptive survey, not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Perception-based questionnaire results (TAM indicators) are not clearly a learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI); the design also fails the protocol's comparison and design criteria.

quote: This study explores the role that English for Academic Purposes or EAP plays in enhancing the academic writing skills of Chinese students.
rationale: The record is a review of current practices (title says "A review of current practices and future directions") with no primary empirical study, no control-group comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. It is not an empirical study, and the content is English academic writing rather than STEM. Excluded under E6 as the first applicable code; E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply.
rationale_note: Decision is clear from the abstract.

quote: The article reflects on experiences with portfolio assessment, highlighting challenges such as students' reading and writing practices, the integration of artificial intelligence, and feedback quality.
rationale: The abstract describes a reflective/experience-based article on portfolio assessment in physiotherapy education, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparison design; generative AI is mentioned only as a challenge. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the abstract also does not describe a comparison group or any quantitative outcome, so E3/E5 would also plausibly apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in order given the reflective nature of the article. Domain is physiotherapy (health professions), which may itself fail E2.

quote: Using a pre-test and post-test design, alongside interviews, the research evaluates students' writing performance and attitudes toward using AI in their writing practice.
rationale: The study is about IELTS essay writing, which is English language learning and non-STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). The abstract also describes a pre-test/post-test design with no mention of a control group that does not use generative AI, which points to a single-group design (E3 would also apply), but E2 comes first in the code order and is clearly met from the abstract.

quote: The English-Ukrainian translation of scientific and technical literature using ChatGPT-5.3 has been tested.
rationale: Abstract describes a professional translator testing ChatGPT on translating scientific and technical texts. The content is translation studies, not STEM learning content, and the user is a professional translator rather than a learner. No control group, learning outcome, or learner population is described. Exclusion under E2 (content not STEM) as the first applicable code; the study is also not a learner-facing learning activity with a comparison group.
rationale_note: Abstract stage exclusion; positive evidence of non-STEM domain (translation studies) and no comparison group or learning outcome.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was carried out with 220 university respondents
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of AI tool use and self-reported productivity, with no intervention and no control group. Correlational/survey design fails the Design and Comparison criteria. Excluded on E3 as no comparison group without generative AI exists. Outcome is self-reported productivity rather than a learning measure, and the domain (research activity across five disciplines) is not clearly STEM.

quote: The aim of this study is to examine ChatGPT's evaluations of pre-service science teachers' designs within an AI-supported experiment design process. The study was conducted using a case study design, one of the qualitative research methods.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study with content analysis of designs and ChatGPT interaction texts. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical quantitative study under the protocol. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first applicable code in the order given; E3 and E5 would also apply on the same evidence, but E6 is the most fundamental. Abstract stage positive evidence of failure is present, so exclude is appropriate.

quote: This study investigates the ways in which engineering faculty members and students in Eastern Visayas, Philippines, adopt and use artificial intelligence (AI) tools
rationale: The study is a descriptive-correlational survey of adoption and usage rates among faculty and students. It has no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition and no learning outcome measure; it reports only adoption, usage, and perceptions. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also fails as a survey, but E5 is the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering given the abstract's content.

quote: A thoughtful discussion of AI in psychiatry requires an in-depth look into the technology itself.
rationale: The record is an opinion/commentary piece in Psychiatric News (editorial-style article by a psychiatry resident) discussing LLMs. It reports no study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that it is a non-empirical commentary.

quote: Adopting an exploratory qualitative research paradigm, this study used a combination of purposive and maximum variation sampling strategies to recruit n = 55 undergraduate and postgraduate students
rationale: Qualitative grounded-theory study with semi-structured interviews and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code; the design also fails the protocol's Design and Outcome criteria. Note the record's stage is abstract, and the exclusion is grounded in explicit positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: The study used a descriptive qualitative approach with data collection techniques in the form of observation, interviews, documentation, and questionnaires
rationale: Abstract gives positive evidence of failing several criteria. The study is a descriptive qualitative design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The content is Arabic language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. Generative AI use by students (ChatGPT) is present, and the population is higher education.
exclusion_code_note: E2 is first applicable code in protocol order (E1 not applicable; intervention is learner-facing GenAI)

rationale: Study concerns English as a second language (EFL) oral communication skills, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so it fails the Domain criterion and is excluded under E2. Also, the abstract describes a questionnaire and observation quantitative design with no clear comparison group, which would raise E3 and E5 concerns, but the first applicable code in order is E2 as written in the protocol. Ordering rule: E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage; E2 is the first clear positive failure.

quote: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis tren publikasi, struktur tematik, serta celah penelitian ChatGPT dalam pendidikan matematika berbasis data Scopus periode 2023–2026.
rationale: The study is a bibliometric analysis (VOSviewer co-occurrence of author keywords) of 85 Scopus articles. It is not an empirical study of learners interacting with generative AI and has no control group or learning outcome measure. Under E1 the intervention is not learner-facing AI in any study it reports, but the decisive reason is that it is a review-type bibliometric analysis, so E6 applies as the first failing code in the order needed (E1 is not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the cleanest fit).

quote: Automated Essay Scoring (AES) and Automated Writing Evaluation (AWE) systems for English as a Second Language (ESL) learners
rationale: The review concerns ESL writing feedback, which is language learning and not STEM content. This fails the Domain criterion, so it is excluded under E2. It is also a meta-review rather than a primary empirical study, which would be a further problem under E6, but the first applicable code in order is E2. Note that the E1 check is not clearly failed at abstract stage since AES/AWE is not clearly generative, though large language model-based systems are mentioned among tools.
exclusion_code_note: E2 precedes E6 in the protocol order; E1 not clearly met but not positively failed.

quote: Students wrote a newspaper-style synthesis without AI (baseline), then completed a parallel task after explicit DISCO training with permitted ChatGPT (GPT-4) use.
rationale: Single-group pre-post design with no control group (the abstract explicitly states "no control group"). Per protocol and borderline rules, one group measured before and after is E3. Domain (upper-division biology writing) is also questionable as STEM content, but E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: EduGrader, an open-source, multi-model grading platform integrating several LLMs
rationale: The AI is used for grading student responses (AI used only for grading), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies. Also no control group or learning outcome is evident; the Pearson correlation with human graders is an agreement measure, not a learning outcome. Exclusion on E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: A one-group pretest–posttest design was used to evaluate teacher learning gains.
rationale: The study's participants are in-service teachers (91 teachers at a pesantren), which the protocol excludes from the population. The design is also a single-group pretest-posttest, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (E3 would also apply). Under the rule that exclusion codes are reported in order, E4 is the first applicable code listed for this record, because the population failure is the earliest criterion that clearly fails in the protocol order. Note that E3 would also apply; the first-in-order rule points to E4 since the protocol's exclusion codes are listed E1 through E10 and E4 precedes... (Correction: E3 precedes E4 in the code order, so the first applicable code is E3.)

quote: Through a comprehensive systematic review of literature spanning from 2010 to 2026, including empirical studies and case analyses
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper and systematic review of literature, not an empirical study with a control group and a quantitative learning outcome from its own data. It has no comparison group design, so the record fails the design and the empirical-study requirement. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies. The reported percentages come from the reviewed literature, not from an included experiment.

quote: Following the success of the first two conferences online, in 2023 the network organized its first fully in-person event on the theme of Cultivating the Possible: Reimagining Education and Society.
rationale: The record is a conference report/editorial overview of the 3rd International Conference of Possibility Studies. It is not an empirical study: it reports no experiment, control group, participants, or learning outcome. A generative AI keynote is mentioned only descriptively and does not make it an eligible study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). It would also fall outside publication type eligibility as an editorial-style conference summary.

quote: Getaneh Alemu is an experienced Cataloguing and Metadata Librarian with over two decades of experience in higher education and libraries.
rationale: This record is an interview with a practising librarian about AI in cataloguing. It is not an empirical study: it has no comparison group, no learners, and no learning outcome. It fails the protocol's design and outcome requirements, so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are not assessable from this text.

quote: This paper explores academic integrity assurance through the lens of “effect types”.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/theoretical discussion of academic integrity and assessment design using an analogy with compiler optimisation and effect types. It reports no empirical study, no intervention with learners interacting with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under E6 (not an empirical study), it is excluded. Earlier codes were considered, but E1 cannot be confirmed as a positive failure from the abstract, and E6 is the clearest first applicable code.

quote: The study adopted a quantitative approach, employing survey method in critically evaluating the role of AI in transforming physics pedagogy, through the lens of teacher perceptions and systemic implications.
rationale: The study is a survey of 141 physics teachers measuring perceptions, not an experiment with a control group or a learner outcome. Population is in-service teachers, not students. Per the protocol, survey designs and perception-only outcomes are excluded. E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) is the closest code; the design is a survey, which the protocol lists as excluded. Abstract-level evidence is sufficient to exclude.
rationale_code_note: E6 chosen because the design is survey-based and non-experimental; no learner quantitative outcome exists.

quote: This study investigates the potential of LLMs like ChatGPT for qualitative data analysis, focusing on open, axial, selective coding, theme or pattern identification, and inter-rater reliability.
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT used by researchers for qualitative coding of data, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. This is research-tool use, so E1 applies. The abstract also shows no control group, no learner population, and no learning outcome, and the content is qualitative-research methodology rather than STEM. Those points are not needed for the exclusion, since E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Comparative analysis of learning outcomes between 2023 and 2024 revealed a statistically significant improvement in final exam scores from 14.40 to 22.36 points (p < 0.001).
rationale: Generative AI (ChatGPT) use by university learners in a software education course with a final exam outcome. However, the comparison appears to be a 2023 cohort versus a 2024 cohort, which may be a historical control rather than a concurrent non-generative-AI comparison group. The abstract does not state whether the 2023 group was a control without generative AI, nor whether the design is a quasi-experiment. Domain (software education, liberal arts) is plausibly STEM-adjacent but not clearly stated. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so unsure; resolve at fulltext by checking the comparison group and design.

quote: I suggest that finding a proper framing of the phenomenon at issue would be a helpful starting point for such analysis.
rationale: The record is a legal/conceptual commentary on LLMs and framing, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, comparison group, or learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Its focus is copyright and creativity rather than STEM learning.

quote: We designed a randomized controlled trial, in which adult high school students attempt to solve CME tests across six medical specialties
rationale: This is a trial protocol (registered report) with no results yet: "As of October 2024, the acquisition of data and students to participate in the trial is ongoing." It is not an empirical study with outcome data, so E6 applies. It also targets medical CME tests for physicians/laypersons in medical specialties, which falls under health professions education rather than STEM, and the population is not clearly K-12 or higher education students. Only the first applicable code is reported per protocol order; E6 is the first code that clearly applies given the explicit protocol status.

quote: Investigating AI Writing Tools in Enhancing Academic Writing Skills of Diploma in TESL Students of a Private College in Malaysia
rationale: Content is academic writing for English as a second language (TESL), which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The design also appears to be a single-phase survey with correlation and regression, not a controlled comparison with a non-generative-AI group (would be E3 as well), but E2 is the first applicable code. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: VocQGen is an automated tool designed to generate multiple-choice cloze (MCC) questions for vocabulary assessment in second language learning contexts.
rationale: The tool generates vocabulary quiz items for second language learning (Academic Word List), which is language learning rather than STEM content. This is a positive failure of the domain criterion, so exclude under E2. Also, the tool is used to generate questions for assessment and the abstract describes expert review and pilot testing rather than a learner-facing generative AI intervention with a control group, so other criteria are unclear. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly met.

quote: This research uses a quantitative approach with a correlational (associative) research type.
rationale: The study is correlational, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Its content is fantasy makeup theory (beauty/cosmetology), which is not STEM. Under the exclusion-code order, E2 (content not STEM) is the first code that applies, since it is checked before E3 and E5. Note that the design also fails E3 and the study is correlational, but the first applicable code in order is E2.

quote: Установлен положительный дидактический эффект от внедрения чат-ботов в форме увеличения количества верных ответов на задания по изученной теме.
rationale: Abstract stage. Mathematics (integration) with university students, and a quantitative outcome (number of correct answers) is reported. The chatbot is described as a scenario/decision-tree bot with graphic cards, which may not be generative AI; the abstract later mentions LLM models only as a future stack direction, so intervention status is unclear. The abstract does not state whether a control group existed (the "pedagogical experiment" could be pre-post only), so comparison and design are unclear. Per the abstract-stage rule, these unresolved points warrant advancing to full text rather than excluding. Language is Russian with an English abstract; language is not judged at this stage.

quote: Finally, the paper presents the results of a small-scale survey among students, gauging their experiences using GenAI for individual and collaborative tasks
