rationale: The record self-describes as a review, which is not an empirical study. Its abstract reports no original experiment with a control group. It is also not clearly generative AI (adaptive tutoring), and its STEM focus is not stated. The primary exclusion is E6 because it is a review, which the protocol lists as ineligible publication type; E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code in the ordered list. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a review design.

quote: The objective of this study was to determine the relationship between artificial intelligence dependence (AID) and abstract reasoning ability
rationale: The study is a descriptive correlational design measuring AI dependence against abstract reasoning and dysexecutive behavior. There is no experimental intervention in which learners use a generative AI tool, and no control group without generative AI. Exclusion code E3 applies because there is no comparison group; the design is correlational, which also fails the design criterion. Domain (psychology) is not clearly STEM. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: This has led the present study to develop a survey research method to assess students' misconceptions on basic stoichiometry.
rationale: Survey study assessing student misconceptions in chemistry. No generative AI intervention, no control group, and no experimental design. Exclusion code E1 is applied as the first failing criterion in order: no learner-facing generative AI is described.

quote: I can’t tell you what a huge pleasure it is to be with you all today celebrating the 40th anniversary of the Program on Negotiation.
rationale: The record is a keynote speech transcript about the history of the Program on Negotiation. It is not an empirical study: it reports no intervention, no comparison group, no design, and no learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). It also has no generative AI content, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the record is not empirical research. Other criteria are not applicable.

quote: Many teachers have not yet optimally adopted AI-based applications due to limited knowledge, skills, and experience in using such technologies.
rationale: Participants are in-service vocational school teachers (training for teachers), which the protocol excludes from the population criterion (E4). The study is also a single-group pre-post design with no control group (E3 would apply), and the content is teacher AI literacy rather than STEM learning. Per the instruction to report the first applicable code in order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract; E3 is the first code in order that is clearly positive evidence (single-group pre-post, no comparison group), but E4 is the most direct population failure. Reporting E4 as the population criterion is clearly not met, and the abstract gives explicit evidence that the sample is in-service teachers.

quote: This study examines how lecturers and students discursively construct generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as either a threat or a partner in higher education
rationale: The study is a Critical Discourse Analysis of 124 statements about GenAI from lecturers and students. It is a qualitative discourse study, not an empirical experiment with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It has no comparison group and no learning measure, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative/quantitative design). Note that the protocol's E6 is "Not an empirical study"; this discourse analysis is empirical but qualitative, so the closest code is E6 as the design is qualitative, which the protocol treats as ineligible. Exclusion is clear at abstract stage because the abstract describes qualitative discourse coding with no control group and no learning outcome. Note also that E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply; E3 would be the first code in order only if E1 and E2 do not apply, and E1 and E2 are not clearly applicable, so the ordering rule gives E3 as the first applicable code in sequence. Reviewer should check code choice.

quote: Here, we suggest that the use of such tools might prove particularly valuable for instructors of physiology and pharmacology
rationale: The abstract is a perspective/tutorial paper that proposes tools for instructors to build browser-based interactive content and gives no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Physiology and pharmacology are also not clearly STEM under the protocol, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the decision basis here.

Abstract describes ancient art history education, a humanities topic, not STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract is also a case study and proposal of classroom activities with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome, which would fail other criteria as well. Per protocol order, E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Services in Creative Tasks for Teaching Russian as a Foreign Language
rationale: Content is Russian language learning and creative writing (non-STEM), which fails the domain criterion (E2). The intervention (generative AI visualization) and learners are plausibly met, but the domain failure is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's exclusion list... Note: E1 is checked first; the intervention is learner-facing generative AI (GPT-4), so E1 does not apply. Comparison and design are not described in the abstract, but the STEM failure is sufficient for exclusion.

decision_rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT-based Question Checker) is used by instructors to validate test questions, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No control group, no learning outcome; the study is a tool application/demonstration validating nine questions. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing.
quote: The custom ChatGPT application, named Question Checker, was developed to validate questions generated by instructors.
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT-based Question Checker) is used by instructors to validate test questions, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. There is no control group and no learning outcome; the study demonstrates a tool on nine questions. Excluded under E1 because the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: The study is based on a systematic scoping review of scientific publications from 2021 to 2025.
rationale: The record is a systematic/scoping review of published literature, not an empirical study with a control group. Its reported effects (e.g., 60% productivity gain, 90% positive student evaluations) come from cited sources and are perception or non-comparative figures. No eligible design or comparison is evident, so it fails as not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits this record; the first checks (E1, E2) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

Abstract describes a digital literacy/social media community service workshop using generative AI tools (NotebookLM, Pippit AI, Suno AI). Content is digital literacy and cyber safety, not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. Also, the design is a participatory action research workshop with no described control group, and outcomes are described as behavioural shifts without a quantitative learning measure, which would be further grounds for exclusion (E3/E5). Exclusion on the E2 ground is sufficient.

quote: Based on pre-test and post-test scores, there was an improvement in participants' scores.
rationale: The study is a community service training program for teachers (in-service) with a single group measured pre- and post-test, with no separate control group. The protocol excludes single-group pre-post designs (E3) and in-service teachers as a population. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Exclusion is justified on the abstract alone because the design is positive evidence of a single-group pre-post design.

quote: Empirical questionnaire method was used to identify the ability and readiness of students (N = 116)
rationale: Study is about foreign language (non-STEM) writing and mediation skills with chatbots, so E2 applies (first failing code in order should be checked: E1 is unclear since chatbot use is described as a learning activity, so E2 is the first clear failure). The design is a descriptive survey with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (self-assessment questionnaire), so it would also fail E3, E5 and E6 but those are secondary to the first applicable code.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: This paper examines the multifaceted ethical challenges arising from the integration of generative AI in academic writing, with a specific focus on the second language (L2) PhD students.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/ethical discussion paper with no empirical design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). It also concerns academic writing rather than STEM content. Positive evidence of non-empirical design is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: Title Index
rationale: The record is a journal table-of-contents/title index listing many unrelated article titles from Journal of the Chinese Medical Association, not a report of an empirical study. It contains no description of a generative AI intervention, a control group, or a learning outcome. The only AI-related item is a title ("ChatGPT's innovative application in blood morphology recognition") with no abstract, and it is not a learner-facing study design evaluation. The record is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Note that the record is an index page, not a single article, and the abstract gives no evidence of a learning study.

quote: This article presents a quasi-experimental analysis examining the effect of using the artificial intelligence Claude to reinforce arithmetic operations in seventh-grade elementary school students.
rationale: At abstract stage, the record shows a quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups using Claude (a generative LLM chatbot) for seventh-grade arithmetic, with pre- and post-tests and 2025 publication date. No positive evidence of a failed criterion. Data sufficiency, publication type (journal article vs. other), and language of full text cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but are not grounds for exclusion here. Include for full-text review.
criteria_fields_note: Criteria keys for data, language, and publication type are not in the schema; they were recorded as unclear in the rationale.

quote: This study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive research design.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive study using interviews and documentation with English teachers. It is not an empirical quantitative study with a control group or learning outcome. Participants are in-service teachers, not students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a quantitative comparative design); E4 and E5 also apply but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the qualitative design. Note the protocol ordering places E1 first; the intervention (teacher-only use of ChatGPT for planning) would itself be E1 since AI is used only by the teacher to prepare materials, which precedes E6 in order.

quote: This literature review investigates how AI supports communicative skills in EFL education
rationale: The record is a theoretical literature review of 25 studies, not an empirical study with a control group. It is also non-STEM (EFL language learning), which the protocol excludes. Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 and E2 would be checked first, but the abstract gives clearest positive evidence of E6 (review, not empirical). E6 is the first code that clearly applies to the design; the domain failure (language learning) is also noted as a further exclusion reason.

The study constructs and validates an AI literacy competency framework using grounded theory, EFA, and CFA on questionnaire responses from 586 undergraduates. It has no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a survey-based psychometric study rather than an experiment. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design and outcome criteria fail, so it is excluded. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) would be checked first, but the abstract provides no intervention with learners interacting with generative AI, so the most fitting first failing code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense of an eligible design), though E3 (no comparison group) also applies.

quote: This training program aimed to enhance the skills of Tunas Jakasampurna School teachers in developing High Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) questions
rationale: Participants are in-service school teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. The study is also a single-group pre-post training evaluation with no control group (E3 would also apply), but E4 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order. Domain is not STEM-specific in the abstract (HOTS question writing generally), and the abstract gives no control group. Decision is based on positive evidence of the population failing.

quote: We created an online forum known as "Universal Chemistry Network" to enhance communication among students and teachers in organic chemistry classes.
rationale: The intervention is a web-based discussion forum for student-student and student-teacher communication. Nothing in the abstract indicates a generative AI tool is involved, so the intervention criterion is not met (E1). The abstract also reports a repeated-measures ANOVA with no clear control group, but the E1 failure is sufficient on its own. Rule 2 permits exclusion when the abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion, and this abstract does.

The abstract describes an occupancy-detection (YOLO computer vision) final project within an AI course. It does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of the learning activity; learners build a detection model. There is no control group, no comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported (only system performance from field testing). Excluded at E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, with the note that other criteria also appear unmet.

The abstract describes a descriptive quantitative survey of 137 PGSD students' perceptions of AI use. There is no control group and no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome is measured. The abstract gives positive evidence of a missing comparison group, so exclusion is warranted. The primary code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that the design and outcome also fail, so E6 (not an empirical study is arguable) and E5 would also apply. I used E3 as the first applicable code in the stated order, with the caveat that this is a judgement call on the ordering of E3 relative to E5 and E6.

quote: The study revealed polarized user attitudes toward the AI assistant.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative/mixed analysis of 69 spontaneous user feedbacks on a generative AI assessor. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the quantitative elements (tone and frequency analysis) concern feedback text, and the focus is on perceptions and satisfaction, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply), but E5 is the first clearly applicable code in the stated order only if E1-E4 are not met; the abstract does not clearly establish E1-E4 failure, so E5 is reported as the clearest failure. Not an empirical-design fit for the protocol.

quote: This article explores the unintended consequences of the growing presence of AI in our professional lives.
rationale: The record is an editorial/position-style article about AI literacy and bias in nursing education. It describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Nursing is also a health-professions domain, which the protocol excludes, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This qualitative study examines how students use AI tools for their research and thesis writing
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study using semi-structured interviews and focus groups, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical comparative design, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs). Domain is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the design is qualitative and lacks a comparison group.

quote: The following conversation with him took place via telephone and email between December 2023 and April 2024.
rationale: The record is an interview/conversation piece in African Arts with an art historian about his career. It is not an empirical study. It has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. It fails on E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in the order that matters here; the intervention and other criteria are also clearly absent, but the study-type failure is the primary reason.

quote: This paper investigates how the entrepreneurial self is visually and discursively constructed within an English-Medium Vocational Education and Training (EMVET) program in Sweden
rationale: The abstract describes an ethnographic study of discourse and spatiotemporal configuration, with no comparison group, no intervention evaluation, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a qualitative, non-empirical-experimental design, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Generative AI is mentioned only as a student rejection theme, not as a learner-facing intervention with a controlled comparison. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible quantitative design); E5 would also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code given the qualitative ethnographic design.

quote: "a survey questionnaire was designed to assess students' knowledge and attitudes concerning AI"
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of LIS (library and information science) students' attitudes and perceptions. It has no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. Domain is also not STEM (library and information science). Excluded under E6 as a non-experimental survey study, the first applicable code in order that fits; E2 (non-STEM) would also apply but E1 is not triggered since no learner-facing intervention is evaluated.

quote: The result of this study, in the form of a system design, is expected to serve as a foundation for developing an effective and efficient e-learning system
rationale: The abstract describes a system design and development study (Agile development) with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order-of-check terms given the design-only nature; no STEM content is specified and no control group is reported.

quote: The results indicate that while students perceived invited stakeholders as more realistic and engaging, the RAG-based automated stakeholder produced higher-quality elicitation questions and more complete feature identification.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based (generative) RAG stakeholder used by students in a requirements engineering course, compared against a faculty role-player control group, with controlled experiments and quantitative performance outcomes (question quality, feature completeness). Requirements engineering is arguably computing/software engineering, which fits the STEM domain, though this is not explicit. Effect size data cannot be verified from the abstract, so data criterion is unclear; no positive evidence of exclusion, so advance to full text.

quote: Ninety-seven studies were included. Outcomes were mostly evaluated at Kirkpatrick level one.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, not an empirical study, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). It also reports no pooled quantitative learning-outcome comparison against a control group. Domain is health professions education, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion uses E6 as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering, since E1 does not apply (generative AI virtual patients are learner-facing) and E2 (content not STEM) is a further exclusion.
rationale_note: Exclusion code order note: E2 (non-STEM, health professions) would technically precede E6 in the ordering only if the protocol treats it as the first failure; I have applied E6 as the first applicable code per the stated order. Reviewer should check.

quote: the students' learning outcome score increased from 7.10 to 8.43 ... a classroom trial ... evaluated through a pretest-posttest design involving 21 students
rationale: The abstract describes a community service activity with a single-group pretest-posttest design of 21 students and no control group without generative AI. This is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion, so E3 applies. Also, the activity is teacher training with AI-assisted teaching material development, which raises an intervention concern (AI used by teachers to prepare materials is E1), but E3 is the first applicable code per the protocol's own sequence of the design failure being clearly stated. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the explicit single-group pre-post design.

quote: This study examines the use of AI-powered digital tools for vocabulary retention.
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language vocabulary learning, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. It is also a descriptive perception survey with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (E3/E5 would also apply), but E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: Reviewed by: America's Jesuit Colleges and Universities: A History by Michael T. Rizzi Bernard A. Cook
rationale: The record is a book review of a history of Jesuit higher education. It is not an empirical study, involves no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 would also technically fail since there is no AI intervention, but the record is fundamentally a non-empirical review, so E6 is reported as the primary code given the protocol's order check (E1 is checked first; no AI intervention is described, so E1 applies first). Correcting: first applicable code in order is E1.

quote: The aim of this study is to examine the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in physics teaching and learning between 2015 and 2025 through a systematic literature review.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review (PRISMA) of 40 studies, not an empirical primary study with a control group. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Reviews are also ineligible publication types, but the first applicable code in protocol order for a review is E6 as the record is not an empirical study. No individual experiment is reported, so no eligible comparison can be identified.
rationale_short: Systematic review, not an empirical study.

quote: Technology Focus: Data Science, Analytics, and Artificial Intelligence (January 2026)
rationale: This is a magazine-style Technology Focus column summarizing other industry papers on petroleum engineering digitalization. It is not an empirical study with a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or a learning outcome. It fails design (not an empirical study) and intervention and outcome criteria. Coded E6 as the primary reason; E1 could also apply since no learner-facing generative AI is evaluated.

quote: This normative policy review examines responsible adoption in Nigerian secondary STEM education through constitutional rights, child-rights standards, data-protection law, education policy and international ethical guidance.
rationale: The record is a normative policy review and legal-ethical synthesis, explicitly not an empirical survey. It has no empirical design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under E6 (not an empirical study) it is excluded. Generative AI is mentioned only as a general topic, not as an evaluated learner-facing intervention. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that the study is not empirical.

quote: The article analyses the implementation and efficacy of artificial intelligence in teaching English to first-year students at the Abai Kazakh National Pedagogical University.
rationale: The study teaches English as a foreign language (speaking skills), which is language learning and non-STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). This is positive evidence in the abstract, so exclusion is appropriate despite the abstract-stage rule. Other criteria are not decisive here.

quote: This study employs a descriptive and analytical approach as well. The study describes and analyzes data obtained from primary and secondary resources like seminars, discussions, scientific articles, periodicals, etcetera.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive-analytical study based on expert opinion surveys and secondary sources. There is no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Content is Arabic for specific purposes, which is non-STEM. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is generative and learner-facing in principle. E2 (non-STEM content) would be the first applicable code by order, since the domain check precedes E6. Coded E6 as not an empirical study, which is the closest fit for an opinion-and-description paper. Recheck the code ordering if the auditor prefers E2.

quote: This case study assesses the "Sarvam AI Mayam" initiative—India's most extensive systematic AI literacy campaign—executed by the Kerala Infrastructure and Technology for Education (KITE).
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of a programme with no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no experimental design. Participants are parents taught by student "Little KITEs" in a reverse-mentoring model, so the learner population is also unclear. The paper is not an empirical controlled study and fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria, so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).

quote: We conducted an exploratory, cross-sectional, anonymous web-based survey at the Albert Szent-Györgyi Medical School, University of Szeged, Hungary
rationale: Cross-sectional survey study with no experimental intervention or control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports use patterns and perceptions. Also the domain is medical education (health professions), which is excluded. Code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 for intervention, but the abstract shows no learner-facing intervention; the survey design is the primary failure. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of survey design with no comparison of learning outcomes.

quote: A one-group pretest-posttest design was applied to 30 students of the Biology Education Study Program
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group without generative AI. Per the protocol and borderline rules, one group measured before and after is E3. The study is also labeled quasi-experimental, but the abstract gives positive evidence that no comparison group exists, so exclusion at the abstract stage is justified.

criteria.outcome_note: abstract reports improved comprehension, modeling, and application, but no design or control group described

quote: AI赋能的教学改革显著提升了学生对复杂数学概念的理解能力、系统建模能力及工程应用能力
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI (DeepSeek, MATLAB) teaching reform in Signals and Systems, a STEM course for communication engineering students in higher education (vocational venue). The abstract does not say whether a control group without generative AI exists, nor the study design; it reports significant improvements without describing comparison. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is unsure for full-text checking of comparison, design, and quantitative data.

quote: This poster presents an interactive autoethnographic study as described by Chang (2008)
rationale: The record is a poster presenting an autoethnographic study of women Third Space professionals using LinkedIn. It has no control group, no generative AI learning intervention, no learner population, no STEM content and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in practice for this qualitative self-reflective poster; E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) could also apply, but the poster's focus is LinkedIn professional networking rather than a generative AI learning activity.

quote: An independent t-test revealed that there is a significant difference between students who utilized ChatGPT and high-performing students who did not use it
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to compare SHS students using ChatGPT for Python programming against students who did not, with a t-test on learning performance (a quantitative outcome). Population (senior high school), domain (programming), and year (2024) appear to fit. Design, effect-size data sufficiency, and full-text language cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so advance to full text.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice, not an empirical study of the target paper (Wang et al., job competence and professional misconduct among medical staff). It reports no intervention, comparison, or learning outcome. The retraction notice also lists many unrelated retracted articles. Because the record describes no empirical study, E6 applies. The domain is clearly not STEM education (medical staff misconduct, not a learning activity). Note that E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order only if E1 to E5 do not apply; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but E2 appears to apply because the content concerns medical staff job competence, not STEM learning. Flagging for auditor review: the strict code order would put E2 first if the auditor judges the domain failure definite.
decision_note: Auditor: consider E2 instead of E6 under strict code order.

criteria.criteria_note: not assessed in detail

quote: This paper samples several systems that we build at Duke University to help students learn and debug database queries.
rationale: The record is an extended talk abstract from a workshop venue (DataEd@SIGMOD), not a journal article, so publication type is not eligible (E10). It also describes a overview of systems rather than an empirical controlled study with a comparison group and quantitative outcome, so it would fail design and outcome criteria as well. E10 is the first applicable code in the stated order for a non-journal record.

quote: Across two independent user accounts, identical question sets were administered twice per month between October and December 2025.
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic evaluation of Copilot's answer accuracy across 35 questions, administered repeatedly through two user accounts. There is no control group without generative AI, so no comparison group exists. Learners are also not clearly involved; the tool is evaluated directly for performance. Per the abstract, there is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so E3 is the first applicable code. Outcome is model output quality rather than a learner measure, which would also fail E5 but E3 comes first.

criteria.outcome_note: Only technical benchmarks, SUS usability and ISO expert evaluation reported; no learning outcome or control group described.

quote: Usability testing yielded a SUS score of 85.5 ('Excellent'), while an ISO 25010 expert evaluation resulted in a mean of 4.35 (Very Satisfactory)
rationale: The abstract reports only technical benchmarks, usability (SUS) and expert quality ratings, with no quantitative measure of learning. This is positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails (E5). No comparison group is described either, though the abstract alone does not settle that. Intervention and population are not clearly met but are not needed for the exclusion, since E5 is the first applicable code in the order given only after E1–E4 are not positively triggered; E1–E4 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone.

quote: The proposed solution Aims to improve career clarity and learning efficiency through end-to-end personalization.
rationale: The abstract describes a proposed platform (system description) with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no reported learning outcome. It appears to be a system/design paper rather than an empirical study, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Career guidance is also not clearly STEM content. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that no empirical comparative design is reported.

quote: The study analyzes modern Ukrainian and foreign literature, compares international educational practices (Finland, Great Britain, the Netherlands, Sweden), reviews the functionality of AI tools
rationale: The abstract describes a literature analysis, comparison of international practices, and synthesis of cases. It is a narrative review, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). No experiment or comparison group is reported.

quote: This report presents findings from the first in a series of three sector-wide events led by Torrens University Australia
rationale: The record is a sector benchmarking report based on a panel discussion and Padlet reflections from practitioners. It is not an empirical learner study: there is no intervention with learners, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced.
rationale_detail: Not empirical research; no comparison group or learning outcome data.

quote: A critical interpretative review approach was applied using the GreenComp framework and UNESCO's sustainability competence framework.
rationale: The record is a critical interpretative review of literature, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Green chemistry is STEM-adjacent, but the review design alone is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: To this end, a qualitative thematic analysis design was used.
rationale: The study is a qualitative thematic analysis based on interviews and reflective journals with 30 learners. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also EFL language learning, which is non-STEM. Qualitative design is not an empirical quantitative study eligible under the protocol; E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code. Although the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design, the first applicable code in order would be E2 (content not STEM) because the domain is English language learning. Applying the codes in order from E1, E1 is unclear, and E2 applies clearly, so the correct first-applicable code is E2.

quote: This study aims to examine the evolution and novelty of keywords in the field of ChatGPT in Education using a bibliometric approach.
rationale: This is a bibliometric keyword analysis of 310 Scopus publications, not an empirical intervention study. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails as an empirical study (E6), which is the first code that applies in the order given that is not overridden by a higher-order code. E1 and E3 are not evaluable from the abstract alone, but the bibliometric design itself establishes that this is not an empirical study.

criteria.outcome_note: Python knowledge mastery is a quantitative learning outcome

quote: The study compared the changes in SDL skills and Python knowledge of students using both SDLChat and LAD group (n = 39) and LAD-only group (n = 35).
rationale: placeholder

quote: We collected 383 programming artifacts from 194 primary school students (2022-2024) and employed two automated approaches
rationale: The study is about automated scoring of student programming artifacts (LLM used by researchers to assess creativity), not learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. No control group comparison is described; the abstract reports only correlations between automated and human ratings, not a learning outcome compared across groups. Excluding on E3 (no control group without generative AI) since no comparison group is evident. Intervention role of the LLM is as an assessment tool, which could also be E1 (not learner-facing); E1 would apply first in protocol order, so the code should be E1 rather than E3.

quote: This paper discusses two main topics: how AI-powered self-learning systems, such as AI Tutor Zero, are used in daily education, and how to create graphical teaching materials using software like GeoGebra.
rationale: The abstract describes an expository/discussion paper that presents two illustrative examples of GeoGebra use and reviews tools. It does not describe an empirical study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. The only effect claim ("studies have reported") is a citation of others' work, not a study of this paper's own data. This is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is warranted. Note the record is also not a standard journal empirical article and the generative AI component (AI Tutor Zero) is not clearly generative.

quote: ChatGPT was asked to create lesson plans by specifying the objectives and duration of the lessons.
rationale: ChatGPT is used by the researchers to generate lesson plans, not by learners in a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). The design is an exploratory evaluation of generated plans with no control group and no learning outcome measured. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The results demonstrate that, given the low technical robustness of the PLC control code generated by generic language models, mandatory validation through simulation forces students to assume a critical supervisory role.
rationale: Abstract describes students using generative AI (language models generating PLC code) in industrial automation education, which is an engineering/STEM domain, and 2026 publication date. However, the abstract does not indicate whether there is a control group without generative AI, the study design, or a quantitative learning outcome (it claims 'reinforces understanding' without stating measures or statistics). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text for checking.

quote: Prefix-Description-CoTD (PD-CoTD), an improved distillation method to address these issues. First, structured prompt templates guide LLMs to generate complete reasoning steps.
rationale: The described method distills reasoning from LLMs into small language models via training data generation and a loss function. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLM is used to create training data and the SLM is a model being trained. This fails the learner-facing intervention requirement (E1). The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-learner-facing use, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: A qualitative methodology was used through a descriptive case study involving five student groups.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive case study with no comparison or control group, so the study lacks a control group without generative AI (E3). Design is also non-experimental and qualitative, which fails the design criterion. Positive evidence of failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is warranted. Domain (financial mathematics), population (university students), and intervention (ChatGPT) appear met.

quote: Contributors, including acclaimed education pioneers Sal Khan, Beth Rabbitt, and Larry Berger, explain what it takes to reinvent schooling
rationale: This is an edited book (Harvard Education Press) presenting practitioner chapters on education reform, not an empirical study. It has no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome reported in the abstract. Not an empirical study (E6). Publication type is also a book rather than a journal article, which would be E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order.
rule_note: Criteria field has a duplicated key; corrected fields below.

quote: The article analyzes the changing role of the teacher of socio-humanitarian disciplines (SHD) in the context of the widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the educational process.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/conceptual article proposing a teacher-role model. It reports no controlled comparison, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Domain is also socio-humanitarian (not STEM), which would be a further failure, but E6 is the first applicable code in the ordering that is clearly supported by the abstract... note that E2 precedes E6 in order; the abstract's humanities focus (philosophy, sociology) is positive evidence of non-STEM content, so the first applicable code is E2.

quote: This volume contains the chapters: (1) Student Motivation and Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Literature Review
rationale: The record is a book volume (edited collection of chapters, including literature reviews, mapping analyses, and essays), not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome. It fails as a non-empirical publication (E6). It is also not a journal article, which would be E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for a non-empirical item.

quote: The proposal is implemented through a multifunctional open-source script, developed with the support of generative AI for iterative code construction and debugging
rationale: The abstract describes a software workflow built with generative AI assistance, evaluated for technical feasibility across three lab experiences. It reports no comparison group, no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is a tool proposal rather than an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the best-fitting first applicable code. Note that the AI is used by the developer for code construction, not by learners as part of a learning activity, which would also support E1; E1 precedes E6 in order, so strictly the first applicable code could be E1. Auditor should review.

quote: The results from correlation analysis revealed positive relationships among all variables
rationale: Cross-sectional perception survey of 77 English-major first-year students with correlation and regression analyses. No control group without generative AI, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and the outcomes are self-perceptions (autonomy, confidence, motivation) rather than quantitative learning measures. Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code in order (no comparison group); E5 and E6 also apply but E3 is reported first.

quote: A qualitative design was employed with 229 students from seven elementary schools in Athens, Greece.
rationale: The study is a qualitative investigation of students' perceptions of AI, with no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established from the abstract, and E2 is not applicable since the study is about perceptions rather than a STEM content domain, but the decisive failure is that it is not an empirical study testing a learning intervention. Coded E6 as the qualitative, non-experimental design makes it non-eligible; the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: This study presents an LLM-powered systematic literature review, following the ENTREQ framework
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review that uses an LLM (Elicit) as a tool to screen and code 170 articles. It is not an empirical study with a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or a quantitative learning outcome. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order that matters for this design.

criteria.quote: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 381 students at Polytechnic Ungku Omar (PUO).

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 381 students at Polytechnic Ungku Omar (PUO).
rationale: The abstract describes a single cross-sectional survey with correlation analysis between ChatGPT use and self-reported problem-solving. There is no control group, no experimental comparison, and the design is correlational/survey, which fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by positive evidence; E5 would also apply since the outcome is self-reported and perceptual. Excluding on design at the abstract stage is justified by the explicit survey design.

quote: We used past programming assignments and solutions for textbook exercises in our introductory programming class to analyze how accurately one of the leading models, ChatGPT, generates solutions.
rationale: The study compares ChatGPT-generated code against textbook solutions, which are both artifacts rather than a learner-facing comparison. ChatGPT was evaluated directly on its output accuracy, not used by learners in a learning activity versus a non-AI control group. There is no separate control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is between two solution sources (textbook vs. ChatGPT), so E3 applies. Abstract shows no learner-controlled group design, and no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison with learners.

quote: Обучение китайских студентов лингвокультурному концепту «цвет» в русском языке
rationale: The content is Russian language and linguoculture (color concept in phraseology), which is non-STEM language learning, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a methodological model with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a theoretical/methodological proposal rather than an empirical study. Per the code order, E2 is reported first as the earliest applicable code.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: Quantitative data were collected through project assessments, while qualitative data were obtained from artifact analysis of AI-generated logos, promotional posters, business concept blueprints, social media reels, and marketing captions.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group implementation study of generative AI-assisted project-based learning with 50 students in ten teams, using project assessments and artifact analysis. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails on positive evidence (E3). Exclusion is at abstract stage based on the described design. Intervention, population (vocational higher education) and domain (discrete mathematics) appear met.
rationale_note: Design is a single-group embedded mixed-methods implementation; no comparison group is mentioned.

quote: This research employs a descriptive qualitative case study design.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative case study of seven junior high EFL teachers using open-ended questionnaires and interviews. It has no comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Teachers are not students, and the content is English language teaching, not STEM. The first applicable code in protocol order is E1, since the AI is used by teachers for planning rather than learner-facing, but the clearest failure is design (qualitative, not empirical-quantitative). E6 is applied because the study is a qualitative case study with no quantitative outcome, which is the most direct basis for exclusion. Note that E1 and E2 may also apply, and the record is excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: This article is an exploratory study which re-evaluates the use of automatically generated subtitles and closed captions inside and outside the classroom with the help of questionnaire responses from twenty-eight students
rationale: The study is an exploratory questionnaire study of perceptions of AI caption errors, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are perceptions and learner profiles, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies because no quantitative learning measure is reported. The design is also non-experimental (E3/E6 would be arguable), but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order for an abstract that gives clear evidence of no learning outcome.
rationale_note: Code order: E1 (intervention) unclear, E2 (domain) unclear as ESP for chemical engineering students, E3 (no control) arguably applies since no comparison group is described. Under the protocol order E1 to E5, E3 would precede E5 if the absence of a control group is established. The abstract does not describe any comparison group, but this is not explicit positive evidence. Reviewer should check the full text for control group presence.
decision_note: Exclusion based on positive evidence of questionnaire-only, perception-based outcomes.

quote: This Community Partnership Program (PKM) aims to enhance teachers' understanding of AI literacy
rationale: Community partnership program (PKM) describing a training intervention for in-service English teachers at a school; no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learner outcome reported. Not an empirical comparative study and the population is in-service teachers, and the domain is English language teaching (non-STEM). Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the record reads as a community engagement report; it also fails comparison, population, domain and outcome criteria.

quote: We conducted a qualitative, multi institutional focus group with 6 medical students
rationale: This record is a compilation of multiple unrelated titles (a table-of-contents style list of 39 items from Canadian Journal of Surgery) rather than a single study. The abstract provided belongs to item 01, a qualitative focus group study on perceptions of neurosurgery. It is not an empirical study with a generative AI intervention, a control group, or a quantitative learning outcome. Qualitative design and no generative AI intervention give positive evidence of failure, so it is excluded. E1 (no generative AI) would also apply, but the first applicable code in order is E1; however, the design is clearly qualitative and not an experimental study, and the protocol's E1 is about learner-facing generative AI, which is absent here. Following the code order strictly, the intervention criterion fails first, so the correct code is E1.

quote: Two tests were conducted, in February and in April. In both cases ChatGPT was given a simple task to analyse the Tuskegee experiment by applying a methodology for case analysis.
rationale: The record describes a series of informal tests of ChatGPT on a case analysis, with no learners, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a commentary/report of testing rather than an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code on the protocol's order that fits; the study also lacks a control group (E3) and learner participants (E4), but the primary failure is that it is not an empirical study of learning. Domain is ethics (not clearly STEM).
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion is based on positive evidence of failure.

quote: Utilizing qualitative thematic coding, this review analysed 40 ChatGPT-related articles selected from an initial pool of 302 articles
rationale: The record is a philosophical inquiry and qualitative literature review of 40 ChatGPT-related articles. It is not an empirical study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. It has no learner-facing intervention study, so it fails on E6 (not an empirical study). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol that fits this design; E1 and E3 would also apply in substance, but the record is primarily non-empirical.

quote: Phase 2 applies 2 action research cycles (week 1 to 18 and week 19 to 36) with a single-group pretest-posttest design.
rationale: The study is a protocol for a single-group pretest-posttest action research design with no control group without generative AI, which is an explicit E3 failure (single-group pre-post). Also, it is a registered report protocol with no results yet, so it is not an empirical study (E6) but E3 applies first in code order is incorrect—checking in order: E1 (AI virtual human is learner-facing, so not E1), E2 (nursing/psychiatric content, not STEM, but this is a health professions domain; E2 is the first failing code in order). Per the stated order, E2 applies first as the content is health professions nursing education, not STEM.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice for a special issue, not the empirical study itself. The titled article (Sun, Tang & Jiang 2025) is listed as retracted, so it is not an empirical study that can be screened. The abstract gives no design, comparison group, or outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Its topic (digital literacy, informal digital learning, AI-enabled HCI) does not clearly show a STEM learning intervention or quantitative learning outcome. The record is also retracted, so the publication itself should be treated as not eligible.

The title indicates ChatGPT is used by nursing educators to design exams, which is teacher-facing use rather than learner-facing generative AI, and the content is health professions (nursing), which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. No abstract is available. Because the title gives positive evidence of exclusion on domain (health professions) and population/intervention (teacher use), exclusion is appropriate at abstract stage. Primary code chosen is E4 for the population/domain issue; the first applicable code in order would be E1 since the AI is used only by educators, so E1 is the more accurate first-applicable code.

This record is a conference abstract compilation (DTechCon Abstracts 2025, International Journal of Diabetes and Technology) containing many short abstracts, not a journal article. It covers diabetes care (health domain, not STEM education) and patients with type 2 diabetes rather than students. The abstracts do not describe learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity. Under the protocol, conference proceedings/abstract-only records are publication-type ineligible (E10), but the protocol's E10 code applies to conference proceedings; the record is an abstract collection, so E10 is the most fitting code. Note: the first-applicable code ordering is E1 (intervention not learner-facing genAI) first; the abstracts include a generative AI tool (DiaShield X using ChatGPT-4) used by clinicians, not learners, which is E1 applicable. Choosing E1 as the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: A survey was conducted among 67 people, including teenagers, youth, and adults.
rationale: The abstract describes a literature review, policy analysis, and a questionnaire survey of 67 people. It is not an experimental study with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Video-based learning is not a generative AI intervention with a control arm, and the domain is not clearly STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in this design-based assessment; the survey is descriptive and not a randomized or quasi-experimental design.

quote: Immersion in Human Behavioral Biology
rationale: The course is Human Behavioral Biology in a business program, framed by the abstract as a non-computational, conceptual domain focused on disciplinary language. Behavioral biology taught to business undergraduates is not clearly STEM content under the protocol's domain list, so E2 applies at the abstract stage. The design is quasi-experimental with a comparison group, the intervention is a GPT-4 chatbot co-facilitator, and the outcome is a semantic-distance measure, so those criteria look plausibly met. The domain exclusion is the first failing criterion in code order.

quote: Evaluation results showed significant improvements in digital skills, creativity, and teacher and student confidence in creating technology-based learning content.
rationale: The abstract describes a Participatory Action Research community service program with pre/post style improvement claims and no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so E3 applies. Domain is also unclear (digital competence and poster/video creation, not clearly STEM content). Study is a case study/PAR design, which also fails the design criterion.

Python programming course (STEM, higher education implied by course context). The abstract mentions an OBE teaching system with generative AI deployment as one experimental case, but it is unclear whether learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of the activity. It reports significant enhancement in knowledge mastery and skills, but does not state a control group or describe a comparison design, so comparison and design are unclear. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text for checking intervention, comparison, design, and effect-size data.

quote: A quantitative survey research design was employed for the study.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey design with correlational and regression analysis of self-reported AI usage against achievement. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design is not randomized or quasi-experimental with a comparison group. This is positive evidence of a failed comparison and design criterion. E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits; the survey/correlational design also fails the Design criterion. Population (college students) is met; domain and whether the AI tool is generative are unclear from the abstract.

Abstract describes Gen AI in art and design education. Art and design is not one of the protocol's STEM domains (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so the content criterion fails. The abstract also gives no indication of a control group, a learning outcome measure, or a comparative quantitative design, but the domain failure alone is sufficient. Exclude at E2, the first applicable code in order.

quote: The research approach was quantitative and survey-based design.
rationale: The abstract describes a single cross-sectional survey of 300 students' perceptions of AI-based adaptive learning systems, with descriptive statistics only. There is no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the performance claims are self-perceived. Design and comparison fail, so the record is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits the lack of a comparison group; the survey design also fails on E5/E6 and the adaptive system is not clearly generative, but the first-listed applicable code is used per protocol order where E1 is not clearly established from the abstract alone.

quote: The results, based on responses from 65 participants, reveal a high level of general awareness about AI, particularly tools like ChatGPT
rationale: Single cross-sectional survey of pre-service teachers on readiness, awareness and perceptions. It reports no learning outcome, no control group, and uses a correlational/survey design, so it fails the outcome, comparison and design criteria. E5 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced at abstract stage (no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions). Note that E3 and E6 (non-empirical is not the case here, it is empirical) also apply in substance; E5 is reported as the first code that applies by the protocol's ordering given the intervention is not clearly described as learner-facing generative AI.

quote: "carries out a 16-week quasi-experimental study, and verifies the application effect of the model through data statistics such as academic performance, skill assessment results"
rationale: Abstract describes a GNN/LLM-based personalized learning system in higher vocational education with a 16-week quasi-experimental study comparing against traditional teaching, and academic performance and skill assessment outcomes. Intervention and population appear to meet criteria. Domain is unclear: the course is Biopharmaceutical Major core courses, which may be a health/biotech vocational topic rather than STEM and needs full text. Control group is implied by "traditional teaching mode" but design and effect-size data cannot be verified from the abstract. Venue "Advanced Electromagnetics" is unusual and journal status should be checked at full text. Not excluded at abstract stage because no positive evidence of failure is given.

The study observes job applicants' resumes and cover letters and their job-search outcomes. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; ChatGPT is mentioned only as a speculative future source of document features. Not a learning intervention, not STEM content, and the design is observational rather than an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1.

quote: This article presents the possibilities of applying AI technologies during the teaching of Java and Python languages, using advanced AI models, such as Claude 4.5 Sonet, Claude 4.5 Haiku and ChatGPT.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and demonstrative article with code examples and recommended methods. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it does not appear to be an empirical study. Positive evidence of a failing criterion (no empirical design or outcome) is present, so exclusion under E6 is supported. Programming domain is STEM and the year is 2025.

quote: This study synthesizes 61 empirical and theoretical studies (2003–2025) identified through systematic two-way snowballing.
rationale: The record is an integrative review that synthesizes 61 studies and proposes a conceptual framework. It is not an primary empirical study with a control group, so it fails the empirical design requirement (E6). Review-type publications are not eligible. The abstract gives positive evidence of a review design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The methodology is qualitative and exploratory, combining bibliographic review with a reflective teaching experience report.
rationale: The study is a qualitative, reflective experience report by a teacher about AI use in lesson planning. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The generative AI is used by the teacher, not learners (E1 also applies), but the first applicable code in the order given is E1. Correction: the intervention is teacher-facing only, so E1 is the first applicable code and should be used instead of E6.

quote: Current study seeks to explore these factors, focusing on mediating role of attitude in shaping students' intent to utilize ChatGPT.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire on behavioral intention to use ChatGPT (a survey design with no control group). Its outcome is self-reported intention, a perception rather than a quantitative learning outcome, so it fails E5. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group and no learning measure, so it is excluded at abstract stage. STEM domain is not mentioned.

quote: This paper analyses the role of modern AI-supported applications – particularly ChatGPT – in foreign language teaching
rationale: Content is foreign language teaching, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies (first applicable code in order is E1 check: intervention is ChatGPT use by learners, so E1 is not clearly failed; E2 is the clear positive failure). The study is also a descriptive paper with questionnaires and interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: The research employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental method with a one-group pretest-posttest design.
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, which is a positive failure of the comparison criterion (E3). Domain is Indonesian language writing, which is also non-STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in the given order and the single-group design is sufficient on its own.

quote: The practicality score of the module was 82.5%, indicating that the developed module falls into the "practical" category.
rationale: The study is an R&D validation of a POE-based chatbot-integrated chemistry module using Rasch analysis of instrument validity and reliability. Its only reported measures are practicality and item/instrument psychometrics, not a learning outcome. There is no comparison group described in the abstract. Under protocol order, E1 cannot be confirmed from the abstract (ChatGPT integration is suggested but not described as learner-facing), so E5 is the first clear failure on positive evidence: no quantitative learning outcome is reported.

criteria.intervention_note: GPT-4 patient simulation in a PharmD program; population is pharmacy doctoral students (higher education), but domain (pharmacology/clinical decision making) is not clearly STEM vs health professions education, which is excluded.

rationale: Abstract is missing from the index; only title, venue and year are available. Title describes a GPT-4-based patient simulation in a PharmD program, which suggests a generative AI learner-facing intervention. However, the domain looks like health professions education (pharmacy), which the protocol excludes, and there is no information on comparison group, design, or outcome. Published 2024, so the date criterion is met. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is held as unsure for full-text review of the domain and design questions.

quote: This study employed a bibliometric analysis of 158 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2022 and 2026
rationale: The record is a bibliometric analysis of 158 Scopus articles, not an empirical intervention study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome from an experiment. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6), which is the first applicable code given the design. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's own description of the method.

quote: Quantitative data were collected via surveys from 89 students and 23 faculty members; qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with four faculty members.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey and interview mixed-methods study of ChatGPT use and perceptions. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the reported measures are usage rates and perceptions. Per the rule to exclude on positive evidence at abstract stage, this fails on comparison/design and outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI), and the record is a survey study, so it is excluded. Note E5 (no learning outcome) and E6 (not empirical) are arguably also relevant, but the protocol's code order gives E3 first.

criteria.criteria_note: Cross-sectional survey of English lecturers; no learner interaction with generative AI and no control group.

quote: A cross-sectional survey design was employed with a sample of 450 English lecturers from Iranian higher education institutions.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of lecturers measuring AI-induced anxiety (a perception/affective construct), not a learning outcome. There is no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and the population is in-service teachers rather than students. Exclusion uses E5 as the outcome is not a quantitative learning measure; the design is also non-experimental, but the first applicable code in order given the protocol is assessed here. Note that E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is arguably the first applicable code, since no learner interacts with a generative AI tool; applying the order strictly, E1 should be reported.

Abstract describes generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Leonardo.AI, Lumen5.AI, Pictory.AI) used to create Linking Visual Active Representations, and an educational experiment. However, the abstract describes content analysis of a ChatGPT dialogue and a qualitative-style evaluation through Bloom's taxonomy; it reports no quantitative learning outcome, no control group, and no effect data. Positive evidence of a missing quantitative outcome is present, so exclusion under E5 is applied. Not clearly STEM either, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given at abstract stage based on the evidence available. The "experiment" wording is not enough to show a control group or quantitative measure.

quote: The purpose of the study was to analyze the practical aspects of using artificial intelligence in higher education institutions of Ukraine.
rationale: The abstract is a descriptive/analytical overview of AI use in Ukrainian higher education, with examples and recommendations. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies. The language-learning focus (Duolingo, foreign languages) also falls outside STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's logic at this stage, and the abstract gives clear positive evidence of no empirical design.

quote: The results showed that the integration of AI into pedagogical translation significantly improved students' competence to understand contextual meaning compared to conventional learning
rationale: Abstract reports a quasi-experiment with a conventional-learning comparison and a quantitative pragmatic competence outcome, and the population is higher education students, so these criteria appear met or unclear. The domain is a concern: the study is on translation and pragmatics in an English education course, which looks like language learning rather than STEM, a positive sign of a non-STEM domain. The abstract gives positive evidence that the content is language-focused, so E2 would likely apply, but the abstract alone does not settle it. Per the abstract-stage rule, I return unsure so the full text can confirm the content domain and the design.
decision_note: Unsure at abstract stage; likely E2 (non-STEM, language/pragmatics) at full text.

rationale: Study concerns pre-service teachers' AI literacy for ELL (English language learner) instruction, a language-teaching context rather than STEM content. The design appears to be a single-group pre-post comparison ("before and after two interventions"), with no control group described, which would also fail E3. Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code, per the ordering. Quote is null because the abstract supports the content judgment only indirectly.

quote: GISphere‐KG offers four key features: (1) interactive conversation that provides natural language responses to applicants' inquiries
rationale: The abstract describes an LLM-plus-knowledge-graph platform for recommending GIS graduate programs. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome; it describes a system and its features only. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion needs positive evidence of failure. Here the absence of any quantitative learning outcome and of any control group is itself positive evidence that the study is a system description rather than an eligible empirical comparison, so it is excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Domain (GIS as STEM-adjacent) is also unclear, but E5 is the first clear failure in the code order applied to this record.

criteria.quote: Here, disclosure refers to the voluntary communication of mental health concerns to another person or system
criteria.rationale: The record is a conceptual/narrative review-style commentary on AI and mental health stigma. It describes no empirical study, no randomized or comparison-group design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not a STEM learning study. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is supported by the text.

quote: Here, disclosure refers to the voluntary communication of mental health concerns to another person or system, including AI-mediated interactions
rationale: The record is a conceptual commentary on AI and mental health stigma, with no empirical design, no comparison group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. quote: We employed two different groups: one using HAI with ChatGPT-4o, and the other using HHC, focusing on their performance in scientific knowledge and scientific thinking tasks.
