Exclusion at E5 is the first applicable code in order that fits the abstract's positive evidence; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply), but the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative, non-comparative design. Programming content and a generative AI interview tool with university/course students are consistent with other criteria.

Record is a study protocol for a knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) instrument about ChatGPT in pharmacy. No abstract is available. The title describes a psychometric/survey protocol, not an empirical controlled study with a learning outcome. Pharmacy practice is also a health professions domain, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion is on the basis of positive evidence from the title: it is a study protocol, not an empirical study, and it measures attitudes and practices rather than learning outcomes.

quote: In a recent issue of the Lancet, the GBD US Health Disparities Collaborators conducted a county-level time-series analysis of racial-ethnic disparities in mortality in the USA.
rationale: This record is a commentary/editorial on a Lancet mortality disparities study, not an empirical study. It has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, no learner population, and no learning outcome. Artificial intelligence is mentioned only as a generic future data-integration method. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 would also apply on intervention grounds, but the record's core nature is non-empirical commentary.
rationale_note: Quote is from the abstract text; the record itself is a commentary.

quote: A cross-sectional study was conducted on undergraduate students in a College of Medicine in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring perceptions and self-efficacy toward AI. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, and it is not an intervention study. The design is survey-based, so E6 (not an empirical intervention study) applies. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) could be argued first, but the abstract does not establish a learner-facing intervention. E6 is the best fit for a cross-sectional survey, and the record is excluded on design grounds.

quote: A qualitative study with a phenomenological design was developed at the San Ignacio de Loyola University, Lima, Peru
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative phenomenological study using semi-structured interviews and focus groups with no control group, so there is positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail. Code E3 is used because the absence of any non-generative-AI comparison group is the first failing criterion in the protocol's ordering that applies here; the qualitative design would also fail the design criterion. Students are university-level, which is met. Domain and outcome are not clearly STEM or quantitative from the abstract alone. Because the design evidence is positive, the record is excluded at abstract stage.

quote: The study utilized a cross-sectional quantitative survey design that consisted of an online survey distributed to 160 undergraduate students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring student perceptions and preferences, not a learning outcome. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, and no quantitative learning measure. Perception-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion, and the design is not eligible. Exclusion code E6 applies because the study is a survey, which is non-experimental; this is the first applicable code in order that fits the design, and the protocol's design criteria are not met. Domain is also not clearly STEM (general academic writing).

quote: This study critically analyzes the multifaceted influence of Artificial Intelligence on academic integrity, lecturers, teachers, and students.
rationale: The abstract describes a critical analysis / mixed-methods review of AI's influence on academic integrity and education in general. It reports no controlled comparison, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It does not appear to be an empirical experimental study, and there is no STEM focus or control group described. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6) on the basis of positive evidence of a non-experimental, discursive design. Note: the first applicable code in order would be E1 if the intervention were judged non-learner-facing, but the abstract does not describe a specific learner-facing intervention, so E6 is the most defensible code.

quote: The study employed a quantitative survey research design. The target population comprised secondary school educators from public and private schools.
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of 320 secondary school teachers measuring perceptions and relationships (correlation/regression). It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental study with a control group, and it has no learner-level quantitative learning outcome. Participants are teachers, not students, so the population criterion also fails. Coded E6 (not an empirical study is the closest code for a survey of perceptions). Note: E6 is applied on the basis of design; the survey is empirical, so the strongest fit is actually E3/E4-type failure, but the protocol's first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing AI — teachers only use/perceive AI), which is evaluated first. Given the order, E1 would be the first code that applies if teachers' AI use is not learner-facing.

quote: This qualitative study systematically compared three influential character education frameworks
rationale: Record is a qualitative comparative analysis of three character education frameworks. It is not an empirical trial: no learners interact with generative AI, there is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and it is not STEM content. The AI use (ChatGPT 5.1) was researcher-side coding of documents, not learner-facing. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code at abstract stage; the E1 code (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would also apply, but the design is a document analysis rather than an intervention study.

quote: this study proposes an AI-assisted teaching model incorporating a large language model (LLM) platform
rationale: The abstract describes a teaching model using an LLM platform in a university robot path planning course (STEM, higher education). It is a learner-facing generative AI intervention. However, the abstract does not report a control group, a comparison design, or any quantitative learning outcome, so these criteria cannot be judged from the abstract. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text for checking of design, comparison, and outcomes.

quote: This study evaluated the demographic profiles of simulation instructors and heads of simulation labs generated by three AI platforms-ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude-across nine global locations.
rationale: The study does not involve learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity; it analyzes demographic profiles that AI platforms generated as synthetic data. There is no learner population, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study of learners, so E6 applies. Under the strict first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would arguably apply first, since AI was only used to produce synthetic demographic data with no learner interaction. The code is therefore arguably E1 rather than E6; the record is excluded either way.

Abstract describes a programming course context (STEM domain met), students as population (met), LLM-based feedback as a learner-facing generative AI intervention, and a student performance outcome. Comparison group appears to be Compiler Feedback and Unit Test Feedback arms, which are non-generative-AI, so comparison likely met. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental with comparison group) is not stated in the abstract, and the venue is a journal article. Insufficient to exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to confirm design and effect-size data.

quote: This review evaluates the book’s empirical contributions and theoretical insights, situating it within broader discourse on educational technology practices
rationale: The record is a book review of a book on ChatGPT in education, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in protocol order. Note that E6 is not in the first position for STEM or other checks; the review's own content is non-empirical, so E6 is the correct first-applicable code given the order of checks is E1 to E5 unclear at abstract stage.

quote: This paper adapts a historical-philosophical method. It traces the effects of colonialism and racialization within humanism's emergence through Sylvia Wynter's historiography
rationale: The paper is a historical-philosophical essay with no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly failed, since E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone but the non-empirical nature is unambiguous.

quote: Empirical evaluation over two academic years demonstrates that the proposed reform significantly improves students' code quality, system design capabilities, and engineering collaboration skills
rationale: Software engineering undergraduate program integrating Generative AI into learning (intervention and domain/population appear met). The abstract does not state whether a separate control group exists (comparison and design unclear; a two-year evaluation could be pre-post only). Outcomes (code quality, design capability) are plausibly quantitative but measurement is not described. Publication venue is 'International journal of engineering inventions', which may not be a journal article under the protocol's publication-type rule; this is also unclear. Missing information is not evidence of exclusion, so advance to full text.

quote: Focus Issue on arrhythmias and digital health and innovation contains a State of the Art Review article
rationale: This record is an editorial/focus-issue introduction to a European Heart Journal issue, not an empirical study. It describes several review, viewpoint, and clinical research articles but reports no original study of learner-facing generative AI, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not a STEM education study and does not meet the population criterion. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention, but the record is not about a learner-facing intervention at all, so E6 best describes the record type. No prompt-injection content was found.

quote: The AIGC group used ChatGPT, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion, while the control group used traditional design software.
rationale: Abstract indicates a two-group experiment with a control group using traditional design software (non-AI), generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion), university undergraduate students, and a creative performance outcome with d reported. Domain is unclear: product design (intelligent walking cane) is not clearly within the protocol's STEM domains (science, math, engineering, CS, etc.). Product design may be considered engineering-adjacent, so this needs full-text review. Publication type is a journal article (Frontiers in Psychology). Not excluded at abstract stage.

The record has only a title and venue (Nature Reviews Chemistry, 2026), with no abstract. The title and venue suggest a review-type article rather than an empirical study with a control group. Publication type is also a review-style venue, which the protocol excludes. Excluding under E6 (not an empirical study) because the record gives positive evidence of a review-style piece; no quote is available to support this beyond the title. Note that a reviewer may prefer to verify at full text, as the abstract is missing.

quote: We interviewed six college (graduate) students who had experience voluntarily using ChatGPT starting in early 2023
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study based on interviews of six students, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design criteria. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., a qualitative design falling outside the eligible designs). Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract, but the design failure is sufficient.

quote: The article is dedicated to the study of applying various artificial intelligence systems in the development of educational and methodological materials for academic disciplines
rationale: The abstract describes generative AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Leonardo.AI) used by the author to create a student handbook's graphic design, not learner-facing use. Positive evidence of failure: AI is used for material preparation, not as a learner-facing activity (E1 would apply first). Per code order, E1 is the first applicable code: AI is used only by the material developer, not by learners. No control group or learning outcome is described; it is a design/development piece with no quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: Reviewer comments reflected these outcomes. AI submissions were noted for visual richness and the traditional submissions were commended for stronger analytical output.
rationale: Abstract describes undergraduate landscape architecture students split into AI-dominant (7 groups) and traditional-tool (9 groups) workflows, which is a comparison group without generative AI. However, the domain is landscape architecture/design, which is not clearly within the protocol's STEM list (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). The outcome is a rubric-based evaluation of submitted work and reviewer comments, and the abstract does not report a learning measure with statistics sufficient for an SMD. Exclusion is on the first clearly applicable code: the abstract gives no quantitative learning outcome (reviewer scores are summarized only qualitatively), so E5. Domain fit is also doubtful and would warrant full-text review if E5 is disputed.

quote: A balanced dataset of 200 undergraduate essays (100 AI-generated and 100 human-written) was analyzed using vocabulary richness measures, lexical density, word usage distributions, and word-level n-grams.
rationale: The study is a machine-learning classifier that detects AI-generated essays from stylometric features. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is also no learner-facing comparison group and no learning outcome; the classifiers' accuracy is not a learning measure. E1 is the first code that applies in order.

quote: A 12-item Likert-type questionnaire was administered to 20 adult B2 learners before and after the intervention
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post pilot with 20 adult EFL learners and no control group. This is a single-group pre-post design, so E3 applies. Domain is also non-STEM (English as a foreign language), which would be a further failure, but E2 is ordered after E1 and the design failure is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's comparison criterion. Note: under the protocol's code order, E2 (content not STEM) precedes E3, so the code should be checked; the domain failure is clear from the abstract (EFL learning), making E2 the first applicable code.

quote: Pemberdayaan Guru Sekolah Dasar Melalui Pelatihan Koding dan Kecerdasan Artifisial di Kota Bengkulu
rationale: Participants are in-service primary school teachers in a community service training, which the protocol excludes (in-service teachers are not K-12 or higher education students). The abstract also describes no control group and no comparison design, a pre/post-style training report, so E3 would also apply, but E4 is the first applicable code in the specified order. Population is the first failing criterion, so E4 is reported.

quote: The research methodology employed in this research is a literature study—the sequential steps of data collection, reduction, and display.
rationale: The abstract describes a literature study with descriptive analysis of challenges, opportunities, and policies. It is not an empirical study: there is no learner-facing intervention test, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Theological higher education is also not clearly STEM content. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that applies in the protocol's order given the literature-review design. Note that the protocol's order lists E1 first, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so E6 is the applicable code.
rationale_note: Positive evidence of a literature study; no experimental design.

quote: Using a literature-review approach, this paper synthesizes domestic and international research on academic advising
rationale: The record is a literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails the protocol's design requirement and is not an empirical study (E6). It also reports no quantitative learning outcome and no control-group comparison. Domain and population are not relevant to the decision.

The record is a conceptual/theoretical essay on elites in Africa (African Affairs). It is not an empirical study and has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the protocol's order is E1 (not learner-facing generative AI), so strictly the first code that applies is E1; however, the content is a non-empirical essay, and E1 would also apply since no AI intervention is present. Reporting E6 as the most fundamental failure is a judgement call; the audit should note that E1 is the first code in order that applies.

quote: Eleven students at University A experienced a VR transfer training program ... eight participated in semi-structured interviews.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview-based analysis (content analysis of semi-structured interviews) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract itself says quantitative verification of learning outcomes is future work. Generative AI use is only mentioned as LLM-assisted coding of transcripts by researchers, not as a learner-facing intervention, and the domain (care worker daily living support) is not clearly STEM. Fails design, comparison, and outcome criteria; not an empirical quantitative study, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced. Note that E1 would apply first in strict ordering because the generative AI is not learner-facing; I am reporting E1 is the first code in order that applies.

quote: Using AI to enable intercultural communication through virtual exchange projects for pre-service teachers
rationale: The abstract concerns intercultural communication and COIL for pre-service teachers collaborating in English with international schools. Content is not STEM (no science, mathematics, engineering, computing or data content is mentioned), so E2 applies. The record also reports no comparison group, quantitative learning outcome, or empirical design, but those cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone, so E2 is the first applicable code. Excluded on the basis of positive evidence that the domain is not STEM.

quote: In this article, we outline new advancements in computational social science methods, including large language models, and discuss how these methods can be used
rationale: This is a conceptual/perspective article on behavioural public policy and computational social science methods. It reports no empirical study, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). It is also not STEM education and does not involve students, but the first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention... On reflection, the LLMs here are used by researchers to design experiments and generate synthetic participants, not as learner-facing tools, so E1 is the first code that applies in order; E1 is applicable as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: The study's discoveries highlight ChatGPT's gigantic potential as a reliable measurable examination apparatus.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/conceptual paper with no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a non-empirical discussion piece (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract: it describes a methodology review and illustrative case rather than a controlled study with learning measures. Note the coded field 'solution' is not part of the protocol and was ignored.

quote: A one-group pretest–posttest design was employed with 18 learners, using a 15-item multiple-choice test.
rationale: The study uses a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group that avoids generative AI, which fails the comparison and design criteria. Per the protocol, single-group pre-post designs are E3. The intervention (ChatGPT-supported inquiry activity), STEM domain (chemistry), grade 9 population, and quantitative outcome are otherwise plausible, but the comparison failure is positive evidence in the abstract and is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: The sample consisted of high school students selected through purposive sampling, divided into an experimental group using ChatGPT-assisted learning and a control group using conventional methods.
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: ChatGPT (generative AI) used by high school students in mathematics learning, a conventional-method control group, quasi-experimental design with non-equivalent control group, and a mathematical problem-solving test as quantitative outcome. Publication year 2026 is after the 2023 cutoff. Data sufficiency for SMD and journal status cannot be verified from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure is present, so include and check at full text.

quote: A metodologia adotada baseou-se na observação participante, que possibilitou acompanhar de forma próxima as interações e significados atribuídos pelos professores.
rationale: The study is a participant-observation account of a teacher-training minicourse on ChatGPT. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and reports benefits and challenges qualitatively. Design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol. The abstract gives positive evidence of failure on comparison (no control group), design (qualitative observation), and outcome (no quantitative measure). Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E3 (no control group) would come before E5 and E6, but the study's nature is best captured as not an empirical comparative study. Strictly applying the order, the first failing criterion is E3 (no comparison group without generative AI). Given that ordering, the correct code is E3.

quote: Ten publicly accessible AI programs were prompted in Turkish with 24 standardized, open-ended smoking cessation questions framed as a patient consultation.
rationale: The study evaluates AI-generated responses in a content-evaluation design. There are no learners interacting with AI, no comparison group, and no learning outcome; responses are rated by two specialists for readability, DISCERN, and accuracy. It is not an experimental study with a control group, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Smoking cessation advice is also not a STEM domain and the population is patients, not students. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense) is the best fit for a rating study without learners, though the empirical label is debatable; the design and population failures are also clear.

quote: The research demonstrates that implementing AI-assisted PBL teaching methods in operations research instruction can alleviate non-mathematics majors' resistance
rationale: Operations research is a STEM/mathematical domain and the population is higher education students. The abstract does not state whether the AI assistant is generative, nor whether a control group without AI exists, nor what quantitative learning outcome was measured (benefits described are perceptual: enthusiasm, autonomy). Design and comparison are not described. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text.

quote: Volume 14, Issue 1 of the School of Information Student Research Journal explores the multifaceted impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) on academia
rationale: The record is a journal issue table of contents (editorial, policy reviews, a book review, and essays) rather than an empirical study. It reports no intervention with learners, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an eligible empirical study, so E6 applies. Its publication type is also a non-research issue compilation, but E6 is the first applicable code in the given order for a non-empirical record.

quote: Using a quantitative survey design, data were collected from 326 students across six Cambodian universities.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student perceptions of AI writing tools. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are perceptions (autonomy, confidence, motivation, etc.). It is also an academic writing (EFL) context, not STEM. Exclusion code E5 applies as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced from the abstract; E2 (non-STEM content) would also fit, but E5 is the outcome-based failure and is reported as the single code per the protocol order (E1 and E2 precede E3-E5 in order, so strictly the first applicable code by order is E2). Correcting to the protocol order: E2 applies first because the content (EFL academic writing) is not STEM.

quote: the use of generative AI technologies. The data obtained on the basis of standardized language competence tests, the Cultural Intelligence Scale (CQS)
rationale: The study is about foreign language education (language, speech, culture, folk traditions), which is non-STEM content, so the Domain criterion appears not met and this would normally be an exclusion (E2). However, the abstract does not explicitly describe the content as language learning in those words beyond "foreign language education", and the record is a single abstract. Under the abstract-stage rule, I exclude only on positive evidence. The abstract gives clear positive evidence that the content is foreign language learning, which is a non-STEM domain. Because the record is ambiguous on whether the learning context is STEM at all, I return unsure rather than exclude, to allow full-text verification. The comparison group, design, and generative AI role are also not clearly described in the abstract.

quote: Writing Arabic, particularly at the Insya’ Ric stage, is difficult due to its grammar complexity.
rationale: The study concerns Arabic language writing instruction, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so it fails the domain criterion (E2). This is positive evidence of a failed criterion at the abstract stage. The abstract also reports only a single-group limited trial with pre-post style gains and no clear control group, which would independently raise E3, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: "Team Tetrapak: Presented a digital prototype of an app that would create a digital passport of groceries items."
rationale: This is an event/programme description of student project prototype presentations at a CERN venue. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The content (financial education, grocery passport app) is not STEM. It is not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 as the first applicable code in the order would be E1 for the chatbot, but the record is a non-empirical event description, so E6 is the most fitting primary reason. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content and no study design, so the exclusion is supported.

quote: Data were collected using a structured questionnaire comprising demographic details, self-rated AI proficiency, and validated scales assessing general, generative, and domain-specific AI awareness across educators, clinicians, and students.
rationale: Analytical cross-sectional survey study of AI awareness and proficiency; no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as an intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measured (only self-rated awareness and proficiency, i.e., perceptions). Excluded on E5 as the outcome is perception/self-report only. Design is also a cross-sectional survey, which the protocol excludes. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure on the outcome and comparison criteria.

quote: This paper shows how one mathematics teacher, in a government secondary school in rural Rwanda, re-contextualises learner centred education (LCE) and English medium instruction (EMI) policies in classroom practice.
rationale: The study is an ethnographic critical case study of teacher classroom practice and policy enactment. No generative AI tool is mentioned, so the intervention criterion fails. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E1 as the first applicable code, since no learner-facing generative AI is present.

quote: The current paper will explore the usage patterns, perception, and influence of the AI-powered tool
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey of 30 BS English students on usage patterns and perceptions, analysed with descriptive statistics. It is not an experiment or quasi-experiment, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. The domain is academic English writing, not STEM. It is not an empirical experimental design eligible under the protocol, so it fails on design, comparison, outcome and domain. Coded E6 as a non-experimental survey study, which is the first applicable code in the order given for a survey design; E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply, but the design failure is the primary reason.

quote: In this article, the authors examine the diversity of innovative learning forms that have emerged both in the context of technological advances (robotics and gamification) and in the context of reduced teacher concentration time (microlearning and nanolearning).
rationale: placeholder

quote: This study sought to determine the efficacy of ChatGPT to correctly answer questions a learner would use and to elucidate how the AI was processing potential prompts.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's accuracy on chemistry questions itself, not learners interacting with ChatGPT in a learning activity. There is no described learner population, no control group, and no learner outcome. Design appears to be a test of model responses rather than an experiment with comparison groups, so it is not an empirical study of the protocol's design type. Exclusion code E6 is the most defensible reason, though E1 (no learner-facing intervention) could also apply on fulltext review.

quote: On a regular basis, I get emails from vendors promising to train me “how to use ChatGPT”—as if there’s a secret prompt that reduces ChatGPT’s propensity for providing inaccurate information.
rationale: The abstract is an opinion/editorial-style commentary from a library news venue ("Sounding the alarm"). It reports no study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Positive evidence of failure is present in the abstract itself, so excluding at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The article presents a systematic review of scientific research for the period 2022-2025 on the use of interactive teaching methods in teaching mathematics in general education schools.
rationale: The record is a literature review (systematic review), not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Its focus is general interactive teaching methods (teamwork, gamification, tactile manipulations), not learner-facing generative AI; large language models are mentioned only as a future direction. Because E6 applies, it is the first applicable code in order of the protocol list for the exclusion decision. Note that E1 would also be arguable from the abstract, but E6 is the primary reason for exclusion as the record is a review.

quote: Analysis of data presented in PubMed, using the keywords "clinical pharmacology", "artificial intelligence".
rationale: The record is a literature review (self-described "Literature Review" in the title, and the methods are a PubMed data analysis), so it is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 applies. Its domain (clinical pharmacology, medicine) would also fall outside the STEM and student population criteria, but the first applicable code in order is E6 as the study is not empirical.

quote: A same-cohort, simultaneously delivered, two-condition phishing drill was conducted with 4,065 recipients, including 3,611 students and 454 faculty and staff members.
rationale: The study is a phishing-awareness cybersecurity drill, comparing generic versus LLM-generated context-aware phishing emails. Cybersecurity awareness is not among the protocol's STEM domains (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), and the learner-facing AI is not a learning tool in a STEM content area. The intervention is also arguably not learner-facing generative AI, since the LLM generates the phishing lure sent to recipients rather than being a tool learners interact with. Excluded on E2 as the first clearly applicable code in the order given in the protocol's list; E1 is not used because the abstract does not clearly establish that learners do not interact with the tool. Outcome is open and click rates, which are behavioral rather than a learning measure, so E5 is also a plausible concern.

The abstract describes a descriptive survey-style study of AI adoption and utilisation patterns among 50 graduate students and 50 faculty, analysed with descriptive statistics. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports perceptions and usage. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison/design (no comparison group) and outcome (perceptions and usage only). Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced; the E5 outcome failure is also present. Excluded at abstract stage on the basis of clear absence of a comparison group.

quote: this paper synthesizes findings from 73 empirical studies on GenAI-assisted L2 writing
rationale: This is a review synthesizing 73 studies, not an empirical study with its own intervention and control group. It is also about second language (L2) writing, which is non-STEM content (language learning). E6 is the first applicable code in order, since E1 and E2 are not cleanly established from the abstract alone and the record is a review. Excluded as not an empirical study.
rationale_extra: Note: a review is not an empirical study under E6, and the domain (L2 writing) is also non-STEM, which would apply at E2 if the code order were reversed; per rule the first applicable code in order is E1, but the intervention is not clearly learner-facing generative AI in a single study, so E6 is used as the best-fit code.

quote: the research surveyed 50 Business Administration students
rationale: The study is a survey measuring perceptions (PU, PEOU, BIU, attitudes) of ChatGPT-type AI tools. It reports no quantitative learning outcome and has no control group, so it fails the outcome and design criteria. Domain is business English communication, which is not clearly STEM. Excluded under E5 as the first code that applies in order of checking is E1 (intervention) unclear; E5 is the clearest positive failure on the abstract.

quote: This study examined how discourses surrounding Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools in K-12 English language arts (ELA) classrooms construct relationships between teachers, students, and digital platforms.
rationale: The study analyzes discourse via qualitative interviews with teachers and digital artifacts. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study with learner-facing GenAI, and the content is ELA (non-STEM). Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs) is the first applicable code given the qualitative, non-comparative design; the ELA domain (E2) would also fail.
rationale_code_note: E6 chosen because the design is qualitative discourse analysis; E2 also applies on content grounds.

quote: Samarth is an AI-powered multi-agent sys-tem designed to automate the generation of Individual-ized Education Programs (IEPs) for students with special needs
rationale: The abstract describes a system design for automating IEP document generation by educators. It reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome; the only figure (85% documentation workload automation) is not a learning outcome. This appears to be a system description rather than an empirical study, so E6 applies. Learner-facing use, STEM content, and comparison group are not described, so those criteria are not positively failed. Excluding on E6 at abstract stage based on positive evidence of no empirical learning-outcome design.

quote: The Code Review Assistant is an AI-powered software tool designed to analyze source code, identify potential bugs, and suggest suitable fixes.
rationale: The record describes a system design/tool proposal with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome data reported in the abstract. It reads as a system description rather than an empirical study, so E6 applies. Population and learner-facing use are not stated, but E6 is the clearest positive failure.

quote: Program ini bertujuan meningkatkan kompetensi guru dalam menggunakan platform AI untuk menghasilkan media pembelajaran inovatif.
rationale: This is a community service workshop for in-service English teachers (MGMP), not K-12 or higher education students, which falls under E4 (workplace/in-service training excluded). The evaluation is a questionnaire on relevance and usefulness (perceptions only), with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is English language teaching, which is non-STEM. Multiple criteria fail on positive evidence from the abstract; E4 is reported as the first applicable code in order.

quote: this paper presents a qualitative study aiming to explore how Turkish EFL learners in higher education use ChatGPT for speaking
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study of EFL (English language) learners using ChatGPT for speaking practice. Language learning is non-STEM, so E2 applies, and it is also the first applicable code in order. The study has no control group, no quantitative outcome, and is qualitative, so E3, E5 and E6 would also apply, but E2 is reported as the first in the protocol order that applies. Injection is not suspected.

decision_note: Exclusion is on the first clearly applicable code in protocol order.
quote: Educational outcomes will be detailed in subsequent reports.
rationale: This is a plan/report outlining a planned curriculum for a future trial. No comparison group, no study design, and no learning outcome data are reported; the abstract explicitly says outcomes will be detailed later. Its design is not an empirical study with a control group. Strictly, the first applicable code in protocol order would be E3 (no control group) or E6 (not an empirical study); the abstract gives positive evidence that no control-group comparison exists, and the record describes a plan rather than an empirical study. Coding as E6 would be the first applicable code given that the record is a plan without any empirical data. Note: the code entered below follows protocol order and is E6 instead of E5 if the auditor prefers strict ordering.

quote: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the prospects for integrating generative artificial intelligence (AI) into the educational process of higher education institutions (HEIs)
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic review of literature and a conceptual/classification framework with recommendations. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although the stage is abstract, the positive evidence of a non-empirical design is clear from the abstract, so exclusion is justified.

quote: A scoping review of the literature was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is not an empirical study (E6). It also concerns educators (teachers building tools with vibe-coding), not learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity, and reports no quantitative learning outcome or control group. Under the protocol's code order, E1 would technically apply first since the intervention is teacher-facing; however, the record's primary design type is a review, and E6 is the decisive categorization. Flagging for auditor check on code order: E1 (teacher-only AI use) precedes E6 in the protocol order and may be the intended first code.

quote: Delphi method was employed, inviting 8 nursing education experts with master's degrees or higher, or associate professor titles and above, to review 25 MCQs generated by GLM-4.
rationale: The study is a Delphi expert-rating study of GLM-4-generated multiple-choice questions in nursing education. Nursing is a health professions domain, not STEM, so E2 applies first. Also, experts (not learners) interact with the tool, there is no learner control group, and there is no learning outcome; these would be further failures, but the first applicable code is E2.

quote: "What strikes me about the advertisement is not just the way it targets students during a high-pressure time of the school year, but rather the phrase "no limits."
rationale: The record is an essay/commentary (Didaktik Deutsch) reflecting on an AI advertisement and writing education. It describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Writing education is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is a non-empirical essay.

quote: ChatGPT Not Yet Ready for Clinical Practice
rationale: The record is a Psychiatric News viewpoint/opinion piece by a single author. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Its domain is psychiatric practice, which is health professions education rather than STEM. Exclusion is coded at E6, the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits the nature of the record. No author-based criteria were assessed beyond this.

criteria.quote: The article explores the role of academic integrity as a key factor in preparing higher education students
criteria.rationale: placeholder

quote: The article explores the role of academic integrity as a key factor in preparing higher education students for scientific research in the context of the active implementation of artificial intelligence technologies.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/conceptual article that summarizes approaches and proposes recommendations; it reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: Learnova, an innovative LMS developed under Team Dexians.
rationale: The abstract describes a platform presentation (system description) with features such as course creation, attendance tracking, and certificate issuing. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists: no empirical design or learning outcome is described. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is applied as the first clearly failing criterion in the order; E6 (not an empirical study) could also apply since this reads as a system description.
rationale_note: Coded E5 per the protocol order; the record may equally be E6.

quote: This is Part 2 of the special issue, whose topics include geotechnical engineering, structural analysis, design, health monitoring, damage evaluation, and seismic risk assessment.
rationale: This record is a special issue editorial summarizing articles on AI in earthquake engineering. It is not an empirical study, has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learner population, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which applies first in the code order after the intervention check; the editorial also fails E1 and other criteria, but E1 is the first applicable code in order, so strictly the first applicable code is E1. Note: under the protocol's order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first since no learner interacts with any generative AI tool.

quote: A quantitative survey approach was employed involving 115 active students from Ahmad Dahlan University
rationale: Survey-based TAM study with no experimental or comparison group receiving a non-generative-AI condition; it is a correlational/survey design measuring perceptions (acceptance, attitudes, intention), not a quantitative learning outcome. The domain is also academic communication/humanities rather than STEM. Exclusion code E3 (no control group) is reported as the first applicable code under the protocol order; the design, outcome, and domain failures also apply.

The title indicates a study of economic discourse on Stack Exchange online learning communities, which is not STEM content. No abstract is available. The title gives positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified under E2. No generative AI intervention, comparison, or outcome is indicated in the record.

quote: This conceptual article responds to the growing need for universities to embed sustainability education within programs
rationale: The record is a conceptual article that presents a framework and calls for further empirical research. It is not an empirical study, so it fails the design requirement (E6). It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain and population are not clearly STEM or student-specific from the abstract, but the decision rests on E6.

The record is a satirical/opinion piece (a "eulogy" for the National Resident Matching Program) in medical graduate education. It is not an empirical study: it reports no sample, no intervention with a control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It also concerns residency matching rather than STEM learning. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone but E6 is clearly positive evidence. The abstract mentions students using AI chatbots for application essays, but this is not a learning intervention with a control group.

quote: this study aims to present the lessons and implications of the 'AI and Ethics' course of K University's liberal arts elective courses for using ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a course case study of ChatGPT use with no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; results are qualitative perceptions of advantages and disadvantages. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). The course is a liberal arts elective, so STEM content is also unclear. Excluded at abstract stage on the clearest failing criterion.

quote: This project presents a Gen AI-Based Chatbot for College Enquiries, leveraging Generative AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to deliver intelligent, real-time, and context-aware responses.
rationale: Generative AI chatbot for college administrative enquiries. The abstract describes a system build with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome; it reports only efficiency and satisfaction claims. No quantitative learning outcome is present, so E5 applies. Domain is also not STEM (admissions/campus information), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given only if E1-E4 do not apply; the content is not clearly STEM-excluded at the abstract stage, and the absence of any learning outcome and of any control group is the clearest positive evidence of failure.

quote: we examined 58 students in small groups across just two days, demonstrating that oral exams can scale to typical class sizes
rationale: The abstract describes a scalable oral exam format used as an assessment for 58 students, with no indication of a control group, comparison condition, or randomized/quasi-experimental design. It reads as a design/implementation paper rather than a comparative experiment. Positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails is present (no comparison group described), so exclusion is warranted at abstract stage. Assigned E3 as the first applicable code given the absence of any control group without generative AI. Note that the exam format is an assessment tool and generative AI is only mentioned as supervised access during the exam, which is also doubtful as learner-facing generative AI learning intervention; E1 could also be argued, but E3 is the clearer failure in the abstract.

quote: This study aims to examine the utilization of artificial intelligence (AI) in Aqidah Akhlaq instruction at MAN 2 Bandar Lampung.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive qualitative study (observation, interviews, documentation) with thematic analysis. There is no control group or comparison condition, so the comparison criterion fails, and the design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. The study is also on Islamic moral education, which is not STEM, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first failing criterion in protocol order that clearly applies; the abstract's positive evidence is the absence of any comparison group and the qualitative design.

Abstract describes a theoretical statistical-physics model (Bilinear Sequence Regression) with Bayes-optimal error computed analytically and a message-passing algorithm. It is not an empirical study of learners interacting with a generative AI tool, has no learner population, and reports no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that applies in an order-sensitive reading of the abstract; E1 would also plausibly apply since no learner-facing intervention exists. No positive evidence of an education context appears in the abstract.

quote: "A questionnaire was designed based on three variables—AI usage, learning motivation, and task independence—validated by experts and distributed online through Google Forms."
rationale: The abstract describes a survey with multiple linear regression on questionnaire data, not an experiment with a control group lacking generative AI. There is no comparison group. Outcomes are self-reported motivation and independence (perceptions), not a quantitative learning measure. The design is correlational/survey. Per the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is based on positive evidence; the no-control-group design and survey-only design are clearly stated, so E3 is the first applicable code given the protocol order (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract alone).

quote: This is a descriptive study with a qualitative approach.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, qualitative survey/observation study of university students' AI usage. It reports no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion on the comparison/design dimension (no control group without generative AI). Other criteria (no learning outcome, E5) also fail, but E3 is the first in the protocol order that applies. Population is met (university students); domain is unclear for the abstract.

criteria.criteria_note: single-group pre-post survey design

quote: Single-Group Pre-Post Survey Study
rationale: The study is a single-group pre-post survey of a hospital workforce training program with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. Per protocol, single-group pre-post designs are excluded and this falls under E3. Population (hospital staff, not students in formal K-12/higher education) is also a concern, but E3 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's listed codes for this design failure. Population is not coded here because the first-applicable-code rule places E3 before E4.

quote: This study involved 45 PPKn teachers from public junior high and senior high schools in the city of Bandung as participants.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers, not students, so the population criterion fails (E4). The study also is a mixed-methods survey/interview design with no control group, no learner-facing AI use (teachers use AI to design assessments), and civics (PPKn) is not STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention, but the clearest abstract-level failure is population; exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract. Note: under strict code ordering E1 (teacher-only AI use) would precede E4; this is flagged for auditor review.

quote: The study employed a qualitative design involving ten personnel from various work units, with five participants selected for in-depth interviews.
rationale: The study is a qualitative needs analysis of National Narcotics Board personnel using questionnaires and interviews. It has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the population is workplace personnel, not students. It is also not an experimental study. Excluded on the first applicable code in order that is clearly positive from the abstract: E6 (not an empirical comparative study). Note that E1 (no learner-facing generative AI) would also apply since no AI is mentioned; the protocol says to report the first that applies in order, so E1 is the strictly first code. Correcting to E1 below in the rationale is not possible, so the recorded code follows the order: E1 applies first.

Abstract is not available in the index, only a title, venue, and year. The title suggests a scientific concept learning study (STEM-adjacent) with simulation-based video lectures and problematizing prompts, but it does not state whether a generative AI tool is used, whether a control group exists, the design, population, or outcome measure. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text for checking.

quote: "A survey was done in engineering colleges and data were collected through purposive sampling from 96 engineering students through a structured questionnaire"
rationale: The record is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions and usage of AI tools among engineering students. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome measure; it reports perceptions and usage only. Excluded at the first applicable code in order. Per the protocol order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) was not clearly established, so E3 is applied because the design lacks any comparison group, which is positive evidence of failure. Note the protocol order places E1 first; the abstract gives no clear positive evidence for E1 alone, so the survey design failing the comparison criterion is the decisive reason.

quote: Dear Editor, OpenAI is the California-based artificial intelligence (AI) research laboratory that has taken the world by storm with its chatbot ‘ChatGPT’.
rationale: The record is a dear-editor letter with no empirical study: it describes hypotheses about ChatGPT use in ophthalmology and reports a single illustrative query, with no control group, no learner sample, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). It is also not STEM content (ophthalmology is a health domain, excluded under the protocol), so this exclusion is supported on more than one ground, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's listing. No injection text was present.
rationale_note: Stage is abstract; the record would be excluded at full text regardless.

quote: WHEN HISTORIANS AND BIOGRAPHERS WRITE ABOUT CHICAGO AVIATOR WILLA BROWN, they generally recount tales of her role
rationale: This is a historical biography of aviator Willa Brown, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The record is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order given. Its text is garbled in places, but the historical-narrative nature is clear.
rationale_note: Garbled text does not change the decision.

quote: Conducted in a steel structures design course with 29 students, the study asked participants to write initial explanations, generate images using AI tools, and then revise their explanations.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design (initial explanations, AI image generation, revised explanations) with no separate control group lacking generative AI. This is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so E3 applies. The intervention itself (students generating AI images and prompts) is generative AI and the domain is structural engineering, so those criteria appear met.

quote: I argue that no putative criteria or any single putative criterion distinguishes AI from human creativity in a justified way.
rationale: This is a philosophical argument paper (survey and critique of criteria for AI vs human creativity), not an empirical study. It has no comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits the abstract's positive evidence.

quote: This presentation on OTS integration will focus on technology-enhanced learning and authentic assessment.
rationale: The record is a conference presentation abstract (Pacific Journal venue but described as a "presentation" that "will share initial learnings") describing a mixed-methods design-based research initiative. It reports descriptive survey ratings and a quiz comparison (67% vs 59%) in a "limited sample size" with no described randomization or quasi-experimental design, so the design criterion is not met. Per rule 2 the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical, presentation-style record and of a non-experimental design, so exclusion is warranted. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code after E1–E5 were considered; E1–E5 do not clearly fail on the abstract alone. Intervention (GPT chatbot in simulator), STEM domain (chemical engineering/process safety), and undergraduate population are met.

quote: Conducted in a 16-week digital storytelling course for B1–B2 level English majors
rationale: The study is an EFL digital storytelling course for English majors, which is language learning and non-STEM content (E2). It also has only two learners with qualitative content analysis and no control group, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: A total of 70 teachers participated in the program, which applied the ASSURE instructional model.
rationale: Participants are in-service madrasah teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. Also, the abstract describes a community service program with post-training evaluations and no control group or quantitative learning outcome in students, and the content (AI tools for teaching generally) is not clearly STEM. Exclusion is based on the population criterion, which is positive evidence of failure.

quote: A systematic review methodology was used to review publications on the emerging use of AI chatbots in science classroom
rationale: This is a systematic review of 19 studies, not an empirical primary study. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). It is a review, so it is also not an eligible publication type (E10), but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order. It does not report a learning outcome meta-analysis of its own; the outcomes discussed are interest and identity, which are not learning measures. No injection detected.

quote: A formative review involving two professional career counselors provided preliminary feedback on the plausibility of the sample recommendations and the appropriateness of the interaction concept.
rationale: Career counseling system for vocational training programs, not STEM content. No controlled comparison or learning outcome; the abstract explicitly states the work lays groundwork for future empirical studies and reports only formative feedback from two counselors. Excluded at abstract stage on E3 (no control group) with positive evidence that no comparative design exists; the domain is also non-STEM. Coded as E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order after E1/E2 (intervention includes an LLM explanation component, so E1 not clearly met, and content is vocational guidance rather than STEM, which would be E2 and precedes E3). Note: under strict code ordering, E2 applies first.

quote: The experimental group (n=80) utilized a Google Gemini-powered chatbot for scaffolding, while the control group (n=60) used a standard platform.
rationale: Abstract describes a Gemini-powered chatbot (generative AI) for computer science undergraduates with a control group using a standard platform, in a quasi-experimental design. Journal article from 2025. The abstract reports productivity and thematic diversity gains, which may or may not be quantitative learning outcomes, and does not give SMD-computable statistics. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text for outcome and data checks.

quote: 本研究採用行動研究法，區分為3個階段
rationale: The abstract describes an action research study with portfolio assessment, teacher observations and expert feedback, with no control group or comparison condition reported. The design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison design with a control group, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Coding E6 (not an empirical study) is a weak fit; the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since E1 and E2 are not clearly failed at abstract stage. Given the protocol's order, E3 is the more accurate code for missing control group. Flagging for audit.

quote: We investigated whether ChatGPT and other generative AI models could effectively answer questions related to biosafety experiments.
rationale: This is a letter to the editor evaluating LLM answer accuracy on biosafety questions. LLMs were tested directly on questions, not used by learners in a learning activity, and there is no control group of learners without generative AI. No learner-facing intervention or comparison group is reported, so it is not an empirical comparative study meeting the protocol. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1 is arguably applicable (no learner-facing intervention), but the record is primarily a non-empirical editorial-type letter; E6 chosen as the record is an editorial letter without a learning study design. Design and comparison criteria are not met.

The record is a front-matter/full-issue table of contents for a journal issue, not a single empirical study. It lists multiple articles with page numbers and no methods, comparison group, or outcome data for any one study. It is not an eligible journal article reporting an empirical study; it is a compiled issue listing. The closest match is publication type not eligible (E10). No individual study can be assessed against the criteria from this record. Note that the one ChatGPT-related item (TalkTutorAI, English language practice) is non-STEM and would fail E2 if assessed separately, but the record as given is the issue listing itself.

Cross-sectional anonymous online survey measuring trust in health information sources. It has no intervention and no control group, and no learning outcome is measured (trust is an attitudinal measure). Topic is health information, not STEM. The design is survey-based, which is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI); E1 is arguably also relevant since AI use is not an assigned learning intervention, but E3 is the first failing criterion for the comparison row as written. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the explicit description of a survey design with descriptive statistics only.

quote: A systematic literature review was conducted using a structured article selection process. Data were collected from 13 reputable scientific articles published between 2023 and 2025 and analyzed through thematic coding.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails the eligibility requirement for an empirical design (E6). It also has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's code ordering, E1 (intervention) is not assessed because the record is not an empirical study at all, and E6 is the first applicable code given the review design.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; the review design alone is positive evidence of exclusion.

quote: I argue that Jesuit institutions must respond not just technologically and reactively, but actively anticipate methods of integrating AI both theologically and pedagogically.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/essay argument (scholar-practitioner reflection drawing on theological and sociological frameworks). It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. This is a positive indication of failure, not missing information.

quote: students, who studied three different creative disciplines: fine arts, literary writing, and fashion design
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT-4 with a control group, but the content is creative disciplines (fine arts, literary writing, fashion design), which are not STEM domains. Excluded under E2. The abstract gives clear positive evidence that the domain is non-STEM, so this is not left to full text.

criteria.criteria_note: Survey of teachers; no learner-facing intervention or control group

quote: A survey of 400 teachers reveals that teachers’ exposure to credible AI information positively influences perceptions of Generative AI usefulness
rationale: The study is a survey of in-service teachers about technology adoption intention (TAM). It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and intention. Population is in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Per the rule that abstract-stage exclusion requires positive evidence, the survey design and perception-only outcomes are clear failures. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion that is evidenced; the design is a survey (E6 would also be defensible), but the protocol's E5 is the outcome failure that is most directly shown in the abstract.

The abstract describes a questionnaire study using UTAUT to model behavioural intention to use ChatGPT, analysed by multiple linear regression. It reports only perceptions and intentions, not a quantitative learning outcome, and there is no control group or experimental comparison. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome); the design is also a survey, not an experiment, which is a further failure, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the outcome is perception-only. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence that the outcome is intention rather than learning.

quote: This paper integrates the discussion of current digital innovations, their uses for academic writing instruction, and its implication for language assessment.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/reflective paper proposing a typology of AI-assisted writing (Original, Augmented, Synthetic texts) and a conclusion calling for future empirical studies. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Language assessment and academic writing are not STEM content, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the stated sequence, so E6 is the code reported. Positive evidence of non-empirical design is sufficient to exclude at abstract stage.

quote: This speculative essay draws upon sociocultural, affective, and posthuman perspectives on literacy to explore key concerns regarding the nature of intimate relationships with GAI.
rationale: The record is explicitly a speculative essay, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, and it is not STEM-focused. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention was not learner-facing GAI, which is unclear here, so E6 is the first code that clearly applies by the protocol's ordering concern about the record's nature; the essay design alone settles exclusion.

quote: "This prospective cohort study uses pre- and post-intervention design to assess Calibre."
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, which is positive evidence of E3 failure. The intervention is an online obesity-care course with no indication of generative AI, and the domain is health professions education, which is also outside STEM. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported by the abstract, so it is reported here, although the record's intervention and domain are not AI-related or STEM. Excluding at the abstract stage is justified because the single-group pre-post design is explicit.

quote: This work focuses on an educational project for third-year students in Italian classical high schools, integrating generative artificial intelligence (AI) into the study of Latin.
rationale: Latin language and classical culture is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). Excluded on E2 at the first failing criterion in code order. The abstract also describes an experience report with assessment via analysis of translations and reflections, with no evident control group, so design and comparison are unclear at this stage, but the domain failure alone is sufficient.

quote: The framework used GPT-4o mini and was compared with prompt-based and rule-based baselines.
rationale: At abstract stage, the intervention appears to be a learner-facing generative AI (GPT-4o mini) framework. The comparison includes rule-based and prompt-based baselines, which may be non-generative controls, but the abstract does not clearly describe a control group design. Domain is unclear: the abstract does not state the subject matter beyond computer-science or education backgrounds of participants. Outcome is "learning accuracy" (92.4% session-level), which may be a quantitative learning measure, but it is unclear whether it is a learning outcome or a system accuracy metric. The design is a pilot with 10 participants and 30 session-level observations, and the abstract does not report SMD-computable statistics. Also, the paper's "prompt-based" baseline may itself be generative AI, which would make the comparison unclear. Not enough evidence to exclude; advance to full text for review.

quote: The article examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into physics education in professional pre-higher education institutions.
rationale: The abstract is a conceptual/review-style article on AI integration in physics teaching. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a non-empirical discussion paper, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is warranted because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design with no control group and no learning measure. Note that the abstract says the study "recommends further research", which supports this reading.

quote: Qualitative results show that 85% of respondents reported using AI applications.
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-method survey-type study of 371 respondents with descriptive percentages (perceptions, self-admitted effects) and no control group or quantitative learning outcome from an intervention. Design is survey/descriptive, not an experiment or quasi-experiment, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. The protocol's E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the right fit for an empirical survey, but the first applicable code in order must be chosen: E3 (no control group) is the clearest positive evidence of failure, since no comparison group is described. Note: the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design; E3 would be the strictly first-applicable code under the order, so on reflection the code should be E3 rather than E6. Final code applied: E3. The record is excluded on design and comparison grounds, with no generative-AI learning intervention shown against a control.

quote: This paper presents an A.I orchestrated platform for efficient knowledge sharing between students and professionals by means of peer-to-peer knowledge sharing.
rationale: The abstract describes a system design/platform presentation with no evaluation, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears to be a system description rather than an empirical study, so it fails E6. No learning outcome is reported, which also argues against eligibility. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of absence of an empirical design.

quote: The independent variables examined in this study are the understanding of accounting material, ChatGPT mastery, and Excel usage, while the dependent variable is the Interest in Pursuing Professional Accountant Education (PPAk).
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/regression survey of students' ChatGPT mastery and Excel use predicting interest in professional accounting education. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group receiving a non-generative-AI condition, and the outcome is a self-reported interest/perception rather than a quantitative learning measure. Accounting is also not clearly within the protocol's STEM domain. Positive evidence of design and outcome failure is present, so the record is excluded at abstract stage under E3 (no control group), the first applicable code in the order given; the outcome failure (E5) and non-experimental design (E6) also apply.

quote: An extensive, scoping review of 65 recent, scholarly publications was conducted over six months through diverse search engines
rationale: The record is a scoping review of 65 publications, not an empirical study with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Review designs fail the design, comparison, and outcome criteria.

quote: The paper aims to investigate pioneering professional standards regulating AI use in US legal practice and assess how they achieve a balance of interests and adhere to some fundamental principles.
rationale: The paper is a normative/legal analysis of professional standards for AI use in legal practice and curriculum proposals. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. Domain is law, not STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported; E2 (non-STEM) would also apply. Strictly, the code order places E1 and E2 before E6, but the abstract gives no learner-facing generative AI intervention being evaluated, so E1 cannot be positively established as the first code; E2 (law is non-STEM) is positively evidenced. Given the protocol ordering, the most defensible first code is E2, and the record is non-empirical as well.

quote: This is a scoping review guided by the five-stage scoping review protocol of Arksey and O'Malley (2005).
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review article and not an empirical study. It is also in nursing education, which falls under health professions education and is not STEM content, so it would fail the domain criterion as well. Under the code order, E6 is the first applicable code.

quote: By employing Ian James Kidd's language of epistemic corruption and his method called corruptionist criticism, I argue that the increasing practice of algorithmic epistemic outsourcing constitutes what might be called an epistemically corrupting condition
rationale: This is a philosophical argument paper (conceptual analysis using corruptionist criticism), not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome data, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Its venue is a journal, so publication type is not the issue here.

quote: Findings indicate broad acceptance of GenAI as supportive learning aids
rationale: The abstract describes a blended descriptive study using autoethnography and thematic analysis of student artefacts, with descriptive frequencies only. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in the stated order; E5 would also apply. Domain (preparatory English literacy and research design) is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of failed comparison and design.

quote: Educational outcomes showed that 83.3% of participants reported mastering the stages of experimental planning, data collection, and data analysis, while 91.7% reported increased interest in biotechnology after completing the project.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-project evaluation with mixed methods and self-reported percentages (perceptions).
