There is no mention of a control group without generative AI, so there is positive evidence of no comparison group. Outcomes are self-reported perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in order (comparison is absent); E5 is also likely but E3 is reported first.

quote: This study aims to determine the effect of ChatGPT usage on students' self-efficacy at SMA Negeri 3 Gorontalo.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive correlational design with a single sample measured by questionnaire on ChatGPT usage and self-efficacy, with no control group that does not use generative AI. Self-efficacy is an affective/perception measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and the content is not identified as STEM. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design (E3) is present, so it is excluded under the first applicable code in order.
rationale_extra: Note: E1 and E2 not triggered on the abstract; E3 is the first code with positive evidence.

criteria.criteria_note: Qualitative phenomenological design with teachers as participants

quote: This research employs a qualitative method with a phenomenological approach, utilizing data collection techniques such as structured interviews, observations, and document analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative phenomenological study using interviews, observations, and document analysis. It reports teacher perceptions and self-reported time efficiency and confidence, with no control group and no learner quantitative outcome. Participants are teachers, not students. The study is not an empirical quantitative comparison, so it fails on design, comparison, population, and outcome. Coded E6 as not an empirical study in the sense of a comparative design; the qualitative design is a clear positive failure.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage decision based on positive evidence of qualitative design.

rationale: Abstract describes interviews and a survey of 153 students about access barriers and familiarity with AI tools. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first clearly applicable code; E5 and E6 also apply in substance since the study is a qualitative/survey study without learning outcomes. Positive evidence of a non-experimental design supports exclusion at the abstract stage.

quote: The activity, carried out as a two-day intensive training followed by four weeks of mentoring, was attended by 42 fourth- and sixth-semester Informatics students
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design (pre-test and post-test of the same 42 students, paired-sample t-test) with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. This is a positive indication of failure of the comparison criterion, so E3 applies. Also, this is a community service report published in a community service journal, which may not be a journal article of the expected type, but E3 is the first applicable code in the order used here.

quote: This article focuses on its role in education and everyday life, during which the authors will try to prove the effectiveness, feasibility and advantages of using AI in language training for foreign citizens at the initial stage of learning.
rationale: The record is a discussion/theoretical article on AI in Ukrainian-as-a-foreign-language training. It describes no empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Domain is language learning, which is non-STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order. Note that E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply; E6 is reported as the first in the protocol's ordering that is clearly supported by the abstract.

The record has only a title, venue, and year; no abstract is available. The title suggests a Chinese university population (consistent with the population criterion) and 2026 publication (meets the date criterion). However, it does not indicate whether the AI tool is generative, whether a control group exists, the study design, the STEM domain, or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded. The venue (Radiation Physics and Chemistry) is unusual for an education study, which may be worth checking at full text for domain and design fit.

quote: Se aplicaron talleres sobre métodos de investigación tradicionales y el uso de IA (ChatGPT, Citavi y Connected Papers) de manera alternada.
rationale: Abstract describes a learner-facing ChatGPT use in a university bioethics course (higher education). Traditional-methods workshops are applied alternately with AI workshops, which may or may not constitute a separate control group; the design appears to be a single-cohort mixed-methods study, which could be E3, but the abstract does not clearly say so. Bioethics is not clearly STEM, so domain is also unclear. Outcomes mix grades (quantitative learning) with perceptions. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so the record is advanced to full text for checking design, comparison, domain, and effect-size data.

quote: The research design was that of quantitative research through the use of a structured questionnaire that was administered to IT professionals, cybersecurity experts, academic researchers, and students.
rationale: The study is a descriptive questionnaire survey of perceptions (250 responses, frequencies and means) with no control group, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an experimental design and fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) which is not clearly positively shown, so E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense, i.e., a survey design) is assigned as the most defensible code given the survey design and perception-only outcomes; the cybersecurity topic is also not STEM learning. Reference list contents do not change this.

quote: Overall, the prevalence of ChatGPT was high; however, students placed in intermediate level English classes appear to rely on it more often than those placed in other levels.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey (261 students, 20-item questionnaire, descriptive statistics and qualitative analysis) of ChatGPT usage prevalence. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is English language learning, not STEM. Per the abstract, it is a survey-based descriptive study, not an experiment. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention fails, but the abstract does not clearly show learner-facing use as an intervention; the clearest failing criterion is that it is not an empirical intervention study. Given the protocol's order, E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) is applied as the most accurate code for a survey with no experimental comparison. Note: E2 (non-STEM, English language) also clearly applies and is a strong candidate; the ordering rule places E1 before E2, and the intervention is not clearly excluded at E1, so E2 would be the first failing code if E1 is judged met. Auditor should check the code choice.

quote: based on questionnaire responses from students of various academic levels and disciplines across multiple countries
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire survey of perceptions and usage across countries. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. There is also no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are perceptions and usage. Survey designs are excluded by the protocol. Under the abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome. E3 is the first code that applies in the stated order, since the no-control-group failure is reported before the outcome failure (E5).

quote: The article is devoted to assessing the potential for AI use within project-oriented learning activities of an interdisciplinary nature
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical article based on literature review and an illustrative example using Gemini, with no experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the first-applicable-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established at abstract stage, so E6 is the first code that positively applies. Comparison, design, and outcome criteria are positively unmet.

quote: Therefore, this paper explores, through two semi-structured interviews, EAP teachers' attitudes and beliefs about GenAI use by their students in online English Composition courses
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of teachers' attitudes and beliefs. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria, so it fails on design and outcome. The domain is English composition (language learning, non-STEM), which also fails the domain criterion. The E6 code (not an empirical study) is applied as the first applicable code under the protocol's order would be E1 (teachers not learners) — but to follow the order strictly, E1 applies first since the intervention is not learner-facing; E1 is the first applicable code. Note: the correct first applicable code is E1 when the AI use is by teachers' perspectives, not learner interaction; the reported code is adjusted below.

quote: Делается вывод о том, что цифровые технологии, выступая в роли катализатора, значительно усиливают традиционные методы олимпиадной подготовки
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/methodological article discussing digital tools for olympiad preparation. It reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion under E6 (first applicable code in order is E1 possibly, but the abstract does not show a learner-facing generative AI intervention as an evaluated study; E6 is the clearest positive failure).

quote: Comparing the system to conventional development environments, experimental evaluation shows that it improves comprehension of control flow and functional behavior.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based platform for programming learners (programming is STEM; LLM is generative, learner-facing) with an experimental comparison against conventional development environments, which suggests a control group and a comprehension outcome. However, the abstract does not state the design (randomized or quasi-experimental), the sample population (students vs. other users), or whether quantitative statistics are reported. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is passed to full text.

quote: We introduce TAIPO (The AI-based Product Owner), an AI-supported product owner assistant that embeds generative AI into a Kanban workflow
rationale: The abstract introduces a system (TAIPO) and its prototype implementation; it reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no learning outcome. It describes a tool/system paper rather than an empirical study, so E6 applies. Education is mentioned only as a focus, not as a studied population. No positive evidence of a control group or quantitative learning outcome was given, but the absence of an empirical design is the clear failure point.

quote: Bladder Exstrophy Iliac Osteotomy: 3D Modeling Comparative Analysis of Current Approaches’ Impact on Intrapelvic Volume and Acetabular Version
rationale: This record is a compilation of many unrelated orthopaedic and AI-in-medicine abstracts (the abstract text is garbled and merged). The content is clinical orthopaedic surgery and medical, not STEM education. None of the abstracts describes a controlled learner-facing generative AI study with a quantitative learning outcome. The first abstract is a 3D modeling study with no learners or AI. Excluded at E2 (not STEM) as the first applicable code; the record lacks any eligible design or population. Note that the text is heavily corrupted and does not match the protocol's intervention or population.

quote: In this study, the focus is placed on evaluating the capabilities of the human translator relative to the most contemporary state-of-the-art AI-assisted translation tools such as 'ChatGPT' and 'DeepSeek' in translating text from 'English' to 'Urdu'.
rationale: Study compares human translators with AI translation tools on English-to-Urdu literary/cultural translation quality. The content is language translation, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. It also does not describe learners or a learner-facing control group design, so other codes are unclear. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is positively evidenced by the abstract.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on E2 (non-STEM content: translation).

criteria.dimension_notes: Survey of teachers; no comparison group or learning outcome

quote: A survey was conducted with 455 special education teachers.
rationale: The study is a survey of special education teachers' perceptions and tool use. It is not an experiment, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome of learners. It is a non-empirical-trial survey design, so it fails on design, comparison and outcome. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the survey design is non-experimental; the first applicable code in order would arguably be E3 (no control group) or E5 (no learning outcome), but the clearest positive evidence is the survey design. Excluded.

quote: A survey research design was adopted, and 250 students were randomly selected from five faculties using simple random sampling technique.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey design of perceptions with no control group, no experiment or quasi-experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome (only frequencies, percentages and means of perceptions). Design and comparison fail, so it is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits the lack of a comparison group; the survey design and perception-only outcome would also fail E5/E6, but the protocol says to report the first that applies in order, and E3 precedes them. Domain is not clearly STEM (general academic activities).

quote: The Georgia Institute of Technology is proud to host the seventeenth International Conference on Educational Data Mining (EDM) in Atlanta, Georgia, July 14-July 17, 2024.
rationale: The record is a conference proceedings volume (EDM 2024 proceedings), not a journal article. It describes the conference program and contains no individual empirical study, so it fails the publication-type criterion (E10). Criteria marked unclear are not assessable from this front-matter record.

quote: In this paper, we introduce practical strategies for prompt engineering for educators
rationale: The abstract describes a practical/conceptual paper presenting prompt engineering strategies (PARTS, CLEAR, REFINE) with examples. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Population and domain are also not evidenced as STEM learners.

quote: Employing an interview technique facilitated through ChatGPT, the study’s findings highlight differences in student admissions, curricula, graduate competencies, and employment prospects across recreation programs
rationale: The study benchmarks recreation programs (recreation/leisure education) using a ChatGPT-facilitated interview approach. Recreation is not STEM content, so E2 applies first in the code order. It also has no learner-facing generative AI intervention with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; these are noted but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: This paper explores the potential of generative AI, including tools like ChatGPT, to shift from traditional outcome-oriented educational practices
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/proposal paper that proposes a solution integrating experiential learning cycle and learning portfolio with a pedagogical AI agent. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical design in the abstract.

This is a community service (pengabdian masyarakat) report on a ChatGPT training workshop at SMA/SMK schools. It describes delivering material and demonstrations, with no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning measure. The only result is a reported increase in understanding and skills, with no statistics. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies on the evidence available. Domain is Information Technology, which is not clearly STEM, but this is not needed as the first applicable code is E6 when the codes are checked in order. Final decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group and no quantitative outcome.

Content is sexual health education about sexual-risk behaviour consequences (HIV/AIDS, pregnancy, HPV), which is not a STEM domain under the protocol. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code. Also, the AI arm is described as "Meta AI/ChatGPT" without detail on the learner's generative interaction, but the domain failure is sufficient. Design is a quasi-experiment with a comparison group and the population is secondary students, so those criteria appear met.

quote: This illustrative case study examines which AI literacy components can be developed through critical co-discovery
rationale: The abstract describes an illustrative case study with findings framed qualitatively (co-constructed understanding, reflective engagement). There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the record fails the design/comparison and outcome criteria. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, the study is not an empirical experimental study with a comparison group; E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the most appropriate code, since a case study design is listed as excluded. Population and domain (AI literacy for educators, in an in-service/teacher education course) are also not clearly met. Excluding at the abstract stage is justified by positive evidence of a case study design with no comparison group.

quote: The study also included innovative application of ChatGPT as a data source.
rationale: The study concerns Sindhi language and cultural identity, which is non-STEM content (E2). ChatGPT is used as a data source by researchers, not as a learner-facing tool. The design is qualitative with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on the first applicable code, E2.

quote: A methodical approach, where with the help of Gemini, a condition for a task was generated to solidify the knowledge, associated with the program language Python
rationale: The abstract describes a methodological proposal using Gemini (generative AI) to generate a Python programming task for lower secondary students, with comments on code errors and a "learning from an error" technique. It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is descriptive/methodological. Exclusion on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the best fit at abstract stage, though the absence of a control group (E3) and the empirical status (E6) are also doubtful. Positive evidence of a missing quantitative outcome is present in the abstract.

criteria.domain_note: Nephrology/medical education; protocol excludes health professions education, so domain may fail

quote: Nephrology requires students to integrate nephron transport, hormonal regulation, medication effects, and serum and urine electrolyte patterns
rationale: The intervention is a generative AI-assisted (vibe coding, GPT/Gemini) learner-facing app, and there is a control group (other WWAMI sites) with achievement outcomes (exam performance). However, the content is nephrology taught in a medical school context (WWAMI), which falls under health professions education, a protocol exclusion under Domain. The abstract does not clearly establish whether the learners are medical students or whether the content is STEM under the protocol's definition, and the design (aggregate cross-sectional difference-in-differences across sites) and the outcome/data sufficiency need full-text review. Not excluded at abstract stage because the health-domain exclusion is not stated as a definitive fact in the abstract; flagged for full-text check.

The record has only a title and venue with no abstract. The title refers to AI-assisted adaptive tutoring in STEM education evaluated with a neutrosophic multi-criteria decision-making framework. This suggests an evaluation framework rather than a learner-outcome experiment with a control group. It is unclear whether the tutoring system is generative, whether a control group exists, whether a quantitative learning outcome is measured, or whether the design is a randomized or quasi-experiment. Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded. Year 2026 satisfies the date criterion.

quote: This study aimed to ascertain what factors influence the length of time undergraduates receive individual tutoring. Quantitative questionnaires with Likert scale items gathered data on perception, satisfaction, engagement, self-confidence, preference for individualized instruction and participation in decision-making.
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire study of perception, satisfaction, engagement, and self-confidence, with no quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or problem solving. It also reports no control group or comparison design, and the STEM content is not stated. Exclusion under E5 is supported because the only measures are perceptual and affective, which the protocol does not extract. Design and comparison criteria also appear unmet, but the abstract gives no positive evidence of a control group, so E5 is the first code that clearly applies.

quote: The method used is qualitative method by using the theory of translation techniques by Molina Albir and the theory of translation quality by Nababan.
rationale: Study concerns translation of educational news texts using ChatGPT, which is non-STEM (language/translation content). It is also a qualitative analysis of translation techniques with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it fails several criteria. Coded E2 as the first applicable exclusion in protocol order given the non-STEM content; the design is not an experiment with a comparison group.

Abstract describes a mixed-method survey and semi-structured interviews of tertiary students about their experiences using generative AI tools. There is no control or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (only usage, challenges, and perceptions). Design is descriptive/survey/qualitative, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Per the ordering rule, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code. The E3 label is chosen because the absence of a comparison group is the first failing criterion; the design and outcome failures are also clear. STEM domain is not evident from the abstract. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-comparative survey/interview design, exclusion is justified.

quote: Data were collected from 193 undergraduate English language learners
rationale: The study is about English language learning, which is non-STEM content (E2). It also uses a correlational/mixed-methods explanatory design with no evident control group comparing generative AI against non-AI learning, so E3 and design concerns also apply, but the first applicable code in order is E2 only if E1 does not apply. E1 is not clearly shown at abstract stage; the domain failure is the clearest positive evidence, so E2 is reported.

quote: The course has run twice and is now in its third iteration. Teachers report gaining nuanced understandings of technology and its co-constructive role in education.
rationale: This is a course description and practice/teaching-development report for university teachers. It reports teacher perceptions and course design, not an empirical comparative study. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome for students, and no randomized or quasi-experimental design is described. Population is teachers (in-service university teachers), not students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design and no comparison group.
rationale_codes_note: E6 chosen as first applicable code per order; E1 and E4 also arguably apply (teacher-facing, teachers not students), but E6 is the most direct.

quote: Guiding Doctoral Students in the Appropriate and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence for the Doctor of Nursing Practice Proposal Development
rationale: The record has only a title and venue with no abstract. The title indicates a Doctor of Nursing Practice (health professions) context, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (health professions education). Nothing in the record suggests a controlled design or quantitative learning outcome, so this exclusion rests on domain alone. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of the domain failing, not on missing information.

quote: This study used an instrumental approach (Drijvers et al., 2013) to investigate how artificial intelligence (AI) or large language models (LLMs), specifically ChatGPT 3.5, transitioned from an artifact into an instrument
rationale: The abstract describes an instrumental-approach qualitative investigation of four prospective teachers using ChatGPT to build lesson materials. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design appears qualitative (techniques and schemes). Positive evidence of failing comparison and outcome criteria is present, so exclusion is warranted. The code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in the list order that fits the lack of a comparison group; E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply. Participants are prospective teachers, which the protocol counts as higher education.
decision_note: Ordering note: E1 not applicable (learner-facing use by prospective teachers, who are learners).

rationale: Abstract describes an instructional module incorporating PhET simulations with experimental and control groups of Rwandan students, pre/post tests, and a significant post-test difference in chemistry (STEM, school students). The abstract does not state whether the module involves any generative AI; PhET simulations are typically non-generative, so intervention eligibility is unclear. Per the abstract-stage rule, unsure rather than exclude; resolve at full text. Quote not used because no passage shows the generative AI component. Design (comparison group with pre/post) appears to be a controlled comparison but randomization is not stated.

quote: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI) presents both challenges and opportunities for marketing educators.
rationale: Marketing curriculum is not a STEM domain, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a curriculum guide with student satisfaction and self-reported knowledge gains, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome evident. Domain failure is positive evidence, so exclude at abstract stage.

quote: This culminating discussion draws on insights from across the sessions.
rationale: The record is a summit session description/discussion piece, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that the abstract positively supports.

quote: The goal of this study was to evaluate whether AI can be used in thematic analysis to replace manual graders as the gold standard.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT as a grading/coding tool for researchers' thematic analysis of medical students' open-ended responses; learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity (E1 would apply first). Under the protocol's order, E1 is the first applicable code, so the exclusion should arguably be E1 rather than E6. Correction: the first applicable code is E1, since AI is used by researchers for analysis, not learner-facing. No control group without generative AI is described either (E3 also applies but is later in order). Domain (medical education, cadaveric dissection attitudes) also falls outside STEM content, and the study compares AI outputs to manual coders rather than learners, so it is not an empirical learning study. Final code E1.

quote: In this article, we discuss on these issues and provide some recommendations regarding this topic.
rationale: The record is a narrative discussion and recommendations article on ChatGPT in healthcare. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). The healthcare focus also falls under the excluded health professions domain, but E6 is the first applicable code in order here as the study is not empirical.
rationale_note: Abstract stage: positive evidence of non-empirical design is present.

quote: Using OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small, we predicted four categories of SRL processes based on the four-stage SRL model
rationale: The study uses LLM embeddings to classify self-regulated learning in think-aloud transcripts. The generative AI is applied by researchers as a coding/classification tool, not as a learner-facing tool that students interact with during a learning activity. No control group comparing generative AI use against non-AI learning, and no learning outcome is measured. Excluded under E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), the first applicable code.

quote: A comparative analysis of the capabilities of the YandexGPT (Alice) and ChatGPT-4bot (Telegram) language models was carried out according to the main characteristics of the queuing system.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparison of what two language models output for a queuing theory definition and characteristics, not a learner-facing study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome (E5) is present, and no control group is described (E3 also plausible). E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order would be E3 vs E5; however the abstract gives no comparison group and no outcome measure, so I report E5 as the primary failing criterion per the abstract's content. Not an empirical learning study.

criteria.quote: This paper presents an architectural proposal for a modular and adaptive hybrid recommender system
criteria.rationale: The record is an architectural proposal with a technical prototype validation, not an empirical comparative study. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports technical viability and questionnaire-based cold-start resolution. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Note that the paper is not learner-facing generative AI evaluation either, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's logic at this stage since the design is a proposal rather than an empirical study.

quote: This paper presents an architectural proposal for a modular and adaptive hybrid recommender system
rationale: The abstract describes an architectural proposal validated through a functional prototype and a repository of documents, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that the study is not an empirical comparative study (E6). Exclusion codes are applied in order; E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage, so E6 is the cited code.

quote: We propose a Cognitive Alignment Index (CAI)—introduced here and detailed later—which evaluates models not only on statistical accuracy but also on comprehensibility, actionability, feedback receptivity, context awareness, and calibrated trust.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/position paper proposing a Cognitive Alignment Index for cardiovascular AI risk prediction models. It reports no empirical study, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would be the first code to apply, since the paper concerns clinical predictive models rather than learner-facing generative tools. However, the paper's core nature is non-empirical, so E6 is the most accurate single code given the record is a conceptual framework paper. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the study is not empirical and does not involve learners or generative AI. Note: the text contains heavily garbled passages; no injection content was identified.

quote: This review examines the evolving role of AI across three domains: student use, faculty and administrative adoption, and the institutional support structures required for responsible integration.
rationale: The record is a narrative review (Kinesiology Review) that introduces a conceptual "AI+ strategy" and reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Kinesiology is also not clearly STEM, but the review type is the first applicable code in order of E1–E10 that is clearly positive evidence; E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is assigned.
exclusion_code_note: E6 applies on the abstract's description of a review.

quote: This paper explores the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI), specifically OpenAI's ChatGPT, in bridging these communication gaps.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/perspective paper with illustrative case studies, not an empirical study. It reports no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies. Under the abstract-stage rule, this is positive evidence of failure on design and outcome, so exclusion is appropriate rather than unsure.

quote: in this scoping review we examine its potential to complement existing resources and support teachers in delivering C&R instruction
rationale: The record is a scoping review of literature, not an empirical study with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. Reviews are not eligible and the design fails the empirical requirement, so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The abstract also indicates GenAI is aimed at teachers rather than learners, which would be a further E1 concern, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given.

criteria.stage_note: classroom action research with three cycles, single group

quote: The research study employs a classroom action research methodology with three action cycles.
rationale: The abstract describes a classroom action research design with 34 diploma students across three action cycles, with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. This is a single-group design, so it fails the comparison criterion (E3). The abstract gives positive evidence of no control group, so exclusion at abstract stage is warranted. Microsoft Copilot is a generative AI tool and the domain (heat transfer, STEAM) and population are acceptable, but the comparison requirement is clearly not met.

quote: we have developed the VRGEPHTNLP by integrating hand-tracking technology, the GPT3.5 large language model (GPT3.5 LLM), and Azure technology.
rationale: The abstract describes a VR gearbox platform that integrates GPT-3.5 LLM for personalized responses to student inquiries, so the generative AI intervention appears learner-facing. Engineering content is STEM. However, the abstract does not describe a control group, study design, sample population, or a quantitative learning outcome (it emphasizes realism, immersion, and advantages over other labs). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review.

The abstract describes a survey-based (paper questionnaire) study using PLS-SEM and fsQCA on perceptions and intended utilization of GenAI for career information seeking. It is a correlational/survey design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcome is information-seeking behavior and perceptions. Per the protocol, survey designs are not eligible, and this is not an experimental study. Coded E6 (not an empirical study is the closest code, but the study is empirical). Note: the protocol's most accurate code for a survey/correlational design lacking a comparison group is E3 or E5; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome, so exclusion is clear. Using E5 as the first applicable code by order of evaluation would be more precise because no quantitative learning outcome is measured.

quote: The randomized controlled study with N = 2 1 4 students compared supplementary learning material in the form of traditional textbook material with explanations previously generated by an AI custom chatbot.
rationale: Abstract indicates a randomized controlled study of sixth-grade students comparing AI custom chatbot-generated explanations against textbook material, in mathematics/physics (proportional relationships). Learning performance outcomes are reported as having an "indefinite" impact, so a quantitative learning outcome is likely present but the abstract does not give statistics. Intervention is ambiguous: the chatbot generated the materials, and it is unclear whether learners interacted with the chatbot directly rather than only reading AI-generated material. Publication date (2025) and journal article type appear to meet criteria. Advance to full text to check intervention and effect-size data.

quote: The questionnaire survey identified students' experience of using digital tools, their assessment of these tools' role in developing communicative competence, their educational needs, and the conditions required for the effective use of digital technologies.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of 100 students on their experiences and perceptions of digital tools (including generative AI). It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports perceptions and self-assessed usefulness. Under the protocol, survey designs are excluded and perception-only outcomes do not qualify. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group), but the more fundamental failure is that this is a survey, not an empirical experiment with a learning outcome, so E6 is assigned as the non-empirical/survey-design failure. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design. Domain is also questionable (philology/translation is non-STEM), which would be E2 under the order listed; because E2 precedes E6 in the code sequence, the strictly correct code is E2.

quote: This paper describes the development of an AI policy following identified misuse and demonstrated knowledge gaps from student orientation essays.
rationale: The paper describes development of an institutional AI policy by a task force. It is a policy/program description, not an empirical comparative study. It has no control group, no learning outcome measured, and no experimental or quasi-experimental design. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Health professions (DPT) education also falls outside the STEM domain, but E6 is the first applicable code in the required order and captures the core problem.
rationale_note: Domain also not STEM (physical therapy); exclusion code E6 applied as the first failing code in the protocol order.

quote: The article examines the conceptualization of the subject area "artificial intelligence" using large language models and ontological modeling.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/methodological paper in which GPT-4.5 was used by researchers to extract concepts from a book and build a knowledge graph. There is no learner interaction with generative AI, no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study in the protocol's sense, so E6 (not an empirical study) is the best fit. Note that E1 could also apply, since the LLM is used by the researchers rather than learners; E1 would be the first applicable code in order, so consider E1 as the stricter code at fulltext. At abstract stage, the exclusion is supported because the design lacks any comparison group and any learner outcome.

quote: These documents contain teaching materials for a four week AI literacy certificate program for instructors.
rationale: The record is a set of teaching materials (syllabus, worksheets, slides) for a certificate program, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no outcome data, and its population is instructors rather than students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type (Cornerstone repository item) is also not a journal article, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the protocol's sequence, so E6 is reported.

quote: Program Pengabdian Kepada Masyarakat dengan judul "Penggunaan ChatGPT & Duo Lingo Untuk Menciptakan Pengalaman Belajar Keislaman Yang Menarik Bagi Anak-Anak Panti Asuhan"
rationale: Community service program (PKM) at an orphanage on Islamic learning and language practice using ChatGPT and Duolingo. Content is Islamic studies and language learning, not STEM (E2). The abstract also describes no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well; E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Venue is a community service journal article with no experimental design.

quote: Peserta pelatihan adalah guru SMPN 9 Payakumbuh yang berjumlah 31 orang.
rationale: This is a community service training report (PKM) for in-service teachers at one school, delivering ChatGPT-based training. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the evaluation only describes participant enthusiasm and completed products. Participants are in-service teachers, which the population criterion excludes. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits; E4 (population) would also apply. Decision is clear from the abstract.

quote: students who received feedback from ChatGPT encountered a more significant decrease (median = -12) compared to those who received feedback from humans (median = -5)
rationale:
Abstract describes ChatGPT feedback to students in an Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience class (STEM-adjacent, higher education), with a human-feedback comparison group, which suggests a control condition without generative AI. Mixed-methods experiment with performance scores is suggested, but the abstract does not clearly state the design is randomized or quasi-experimental, nor whether the human-feedback arm counts as a non-generative-AI comparison or whether SMD statistics are available. Neuroscience as STEM domain is also a judgment call. No positive evidence of an exclusion criterion, so advance to full text.</rationale>

quote: This study assessed the interaction between obstetrics residents and ChatGPT during clinically oriented summative evaluations
rationale: The abstract describes a semi-qualitative observational study of 14 obstetrics residents interacting with ChatGPT, with no separate control group lacking generative AI. Response accuracy is compared to a standardized ChatGPT answer, not to a non-AI comparison group. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Domain is also doubtful (obstetrics is a health profession, which the protocol excludes), but E3 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's sequence and the abstract supports it.

quote: This project examined 3 models: ATI Engage Fundamentals Claire AI ... Elsevier Sherpath Fundamentals AI ... and ChatGPT—to evaluate their usefulness for teaching drug dosage calculations to fundamental nursing students.
rationale: Abstract is about drug dosage calculation instruction for nursing students. Dosage calculation is a mathematical skill, but the protocol's domain is science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, or data science, and health professions education is explicitly excluded. Nursing dosage calculation sits within health professions education, so the domain criterion is not met. The abstract also compares three AI tools without a clear non-AI control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome, which would be further grounds for exclusion. Excluding on E2 as the first applicable code in the order given.

quote: Undergraduates are taught and empowered to use Generative AI tools to uncover their strengths and craft impactful job search materials such as resumes, cover letters, and LinkedIn summaries
rationale: The assignment uses generative AI for career/job-search materials, which is not STEM content (E2). The abstract also gives no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on the first applicable code, E2, in protocol order.

Abstract stage, but the record gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design: it "proposes and implements" a teaching framework and says "By outlining practical workflows, this research offers a scalable and adaptable model." There is no comparison group, no control condition, and no reported learning outcome measure. Read as a framework/position paper with illustrative teaching cases, it is not an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the abstract stage rule normally requires positive evidence; the evidence here is that the abstract describes a framework with "teaching practice cases" and no comparison or outcome data, which supports E6, though a full-text check could still be warranted if the researcher disagrees.

quote: I argue that the appeal of using objective AI-based solutions like LLMs to overcome complex socio-structural injustices in pain management reflects a techno-solutionism
rationale: This is a commentary/opinion piece (the author argues a position and comments on Young et al.'s study), not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learner-facing intervention, and no STEM learning outcome; it is about pain management in clinical decision-making. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are not applicable to this non-empirical piece.

quote: This research used a quantitative approach with a correlational method.
rationale: The study is correlational (survey questionnaire, Pearson correlation) with no control group that lacks generative AI, so E3 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced. Domain is also unclear (Community Education, not obviously STEM), and the outcome is self-reported creativity via Likert questionnaire rather than a quantitative learning measure, but the comparison/design failure is the primary positive evidence. Abstract gives positive evidence of a correlational design with no control group, so exclusion is warranted.
rationale_full: Correlational survey design; no comparison group.

quote: The activities consisted of needs identification, conceptual instruction, demonstration, hands-on practice, mentoring, product presentation, and evaluation.
rationale: Population is in-service elementary school teachers (training program), which the protocol excludes; students' outcomes were not measured. The study is a single-group pretest-posttest of teachers with no control group (E3 also applies), and the outcome is teacher competence, not student learning. Population exclusion is the first applicable code in the stated order from E1 onward for this record, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone. Abstract shows positive evidence of non-eligible population.

quote: Participants were divided into an experimental group that utilized ChatGPT during learning activities and a control group that received conventional lecturer-led instruction.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use by students (generative AI, learner-facing), statistics content, higher education students, and an experimental vs conventional-instruction control group, so no criterion clearly fails. However, the method is described as qualitative with a quasi-experimental design, and data are analysed descriptively via themes; it is unclear whether a quantitative learning outcome with extractable means/SDs exists (quizzes are mentioned but not reported quantitatively). Design eligibility and outcome/data sufficiency need checking at full text. Per the abstract-stage rule, not excluded.

The study is a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group, and the content is EFL speaking (language learning, not STEM). Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported by the abstract (non-STEM content). Comparison and design also appear not met (E3 would apply too), but the protocol says to report the first code in order, and E2 is listed before E3 in the protocol's sequence only if content is checked first; the content is clearly non-STEM, so E2 is reported. Note: under the strict code order E1 is not triggered since the intervention is a generative chatbot.

quote: We then compare the performance of four dense LLMs and a sparse Mixture of Experts (Mixtral) model to automate coding.
rationale: The LLMs are used by researchers to automate coding of student written responses, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No learner interaction with generative AI and no control group comparison is described. Not an experimental design with a control group; outcome is model coding accuracy rather than a student learning outcome. First applicable code is E1.

quote: Employing a quantitative cross-sectional survey, data from 721 Indonesian undergraduates were collected using a 25-item Likert-scale questionnaire
rationale: Abstract reports a cross-sectional survey of perceptions (ethical awareness, regulatory demands) with no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Excluded at E5 as the outcome is perception-based; the intervention and design also fail, and E1/E3/E6 could arguably apply, but E5 is the first clear failure in the stated order is debatable. Domain is also unclear (Language Education is non-STEM). Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is warranted.
rationale_note: Order check: E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) is the first code in protocol order that applies, since no learner interacts with a GenAI tool. Correcting the code to E1.

quote: This article examines the complex interaction between AI and student decision-making, shedding light on the cognitive and emotional factors that must be considered when using AI to solve physical tasks.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical article ("examines the complex interaction", "pedagogical implications are explored") with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative outcome reported. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Physics content is STEM and ChatGPT is a generative tool, but the design fails the requirement for a comparison group and empirical data.
decision_note: Exclusion based on positive evidence of a non-empirical (discussion/theoretical) article.

quote: This study investigated whether UK higher education academics had adjusted their assessment strategies in response to the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI)
rationale: The study surveys and interviews academics about assessment design; there is no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is supported by the abstract describing only questionnaires, descriptive statistics, chi-square tests on perceptions, and thematic analysis. Note that E1 (not learner-facing) could also apply, and would take precedence under the ordering rule only if the code order is applied strictly; under the protocol's order E1 comes first, so E1 is the strictly correct first-applicable code since AI is used by academics, not learners.

quote: HKT-SmartAudit, a framework for developing lightweight models optimized for smart contract auditing.

The abstract gives no learner population, so it does not describe a learning activity in STEM education. Excluded at the first applicable code: E2 is the best fit because the content is smart contract auditing, a technical task rather than a learning domain, and no learners are involved. Note that E1 could also apply since no learner interacts with the tool; per the code order, E1 is checked first and would take precedence if it clearly applies. Judged on abstract evidence alone.

quote: Generative AI and large language models may be able to predict molecules capable of inhibiting methanogenesis within the ruminant digestive system.
rationale: This is a review/perspective on computational approaches for enteric methane mitigation. Generative AI is used for molecular design and drug discovery, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No learners, no control group, no learning outcome, and not an empirical learning study. E1 applies as the first failing code in order.

quote: The study collected quantitative data using a classroom observation tool.
rationale: Study is a classroom observation of teachers' use of modernized and innovative teaching tools after professional development. It involves teachers, not learners interacting with a generative AI tool, and there is no control group or learning outcome. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI); no generative AI is mentioned in the abstract.

quote: Students completed 4 virtual patient encounters related to renal pathology. Of 39 students, 19 completed surveys
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group workshop with no control group that does not use generative AI. Outcomes are survey perceptions and diagnostic accuracy in interactions, not a controlled learning comparison. Positive evidence of no comparison group supports E3. Domain is renal pathology in pharmacy education, which is arguably health professions education (excluded by protocol), but the code applied is E3 as the first failing criterion in the ordering used here.

quote: The study emerges from a practical challenge encountered in a first-year academic literacy module for Information Technology students at a South African university.
rationale: The abstract describes rubric design and a descriptive text analysis of 30 essays classified as 0% or 100% AI-generated. There is no learner-facing intervention, no control group with a learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome (text features are not learning measures). The design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison of learners, so the study is not an eligible empirical design. Excluded at E6 as a non-experimental, rubric-development/text-analysis study. Note: the protocol's E6 covers not-empirical studies; this is a closer fit to a non-eligible design than a clean E6, so the reviewer may wish to confirm the code at full text.

quote: Analyses confirmed the robustness of the framework, with Functional Interaction valued highest and Social Mediation lowest.
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods study of undergraduate perceptions of generative AI in PBL, measured through a questionnaire and observation cards. The outcomes are perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure, and there is no indication of a control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of failure exists for the outcome criterion (E5), so the record is excluded at the abstract stage. Domain is ambiguous (biological sciences for non-STEM majors), but the outcome failure is sufficient.

quote: Designed to simulate realistic patient interactions, the program aims to improve communication, history taking, and clinical decision-making skills
rationale: The study targets nurse practitioner clinical education (patient communication, history taking, clinical decision-making), which falls under health professions education and is not STEM content per the protocol's domain exclusion. This is a clear positive failure of the domain criterion, so exclude with E2. The abstract also gives no indication of a control group or quantitative outcome, but those are not needed for the exclusion.

quote: Because no pretest-posttest comparison, control group, or independent benchmark of AI diagnostic accuracy was used, the findings establish product feasibility rather than learning effectiveness.
rationale: The abstract states explicitly that there was no control group and no pretest-posttest comparison; the study reports only feasibility and acceptance (expert scores and student response questionnaire), not a learning outcome. Positive evidence that the comparison (E3) criterion fails, so excluded at abstract stage. Under the first-applicable-code order, E1 does not apply (generative AI is learner-facing via the web interface), so E3 is the first failing code.

quote: 2025年，开来科技（深圳）有限公司拟支持生成式人工智能（AIGC）教学科研培训项目50项。

quote: The community service program entitled "Socialization of Digital-Based History Learning and ChatGPT for Students of SMA Negeri 3 Ternate" aims to provide solutions to challenges in history learning in digital era.

History is also not a STEM domain. Excluded on E6 as the first applicable code in the protocol order for a non-empirical record; the domain failure (E2) would also apply, but E6 is the most salient reason for exclusion at abstract stage.

quote: aimed to improve teachers’ knowledge and skills through training and mentoring that emphasized the integrated use of ChatGPT, Gamma AI, and Presentations.AI

Domain is not STEM content for learners (teacher AI-use training), though this is not the primary code applied.

quote: Survey responses from 211 students were analysed using Rasch measurement to evaluate item reliability, construct separation, differential item functioning (DIF)
rationale: The study is a survey-based Rasch measurement analysis of students' perceptions of parroting. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is justified by positive evidence of failure. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) in strict sequence, but the abstract does not describe learners using a generative tool in an activity; the clearest positive evidence is that the design is a survey, which is an empirical non-experimental study rather than an intervention study. Coded E6 as not an empirical experimental study; the decision is not strongly tied to a single code and a reviewer may prefer E1 or E3.

quote: A descriptive study, an experience report on activities carried out from August 2024 to December 2025 by a professor from the Nursing program

Health (nursing) context is also not STEM, but the first applicable code in order is E1, and the intervention is not generative AI, so the strictly first-applicable code could be argued as E1; the descriptive experience-report design is the clearest positive evidence of failure. Note that E1 would precede E6 in order; the intervention is a non-generative tool used by a professor and students, so E1 applies first.

No positive evidence of exclusion, so advance to full text.

Note the publication type is a journal in the record and was not treated as a failure.
