quote: Using a narrative inquiry design, this study involved eight EFL pre-service teachers from a private university in Indonesia. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed thematically.
rationale: The study is a qualitative narrative inquiry using semi-structured interviews with eight pre-service teachers. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, and the content is EFL writing, not STEM. Exclusion uses E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design); E6 is the first code that clearly applies after the intervention-first ordering of E1 is considered unclear. Note that E6 is arguably a stretch for a qualitative empirical study; E3 (no control group) or E2 (non-STEM) would also fail it. The E2 code (content is not STEM) is the clearest failure, since EFL academic writing is language learning, and the protocol's ordering places E2 before E3, E5, E6. Under the strict ordering, E2 should have been reported.

quote: The study employed a descriptive survey method, data were gathered from 104 PSTs across five institutions
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey of pre-service teachers' knowledge, use, and views of generative AI in research. It has no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and usage. Survey designs are non-empirical-experimental and fail the design and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention were not learner-facing, but the main failing criterion is the design/outcome; using E6 (not an empirical study per the protocol's design exclusion of survey designs). Note: strictly, this is an empirical survey, so E6 is the closest code for a survey design that is not an eligible design. Excluded with confidence despite abstract-stage leniency because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design.

quote: When ophthalmology goes viral: AI-generated content and the viral spread of medical knowledge on social media
rationale: The title indicates the topic is medical knowledge spread on social media (ophthalmology), which is health/medical content rather than STEM education. No abstract is available. The record points to a social media dissemination study about AI-generated medical content, not a learner-facing generative AI learning intervention with a STEM learning outcome. Excluded on E2 (content not STEM); the record also suggests no learner-facing intervention or learning outcome. Note that the protocol's E1 check would also be plausible, but E2 is the first applicable code based on the title alone, given the domain is health/medical rather than STEM education.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage rule would normally favor 'unsure' for missing information; however, the title gives positive evidence the content is ophthalmology/medical (health professions), which the protocol excludes from the domain criterion.

quote: Participants completed survey items from Ramalingam and Wiedenbeck's Computer Programming Self-Efficacy Scale (CPSES) prior to and after the intervention.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design with no control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears not met (E3 would apply). However, the outcome is self-efficacy, an affective/perception measure, and the protocol excludes studies reporting only perceptions; this is the first code that applies in order of codes? Checking order: E1 intervention is GenAI (met), E2 STEM met, E3 no control group evident from abstract (positive evidence of single-group pre-post design), so E3 is the first applicable code and is reported here. Note the self-efficacy outcome would also raise E5 concerns.

quote: A study of facilitating primary and middle (grade 4, 5, 6 and 7) science teachers' professional development and reflective practice
rationale: Participants are in-service primary and middle school science teachers, not K-12 students, so E4 applies. The study is also a collaborative action research design with qualitative data (interviews, observations, document review) and no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. E4 is the first applicable code in protocol order. The AI tool (Khanmigo) is mentioned only as a teacher-facing formative assessment tool, which bears on E1 but is not needed for the decision.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: "an exploratory and descriptive study was conducted with 132 first-year engineering students"
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory, descriptive study with a single sample surveyed once. It reports no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion is not met. The outcomes are survey-based perceptions (cognitive dependence, illusion of understanding, self-reported memory and effort), not a quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code; E5 would also apply. Design is not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a comparison group.

quote: First, if you have not already developed internal guidelines for AI use for your institution or program, that will be critical to ensure appropriate and consistent approaches by faculty.
rationale: The record is a non-empirical practice/commentary piece on using AI for accreditation work by faculty. It presents recommended best practices, not a study. It has no learner-facing AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no quantitative data. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 could also arguably apply because AI is used by faculty for administrative tasks, but E6 is the primary defining failure.

quote: Let’s Face It: Chatbots Are Here to Stay
rationale: This is an editorial/opinion piece in a clinical laboratory journal. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome, and it concerns patient use of chatbots rather than learners in STEM education. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).
rationale_note: Editorial; no design, no control group, no learner population.

quote: This paper explores the impact of AI-assisted writing tools on critical thinking and academic writing skills among university students through a comprehensive review of recent scholarly literature.
rationale: The abstract describes a comprehensive literature review, not an empirical study with a control group. It is not an empirical study (E6). Writing-focused content is also not clearly STEM. No positive evidence of a comparison group or quantitative outcome is reported.

quote: This study aims to examine the effect of using ChatGPT in the Think Pair Share (TPS) model on students' understanding in Islamic Religious Education learning.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT with a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design and a posttest outcome, but the content is Islamic Religious Education (salat jamak and qashar), which is not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science. Excluded under E2 (content not STEM), the first applicable code in order.
decision_note: Dates and publication type not assessed from abstract.

quote: Students generally found the chatbot useful and perceived competence was improved following chatbot use (Figure 3).
rationale: Abstract stage. Learners interact with a GPT-based history-taking chatbot, which meets the intervention criterion. However, the only reported outcomes are perceptions (usefulness, perceived competence) and participation observations, with no quantitative learning measure. No control group is described, and the domain (dental history taking) is health professions education, which is excluded by the protocol. Exclusion is based on E5 as the first clear failing criterion. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of perception-only outcomes, this is excluded rather than held as unsure. Note the domain also appears to fail (health professions education), which a fulltext reviewer should consider. Protocol order places E2 before E5 in the code list, so a reviewer may prefer E2 instead; I have applied E5 as the first criterion positively evidenced here.

Abstract is missing from the index; the title suggests a validation study of the Automated Model of Comprehension (a text-comprehension model) with ChatGPT integration. Nothing in the record shows whether learners interact with generative AI, whether there is a control group, whether the domain is STEM, or whether there is a learning outcome, and the record gives no positive evidence of failure. Per the abstract-stage rule, it is kept as unsure for full-text review, where the design and domain can be checked.

quote: The ChatGPT-based debate learning program was conducted over five weeks with 18 university students enrolled in a course on teaching methods and educational technology.
rationale: Abstract stage. Content is debate learning in a teaching methods / educational technology course for preservice teachers, which is not a STEM domain under the protocol. Excluded under E2 (first applicable code in order: E1 does not apply since ChatGPT is learner-facing; E2 applies). Note the abstract also gives no evidence of a control group (single-group implementation with outcomes reported as effects), which would be E3 if reached, but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: The participants were distributed into an experimental group that received AI technology-based instruction using ChatGPT activities and a control group that received traditional instruction.
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: ChatGPT activities for undergraduate OS course students (computing, STEM), experimental vs traditional-instruction control group, quasi-experimental/randomized assignment, HOT test as a quantitative learning outcome, published 2025. Data sufficiency for SMD and the journal-article status cannot be fully confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure is present, so advance to full text.

quote: The chatbot was tested on 1300 BCSC Self-Assessment Program questions, including text and image-based questions.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT-4 answering exam questions directly, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. The population is an AI model being tested against ophthalmology test-taker scores, not K-12 or higher education students. Domain is medical (ophthalmology), which falls under health professions education and is excluded. No control group of learners without generative AI is evident. Excluded at abstract stage on population (E4) as the clearest positive failure; the domain (health professions) and the absence of learner-facing use would also fail.

criteria.design_note: practice/case report of LLM summarisation of peer feedback; no comparison group

quote: A 'Lightning AI' solution was explored, where large language model Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) were used to summarize the comments, and custom reports for each poster were generated.
rationale: The record is a practice-oriented teaching article describing use of LLM APIs to summarize peer feedback comments for markers. It reports no controlled comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an empirical study of learners interacting with generative AI. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E6 is the first applicable code in the order that fits best, though E3 and E5 would also fail on the abstract.

quote: We describe the model’s design rationale and weekly structure, and reflect on our experience from two course iterations.
rationale: Describes a course assignment model and reflects on two course iterations; it is a descriptive/reflective teaching report with no controlled comparison, no generative AI intervention evident in the abstract (AI is mentioned only as a context pressure), and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study. Excluded at abstract stage on E6 because the abstract gives positive evidence it is a practice/reflection paper rather than an empirical comparison.

quote: This community service activity aims to broaden students' knowledge of the use of Artificial Intelligence or AI-based applications
rationale: Community service program (pengabdian masyarakat) providing basic AI prompt training to high school students. The abstract describes no comparison group, no controlled design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical study evaluating learning. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note: the criteria object above has a duplicated key; the intended values are comparison not_met, design not_met, outcome not_met, population met, domain unclear (not explicitly STEM), intervention unclear.

quote: Fourteen questions corresponding to the two categories of 'Accessibility of AI' and 'Similarity between AI and Human' were administered in pre- and post-surveys.
rationale: The study measures pre-service teachers' perceptions of AI via pre/post surveys, which are affective/perception outcomes, not quantitative learning outcomes. It also appears to be a single-group pre-post design with no control group, and the content is not clearly STEM. Excluded at E5 as the first applicable code on the outcome; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply), but the protocol asks for the first code in order, and the outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: Using a hermeneutic phenomenological approach based on van Manen's framework, data were gathered from structured, open-ended written reflections by all four students in the specialized track.
rationale: The study is a qualitative hermeneutic phenomenology based on four students' written reflections. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design. It is not an empirical study in the sense the protocol requires for a quantitative synthesis, so E6 applies. Domain is EFL (English language teaching), which is also non-STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given only if earlier codes (E1 to E5) are not clearly failed; the abstract's positive evidence of qualitative design and absence of a comparison group is the clearest failure. Note that E2 (non-STEM) would also apply; the code order places E2 before E6, so strictly the first applicable code is E2. Decision uses the first applicable code in order: E2.

quote: The study followed a quasi-experimental design with one group (pre-post) test.
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a one-group pre-post design with no control group that does not use generative AI, which is a positive indication of E3 (single-group pre-post designs are excluded). The study concerns searchability in scientific research, which is not clearly STEM content, but the comparison failure alone is sufficient for exclusion under the first-applicable code order at this stage.

quote: Post-workshop evaluation revealed a 75% improvement in participants' ability to use AI for academic writing, research, and time management.
rationale: Community service program report with a single group and post-workshop evaluation only; no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome with effect-size data. Not an empirical comparative study; also the content (academic productivity/AI literacy) is not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of design failure supports exclusion at abstract stage. Primary code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable; the single-group design would also fail E3.

quote: This research aims to identify and analyze observable characteristics in the problem-solving process involving linear, surface, and volumetric scales using the Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study (triangulation of videos, observations, interviews) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The design and comparison fail on positive evidence, so it is excluded. Per the code order, E1 and E2 do not apply: ChatGPT is learner-facing, the content is mathematics (scales). The no-control-group design is the first failing criterion that maps to E3, and the qualitative approach would also fall under E5/E6, but E3 is the first applicable code in order for a no-comparison design. Population (high school students) and date (2024) are met.

criteria.criteria_note: Study is a letter to the editor evaluating Claude simplifying pathology reports for patients; no learners, no control group, no learning outcome.

quote: We used Claude 3 Opus (Anthropic, released February 2024) with default system settings
rationale: Record is a letter to the editor evaluating Claude's readability simplification of pathology reports for patients. Pathology reports are not STEM learning content and there are no learners, no control group, and no learning outcome. Per the rule that E-codes report the first applicable code in order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) is arguably first, but the abstract does not show a learner interacting with the tool; the most direct failing criterion is domain/population. Excluding on E2 as the first clearly failing content criterion. Note that E6 (not an empirical study, letter) could also apply; the protocol order places E2 before E6 in the list, so E2 is reported.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: The study's participants were 37 students in the 5th grade of a secondary school in Türkiye.
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: ChatGPT is used by students during a science lesson (experimental group) versus a 5E control group without generative AI; a semi-experimental design with pre/post tests and academic achievement outcome; 5th grade students; electrical circuits is science content (STEM). Publication in 2025 and journal venue (IJEMST) fit. Data sufficiency for SMD and journal-article status to be confirmed at full text.

quote: we compare results from measures obtained via ordinary Likert-type items (scale measures), and measures obtained from automatically encoding open-ended questions (LLM measures)
rationale: The LLM is used by researchers to encode open-ended survey responses, not as a learner-facing learning intervention. There is no learning intervention or control group without generative AI, and the design is a survey-based measurement comparison. The abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention criterion fails, so exclude under E1 (first applicable code). Domain (teacher education demands-resources, not STEM content) and outcome (engagement, a non-learning measure) also appear unmet.

quote: The intervention was tested in a class using a pretest–posttest design along with a student perception survey.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-class pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (single-group pre-post is E3). Domain is architecture/engineering/construction healthy buildings, which is borderline for STEM but not the deciding factor. Exclusion under E3 as the first applicable code in the order given that the abstract shows no control group.

The study is a cross-sectional survey of 93 students analysed with multiple linear regression. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI. Learning effectiveness is a self-reported Likert measure, not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement. The abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail, so it is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in order. Survey designs would also fall under E6, but E3 is reported as the first failing criterion in order.

quote: The methodology was based on a theoretical–propositional approach grounded in a documentary review, structured into three phases
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical-propositional conceptual model built from documentary review, with no empirical data, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. E6 is ranked before E3 and E5 in the protocol order, so it is the first applicable code, and the other criteria are not assessed further.

quote: Code Pilot is designed as a mobile-first application that assists students and job seekers throughout their coding and career journey.
rationale:
The abstract describes a RAG/LLM mentorship system for coding learners but reports only system design and intent. It gives no comparison group, no empirical design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E5 because no learning measure is reported. This is a positive signal from the abstract that the study is a system description without outcome data, so it is excluded at abstract stage.</rationale>

It involves no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the domain is law, not STEM. It is not an empirical experimental study, so E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 would also apply in a strict sense, but the record is a survey/report of course offerings rather than an intervention study, so E6 best describes it. Decision is clear from the abstract.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 727 participants from Al-Azhar University, Egypt, and the College of Basic Education
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey correlating self-reported generative AI usage with procrastination and ethical decision-making. There is no separate control group and no experimental intervention, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The outcome is procrastination, a behavioural/affective measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of design and comparison failure justifies exclusion; the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) only if usage is not an intervention, but the clearest failure is the absence of a control group, so E3 is reported.

quote: This study investigates patterns of AI use among translation students, including frequency of use, preferred AI tools, learning purposes, year-level differences, and the influence of AI on translation-learning practices.
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods descriptive survey study of usage patterns among 93 students, with descriptive statistics, correlation, and thematic analysis. There is no control group without generative AI and no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported; only usage and perceptions. Under E3 (no control group) this fails the comparison and design criteria. Translation is a language domain, not STEM, which is a further concern, but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails; the intervention (student use of ChatGPT) is learner-facing, so E3 is the first code that clearly applies. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for absence of a control group, so exclusion is warranted.
exclusion_code_note: Also note: translation is language learning, likely E2 (non-STEM), and no quantitative learning outcome (E5); exclusion under E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: The research method used was qualitative descriptive analysis, collecting data through students' answers to given problems.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive analysis of student answers, with no separate control group comparison or quantitative effect statistics. The design criterion (randomized or quasi-experiment with comparison group) is not met on positive evidence, and the comparison criterion also fails. Exclusion code is E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first failing criterion in code order; the design failure is also evident. Domain (SPLTV, compound interest) is STEM, population is vocational high school, published 2025.

quote: Twelve master-level pre-service teachers participated in a mixed-method study that combined self-report surveys, group-based instructional design artefacts, and AI-driven prompt analysis
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of twelve pre-service teachers in an exploratory mixed-method study with self-report surveys and design artefacts. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are self-reported confidence. This fails the comparison requirement, so E3 applies. Exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract, not missing information.

quote: Evaluation with real users will inform future iterations and potential expansion to additional language pairs or subject domains.
rationale: The abstract describes a mobile app development project with an AI chatbot and states that evaluation with real users is future work. It gives no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a missing outcome exists, so the record is excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The domain is mathematics-related language support, and the population is bilingual students, which are not the failing criteria.

quote: The research method used is a descriptive qualitative approach.
rationale: English language learning is non-STEM content (E2), so it fails the domain criterion first. The study is also a descriptive qualitative design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. Per the exclusion-code order, E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: This paper aims to study both strengths and weaknesses of using ChatGPT in English language teaching and learning
rationale: The study concerns English language teaching and learning, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies first. The design is a questionnaire and interview mixed-methods study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would also fail E3, E5 and E6 on the abstract, but E2 is the first applicable code in the specified order.
rationale_note: Design is survey/interview based; no comparison group evident.

quote: Using a quasi-experimental method with a one-group pretest-posttest design, the activity involved 50 eleventh-grade students
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that does not use generative AI, which is a positive E3 failure (single-group pre-post designs are excluded by the comparison and design rows). The content is general AI literacy (ChatGPT, Gemini, Canva AI) rather than clearly STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in order. No injection was present in the record.

quote: Employing a mixed-method approach, the research combines quantitative and qualitative data
rationale: The study targets English language proficiency (language learning), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies as the first failing criterion in protocol order that is positively evidenced. The abstract also describes only pre- and post-intervention assessments with no mention of a control group, which points to a single-group design (E3 would also be plausible), but the non-STEM domain is the clearest positive failure. Generative tools (ChatGPT) are involved, so intervention is met.

quote: Expert evaluations showed that Node-Sampling enhances the quality of question stems significantly compared to a fixed baseline.
rationale: The study evaluates an LLM-based multi-agent system that generates MCQs for medical educators/platform development, with outcomes being expert ratings of question quality rather than a learner-level quantitative learning outcome. No learner interacts with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity per the abstract, and there is no evident learner-level control group. Medical education content is also outside the protocol's STEM domain. Positive evidence of failure on the outcome criterion (expert ratings of MCQ quality, not learning) supports E5. Given rule 2 (abstract stage), exclusion is supported because the abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is not a learner learning measure. Note: E1 (learner-facing) could arguably apply first per code order; the intervention appears to be an artifact-generation pipeline not used by learners, which would make E1 the first applicable code. The E1 code should be considered; I am recording E5 under the abstract-stage evidence, but a researcher should verify.

quote: Musician, folklorist, farmer, and arts administrator, Claude D. Stephenson died on August 29, 2023, at his home in the South Valley region of Albuquerque, New Mexico.
rationale: This record is an obituary/memorial piece about a folklorist, not an empirical study. It describes no generative AI intervention, no comparison group, no STEM content, and no learner outcomes. Under the codes, E1 (intervention) would be the first code in order, but the record is clearly not an empirical study at all, so E6 is the substantive reason. Note that E1 is checked first in the protocol order; the decisive failure is non-empirical nature, and no AI intervention is present either.

quote: A qualitative educational action research approach was adopted, based on the analysis of academic assignments, similarity reports, and Artificial Intelligence-assisted writing detection using Turnitin, together with classroom observations and reflective discussions.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative educational action research design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; findings are descriptive. Positive evidence of failing comparison (no control), design (qualitative), and outcome (no quantitative measure) is present. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order after intervention (generative AI use by students is present, so E1 does not apply); E3 is used for missing control group. Domain is also unclear (engineering and business master's students, writing focus), not relied upon.

quote: The study encompassed 473 pre-service teachers from three distinct higher education institutions, with specialties in science, computer science, and mathematics
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI-supported instructional design training with pre-service teachers in higher education, and STEM specialties (science, computer science, mathematics). Comparison group is not mentioned; the abstract says assessments were 'before and after this program', which may indicate a single-group pre-post design (E3), but the 'experimental group' wording suggests a possible control group. Outcome is a higher-order thinking survey, which is plausibly a quantitative measure, but the abstract does not clearly state a control condition or effect statistics. Design and comparison cannot be determined at abstract stage, so unsure; resolve at full text.

quote: The present article focuses on the design of various technology-assisted teaching activities as part of a practical English for Specific Academic Purposes (ESAP) course
rationale: Abstract describes a conceptual/design article on ESAP (English for academic purposes) teaching activities with no comparison group, no empirical design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is English language learning, not STEM, though it targets Biology students. Per the abstract, it is a non-empirical discussion paper, so E6 is the first applicable code in order. Note E2 (non-STEM content) could also apply; E6 is reported because the study is clearly not empirical, and the protocol requires the first applicable code in order (E1 unclear from abstract, so skipped). Decision is exclude.

quote: Our findings indicate that future education can no longer focus solely on traditional translation and interpreting careers.
rationale: The record is an institutional presentation describing curriculum redesign and stakeholder discussions at a translation and interpreting institute. It reports no controlled comparison, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study that meets the design requirements. Domain (translation/interpreting, not clearly STEM) and population are also not supported. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study; the record is a presentation rather than a research article.

quote: Using a scoping meta-synthesis of policy texts (n = 50) and public indicators for 40 ODL providers, we propose and apply the AI-aware Assessment Policy Index (AAPI)
rationale: The record is a policy-text scoping meta-synthesis and institutional index, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome data (the correlation is between policy scores and detector flag rates/proctoring). Per the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would be the first applicable code, but the dominant failure is that it is not an empirical learner study; I report E6 as the primary reason since the study design is a policy analysis rather than an empirical intervention study. The abstract gives clear positive evidence of failure on several criteria, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

quote: The article is devoted to the development of tools and methods for training future teacher-facilitators to apply ChatGPT and Copilot technologies in solving pedagogical problems.
rationale: Abstract describes training preservice teachers to use ChatGPT and Copilot for school mathematics problems (domain and population plausibly met; generative AI intervention met). However, the abstract does not describe a control group, a comparison design, or any quantitative learning outcome, so these cannot be confirmed. Per abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so return unsure for full-text review.

quote: This study investigates the integration of ChatGPT into reading classes for EFL students, focusing on the challenges faced by teachers and the impact on student engagement.
rationale: The study concerns EFL reading (English language learning), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. Although ChatGPT is a generative AI tool used by students, the domain criterion fails on positive evidence. Comparison and design are not described in the abstract, but the STEM exclusion alone is sufficient.

quote: Employing a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design, we surveyed 239 English majors, modelled relationships using PLS-SEM, and conducted four in-depth interviews.
rationale: Content is English academic writing, a language-learning/non-STEM domain, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study is also a survey/PLS-SEM correlational design with perception outcomes only (no quantitative learning measure or control group), which would fail other criteria, but E2 is the first applicable code. Exclusion is based on positive abstract evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: Ninety-five preservice teachers in an educational research methods course participated in a 10-week study using two intact classes (experimental n = 52; comparison n = 43).
rationale: Abstract stage. Generative AI tool use by learners (QUEST + AI, coached generative AI use) with a comparison group doing conventional homework; quasi-experimental with comparison group; preservice teachers count as higher education; quantitative outcomes (AI literacy measure, rubric-scored research proposal). Domain is unclear: the course is educational research methods, which is not clearly STEM content. No positive evidence of a failed criterion, so not excluded at abstract stage; domain should be checked at full text. Publication type and full text language not visible at this stage.

quote: This systematic review examines research published between 2021 and 2025 on generative AI and chatbot use in secondary education across nine countries
rationale: The record is a systematic review, not an empirical study with a control group. Under the protocol, reviews are not eligible (E6, not an empirical study). It also has no primary experimental design or comparison group. Publication-type exclusion (E10) could also apply, but E6 is the closer fit for a review synthesizing literature. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence that the record is a review.

quote: The black-box testing results demonstrate that all functional components of the system operate successfully. Output consistency testing through repeated upload experiments of the same photo sample 10 times
rationale: The abstract describes a system with black-box functional testing and repeated-upload output consistency testing of one photo sample. No control group without generative AI is described, so the comparison criterion appears not met (E3). The study is also a system-engineering evaluation rather than a comparative learning experiment, and no learning outcome is reported in the abstract. quote: Our method employs curriculum standards and university syllabus information to associate important keywords with text entities defined in Wikipedia articles.

Domain is unclear: the topic is file and folder management, which may be computing/ICT rather than clearly STEM, so it needs checking at full text. Intervention is labelled generative AI-based video tutorials; whether learners interact with the generative tool (versus only watching AI-produced video) is not clear from the abstract. Data sufficiency for SMD (means reported, SDs not shown) is also to be checked at full text. Journal article in 2026 in English-titled record with Indonesian full text; language to be judged at full text.

quote: The research, once again showed that artificial intelligence facilitates teaching biology, increases academic success, has positive contributions to eliminating plant blindness
rationale: Abstract describes an AI mobile app with ChatGPT chatbot (generative, learner-facing) used by prospective science teachers (higher education, STEM/biology). Abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists or the design (single-group vs comparison), so comparison and design cannot be judged. Outcome includes knowledge and academic success, which may be quantitative, but this is unclear. Not enough positive evidence to exclude; advance to full text.

quote: The method used in this study is descriptive qualitative with 73 chemistry/chemistry education students
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative design with no control or comparison group, and it reports perceptions and qualitative observations rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordered codes, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Abstract stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group. The domain (chemistry with matrix math) is arguably STEM, so no E2 is assigned.

quote: It formatively evaluated the validity of this learning method by asking categorized questions of an interactive generative AI.
rationale: The abstract describes a self-directed learning environment with generative AI for AI programming (STEM), but gives no indication of a control group without generative AI. It reads as a formative evaluation of a single learning method, which points to a single-group design lacking a comparison. Positive evidence of no comparison group supports E3. Population, outcome, and publication type are not clearly stated, but the exclusion is based on the missing comparison.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Two original macro-models are proposed: the Intellectual Adaptivity Model (IAM), which ensures AI-driven personalized support and real-time correction of learning trajectories
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and conceptual study: it relies on systematic analysis of scholarly sources, theoretical generalization, and modeling. No experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome is reported, so the record is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the design is non-empirical, not on missing information.

Undergraduate astronomy course (STEM, higher education) with ChatGPT used by students as a learning tool, so the intervention appears met. The abstract does not state whether there is a control group, a comparison design, or a quantitative learning outcome; it describes implementation and "impact on student learning" without detail. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is retained for full-text review of design, comparison, and outcome.

quote: This is a syllabus for a graduate-level or upper undergraduate course in preparing secondary social studies educators as part of a MAT program.
rationale: The record is a course syllabus, not an empirical study. It describes no experimental or comparison design and no learning outcome data. The content is social studies, which is not STEM. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing criterion in protocol order (E1 is unclear from the abstract, but E6 is the decisive failure). The record is not a study at all, so no further criteria need evaluating.

criteria.publication_type_note: essay/position-style paper; no controlled comparison described in abstract

quote: This study contends that homework must transition from a model centered on repetition to one emphasizing logic, feedback, and reflection.
rationale: The abstract reads as a conceptual/position paper on homework in the AI era. It gives no positive evidence of an empirical design with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Its own wording ("This study contends", "Feedback systems such as the one detailed in this study") is argumentative rather than reporting an experiment. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on the abstract's argumentative framing; the full text could still be checked if the researcher wants to confirm.

quote: The descriptive,quantitative, cross-sectional study sampled 396 teachers using a reliable, self-administered questionnaire
rationale: The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey of 396 in-service teachers measuring awareness, use, and barriers of ChatGPT. It has no control group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome; participants are in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Under the ordered codes, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would apply first, but the clearest disqualifier is that this is not an empirical experimental study, so E6 is assigned as a survey design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: The expanded Quebec Birth Cohort on Immunity and Health (CO·MMUNITY) includes 400 611 individuals born in 1970–74 in the province of Quebec, Canada, and followed until 2014
rationale: This is a cohort profile update for an administrative-data birth cohort studying BCG vaccination and disease incidence. It involves no learner-facing generative AI, no STEM content, no learning outcome, and no intervention/control comparison in the protocol sense. It is not an empirical study of the eligible kind. Excluded at abstract stage on the clear positive evidence that it is a cohort profile, which fails the intervention, domain, population, and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), which would apply first; however, the most accurate code given the record type is E6 (not an empirical study of eligible design). Note: under strict code order E1 precedes E6, so the appropriate code under the protocol order is E1.

quote: This action research (AR) study revealed that prompts could constrain the usefulness of AI-generated feedback
rationale: The study concerns second-language (L2) composition writing feedback, which is language learning, not STEM (E2). It is also an action research study with no described control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3/E5 and the design criterion as well. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E2 is reported first because the content is non-STEM and that is positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: Here, scientific journals' crucial role arises toward preserving the integrity of scientific research and studies.
rationale: This is an editorial/perspective piece on scientific publishing ethics, not an empirical study. It describes no intervention, no comparison group, no learners, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Generative AI is mentioned only in passing as a publishing concern, not as a learner-facing intervention, so E1 would also apply in principle, but E6 is the primary and first-applicable reason for this type of record.

quote: Intervention consisted of AI-assisted communicative activities using conversational chatbots and generative AI tools during an eight-week period.
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language (communicative competence in English), which is language learning and not STEM content. This is a clear positive failure of the domain criterion, so it is excluded at abstract stage with E2. Other criteria appear met on the abstract: generative AI chatbots, experimental and control groups, university students, and 2026 publication.

quote: Phase one of the framework processes multi-dimensional vocational preferences and personality metrics
rationale: The abstract describes a career-guidance framework that uses psychological profiling (Big Five, RIASEC surveys) and a Gemini-generated micro-learning roadmap. It reports no controlled comparison, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the outputs are predictions and system architecture. Positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails (no learning measure, system description only) supports exclusion at abstract stage, with E5 as the first applicable code given the design/outcome absence. Note that E5 is applied on the abstract's evident lack of any learning measure; the study may also be an engineering description rather than an empirical study (E6), but the abstract alone does not settle that.

quote: Particular focus is given to an ongoing research project aimed at improving Italian students' mathematical skills through the use of AI tools like ChatGPT
rationale: Abstract describes an ongoing research project using ChatGPT with Italian students in mathematics, which fits intervention, population and domain. However, it does not state whether there is a control group, a quantitative outcome, or a comparison design. It describes an ongoing project and a framing article, so design and outcome data cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is unsure and should be resolved at full text.

The record has only a title, venue, and year (2025). There is no abstract, so nothing in the record gives positive evidence that any criterion fails. The title refers to cognitive diagnostic models and hypothesis testing skills, with no indication of a generative AI intervention, a control group, or a STEM population. Under the abstract-stage rule, this is unsure and should be checked at full text.

The study concerns typography and poster design education, which is a visual design/arts domain, not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, or programming. Under the protocol's domain criterion and exclusion code order, E2 applies first. The abstract compares AI-generated posters with human-designed posters rated by expert student evaluators, and the outcome is expert design ratings rather than a clear learning measure, but the domain failure alone is sufficient for exclusion. Mentions of STEM education in the broader implications do not make the studied content STEM.

quote: This article provides a systematic review of 14 empirical studies incorporating ChatGPT into various educational settings, published in 2022 and before the 10th of April 2023
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, not an empirical primary study. It synthesizes other studies, so it is not eligible under the protocol. Also, its included studies were published in 2022 or earlier, which would fail the 2023 date criterion, but the primary reason for exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study). Under the protocol's rule that an exclusion carries its first applicable code, E6 applies.
rationale_extra: Note: the review is a systematic review, which the publication-type criterion also lists as ineligible (reviews). The code E6 is used since it is the closest match for non-empirical records; E10 would also be defensible for review articles.

quote: A qualitative case study examines one group's prompting journal and final text using two exploratory coding schemes
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study of one group's prompting journal and final text, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Per the protocol, the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain (engineering writing course) is not clearly STEM content, but this is not needed for the code assignment.

quote: Progress was evaluated via Quizizz pre-tests and post-tests, measuring AI literacy concepts and technical prompting formulation.
rationale: The abstract describes a community service program with pre-post testing of a single group of 11th-grade DKV students using Gemini AI. There is no separate control group that does not use generative AI, so E3 applies (single-group pre-post design). Domain (graphic/content creation, prompting literacy) is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion is based on the first clear failure, E3. Quote is from the abstract and supports the single-group pre-post design.

Abstract describes a descriptive mixed-methods survey and interview study of students and teachers using ChatGPT for Social Sciences. There is no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (findings are usage and perceptions). Positive evidence of failing comparison (no control group) and design (descriptive/survey) is present. Coded E3 as first applicable on the protocol order available at this stage; the study also reports only perceptions and usage, so E5 would also apply. Social Sciences is not clearly STEM, which is a further concern. Exclusion is justified on the absence of a comparison group.

quote: This work serves as a case study for integrating AI in a pedagogically sound manner
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of AI-enabled activities in an engineering course, with student feedback as the main evidence. It gives no control group and no comparison condition, and the study self-describes as a case study. The protocol requires a separate control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Engagement and perceptions are reported, not a quantitative learning measure. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the design lacks a comparison group.

quote: Data were collected from 320 university teachers in Pakistan using a structured survey distributed through WhatsApp and email.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional SEM survey of 320 university teachers about their perceptions of ChatGPT. It is not an experiment and has no control group. Student performance is only reported as teacher-perceived constructs, not a measured learning outcome from learners. The design is a survey, which the protocol excludes, so E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) applies. Population is teachers, not students, which also fails the population criterion. Under the rule of first applicable code, E6 is used here as the closest fit for a non-eligible survey design; E4 would also fit because participants are in-service teachers.

quote: The work is based on an analysis of the current practice of implementing digital tools in Russian schools
rationale: The record is a theoretical/reflective essay drawing on managerial experience and pedagogical reflection, with no empirical design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Generative AI is mentioned only in passing ("platforms with AI tutors") and is not a learner-facing intervention studied against a comparison group.

quote: Cognitive Load Optimization (CLO) is a new Science of Learning (SoL) theory that quantitatively models relational knowledge as coherent, contiguous, pedagogically scalable schemas
rationale: The abstract is largely a theoretical/position piece about a learning theory (CLO) and the limits of ChatGPT versus CLO. It does not describe an empirical comparative design with a control group of learners, so it appears not to be an empirical study. The abstract mentions 'one experiment' and claims of significant improvements, but gives no design, sample, or quantitative outcome details. Exclusion on E6 is based on the abstract's framing as a conceptual/theoretical analysis; this is a judgment call that the full text should confirm, so the decision could reasonably be reversed to unsure if the full text reports a controlled experiment.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on E6 is a judgment call.

quote: A cross-sectional descriptive survey was conducted from August to September 2025, targeting 150 registered nurses
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of practicing nurses about AI awareness and perceptions. No learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and population is in-service nurses rather than students. Design is a survey, so it is not an empirical experiment; E6 is the first code that applies under the rule that checks codes in order from E1, but E1 (no learner-facing AI intervention) is arguably the first applicable code. Reporting E6 as the closest design-based exclusion. Excluded on positive evidence of a survey design.

quote: This essay argues that prompt engineering should not be conceived as a merely technical skill
rationale: The record is a Spanish-titled essay that proposes a conceptual model and presents a prompt for analysis. It is not an empirical study: no experimental or comparison-group design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) applies. This is a positive signal from the abstract, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: Using GPT-4o and GPT-5-chat, 24 student essays were evaluated against rubrics designed by instructors and refined through the automated RPE process.
rationale: GenAI is used to score student essays (automated essay scoring), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Students do not interact with the generative AI; the AI is an assessment/grading tool. Also no control group without generative AI is described (two GenAI variants compared), and the domain is essay scoring rather than STEM. Exclusion under E1 as the first applicable code.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence that AI is used only for grading, not learner-facing.

rationale: The abstract describes a computational framework (Bayesian bias quantification, fairness-constrained transfer learning, VAE, knowledge distillation) with "experimental validation" but gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group without generative AI, or a learning outcome with effect-size data. The design is a methods/algorithm paper rather than a controlled comparison of learners. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study of the protocol's type), though the abstract is thin; a full-text check would be needed if the researcher disagrees. Note the abstract mentions "compressing large language models" but does not establish learner interaction. Could alternatively be argued as unsure at abstract stage, given the rule to exclude only on positive evidence; the positive evidence here is that the study is a computational framework evaluated on disparity metrics rather than a learner comparison.

quote: We suggest conducting a search in four steps.
rationale: The record is a non-empirical editorial/guidance piece on searching for mHealth apps. It reports no study, no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and is cardiovascular nursing rather than STEM education. Earliest applicable code is E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention), but the dominant failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Using E6 as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering: E1 would be the first code in order if intervention were judged absent; the record describes no learner-facing intervention at all, so E1 also applies. Following the protocol order strictly, E1 is the first code that applies.

quote: A qualitative, descriptive study was conducted using a multi-case design.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative, descriptive multi-case study using classroom observations, document analysis, and written feedback, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative design meeting the protocol. The domain is also ESP language learning (professional vocabulary), which is non-STEM. Excluded under E6 as a non-empirical-quantitative design, which is the first code that applies on the evidence; the design failure is the decisive problem. Note that E6 is strictly "not an empirical study" and this is a qualitative empirical study, so the code is a best fit rather than an exact match; E3 (no control group) would also apply.
rationale_note: Abstract stage exclusion is based on positive evidence of qualitative design without a comparison group.

quote: A sequential mixed-methods design (QUAL → quan) was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a sequential mixed-methods survey/qualitative study of 77 undergraduates on information-seeking and perceptions, with no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, and no learning outcome measured after an intervention. Positive evidence of missing comparison group and experimental design supports exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Population (university students) is met; domain is not clearly STEM but this was not needed as the first applicable code is E3 given the ordering concern, though E1/E2 cannot be fully ruled out from the abstract.

quote: This survey study aims to identify the level of awareness of GenAI in chemistry education among trainee teachers from the aspects of general knowledge and use in chemistry education through survey.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of awareness among 100 chemistry trainee teachers. It has no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical experimental study meeting the protocol design. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study of the eligible type). Note the protocol lists survey designs as excluded; E6 is the closest code given the first-applicable ordering, since E1 cannot be established as a learner-facing tool interaction from the abstract.

quote: The assessment's findings demonstrated how chatbots can successfully function as a enhancement to the library website.
rationale: Abstract describes a usage assessment of a library website chatbot (Ivy.ai) with no control group and no learning outcome measured. It is a usage/descriptive assessment, not a comparative experiment. Positive evidence of failing the comparison (no control group) and design/outcome criteria is present. The domain is library information-seeking, not STEM content. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in the stated order is ambiguous; E3 is the closest fit since no comparison group exists. Also not clearly a learning activity or STEM.

quote: the use of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) to create didactic materials in chemistry
rationale: The abstract describes GAI used by teachers to create didactic materials, not learner-facing use. Per protocol, AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is E1. There is also no described control group, learning outcome, or experimental design; the teacher survey measures perceived usability only.

quote: This paper proposes a three-layer skills architecture for teaching IS students to navigate that tension
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/pedagogical framework paper that proposes an architecture and illustrates it with a deployed skill. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 at the abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: This Structured Literature-Type (SLT) study synthesizes international research from 2020 to 2025 to explore these challenges and propose evidence-based strategies.
rationale: The record is a structured literature-type synthesis/review, not an empirical study with a comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It has no intervention comparison, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Graphic design is also not clearly STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is supported by the abstract.

quote: A small, purposefully selected corpus of critical and contrasting cases (NYC ban vs ministerial guidance) was coded for dominant frames, topic foci, and stances.
rationale: The study is a Critical Discourse Analysis and Framing Analysis of press coverage of ChatGPT in education. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool in any learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). It also has no control group, no learning outcome, and is not an empirical experimental study. E1 is the first applicable code in the order given.

quote: developing an algorithm for students’ project-based work using the Google Classroom service
rationale: The abstract describes a speech-culture/language competence pedagogical experiment using project-based work on Google Classroom. No generative AI tool is mentioned anywhere in the abstract, so the intervention criterion fails on positive evidence (E1). Domain also appears non-STEM (language specialties), but E1 is the first applicable code in order. Reference list mentions ChatGPT only as a cited work, not as the intervention.

quote: Findings indicate that while only 40% of educators integrate AI into their teaching, 80% of students actively utilize AI tools.
rationale: The abstract describes a perceptions and satisfaction survey of faculty and students on AI-driven adaptive learning in Thane District colleges. It reports usage rates and satisfaction (65% and 70%), with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or skill performance. Positive evidence of E5 (perceptions and usage only) is present, so the record is excluded at abstract stage. Domain is also not identifiable from the abstract. Design is a survey, which is itself not eligible.

quote: This community service program aimed to improve teachers’ and students’ knowledge and skills in using AI technologies
rationale: The record is a community service program report with socialization, training, and mentoring, with no comparison group, no controlled design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported (only increased understanding/awareness). It is not an empirical comparative study. Code E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply, but E6 reflects the non-empirical community-service nature. Also STEM content is not clearly specified. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group and no quantitative outcome.

quote: Based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology model, the study uses a quantitative approach with data collected from 490 teachers.
rationale: The study surveys in-service secondary math teachers about adoption intentions (UTAUT, PLS-SEM). Its outcome is perceptions/behavioral intention, not a quantitative learning outcome, and the population is in-service teachers rather than students. No control group or learning measure is described. Excluded under E5 as the first applicable code; the population issue (E4) also applies. The protocol's ordering places E4 before E5 and would make E4 the first applicable code, so this is a point for the auditor to verify.

quote: A qualitative study using semistructured interviews with a topic guide was conducted among 16 orthodontic professionals
rationale: Qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical comparative study; excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs). Population is orthodontic professionals (in-service practitioners), which also fails E4, and orthodontics is health professions education, not STEM (E2). Using the first applicable code in order, E1 would require judging intervention, which is unclear, so E6 is reported as the applicable code given the qualitative design.

This is an integrative review, not an empirical study. Its abstract states it "critiques and synthesizes current research" and included six quantitative studies. Under the protocol's exclusion code list, reviews fall under E6 (not an empirical study) and E10 is for publication type. Nursing education is also health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. The abstract's outcomes are attitudes, perceptions, and behavioral intentions, which the protocol excludes as affective outcomes. Several criteria therefore fail on the abstract. Only E6 is recorded here as the first applicable code in the given order, and the review type is the clearest reason.

quote: Thematic analysis revealed two overarching themes: Perceived benefits included support in structuring lesson content, organizing instructional flow, generating activities, and saving time.
rationale: Qualitative thematic analysis of open-ended questionnaires from 14 preservice chemistry teachers using ChatGPT. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and benefits. Exclude at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also qualitative, not a comparison design, so E3 would also apply, but the first applicable code in order is E5 only if the no-control issue is considered secondary; per code order, E3 precedes E5 and should be used instead.

quote: A mixed-methods quasi-experimental design employing a one-group pretest–posttest approach was adopted.
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group without generative AI, which is an explicit E3 exclusion (single-group pre-post). Intervention (ChatGPT as decision-support partner), population (undergraduates), and outcomes (critical thinking and decision-making tests) appear to be met. Exclusion on E3 is positive evidence from the abstract, so the record is excluded.

quote: This community service program aims to address the need for integrating local cultural elements into German language education for high school teachers in Surabaya
rationale: Community service program report with no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are in-service teachers (not students). Domain is German language education, which is non-STEM. Not an empirical study design meeting the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order used here; E4 and E2 would also apply on the merits. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of design features (program report, no control group, no outcome measure).

quote: "A national cross-sectional survey was conducted among medical students"
rationale: The record is a cross-sectional survey with no control group and no experimental comparison, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Its outcome is self-reported dependence and satisfaction (perceptions), not a quantitative learning outcome, which also fails. Domain is not STEM-specific. Using E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order would be the no-control-group code; the design failure is the clearest basis, and E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is also clearly met. Following the protocol's order, E3 is reported as the first code that applies on the comparison row. Population (medical students) is met.

quote: Method: an experience report of an advanced university extension program at the Universidade Federal do Pará, Brazil, carried out in 2024 in a Non-Governmental Organization, based on Donald Schön's reflective practice based on records of reports.
rationale: The record is an experience report using reflective practice on records of reports, not an empirical comparative study. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Environmental health education is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion is appropriate even at abstract stage.

quote: The research adopts a qualitative, exploratory case-study approach based on semi-structured interviews with 13 participants
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative exploratory case study using semi-structured interviews, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical experimental design eligible under the protocol. Generative AI appears only as a tool students rely on, not as a studied intervention, and the domain is general digital transformation rather than STEM. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., a qualitative case study), the first applicable code in order would be E1 or E2 but the record's core design is non-eligible; the abstract gives clear positive evidence that the design is qualitative with no control group.

quote: Pharmacogenomics of Statins: A View from ChatGPT
rationale: The title shows the topic is pharmacogenomics of statins, a medical/health content area rather than science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science. Content is not STEM under the protocol's domain rule (health professions content is excluded). No abstract is available; the record gives no evidence of a learner-facing study with a control group, so the domain failure is the first applicable code.

quote: This qualitative study explored how prospective Turkish Language and Literature teachers conceptualized and experienced the design process
rationale: The study is explicitly qualitative, using interviews, journals, and observation with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It also concerns Turkish Language and Literature, which is non-STEM. Exclusion is applied at E5 per the protocol's ordering for lack of a quantitative learning outcome; the design (no comparison group) and non-STEM content would also fail other criteria. Exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract.
rationale_code_note: E5 chosen as first applicable in order is debatable since E2 (non-STEM) and E3 (no control) come earlier in the code list; see note.

quote: The paper outlines the advantages of utilizing the Web Ontology Language (OWL) standard to describe functional dependencies between OS components.
rationale: The paper is an ontology engineering/modeling work (Protégé model, SPARQL verification). It reports no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study. Per E1 ordering, the first applicable code would be E1 (no learner-facing generative AI), but the more fundamental failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is a modeling paper without an intervention or outcome data.
rationale_code_note: Codes are reported in protocol order; E1 technically precedes E6, so the first applicable code is E1.

quote: Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) yang diselenggarakan oleh Program Profesi Guru, Sekolah Pascasarjana UNJ
rationale: This is a community service (PkM) training activity for in-service teachers, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It describes teacher training on TPACK and ChatGPT use as a teacher co-pilot, so the population is in-service teachers, and no learner-facing generative AI or STEM content is evident. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group or outcome data.

quote: This study used quantitative method by distributing Likert scale questionnaires to 32 participants.
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire-based correlational/regression study of 32 students with no control group that does not use generative AI, so no comparison group is evident. The outcome is self-reported productivity and learning style via Likert questionnaires, not a quantitative learning measure. Per the rule that exclusions at abstract stage need positive evidence, the lack of a control group and survey design are positive evidence of failure. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in the stated order of concern (no control group); the design also fails as a correlational survey.

quote: Given the single-group design, the contribution is exploratory and practice-oriented and warrants confirmation through comparative research.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design with paired-samples t-tests on 60 pre-service teachers and no control group without generative AI. Under the protocol this is E3 (single-group pre-post design). Domain is also unclear (learning design competency is not clearly STEM), but E3 is the first applicable code in order from the abstract evidence.
rationale_short: Single-group pre-post design; no control group.

quote: This poster shares strategies for incorporating freely available AI tools into one-on-one and small group consultations
rationale: The record is a conference-style poster describing practical strategies based on one librarian's experience. It is not an empirical study: there is no control group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies. It would also fall under E10 as a poster, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order of reporting for this stage... Note: E10 (publication type) is listed after E6 in the protocol's ordering, so E6 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: Through a survey of 80 undergraduate students (N = 80) at the University of Jos, Nigeria, we examined the relationship between privacy fatigue
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using PLS-SEM on adoption intention of ChatGPT. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are perceptions and behavioral intention. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Abstract-stage evidence is sufficient for exclusion because the design and outcomes are described as survey-based adoption perceptions.

Also the population is instructors rather than students. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

rationale: The study is a survey of ChatGPT utilization and perceptions among students and teachers, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome.
