Exclusion code E5 is the most direct fit at the abstract stage; the design also fails, and E3 (no control group) could be argued, but the abstract gives clearest evidence of no learning outcome. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of a survey design with no learning outcome.

criteria.stage_note: survey of school administrators and teachers

quote: The research instrument was a 5-level rating scale questionnaire with an IOC value between .67 and 1.00
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of school administrators and teachers about the operation of a student care system. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative design) is the first applicable code; it is a survey design, which the protocol excludes under Design. The abstract mentions ChatGPT only as a recommendation for teachers, not as a learner intervention.

quote: This scoping review aims to explore and map the existing literature on educational CAs developed for programming education
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review article and not an empirical study. It reports no comparison-group experiment or quantitative learning outcome from primary data, so it fails E6 (and would also fail the design and outcome criteria). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code given the review-type design; E10 (publication type: reviews) would also apply, but E6 is the closest match to "not an empirical study" under the stated order, and the review nature is the decisive feature.
rationale_note: Note for auditor: the protocol lists reviews under E10 (publication type not eligible). Given the ordering, E10 is arguably the more precise code. Please verify.

quote: Development of an AI-Integrated English Writing Class Model for Artificial Intelligence Literacy
rationale: The study is an English writing class (language learning, non-STEM content), so it fails the domain criterion (E2), which is the first applicable code in order. The abstract also describes a pre-post attitude test on a single group with no control group, which would additionally suggest E3, but E2 is reported first. Generative AI use by students is described, so the intervention is plausibly met.

quote: This study aims to map the research landscape of personalized and adaptive learning from 2001 to 2025 through a bibliometric analysis of 922 peer-reviewed documents sourced from the Scopus database.
rationale: The record is a bibliometric analysis of 922 Scopus documents, not an empirical learning study. It has no experimental intervention, control group, or learning outcome. Under the protocol's E1 to E10 order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code. Exclusion is justified on positive evidence that the design is a bibliometric review, not an empirical study.

quote: This practice-based reflection examines the use of large language models to rapidly produce a classroom demonstration in an undergraduate JavaScript course.
rationale:
The paper is a practice-based reflection with a self-described non-experimental method. The generative AI is used by the instructor to produce a demonstration, not as a learner-facing tool, which is also E1. Per the rules, the first applicable code is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing), but the primary and clearest failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). No control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported. Coding E6 as the decisive reason since the record describes a reflection with no empirical data.</parameter>
<parameter name="rationale_note">none

quote: This paper proposes an AI-enhanced instructional model for linear algebra organized around a closed loop of concept construction, inquiry-based learning, and formative feedback.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical instructional model and discussion of its application; it reports no comparison group, no experiment or quasi-experiment, and no quantitative outcome data. The claim that GenAI "can effectively support" learning is asserted, not measured. This is a non-empirical paper, so E6 applies. Comparison and design are not met on the abstract's description, so the record is excluded on E6 as the first applicable code in order.

quote: This research is a survey study that integrates both descriptive and correlational approaches.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey study with descriptive and correlational analysis of 600 graduate students, with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. Survey and correlational designs are excluded by the protocol. The E3 code is used because the study lacks a comparison group; the design criterion is also not met. Domain is unclear since the Master of Educational Administration program is not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of design failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: "I prepared this Points of Reference after reading about artificial intelligence (AI) and the many recent improvements in its capabilities."
rationale: The record is a Points of Reference editorial-style commentary on AI and chatbots in environmental toxicology publishing. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6), which is the first applicable code in the stated order for an abstract-stage record with clear positive evidence of non-empirical design.

quote: This applied research utilized a scientometric approach.
rationale: The record is a bibliometric/scientometric mapping of Web of Science publications on AI and information seeking behavior. It is not an empirical intervention study: there is no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol, it fails the design requirement (not an empirical study in the sense of experiments/quasi-experiments), so E6 is the first applicable code. Note that E1 could arguably apply first, but the paper has no intervention at all, so E6 best describes it.

quote: The first systematic study of how ChatGPT might affect the white-collar workplace has found that AI may be more useful for creative tasks than analytical ones.
rationale: This record is a Significance magazine news piece (Year 2024), not a journal empirical study. It is a news roundup covering many unrelated stories. The ChatGPT item describes a study of consultants at Boston Consulting Group, which is workplace training/professional work rather than students and not STEM learning. The piece is not an empirical study report, so E6 applies. Note that the protocol's first applicable code in order would be E1 or E4, but the record itself is a news item, so E6 is the most direct failure.

quote: We evaluated the system using a dataset of 1000 handwritten vector equations typical of the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' Level H2 Mathematics syllabus.
rationale: The evaluation is a technical accuracy test of GPT-4o and GPT-4.1-mini on a dataset of 1000 handwritten equations, with no control group of learners and no learning outcome measured. Accuracy of model output is not a quantitative learning outcome, so E5 applies. The study is not a learner-facing controlled experiment. Domain is STEM (mathematics). Exclusion is positive per the abstract, so exclude rather than unsure.

quote: This research draws upon existing literature and employs an autoethnographic approach, critically reflecting on our experiences as trainers and thesis supervisors
rationale: The record is a case study/autoethnographic reflection on a translation training program, with bibliometric and content analysis of theses. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails on design, comparison and outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable; E3 (no control group) would also apply. Domain (game translation) is also not clearly STEM.

criteria.quote: A cross-sectional survey design was employed, utilizing an online self-administered questionnaire that yielded 296 valid responses
criteria.rationale: Cross-sectional survey measuring perceptions and needs; no experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Survey design is not an eligible empirical design under the protocol; coded E6 as not an empirical study meeting the design requirements (survey design is excluded by the Design criterion). Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of a survey design with perception-only measures.

quote: A cross-sectional survey design was employed, utilizing an online self-administered questionnaire that yielded 296 valid responses
we used ChatGPT as a source of feedback for students' argumentative essay writing tasks
rationale: Content is argumentative essay writing, a non-STEM domain (language/writing), so E2 applies. The study compares ChatGPT feedback with peer feedback on feedback quality and correlates essay quality with feedback quality, with no learning-outcome comparison against a no-GenAI control group, so it also looks unlikely to meet the design and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E2.

quote: A Study on the Potential Use of ChatGPT as a Supplementary Tool for Learning Korean Complaint Speech Acts
rationale: The study concerns learning Korean complaint speech acts, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also reports only learner perceptions and conversation log analysis, with no quantitative learning outcome and no comparison group. E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order, so it is reported.

quote: This qualitative case study examines the 16-week autonomous use of AI technologies by thirteen female pre-service teachers at a Punjabi government college.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group. Per rule 2, exclusion requires positive evidence; the design is clearly qualitative (positive evidence), so the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). E5 (no quantitative outcome) also applies; E3 is reported as the first code in the order that fits the design failure. STEM domain is not stated in the abstract.

quote: The study employed a correlational design. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale closed-ended questionnaire
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational survey design with simple linear regression, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Correlational and survey designs are excluded by the protocol's Design row and the comparison requirement is not met. The outcomes are self-reported Likert questionnaire measures of AI use, learning assistance, and misconduct, not a quantitative learning outcome. Population (university students) appears met. Exclusion code E3 is applied because the absence of a control group without generative AI is the first failing criterion in the protocol's ordering, though the design failure would also support exclusion. Note that the code order in the protocol places E1 and E2 earlier; intervention and domain are not clearly failing from the abstract, so E3 is the first applicable code given the abstract evidence.

quote: The study compares three high school Teaching Sequences (TSs) on electrolysis, developed with and without AI's assistance.
rationale: The generative AI (GPT-3.5/GPT-4) was used to create teaching sequences, i.e., by teachers/researchers for lesson planning, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. The comparison is between teaching sequences authored with or without AI, with no learner outcome measured. Excluded under E1 (AI not learner-facing). Also no quantitative learning outcome is reported in the abstract (E5 would also apply), but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: A course-specific chatbot was designed and constrained using authenticated Hadith terminology, the officially adopted textbook in Hadith Sciences
rationale: Hadith Sciences is an Islamic religious studies subject, not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science. Fails the domain criterion (E2), which is the first applicable code in order when considering the other criteria as plausibly met from the abstract (generative chatbot, quasi-experimental control cohort, course grades as outcome). Excluded on positive evidence that the content is non-STEM.

quote: A controlled classroom study is planned as the next step.
rationale: The abstract describes a system design/proof of concept (Lion-AI, a RAG-based Socratic chatbot for CS students) and states that a controlled classroom study is only planned. No comparison group, empirical design, or quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that clearly applies; the study also arguably fails E6 (not an empirical study), but the abstract gives no evidence of data collection, so E5 is reported as the primary reason.

quote: A qualitative methodology of documentary review and inductive coding applied to indexed academic publications was used.
rationale: The abstract describes a critical literature review using qualitative documentary review and inductive coding, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Positive evidence of this failure is present, so abstract-stage exclusion is appropriate.

quote: This pilot study aims to analyse primary school teachers’ perceptions of online escape games.
rationale: The study analyses primary school teachers' perceptions using Q methodology, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome in learners. Participants are teachers, not students, and the design is perception-based (Q-sort). ChatGPT is used only as an analysis tool, not as a learner-facing intervention. The abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is perceptions rather than learning, so E5 applies. Population (teachers) and design also fail, but the first applicable code in order that fits best is E5 given the perception-only outcome; E1 could arguably apply first since ChatGPT is not learner-facing. Under the stated order, E1 is checked first: the generative AI in this paper is used by researchers for data analysis, not by learners in a learning activity, so E1 is the first code that applies.

quote: The model was evaluated using benchmark testing on a separate dataset, with performance measured using accuracy and F1 score.
rationale: The chatbot is generative (LoRA fine-tuned LLM with RAG) and the abstract is about polytechnic/TVET education. However, the evaluation is model benchmark accuracy on a separate dataset (85% vs 60% baseline), not a learner outcome. No learner-level quantitative learning measure is reported, and no learner-facing control group is described. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is a model benchmark rather than learning.

quote: Roman Urdu hate and offensive language detection is difficult
rationale: Hate speech classification in Roman Urdu is not STEM content, and the abstract describes a classifier training method rather than a learner-facing generative AI intervention. Excluded under E2.

quote: Using a qualitative case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews and focus group discussions with seven teacher educators and four graduate students
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study with interviews and focus groups, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract and E3 is the earliest clear failure. Domain is also unclear (writing, not clearly STEM). Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group and qualitative design.

quote: This article focuses on the DTP Framework - Discussion forum, Team practices and Peer assessment, which sets up a suitable learning environment for the learners
rationale: The intervention described is a discussion forum, team practice and peer assessment framework (DTP), with no indication that learners interact with a generative AI tool. The GenAI mention is only contextual ("In the GenAI era"). Positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. Software engineering is STEM and students are higher education, but these do not change the exclusion.

quote: This study analyzes the perception of health sciences faculty regarding the use of ChatGPT in their teaching practices
rationale: Non-experimental, cross-sectional perception survey of faculty (not students) in health sciences (Nutrition, Nursing, Psychology, Dentistry). No control group, no learner-facing intervention, no quantitative learning outcome; perception data only. Health-profession content and in-service faculty population also fail the protocol. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order for this record's perception-only outcome; the design also fails comparison and design criteria.

quote: Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis (RTA), with the Family Resemblance Approach to NOS (FRA – NOS) as an analytical orientation.
rationale: The study is a reflexive thematic analysis of Nature and Science commentaries about AI. It is not an empirical intervention study with learners: there is no learner-facing generative AI tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the record more fundamentally is a non-empirical qualitative commentary analysis, so E6 (not an empirical study) is the most accurate single code. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence of qualitative design. Ordering note: the protocol says report the first code that applies in order; E1 precedes E6, and no learner-facing AI is described, so E1 could be argued. I am recording E6 as the primary design-level failure.

quote: Twenty English teachers from the Musyawarah Guru Mata Pelajaran (MGMP) participated in training sessions designed to improve confidence and practical competence
rationale: The participants are in-service English teachers in a community service workshop, not K-12 or higher education students. The content is English language teaching, which is not STEM. The design is a single-group pre-post program with no comparison group. Exclusion is based on population (E4) as the first applicable code in order, although E2 (non-STEM content) and E3 (no control group) also apply.

quote: SOCIETY OF CRITICAL CARE MEDICINE 55TH CRITICAL CARE CONGRESS
rationale: The record is a conference program listing of abstracts from the Society of Critical Care Medicine Congress, not a journal article reporting an empirical study. It contains no description of a generative AI intervention, a control group, or a learning outcome. Multiple abstract titles in the list are not about generative AI learning interventions in STEM. Per the protocol, conference proceedings are not eligible publication types (E10), but since this is a program listing of many unrelated abstracts rather than a single proceedings paper, the most accurate code is E6 (not an empirical study). No abstract gives positive evidence of a generative AI STEM learning study, so the exclusion rests on the record being a non-empirical conference listing.

quote: This research was conducted at Universitas Negeri Manado on students of the Mathematics Education Study Program, using a qualitative approach.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative perception study using questionnaires and a Likert scale, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. The design is not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a comparison group, and the outcome is perception-based rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in order, with the design and outcome also failing. Positive evidence of failure is present in the abstract, so exclusion at this stage is appropriate.

quote: Thus, this study explores ChatGPT's potential to act as a pedagogy expert annotator.
rationale: ChatGPT is used by researchers to annotate a dataset for training ITS instructor models; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This fails the learner-facing intervention requirement (E1). No learner control group, learning outcome, or STEM content is described in the abstract.

quote: We conducted a comprehensive content analysis to scrutinize the applicability and competence of ChatGPT in addressing BCPS exam inquiries
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to pharmacotherapy specialist exam questions rather than learners interacting with a generative AI tool. There is no learner population and no control group; the design is a content analysis of model outputs. The record fails on population (not students), comparison (no control group without generative AI), and design (not an experimental or quasi-experimental study). Health pharmacotherapy content is also outside the STEM domain as defined by the protocol. Exclusion code E4 is applied as the first clearly applicable code in the protocol's order, given no learner participants are present. Although E1 (not learner-facing) could also be argued, the abstract gives no learner involvement at all, so E4 is the primary code applied here.

quote: The work takes a close look at how emotional intelligence can be woven into the way language is actually used and taught
rationale: The study concerns bilingual language acquisition and social-emotional learning, which is non-STEM content (language learning). Excluded on E2 (content is not STEM). The abstract also gives no indication of a control group or a quantitative comparison design; the pilot data are described only in terms of gains and perceptions, so other criteria are unclear. Only the first applicable code is reported.

quote: This study presents a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis examining how chatbots and virtual agents are used in educational and professional training.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Its synthesized studies also span medicine and non-STEM contexts, and it is not a primary experiment with a control group. Excluded on the first applicable code, E6.

quote: A descriptive-correlational design was used to obtain data from 279 students at a public state university in the northern Philippines
rationale: Per the protocol, the record is a descriptive-correlational survey study. It has no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as an intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Surveys of dishonesty and epistemological beliefs are perceptions or self-report, not learning outcomes. Under the protocol's E-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would be the first code to apply, since no AI tool is used as an intervention. However, the defining feature is a non-empirical-trial survey design. I am coding E6 (not an empirical study) as the best fit for a correlational survey without any intervention. Generative AI is mentioned only as background context. The record is excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence of design failure.

quote: Student performance on open-response calculations involving acid and base solutions before and after instruction in general chemistry and analytical chemistry courses was compared with the output from the artificial intelligence chatbot ChatGPT.
rationale: Abstract describes a comparison of student performance against ChatGPT output (chatbot responses to the same problems), with no separate control group of learners that does not use generative AI. Students' pre- and post-instruction performance is not a non-AI control. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 at abstract stage. Note: the criteria object in this call was partially malformed; the decision and code are the substantive output.

quote: We investigated the use of generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) to automate a peer review process to enhance CS students' engagement with code review
rationale: Abstract describes genAI-powered code review for CS students in higher education (intervention, population, and domain appear met). It is unclear from the abstract whether there is a control group without genAI (comparison and design unclear), and the outcome is described as engagement and issues identified/fixes, so whether a learning outcome is measured is unclear. No positive evidence of failure, so not excluded at abstract stage; full text needed.

quote: This study investigates the intuitive ("organic") capabilities of Generation Z students in designing Generative AI prompts
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative content analysis of 125 student-written prompts with no experimental manipulation and no control group, so there is no comparison group without generative AI. The design is qualitative/descriptive, and the outcome is a categorical typology rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code on the protocol's ordering that is supported by positive evidence in the abstract (no control group), though E5 and E6 also plausibly apply.

quote: corpus pedagogy empowered by Artificial Intelligence is explored as a new kind of tech intervention
rationale: The AI system (GPT-4 API) is used to analyze a corpus and produce linguistic/psychological analyses; the abstract reports tool-versus-human processing efficiency and precision, not learner-facing use in a learning activity. This indicates the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). No control group of learners without generative AI is described, and the outcomes are system performance and implementation metrics rather than learner learning outcomes, so E3 and E5 would also apply, but the first applicable code in order is E1. Content (psychology EMI) is also not clearly STEM. Excluded on positive evidence at abstract stage.

quote: ChatGPT has "passed" the medical biochemistry university examination with an average score of 117 out of 200 (58%) in both papers.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to examination papers directly, with no learner group and no control group. This is a performance assessment of the model itself, not a controlled comparison of learners, so there is no comparison group without generative AI. Excluded under E3. Medical biochemistry is also arguably outside the protocol's STEM domain, but E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: The results showed a 52% increase in students' ability to construct theoretical frameworks and literature reviews, and a 67% increase in understanding citation ethics.
rationale: This community service activity reports pre-post percentage increases in students' abilities with no mention of a control or comparison group, so it appears to be a single-group pre-post design, which is excluded under E3. Domain is also unclear (research skills and citation ethics are not clearly STEM). The abstract gives positive evidence of the missing comparison group, so E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: ACEPS 2025 Abstracts Supplement Table of Contents
rationale: The record is a conference abstract supplement table of contents, not an empirical study with a control group. It lists many abstracts across plastic surgery residency topics; none is identifiable as a randomized or quasi-experimental STEM learning study with a generative AI intervention. Also a conference-type publication (E10 possible), but the first applicable code in order is E1 check: the record does not describe a learner-facing generative AI intervention, and it is not an empirical study, so E6 is assigned as the most direct code. No quantitative learning outcome or STEM content is evident.

quote: Рассматривается промпт-инжиниринг как современный инструмент оптимизации процесса обучения иностранным языкам
rationale: The record concerns foreign language learning (non-STEM content), so it fails the Domain criterion (E2). Also, the abstract describes a conceptual/methodological article with pilot sessions and a table of AI response quality, with no described control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so further criteria would likely fail too. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported.
rationale_note: Criteria flags: comparison not_met (no control group described); design unclear; outcome unclear.

quote: Each question was fed into ChatGPT based on GPT-3.5, exactly once per session, and all responses were documented.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to exam questions directly, with no learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity (E1 would apply under a strict reading), and there is no human learner or control group. The design is a model-benchmarking comparison of English versus Korean prompts, not an empirical study of learners. Population is not students (E4 also applies). Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first applicable code, so the exclusion should be re-coded as E1 if the auditor applies the order strictly. Note: I selected E6 in error on reflection; the correct first-applicable code is E1.

quote: Program Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kapasitas guru pendidikan Islam
rationale: Community engagement (pengabdian masyarakat) training program for in-service teachers at a Thai Islamic school. The population is in-service teachers, not students, and the design is a service report with no comparison group. The evaluation reports improvements without a control group or a quantitative learning outcome in students. Exclude as not an empirical study (E6) at the first applicable code in the order; E4 (population) would also apply. Strictly, E4 comes before E6 in the code order, so the population exclusion is the first applicable code.

quote: The study explores the perceptions of chemistry teachers in Kigali City regarding the use of dynamic simulations in teaching chemical kinetics.
rationale: Abstract describes a perception survey and interviews of in-service chemistry teachers, not learners. There is no generative AI tool (dynamic simulations are not shown to be generative AI), no control group, and no learning outcome measured. Participants are in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion is on the first applicable code in order; E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would apply first because no generative AI is involved and no learner interacts with one. Coding E6 (not an empirical study) is not accurate either since it is empirical, so the closest accurate primary code is E1 on the intervention. Reporting E1 as the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: Surveys conducted in the Fall 2025 semester suggest that the assignment reinforced student content understanding and reiterated the importance of responsible AI use.
rationale: Abstract describes an undergraduate microbiology writing assignment using generative AI, but the only evidence reported is survey-based self-report and perceptions, with no quantitative learning measure or control group. Design appears to be a single-cohort descriptive report. Positive evidence of failure on outcome (perceptions only) and design (no comparison group) supports exclusion. E5 is the first applicable code in protocol order given no quantitative learning outcome; E3 (no control) could also apply, but E5 is the earlier-listed reason when the outcome is only perceived.

quote: In a single week, a physician can produce dozens of progress notes totaling tens of thousands of words of clinical text.
rationale: The record is a commentary/perspective piece on progress note writing in graduate medical education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as a future possibility, not as an intervention learners used. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6), which is the first applicable code in the order given for an opinion piece; the domain (clinical writing in medicine) also does not fit STEM.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is based on positive evidence that the record is a non-empirical commentary.

criteria.design_note: website audit / descriptive coding, no control group

quote: Findings suggest HSI community colleges rarely utilize AI chatbots, and when they do, they often do not facilitate access to Spanish-language information
rationale: The study is a descriptive website audit of chatbots at HSI community colleges, coding presence and interaction quality. It has no learners in a learning activity, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical learning study under the protocol; the closest fit is E6 (not an empirical study of the eligible type). Its systematic review element does not change this. Stage is abstract, and the abstract gives clear positive evidence of failure on the comparison, design, and outcome criteria.
rationale_note: Exclusion code chosen as E6 for a non-learning descriptive audit; E1 could also arguably apply since chatbots are not learner-facing in a learning activity.

quote: I approached this survey review of six recent publications on language learning using technology
rationale: The record is a book review of six books on technology in language teaching (ELT). It is not an empirical study, has no control group or quantitative learning outcome, and its domain is language learning rather than STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that applies in order of the protocol's logic; the E2 non-STEM content problem would also apply.

quote: This ethnographic study investigates the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in creative pedagogy for Teaching English to Young Learners (TEYL)
rationale: The study is about teaching English to young learners, which is language learning and not STEM. It is also an ethnographic design with no control group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Domain is the first failing criterion in protocol order, so E2 is reported. Note that the protocol lists E2 before E3, so E2 is the first applicable code.
rationale_note: Exclusion codes are reported in order; E2 (non-STEM) applies first.

quote: This article explores how AI could fundamentally reshape business schools, suggesting we may be entering a “third epoch” of management education
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/strategic analysis ("this article explores", "we analyze ... through the lens of a value-based strategy framework") with no experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a non-empirical article, so it fails E6. Earlier codes are not clearly triggered, so E6 is the first applicable code in the order that matters for this record; the abstract provides positive evidence that the study is not empirical.

quote: Participants included English (N=35), German (N=9), and French (N=9) language teachers in the pre-sessional program of a Turkish university
rationale: Participants are in-service language teachers, not students, so the population criterion fails. The study is also a mixed-method questionnaire and interview design with no control group and no learning outcome, and the content is foreign language teaching rather than STEM. The first applicable code in order is E4, though the record would also fail E3, E5 and E2 on the abstract.

quote: This study examines Lithuanian students’ attitudes toward AI integration across universities, colleges, and vocational schools (N = 803) using mixed methods combining quantitative surveys with qualitative content analysis.
rationale: The study is a survey of attitudes and usage rates with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are perceptions and usage, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is survey-based, so it also fails the comparison and design criteria, but E5 is the first applicable code in order.

Abstract is not present in the index; only title, venue, and year are available.
