rationale_note: Note: E4 is listed in the protocol order before E5, so E4 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: The Database of Combined Slave Trade Voyages (DCSTV) ... combined the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database, the Intra-American Slave Trade Database, and the African Origins Database
rationale: This is a data-resource description for a historical slave-trade database, not a learning study. No learner interacts with any generative AI tool, there is no control group, no learning outcome, and the content is historical rather than STEM. The record fails several criteria; E1 is reported as the first applicable code in order. Not a journal article in the protocol's sense either, but the first applicable code is E1.

quote: The subjects of the study were 109 active undergraduate students in the Economics Education Study Program, class of 2023.
rationale: The study is a descriptive quantitative survey using simple linear regression on questionnaire data about ChatGPT use and learning interest. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The outcome is a self-reported affective measure (learning interest), not a quantitative learning outcome, and the domain (economics education) is not STEM. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Information retrieval and analysis of scientific sources were conducted using the scientometric databases of PubMed
rationale: This is a bibliosemantic literature review, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learner-facing generative AI intervention evaluated, and no quantitative learning outcome. Population is pediatricians in continuing professional development, which is also outside the protocol's population. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first that applies in the code order that is clearly supported; E1 and E4 are also plausible, but the review design is the decisive failure.

quote: Results showed that students using a self-assessment chatbot scored 10 points or the equivalent of a full letter grade higher on a posttest than those using the standard Chat GPT.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study uses a ChatGPT-based (generative) chatbot with a comparison to standard ChatGPT. The comparison is a generative AI variant without self-assessment, not a non-generative control, so comparison criterion is not clearly met; however the abstract does not state that the comparison is only generative variants, and the design (experimental vs quasi) and effect-size data are not described. Population (college students), math domain, and posttest outcome appear to fit. Nothing gives positive evidence of failure, so include for full-text check of the control condition (likely E3 if both arms use generative AI).

criteria.exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen as first applicable code

quote: This paper analyzes 52 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2024, utilizing NLP techniques to identify prevalent unigrams, bigrams and trigrams related to AI in higher education.
rationale: The record is a bibliometric/NLP analysis of 52 published articles, not an empirical intervention study with a control group. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion codes in order, the first applicable code is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) arguably, but the core failure is that it is not an empirical study, so E6 is assigned as the most fundamental failure. Decision is exclude; the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a review-type design.

quote: This work adopts a comprehensive analytical and comparative study design, combining a systematic review of current AIGC technologies with practical workflow demonstrations and pedagogical integration models.
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic/literature review and workflow demonstrations rather than an empirical experiment with a control group. No learner-facing comparison or quantitative learning outcome is reported; benchmarks are of generative model outputs (CD/EMD/F-score, PSNR), not learners. The study is not an empirical comparative trial, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in code order (E1 is ambiguous since the AIGC tool use by learners is not clearly described, but the non-empirical nature is clear positive evidence).
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of non-empirical design.

quote: Rates and Characteristics of Registered Cornea Transplant Trials: An Analysis of Clinicaltrials.gov
rationale: Record is a conference abstract collection (World Cornea Congress IX 2025 abstracts), not a journal article. It describes registry analyses and clinical case series in corneal transplantation with no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no STEM content. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention not generative AI) would be the first code that applies, since no learner-facing generative AI is present at all. Note: the honest first-applicable code is E1 by the ordering rule; the record also fails E10 (conference proceedings). Coding E6 was an error; the correct first code is E1.

quote: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 401 participants aged 18–35 years
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional online survey comparing AI users and non-users on burnout and executive functioning self-report scales (BAT-22, BDEFS-SF). There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no learner-facing intervention or learning outcome; the outcomes are self-reported psychological measures and perceived usefulness. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Under the abstract-stage rule, the exclusion is supported by positive evidence that the design is a survey, which is also ineligible under the Design criterion. Using the first applicable code in order, E5 is reported here; the design is a survey and would fail the design criterion. Note that the code order places E1 first, but the abstract does not clearly establish whether the AI use is learner-facing within a learning activity, so E1 was not assigned.

quote: Six JC sessions were conducted with sixteen residents across two subspecialties, accompanied by structured observations, feedback forms, and pre-/and post-focus groups
rationale: Abstract shows a postgraduate dental residents journal club with an LLM, a design-based research approach with observations, feedback forms and focus groups, and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Dental/medical education and journal club appraisal is not STEM content under the protocol's domain list. Excluded on the first applicable code, E2 (content not STEM). The record is also not eligible on comparison (no control group, E3) and outcome (perception-based only, E5), but E2 is reported as the first applicable in the code order.

quote: Evaluation through pretest and posttest revealed a significant improvement in students’ understanding, with the average correct answers increasing from 68% to 85%.
rationale: Single-group pre-post design with no control group, which is positive evidence of failing the comparison and design criteria (E3, per the borderline rule "One group measured before and after: E3"). The domain is general AI literacy, not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on the positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: A survey of students from four master's degree programs (n=98) showed that most of them had worked with neural networks before their legalization at the university.
rationale: The study is a survey of graduate students about their experiences with neural networks. It reports perceptions and usage only, with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group. The design is survey-based, not an experiment. The domain (media/humanities) is also not clearly STEM. Excluded on E5 as the first applicable code at abstract stage; the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey without learning outcomes.

criteria.criteria_note: descriptive survey of lecturers

quote: A descriptive survey study design was used, using a sample of 100 language instructors drawn from regional colleges of education.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of 100 language lecturers about digital literacy and AI use. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no learning outcome, and the sample is teachers rather than students. Language teaching is also non-STEM. Excluded as not an empirical study of the protocol's type (E6), the first code that clearly applies; the design is survey-only with no comparison group.

quote: The research employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT (generative AI) in a quasi-experimental design with a control group, and measures English proficiency via pre/post tests in higher education. However, the content is English language learning, which the protocol explicitly excludes as non-STEM (domain). Excluded under E2 at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: This review synthesizes multi-method empirical literature, strategic implementation frameworks, and technical benchmarks to evaluate the integration of artificial intelligence, learning analytics, and smart learning technologies across university environments.
rationale: The record is a review (synthesis of existing literature and frameworks), not an empirical study with its own controlled comparison. Under the protocol's publication-type and empirical-study requirements it fails at E6 (not an empirical study). Its abstract also reports no eligible comparison group or quantitative learning outcome of its own, and it covers broad digital transformation rather than STEM-specific generative AI learning interventions. Reviews are excluded under the protocol, so this exclusion is clear at abstract stage.

quote: Presented at the Ninth European Conference on Information Literacy (ECIL) September 22nd -25th, 2025, Bamberg, Germany
rationale: The record is a conference presentation (ECIL 2025) about a library faculty-AI literacy program, not a journal article. It is excluded as publication type not eligible (E10). It also has no comparison group, no learner-facing AI intervention for students, no STEM content focus, and no learning outcome measured, so other criteria would fail as well, but E10 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the abstract-stage evidence.

quote: This article investigates how AI-driven pedagogical strategies can be effectively integrated into foreign language programs within higher education
rationale: The study concerns foreign language acquisition, which is non-STEM content and is excluded under the Domain criterion (E2). The abstract also describes three illustrative case studies without a described control group, which points to a design that does not meet the protocol. E2 is the first applicable code in the specified order for this record.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: A descriptive survey design was employed which involved 350 students selected through simple random sampling technique in Ondo state.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey with no experimental or comparison group, so there is no control group without generative AI (E3). The study also reports only perceptions and attitudes, not a quantitative learning outcome (E5 would also apply). Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E3 is given because the design lacks a comparison group. Exclusion is justified on positive evidence of a failed criterion.

quote: The disruptive nature of technology in higher education is not a new phenomenon, but the progressive drumbeats grow louder and louder amidst several chaos-inducing influences.
rationale: The record is an opinion/commentary piece (it reflects on a Chronicle article and offers personal reflection on nursing education). It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). No quantitative outcome or comparison group is described. Excluded on the first applicable code in order; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract but the design failure is positive evidence.

quote: The experimental testing of twenty reference queries suggests that ChatGPT has a relevance rate of 85 percent
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-method study with a survey, case study, and testing of 20 reference queries for relevance. No control group without generative AI is described, and the outcome is library-service relevance and user perceptions rather than a learning outcome. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude at abstract stage with E3 as the first applicable code. Note that the study is also a library-services context rather than learner-facing STEM learning.

quote: The study adopts a critical inductive methodology, combining an in-depth literature review with an analysis of international case studies
rationale: The paper is a conceptual/literature-review piece proposing a framework. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; E3 and E5 also would fail but E6 is the root reason.

quote: The study was conducted in May 2024, during which the experiment participants (ChatGPT generator software and 62 master's majoring in pedagogy...) were asked two research questions.
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of open-ended student free-writing responses compared with ChatGPT outputs. There is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the design is qualitative rather than an experiment with a comparison group. Domain is pedagogy/didactics, not clearly STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention failed, but the abstract does not show learner-facing generative AI use in a learning activity, so E1 is arguable; E5 is the clearest positive failure (no quantitative learning outcome, qualitative design). Excluding under E5 as the most clearly evidenced failure.

quote: Dear Editor, Strabismus, a prevalent ocular motility disorder, affects approximately 2%–4% of the global population
rationale: Record is an editorial-style letter (“Dear Editor”) about a smartphone-based strabismus measurement tool. It is not an empirical study and reports no learning intervention, control group, or learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order: the record is not an empirical study. Note that E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is arguably also applicable because the tool is a clinical diagnostic device, and the domain is clinical ophthalmology rather than STEM education; E6 is reported as the first code that applies on the stated order. Publication type (E10) is also a possible concern, but the record is best characterized as a letter/editorial, which is E6.

quote: Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian survei yang bertujuan mengetahui persepsi siswa kelas XI terhadap penggunaan ChatGPT
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student perceptions of ChatGPT in physics. It has no control group and no learning outcome measure; it reports only perceptions and satisfaction. The design is a survey, which the protocol excludes. Under the ordering rule, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first code that applies, though E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study design) also apply. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey with perception-only outcomes.

quote: the effectiveness of this technology was verified using L. N. Tolstoy's epic novel War and Peace
rationale: The study concerns philological disciplines (literary text analysis of War and Peace and Martin Eden), which is non-STEM content. This is positive evidence of a failed domain criterion, so exclude under E2. Intervention (generative AI tools Canva, D-ID) and comparison design are not clearly reported in the abstract, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion. Population is higher education students (Higher Pedagogical College), which is met.

quote: However, the study is limited by the absence of a control group and its focus on a single national educational context.
rationale: The abstract states the study has no control group and describes a quasi-experimental pre-post design with a single group, which fails the comparison requirement (single-group pre-post designs are excluded). Exclusion code E3 applies. Note that the abstract explicitly gives positive evidence of the missing control group, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. No injection content was present.

quote: A quasi-experimental, single-group pre-post design was carried out over nine months with 31 students aged 10 to 16 in Delhi, India.
rationale: The study uses a single-group pre-post design with no control group, which the protocol explicitly excludes (E3). The abstract also states that the design included no control group. Domain is unclear because vocabulary and digital literacy are not clearly STEM, though mathematics case studies are mentioned. E3 is the first applicable code given the comparison failure.

quote: This study adopted a mixed-methods approach with a pre-experimental One-Group Pretest-Posttest design.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion (E3). The content is also business writing/English for Specific Purposes, which is non-STEM (E2), but E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order, and E2 would be checked first only if ordering were different; under the stated order of checking E1 then E2 then E3, the domain issue is also a failure. Note: per the protocol order, E2 precedes E3, so the code should be considered E2 as well; the non-STEM domain (English business writing) is clearly stated in the abstract. Reporting the first applicable code in order: E2 applies before E3.

quote: The article presents a comprehensive analysis and theoretical justification of didactic conditions
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical justification of didactic conditions and explicitly states that experimental testing of the conditions is left for future research. There is no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome, so the record is not an empirical study. Generative AI is mentioned as an assistant, but the design criteria fail regardless. Exclude at E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order the protocol lists.

quote: This study chose a comparative case study design because examining programming instruction with two different data analysis methods (human researcher and AI-supported) requires a comparative perspective.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT only by researchers to analyze teacher interview data, so no learners interact with generative AI (E1 would apply first in protocol order). Under the required code order, E1 is the first applicable code, so this should be coded E1 rather than E6. The design is a comparative case study of qualitative analysis with no learner control group and no learning outcome, so it also fails comparison and outcome criteria. Abstract stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence that AI is used only by the researcher.

quote: The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test yielded Z = −3,408 with p-value = 0.001 (p < 0,05), confirming a significant difference in student self-efficacy before and after the six-week AI virtual tutor intervention.
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with 15 students and no control group, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (E3). The outcome is self-efficacy, an affective measure, which the protocol excludes from extraction; this is also a concern, though E3 is the first applicable code in order. Population (university mathematics students) and domain (real analysis) are met.

quote: The study conducts a small-N comparative documentary analysis of post-2023 AI-related policy, curriculum, legal and platform documents from the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, the USA, the European Union, Finland and France.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparative documentary analysis of policy and platform documents, not an empirical learner study. There is no control group, no learner sample, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study) in the sense of the protocol's design requirements. Note that E6 is the first code that applies on the abstract's evidence; E3 and E5 would also fail. Exclusion is appropriate even at the abstract stage because the positive evidence (documentary analysis) clearly rules out a comparative quantitative design.

quote: This presentation explores how AI-supported assessment tools—specifically Co-Grader and ChatGPT—can be used to enhance, rather than replace, relational teaching in secondary science education.
rationale: This is a conference-style presentation describing a teacher's practice. The AI is used by the teacher to grade and personalize feedback, not as a learner-facing tool (E1 would apply on intervention grounds). Per rule order, E1 is first: AI is used only by the teacher to prepare and deliver feedback, so learners do not interact with generative AI as part of a learning activity. Abstract gives positive evidence of teacher-only use, so the intervention criterion fails. Additionally, no comparison group is described, and the record is a presentation rather than an empirical journal article (E6/E10). Reporting E1 as the first applicable code under the protocol order.
decision_note: Coded E1 as first applicable; see rationale.

quote: This study uses a qualitative approach with semi-structured interviews to explore the views and experiences of informants regarding this dishonest behavior.
rationale: Qualitative interview study on factors driving plagiarism; not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, no learning outcome measured, and generative AI is only described as a misuse trend rather than a learning intervention. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would be the first applicable code since no learner-facing AI intervention is evaluated, but the clearest failure is that the record is a qualitative, non-empirical-experimental study; E6 is assigned as the most fitting code for a qualitative study. Exclusion is positive evidence based on the abstract's stated qualitative design.

criteria.stage_note: comparison group not explicit in abstract

quote: We examined the impact of the LPLE using a mixed-methods approach with a quasi-experimental design through the lens of self-determination theory.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is a quasi-experiment with a large language model-based programming learning environment for first-year high school students, measuring programming ability (a quantitative outcome). The abstract does not state the control condition, but this is missing information rather than positive evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text to verify the comparison group.
rationale_note: Advance for full-text check of control group.

quote: Third-year medical students took histories with ChatGPT 3.5 after entering a predefined prompt covering cardiological diseases.
rationale: Content is medical history taking and empathic communication in medical education, which falls under health professions education and is not STEM (E2). The study also reports no control group and no learning outcome measure (only interaction coding and autonomy questionnaire), so E3 and E5 would also fail, but E2 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract shows no comparison group, so this is a clear exclusion.

quote: This review uses a bibliometric mapping approach on 7,569 indexed documents
rationale: The record is a bibliometric mapping study of Scopus documents, not an empirical intervention study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI appears only as a topic trend. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would be the first applicable code, but the primary reason it is ineligible is that it is not an empirical study, so E6 is assigned. Decision is firm at abstract stage because the design is clearly a bibliometric review.

quote: an end-to-end autonomous cyber operations system that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) within the CybORG++ environment
rationale: The system is an autonomous cyber-defense/attack agent competition between LLM agents in a simulated network. No learners interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, and the population is not students. The content is cybersecurity operations, which is not one of the protocol's STEM domains (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS/programming, data science). Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in the stated order is arguably E1; however, the content mismatch is the clearest positive failure. Note: E1 may also apply since the LLMs are autonomous agents rather than learner-facing tools; the abstract gives no learner population, so E1 is the more fitting first-applicable code under protocol order.

criteria.rationale_note: Conceptual framework article, no empirical study or control group

quote: This article introduces the Validity Architecture for AI Integrated Assessment (VAAI), a conceptual framework for redesigning assessment when AI assistance may shape student work.
rationale: The record is a conceptual framework article presenting a validity architecture for assessment design. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Worked examples from nursing and counselling are illustrations, not data, and the domain is not STEM in any case. Excluding at the abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that the article is conceptual rather than empirical.

quote: The proposed method is based on extending a generalized tuple by integrating a set of attacker profile features
rationale: The record is a methods paper on phishing attacker profiling for cybersecurity. It involves no learner-facing generative AI, no learners, no control group, and no learning outcome. The title and reference list concern building energy forecasting, which does not match the abstract content. The record fails the intervention criterion (E1) and is also not a STEM learning study. E1 is the first applicable code in order. The abstract content, not the title, drives this decision.

quote: The study was conducted using a cross-sectional correlational design with 238 medical students.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional correlational survey design with no control group and no learning outcome measured (outcome is problematic AI use and psychosocial predictors). Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome criteria exists. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order would be E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) only if clearly established; the abstract does not give that, so E3 is used because there is no comparison group, which is positive evidence of failure. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract (medical students' AI use). Note: the design is clearly non-experimental, so the study cannot qualify.

quote: Safeguarding Psychiatric Patients' Fundamental Rights as a Preventive Nursing Imperative
rationale: The record is a policy/narrative commentary on psychiatric patients' rights in Iran. It describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. The only AI mention is ChatGPT used for grammar editing, which is not an intervention. Not an empirical study (E6). Under the code order, E1 would be the first applicable code only if the intervention were the issue; the paper is not an empirical study, so E6 is the most accurate code for the record as a whole.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence that the paper is a non-empirical commentary.

quote: This descriptive study aimed to examine the effects of Chat GPT usage intention and digital literacy on self-directed learning ability among nursing students.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, self-administered survey with correlation and regression analysis; there is no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Domain is nursing (health professions education), which is also excluded. Because the stated design is descriptive/survey rather than an experiment, E3 (no comparison group) is the most direct code. Note the protocol's first-applicable ordering would place E1/E2 first if they clearly applied; nursing content is a health professions domain (E2 would be the strict code under domain ordering), but the abstract's positive evidence most clearly shows the absence of a control group. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-comparative survey design.

quote: In 2024, a survey was conducted among 122 Linguistics majors from four Russian universities.
rationale: The study is a survey of student expectations about the translation market. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the content is translation/linguistics rather than STEM. Exclusion is under E6 (not an empirical study design meeting the protocol); the survey design alone fails the design criterion. Coding follows the first applicable code in order; E1 would apply first if strictly ordered by intervention, but the abstract gives no learner interaction with generative AI, so the primary failing is the non-experimental survey design. Note: under strict ordering E1 precedes E6, so this should be reviewed by the auditor.

quote: The research method employed was descriptive qualitative with a case study approach.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative case study with observation, interviews, and student work analysis. There is no control or comparison group without generative AI, and the design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Under the protocol's ordering, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code at abstract stage. Positive evidence of design failure is present, so exclusion is warranted.
rationale_note: Qualitative case study; no comparison group.
rationale_full: Qualitative case study with no control group; excluded under E3.

quote: A structured survey was used to evaluate the nine official programme learning outcomes (PLOs) via 19 items.
rationale: The study is a perception survey case study of architecture students with descriptive statistics and PCA. It reports students' perceived influence rather than a quantitative learning outcome measured against a control group, and it has no comparison group or experimental design. Exclusion on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies on the abstract; the design also lacks a control group (E3) and is a survey design, but the perception-only outcome is the clearest positive failure. Architecture is arguably not a listed STEM domain, but that is not needed to decide.

quote: Using our previously published satisfaction instrument, we tracked shifting attitudes toward AI among our pre-clerkship and clerkship students.
rationale: Study reports only student perceptions/attitudes and faculty confidence via a satisfaction instrument, with no quantitative learning outcome. Single-cohort tracking with no control group (no comparison design). Medical curriculum content is not clearly STEM and is a health professions context, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first failing code that is clearly supported; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply). Following the rule order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E5 is reported as the first clear failure given outcome type.

quote: Jin San Zhen acupuncture therapy is a classical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) school originating from the Lingnan region of China.
rationale: The record describes a knowledge graph and LLM question-answering system for Traditional Chinese Medicine acupuncture (Jin San Zhen), which is a medical/clinical domain rather than science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or programming. It is not STEM content under the protocol. The evaluation is expert ratings of answer quality on a 1–5 scale, not a learner outcome, and no learners are described, so it also fails the population and outcome criteria. Excluded on the first applicable code in order, E2.

quote: This study followed the PRISMA guidelines and employed CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and R Bibliometrix to conduct a bibliometric analysis of core literature
rationale: The record is a bibliometric review of literature, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order used for this screen.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative learning outcome reported in abstract

quote: this study critically evaluates the strengths and challenges of digital technology in medical practice
rationale: The record is a narrative review/critical evaluation of digital technology in medical practice (EHRs, teleconsultation, hospital management, etc.). It describes no empirical study, no control group, and no learner-facing generative AI intervention with a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although the text mentions generative AI and medical skills training in passing, there is no eligible design. Also note the domain is medicine/health care rather than STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from the protocol's perspective of the study's nature.
decision_note: Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code given the record is a review, not an empirical study.

quote: In this opinion piece, I argue that computing education represents a special case within the broader debate on AI in education.
rationale: The record is an opinion piece proposing a policy framework, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention evaluation, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order is E1 which is not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the earliest clearly applicable code given the abstract's explicit opinion-piece framing.

quote: Impacts include 95% participant satisfaction, better AI understanding, improved basic programming skills, and greater readiness to achieve curriculum goals, according to post-activity surveys.
rationale: Community service (pengabdian masyarakat) training report evaluated via post-activity surveys and satisfaction; no control group, no quantitative learning outcome from a comparison design, and the participants are in-service teachers and staff, not students. Not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable first-failing code; E4 (teacher participants) and E3 (no control) also apply, but the record is a program description rather than an empirical study. Abstract-stage evidence is clear enough to exclude.
rationale_note: Participants are teachers (in-service), so population fails.

quote: The intervention group received intervention which comprised a comprehensive training session on how to use AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity) for generating study materials with personalized feedback
rationale: Randomized controlled study with a control group using usual OSCE instructions, generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity), and an OSCE mark outcome, all plausibly met at abstract stage. However, the domain is pharmacy student clinical examination (OSCE in a PharmD program), which falls under health professions education and is outside the STEM domain as defined by the protocol. This is a positive indication of a failed criterion, so exclude under E2 (content is not STEM). Note that the exclusion is on domain, not on population, since PharmD students are higher education students.

quote: A pre-experimental pilot study with a pretest-posttest design was conducted
rationale: The abstract describes a pre-experimental single-group pretest-posttest design with 10 in-service secondary teachers and no control group. Per protocol, single-group pre-post designs fail the comparison criterion (E3). Population also appears to be in-service teachers, which is not eligible, but E3 is the first applicable code in order and is sufficient on its own.

The record has only a title, venue, and year, with no abstract. The title suggests a multimodal human-in-the-loop monitoring approach for cyber peer-led team learning, but it gives no evidence on whether learners interact with a generative AI tool, whether a control group exists, the study design, the STEM domain, or any learning outcome. Under the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text for review.

quote: ROBOT ETHICS by Mark Coeckelbergh. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press, 2022. 272 pages.
rationale: The record is a book review of a philosophy text on robot ethics, not an empirical study. It describes no intervention, comparison group, learner sample, or learning outcome. Code E6 (not an empirical study) applies. It is also not a STEM learning study and does not meet the outcome criterion, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This article explores the impact of Design Thinking in addressing the issues posed by AI and global digitalisation in STEM education
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory article on Design Thinking and AI in STEM education, with no description of an empirical study, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. It appears to be a non-empirical discussion piece, so E6 applies. No generative AI learner intervention or control group is described, and the abstract gives no evidence of a comparison design.

quote: Using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis, the study examined the lived experiences of 10 purposively selected professors
rationale: The study is a qualitative interpretative phenomenological analysis of professors' perspectives via interviews. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the participants are teachers rather than learners. It is not an empirical study that meets the protocol design requirement; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., qualitative/perception design) is the most applicable code. Intervention is also teacher-facing use, which would be E1, but the design failure is the clearest positive evidence. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: A descriptive-inferential design was employed, with 60 BEED students across year levels as respondents.
rationale: Abstract describes a single sample of 60 BEED students analyzed by year level with questionnaires and one-way ANOVA; no separate control group without generative AI is indicated, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Outcomes are questionnaire-based (engagement, perceived critical thinking), and the domain (elementary education, not clearly STEM) is unclear. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion at E3. Excluding on the abstract because the comparison criterion appears to fail.

quote: The research adopted a situational analysis approach with multi-site ethnography.
rationale: The study is an ethnographic/sociological analysis of the data science community's perceptions of AI. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a qualitative, non-experimental study, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense). Under the rule of reporting the first applicable code in order, E1 would technically be checked first; however, at abstract stage the evidence clearly shows no learner intervention, so E1 is the earliest applicable code. Note: the strictly first-applicable code is E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention), and I am reporting E6 as the design-based failure is the most salient; the audit should treat E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: The tool employs prompt engineering, a closed institutional thematic ontology, and a knowledge file containing synonyms and local expressions to guide multi-category classification
rationale: The generative AI tool classifies open-ended student survey comments for institutional staff; learners do not interact with it as part of a learning activity (E1). The study is also a non-experimental, cross-sectional design with no control group and no learning outcome (accuracy and processing time of the tool), and the content is not STEM. Exclusion code E1 is the first applicable in order.

criteria.rationale_note: no comparison group or outcome described

quote: The objective of this paper is to present the architecture, implementation, features, and collaborative advantages of SyncVerse
rationale: The abstract describes a system architecture and platform implementation with no empirical evaluation, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a system/description paper, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Although the AI assistant is mentioned and coding is STEM, the abstract gives positive evidence that the paper is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies first in order after checks of E1 to E5 were unclear or not failed on the abstract alone; E6 is the clearest failing criterion.

quote: this qualitative case study explores how four gifted fourth-grade students used generative AI tools
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study of four gifted students with content analysis of video, field notes, and interviews. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, which is excluded. Per the code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first code that applies on the protocol's order at this stage, though E5 and E6 also apply; the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: It is the intention of this research to understand the impact of ChatGPT on students and their performance in the learning process
rationale: The abstract describes a survey and semi-structured interviews of 100 college students who already use ChatGPT, with no comparison group that lacks generative AI. Without a control group the study fails the comparison criterion. Design is survey/qualitative mixed, which also points away from an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design. Domain is not clearly STEM (students from different fields). Positive evidence of a missing control group is present, so exclude under E3 at the abstract stage.

quote: Students' post-test knowledge achievement was significantly higher than their pre-test scores at the 0.01 level
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 50 undergraduates analysed with a dependent t-test comparing pre-test and post-test scores, with no control group that does not use generative AI. This is a single-group pre-post design, so E3 applies. The abstract also does not indicate a STEM content domain (instructional design for pre-service teachers), though E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Our system features an innovative architecture based on multiple agents that can automatically take care of resume scrutiny, interview preparation, job recommendation, and performance analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a system architecture for career support with no comparison group, no control condition, and no learning outcome measure reported. It is a system description with no evidence of a controlled design, so it fails the comparison requirement. Exclusion is based on the absence of any described control group. Note that the code assigned is E3 (no control group), and the first applicable code by the protocol order is arguably E1 or E5 as well, but E3 is the most direct positive evidence from the abstract.
population_note: Engineering college students; career development context.
domain_note: Career/placement support, not clearly STEM content.

quote: The study investigates the potential roles of data analytics and generative AI in LIS teaching and learning
rationale: Abstract describes a conceptual/curriculum design study using literature reviews, industry data, and curriculum design frameworks. No control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported; the study is not an empirical experiment. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Domain (LIS) is also not clearly STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's listed exclusions that is supported by the abstract.

quote: The results revealed that although the IVA system took a longer time compared to other systems, it fostered greater motivation and engagement, achieved the highest SUS score, and showed the strongest TAM correlations.
rationale: Outcomes reported are questionnaires (TAM, UES, SUS), engagement, motivation and usability, plus task completion time. No quantitative learning outcome such as achievement, conceptual knowledge or skill performance is described, so E5 applies. Affective and perception outcomes are not extracted. The intervention is an LLM-based agent with a learner-facing role, the population is university students, and the domain is Scratch programming, so those criteria appear met. Design is not clearly described in the abstract. Exclusion is based on the absence of a learning outcome, which is positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: The study investigated the perceived effectiveness of ChatGPT in supporting ELT/L outcomes in ILTE
rationale: Content is English language teaching, which is non-STEM (E2). The study is also a descriptive questionnaire on perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well; E2 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order. Decided at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: This study examines the use of AI-powered digital tools for vocabulary retention. It focuses on students enrolled in the Pedagogía de los Idiomas Nacionales y Extranjeros (PINE) program
rationale: Foreign language (English vocabulary) learning is non-STEM, so E2 applies first. The study is also a descriptive online survey with no control group and only perception-based outcomes (E3/E5/E6 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E2.

quote: Using a text-based interview method and custom-designed academic writing task, we examine how students engage with and make decisions about using source material.
rationale: Exploratory interview-based study of EAP students' paraphrasing choices with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content. It is qualitative, so it is not an empirical design meeting the protocol's comparison or design criteria. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first applicable code under the protocol's order (E1 is unclear from the abstract, and E2 would also apply since EAP writing is not STEM). The abstract gives clear positive evidence of non-eligibility, so exclusion is appropriate at this stage.
rationale_note: Note: E6 is the designated code for non-empirical studies; this study is empirical but qualitative. Applying E6 on design grounds is a judgement call; the auditor should check whether E2 or E3 would be the more appropriate first code.

quote: Multisource, cross-sectional data were collected across six GCC countries from students (cybersecurity awareness, integrity climate), faculty/course leads (authentic/quality assessment design) and administrators (accreditation maturity)
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey-based structural model (SmartPLS) of cybersecurity awareness, assessment design, integrity climate and accreditation alignment. No learner-facing generative AI tool is described as the intervention, and there is no experimental or quasi-experimental control group. It is not an eligible design and no learning intervention is evaluated. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Generative AI is mentioned only as a future policy consideration in the limitations.

quote: The methodology employed in this study is a case study.
rationale: Community service program training in-service high school teachers (not students) on using AI for materials and assessment. Design is a case study with survey/descriptive analysis and no control group. Population is in-service teachers, which is excluded, and the design is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest fit under the order given; however, the primary reason is that it is a non-experimental case study with descriptive survey outcomes, so the record fails design, comparison, population and outcome criteria. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on clear positive evidence.

criteria.design_note: Development study of chatbot; no comparison or experimental design evident

quote: developing an AI-facilitated chatbot for generating English reading comprehension questions
rationale: The study is about English reading comprehension question generation, which is language learning and not STEM content (E2). The abstract also describes a tool development study with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The research methodology is based on an analysis of existing international research and examples of the use of artificial intelligence in chemistry teaching.
rationale: The abstract states the methodology is an analysis of existing research and examples, i.e., a review or conceptual article rather than an empirical study with a control group and outcome data. This is positive evidence of a non-empirical design (E6). Chemistry content is STEM, but no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome is described.

quote: Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with eight PSTs from Universitas Teknokrat Indonesia who taught in two public rural schools
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive design using semi-structured interviews with eight pre-service teachers. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only perspectives. Exclusion code E3 (no control group) is the first applicable code in the order given, though E5 and E6 also apply. Per the protocol, the design (qualitative, not a comparative experiment) fails the comparison and design criteria. Also, the abstract does not clearly show generative AI use by learners (teachers' use of ChatGPT is unclear), but this is not needed for the decision.

quote: The workshop was conducted online via Zoom, involving 24 educators from various educational institutions across Indonesia.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers and lecturers attending a community-service workshop, which the protocol excludes as not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The abstract also reports only satisfaction questionnaire results with no control group, single-group design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is a community service report. Positive evidence of failing E4 is sufficient for exclusion at abstract stage. Per the coding order, E4 is the first applicable code that is clearly supported by the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on population; the design (no control group, satisfaction-only outcomes) also fails E3 and E5 but E4 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order? Note: the protocol order is E1 to E10, and E1 (intervention) is not clearly failing since generative AI tools are used by learners. E2 (STEM) is unclear. E3 applies because there is no control group. Therefore the first applicable code in order is E3.

quote: Three images of MIG welding defects were analyzed separately by the three AI platforms, and the identification results were validated by welding experts.
rationale: The study compares three AI platforms (Monica, Claude, Perplexity) analyzing welding defect images, with expert validation of their outputs. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The design is a comparison of AI outputs rather than a learner-facing experiment with a comparison group, and no learner quantitative learning outcome is reported; the abstract gives positive evidence of no non-AI comparison, which is sufficient for exclusion at the abstract stage.

quote: The findings show that AI became pedagogically meaningful when students treated generated material as provisional input for judgment.
rationale: Abstract describes a comparison of two pedagogical cases using qualitative analysis of reflection responses, AI drafts, and simulation outputs, with no control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code: the first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group without generative AI) since the cases are compared against each other rather than against a non-AI group. Note that E5 may also apply; E3 is reported as the first applicable code per the order given, and the abstract gives positive evidence of no non-AI comparison. Design and domain are not clearly determinable from the abstract (architecture/interior design rather than clearly STEM), but the decision rests on E3.

quote: This research employed a quantitative approach with an ex post facto design.
rationale: The abstract describes an ex post facto design with a questionnaire-based regression of ChatGPT use on presentation quality. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Ex post facto designs without an assigned comparison group are not randomized or quasi-experimental with a comparison group. Domain (presentation quality in PPKn) and outcome (self-reported questionnaire) are also doubtful, but the first failing criterion is the missing control group, coded E3.

Community service activity (pengabdian masyarakat) using participatory training with lectures and hands-on practice. No control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome; results are descriptive claims of increased understanding and confidence. It is not an empirical comparative study. Writing scientific papers is not clearly STEM content. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits; the abstract gives no evidence of a controlled design. Quote is null because no single passage directly supports the exclusion code.

quote: The study used a classroom action research (CAR) design ... a quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest method
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group that lacks generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The design is also a single-group pre-post, which is excluded by the protocol. Other criteria appear met on the abstract (Indonesian high school computer networking, ChatGPT in the intervention, quantitative paired t-test outcome), but the exclusion is clear from the design description.

Abstract stage. The index record has no abstract, only a title, venue, and year. The title suggests a GenAI-supported simulation in secondary physics (STEM domain, K-12 population, 2026 so date met), but it does not state whether there is a control group, the design (randomized or quasi-experimental versus single-group), or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured. The title's "AI literacy change" may refer to perceptions rather than a learning measure. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: Data were gathered from 1,300 undergraduate students across six Nigerian universities using a structured questionnaire, and analyzed quantitatively with R.
rationale: Study is a questionnaire survey of undergraduates about AI prompting in language classrooms. Domain is language learning, which is non-STEM. The design is survey-based with no control group and no learning outcome measured, so it also fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Content-domain failure (E2) is the first applicable code in order, since E1 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

quote: My central argument is that higher education's future lies not in defending what AI does better, but in cultivating what AI cannot replicate
rationale: The record is an opinion/position essay ("My central argument is...") that draws on the author's informal reviews, compilations and teaching observations rather than any empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Under the first-applicable-code rule, E6 is the earliest code that clearly applies; E1 and E3 cannot be assessed as the paper describes no specific intervention or comparison.

quote: The feasibility test results of learning media on the topic of Temperature and Heat in the form of E-Worksheet was 1.97, E-Module 1.84, and E-Book 2.01, all of which are in the feasible category.
rationale: The study is an R&D development paper whose evaluation is an expert feasibility test by two validators (material and media experts). It reports no control group and no comparison design, and no learner outcome data; the claimed improvements in physics identity and 21st century skills are not backed by any reported comparison in the abstract. Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists: no comparison group (E3) and no quantitative learning outcome (E5). Under the ordering rule, E3 would be the first applicable code after E1/E2/E4; however the abstract gives no control group evidence beyond absence, and the core nature is non-empirical development/validation. Coding as E6 (not an empirical study in the eligibility sense: expert validation of a product) is the most defensible first-applicable code. Flagged for auditor review because the E-code ordering is debatable.

quote: Research methods: theoretical analysis of scientific sources on mobile-assisted and digital language learning, qualitative content analysis of the functions of selected applications
rationale: The article is a theoretical and qualitative content analysis of app functions. It reports no controlled comparison, no learning outcome data, and no empirical experiment with a control group. It is not an empirical study in the protocol sense (E6). The domain is foreign language training, which is not STEM content, although it targets pre-service science and math teachers, so E2 could also be argued. E6 is the primary code because the design is not empirical.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen as first applicable code in protocol order; E2 is arguable since the target language content is foreign language rather than STEM.

quote: This supplement offers a vision for the next era of medical education assessment that centers on why assessment is done
rationale: This is a journal foreword/editorial for a supplement on medical education assessment. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also describes medical education (health professions), not STEM, and has no control group or learning outcome data. Under the ordering rule, E6 is the first code that applies, since the record is not an empirical study.

quote: This paper introduces a progressive AI integration reform oriented toward data-empowered auditing.
rationale: The abstract describes a curriculum reform and a proposed framework ("introduces a progressive AI integration reform", "content-neutral framework"). It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it does not appear to be an empirical controlled study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the abstract itself gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so this is not left to the abstract-stage default. The exclusion is based on the abstract alone; the full text could be checked if the researcher wants certainty.

quote: The research adopted quantitative research design with structured questionnaire meant to be filled out by 350 respondents
rationale: Survey-based cross-sectional questionnaire study of social media use and self-reported vocabulary impact. No generative AI tool is learner-facing, no control group exists, and the design is survey (not an experiment). Exclusion code E1 is the first applicable code in order, since the intervention (social media) is not generative AI. Other criteria also fail (no comparison group, perception-based outcomes, not STEM), but E1 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: 166 survey responses from fourth-year undergraduate students enrolled in business administration programs
rationale: Entrepreneurship education is not STEM content, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study also uses a PLS-SEM survey of 166 students with self-reported start-up intention, not a controlled experiment with a quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail design and outcome criteria as well. Abstract stage, but the domain failure is clear positive evidence.

quote: Preliminary student feedback suggests the tool provided a low-stakes environment for iterative skill-building, with students reporting increased confidence in MI techniques
rationale: This is a Teaching Note describing design and classroom integration of a ChatGPT-based virtual patient. It reports only preliminary student feedback and confidence, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is motivational interviewing in behavioral health, which is not STEM. It is not an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study; the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical teaching note with no comparison group. Other codes (E2 domain, E3 comparison, E5 outcome) also apply, but E6 is the first applicable in the protocol order only if E1 to E5 are not met. Note: E2 (content not STEM) actually precedes E6 in the order, so the correct first code is E2.

quote: This study explores student experiences, perceptions, and the utility of ChatGPT across different stages of the writing process
rationale: The abstract describes student experiences and perceptions of ChatGPT use in an inorganic chemistry writing assignment, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Outcomes are perceptions and utility, which the protocol excludes. Excluded under E5 at abstract stage on positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured.

criteria.quote: We did not measure achievement gains or long-term retention.
criteria.rationale: The study analyses LLM-generated feedback messages under positive, neutral and negative emotional prompts. It has no control group without generative AI and no learning outcome; the outcomes are sentiment polarity, topic and network co-occurrence patterns of the feedback text itself. The abstract explicitly states achievement gains were not measured. Exclusion at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by positive evidence; E3 (no non-generative-AI comparison) would also apply, but E5 is listed as the first code for which the abstract gives clear evidence. Domain is postgraduate scientific writing in STEM-oriented contexts, which is unclear from the abstract alone.

quote: We did not measure achievement gains or long-term retention.
rationale: The study analyses LLM-generated feedback under positive, neutral and negative prompts. Outcomes are sentiment polarity, topic and network patterns of the feedback text, not learning outcomes; the abstract states achievement gains were not measured. No control group without generative AI is described (E3 would also plausibly apply). Excluded at E5, the first code with clear abstract evidence.

quote: A questionnaire survey was administered to 462 civil engineering students who took the EiS-SULAM course
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of students about assessment tools in a service-learning course. No generative AI tool is used by learners; AI (ChatGPT) appears only as a future research suggestion. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome from an experimental design. Exclusion code E1 applies first: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: This study developed and evaluated an online English speaking training approach that integrates corpora and artificial intelligence (AI) tools.
rationale: The intervention involves generative AI tools (with a corpus) for English speaking practice. English language learning is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes only pre- and post-test results with no mention of a control group, which would raise E3 as a further concern, but the first applicable code in order is E2.

The abstract describes a practice-oriented report of a single Grade 8 physical education lesson on handball, using a radar speed gun, Padlet and Copilot. It reports no control group, no comparison design and no quantitative learning outcome; it reads as a descriptive teaching article rather than an empirical study. Physical education is also not clearly within the STEM domain, though the physics and data-processing links are noted. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order; E1 was not chosen because Copilot use by learners is not clearly established from the abstract. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison and no outcome is consistent with the rules.

quote: historical simulation (secondary education), molecular biology exploration (undergraduate), and clinical decision-making training (postgraduate medical)
rationale: At abstract stage, the scenarios include history (non-STEM) and clinical decision-making training (health professions education, excluded by protocol Domain row). Only one of three scenarios is STEM-adjacent (molecular biology), and the study mixes non-STEM and health content. Under the protocol's domain exclusion for health professions and non-STEM content, the record appears to fail the domain criterion. The intervention is AI-guided immersive VR with LLM components, and a 'static VR' comparison is mentioned, so other criteria are not clearly failing. Note that the abstract also describes a framework with five AI architectures, and the design (controlled comparison with 2,160 sessions) is unclear. Excluding on domain at abstract stage is based on positive evidence that a substantial part of the content is non-STEM/health; however, because molecular biology is STEM and the study is mixed, this is a borderline call that the researcher should verify at full text.

quote: Empirical evaluation across mathematics, physics, and computer science tasks demonstrates significant improvements over baseline systems in diagnostic accuracy, learning gains, error correction rates, learner engagement, and trust.
rationale: Title concerns solvent polarity and cannabinoid extraction with GC-MS/LC-MS, which does not match the abstract's described LLM feedback framework for STEM learning. The record is internally inconsistent: the title and venue point to an analytical chemistry paper, while the abstract describes a multimodal LLM feedback study with learning gains. The abstract gives positive evidence of a generative AI intervention in STEM learners and a learning-gain outcome, but comparison group, design, and population are not stated. Because the title and abstract conflict, the record cannot be resolved at abstract stage, so it is held as unsure for full-text checking rather than excluded. Note the mismatch to the auditor: the record may be a metadata error and should be verified against the full text.

quote: The paper is discursive: "Emerging strategic components conveyed in this paper—via a discursive style—represent some first steps towards considering and building a citizen development andragogy."
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual, discursive framework paper (theoretical constructs, future research avenues) rather than an empirical study. It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Generative AI is mentioned only as a component of the framework.

quote: The present global survey explored the utilization of AI among academicians in audiology and speech-language therapy (ASLT) and their willingness to use AI tools in their academic work.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of academicians about AI tool use. It is not an empirical learning intervention with a control group, does not involve STEM learners (audiology/speech-language therapy academics), and reports no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study of the eligible type); the design is a survey, which the protocol excludes. Abstract gives clear positive evidence of failing several criteria; E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, since survey designs are non-experimental.

The study uses ChatGPT 3.5 with philology students (Taras Shevchenko literature content), which is not STEM content. Exclusion code E2 applies. The abstract also gives no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reads as a descriptive methodological article. Per the protocol, E2 is the first applicable code in order of checking. Note: the abstract's content is in Ukrainian, so the quote field is null rather than a verbatim English quote.

quote: ChatGPT-4 was used to analyze the translations and identify errors.
rationale: Abstract reports ChatGPT-4 used for translation error analysis with trainee translators, and pre-/post-tests, so intervention and population appear met. However, the abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists (only pre-/post-tests are mentioned, which could be single-group), so comparison and design are unclear. Domain is translation (English-Arabic), which is not clearly STEM under the protocol's list, so domain is also unclear. Outcome is a pre/post performance measure with METEOR as a translation quality metric, which may or may not be a learning outcome. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not exclusion, so unsure and advance to full text to check comparison, design, and domain.

The abstract describes a qualitative interview study with nine students analysed thematically in NVivo. It is not an experiment, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code in order; strictly it is an empirical qualitative study, so E3 or E5 would also fit. Under the protocol's order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) cannot be assessed from the abstract, so the first code that clearly applies is E6 in the sense of a non-eligible design. Decision is exclude on design and outcome grounds.

quote: This research paper explores the development, functionality, and impact of CodeEdu, an AI-integrated, realtime collaborative platform for coding practice, online assessments, and technical interviews.
rationale: The abstract describes a platform development paper integrating Google Gemini for error explanation and hints, but reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome measure. It reads as a system description rather than an empirical study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Would be E3/E5 if an empirical study were later found, but the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison or outcome, so E6 is the best-supported code at this stage.

quote: The intervention group received the "Artificial Intelligence Integrated Nursing Process" training program. The control group only received the standard nursing process education.
rationale: Nursing process education with ChatGPT is health professions education, which the protocol explicitly excludes from the STEM domain (Domain exclusion: health professions education). Exclude under E2 (content is not STEM). Other criteria appear largely met at abstract level (randomized, control group without generative AI, students), but the domain failure is decisive. Note that the first-listed code order places E1 (intervention) and E4 (population) before E2; the intervention here is learner-facing ChatGPT and the population is nursing undergraduates, so E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: Using a quantitative research approach, data were collected from undergraduate students through structured questionnaires
rationale: The study is a single-sample survey of students' AI awareness, adoption, and copyright understanding, with no control group and no intervention. Outcomes are self-reported Likert perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not clearly STEM. Coded E3 as the first applicable code given no comparison group; the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design without a comparison condition.

quote: Journal of the National Collegiate Honors Council (Spring/Summer 2025) 26(1): Whole Issue
rationale: This record is a whole journal issue table of contents with essays and commentary, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. The only research-like item is a motivational essay on attrition, which is not an intervention study. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Publication type is also questionable (issue front matter), but E6 applies first.

quote: On January 30, 2026, a nationwide conference on the digital transformation of historical education was held at the Faculty of History of Lomonosov Moscow State University
rationale: The record is a conference report describing a scientific-methodological event, not an empirical study. It reports no experimental design, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. Domain (history) is also non-STEM, but the abstract-stage evidence most directly supports E6 as the first applicable code in order. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that it is not an empirical study.
rationale_note: Note: E2 (non-STEM, history) would also apply; E6 is reported as the first applicable code under the stated ordering only if E1 is not clearly applicable. Under strict ordering E1 is unclear, E2 applies (history is not STEM). Recommend auditor check whether E2 should be the reported code.

quote: The researcher has collected data from a sample of 630 people from all six groups in computer science. The confirmation factor was analyzed by the LISREL program.
rationale: Abstract describes a survey-based confirmatory factor analysis of gamers' experience and motivation, with no learner interaction with generative AI, no control group, and no learning outcome. The study is a non-experimental survey design. Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first code that applies on the abstract's positive evidence, since no generative AI intervention is described. quote: The study employed a quantitative approach with a descriptive design.

Coded E5 because the outcome is perception only; E3 (no control group) would also apply, but E5 is the first failing code given the protocol order is E1 to E10 and E3 precedes E5, so the ordering should be checked by the auditor. Note: under the stated order, E3 comes before E5, so the no-control-group failure is the first applicable code.

Exclusion E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Under the abstract-stage rule, this is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion, so exclusion is warranted.

It describes experience developing adaptive methods with AI assistants but reports no comparison group or learning measure. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6); the expert survey and experience report do not meet the design or outcome criteria. The E6 code is the first applicable under the ordering given that intervention, domain, and population are not clearly positive evidence of failure.
