Domain is also unclear (scientific publication writing, not evidently STEM), but the design failure is decisive.

quote: Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa website berhasil berjalan stabil dengan waktu respons rata-rata 3–5 detik
rationale: This is an R&D software development paper. Testing covers unit, integration, system and user acceptance testing, with response time and usability-type results. There is no control group and no learning outcome measured on learners. Exclusion code E5 is used because no quantitative learning outcome is reported. The design criterion also appears unmet, since there is no comparison group. Under the abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of failure on outcome and comparison.
rationale_note: Exclude is based on positive evidence in the abstract: the study reports system performance and acceptance testing, not learning outcomes, and has no comparison group.

quote: The article provides an overview of the main application areas of generative AI models in education.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/overview article analyzing the definition of generative AI and its application areas. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome data. This is not an empirical study (E6). Earlier criteria could not be positively confirmed or refuted from the abstract alone, but E6 applies on positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: This position paper is to examine possible methods for incorporating ChatGPT into higher education.
rationale: The abstract describes itself as a position paper that examines possible methods and discusses papers on ChatGPT. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Under the rules, the abstract gives positive evidence that the design criterion fails, so the record is excluded.

criteria.design_note: survey-based quantitative study with perception measures and a t-test; no evident control group

quote: The study's findings show that AI significantly and favorably impacts pupils' development of digital literacy
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of students' use of AI and perceptions (perceived usefulness, ease of use, intention to use), with no described control group and no clear quantitative learning measure; the digital literacy claim rests on survey responses. Survey/perception-based design and outcomes point to E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Also the venue (International Journal of Religion) and the non-STEM framing (economic education) raise doubts, but the abstract does not clearly establish a non-STEM domain, so E2 is not applied. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the outcome is perception/survey-based and no comparison group is described.

quote: A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, with three teachers at SD Negeri 115 Pekanbaru selected as subjects through purposive sampling.
rationale: AI is used only by teachers to prepare teaching materials, which is E1 (not learner-facing). The design is a descriptive qualitative study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Those who approach mapping as a rhetorical tool rather than mere window dressing have much to offer, and the proof is in a number of digital maps that music scholars have produced over the past decade.
rationale: This is a critical review essay in a musicology journal about digital maps of music history. It is not an empirical study: there is no intervention with learners, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). It also does not involve generative AI (E1) and concerns music history, not STEM (E2). The record is not a fit on any criterion and is excluded on the first applicable code in order, which for an essay of this type is E1 if read strictly; however, the clearest and most fundamental failure is E6, since the piece is a non-empirical review. Note that the protocol says to report the first applicable code in order (E1 precedes E6). On the strict order, the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies first. The decision is exclusion; the code applied follows the ordering rule.

quote: The article theoretically substantiates and empirically verifies innovative strategies of higher education management under martial law and the post-war recovery of Ukraine.
rationale: Abstract describes a theoretical management-strategy paper using regulatory analysis, qualitative content analysis, teacher surveys and institutional reporting. No learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome are reported. Generative AI appears only as a future research direction. Excluded as not an empirical study of the eligibility design, with E6 as the most applicable code; E1 would also fit since no learner-facing generative AI is described.

quote: This article examines the challenges and prospects of legal informatics in the age of generative AI
rationale: The record is a theoretical/position article combining theoretical analysis with a course case study and exploratory student survey data. It reports no controlled comparison and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study with a comparison group. Legal informatics is also not clearly STEM content. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the abstract gives positive evidence that the design is non-experimental and the outcome is survey-based perception data.

quote: Analog horror is a type of short amateur cinema made and circulated on social media for free, primarily on YouTube
rationale: This is a humanities essay in Film Quarterly on the folklore of analog horror films. It is not an empirical study: there is no learner, no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the record describes no AI intervention at all, so E6 (not an empirical study) is the most accurate single code. Protocol order would otherwise put E1 first, so this is a judgment call that the auditor should check; the core reason is that the paper is a non-empirical critical essay. The record also contains garbled text, but no instruction to the reviewer was found, so injection is not suspected.

quote: Tumor boards are multidisciplinary teams of healthcare professionals that are working together to encompass the full spectrum of care around diagnosing, planning treatment, and advising outcomes for individual cancer patients.
rationale: The record is a narrative perspective/review article on data scientists in tumor boards for the Global South. It has no empirical design, no control group, no learners interacting with generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies. Domain is oncology/health, not STEM education, so E2 would also apply, but E6 comes first in the code order.

quote: This cross-sectional study was conducted on medical students in Sumatra from November 2024 to February 2025.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of medical students on AI readiness (MAIRS-MS questionnaire). There is no intervention with learners interacting with a generative AI tool and no control group; the design is correlational/survey. The topic is healthcare education, not STEM content. Outcome is a self-reported readiness score, not a learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's rules as the absence of a comparison group; the record also fails on design, domain, and outcome, but the code reported is E3 as the primary failure at this stage.

quote: The article addresses the issue of ensuring academic integrity in the context of distance learning
rationale: The abstract describes a system for automated generation and assessment of parameterized assignments and LTDL, with no learner-facing generative AI intervention. Generative AI is mentioned only as a cheating risk. No controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome is reported; the 'study' is a system design paper. Excluded at E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: "Esta investigación analizó la percepción sobre el uso pedagógico de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA)"
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods case study of perceptions and a concurrent triangulation design with no control or comparison group. Although the sample is secondary STEAM students and the domain is STEM, there is no separate non-generative-AI comparison group and the outcomes appear to be perception-based descriptive percentages, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion is made on E3 as the first applicable code for the absent control group; the case-study design also conflicts with the protocol's design criteria. Abstract evidence is positive for the absence of a control group, so exclusion is warranted even at the abstract stage.

criteria.stage_note: Generative AI used by researchers for data coding and analysis, not as a learner-facing tool

quote: The integration of Generative AI effectively reduced analysis time and enhanced precision in natural language processing
rationale: Generative AI is used by the researchers for systematic thematic coding and data synthesis, not as a tool learners interact with during the learning activity. The study is also descriptive, with no control group and no comparison design evident from the abstract. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Quote is from the abstract.

quote: The paper outlines the process of evolution and validation of the CTMM within university contexts, integrating generative artificial intelligence as a methodological tool to strengthen the assessment of computational thinking.
rationale: The abstract describes refinement of a measurement model for computational thinking, with generative AI used as a methodological/assessment support rather than as a learner-facing intervention. No control group or comparative quantitative learning outcome is described; the results concern model coherence and applicability. Positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome comparison supports exclusion under E5. Exclusion is based on the abstract only.

quote: The purpose of the article is to provide a comprehensive analysis of contemporary non-formal media education practices in Ukraine, online courses, and digital educational platforms
rationale: The paper is a descriptive analysis of Ukrainian non-formal media literacy projects and online courses. Its only empirical component is a student survey measuring perceptions and interest, not a quantitative learning outcome, and there is no control group. It has no generative-AI learner intervention and is not STEM content. The main reason for exclusion is that it is not an empirical study with a comparison group; the design is a content analysis and survey, so E6 applies as the first code in order that fits. Note that E1 would be the first in the code order if the intervention test were applied strictly, since no learner-facing generative AI tool is evaluated; the decision is exclude either way.

quote: We examined these relationships in an AI literacy activity ( N = 30) in which students interacted with two avatars of GPT (one RAG, one non-RAG)
rationale: Abstract describes GenAI (GPT) avatars with students in higher education, which is consistent with the intervention and population. However, the design appears to be two avatar conditions within one sample with no clear non-generative-AI control group, which suggests E3 may apply. The outcomes reported are mainly presence, intent, and expectations (perceptions and intent), and it is unclear whether any quantitative learning outcome exists. The domain (AI literacy) is not clearly STEM. Several criteria cannot be judged from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text to check the comparison, outcome, and domain.

quote: This paper examines the educational benefits and challenges based on survey results
rationale: The abstract describes a junior college VBA programming course using ChatGPT, which fits the intervention, population, and domain. However, the evaluation is based on survey results, which are perceptions and do not constitute a quantitative learning outcome. No control group or effect measure is mentioned. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Abstract-stage evidence is sufficient for this exclusion because the stated evaluation method is survey-only.

quote: The results of automated scoring performed by a publicly available base LLM-provided with items and scoring rubrics-were then compared with those obtained after fine-tuning.
rationale: The study fine-tunes an LLM to score student constructed responses. The generative AI is used by the researchers for automated scoring, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Under E1 the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. No control group of learners without generative AI is described, and the design is a model-performance comparison, so E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: The research methodology employed in this study involved the adaptation of the Survey of Attitudes toward Statistics (SATS-36) to pre-service teachers
rationale: The study is a survey-based psychometric validation of the SATS-36 with attitudes as the outcome. No generative AI tool is involved, no learner-facing intervention or control group exists, and attitudes are affective outcomes, not learning measures. Exclusion under E1 as the first applicable code (no learner-facing generative AI intervention).

quote: This article focuses on the AutoScholar Advisor system, a system that continuously analyzes data using modern methods from the fields of artificial intelligence (AI), data science, and statistics.
rationale: Abstract describes a conceptual/position article about an advising system with case studies; no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome is reported, and no empirical comparative design is indicated. The abstract gives positive evidence that the record is not an empirical comparative study (E6). STEM content and generative nature of the system are not clearly stated, but the exclusion rests on E6 as the first applicable code.

quote: This embedded qualitative multiple-case study explored how university teachers of English as a Foreign Language in Vietnam reasoned professionally about generative artificial intelligence.
rationale: The record is a qualitative multiple-case study of teachers' professional reasoning, with interviews and document analysis. It is not an empirical comparative study with a control group, has no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is EFL (non-STEM) and the participants are teachers rather than students. Excluded at the first applicable code in order; E1 is unclear from the abstract, but E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., a qualitative design outside the eligible designs) is the clearest applicable reason. Abstract-stage positive evidence supports exclusion.

quote: Dr Sigler gave an example used at her institution: A Chatbot was used to simulate typical interactions, such as the antimicrobial stewardship pager
rationale: This record is a conference symposium-style snapshot summary (Infectious Diseases in Clinical Practice) of multiple clinical trials and sessions, not an empirical study of learners using generative AI. The only AI-education content is a presenter's description of a chatbot example and a discussion, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not a journal article reporting an eligible study. Coded E1 as the first applicable exclusion, since the AI component is not an evaluated learner-facing generative AI intervention; the record also lacks any comparison group, STEM content, and learning outcome. Injection not suspected.

The record is a sentiment analysis of public X (Twitter) posts about ChatGPT using a Naive Bayes classifier. It has no learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity, no control group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study of learners. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study of the protocol type); the sentiment analysis of social media posts does not meet the design requirement. Using the first applicable code in order would be E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), since the study does not involve learners interacting with a generative AI tool. Given the ordering rule, E1 is the first code that applies, so the exclusion code should be E1 rather than E6.

The abstract describes NLP classifiers for author attribution and detection of machine-generated text (Gemini used only to create datasets). Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, and there is no learning intervention or control group. This is not a learner-facing generative AI study, so E1 applies. Exclusion is clear from the abstract: the study is a detection/attribution method evaluation, not an intervention study.

quote: In this paper, we outline central principles from the theory, with particular attention to how they have been brought into the L2 field.
rationale: The record is a theoretical/review article on Sociocultural Theory and corpus-based concept-based language instruction. It describes itself as outlining principles and suggesting future research; it reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative outcome. Generative AI appears only as a future research direction. It is not an empirical study (E6). Content is also L2 English/Spanish language learning, which is non-STEM (E2), but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by protocol... note: E1 is checked first; the generative AI element is only prospective, not a learner-facing intervention in the study, so E1 applies first in strict order. Given the strict code order, the first applicable code is E1.

quote: The materials that comprise this framework consist of a set of learning objectives, some course descriptions for core courses, and a flexible course outline for an Introduction to Science course
rationale: The record describes a curriculum framework/resource (learning objectives, course outline) for an open science minor, not an empirical study. It has no comparison group, no generative AI intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also labeled "Made without GenAI". Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E1 and E3 would also apply on the abstract evidence.

rationale: The study is a community service activity with 19 in-service teachers and education staff, which the protocol excludes as non-student participants (E4). quote: Nearpeer anatomy tutoring sessions were very popular among McGill University medical students (80% turnout).

Item 01 (near-peer anatomy tutoring) reports only attendance and satisfaction Likert scores, with no generative AI, no control group, and no learning outcome. Excluded on E6 as not an empirical study; the record also shows no generative AI intervention or comparison group, so further criteria are not met.

quote: We advocate a shift from content delivery to concept integration anchored in clinical reasoning and data literacy.

rationale_note: Exclusion based on abstract alone; positive evidence of non-empirical commentary.

quote: Methodologically, a qualitative bibliographic study was conducted based on academic publications related to Artificial Intelligence, digital technologies, and Distance Education.
rationale: The record is a qualitative bibliographic (literature) study, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no SMD-computable data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract but are moot given the design.

quote: The platform has two main parts: one that creates quizzes and another that generates study materials.
rationale: This is a platform/system description. The abstract states that evaluation was "based on iterative development testing rather than a formally controlled evaluation," with no control group, so there is no comparison group without generative AI (E3). It also reports no learning outcome (E5 would also apply), but E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order is E3 before E5. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a missing control group and no controlled evaluation.

quote: We present an enterprise platform architecture for AI-based mental health intelligence and early intervention systems‚ from the standpoint of large-scale distributed systems engineering‚ rather than a new class of clinical algorithms․
rationale: The paper presents a conceptual architecture evaluated only qualitatively against non-functional requirements. It is not an empirical study, has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the content is mental health rather than STEM. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol's conceptual order, with positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: Researchers surveyed 31 students between August and December 2025 to understand what they really think about tools such as ChatGPT and similar programs.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of perceptions of 31 students with no experimental or control group and no learning outcome measured. Design and outcome criteria clearly fail, so the record is excluded. Under the protocol's code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, so E5 is the first clearly applicable code; the study is also not an experiment, which the design criterion would catch at full text. Population (business management engineering students) and STEM domain are not clearly established but are not the deciding factors.

quote: This paper examines the transformative potential of AI-augmented education observing human–AI collaboration
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/discussion paper that examines potential benefits and challenges and proposes recommendations. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical design in the abstract.

quote: It is a qualitative research paper that examines how speech acts are built in ESL environment
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study (interpretivist, DCTs, interviews, thematic analysis) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study that meets the design requirements; no quantitative comparison is described. Also the domain is ESL/pragmatics, which is non-STEM (E2 would apply too), but the first applicable code in order is E1 check: intervention is ChatGPT interaction (met), then E2 applies because content is language learning, not STEM. Given the rule to report the first applicable code in order, the correct code is E2 since it precedes E3 through E6.

quote: The resulting Minimum Viable Product (MVP) was evaluated by a target population, validating its functionality and pedagogical value. The results showed high acceptance
rationale: The record describes a web application (LogicLoop) with an LLM feedback component for programming, which meets the intervention and domain criteria. However, the evaluation reported is a user-acceptance evaluation of an MVP, with no described control group and no quantitative learning outcome (results concern acceptance, speed, effectiveness and confidence). It is a development/evaluation report rather than a comparative empirical study with a learning outcome, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 is applied as the most fundamental failure (not an empirical comparative study); the abstract gives positive evidence of no control group and perception-only outcomes.

quote: involving 53 teachers from various subjects

Outcomes are descriptive self-report and competence percentages, not a comparative quantitative learning measure.

quote: Marking the Charter's anniversary (Thomas et al. 2025) means retooling its tenets for the world we live in now.
rationale: The record is a position/commentary article in Health Promotion International reflecting on the Ottawa Charter's 40th anniversary. It describes no empirical study, no learners, no generative AI intervention, and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Domain and population are not applicable to this text. No injection attempt observed.
rationale_note: Exclusion code E6 applied as first applicable in order; E1 would be arguable but the paper has no learner-facing intervention at all, so E6 is the primary reason.

quote: A user satisfaction evaluation using the Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) method with 54 respondents yielded a score of 89.34%
rationale: Abstract describes a RAG-based academic information chatbot for university administrative services. Not a learning activity and not STEM content. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clearly applicable code in a reasonable reading; the design also shows no comparison group (E3) and the content is administrative rather than STEM (E2).
