quote: Despite growing interest in AI-supported language learning, little research has examined chatbot use specifically as a structured pre-exchange preparation tool for reducing FLA
rationale: The study concerns foreign language learning and intercultural exchange (non-STEM content), so E2 applies first in the code order. It also shows no control group (single-cohort survey of 148 students) and only perception-based outcomes (confidence, anxiety, willingness to communicate, self-reported), which would fail E3 and E5 as well, but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: A structured questionnaire was distributed to 300 students. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, and moderation analysis.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire on technology acceptance (TAM/IS success model). It reports perceptions and intention to use, not a quantitative learning outcome, and has no control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of failure exists on comparison, design (survey, correlational), and outcome criteria. Exclusion uses E5 as the first applicable code in the stated order is E3 (no control group) ... see note: E3 is checked before E5 in the listed order, so the code should be E3 instead.

quote: Teaching uses hollowed-out map silhouettes as creative medium. Practice is documented qualitatively across two cycles.
rationale: The intervention is paper-based art workshops with no generative AI tool used by learners. The study is a qualitative action-research design over two cycles with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Art education is also not STEM. E1 is the first applicable code in protocol order, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. The record's acknowledgments mention generative AI only as a funding project title, not as an intervention.

quote: This study employed an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design (Creswell & Clark, 2018). Phase one involved surveying ELMC completers and non-completers.
rationale: The record is a survey and focus-group mixed-methods study of perceived supports and barriers for an emergent literacy micro-credential. It has no control group, no generative AI learner intervention (the GPT-4o use was for qualitative transcript analysis by researchers), no quantitative learning outcome, and the content is early literacy rather than STEM. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would apply first; the record is also clearly not an empirical learning-outcome study. Coding as E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an intervention evaluation) is a judgment call; E1 is arguably the first applicable code under strict ordering. Auditor should consider whether E1 is preferred.

quote: Kajian awal sorotan literatur sistematik ini dijalankan bagi menyintesis kajian empirikal berkaitan persepsi, penerimaan, manfaat, dan cabaran penggunaan GenAI dalam pendidikan tinggi.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review (secondary synthesis of 43 articles, thematic synthesis), not an empirical primary study. It therefore fails E6 (not an empirical study). It also does not report its own experimental comparison group or quantitative learning outcome; it synthesizes perceptions, acceptance, benefits and challenges. Journal-article status is not contested here. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract.

quote: It proposes the German AI Assisted Instructional Design and Evaluation framework, or G-AIDE, a six-stage process
rationale: The abstract is a position/conceptual article that proposes a framework and analyzes it; it reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Also, AI is used by teachers to design materials rather than by learners, which points to E1, but E6 is the primary, unambiguous failure at abstract level. No comparison or outcome data are described.

quote: This research investigates the effectiveness of ChatGPT 3.5, ChatGPT 4.0 by OpenAI, and Chatbot Bing by Microsoft in solving statistical exam-type problems in the educational setting.
rationale: Generative AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Bing) and statistics content, with undergraduate engineering students. The abstract describes error rates of the chatbots themselves in solving problems, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group that does not use generative AI. No comparison group or learning outcome for students is evident. Design and comparison are not described, so the record cannot be excluded at the abstract stage; it needs full-text review to check whether a non-AI comparison exists and whether a learning outcome is measured.

quote: The research adopted a quantitative correlational design in which a sample of 200 postgraduate students was selected through convenience sampling technique.
rationale: The abstract describes a quantitative correlational survey design with no separate control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail on positive evidence. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing code in order. The study also does not appear to be an experiment, and the domain (general academic integrity in education, not clearly STEM) is unclear. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the correlational design is positively stated.

quote: The laboratory experience with ChatGPT was structured in three phases: an analysis of students' perceptions of AI, training on the basic principles of AI, and finally, an educational design activity using artificial intelligence systems.
rationale: Abstract describes a ChatGPT laboratory for socio-pedagogical educator students with perceptions analysis and an educational design activity. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is described, and the content (socio-pedagogical/socio-healthcare education) does not appear to be STEM. Positive evidence of a failing criterion exists: the only measured element is perceptions, and no comparison group is mentioned. Excluded at the first failing code in order; E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is learner-facing. E2 (non-STEM) is also a plausible failure, but the stronger basis is the absence of a quantitative learning outcome, so E5 is given.

quote: Using collaborative autoethnography, we document our experiences across Australian universities and situate them within neoliberalism's colonization of higher education.
rationale: The paper is a critical/theoretical essay built on collaborative autoethnography and argument; it is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Social work is also not STEM content, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order is E1 or E2 at face value; the abstract does not give a clear learner-facing GenAI intervention, so the primary and clearest failure is E6 as the study is not empirical in the quantitative sense the protocol requires. The abstract gives no comparison group or quantitative outcome.

quote: Based on the survey, 97% of respondents reported that MYResearchMap helped them identify new research ideas
rationale: Abstract describes development and evaluation of a system with survey-based perceptions of respondents (students, lecturers, librarians). No control group or comparison condition is described, and outcomes are perceptions/satisfaction rather than a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (no control group) and of a non-learning outcome, so excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in order is a missing control group; E5 could also apply. Coded E3 as the primary failure.

quote: Implemented in an introductory programming course (N = 60) at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin, Malaysia, the study employed a mixed-methods, quasi-experimental pre/post design.
rationale: Abstract describes a programming course (STEM, higher education) using GenAI (ChatGPT) with a quasi-experimental pre/post design. However, the abstract does not mention a separate control group, so comparison is unclear; the design may be single-group pre-post, which would be E3. Outcomes include self-efficacy (affective, not extracted) and an assessment of evaluating GenAI outputs, so a quantitative learning outcome is possibly present but unclear. Rule 2 favors advancing to full text rather than excluding on missing information.

quote: Using a qualitative case study approach, the research investigates how final-year students incorporate AI tools such as ChatGPT, Quillbot, and Claude AI throughout the thesis development process
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study based on semi-structured interviews with twelve students, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study meeting the design criteria. Content is English language education thesis writing, which is not STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense; qualitative design), the first code that clearly applies in the order given is E2 for content, but the qualitative design is the decisive failure; reporting the first applicable code in order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is used to reflect the qualitative, non-quantitative design.

quote: This quantitative descriptive–correlational study examined whether awareness of and compliance with an institutional AI Use Policy are associated with lower dependency on AI tools
rationale: Correlational survey design with no experimental or quasi-experimental control group that lacks generative AI; the study compares students by policy awareness/compliance. Outcome is AI dependency (a self-report index), not a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is the first clearly applicable code in the protocol order that the abstract supports (no comparison group without generative AI). Note that the design itself also fails the Design criterion, so this is a clear exclude at abstract stage.

quote: This paper synthesizes four recent empirical studies—a randomized controlled trial of AI in high-school mathematics, a field experiment with elite management consultants, a classroom trial of an AI physics tutor, and a neurophysiological study of AIassisted writing
rationale: The record is a synthesis/position paper that argues a conceptual framework from four previously published studies rather than reporting its own empirical study. It is not an empirical study of the protocol's design types, so it fails E6. Published 2026, so the date criterion is met; no other exclusion is needed.

quote: Evaluated on real-world data validated by 10 expert AEP teachers, the multi-agent AI system successfully retrieved verified local context and achieved 73.5% zero-shot accuracy
rationale: The abstract describes a system architecture (data warehouse/knowledge graph) evaluated by expert teacher validation and a zero-shot accuracy figure. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no learner outcome measure, so it does not appear to be an empirical controlled study. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the best fit, though the abstract is not fully explicit; the judgement is based on the absence of any comparison design. Note that the rule at abstract stage asks for positive evidence, and the abstract does give positive evidence of a system-evaluation design without a control group.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on design evidence; quote refers to evaluation method.

quote: Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study.
rationale: This is a personal reflection/commentary by a rheumatologist and graduate student, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome. The record states that no new data were created or analyzed. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). It is also not a STEM learning intervention study.

quote: This is a perspective paper. The viewpoint analysis is based on a review of formal academic and training programs
rationale: The record is a perspective/viewpoint paper, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Clinical informatics education is also health-related, which further argues against eligibility, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Exclusion code follows protocol order; E1 and E2 were not clearly established from the abstract alone, but E6 is decisive.

quote: The study found a significant increase in GenAI use among participants.
rationale: The participants are higher education faculty engaged in professional development, not students, so the population criterion fails (E4). The content is faculty course design and GenAI use, not a STEM learning domain, and the reported outcomes are self-reported use, time savings, and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. No control group is mentioned. Under the rule for abstract-stage decisions, the population failure is positive evidence, so exclusion is justified on E4, the first applicable code in the protocol's order.

quote: This paper presents KOA (Knowledge Optimization Assistant), an AI-integrated web-based productivity intelligence platform designed to bridge this gap.
rationale: The abstract describes a platform/architecture paper with no mention of a control group, comparison condition, or experimental design. It reports no learning outcome data, only platform design and deployment. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present (no comparison described, system-description paper), so exclude at abstract stage under E3 as the first applicable code is not clearly established but the design lacks any comparison. Note: the abstract gives no evidence of an empirical comparison, so E3 is the most defensible code.
decision_note: Exclusion based on absence of any comparison group; the abstract is a system description with no evaluation described.

quote: Five successive attempts of each chatbot to answer 200 United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE)-style questions were evaluated based on accuracy, relevance, and comprehensiveness.
rationale: The study compares chatbots' accuracy on MCQs against student averages, not a learner-facing intervention with a separate control group. Chatbots answered the questions themselves; there is no control group of learners without generative AI, so E3 applies. Students' scores serve as a benchmark, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Also, the content is medical neuroscience, which may fall outside the STEM domain per the protocol's exclusion of health professions education. Exclusion on E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported.

quote: the authors used Gemini (Google) in order to translate the manuscript from Vietnamese to English and to improve the grammatical quality and readability of the text.
rationale: This is a cross-sectional KAP survey of primary school students on myopia prevention. Generative AI appears only as a writing aid used by the authors, not as a learner-facing intervention. The study has no intervention or control group, so it is not an experiment. It is also not STEM content and reports knowledge/practice survey measures rather than a learning outcome from an intervention. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1, since no learner-facing generative AI is present.

quote: "systematic narrative hybrid review of 19 open-access studies"
rationale: The record is a literature review (systematic narrative hybrid review), not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also addresses EFL writing, which is non-STEM content. Its perception focus provides no quantitative learning outcome. The review design gives no control group. Per the ordering rule, E6 is reported first as the applicable code because it is the first criterion that clearly fails in the protocol's code order that is not E1 or E2; the abstract gives no evidence of learner-facing generative AI in a STEM study, so the E2 non-STEM content issue is also present and noted.

quote: استخدمت الدراسة المنهج المزجي، حيث شارك 21 طالبًا في الجزء الكمي
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods study of 21 students' perceptions measured by questionnaire and interviews. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the quantitative data are perception-based rather than a learning outcome. Exclusion under E3 (no control group) is the first applicable code in the protocol order, supported by the design description. Decision is based on positive evidence in the abstract that no comparison group exists.
quote_text: استخدمت الدراسة المنهج المزجي، حيث شارك 21 طالبًا في الجزء الكمي
quote_translation: The study used a mixed-methods approach, with 21 students in the quantitative part.

quote: Two human evaluators compare the automatically generated LOs to the human-crafted ones in terms of their alignment with course goals, meeting the SMART criteria, mutual overlap, and appropriateness of ordering.
rationale: The study compares LLM-generated learning objectives with instructor-authored ones, rated by two evaluators on quality dimensions. There is no learner-facing use of the LLM and no learner quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, or skill performance). Outcomes are expert ratings of the artefacts, not learning measures. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Note that E1 could also arguably apply since the LLM is used by instructors to design curricula, not by learners; E5 is reported here as the outcome fails regardless. Abstract-stage exclusion is based on positive evidence that the outcome is not a learning measure.
decision_note: Protocol order would place E1 first: the LLM is used for curriculum design by educators, not learner-facing. Strictly, the first applicable code is E1.

quote: My career, so far, has spanned the birth, childhood, adolescence, and maturity of a group of procedures and techniques based on the simple idea of passing catheters and other devices across the major and minor duodenal papillae
rationale: The record is a personal historical essay on ERCP (a series-style history piece), not an empirical study. It describes no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E1 would also apply since there is no generative AI, but E6 reflects the record type. Positive evidence of failure is clear from the content, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: A quantitative predictive correlational design was employed with 143 pre-service special education teachers (SETs)
rationale: The study is a predictive correlational design with no control group, so no comparison without generative AI exists (E3). It also measures ChatGPT use intensity and self-efficacy/stress perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and the content (teaching students with disabilities) is not STEM. E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract; the design is correlational, which would also fail the design criterion.

quote: Investigating the Psychological Impact of Corrective Feedback on ESL Students' Language Anxiety
rationale: The study concerns corrective feedback (human teacher feedback types) on English as a Second Language anxiety, which is non-STEM content (language learning). The abstract gives no generative AI intervention; the AI references in the reference list are not the study's intervention. Fails the domain criterion (E2), and also the intervention criterion is not supported by the abstract. Per the protocol's code order, E1 would come first if intervention failure were the primary issue; however, the abstract's positive evidence of a non-STEM domain is clear. Also the outcome is affective (anxiety), which the protocol excludes from extraction. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.
exclusion_code_note: E1 arguably applies first since no learner-facing generative AI is described; reporting E2 per the stronger positive evidence.

quote: Using an AI-generated short survey to gather quantitative and qualitative data through a discussion exercise, 126 undergraduates with four different professors were asked to share their answers and views.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of perceptions and familiarity with AI tools among 126 undergraduates, with no control group, no learning outcome, and no experimental design. It is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. Domain is not STEM-specific either. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible design) is the most applicable; the design is a descriptive survey. Note that the first applicable code in order would strictly be E1 or E2 if those were clearly met, but the abstract gives positive evidence only of a perception survey without a comparison group, so E6 is assigned.

quote: This paper examines how academic integrity is conceptualized and practiced in Swedish higher education in the context of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT.
rationale: The abstract describes a policy and phenomenographic analysis of student reflections on AI use, with no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study eligible under the protocol. Domain is not STEM (academic writing course). Excluded at E6 as a non-experimental, conceptual/qualitative paper; the first applicable code in order would be E1 or E2, but the abstract does not give clear positive evidence for those, so E6 best reflects the design. Positive evidence of qualitative design supports E6.

quote: Impacts of virtual reality-aided physical training on the balance ability and energy expenditure of children with moderate intellectual disability
rationale: The record is a retraction notice that bundles many unrelated articles. The only item matching the title is a virtual reality physical training study in children with intellectual disability. It involves no generative AI tool and is not STEM content. Its abstract gives no evidence of a generative AI intervention. Per the protocol's first-applicable code order, E1 applies: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. The study is also a retracted record, which is a further reason to exclude.
rationale_note: Retraction notice; the listed article is a VR physical-training study, not generative AI.

quote: Students completed reflections on the value of the assignments and provided recommendations for using ChatGPT in the future.
rationale: Content is school psychology counseling skills training, not STEM (E2), so it fails the domain criterion first. The abstract also describes a case study with student reflections and no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so comparison, design, and outcome criteria appear unmet as well. The first applicable code in order is E2.

criteria.domain_note: career guidance for blockchain/AI/data science students; STEM-adjacent but not clearly learning content

quote: This paper introduces an AI-powered career development tool made for students and recent graduates.
rationale: The abstract describes a Gemini-based multi-agent career development tool (resume building, practice interviews, learning plans) with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. It is a system description; the abstract gives positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured. Excluded at E5 (first applicable code in order, since intervention is generative AI and population is higher education; E1 and E4 do not clearly apply). Design and comparison are not described, so the exclusion rests on the absence of any outcome measure.

quote: We propose a multi-layered integration strategy for higher education encompassing: 1) Foundational AI literacy modules for all business students
rationale: The paper is a curricular and policy framework proposal, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome data. Domain is financial planning, which is not clearly STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first code that applies.

quote: This study fills the gap by investigating the adoption, perceptions, and ethical implications of AI tools among rural Philippine college students through a sequential explanatory mixed-method cross-section survey approach
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of perceptions and adoption of AI tools with no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is not an empirical intervention study meeting the design criteria. E6 is the first applicable code given the survey design (E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and E3/E5 would also apply but E6 reflects the core design failure). Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the explicit survey design and perception-only outcomes.

quote: ChatGPT-4o simulated realistic patient interactions requiring competencies in clinical case management; problem-solving, clinical reasoning, crisis management.
rationale: The design is a single-group, mixed-methods study (self-assessment survey, interviews, observations) of 21 medical interns using ChatGPT-4o as a virtual standardised patient. No control group without generative AI is described, so the comparison criterion fails. The study is also not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison design. Domain is clinical case management in medicine, which falls under health professions education and is excluded by the protocol. Exclusion is based on E3 as the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's comparison failure at abstract stage; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: The topic of this paper is feedback literacy which emanates from research within the field of higher education pedagogy, and has been taken up enthusiastically within L2 writing and English for Academic Purposes (EAP).
rationale: The abstract is a conceptual/position-style introduction to feedback literacy in applied linguistics and TESOL. It describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. The content concerns language/EAP writing rather than STEM, which also argues against eligibility. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order; E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply, but E6 is earlier in the order only if considered first. Under the protocol order, E1 is not evidenced, E2 is the first content-based failure: the paper is about language learning/EAP, which is non-STEM. Note: the code order requires the first applicable code, so E2 should be considered.

quote: Qualitative analyses of prompts and evaluations were combined with quantitative comparisons across factor levels.
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods study with a survey of acceptance factors and qualitative analysis of prompts. There is no control group without generative AI and no learning outcome measure; the quantitative comparisons are across perception-factor levels within a single group. Design is correlational/survey-based, so the comparison and design criteria fail, and the outcome is perceptions/usage rather than learning. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of missing comparison group and non-learning outcomes. Code E3 is the first applicable in order (E1 is unclear since the intervention is teacher-side lesson design, but E3 is the clearest failing criterion).

quote: A cross-sectional study was conducted over two months (June and July 2024) at a rural medical college in Southern Andhra Pradesh.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional KAP survey with no control group and no comparison of generative AI use against a non-AI condition, so the comparison and design criteria fail. It also reports only knowledge, attitude, and practice (self-reported usage and perceptions), with no quantitative learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order when assessed against the protocol's control-group requirement; E5 would also apply. Exclusion is clear at the abstract stage.

quote: The research design used was quantitative cross-sectional with a sample of 300 university students
rationale: The study is a quantitative cross-sectional correlational survey-style design using scales (AI literacy, AI dependency, procrastination). It has no intervention arm, no control group, and no learning outcome; it is not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the best fit, but per the protocol order the design failure makes it non-eligible; the empirical design is correlational, which the protocol excludes under Design. Among codes, E3 (no control group) is the closest structural failure, but the abstract shows a correlational survey rather than a comparison design. Flagging for auditor review: the strongest reason is design (correlational/survey), and no code exactly matches; E6 is applied as the nearest fit.
decision_note: Also the outcome is procrastination (affective/behavioral self-report), not learning.

quote: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is significantly transforming education across K-12, higher education, and lifelong learning through three key dimensions
rationale: The abstract is a conceptual/framework overview ("AI Competency Framework for Teachers") that describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measure. It does not report data or a design, so it is not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 on positive evidence of a non-empirical (conceptual) paper.

quote: This paper presents the results of a survey of 46 first- and second-year graduates of the educational program "Foreign Language: Two Foreign Languages" on the use of ChatGPT.
rationale: Abstract describes a literature review plus a survey of 46 students on ChatGPT use. There is no control group, no learning outcome measured quantitatively, and the content is foreign language learning rather than STEM. The design is a survey and theoretical review, not an empirical experiment, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order. Note that E1 through E5 are also not clearly satisfied; E6 is the most direct reason based on the abstract alone. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because positive evidence of a non-empirical design and non-STEM content is present.

quote: This article presents reflections of two research methodologists who supervise students in a nursing science PhD program
rationale: The record is a reflective commentary by two methodologists on dissertation supervision. It is not an empirical study: there is no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI appears only as a risk mentioned in the results. Under the rule that codes are applied in order, E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention) would technically apply first, but the primary reason for exclusion is that the article is not empirical, so E6 is reported here. Exclusion is clear at abstract stage.

quote: Based on the research findings, 20 of the 21 questions generated by ChatGPT AI are valid.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT to generate biology multiple-choice questions, which students answer as an assessment. Generative AI is not used as a learner-facing learning activity; the abstract describes question validity, reliability, and student perceptions. There is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome (only psychometric properties of the questions and perception percentages), and the design is not an experiment. E1 applies first: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI as a learning activity. Domain (biology) is also not clearly STEM, but E1 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: Using an integrative secondary evidence synthesis, the study triangulates recent official statistics, large-scale faculty and institutional surveys, peer-reviewed studies, and policy frameworks published between 2020 and 2025.
rationale: The paper is a conceptual framework built on an integrative secondary evidence synthesis, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 would also plausibly apply, but the study is not an empirical study at all, so E6 is the primary reason. Faculty-focused, so not a student population.

criteria.population_note: focus is higher education teachers' digital competence, not students

quote: The article describes the study of the state of formation of digital competence of teachers of a higher education institution.
rationale: The abstract is a theoretical and descriptive article about digital transformation and teachers' digital competence. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome for students. It is not an empirical comparative study. Generative AI (ChatGPT) appears only as one example among many digital resources. Excluded at the first applicable code, E6 (not an empirical study). Population is also not students, but E6 is the first code that applies in order of the protocol's checks.
rationale_note: Population (teachers, not students) would also fail; E4 would come after E1-E3 in order, and E1/E2/E3 cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Reporting E6 as the most defensible single code.

quote: A simulation program using large language models was provided to 35 students in the intervention group in 2023, while 110 students from 2022 who did not participate in the intervention were selected as the control group.
rationale: Generative AI (LLM-simulated patients) used by fourth-year medical students with a non-AI historical control group and a quantitative OSCE outcome. However, the content is medical interviewing in medical education, which is health professions education and therefore outside the STEM domain. Population is medical students, which is health professions rather than the protocol's population framing. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in order: content is not STEM (health professions education is explicitly excluded). Note the record also has a nonrandomized quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, which fits the design criterion.

quote: The first question we have to raise when discussing the thought of Malcolm X is "Which Malcolm X are we discussing?"
rationale: The record is a humanities essay on the political thought of Malcolm X and black nationalism. It is not an empirical study. It involves no generative AI intervention, no learners, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Under the code order, E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) would technically apply first, since no AI of any kind is involved, but the clearest fact is that the record is not empirical research at all. I am coding E6 as the most accurate single code for a non-empirical philosophical essay.
rationale_note: Should the auditor prefer strict ordering, E1 is the first code in sequence that applies, as the paper involves no AI intervention.

quote: Two hundred synthetic medical student profiles were created with systematically varied demographic and academic characteristics.
rationale: Study uses ChatGPT to generate career advising for synthetic medical student profiles; no learners interact with the tool, there is no control group without generative AI, and the content is medical career advising (health professions/non-STEM), not STEM learning. No quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are advising recommendations and competitiveness scores. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), since the LLM is not used by learners as part of a learning activity.

criteria.rationale_note: abstract describes system validation with children, no control group

quote: Finally, the chosen setup is validated through an integration test involving children aged 4 to 6 years.
rationale: The abstract describes a software pipeline and an integration test with children aged 4 to 6, with no comparison group and no learning outcome measured. It reports only system recognition accuracy, not a comparison between conditions. This fails the comparison requirement (E3). Note the abstract also suggests a technical validation rather than a controlled learning study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no control group.

quote: One look at two setups shows how they handle local reasoning differently.
rationale: The abstract compares two RAG system configurations (one encoder-free with full context, one that compresses input) against each other, both using local LLM-based generation. No non-generative-AI control group or business-as-usual comparison is described, so the comparison criterion appears to fail (two generative AI variants only). The abstract also reports response accuracy and latency rather than a clearly described learning outcome, and does not establish a learner-facing STEM learning activity. Positive evidence of E3 is present in the abstract, so exclusion is warranted at this stage.

quote: The model was presented with multiple-choice questions extracted from three separate tests conducted in February 2022, July 2022, and February 2023.
rationale: The study tests ChatGPT-4 answering licensing exam questions alone. There is no control group without generative AI, and no learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity. The design is a single-model performance evaluation, not a comparative experiment. Exclusion is on E3 (no comparison group without generative AI). Note that E1 could also be argued, since the model is not clearly learner-facing, but the abstract's clearest failing criterion is the missing control group.

quote: we conducted a survey that collected quantitative data to describe teachers' intentions, the places they use, the learning that is targeted, and the challenges
rationale: The study is a descriptive teacher survey on outdoor education practices. It involves no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Exclusion under E1 applies first since there is no generative AI intervention at all. The survey design also fails the eligible design criterion, but E1 is the first code in order.

quote: Introductory American Government
rationale: The study is in political science (introductory American government), which is not STEM under the protocol's domain list. This is positive evidence of a domain failure, so it is excluded at abstract stage under E2 (first applicable code, since E1 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract). Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract alone.

quote: This study aims to investigate the perceptions of pre-service English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teachers regarding the use of ChatGPT
rationale: The content is English as a foreign language teacher education, which is non-STEM (language learning). The study is also perception-based with no control group, no learning outcome, and a survey/focus-group design, so it fails comparison, design, and outcome as well. Excluded on the first applicable code, E2 (non-STEM content).

criteria.rationale_note: ChatGPT-4 used by faculty to generate exam MCQs, not learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity

quote: ChatGPT-4-generated and human-generated MCQs were anonymized and MCQs quality was scored using a checklist
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT-4) was used to create multiple choice exam questions, and the outcome is quality ratings of the MCQs by a checklist, not learner outcomes. Learners do not interact with the tool as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies. The abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing. The comparison is between two item-writing sources rather than a learner control group, and the outcome is not a learning measure, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: The study involved a survey conducted with 57 participants.
rationale: Survey of teacher perceptions with descriptive analysis; no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Coded E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) also applies in substance; E3 is reported as the lead code.

quote: This lecture begins with basic terminology and presents three mini projects as first steps for learning Python.
rationale: The record is a special lecture write-up describing Python projects for postgraduate students. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion E6 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced; E1 (generative AI use by learners) is not evidenced in the abstract either, but the design is non-empirical regardless. Comparison, design and outcome criteria are not met.

Abstract is missing from the index, so no positive evidence of any criterion failing is available. Title indicates a programming domain (met) and use of ChatGPT (a generative AI tool, learner-facing likely), but whether there is a control group without generative AI, the design, the learning outcome, and the population cannot be assessed. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so the record is advanced for full-text review. Venue is listed as Educational Data Mining, which may be a conference proceedings rather than a journal article; this should be checked at full text.

quote: This study examines the development of visual literacy in teacher education through a classroom experience based on Cendrillon, the coded picturebook by Warja Lavater.
rationale: The study concerns visual literacy using a coded picturebook, which is not STEM content. The abstract also describes no control group and no comparison design; it reports descriptive group differences in a single classroom activity. Excluded on E2 (content not STEM), the first applicable code in order at this stage. Comparison and design are not clearly met either, but the domain failure is sufficient.

quote: MetaMate, that can be used out-of-the-box, aimed at facilitating efficient (i.e., within seconds) automated data extraction for educational systematic reviewers and meta-analysts.
rationale: The record describes a software tool for LLM-based data extraction for systematic reviews, not a learner-facing generative AI intervention. Its evaluation is agreement between the tool and human coders, with no learner control group and no learning outcome. Under the rule that E1 applies first when the intervention is not learner-facing, E1 would be the first applicable code. The protocol asks for the first code in order, so E1 takes precedence over E6. Because the record is a tool-development report, E1 is the appropriate primary code; the decision is clearly exclude at abstract stage.

quote: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to implementing AI and NLP technologies, such as ChatGPT, in STREAM project-based learning experiences
rationale: The record is titled like a mathematics paper but the abstract describes a conceptual/position paper proposing an approach to integrating ChatGPT in STREAM project-based learning. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that it is not an empirical study (E6) is present, so it is excluded at the abstract stage. The title mismatch with the abstract is noted but does not change the decision.

quote: We tested the widely used ChatGPT and Gemini AI bots to assess their current performance in generating code based on text prompts or image-based information for the two models.
rationale: The study evaluates how well ChatGPT and Gemini generate code for 3D modeling tasks. It does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool in a learning activity, nor a control group, nor a learning outcome measured in an experimental design. The design appears to be a tool-performance evaluation rather than an empirical learning study. Excluded at the first applicable code, E6 (not an empirical study), though the abstract is not fully explicit on design. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, this is an exclusion, not an unsure.

criteria.domain_note: science taught at primary school level, subject not specified beyond 'science' title
criteria.intervention_note: ChatGPT mentioned among many technology tools; generative use by learners not clear

quote: The explanation was given to the first group in the traditional way and to the second group using modern technological means.
rationale: Abstract reports a two-group comparison (traditional vs. technology-based teaching) with periodic tests, in a primary school, and mentions ChatGPT among many tools. It is unclear whether learners directly interacted with a generative AI tool, whether the design is a true comparison with a control group, and whether the content is STEM (title says science). Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure, so unsure; resolve at full text for intervention, design, and data (means/SDs).

quote: This study uses a descriptive method with a qualitative approach.
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative design (observation, interviews, documentation) with 12 students and no control group, so it is not an eligible comparative empirical study. Generative AI (ChatGPT) is mentioned only as one of many internet resources, and the study does not report a quantitative learning outcome; the claim of improved academic performance is not backed by reported statistics. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative design) is applied; E3 (no control group) would also apply and is noted as a secondary concern.

quote: this a cross-sectional survey study investigates the perceptions and preferences of the 80 EFL teachers and the 46 EFL students
rationale: The study concerns English as a Foreign Language (language learning), which is non-STEM content and is excluded by the Domain criterion. It is also a cross-sectional survey reporting only perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order (E1 is not clearly applicable since the intervention question is ambiguous, but domain failure is clear-cut). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by clear positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with JBI guidance and reported according to PRISMA-ScR.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is not an empirical study (E6). Excluded at abstract stage. Exclusion codes are checked in order; E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract (nursing thesis supervision is not STEM, but the abstract does not state the primary content of learning in a way that clearly settles E2), so E6 is the clearest positive failure.

quote: This paper integrates the two by synthesising six recent empirical studies of Chinese and Indian listed firms
rationale: The record is an integrative review and conceptual synthesis of corporate ESG studies in listed firms, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group of learners, no STEM domain, and no learning outcome. The large language model reference concerns a coding method for executive attributes, not an intervention. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study; the first applicable code in order is E1 on intervention, but the record's nature as a review is the core failure and E6 is the most direct fit.
rationale_note: Note: strictly, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) also applies and precedes E6 in order. Reviewer should consider whether E1 should be the code.

quote: To investigate the factors influencing the acceptance of AI-generated simulations by teachers, a Fuzzy DEMATEL analysis was applied with six experts
rationale: The study is a Fuzzy DEMATEL expert-judgment analysis of teacher acceptance factors, not an empirical learning experiment. It has no learner participants, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Population criterion fails because participants are teachers/experts. Under the protocol's ordering, the first applicable code is E1 only if the intervention were not learner-facing; here the primary failure is that it is not an empirical study with learner outcomes, so E6 is assigned as the most fitting code.

quote: The purpose of this qualitative study was to examine the use of ChatGPT as a lesson-planning assistant with preservice teachers (PSTs) of secondary mathematics.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order, since it is the first failing criterion among the ordered checks for a design lacking any comparison. Although E5 (no quantitative outcome) also clearly applies, the protocol asks for the first code in order, and the absence of a comparison group is the earliest failure in the sequence of criteria considered.
rationale_note: Positive evidence of failure: qualitative design, reflective statements analyzed, no comparison group reported.

quote: Data were collected from 127 university students using purposive sampling through a structured questionnaire.
rationale: Writing-focused study using a cross-sectional questionnaire of perceptions and working memory self-report; no experimental control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion on E2 (non-STEM content) is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced by the abstract (academic writing). Design is survey, which would also fail E3/E6, but the first-listed applicable code is E2 given the writing domain.

quote: The AI Music Problem: Why Machine Learning Conflicts With Musical Creativity probes the challenges behind AI-generated music
rationale: This is a book chapter offering a conceptual/humanities and technical discussion of musical AI. It is not an empirical study: there is no learner intervention, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also a book chapter, not a journal article, which would be E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order's most direct reading since the record describes no empirical work at all.
rationale_note: Note: E6 is listed before E10 in order; record is a book chapter, which is not a journal article.

quote: Five virtual focus group sessions guided the co-design of PD activities, followed by a pilot implementation in one biology classroom.
rationale: Participatory mixed-methods design with focus groups, interviews, surveys and student work artifacts from one pilot classroom; there is no control or comparison group, so the comparison criterion is not met. Generative AI is described only as a teacher lesson-planning aid, which would be E1 as well, but the first applicable code in order is E3 only if the intervention is considered learner-facing; the abstract gives no learner-facing generative AI use. Outcomes are teacher perceptions and student work descriptions without a quantitative learning comparison (E5 also plausible). Coded E3 as the primary failure of comparison design.

quote: This paper explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies have been transforming teaching practices in Pakistan.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive questionnaire survey of 189 teachers on AI awareness, adoption and attitudes. It is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a control group, has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no learner population, and no quantitative learning outcome. Fails on E1/E3/E4/E5 as well; the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) since teachers are the respondents and no learner interacts with a tool. Given the rule to report the first applicable code, E1 is the strictly correct code; E6 (not an empirical study) is arguably inapplicable because it is an empirical survey. Correcting: the first applicable code is E1.

quote: Employing a cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from a stratified random sample of 400 university students
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with correlational analyses. There is no randomized or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. The protocol's exclusion code list has no code for correlational or survey designs, so E3 is used as the closest fit for the missing comparison group. Domain is mixed (STEM is one of several fields) and the outcome is a self-reported scale, which are not separately decided here.

quote: Results indicate significant improvement in user coding proficiency, engagement metrics, and problem-solving efficiency compared to traditional learning platforms.
rationale: Programming domain is STEM. The platform includes LLMs for code explanation and hint generation, so the intervention may meet the generative AI criterion, but the abstract does not clarify whether learners interact with the LLM component. It reports comparison to traditional learning platforms, which may be a non-AI control, but the design is not stated. Population and whether the outcome is a quantitative learning measure versus engagement are unclear. No positive evidence of a failed criterion, so advance to full text.
decision_note: Advance to full text for verification of design, comparison and outcome.

quote: New COST Action 'EUropean network to tackle METAbolic alterations in HEART failure' (EU-METAHEART)
rationale: The record is a COST Action network announcement/editorial-style article about a research consortium in heart failure metabolism. It has no generative AI intervention, no comparison group, no learners, no STEM learning outcome, and is not an empirical study. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (not learner-facing generative AI) would technically apply first since no learner-facing generative AI is described; however, the core reason is that it is not an empirical study. Coded E6 as the most accurate description of the record type; E1 would also be defensible on the ordering rule.

criteria.quote: Adopting a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 350 students
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with PLS-SEM of perceptions and reliance; no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome measure. Not an empirical experimental study meeting design criteria; survey design is an explicit exclusion under Design. Coded E6 as a non-experimental (survey) empirical design. Domain is not STEM-specific (academic integrity among pre-service teachers), and no learning outcome is reported.

quote: Adopting a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 350 students
rationale: Cross-sectional survey using PLS-SEM with no control group, no intervention, and no learning outcome. Survey designs are excluded by the protocol's Design criterion. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails; the abstract gives no learner-facing GenAI intervention, but it is a survey of reliance perceptions, so E6 (not an empirical study meeting design) is used as the closest fit. Exclusion is clear on positive evidence of survey design.

quote: Five main articles were analysed and showed that the application of AI consistently has a positive impact on students' learning motivation.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review of five articles, not an empirical primary study, so it fails E6. It also focuses on learning motivation (affective), with no clear quantitative learning outcome reported from a controlled design. Biology is STEM-adjacent, so domain is not the reason for exclusion. Exclusion is based on the review design, which is positive evidence the record is not an empirical study.

quote: The program, implemented by a team from Surabaya State University (UNESA), included theoretical and practical sessions focusing on AI platforms such as Canva AI, ChatGPT, and Bing Image Creator.
rationale: Participants are in-service Pancasila Education teachers receiving community-service training, which the protocol excludes (workplace/in-service teachers). The study is a training/outreach report with only satisfaction-type feedback and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Per the code order, E1 is not clearly triggered (the AI tools are used in teacher material preparation, which is also not learner-facing), but the first clearly failing criterion that is definitive is population (E4). No comparison group, design, or learning outcome is reported either, so this is excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: ChatGPT and Bing Chat were asked the same question, their responses were recorded, and the percentage of each chatbot's code that was extraneous was calculated.
rationale: The study evaluates chatbot outputs directly (code extraneousness, modifications needed) rather than learners' learning outcomes. There is no learner group, no control group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning measure. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the clearest positive failure shown in the abstract; the absence of a comparison group (E3) is also evident, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order only if E1-E4 do not apply. Chatbot use is arguably learner-facing for a coding task, so E1 is not triggered. Population and E3 are not clearly established from the abstract alone, so E5 is used as the reported code.

quote: This column reported in Spring 2023 that the Quora website, now called poe.com, had an AI software program
rationale: The record is a column/essay on Edgar Allan Poe and AI history, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison, no learners, no STEM learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that reflects the record's nature; E1 and E4/E5 also would not be met, but E6 is the primary reason.

quote: the objective of which was to analyze student perceptions about its use
rationale: The empirical component is an exploratory classroom study that analyzes student perceptions only, with no described control group or quantitative learning outcome. The systematic review component is not an empirical study of learners. Perception-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion (E5). Exclusion is supported at the abstract stage because the abstract positively describes a perceptions-only design.
exclusion_code_note: E5 chosen as first applicable in order after E1-E4 are met or not clearly failed.

quote: Through an integrative synthesis of cognitive science, learning theory, computing-education evidence, and the economics of services, we argue that self-paced settings strip away the implicit scaffolding
rationale: The record is a conceptual/integrative synthesis and position paper proposing a reference architecture and cost argument. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Although it cites a survey of undergraduates, that is cited evidence, not this paper's own design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is not an empirical study.

Abstract describes a community-service training program (pengabdian kepada masyarakat) for 25 prospective teachers on AI-assisted scientific article writing, with preparation, training, and mentoring stages. It reports no control or comparison group, and the evaluation is described only as "significant improvement" without a described design or quantitative statistics. The writing-skill focus is also not clearly STEM content. Positive evidence of a failed design criterion (no comparison group) and of a non-empirical program report supports exclusion. Code E6 is applied as the most fitting first-applicable code; the record does not clearly fail the intervention or population criteria, so E6 reflects the non-empirical, single-group program description. Exclusion is based on the abstract alone; a researcher may wish to confirm at full text.

quote: Employing a qualitative descriptive case-study design, data were collected through documentary analysis of institutional policy documents
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive case study using documentary analysis and platform observation, with no controlled comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design criteria. Domain is EFL language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 would also apply, but the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 only if the intervention fails; generative AI is mentioned only as an "emerging" layer, so intervention is unclear. Excluding under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense, qualitative case design) as the design fails clearly; the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative case study without a comparison group.

quote: The main goal of this grand challenge article is to look at current issues, opportunities, and trends about clinical psychology and psychotherapy fields
rationale: This is a grand challenge / narrative review article, not an empirical study. It has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) since the article does not evaluate any learner-facing generative AI; however, the central failure is that it is not an empirical study. Following the rule to report the first code that applies in order, E1 would be the first listed; the article does not describe any generative AI learning intervention at all, so E1 applies first. Abstract-stage rule: exclusion requires positive evidence; the abstract describes a review/perspective article with clinical psychology focus and no AI learning intervention, which is positive evidence of failure. Note the record's text mentions AI only in passing ("a separate paragraph about the contribution of Artificial Intelligence"), with no learner-facing generative AI study.

quote: This study uses a quantitative descriptive method. The data is collected through questionnaires.
rationale: The abstract describes a quantitative descriptive survey study with questionnaires only. There is no control or comparison group, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Outcomes are perceptions and self-reported AI use rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is reported first in the protocol order that applies to the missing comparison group; the abstract also gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design, so the study does not qualify.

quote: The participants were separated into two groups, including those who used AI-supported learning tools and those who did not.
rationale: Abstract reports a two-group comparison (AI users vs non-users) with a critical thinking test outcome in higher education, published 2026. However, it does not state whether the AI tools are generative, and the STEM domain is not indicated (critical thinking, general). Also, the design reports paired t-tests on the AI group and a non-significant control change, which raises concern about a true comparison group. No positive evidence of a failed criterion at abstract stage, so advance to full text to check generative AI use, domain, and comparison design.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title describes reinforcement learning for production and maintenance planning of a single-machine system, an industrial optimization setting. There is no learner-facing generative AI tool and no learning context, so the intervention criterion fails on positive evidence. Exclusion code E1 is applied as the first failing criterion in order. The remaining criteria cannot be assessed from the title alone.

quote: We conducted a cross-sectional perception survey of 54 participants
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional perception survey with descriptive statistics only. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions), and no data for a standardized mean difference. Dental clinical education is also arguably health professions education, outside the STEM domain. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first code that clearly applies, since the design is a survey and not an empirical comparison. The abstract gives positive evidence of failing the comparison, design, and outcome criteria.

quote: This community service program aims to enhance teachers' skills in leveraging AI for the development of learning media.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes from the population criteria (E4). The study is a community service program with satisfaction and perception outcomes only, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, and it is not a STEM-focused study. Exclusion on population is the first applicable code in the stated order here on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: We conducted semi‐structured interviews with 17 stakeholders and used a framework analysis approach to structure and evaluate the collected information.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview series with stakeholders about digital transformation and curricula. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study eligible under the protocol, so E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) applies. Note that E1 would arguably be the first code in order, but the abstract gives no learner-facing AI tool; E6 reflects the qualitative, non-experimental design.

quote: The paper presents the outcomes of the development the generative, ontology-driven Microdictionary platform as part of the POLYHEDRON ecosystem.
rationale: The abstract describes a platform development paper with pilot educational scenarios and "evaluation signals" but no controlled comparison group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. It reads as a system/description paper rather than an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the abstract gives positive evidence that the design lacks a control group and learning outcome, so E3/E5 could also apply, but the primary failure is the non-empirical, development-focused nature of the paper.

quote: Using a theoretical speculation research paradigm, the thesis systematically conceptually decomposes, rigorously propositionally deduces, and deeply conducts theoretical dialogues
rationale: The paper is a theoretical speculation piece with no empirical data, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This article examines former graduate students’ experiences of participating in an inaugural writing mentorship program.
rationale: The record is an autoethnography reporting reflections and experiences, not an empirical comparative study. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also outside STEM (hospitality, recreation, tourism writing instruction). Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly fails at the abstract stage; the E1 and E2 judgments are not clearly determinable from the abstract alone.
rule_note: Criteria fields: comparison not_met, design not_met, outcome not_met, domain/intervention/population unclear.

quote: Pre- and post-training questionnaires indicated a 35% increase in digital skills and a 42% rise in student learning motivation.
rationale: Pre-post single-group community service program with questionnaires; no comparison group. Fails E3.

quote: The study employed an experimental design using a single group of nine preparatory- year students
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group design with pre- and post-tests and no control group, which is an E3 failure. The content is piano performance, which is arguably not STEM (E2), but the single-group design is the clearest positive evidence of failure and is coded first in the order. Generative AI use is also not evident from the abstract: the tool is a VR headset with virtual piano, so E1 could also apply, but E3 is the decisive failure. Excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence.
rationale_note: Exclusion code order: E1 is listed before E3. The abstract does not clearly show a generative AI tool (title mentions generative AI, but the described intervention is VR headset piano training), so E1 is also a plausible code. I am reporting E3 because the single-group design is explicit.

rationale: The abstract describes a single case study in which the first author uses ChatGPT/Gemini to design activities and the team adapts them. There is no control group that avoids generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. The design is a case study, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Under the protocol's code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first failing criterion that applies. The E1 check is ambiguous because AI is used by the team to prepare materials, which points toward E1 as well, but E3 is the clearest applicable failure and is assigned here. Exclusion is justified by positive evidence from the abstract: a case study with no comparison group.

quote: We outline the advisor's role as a mentalizing agent and, at best, a secure base within an attachment relationship, and propose that advisors' ostensive, marked, and contingent behaviors foster epistemic trust
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/conceptual framework on mentorship and attachment ("we outline", "we propose"), with no empirical study, no generative AI learning intervention with a control group, and no learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). The AI discussion is a conceptual boundary case, not an intervention evaluated against a comparison group.

quote: This paper provides a brief overview of the pedagogical applications of AI for teachers in LMICs
rationale: The record is a narrative overview/position paper about AI for teachers in LMICs. It is not an empirical study: there is no comparison group, no design, and no learning outcome. It also involves AI used by teachers rather than learner-facing generative AI (E1), but E6 is the first code that applies in protocol order... Note: per the code order, E1 is checked first; the record's embedded text is garbled and does not describe a learner-facing intervention, so E1 is arguably the first applicable code. The decision is recorded as E6 because the paper is a review/overview that is not empirical, which is unambiguous from the abstract.

quote: This community service program aimed to enhance the pedagogical capacity of Islamic boarding school teachers in Poncokusumo, Malang
rationale: Community service program (not an empirical comparative study). No control group is described, the participants are in-service pesantren teachers rather than students (E4 also applies), Arabic language instruction is not STEM, and outcomes are participant ratings and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code set to E6 as the first applicable code given the non-empirical community-service design; the abstract gives clear evidence of no comparison group, so the record is excluded.

quote: This involved the use of semi-structured interviews among 17 accounting instructors from different UK universities.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of accounting instructors about GenAI and academic integrity. It is not an empirical intervention study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Domain (accounting) is also not STEM, and participants are educators rather than learners. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol order, since the design is qualitative and non-experimental. Decision is made at abstract stage because the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison or outcome.

quote: This book delves into the transformative role of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in the educational sector.

It is also not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome, but the publication type is the first applicable code in the order given for the exclusion, and the abstract itself gives positive evidence of a non-eligible publication type.

quote: The results indicate that while 75% of students use AI for technical tasks, they frequently encounter the "False Positive" phenomenon
rationale: The abstract describes an empirical survey of master's students about AI use and ethics. It reports no controlled comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the reported measures are perceptions and usage. Excluded on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense, since it is a survey/ethics analysis with no eligible design). Note the protocol's design criterion also fails, but E6 is the primary code for a non-experimental survey paper. Clear positive evidence of failure is present, so exclusion is justified at the abstract stage.

E6 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly positive from the abstract.

rationale: Descriptive survey study with no control group, no intervention in which learners use generative AI as part of a learning activity (generative AI tools are only mentioned as a usage trend), and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol the design is a survey, so it is not an empirical experimental study eligible for inclusion. Excluded at abstract stage on clear positive evidence: survey design with no comparison group and no learning outcome. Code E6 is used because the record is a non-experimental survey, which is the closest fit; E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) and E3 (no control group) also apply in substance.

quote: We found that the article "ChatGPT, et al … Artificial Intelligence, Authorship, and Medical Publishing" (1).

It is not an empirical study: it reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. It is also not STEM education content. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported.
