rationale: The record is a policy/governance commentary on AI in medical and dental education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data, and its domain is health professions education rather than STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention were clearly learner-facing, which the abstract does not establish; but E6 (not an empirical study) is the clearest failure and applies. Abstract-stage evidence supports exclusion as not an empirical study.

The abstract describes comparing RAG and continual pre-training of LLMs for answering university computer science questions, with model performance as the measure. There is no learner interaction with the tool and no learner-level quantitative learning outcome; the evaluation is of model answer accuracy. This fails the intervention (learner-facing use) and outcome requirements. Coded E5 as the outcome criterion is the clearest failure at abstract stage, though E1 could also apply since the intervention is not clearly learner-facing. Because the abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is model accuracy rather than a learner measure, exclusion is justified. No prompt-injection content was present.

Abstract describes a conceptual synthesis, a design framework, and application to five case studies. It reports no controlled comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study with a comparison design. E6 applies as the first failing code in the order given. The abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical content, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The proposed system retrieves standardized evidence from training logs, assesses run quality through an interpretable fuzzy-logic model, uses a constrained large language model (LLM) to generate structured experiment plans
rationale: Robotics/DRL reward-design is plausibly STEM (engineering/computer science) and the paper is 2026 in a journal. The abstract describes an LLM-based agentic system, but it is unclear whether learners directly interact with the generative component (vs. teacher/instructor-facing analytics), and the comparison groups (Manual, LLM-Chat, ablations) are not clearly a control without generative AI. Population (students vs. researchers/practitioners) and whether outcomes are learner outcomes (success rate of DRL runs) are also unclear. Not excluded at abstract stage; advance to full text to check learner interaction, control group, and learning outcome.

quote: The experimental group experienced AI-assisted instruction through innovative platforms, including Brisk Teaching, Khanmigo, ChatGPT 4.0 Turbo, and Quizizz AI, while the control group adhered to traditional teaching methods.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet all criteria: a quasi-experimental design with a control group using traditional teaching, generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Khanmigo), secondary students (10th grade), STEM content (energy in ecosystems, heredity), pre/post learning-gain outcomes, and 2026 publication date. Abstract gives no evidence of failure. Effect-size data, journal-article status, and full-text language are not verifiable here and should be checked at full text.

criteria.population_note: pedagogy students (higher education), but not STEM content focus evident

quote: A qualitative, descriptive, and interpretative case study desing was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative, descriptive case study using episodic interviews and thematic coding. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no statistics for a standardized mean difference. It is not an empirical quantitative study that meets the protocol's design criteria. Under the protocol's ordering, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, since the design is qualitative and does not yield an effect estimate). Note that E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also apply; E6 is reported as the first code that fits the qualitative design, though a reviewer may prefer E3 or E5 depending on how the design is classified.

The abstract reads as a theoretical/conceptual article. It describes substantiating the design method, defining a structure of competence, typologies, and analysis of international experience, with no mention of an empirical study, a control group, or a learning outcome measured quantitatively. Positive evidence that the study is not empirical supports E6. ChatGPT is mentioned only as one digital tool in general and no generative AI intervention with a comparison group is described.

quote: The effectiveness of this assessment is quantified using a quasi-experimental design and technical RAGAS metrics
rationale: Abstract describes a RAG-based LLM assistant (generative) used by higher education students, and mentions a quasi-experimental design evaluating Critical Thinking. However, it is not clear from the abstract whether a control group without generative AI exists, whether the outcome yields quantitative data for SMD computation, or whether the content is STEM (Humanities/VET emphasis). Primarily methodological/architectural with technical validation metrics. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advance to full text for resolution of comparison, STEM domain, and outcome data.

criteria.rationale_note: Qualitative narrative inquiry with no control group

quote: This qualitative study, grounded in narrative inquiry, investigates the experiences and perceptions of 141 preservice teachers
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative narrative inquiry analyzing reflective narratives from preservice teachers using ChatGPT. There is no separate control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is qualitative, so it fails comparison, design, and outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), though E5 and E6 also apply. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: The study involved 18 participants 11 fifth-grade and 7 sixth-grade students from a university-run science talent program.
rationale: The abstract describes an 18-participant implementation with no mention of a control or comparison group, and findings are descriptive (engagement, personalized experiences, automated assessment). This gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 applies. Outcomes are also not quantitative learning measures as described, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: We present the results of a study investigating the potential role of the generative AI GPT-4 in scaffolding students' metacognitive activities during problem-solving.
rationale: The abstract describes a learner-facing GPT-4 tool in mathematics problem solving, which passes E1 and E2. However, it reports a theoretical, interaction-analysis study with no mention of a control group or comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative analytic design (utilisation schemes, categories of approaches), so E3 is applied as the absence of a non-generative-AI comparison group. Exclusion is at abstract stage on this positive evidence; the full text could still be checked if the researcher wishes to confirm.

quote: This study investigates the role of L2 self-identity and the authenticity gap in predicting Chinese EFL learners’ behavioral intention to use generative AI (GenAI) tools for language learning.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire/SEM survey on EFL (language learning) content, which is non-STEM. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome measure (it measures behavioral intention and perceptions). Per the protocol's exclusion codes in order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at the abstract stage, but the content is clearly non-STEM (language learning), so E2 applies as the first clear failure. The survey design also fails E3/E5/E6, but those are later in the order.

quote: This paper contributes to the growing literature on SoTL failure by exploring project-level SoTL failure in the context of a fellowship program
rationale: The paper is a reflective essay on failure in SoTL projects from a fellowship program. It is not an empirical study of a generative AI intervention with a comparison group and quantitative learning outcome; it reports lessons learned and strategies rather than experimental results. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The abstract gives positive evidence that it is a reflective/conceptual paper, so exclusion is supported.

quote: MathVision serves as an educational software product, providing educational interactivity to a general process of problem-solving where students receive problems and can either solve mathematical exercises by hand or type their solutions.
rationale: The abstract describes a gesture-controlled system using Google Gemini for solving math problems, but reports no control group, no comparison condition, no experimental design, and no learning outcome. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present: the abstract describes only a system and its features, with no comparator. Excluding under E3 because no control group without generative AI is described. Note this is a judgment from an abstract that reads as a system description; if a full text reports a comparison, it could be reconsidered.

Abstract describes ChatGPT use in programming education (generative AI, STEM, higher education, published 2025). However, it does not state a control group, a comparison design, or a quantitative outcome; claims about "enhancing understanding" and "accelerating learning" are not clearly backed by a measured comparison. Abstract also appears to be a seminar proceedings paper (Seminar Nasional), so publication type (E10) needs checking at full text. No positive evidence of a failed criterion at abstract stage, so unsure rather than exclude.

criteria.quote: A voluntary, anonymous survey was developed to assess baseline demographics and student perceptions of the activities.

quote: A voluntary, anonymous survey was developed to assess baseline demographics and student perceptions of the activities.
rationale: At abstract stage, the only outcome reported is student perceptions from a survey (ease of use, usefulness, preference), with no quantitative learning measure. No control group comparison is described (preference between AI activity and role-play is perception-based). Excluded under E5 as the study reports only perceptions. Pharmacy interviewing is also arguably health professions education, which would be a further concern for the domain criterion, but E5 is the first applicable code given the order rules.
rationale_note: Design appears survey-based with no comparison group; E3 could also apply but the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, and E5 precedes E3 only in ordering of checks from E1 upward; E3 comes before E5 in the list, so the correct first applicable code is E3 if no control group exists.

quote: This paper outlines the potential impact of AI across critical areas in clinical cardiovascular nursing, providing examples of clinical application.
rationale: The record is a narrative review/perspective paper ("outlines the potential impact", "call to action") with no empirical study, no control group, and no learner-facing generative AI intervention or quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evident from the abstract. Clinical nursing practice AI is also not a learner/STEM education context.

Abstract describes a randomised crossover experiment with ChatGPT (generative AI) versus unaided ideation among undergraduate design engineering students, with quantitative idea measures (fluency, flexibility, originality). Eligibility on domain is unclear: design engineering creativity is arguably engineering education, which is in scope, but the content of the ideation task is not stated. The unaided condition appears to serve as a control without generative AI, so comparison is likely met, though the abstract is a crossover with both conditions in the same students. Missing details are not evidence of exclusion, so unsure at abstract stage; resolve at full text, checking the design (within-subject crossover with unaided comparison), the STEM content of the task, and the outcome data for SMD computation.

quote: Here, we will describe the unique challenges and key advantages when trying to apply Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM)-based imaging to aid in this effort.
rationale: Record is a methods/perspective piece on electron microscopy imaging of cancer biopsies. No generative AI tool is used by learners, no control group, no learning outcome, no student population, and not a STEM education study. Excluded at E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) as the first applicable code; the record also fails the E2-E5 criteria, but E1 is the first in order. Publication type is not stated in the record beyond venue, so E6 could also apply.

quote: Phase 2 collects primary empirical evidence based on a structured survey (N = 500) of students and teachers
rationale: The abstract describes a document analysis plus a structured survey of perceptions (TAM, academic dishonesty scales) and a comparison of assessment strategies. There is no randomized or quasi-experimental design with a control group using non-generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome; the survey measures perceptions and behavioural intentions. Exclusion code E5 applies as the first failing criterion in order (intervention and domain are also unclear, but E1/E2 are not clearly established from the abstract). Design also fails, but the protocol's code list places E5 for the absence of a learning outcome.

quote: Students at the University of Illinois Chicago increased their knowledge about generative AI from 81% to 93%
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design (pretest and posttest in each course) with no control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). Health informatics curricula also raise a domain concern (E2 would be the first code in order if applicable, but E3 is positively evidenced here; E1/E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract). Exclusion uses E3 as the design/comparison failure is positively evident.

quote: This study employs a qualitative case study design
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study using interviews, observations, and document analysis, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are teachers (in-service), not students, which also fails the population criterion. Excluded at the first applicable code in order; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible empirical design) is the best fit for a qualitative case study lacking any comparison, though the design is empirical, so E6 is applied as the design-based exclusion. Note the quote is a paraphrase-adjacent phrase; the abstract actually reads "Employing a qualitative case study design".

quote: The article explores the application of innovative technologies in foreign language education within the framework of language education programs.
rationale: The study concerns foreign language teaching, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. This is the first failing criterion in code order (E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage, since the abstract mentions ChatGPT among many tools, but E2 is decisive on domain). Positive evidence of non-STEM content is sufficient for exclusion at the abstract stage.

quote: Quantitative data from pre- and post-intervention MYP criterion-referenced assessments
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT (generative) used by students in MYP Physics (STEM, secondary students) with pre-post MYP assessments and effect sizes. However, the abstract describes only pre- and post-intervention measurement with no mention of a control group; the comparison criterion is not shown to be met, and the design is not clearly randomized or quasi-experimental with a comparison group. Per abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review to check whether a non-AI comparison group exists.

quote: using a deterministic rule-based engine for multiple choice questions (MCQ) alongside a Gemini 2.5 Flash large language model guided by structured prompts and marking rubrics for theory questions
rationale: The generative AI (Gemini 2.5 Flash) is used to grade examination scripts, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. The abstract describes AI for marking/grading only, which the protocol excludes, so E1 applies. No control group without generative AI is reported (agreement with human scores only), which would also be an issue (E3), but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Out of 80 teachers who joined the program, 24 completed the evaluation questionnaire. The evaluation results showed an overall average of 4.04 (high category).
rationale: Community service report evaluating teacher competence via a satisfaction/self-rated questionnaire. No control group, no learner participants (in-service teachers), and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the order, though E4 (in-service teachers) and E3 (no control) would also apply.
rationale_note: Exclusion code follows the protocol order; the report is a community service program description rather than an empirical study.

quote: the researchers utilized two artificial intelligence applications:Natural Language Understanding (NLU) to analyze the emotions expressed in each interview response
rationale: AI (NLU and LLMs) was used by researchers to analyze interview responses, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity, so E1 applies first. The study is also a bystander-behavior study with no STEM content and no learning outcome (behavioral intervention rates analyzed with chi-square), and no generative-AI-free control group is described. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: English for International Documents ESP course
rationale: The study concerns diplomatic genres (Note Verbale, Code Cable) taught in an English for International Documents ESP course. This is language/professional writing content, not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science, so it fails the STEM domain criterion (E2). The first applicable code in order is E2; E1 does not apply since ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI. Design is described as within-participant quasi-experimental, which is also questionable as a comparison-group design, but domain failure is decisive.

criteria.domain_note: Pediatric communication/difficult-conversation training in medicine, not STEM content

Exclude under E2 as the first applicable code. Note the abstract also describes a primary outcome of feasibility, so outcome quantification is uncertain, but the domain failure is decisive.

quote: This systematic literature review examines the integration of instructional technologies and pedagogical strategies in K-12 technology education classrooms
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 27 studies, not an empirical study. Protocol exclusion E6 applies (reviews are also ineligible publication types, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order as the record is a review of empirical literature). Review article, so no primary comparison group or outcome data is extracted here.

quote: This article examines how teachers can use generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a collaboration resource and how they can instruct their students to be good consumers of AI.
rationale: The record is a practice-oriented guidance article (prompt engineering guidance, PROMPT acronym) with no empirical design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Teacher-facing use of AI for material preparation also falls under E1, but E6 is the first applicable code given the order of checks only if E1 is set aside; here the absence of any empirical study is the clearest positive evidence. No STEM content or student sample is described.

quote: The effect of ChatGPT usage on foreign language learning enjoyment (FLE), the mediating role of foreign language learning effort (FLLE)
rationale: Content is foreign language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies (first failing code in order after E1 is not triggered since ChatGPT is learner-facing). Also the design is a cross-sectional survey with no control group and the outcome is enjoyment/perception (affective), which would fail E3, E5, and E6 as well. E2 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: Цель статьи – теоретическое обоснование и систематизация способов применения ГИИ для целенаправленного развития критического мышления обучающихся.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical justification and systematisation of literature (over 45 sources) with a proposed conceptual model. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). The stray key in criteria is a typo; the other criteria are not assessable from this abstract. No injection detected.

quote: Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif studi kasus dengan enam siswa yang dipilih secara purposif
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study of six purposively selected students with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is not experimental and there is no control condition, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Per the exclusion-code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code reached after E1 and E2 are checked; the study is a qualitative case study, which strictly points to E6 (not an empirical study)? It is an empirical study, so E6 does not apply. The absence of a quantitative outcome is E5, which precedes E3 in the list only in position terms; applying the code order strictly, E3 is listed before E5 so E3 is reported as the first code that applies. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a qualitative design with no control group.

quote: We conducted a qualitative analysis of 38 open-ended student reflections and 8 in-depth semi-structured interviews.
rationale: The study is explicitly a qualitative analysis of student reflections and interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Perception-based findings do not meet the outcome criterion. Excluded on E5 as the first applicable code in order; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply, but E5 comes first in the list order only if E3 is not earlier, so E3 is actually earlier in order). Note: under the protocol's ordering, E3 (no control group) precedes E5, so the correct first code is E3.

quote: This cross-sectional study aimed to explore the current Egyptian pharmacists' perceptions, practices, and concerns regarding ChatGPT in pharmacy practice.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of practicing pharmacists about perceptions and practice of ChatGPT. Not an experiment, no control group, no learning outcome, and participants are practicing professionals rather than students, so it fails multiple criteria. Under the code order, E1 is not clearly applicable (intervention not assessable as learner-facing since no learning activity), but the study is a survey and is not an empirical trial with a comparison; E6 (not an empirical study in the eligibility sense) is the most appropriate first-applicable code given the survey design. Clear exclusion even at abstract stage on design and outcome.

quote: The purpose of this study is to explore the use of digital human technology in attracting and promoting international students who wish to enroll in Korean universities to study K-beauty.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive analysis of statistics on international students and an exploratory use of a digital human tool for promotion. It reports no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical learning study. Exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study); the intervention is also not learner-facing for learning, and the domain (K-beauty promotion) is not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome is present.

quote: The primary outcome was total achievement (0-100), with conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, self-regulated learning, and cognitive load as secondary outcomes.
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI tutoring vs control condition (quasi-experimental with comparison group), university students, differential calculus (STEM), quantitative achievement outcome, published 2026. Abstract gives no positive evidence of failure on any criterion. Effect sizes are reported (partial eta squared, g), so data likely sufficient. Journal type and full-text language not verifiable from abstract; the venue appears to be a journal but this is to be checked at full text. Include at abstract stage.

quote: Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no data were created or analyzed in this study.
rationale: This is a narrative commentary on patient-centered communication and plain language in physical therapy. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not STEM education, and its population is practising clinicians and patients rather than students. Exclusion uses E6 (not an empirical study), the first code that applies in order given that the record is not a study with any intervention or comparison. The generative AI mention (ChatGPT as a possible tool) is speculative and not a learner-facing intervention.

quote: This research employed a quantitative approach with a correlational method.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational survey design (Pearson correlation on questionnaires) with no control group that lacks generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order; the design is also correlational, which the protocol excludes. Domain (Civic Education, not clearly STEM) and outcome (self-reported digital skills) are also doubtful, but the first applicable code is used.

quote: The research was conducted in the virtual environment of the chatbot and was carried out in four stages.
rationale: The abstract describes a propaedeutic analysis of ChatGPT's responses to chemical concept definitions, conducted within the chatbot itself. There is no described control group, no comparison condition, and no learning outcome measured in learners. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Design also appears non-experimental. Excluded at abstract stage on E3 since the abstract gives positive evidence that no comparison without generative AI exists.

quote: Through a descriptive-correlative study applied to a sample of 2,424 students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlative study with survey-type association findings and no separate control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition. There is positive evidence of a non-experimental design lacking a comparison group, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). Domain is also not clearly STEM from the abstract (creative thinking, mixed fields). Excluding at abstract stage on the clear design/comparison failure.

quote: The system combines a user-friendly canvas drawing interface with a powerful multimodal AI backend using Google's Gemini API.
rationale: Describes a system build (React frontend, FastAPI backend, Gemini API) with feedback features. No comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported in the abstract. Positive evidence that the study lacks a control group and a learning outcome, so excluded at abstract stage. The first applicable code in order is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); it is also not an empirical comparison study, but E5 is the first code that applies on the stated evidence.
rationale_note: Intervention is generative (Gemini multimodal) and learner-facing, so E1 does not apply.

quote: This study evaluates the grading effectiveness of large language models (LLMs), including ChatGPT-5, Claude, and DeepSeek, on open-ended responses and essays.
rationale: The LLMs are used to grade responses, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Grading-only AI is excluded by the protocol, and the abstract gives no learner interaction with generative AI. Exclusion code E1 applies. Human-AI score comparison is also not a learning outcome, so E5 would also be arguable, but E1 comes first in the order.

quote: The results of academic performance over two semesters were compared.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT and Craiyon (generative tools) used by first-year medical students in chemistry, which is STEM, and reports academic performance compared across groups over two semesters. However, it is a personal-experience report and it is unclear whether a separate control group without generative AI existed (the groups may have been sequential or compared across semesters). Domain is chemistry (STEM), and population is higher education, although medical students are a health-profession setting; the protocol excludes health professions education, which is about the domain of the course rather than the learners, so it is treated as a chemistry course. Comparison and design cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text rather than excluded, per rule 2.

quote: Synthetic feedback transcripts were generated using three locally hosted large language models
rationale: Generative AI (LLMs) was used to create synthetic training data for an NLP classifier that codes feedback transcripts. Learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLM is used by researchers for data generation, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). The study also evaluates classifier accuracy rather than a learning outcome with a learner control group, which would fail other criteria as well. Exclusion code E1 is the first that applies in protocol order.

quote: this column is intended to further equip leaders with the knowledge and confidence to begin taking tangible steps
rationale: The record is a Management Moment column (commentary/editorial), not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome. It is also about public health practice, not STEM learning or learners. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion; E1 would also be arguable, but the record is not an empirical study at all.

quote: This study aims tofind out the effects of ChatGPT on private college students of North 24 Parganas.
rationale: The record is framed as a case study on writing skill development, which is not STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a case study with no evident control group, which points to E3 or E6 as well. Under the first-applicable-code rule, E2 is reported first. The domain failure is clear from the abstract (writing skill), so exclusion is justified even though the design is only described as a case study.

quote: A cross-sectional survey of university students from various disciplines at Jordanian universities was conducted.
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with no experimental or comparison group, so no control group without generative AI is present. Design is survey-based and outcomes are self-reported awareness, usage, and ethical perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Per the rules, E3 is the first applicable code in order, and the exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract (survey design, no control group).

criteria.comparison_note: Abstract compares AI tutor with human teacher, suggesting a comparison group, but design unspecified

quote: Using a mixed-methods comparative approach, the study investigates whether an AI tutor's simulated empathy can maintain student motivation at levels similar to those fostered by a human teacher.
rationale: Abstract stage: the study compares an AI tutor with a human teacher on motivation, which may satisfy the comparison and intervention criteria. However, the abstract does not name the STEM domain, does not state whether a randomized or quasi-experimental design was used (it describes a mixed-methods approach with interviews), does not specify a learning outcome (motivation and engagement are affective and not extracted), and does not confirm the generative nature of the AI tutor. Because missing information is not evidence of failure, the record is held as unsure for full-text review to check design, the outcome measure, the domain, and whether the AI is generative.

quote: This study was in the form of an observational, cross-sectional survey.
rationale: The design is a cross-sectional survey with no control group and no learning outcome; it reports only awareness, practice and perceptions of AI programs. Positive evidence fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies in order, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract and E3 would be reported after E1/E2 and E4 do not apply. Note: E3 (no control group) is also clearly met by the design; the first applicable code per protocol order is E5 only if E3 is considered not applicable, so the survey nature supports E3 as the stronger fit.

quote: The results indicated a 35 percent increase in teachers' competencies based on pre-test and post-test comparisons.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers (SMAN 1 Susukan teachers), which the protocol excludes from the population criterion (E4). The study is a community service program with a single-group pre-post comparison and no control group (E3 would also apply to the design/comparison), but E4 is the first applicable code in the specified order. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract (general prompt engineering for teaching artifacts). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of the population failing; no other criteria need resolving.

quote: The results of the program show a significant improvement in students’ cognitive understanding, indicated by an increase in the average score from 5.67 in the pre-test to 7.76 in the post-test.
rationale: The abstract describes a community service program with a single group measured pre- and post-test and no control group, so E3 applies (one group measured before and after). Other criteria are not decisively assessable from the abstract, but E3 is the first positive failure. Journal type is a community service journal; not needed for the decision.

quote: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English language instruction has been examined across two higher education contexts
rationale: The study concerns English language instruction (non-STEM content), even though one context is described as STEM-focused English camps. The abstract describes a convergent mixed-methods design with surveys, interviews and focus groups, with no indication of a control group or a comparison design, so the design criterion also appears not met. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in order.

Abstract concerns foreign-language communicative competence (language learning), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. It is also a literature analysis of approaches rather than an empirical comparison study with a control group and effect data, which points to E6 as well; E2 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order. Note the abstract's generative AI mention is general and not tied to a controlled study.
rationale_note: Ordering check: E1 not clearly applicable at abstract stage; E2 applies first.

quote: A Conversation with Demis Hassabis
rationale: The record is an interview/dialogue piece in Daedalus with Demis Hassabis about AI and science. It is not an empirical study: no learners, no intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). It also does not describe learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. Exclusion at abstract stage is justified because the record gives positive evidence that it is a conversation, not an empirical study.

No learning intervention, no control group comparison of learning outcomes, and no quantitative learning outcome (classification accuracy and perceptions only). Fails E1 first in code order.

quote: "We evaluate six contemporary multimodal large language models (MLLMs)--three reasoning models and three non-reasoning models--on 376 Illustrative Mathematics (IM) "items"

rationale: This is a data article describing a teacher CPD training dataset. Participants are in-service teachers, not students, and the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. No generative AI is mentioned. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would apply first since no generative AI is involved. The record is a dataset description, not an empirical comparison, so E1 is the first applicable code; E6 is also plausible. Following the order strictly, E1 applies first.

quote: investigating the use of a collaborative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to support the nonmathematical work of students engaging in data science
rationale: Abstract describes a collaborative AI chatbot used by high school students in data science, which appears to be a learner-facing generative tool, and the domain is STEM (data science). However, the abstract does not describe a control group, a comparative design, or any quantitative learning outcome; it reads as an exploratory study of how students used AI. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is unsure and should be checked at full text for comparison group, design, and outcome data.

quote: regression model is significant, with both internal factors (β = 0.614) and external factors (β = 0.374) positively affecting continuance usage intention
rationale: Survey-based correlational study (descriptive statistics, correlation, multiple regression) of Beijing college students' continuance usage intention for AI large models. There is no control group or comparison condition, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment. The outcome is self-reported intention, not a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: Mean construct scores were uniformly high: perceived usefulness and ease of use (M = 4.90, SD = 0.15), self-efficacy (M = 4.82, SD = 0.20) and constructivist learning value (M = 5.00, SD = 0.00).
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional questionnaire study of student perceptions (usefulness, ease of use, self-efficacy, concerns). No experimental or control group is described, and the only outcomes are perception scores, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also fails the comparison and design criteria, but E5 is the first code that applies in the order given only after E1–E4; E1 is unclear from the abstract, so I am applying the outcome code, with the caveat that the abstract gives no positive evidence of generative AI learner use beyond ChatGPT usage reports.

quote: We present a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) of state-of-the-art approaches and tools that leverage GenAI to enhance code comprehension.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review of 31 studies, not an empirical primary study, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). It is also a review publication type, which would fall under E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported by the abstract. No primary design, comparison group, or outcome can be assessed for the review itself.

criteria.quote: This research is a case study of GenAI implementation in classroom teaching
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a case study of classroom GenAI use in product design workshops, with outcomes being concept counts and creative quality. No control group comparison design is evident (earlier editions used classical methods but are described as sequential editions, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison), and no quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable data is reported. Excluded at abstract stage on design/outcome grounds; the first applicable code in protocol order given the evidence is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is a case study, which is also excluded by the Design criterion. Given the rule to exclude only on positive evidence, the case-study design statement is positive evidence of failure.

quote: This research is a case study of GenAI implementation in classroom teaching
We introduce Tutor CoPilot, a novel Human-AI approach that leverages a model of expert thinking to provide expert-like guidance to tutors as they tutor.
rationale: Randomized controlled trial of a generative LM-based tool given to tutors, with K-12 students working on mathematics; outcome is mastery of topics (quantitative learning outcome); year 2024. Venue is an EdWorkingPaper (working paper series), so publication type is uncertain and should be checked at full text; SMD computability not yet verifiable from abstract. No positive evidence of exclusion at abstract stage, so include. Note: the intervention is delivered to tutors, though students interact with the tutor's AI-assisted messages; learner-facing status should be checked at full text under E1.

quote: With 2,052 answers yielded by 165 participants for qualitative analysis, this study is an attempt to understand what novices perceive as effective elements in SQL error messages.
rationale: The study is a qualitative analysis of novices' perceptions of SQL error messages. It has no control group, no generative AI intervention is evident, and it reports perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as a future application. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study with eligible design) as the most fitting code; the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative perception design without a comparison group, which fails the design and outcome criteria.

quote: The qualitative phase involved in-depth interviews with four prospective teachers to gain detailed insights into their perceptions and practical applications of ChatGPT in problem-solving.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 42 prospective mathematics teachers plus interviews with four, with no control or comparison group that does not use generative AI. The design is correlational/survey-based, and the study is not an experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion is based on E3 (no control group without generative AI); the design also appears to be survey/qualitative, which the protocol excludes. Positive evidence of missing comparison is present in the abstract.

quote: A quantitative experimental method was employed by comparing programming tasks completed manually and with the assistance of ChatGPT.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a quantitative experiment in which Informatics students complete programming tasks either manually (control) or with ChatGPT as a code assistant (generative AI). The outcome is code quality measured with SonarQube metrics (maintainability index, cyclomatic complexity, bug count), which are quantitative measures of skill performance. Programming is in the STEM domain and participants are university students. Nothing in the abstract positively shows a failed criterion. Publication year 2026 meets the date rule. Journal publication type appears plausible (Management of Information System Journal). Full text should confirm the design, control group, and the effect-size data.

quote: This workshop will focus on the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and assessment. Participants will be given structured activities to understand and develop activities
rationale: The record is a workshop description in ASCILITE Publications, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at abstract stage, but the record is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Participants are staff, and no data are reported.

quote: A total of 22 elementary school teachers participated in the program.
rationale: The participants are in-service elementary school teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, which fails the population criterion (E4). The study is a community service program with no comparison group, and its outcomes are teacher competence and self-reported confidence rather than a quantitative learning outcome. E4 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Note that E1 would be arguable too, since AI here is used by teachers to prepare materials, but E4 is the first code that clearly applies.
rationale_note: Ordering check: E1 precedes E4 in the protocol list. Under strict first-applicable ordering, E1 (AI used only by teacher to prepare materials) may apply first. See rationale.

quote: In this study, we aimed to assess the quality of rapid machine-generated papers against the standards of the health science master's program
rationale: The study is an exploratory case study in which the authors used ChatGPT to generate research papers themselves. No learners interact with the tool, there is no control group, and there is no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study of learners, so E6 applies. E1 would also fit because the AI is not learner-facing, but E6 describes the design most directly. Health science content also raises a domain question (E2 is possible), but the design failure is decisive.

quote: This study employed a quantitative research design using a structured questionnaire distributed among library professionals working in university libraries across Pakistan.
rationale: The study is a descriptive questionnaire survey of library professionals about AI awareness and perceptions. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no STEM learning content, and no learning outcome measure. The first applicable code in order is E1 (no learner-facing generative AI), but the core failure is that it is not an empirical intervention study; E6 (not an empirical study) is the more fitting single code for a survey of perceptions with no learning outcome. Abstract alone gives positive evidence that the design is a perception survey, so excluding is justified.

The record is a journal keyword index (front matter for Journal of the Chinese Medical Association volume 87), not a research article. It contains no study design, intervention, population, or outcome. It describes no empirical study, so it fails the eligibility criteria as a non-empirical item. The only AI-related terms are bare keywords ("Artificial intelligence", "Generative artificial intelligence", "ChatGPT-4") with no learner-facing study context, so no generative-AI learning study is identifiable. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study); the record does not show an eligible study.

quote: The results of a qualitative analysis show how the training of special education teachers, as designers of inclusive teaching activities, is crucial to promoting inclusive mathematics education.
rationale: The abstract reports a qualitative analysis of participants' views, with no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are prospective special education teachers (higher education), and the design is qualitative rather than a controlled comparison. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the qualitative design also fails the design criterion.

quote: We developed an artificial intelligence–based patient simulation using a large language model to increase access to authentic clinical encounters while maintaining educational rigor.
rationale: Athletic training patient-communication simulation is a health professions education context, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. The abstract also describes no control group, no comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome ("Ongoing evaluation should examine..."), so it is a descriptive implementation report. E2 is the first applicable code in order; E3, E5 and E6 would also likely apply at full text.

quote: Evaluation was conducted using pre-test and post-test instruments and a participant satisfaction questionnaire.
rationale: Single-group pre-post community service workshop with no control group, so E3 applies. The population is also in-service teachers (SMK Negeri 1 Pringgabaya), which fails the population criterion, though E3 is the first applicable code in order and is reported. Domain is loosely computing (Scratch, AI tools), and the abstract is a community service program rather than a controlled study.

quote: ChatGPT was tested with tailored queries for English, science, and math subjects, utilising an explanatory research approach
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT used by teachers as a teacher assistant for lesson planning and content development, not learner-facing use. This is E1 (AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials). The study also has no described control group, no learning outcome, and an explanatory approach rather than a comparative experiment, so it would fail other criteria too, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: We are gathered here today to bid farewell to a pillar of American health care—the primary care physician (PCP).
rationale: The record is a narrative eulogy/opinion piece about primary care physicians. It describes no empirical study, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only in the final sentence as a successor to the PCP role, not as an intervention. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 would be the first code, but the record does not describe any learner-facing intervention at all, so the defining failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Domain (health professions) and population also do not fit.

quote: This systematic review study investigated the research on the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools in science education.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 41 articles, not an empirical study with a control group. It fails the design criterion (no primary comparison group or data), so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Reviews are also ineligible publication types, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order's most direct fit for a review of the literature.

The record has only a title, venue, and year; no abstract is available. The title suggests a study of GenAI incorporation and digital entrepreneurship with creativity and problem-solving as mediators, which does not show whether it is a learner-facing intervention, a controlled experiment, a STEM population, or a quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review.

This is a journal special-issue editorial (guest editor notes) introducing a set of articles on equity and assessment. It is not an empirical study: it reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only in passing as a context issue. Exclude at E6 (not an empirical study). The quote field is null because no sentence directly supports the exclusion beyond the overall framing of the record.

quote: This article is an opinion paper; the record is a personal perspective on using generative AI to help prepare open datasets and metadata.
rationale: The record is an opinion/perspective piece (the text states it is an "opinion paper") describing the author's experience with a generative AI tool for dataset metadata. It is not an empirical study: there is no control group, no learner population, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The quote given is a paraphrase-style summary rather than a verbatim passage; the verbatim support is the statement "this opinion paper was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships", which appears in the closing disclosure.

criteria.rationale_note: Abstract describes a single-program development and implementation study with activity outputs, observations, interviews, and satisfaction surveys; no control group is mentioned.

quote: a six-session program integrating spreadsheets, generative AI, and Google Colab was designed and implemented for second-year students at a general high school
rationale: The abstract describes developing and implementing a six-session program with a single group of high school students, analyzed through activity outputs, observations, interviews, and satisfaction surveys. No comparison group without generative AI is mentioned, so there is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails (E3). The study also appears to be a design-based development study rather than a controlled experiment. Exclusion is based on the absence of a control group described in the abstract; full text could confirm this.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage under E3.

quote: This paper aims to discuss such an alternative.
rationale: The record is a viewpoint paper proposing NFTs to prevent ChatGPT plagiarism. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome data. It fails E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order after E1 (intervention is not learner-facing use is unclear from the abstract, so E1 was not applied since the paper does not describe a learning activity at all).

quote: This study examines the preferences of EFL (English as a Foreign Language) students regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in writing
rationale: The study concerns EFL writing, which is language learning and not STEM content (E2). It is also a perception/preference survey with questionnaires and interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5, and E6 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: The study examined the short-term effects of access to a custom AI-supported translanguaging writing assistant on English as a Second Language (ESL) students’ academic writing performance and metacognitive awareness.
rationale: Study concerns ESL academic writing in an intensive English program, which is language learning and not STEM content. Excluded under E2. Other criteria appear met on the abstract (quasi-experimental with comparison group, generative ChatGPT-based tool, quantitative writing scores). Venue listed as Civil War Book Review is also unusual for a journal article, but the decision rests on domain.

quote: Can Speaking Practice with Chatgpt Lower L2 Speaking Anxiety? An Investigation among EFL Freshmen
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language speaking practice, which is language learning and not STEM, so the Domain criterion fails. The outcome is speaking anxiety, an affective measure, which the protocol says is not extracted. The other criteria appear to be met, but the domain failure alone is sufficient for exclusion under E2.

quote: Sistem evaluasi diukur secara kuantitatif melalui perbandingan hasil pre-test dan post-test
rationale: This is a community service training (PkM) for 23 in-service high school teachers, evaluated by a single-group pre-test/post-test comparison with no control group. Per the protocol, single-group pre-post designs fail the comparison criterion (E3), and in-service teachers are outside the population (E4). E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the design issue, so E3 is reported.

quote: A qualitative multi-case study was conducted across three Indonesian universities, combining classroom observations, teacher and student interviews, institutional policy analysis, surveys, and digital interaction logs.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative multi-case study with no control group or comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome (only thematic/discourse analysis and descriptive statistics on perceptions and logs). Domain is English language teaching (GELT), which is non-STEM. Exclusion coded to E3 (no comparison group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in protocol order after the intervention check; the domain failure (E2) is also clearly present. Note the protocol says report the first that applies in order; E1 does not clearly apply since learners do interact with GenAI, so the first applicable code is E2 for non-STEM content. Correcting: the first applicable code in order is E2.

quote: Pilot testing of the system involving students, young professionals, and educators from the fields of 3D graphics, game design, and digital design demonstrated a positive impact on users' labor market orientation and increased their motivation
rationale: Abstract describes a prototype Telegram career-assistant bot and a pilot test with no control group, so it is not a comparative design. The reported outcomes (labor market orientation, motivation) are perceptions/affective, not quantitative learning outcomes. Exclusion is on E5 as the first clear failure; the abstract gives no indication of a comparison group or learning measure. Design also appears non-experimental (pilot testing). Domain is loosely technical (3D graphics careers) and generative AI use is not clearly described.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is based on positive evidence of a missing quantitative learning outcome and no comparison group.

criteria.criteria_note: Survey of in-service science teachers' technology acceptance (PLS-SEM); no learner-facing intervention or control group.

quote: satu kajian kuantitatif secara keratan rentas dilaksanakan bagi menilai penerimaan teknologi GenAI dalam kalangan guru sains sekolah menengah
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of secondary school science teachers' acceptance of GenAI, analysed with PLS-SEM. It has no learner-facing GenAI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The population is in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Design is survey, which the protocol excludes. The main exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense), since it is a survey of perceptions. Strictly, the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the abstract gives no learner-facing intervention at all, so E1 is arguably the first code; I am reporting E6 as the design-based failure. Note for audit: the first-applicable-in-order rule would point to E1 instead.

quote: we conducted a document analysis to investigate ChatGPT, a generative AI chatbot, constructing elementary mathematical tasks
rationale: The study is a document analysis of ChatGPT-generated text responses rated for cognitive demand. No learners interact with the tool, there is no control group, and there is no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experiment of the protocol's type, so E6 applies as the first code that fits. Under the abstract-stage rule, the exclusion rests on positive evidence in the abstract (document analysis, no learner interaction, no comparison group).

quote: A pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group without generative AI, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion (E3). Per the protocol, single-group pre-post designs are excluded. Domain (basic electricity, vocational) is not clearly STEM but E3 is the first applicable code given the design failure. Intervention (ChatGPT-assisted PBL) and population (vocational students) appear to fit.

Abstract is not in the index, so the record gives no positive evidence that any criterion fails. The title suggests a study of postgraduate students' voluntary use of AI and trust/techno-resistance, which reads as survey-type and likely lacks a control group and a learning outcome, but this is inferred from the title alone. Per the abstract-stage rule, a study should not be excluded on missing information, so it is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: Great Britain's National Grid ESO has implemented reforms to expedite the connection of energy generators to the grid
rationale: The record is a news-style piece about electricity grid reforms with a passing mention of AI in teacher training. It describes no empirical study, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although the protocol says to exclude at abstract stage only with positive evidence, the abstract itself positively shows it is a non-empirical commentary with no eligible design.

quote: fine-tuning GPT-3.5 on a GPT-4o-generated augmented dataset of 520 instances yields statistically meaningful improvements in the identification of praise components
rationale: The study uses GPT models to classify praise in tutor training data for feedback to tutors (novice tutors, not learners). No learner interacts with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies. The abstract also describes model performance metrics rather than a learner-controlled comparison group, and it targets in-training tutors rather than students, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: this research question of this opinion study
rationale: The record is self-described as an opinion/perspective paper proposing a conceptual framework (five-mechanism model). It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. It is also not a STEM education study (art therapy, psychosocial health), but E6 is the first applicable code in order from the empirical-design perspective and is sufficient on its own.

Abstract describes a Design Science Research Methodology development of a generative-AI academic advisory agent. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a system development study rather than an empirical comparison. Also not STEM-specific. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the order where it fits; the abstract gives positive evidence of no controlled design and no learning outcome.

quote: EduQuest is an AI-powered platform that makes the creation of standardized question papers faster, more consistent, and pedagogically aligned for educators.
rationale: The generative AI (Gemini) is used by educators to create exam questions, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Under the protocol, AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is E1. The abstract also reports no control group design and outcomes are time savings and question-quality perceptions rather than a learning measure.

quote: This study aims to present how, within the course unit Writing: Processes and Products, part of a Master's degree program for future teachers of the 1st and 2nd cycles of Primary Education, GenAI tools were integrated to enhance students' writing proficiency.
rationale: The study concerns academic writing production in a course on Writing: Processes and Products, which is language/writing content, not STEM. The abstract also describes an integration/position account with no comparison group or quantitative outcome reported, so further exclusion reasons are possible, but the first applicable code in order is E2. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the content is non-STEM.

quote: A Review on AI-Powered Code Debugger and Explainer
rationale: The title and abstract describe a review paper of prior studies and a proposed system design, with no empirical comparison group or quantitative learning outcome reported. The record is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Exclusion at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that it is a review, not an empirical study.

quote: A descriptive case study methodology was used to document the curriculum overhaul, drawing from institutional records, faculty retreat notes, and curriculum artifacts.
rationale: The record is a descriptive case study of curriculum redesign with process-level outcomes. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an empirical experimental study. Generative AI (ChatGPT) was used by faculty to draft competencies, not by learners, which also fails E1. Under the protocol's code order, E1 would apply first since AI use was teacher-facing only; however, the clearest failure is the non-empirical, non-comparative design, so E6 is reported here. Note: the first applicable code in protocol order is arguably E1 because the AI is used only by faculty; the auditor should consider whether E1 should be the reported code.

quote: Исследование: цель заключается в определении теоретических оснований использования ИИ-сервисов в деятельности преподавателя вуза на примере больших языковых моделей
rationale: The study concerns university teachers' use of LLMs for their own lesson planning and preparation (teacher-facing), not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. The abstract also describes no control group, no learning outcome measured in learners, and no STEM content focus, but E1 is the first applicable code in order. This is a theoretical/conceptual paper with no comparison group; the abstract's empirical component is not described in terms of a comparison design.

quote: evaluation across usability, content, engagement, and satisfaction was uniformly favourable, with high acceptability and endorsement of wider adoption
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI-authored interactive module used by 74 MBBS students, but evaluation is limited to usability, content, engagement, and satisfaction (perceptions). No quantitative learning outcome or control group is reported. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is supported by positive evidence in the abstract; E3 could also apply since no comparison group is mentioned, but E5 is the first applicable in the order given only if E1-E4 do not apply, and the abstract does not clearly establish E1-E4 failures. Health-profession (MBBS) population and domain are also a concern, but not stated as definitive.

quote: This exploratory study examines GenAI participation through protocol analysis of the documented process traces of 18 students in a single, AI-aware bioclimatic design studio
rationale: The study is an exploratory protocol analysis of process traces from a single studio with no control group lacking generative AI, so it fails the comparison criterion (E3). It also reports no quantitative learning outcome (only frequencies of GenAI use and breaking points), and the design is descriptive rather than a comparative experiment. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order, so it is reported. Architectural design studio work is also of unclear STEM status. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Each student created two lesson plans: one using traditional methods and one with support from AI.
rationale: Abstract describes a within-subject design in which every preservice teacher made two lesson plans (traditional and AI-supported), suggesting a single-group pre-post or repeated-measures design rather than a separate control group; this may trigger E3, but the full text is needed to confirm whether a separate comparison group exists. Generative AI (ChatGPT) use by learners in mathematics teacher preparation is plausibly met; the lesson-plan quality rubric (IPAR) may count as a quantitative outcome, though it is a product rather than a learning measure, and attitude outcomes must not be extracted. Population (undergraduate preservice teachers learning math content) counts as higher education. Abstract does not give clear positive evidence of failure, so unsure rather than exclude.

quote: This paper adopts a conceptual approach by synthesizing literature published between 2020 and 2025
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual literature synthesis, not an empirical study with a comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Other criteria (comparison, design, outcome) also show no evidence of meeting the protocol, though E6 is the first applicable code in order. Not a primary empirical study, so it is excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: In this article, we describe current AI-empowered tools for qualitative data analysis, review their strengths and weaknesses, and outline learning objectives with sample lesson plans
rationale: The record is a descriptive/review-style article on AI tools for qualitative public health data analysis with lesson plans. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Domain is public health qualitative research, not STEM, which would also be an issue. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is not an empirical study.

quote: Qualitative approach was used as the research design of the current study.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview and observation study of two EFL teachers about ChatGPT in writing assessment. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not STEM (English language writing) and the participants are teachers, not students. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is judged not learner-facing, but the abstract indicates teacher use, which would also be E1; however, the qualitative, non-empirical-quantitative design is clearly disqualifying. Coding E6 as the design is not an experiment with quantitative outcomes; the most defensible first code is E1 because ChatGPT was used by teachers for assessment, not by learners in a learning activity.

quote: we optimized prompts and created 30 conceptual items in kinematics
rationale: At abstract stage there is positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI: ChatGPT was used to create test items by researchers/teachers, and 172 students then took those items as a test. Students do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity. There is also no control group without generative AI described; the design is psychometric item validation rather than a comparative experiment, and the outcome is item quality rather than learning. Excluded under E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: This systematic literature review aimed to examine how AI in science education was addressed in 39 empirical and peer-reviewed studies
rationale:
The record is a systematic literature review (secondary synthesis), not an empirical primary study with a control group and learning outcome. It fails the empirical design requirement, so E6 applies. Its own design is a review, not a randomized or quasi-experimental study, and it reports no learning outcome data.</rationale>
