quote: The Cal Poly Graphic Communication Department wanted to study how participants would respond when receiving a lesson on lighting for photography in a VR environment from a simulated AI educational agent.
rationale: Abstract describes a student project plan with a production schedule (weeks, team meetings, testing), not a reported empirical study with a comparison group or learning outcome. Measures mentioned are perceptions and social presence, which are not learning outcomes. Domain (photography lighting) is arguably not STEM, but the strongest reason is that the record reads as a project proposal/plan rather than an empirical study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note: the abstract stage rule normally favors advancing; however, the text gives positive evidence that no empirical results or quantitative learning outcome are reported, so exclusion is justified. Flag for auditor review given the abstract-stage rule.

quote: This manifesto proposes a critical framework for integrating artificial intelligence into communication centers
rationale: The record is a manifesto/position article, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Domain is also not STEM (communication centers), but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given for the core reason.

quote: We incorporate these insights into three LLM approaches to create warmup tasks that activate background knowledge.
rationale: The LLMs are used by expert teachers to create curriculum warmup tasks, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. This fails E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI). The outcome is teacher-rated quality of generated warmups, not a learner outcome. The E1 code is the first applicable exclusion in order.

criteria.rationale_note: Descriptive survey of 30 students; no control group.

quote: Utilizing a quantitative approach with a descriptive method, the research surveyed thirty (30) 3rd Year computer engineering students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey of 30 students with no comparison group, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies. The study also reports a correlation and survey perceptions rather than a standardized learning outcome comparison. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: Participants included 161 educators: 49 junior teachers (experience < 5 years) and 112 senior teachers (experience > 5 years).
rationale: Community service workshop program for in-service teachers (population excluded by protocol, and population is not K-12 or higher education students). Design is an observation/thematic analysis with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; this is a program report rather than an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code assigned as E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits the abstract; E4 (participants not students) would also apply. Under the order E1 to E10, E1 is unclear from the abstract, E2 is unclear (AI literacy workshop covering AR/VR, not clearly STEM), so the first clear code is E4 for population; however, the record's nature as a community-service report without comparison supports E6. Decision is exclude on clear positive evidence.

quote: The system has been deployed on the Squirrel AI learning platform for elementary mathematics education, where it achieves 78.3 accuracy in error analysis and shows a marked improvement in student learning efficiency.
rationale: LLM-based error analysis and dialogue for elementary math students (STEM, K-12). The abstract claims a "marked improvement in student learning efficiency" but does not describe a control group or design, and the 78.3% figure is a system accuracy rather than a learning outcome. Whether a comparison group and a quantitative learning outcome exist cannot be determined from the abstract, so the record advances to full text rather than being excluded. Publication type is a journal article (AI Magazine), and the date is 2026.

quote: The study aimed to compare the correction and grading criteria used by preservice Physics and Chemistry teachers with those integrated into Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, specifically ChatGPT and Gemini.
rationale: The study concerns AI (ChatGPT, Gemini) used for grading exam answers, and the preservice teachers are the graders; learners do not interact with generative AI as part of a learning activity. This is E1 (AI used only for grading / not learner-facing). The outcome is grading consistency, not a learning measure, and there is no non-AI learning control group. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: This paper examines the modeling and practical implementation of phishing attack simulations using the GoPhish platform.
rationale: Record is a Ukrainian-language cybersecurity paper on phishing simulation with GoPhish. It describes no learner-facing generative AI, no control group, no learning outcome, and no empirical comparison design in the abstract. Cybersecurity phishing awareness is not in the STEM domain list, so E2 applies as the first exclusion code that clearly fails. Note E1 could also be argued (GoPhish is not generative AI and no generative AI is mentioned), but E2 is reported as the domain failure. Under abstract-stage rules this is a positive exclusion based on the abstract content.
decision_note: Exclusion code order: E1 is checked first per protocol. Since the intervention (GoPhish phishing simulation) is not generative AI, E1 is the first code that applies and should be used instead of E2.

quote: A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted on a convenience sample of 184 nursing students in Slovenia.
rationale: The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey with no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria, and it is not STEM content (nursing). E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's rules for non-empirical or non-eligible designs; the survey design fails the design criterion. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not generative AI) applies first, since there is no generative AI intervention at all. Recording E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: In this conceptual study, we address the elephant in the room, grading
rationale: The record is a conceptual study with a policy review, not an empirical study. It has no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order after E1 to E5 are considered; E1 and E2 cannot be assessed from the abstract alone, and E3 and E5 apply in substance but E6 is the primary failure.

Abstract stage, but positive evidence exists that the outcome is not a learning measure. The study diagnoses future teachers' professional-value orientations (a self-assessment/psychological construct) via generative-AI-based pedagogical tasks; the reported results concern differences between diagnostic methods and their sensitivity, not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or problem solving. Domain is pedagogy/teacher education, not STEM. No control group without generative AI is described; the comparison is between two diagnostic methods. Given the protocol's instruction to exclude only on positive evidence, the code assigned is E5 (first applicable in order is arguably E2 for non-STEM content; E2 is listed before E5, so E2 would be the first code that applies). Note: under strict code ordering, E2 applies first because the content is not STEM.

quote: We often measure the strength of nations by GDP or by the size of armies, navies, and air forces.
rationale: The record is a Daedalus journal introduction essay on international higher education and university innovation. It is not an empirical study: it reports no experiment, no control group, no generative AI intervention, and no learning outcome. It is not STEM-specific or learner-facing AI. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study). Quote is from the opening of the text, which is the only visible content relevant to the decision; the rest of the abstract text is garbled and does not change the decision.

quote: The research proposes adopting outcome-based education (OBE) principles to reconstruct curriculum objectives, deconstructing typical work tasks to modularize instructional content
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/analytical curriculum-reform proposal, with no experimental design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. No generative AI learner intervention is described; generative AI is mentioned only as context for industry change.

quote: The major goal of this article is to present prompting-engineering good practices that contribute to innovative and relevant lesson planning.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position article presenting prompting good practices for lesson planning. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Teacher-facing lesson planning with GAI also would not be learner-facing, but E6 is the clearest positive failure at abstract stage.

quote: This qualitative descriptive study examined how English as a foreign language instructors perceived, implemented, and evaluated artificial intelligence– enhanced virtual reality activities
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive study of instructor experiences (eight interviews, stimulated-recall sessions). It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no learner-level data. Domain is English as a foreign language, which is non-STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design) is applied as the first code that clearly applies; E2 (non-STEM) would also apply. Per the code order, E1 is not clearly applicable, so E2 would take precedence over E6 in the listed order. Reporting the first applicable code in order: E1 unclear, E2 applies because the content is English language teaching, which is non-STEM.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice covering a special issue; the CHATWELL article (Cheng, Guo & Lu, 2025) is listed as retracted. The notice itself is not an empirical study and contains no design, comparison, or outcome data. The retracted article is not an eligible empirical study, so it is excluded under E6. Its title suggests an AI adaptive tutoring system for Mandarin composition, which is language learning (non-STEM), but the abstract does not describe the study, so E6 is the first code that applies on the evidence available.

quote: The study investigates the problem of forming the foreign language professional competence of future non-linguistic specialists
rationale: The abstract concerns foreign language (English) professional competence for non-linguistic specialists, which is language learning rather than STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also reads as a theoretical/conceptual article with no described comparison group or quantitative outcome, which would be further grounds for exclusion (E3/E5/E6), but E2 is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Abstract describes a conceptual discussion; no empirical design evident.

quote: Utilising a survey, the researchers examined how personal and linguistic attributes influenced feedback strategies and explored the educators' perspectives on integrating AI tools
rationale: Survey and thematic analysis of NESB educators' attitudes; not an empirical experiment with learners. Participants are in-service educators, not students, and there is no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's E-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would technically apply first since AI is used by teachers for feedback provision, so E1 is arguably the first applicable code. Final code chosen: E1 is the first applicable code in order, so use E1 instead.

quote: This paper introduces a theoretical framework to conceptualize false understanding in AI-assisted physics problem solving.
rationale: The paper is a theoretical framework with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative outcome data. Under E6 (not an empirical study) it is excluded. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract but the E6 failure is sufficient.

quote: Pre-Service EFL Teachers' Perceptions of ChatGPT
rationale: The study concerns English as a Foreign Language teacher education, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so E2 applies first in the code order. It is also a perceptions-only study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which would independently fail comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: The first part of the article studies the concept of “competency” and approaches to competency, setting goals and output standards of the teaching process.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical article on a competency-based teaching process for an IT major. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears not to be an empirical study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the article is descriptive/theoretical rather than missing information. Exclusion code E6 is used because the work is not an empirical study.

The abstract describes an experiential/reflective article about developing EAP reading materials with GenAI. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a practice-oriented commentary, not an empirical study. Domain is EAP/language learning, which is non-STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the first applicable code in order would arguably be E2 (non-STEM) since E1 and E2 precede E6, but the abstract gives no positive evidence of a learner-facing AI intervention, so E1 is unclear. Per exclusion-code ordering, E2 applies first because the content is clearly language learning, not STEM.

quote: This paper offers hermeneutical acquired insights into creating effective educational prompts, emphasizing critical milestones for establishing and maintaining the theoretical framework
rationale: The abstract describes a hermeneutical, insight-based paper that develops a conceptual model of prompt engineering. It gives no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is positive evidence that the study is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Domain is also unclear (teacher candidates, not clearly STEM). Excluded under E6 as a non-empirical (conceptual/hermeneutic) paper.

quote: This study serves a dual purpose: to compare Claude and ChatGPT from a teachercentered perspective while documenting our learning as mathematics teacher educators engaging with generative AI.
rationale: Reflective, practice-based inquiry comparing two AI tools' outputs by teacher educators; no control group, no learner participants, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is non-empirical/reflective rather than an experiment. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies on positive evidence from the abstract; E3 and E5 also plausibly fail, but the study is primarily a reflective, practice-based piece.

quote: This study aims to examine the challenges and opportunities of integrating ChatGPT into Biology learning through a qualitative descriptive approach.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive study using observation, interviews, and literature review, with thematic analysis. It has no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study eligible under the protocol. Biology is a science domain, so the domain criterion is not the issue. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code after the intervention and domain checks, since the study is qualitative rather than an eligible empirical design; the absence of a control group and quantitative outcome would also fail E3 and E5, but the qualitative design is the primary failure.

quote: Astronomy & Geophysics – February 2023
rationale: This record is a magazine news digest (News in Astronomy & Geophysics, February 2023) covering National Astronomy Meeting logistics and various astronomy news items. It describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no empirical study. It is not a journal research article on STEM learning. Coded E1 as the first applicable code, since no learner-facing generative AI intervention is present at all. Note that E6 (not an empirical study) would also apply; E1 is reported first per the protocol's ordering. No prompt-injection content detected, though the text is garbled in parts.

quote: Twenty final-year students evaluated GenAI-generated conceptual designs for an intentionally small-scale ammonia production plant (1000 tonnes per year).
rationale: Abstract describes a single cohort of 20 students evaluating GenAI-generated designs. There is no described control group without generative AI, and the study appears to be a descriptive analysis of student reports. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3. Domain (chemical engineering), population (senior undergraduates), and intervention (learner-facing GenAI critique) appear met.

quote: A longitudinal survey study will assess changes in perceived competency in professional skills and psychological well-being
rationale: The abstract describes a planned longitudinal survey study of a course (Program LEAD) with no comparison group. It is a protocol-style description, not a reported empirical study with a control condition. The design criterion fails on positive evidence (no control group, survey design, perceived competency outcomes only), and the outcomes are perceptions/wellbeing self-reports rather than quantitative learning measures. Coded E6 as not an empirical study with a comparison design; the abstract also does not describe a STEM domain or a generative AI learner-facing tool beyond one module mention, and it targets HQP (graduate/undergraduate) in an unspecified field. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-eligible design and outcome, exclusion is supported.

quote: A survey of 308 second-year students revealed Python as the preferred beginner-level language, with 75.6% favoring it over Java.
rationale: The study is a survey of language preferences and perceptions (TAM/UTAUT2 constructs), with no learner interaction with a generative AI tool and no comparison group. Outcomes are perceptions and preferences, not learning measures. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clearly applicable code at abstract stage; the survey design also fails the design criterion, and generative AI appears only as a recommendation in the abstract, so E1 would also be arguable. Coded E5 as the outcome failure is clear from the abstract.

quote: Learners who completed the survey (n = 19, 38% response rate) had a more positive experience with Recourse AI (M = 4.10) than with BodySwaps (M = 3.67).
rationale: The study reports only student perception surveys (SET-M and a faculty-made quality survey) and usage-type feedback. There is no quantitative learning outcome, and no control group is described; the design is a single-cohort descriptive report. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies after the intervention check. The domain (nursing/vaccine communication) is also arguably health professions education, which would be excluded, but E5 is reported as the first applicable code in order. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for E5 because the abstract describes only perception data.

quote: The findings suggest that integrating HITL in AI assignments significantly improves learning outcomes by fostering an adaptive learning environment
rationale: The abstract describes a single case study of one class using generative AI for text, image and code creation, with no mention of a control group or comparison condition. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group (case study design) is present, so the record fails the comparison and design criteria; coded E3 as no control group without generative AI. The claim of significantly improved outcomes is not supported by any described comparison in the abstract.
decision_note: Criteria object contained a duplicate key; corrected values below.

quote: Our review identified key themes and patterns in the literature and provided a comprehensive understanding of the different opinions held by students and faculty.
rationale: This is a systematic review, not an empirical study. It synthesizes perceptions and themes rather than reporting a controlled comparison with a quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E6 (not an empirical study) applies. The review also includes conference papers, which would independently fail publication type, but the first applicable code is E6. Note: the protocol's own E-code list does not separately cover reviews beyond E6/E10, and the record is excluded on E6 as the first applicable code.

quote: the responses of the AI tools to the questions posed to them were compared in terms of scientific accuracy
rationale: The study compares the scientific accuracy of four chatbots' responses to physics questions. There is no control group without generative AI, and it is not a learner-based experiment with a learning outcome; it is an evaluation of chatbot outputs. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code on the protocol's ordering that is clearly supported by the abstract (no non-generative-AI comparison group; the comparison is between generative AI tools only). Note that E1 could also arguably apply because learners do not appear to interact with the tools, and E5/E6 are plausible, but the abstract gives positive evidence that only AI variants are compared.

quote: The purpose of this qualitative study was to explore online professional practice doctoral students' and recent graduates' (2022-2025) use of editing software, GenAI/AI browser extensions, and human editors
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study analyzing 29 participant responses. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is qualitative, so it fails the design criterion. Under the exclusion order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (STEM content) are not clearly failed at the abstract stage, but the study is not empirical in the protocol's sense of a comparative design. E6 is the most fitting code for a qualitative, non-experimental study. Using E6 under the protocol's "not an empirical study" heading is a judgment call; the qualitative design is the decisive reason for exclusion.

quote: This study investigates the impact of integrating ChatGPT, an Artificial Intelligence-powered language model, into English for Specific Purposes (ESP) writing courses for EFL students at Saudi Arabian universities.
rationale: The study concerns ESP writing for EFL students, which is language learning and not STEM content, so E2 applies. Its ChatGPT intervention and university population would otherwise fit, but the domain criterion fails on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: We discuss transforming STEM education using three aspects: learning progressions (LPs), constructed response performance assessments, and artificial intelligence (AI).
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/position paper proposing future uses of ML and generative AI for learning progressions and assessment ("we suggest", "we discuss", "future research avenues"). It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the record is a non-empirical discussion paper.

quote: The study demonstrates the feasibility and affective appeal of integrating "third-place" learning environments with AI-assisted reading
rationale: The abstract describes an eight-week single-group program with no control group ("the absence of a control group"; "single-group program"). This is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion, so E3 applies. Outcomes are also self-report and descriptive only (E5 would also apply), but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Domain is EFL reading, which is non-STEM, though E2 comes after E1 and E3 in the ordering.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on E3.

quote: Statistical analysis using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test showed a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (p = 0.0256).
rationale: Abstract describes a single group of 28 fourth-grade students with pretest and posttest measurement only, with no control group that does not use generative AI. This is a one-group pre-post design, which the protocol and borderline rules classify as E3. Domain (greenhouse effect, science) and outcome (Three-Tier Test, drawings) appear met; population is elementary students, so E4 does not apply.

quote: A literature review was conducted using various artificial intelligence applications, including Elicit AI, ChatGPT, and Google Scholar.
rationale: The study is a literature review using AI tools by researchers, not an empirical learner-facing intervention with a control group. It is not an empirical study and it concerns social-emotional learning, which is not STEM. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first applicable code under the protocol order, since E1 (learner-facing AI) and E2 (non-STEM content) would also fail; the code order places E1 first, so E1 might be argued instead, but the primary defect is that this is not an empirical study. No learner outcome or control group is reported.

quote: Methods: This tutorial demonstrates a structured implementation process using ChatGPT (GPT-4 model) for text mnemonic generation and DALL-E 3 for visual mnemonic creation.
rationale: The record is a tutorial describing a student-developed implementation process. It reports no controlled comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the reported 85%/95% success rates are process metrics, not learning measures. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the first-applicable-code order, E1 (generative AI is used, though by the student developer rather than as a clearly described learner activity) was not selected because the abstract does not clearly rule out learner-facing use.

quote: involving 68 participants consisting of teachers, staff, and the principal
rationale: Community service program training in-service teachers, staff and principal (population excluded as in-service teachers / not students). The program is a single-group workshop with no control group and no quantitative outcome; it is a community service report. Exclusion code E4 applied as the first clearly failing criterion in order (E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so E4 is the first positive failure reported). Decision is exclude.

quote: We share examples of GenAI responses to three tasks from secondary mathematics
rationale: The abstract describes an analytical/illustrative paper that shares examples of GenAI responses to tasks. It reports no controlled comparison, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails protocol criteria on design, comparison and outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is assigned as the first applicable code under the ordering, although E3 and E5 would also fail. Abstract positively shows no comparison or quantitative outcome, so exclusion is warranted rather than unsure.

quote: This study examines learners' perceptions of usability, enjoyment, and accessibility in AI-powered English learning platforms
rationale: The study concerns English language learning (non-STEM content), which fails the Domain criterion and is excluded under E2 (first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is clearly not generative; here E1 is not clearly established, but the content failure is positive evidence). The study is also a descriptive UEQ perception survey with no control group and no learning outcome, indicating E3/E5 would also apply; per the code order, E2 is reported as the first clear failure given the abstract. Confirmed as a non-STEM, perception-only study.
decision_note: Excluded on non-STEM content (English language learning).

quote: Through a bibliometric analysis of 126 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2014 and 2024 and indexed in Scopus
rationale: The study is a bibliometric analysis of published literature, not an empirical primary study with a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or a quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Exclusion is supported by the abstract's own description of the method. E6 is the first applicable code given the order, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

quote: This systematic literature review maps the empirical research of 41 papers utilizing GenAI and LA
rationale: This is a systematic literature review of 41 papers, not an empirical primary study. It has no comparison group or eligible design of its own. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). The review's synthesized studies are not extracted as separate records here.

quote: A descriptive cross-sectional study with analytical components was conducted at the Faculty of Medical Technical Sciences in Elbasan, Albania.
rationale: The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey of nursing students' AI use and perceptions. It has no experimental or comparison group without generative AI, and its outcomes are perceptions and self-reported impact rather than a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol's design and outcome rules it fails on several criteria. Using the code order, E1 is not clearly the first failure, so I used E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense, i.e., a non-experimental survey design), though E3 and E5 would also apply. Nursing is also health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain.

quote: this study examines the perceptions of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students regarding the use of ChatGPT to enhance their English language skills
rationale: The study targets EFL learners using ChatGPT to improve English language skills, which is language learning and non-STEM content (E2). It is also a survey/TAM perception study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well. Per the code order, E2 is reported first.

criteria.intervention_note: Web 2.0 tools, not generative AI; ChatGPT used only for coding

quote: The review draws on 14 dissertations and analyzes them using thematic coding facilitated by ChatGPT.
rationale: This is a systematic review of 14 dissertations, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. The intervention is Web 2.0 tools (Quizlet, Google Docs, Padlet) rather than learner-facing generative AI, and ChatGPT was used only by the reviewers for coding. Domain is English language teaching, which is non-STEM. Because the record is a review, E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, and the earlier E1 and E2 codes are not used. The quote is a paraphrase-level sentence from the abstract, and the abstract wording is "analyzed using thematic coding facilitated by ChatGPT"; the quote field uses that wording.

quote: with empirical evidence from the sessions indicating that those embracing AI are more aware of their data analysis and can comprehend advice more readily.
rationale: Abstract describes a statistics help drop-in service with pre-visit AI use. No separate control group without generative AI is described, and the only evidence reported is awareness and comprehension of advice (perceptions), not a quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that the comparison and outcome criteria fail, so exclude at abstract stage under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also not described as an experiment.

quote: The 2025 Advancing Healthcare Innovation Summit (AHIS), held virtually on April 26, brought together a broad international audience
rationale: This record is a conference summit report/event summary, not a journal article reporting an empirical comparative study. It describes multiple presentations with no control-group design, no learner-facing generative AI intervention evaluated against a comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Publication type is not eligible (E10) and it is not an empirical study; E10 is the first applicable code given the venue and format. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of ineligible publication type.

quote: The article explores ways to introduce innovative SMART-technologies into the educational process of higher education institutions.
rationale: The abstract is a discursive overview of AI technologies in higher education. It describes no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is positive here because the abstract shows the article is a conceptual essay rather than missing information.

quote: This study examines the relevance and impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in the design of instructional materials for vocational education through a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, which is a review rather than an empirical study (E6). It has no primary comparison group or quantitative learning outcome from an experiment. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the design is a review.

quote: A two-hour workshop engaged 15 purposively sampled stakeholders, including faculty, staff, application readers, and student ambassadors
rationale: The study is a design-thinking workshop on health professions admissions. It has no control group, no learning outcome (only perception surveys and thematic synthesis of ideas), and its participants are faculty, staff, and stakeholders rather than students. Domain is health professions admissions, not STEM. Generative AI is only a topic of discussion, not a learner-facing intervention. Because the study is not an empirical comparison, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study), though it is arguably a qualitative/descriptive workshop. Exclusion is clear on several criteria.

criteria.rationale_note: Abstract describes a course redesign proposal; effectiveness 'remains to be examined'.

quote: Its educational effectiveness remains to be examined using evidence from implementation.
rationale: The paper proposes an AI-assisted course redesign and explicitly states that its educational effectiveness has not yet been examined. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Even if it were considered further, it lacks a control group and outcome data.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract that the paper is a design proposal without an evaluation.

quote: The article presents an information and analytical review of studies and models devoted to the methodology and specific features of applying artificial intelligence (AI) technologies
rationale: The paper is a narrative information and analytical review of other studies, not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome data. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Reviews are also ineligible publication types, but the first applicable code in order is E6 as the study's nature is a review rather than an empirical report.

quote: The Journal of Applied Informatics and Technology (JIT) has published Volume 8, Number 1 (2026): January-June, comprising a total of 13 research articles.
rationale: This is a journal editorial note describing a volume's contents and peer-review process. It reports no empirical study, no generative AI intervention, no comparison group, and no learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Publication type is also not a research article.

quote: We analyze US accounting programs for AIS faculty's (i) individual features and (ii) association with institutional features.
rationale: The study is a faculty-directory analysis of 1998-1999 AIS faculty and institutional characteristics. No learner-facing generative AI intervention is evaluated, no control group, and no learning outcome. It fails the intervention criterion (E1) as the first applicable code in order. Abstract gives positive evidence of no intervention.

quote: Design a semi-structured interview outline to conduct interviews with 5 undergraduate and 5 graduate physical education teachers
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study using grounded theory with 10 pre-service PE students. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is learner-facing, and E2 is unclear because PE is not clearly STEM. E3 (no control group) is the first clearly applicable code. The design also fails the requirement for a comparison and a quantitative outcome.

quote: This annotated bibliography covers books, journal articles, blog posts, news stories, and other resources about the kinds of hostility that we face as philosophers and as university educators
rationale: The record is an annotated bibliography on hostility toward philosophy teachers and university educators. It is not an empirical study, has no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, no STEM learning outcome, and is not a journal article reporting a study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Also not STEM content (philosophy), but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given only after E1 to E5 checks; E1 and E2 are arguably also applicable, so the first applicable code by order would be E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention described). Note: generative AI is mentioned only as a topic of the bibliography, not as an intervention.

quote: 课堂实践结果表明，AI有助于提高学生学习兴趣和课堂参与度，并改善了实验项目完成质量
rationale: The abstract is a teaching-reform description with classroom practice results. It gives no indication of a separate control group without generative AI, and reports improvements in interest, engagement and experiment quality without describing a comparison design. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison group, so exclude under E3. Outcome measurement and design are also unclear from the abstract alone.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion; the abstract shows no comparison group.

quote: Predicting student performance from lifestyle habits and delivering actionable career guidance remain critical yet largely disjoint challenges in engineering education.
rationale: The abstract describes ML prediction models on a lifestyle dataset and a GPT-4o-mini career guidance pipeline, with no control group comparing learners with and without generative AI. Model performance metrics are not learning outcomes of a learner-facing AI intervention, and there is no comparison design (E3 applies). Also, the record is a system description, not a controlled experiment. Coded E3 as the first applicable code, with the abstract giving positive evidence of no control group.

quote: Q There's been a lot of buzz lately about digital technology, from ChatGPT to virtual care. How important is it for nurse leaders to keep abreast of such topics?
