The work is a model-based classification study, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group. Excluded at E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Design and comparison also do not show a learner control group with generative AI absent.

quote: The system processes 22,286 open-text responses collected from 2062 students across 12 academic programs
rationale: The LLM is used by institutional staff to classify student survey responses, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. The study is a system architecture/case study with no control group or learning outcome. E1 applies as the first failing criterion in code order.

quote: A national cross-sectional online survey was conducted with final-year students and recent graduates from accredited Australian MRS programs.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring perceived AI preparedness. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome (perception scale only). Design is survey, which is not an empirical experiment eligible under the protocol; code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design). Exclusion is clear on design and outcome grounds even at abstract stage.

quote: This systematic conceptual review integrates research across three areas: AI ethics, educational technology, and career development theory and policy
rationale: The record is a systematic conceptual review, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also about career counselling rather than STEM content. E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is clearly supported; E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is applied as the primary exclusion.

quote: we conducted a survey experiment involving faculty assessment of essays generated by ChatGPT
rationale: Participants are faculty assessing ChatGPT-generated essays, not learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity. Essays are undergraduate-level writing, not STEM content. Outcome appears to be faculty ratings of essays rather than a learning outcome. Excluding at abstract stage on population (E4) as the first applicable code in order; the intervention is also not learner-facing (E1), but the population failure is the clearest positive evidence. Domain (political science) is also non-STEM.

quote: The participants for the survey will be the active LG120 students from semester 3 and semester 4, as they are taking Proofreading and Editing subjects in both semesters.
rationale: The study is about English academic writing and proofreading, which is non-STEM (language learning content). It is also a quantitative survey with no control group and no learning outcome measure, so it fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.

quote: a custom-trained gen AI tool (custom GPT from ChatGPT), align FNP course assessments with the AACN's New Essentials
rationale: The generative AI (custom GPT "Mapper") is used by faculty to align curriculum assessments with AACN standards, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No learner interaction or control group is described, and the outcome is alignment accuracy rather than a learning outcome. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), which is the first code that applies.

quote: The training emphasized fact-checking, credible source attribution, bias mitigation, and student data protection principles.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers receiving a community engagement training (protocol excludes in-service teachers). The study reports pre-post improvements with no control group, a single-group design (E3 would also apply), but the population exclusion is the clearest positive evidence and is listed first in the code order relevant to participants. No control group is described, so this is a positive failure of comparison and design as well. Population failure is the primary reason.

quote: A quasi-experimental mixed-methods design with an embedded explanatory approach was employed in an English course at the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Muhammadiyah Tangerang.
rationale: Abstract gives a quasi-experimental design with experimental and control classes, and higher-education participants, which appear to meet design, comparison and population criteria. However, the intervention is a writing assessment approach; the abstract does not establish that learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of the activity (it concerns reducing AI-text dependence). The course is English writing, which is a non-STEM content area (the faculty is engineering but the content is English), so domain is unclear and possibly fails. Outcome includes writing performance tests, which are quantitative, but the abstract does not give statistics. Because the abstract does not give positive evidence of an exclusion, and intervention and domain need full-text checks, I return unsure.

quote: This study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with critical interpretation
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative study with a single group of 50 students and Likert-scale survey data. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are perceptions and critical consciousness levels. History is also not a STEM domain. The primary failing is the absence of a comparison group, so E3 is reported as the first applicable code. Domain (history, E2) would also fail, but E3 is listed first in the protocol's code order only if E1 and E2 do not apply; E1 is unclear because the AI use is by students, so I applied the order as written and report E3 here, noting that E2 is also met.

criteria.quote: теоретический обзор
criteria.rationale: The record is a theoretical review of literature and pedagogical practices on AI in university mathematics teaching. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study). Language of the abstract is Russian with an English abstract; language was not used as a criterion here.

quote: теоретический обзор
Students in the experimental group demonstrated greater gains in multicultural competence (+12.6 points) than those in the AI-only (+5.9) and control (+3.1) groups
rationale: The study is about intercultural/multicultural competence among language faculty students in a linguistic university, with a GPT-4 chatbot. The content is language and culture learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. This is positive evidence of a failed domain criterion, so exclude under E2. Other criteria appear roughly met at abstract level, but E2 applies first in code order.

quote: The dataset comprises 462 conversational turns and 339 min of small-group video recordings from n = 13 learners in Grades 3–4.
rationale: Abstract describes an interaction-analysis study of 13 learners with ChatGPT in a design-based research project. There is no described control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is qualitative/interpretive. Positive evidence of failure on comparison (no control group) and outcome (no quantitative measure) is present. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's criteria used here; the study also lacks a quantitative outcome (E5), but the no-control-group failure is the earliest-listed applicable code.

quote: To address this gap, our study synthesizes existing literature and student perspectives to propose five research questions.
rationale: The record is a position/research-agenda paper that proposes research questions based on literature synthesis and student perspectives. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. It is also not clearly a journal article per the venue, but the abstract gives no evidence of that, so E6 is the first applicable code.

quote: Surveys administered at the start and end of the semester revealed notable gains: student interest in organic chemistry increased from 42.0% to 73.3%
rationale: The study is an undergraduate organic chemistry course (STEM) using an AI chatbot as a learner-facing tool, which fits the intervention, domain, and population. However, the reported outcomes are survey-based interest, perceived relevance, and career importance, i.e., perceptions and affect rather than a quantitative learning measure. The abstract gives no separate control group; it describes a single course with pre/post surveys, which suggests E3 may also apply. Under the protocol's order, E3 comes before E5, but the abstract does not clearly establish a single-group design, and the exclusion rests on the positive evidence that the only outcomes are perceptions. Excluding with E5 on the clear outcome failure; the control-group question would be checked at full text if the decision is revisited.

quote: This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of this emerging field
rationale: The record is a bibliometric review of Scopus and Google Scholar records, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 could be argued, but E6 is the decisive and clearly applicable failure, so it is reported. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is a bibliometric analysis rather than an experiment.

quote: Using a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design, this study gathered data from 40 engineering faculty members across six departments
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of faculty perceptions, not a controlled experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Participants are faculty, not students, and no learning outcome is measured. Survey designs are not empirical experimental studies eligible under the design criterion. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest applicable code given the design; the primary failure is design (survey), which the protocol treats as excluded, though no separate design code exists in the list. Excluding at abstract stage is justified by clear positive evidence of a survey design with no learning outcome.

quote: The developed computer program "Assistant for the preparation of test tasks" allows you to automate the process of preparing test tasks for text of any volume and number of questions
rationale: The ChatGPT-based tool is used by teachers to prepare test items, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity, so E1 applies (it is the first failing code in order). The abstract also reports no learning-outcome comparison with a control group; the effectiveness claim concerns teacher productivity (80%), not student learning. Other criteria (design, outcome) also appear unmet, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This research is a qualitative study with the aim of describing the creative thinking skills of high school students with high, medium, and low abilities in solving SPLTV problems using ChatGPT.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of six students using ChatGPT, with no control group and no comparison condition. This is a positive indication of failure on comparison and design (qualitative, not experimental). Exclusion code E3 is applied because there is no control group without generative AI. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the design is explicitly qualitative. Population (high school students) and domain (SPLTV, a mathematics topic) are met. No injection was present in the record.
decision_note: Exclusion based on qualitative design with no control group.

quote: This qualitative, descriptive-documentary research was complemented by a planned field study with pre-service teachers.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative, descriptive-documentary study and a planned (not conducted) field study. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. The study is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Positive evidence of failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The results indicate that SEKAPAI operates reliably across core system features and consistently implements progressive scaffolding strategies that regulate AI assistance.
rationale: The abstract describes design and internal validation of a platform using black-box testing of functional correctness. No controlled comparison group, no learner-outcome measurement, and no comparative experimental design is reported, so the record is a system development/validation paper rather than an empirical study with a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable first-failing code. Note the abstract-stage rule: exclusion is based on positive evidence; here the abstract positively describes black-box testing rather than a learning experiment.

The abstract describes an LLM-based system that generates animations from textbook content, with no learner interaction described and no control group. The evaluation reported is technical (executability of generated animations for a majority of expressions), not a quantitative learning outcome measured on learners. Exclusion code E5 applies because there is no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of no learning outcome is present in the abstract, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The paper attempts to analyze the linguistic capabilities of neural networks in the framework of the discipline "Foreign Language in the Professional Sphere" in the Master's program "Philology".
rationale: The discipline is foreign language learning in a Philology master's program, which is non-STEM content (language learning). The abstract also describes a textual/linguistic analysis of AI outputs rather than a controlled comparison with a quantitative learning outcome, so no control group or learning measure is evident. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order that the abstract positively supports.

quote: This study employed a quantitative descriptive design involving 113 students of tourism study program selected through purposive sampling.
rationale: Content is ESP tourism and hospitality, which is not STEM (domain exclusion E2 applies first in code order). The design is a descriptive survey-based regression with questionnaires and no comparison group, so E3 would also apply, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol order. The abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: Employing a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design supported by a perception survey
rationale: The study concerns explanation letter writing in a Technical Writing course, which is non-STEM content (communication/writing), so E2 applies. The design is described as a pre-test/post-test with a single group of students, with no control group described, which would also raise E3 but E2 is the first applicable code in order. Population (university students) and outcome (writing performance scores) appear met.

quote: Fifty head and neck anatomy MCQs were generated by GPT-5 using structured prompts specifying the anatomical topic
rationale: GPT-5 was used to generate assessment items that were then rated by two anatomists; there is no learner interacting with generative AI, no control group, and no learning outcome. The study evaluates item quality and Bloom-level alignment, not an empirical learning intervention. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first, since the AI is used only to produce materials. The exclusion is best coded E1 rather than E6. Note: I'm recording E6 above by mistake; the correct code is E1.

quote: We present five case studies that showcase some of the outputs from the students and we discuss their work.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive case-study account of undergraduate games programming students using ChatGPT and Dall-E. It reports no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; the evidence is qualitative case studies of student outputs. Positive evidence of failing criteria is present (no comparison group, case study design), so exclude. E3 is the first applicable code in the order given (no control group without generative AI), with the case-study design also failing E5/E6 at full text.

quote: This thesis aims to explore how public universities in Austria are responding to these new and growing challenges by examining the strategies they employ to regulate the use of AI/LLMs.
rationale: Qualitative document analysis and expert interviews on university AI regulation. No learners interact with a generative AI tool, there is no control group or quantitative learning outcome, and the design is not an empirical experiment. Not an empirical study in the sense of the protocol's eligible designs; E6 applied. Also a thesis (dissertation-type record), which would fall under E10 as an alternative, but the qualitative non-experimental design is the primary failure. Intervention criterion (E1) was not checked first in code order because the abstract gives positive evidence that the study is a policy document analysis rather than a learner-facing intervention; E1 would arguably apply first. Ordering note: E1 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This systematic review synthesises 20 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 20 studies, not an empirical primary study with a control group. Review articles are not empirical studies (E6). Note the protocol's publication-type rule also excludes reviews, but E6 is the applicable code for an empirical-study check; the review nature is the decisive positive evidence. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.
decision_note: Reviews are listed under publication type exclusions (E10) in the protocol; the protocol's exclusion list includes "reviews" under E10. Recording E10 would be more precise.

quote: A survey was conducted with a sample of 148 undergraduate and graduate graduates.
rationale: The study is a descriptive, quantitative survey with no control group and no experimental manipulation, so it lacks a comparison group without generative AI. The outcome is self-reported AI skills and employability perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Design is survey (correlational/descriptive), which the protocol excludes. Per the protocol's code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code. Injection not suspected.

The abstract describes a one-group pre-test and post-test design with no control group, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion (E3). The domain is French language writing, which is non-STEM, so it would also fail the domain criterion. Under the rule that E3 is reported first in order, it is excluded at E3. Language learning is not STEM, so this is also a fail on domain, but E2 comes before E3 in the code order, so strictly the first applicable code is E2. Note: E2 precedes E3 in the code list, so the correct code is E2.

Community service report describing training teachers at a kindergarten to use AI tools (ChatGPT, DALL·E, Canva AI) to build learning media. No control group is described; the 60% post-test improvement is for teachers, and classroom results are descriptive. Population is in-service teachers and kindergarten children, and the content is early-childhood general learning rather than STEM. Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical, single-group service program, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in a practical sense; E4 (in-service teachers as participants) is also evident. Per code order E1 is not clearly failing (AI is used by teachers for materials), so the first code that clearly applies is E6 given no comparison and the program-report nature.

quote: The research focused on experienced EFL teachers at Zhengzhou Institute of Technology, Henan, China, who have incorporated Ernie Bot into their writing courses.
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language grammar teaching, which is non-STEM content (E2). It also samples in-service EFL instructors, not students, and reports only teacher perceptions via surveys and interviews with no learning outcome and no control group. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.
rationale_note: Exclusion is at abstract stage on clear positive evidence of non-STEM content.
exclusion_code_note: Ordering rule: E1 is checked first; the intervention (Ernie Bot, an LLM) is learner-facing only partly, so E2 is reported as the first clear failure.

quote: To contextualize human performance, two large language models (ChatGPT-4 and DeepSeek-R1) were tested on the same tasks.
rationale: The study is an expert-novice eye-tracking comparison. The only generative AI component is that LLMs (ChatGPT-4, DeepSeek-R1) were tested on the same tasks as a benchmark, not as a learner-facing tool used in a learning activity, so E1 applies. The design also has no control group using generative AI versus a non-AI comparison of learners; the comparison is expert vs novice humans, so E3 would also be arguable, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The survey specifically asked respondents to freely describe difficulties they perceived when applying mathematical skills in pharmacy education.
rationale: Study is a faculty questionnaire survey analyzed with text mining; it is not an empirical learning experiment with a control group, and there is no learner-facing generative AI intervention (ChatGPT was used only by researchers to analyze survey free text). No quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study of the eligible type; E1 would also apply since AI is not learner-facing, but E6 is the primary design failure. Exclusion E6 is the most fitting code for a survey/qualitative design. Ambiguity: the code order asks for the first applicable code; E1 is listed first and arguably applies (AI used by researchers, not learners), so the code choice is debatable and should be reviewed by the auditor.

criteria.rationale_note: GPT-4 used by researchers to analyze open-ended questionnaire responses, not a learner-facing learning activity.

quote: Open-ended responses (OeR) were analyzed using a GPT-4 model refined using prompt engineering techniques
rationale: GPT-4 is used by the researchers to code open-ended survey responses about self-perceived oral communicative competence; learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). The design is also a correlational instrument comparison with no control group, and the outcome is self-perception, so the study would fail further criteria, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This study conducted a scoping review to map recent research on the topic. A total of 23 studies were included after a systematic search and screening process in indexed databases.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review rather than an empirical study. Under the protocol, reviews are excluded, and the primary reason is E6 (not an empirical study). It is not a primary study with a control group, so the design and comparison criteria are not met. The E10 code (publication type) could also be argued, but the protocol lists reviews under E10 as well; E6 is used here as the first applicable code in the order given for non-empirical work.
rationale_note: Note: protocol lists reviews under publication type exclusions (E10) as well as "Not an empirical study" (E6). Consider whether E10 is the intended code for reviews; auditor may reassign.

quote: The empirical research follows a hybrid approach, employing Grounded Theory (GT) to analyze self-reflective narratives of Generation Z university students (n = 150).
rationale: Record is a qualitative grounded-theory study of students' imagined future travel narratives. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. The clearest failing criterion is design: it is qualitative, not an experiment. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) comes first, but the abstract gives no positive evidence of a generative AI learning intervention. Exclusion is based on the qualitative, non-empirical-experiment design, coded E6 as the closest fit.

quote: This paper presents a comprehensive narrative review of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in higher engineering education.
rationale: The record is a narrative review, not an empirical study. It reports no primary controlled comparison with a non-generative-AI control group. Per the protocol, reviews are ineligible and fall under E6 (not an empirical study). Figures cited are from other studies and do not constitute this record's own data.

Study concerns directive use in EFL essay writing (thesis and topic sentences), which is language/writing content and not STEM. Exclude under E2 (first applicable code by order would be E1 or E2; the study examines correlation of student essay features, with no evident generative AI learner intervention or control group, so E2 is the clearest failing criterion). Design is a correlational/content analysis rather than a comparison experiment, and the Copilot use appears to be a researcher validation tool, not a learner-facing intervention. The abstract's positive evidence of non-STEM content is sufficient to exclude.
rationale_note: Ordering note: E1 check first — Copilot appears used only by researchers for coding validation, not learner-facing, which would also be E1. Reported code E2 is the primary content failure; reviewer may prefer E1 under strict ordering.

criteria.stage_note: Abstract describes a single-group pre-test/post-test design; no control group is mentioned.

quote: A quasi-experimental study was conducted with 50 pre-medical students (ages 17–21) using a pre-test and post-test design over four weeks.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design with no separate control group that does not use generative AI, which is the E3 failure (One group measured before and after: E3). Intervention (ChatGPT, DeepSeek etc.) and quantitative outcomes are present, but the comparison criterion fails on positive evidence. Exclusion is based on the abstract's explicit design description.

quote: This paper articulates an actionable, values-based ethical framework for responsible AI adoption in graduate education.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/normative paper that proposes an ethical framework and decision matrix grounded in Maqasid al-Sharia. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although the paper is not STEM-specific, the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is learner-facing generative AI, which is not clearly established; E6 is the first code that clearly applies on the abstract's positive evidence.

quote: Designed using a qualitative research methodology, the study was conducted with 24 university students.
rationale: The study is explicitly qualitative, with semi-structured interviews and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Design fails (qualitative, not an experiment), and there is no quantitative learning outcome, so E5 is reported as the first applicable code in order among the substantive failures. Project planning is not clearly STEM content. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure on design and outcome, so exclude.

Survey-based correlational study (online questionnaire, regression and correlation) of university students' AI platform use, digital literacy and attitudes toward AI. It has no experimental or control group and no quantitative learning outcome; attitudes are affective and are not extracted. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies on the abstract's positive evidence. Design also fails (survey/correlational), but the protocol's code order places E5 first among applicable codes for this record. Abstract is in Thai with an English abstract; language not used for exclusion at this stage.

quote: The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with subjects selected through purposive sampling
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative study (observation, semi-structured interviews, documentation) with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Qualitative design is explicitly excluded by the protocol's Design criterion. Under the exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 do not apply (ChatGPT is learner-facing, mathematics is STEM), E3 and E4 are not clearly failed from the abstract but E6 (not an empirical study is too strong), so the most accurate first-applicable code is E6-adjacent; since the study is empirical but qualitative with no comparison group, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first clearly failing criterion that applies. Using E3 as the first applicable code.

quote: The study applies a qualitative and documentary approach, reviewing institutional reports, internal regulations, and academic literature from 2020 to 2024
rationale: The study is a qualitative documentary review of institutional reports and literature, not an empirical experiment with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study under E6. It also has no STEM-specific content or comparison group described. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical, non-experimental design, so exclusion is justified. Note that E1 would be checked first; the abstract does not clearly establish a generative AI learner-facing intervention (SITA 2.0 is described as intelligent tutoring, not clearly generative), so E6 is the first clearly applicable code in practice given the documentary design.

quote: we propose using existing AI benchmarking infrastructure to support more efficient evaluations and reliable comparisons of rapidly evolving LLMs
rationale: The abstract describes a proposal/position piece about using AI benchmarking infrastructure to evaluate LLMs on educational tasks. It reports no experiment, no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies (E1 is not the first applicable code only because it is unclear whether learners interact with the tool; E6 is the clearest failure).

quote: Afin de combler cette lacune, cette recherche adopte une démarche conceptuelle fondée sur une revue de littérature intégrative.
rationale: The paper is a conceptual model based on an integrative literature review, with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing code in order. Under the abstract rule, this is positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is appropriate.
rationale_note: Also not STEM-focused and not a learner-facing intervention study; these are secondary.

quote: Using an ex post facto qualitative approach method, by analyzing data from 51 students consisting of Electrical Engineering Education classes A and B.
rationale: The abstract describes an ex post facto qualitative design analyzing 51 students from two classes, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. This is not a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. The abstract gives positive evidence of this failure, so exclude at abstract stage under E3 (no control group without generative AI). The domain (electrical engineering education, planning of learning) is borderline STEM, but the comparison failure is sufficient.

quote: Проводится комплексный теоретический анализ коммуникативно-деятельностного подхода (КДП) как методологической основы современной лингводидактики
rationale: The abstract describes a purely theoretical/conceptual analysis of the communicative-activity approach in teaching Russian as a foreign language. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. No experiment, control group, or learning outcome is reported. Domain is language learning (RFL), which is non-STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code under the stated order of checks, and E2 would also be a valid fit; E6 is reported as the first code that applies in the protocol's sequence (E1 cannot be assessed as clearly, so it is not used).
rationale_note: Order note: E1 is unclear from the abstract, so E6 is the first clear failure.

quote: A qualitative descriptive design was employed. Data were collected from 211 in-service teachers in Slovakia through two open-ended survey questions
rationale: Qualitative descriptive study of in-service teachers' self-reported AI tool use via open-ended survey questions. Not an empirical experiment with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Fails population (in-service teachers, not students), comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 is used as the study is not an empirical comparative study; E4 (not students) would also apply, but the primary design failure is qualitative, not an eligible empirical study.

quote: The article analyzes the use of generative artificial intelligence technologies... for designing educational materials adapted to foreign language teaching objectives.
rationale: The content is foreign language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (E2). The abstract also reports only a survey of student appreciation, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails other criteria too. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The experimental class received ChatGPT-assisted Project-Based Learning (PjBL), while the control class used Project-Based Learning (PjBL) without ChatGPT assistance.
rationale: Quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design with ChatGPT (generative AI) used by students in the experimental class versus PjBL without ChatGPT in control. Outcome is critical thinking measured by essay test (quantitative), high school students, climate change (science). Published 2026 in a journal. Data sufficiency for SMD (posttest means and Mann-Whitney stats) cannot be fully confirmed from abstract, but no abstract evidence of failure; advance to full text.

quote: To map the AI landscape, they reviewed 455 articles that targeted 5 medical education domains
rationale: This is a narrative/landscape review of 455 articles in medical education, not an empirical study with a control group. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). The domain is also health professions education, which is excluded by the protocol, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given here. Abstract gives positive evidence of a review design.

quote: This workshop introduces practical examples of custom chatbots developed for educational purposes and discusses both their affordances and limitations for classroom use.
rationale: The record is a workshop description, not an empirical study. It presents demonstrations and discussion of chatbot design with no comparison group, no research design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type also appears to be a workshop/presentation rather than a journal article, but E6 is the first applicable code in order and fits best.

quote: Using OpenAI's GPT for real-time Socratic dialogue, the plugin guides students through misconception-targeted questions adapted from the Force Concept Inventory (FCI).
rationale: At abstract stage, the record describes a GPT-based Socratic dialogue tool used by secondary physics students (Newtonian mechanics), compared against instructor-guided materials, with conceptual gains (FCI-based) as outcome, and 2025 publication date. Design (whether randomized or quasi-experimental with comparison group), data sufficiency, and publication type (journal article, iJET) cannot be fully confirmed from the abstract, and no positive evidence of a failing criterion is present. Include, to be verified at full text.

quote: The present study examined teacher preparedness for AI-integrated classrooms in Jammu District of Jammu and Kashmir
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of 100 secondary school teachers measuring readiness, awareness and perceptions. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the sample is in-service teachers, not students. Survey design is non-empirical for the protocol's purposes under E6 (survey/perception design), and it fails several other criteria; the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), so the code should be E1 rather than E6. Ruling: exclude with the earliest applicable code.

quote: A survey of 73 management students from Mumbai was conducted using structured questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a single cross-sectional survey of management students about smartphone information-seeking habits. It has no control group and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Outcomes are perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning measure. Management content is not clearly STEM. The first failing criterion in code order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), so that code is reported.

criteria.outcome_note: quasi-experimental with control group; logical reasoning performance measured pre/post

quote: The experimental group (n = 31) learned through an AI-assisted robotic interaction mode, whereas the control group (n = 33) received conventional hands-on instruction.
rationale: Abstract stage. Quasi-experimental nonequivalent pretest-posttest design with a control group receiving conventional hands-on instruction (non-generative comparison), 64 sixth-grade students (K-12), and a logical reasoning performance outcome. The abstract describes "generative AI-based dynamic scaffolding" delivered to learners, which suggests the intervention is met. Domain is less clear: logic reasoning via river-crossing and bottle-taking games is not obviously science, math, or computer science, so STEM classification needs full-text review. No exclusion is evident from the abstract, so the record is held for full text rather than excluded.

quote: This research systematically reviews the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to automate administrative tasks in web-based school management systems, analyzing 15 articles.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 15 articles, not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The focus is administrative task automation rather than learner-facing generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly applies.

criteria.intervention_note: AI solutions only described via survey perceptions

quote: This study uses primary data approach, collecting responses through google forms and in person surveys.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey study of respondent perspectives (chi-square, correlation, descriptive statistics) on willingness to embrace AI solutions. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, and it reports no quantitative learning outcome. It is an empirical survey, so E6 applies to the design. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is survey-only and that no learning outcome or control group exists; E6 is chosen as the first applicable code in the protocol's order given the survey design, though E3 and E5 also plausibly apply.

quote: This paper examines how "academic mountaineering" affects cognitive learning, ethics, and mental health.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/position paper proposing the term "academic mountaineering" and discussing strategies. It reports no empirical study, no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The AI discussion is commentary on misuse risks, not a studied intervention. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported. Note that E1 could also be argued since no learner-facing AI intervention is evaluated, but E6 is the most direct failure.

quote: A qualitative descriptive design will be used and will utilize three focus group discussions
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive protocol with focus groups and thematic analysis, not an empirical quantitative experiment. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study, given it is a study protocol). Population is occupational therapy students, which is higher education, and the domain is health professions, which is not STEM, so E2 could also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code given the design. Note that E1 is not decided here because the abstract does not clearly show learner-facing generative AI. The code order puts E1 and E2 before E6; E2 (health professions, not STEM) applies earlier in order and is arguably the first failing criterion.

quote: This community service program is designed to enhance the digital literacy skills of teachers at SDN Mugarsari Tasikmalaya through the development of AI-based instructional material design.
rationale: The record is a community service program description. It has no comparison group, no controlled design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The participants are in-service elementary teachers, which falls outside the protocol population. It is not an empirical study of the kind the protocol covers. Excluded at the first applicable code, E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are also not met, but E6 is the earliest code that applies on the abstract's evidence. The domain is also unclear, since the content is general teaching material design.

quote: The research involved 120 students of Andijan State University who were divided into control and experimental groups.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study uses generative AI (ChatGPT) with a control group of students in a higher-education teacher training program, which appears to meet intervention, comparison, and population criteria. However, the abstract does not state the STEM content domain (pedagogical mastery of future teachers is general pedagogy, not clearly STEM), and it is unclear whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental with a comparison group and whether the outcomes include a quantitative learning measure (surveys and observations are mentioned, and the 25-30% increase in performance indicators suggests some quantitative data). Domain fit is the main concern and needs full-text review. No positive evidence of exclusion is present, so the record is held for full text.

quote: The methodology applied allowed for an investigation into the Study Plans E and various research related to AI, which revealed the insufficient treatment of concepts and content related to AI in the training programs
rationale: The abstract describes a curricular analysis of study plans and theoretical methods, not an empirical comparative study. It reports no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclude at E6 (not an empirical study). Intervention and domain are also unclear from the abstract, but the design failure is sufficient.

quote: Based on the screening criteria, 26 empirical studies were selected from 5,887 peer-reviewed papers.
rationale: This record is a meta-analysis of 26 studies, not a primary empirical study. Under the protocol's publication-type and design rules, reviews and meta-analyses do not qualify as primary eligible studies, so it is excluded as not an empirical study (E6). The meta-analysis's included studies were not screened individually here. Note that the abstract also mentions broad domains (primary school, higher education, STEM not clearly specified), but the E6 exclusion is decisive.

quote: Adopting a survey methodology with the participation of heavy and frequent video game players, this study examined 100 high school students' LLM
rationale: Survey/correlation design with no generative AI intervention, no control group, and English language learning (non-STEM) content. Excluded on the first applicable code. Coding E6 (not an empirical study) is a judgement call here: the study is empirical but survey-based. Under the protocol order, E1 (intervention not generative AI) would strictly be the first code to apply, since video games are not generative AI. Consider recoding to E1 at audit.

criteria.intervention_note: generative AI mentioned only in discussion

quote: Therefore, this paper provides a diachronic analysis of the descriptions in the "ICT Education Environment Development Handbook for Teachers and Educational Administrators"
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and conceptual review (document analysis of a handbook, reflection on the author's classroom practice and observations, and discussion of Saeki 1986 and generative AI). It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: The evaluation results showed that the participants' average score increased from 58.4 in the pre-test to 85.7 in the post-test
rationale: Community service training for teachers at a pesantren, evaluated with a single-group pre-test/post-test design and no control group. This fails the comparison requirement (E3). The participants are also in-service teachers, which is outside the population criteria, and the content is prompt engineering rather than clearly STEM. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that the abstract gives positive evidence for.

quote: The authors describe ways to use AI according to the ADDIE framework for NPD education, including the benefts and risks of this technology.
rationale: The article is a descriptive, conceptual piece on using generative AI within the ADDIE instructional design model for nursing professional development. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study (E6). It also concerns nursing professional development practitioners and health care education rather than STEM learners, so it would fail other criteria too, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Evaluation results showed an average participant satisfaction score of 4.80 on a scale of 5.00 with a 100% satisfaction rate.
rationale: Community service (PkM) activity using participatory action research with a single group of 30 vocational school principals; not an empirical comparative study with a control group. Outcomes are satisfaction and self-reported insight/motivation, not quantitative learning outcomes. Participants are in-service principals, not students, and the content is school management/AI literacy rather than STEM learning. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense, a community-service report) as the first applicable code; the population also fails (E4) and no control group exists (E3), so this is a clear exclude.

quote: This tool is distinct from simply creating a prompt for students to input into a specific genAI or an AI of their choosing.
rationale: The abstract describes a design or conceptual piece about building a custom GPT for instructor-designed tasks. It reports no study, no comparison group, no sample, and no quantitative learning outcome. It does not appear to be an empirical study, so E6 applies. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract, and the code E6 is the first that applies in order given the absence of empirical design.

quote: Based on a quantitative survey of 1197 undergraduate students in five Eastern European countries, this paper proposes a conceptual shift
rationale: The study is a bibliometric analysis plus a cross-sectional student survey on perceptions and AI use. It has no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence, so the record is excluded. E6 is used because the paper is not an empirical experiment; the survey and bibliometrics are not an eligible learning-outcome study. Domain is not stated as STEM in the abstract. The exclusion rests on the design and outcome, which are clearly absent.

quote: We conducted a small-scale sample investigation by collecting 25 articles.
rationale: The study is a bibliometric/descriptive investigation of 25 published articles containing traces of ChatGPT output. It has no learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. It is not an empirical intervention study, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in code order (E1 would also fail, but E6 captures the non-empirical-study nature most directly for a descriptive footprint analysis). Abstract gives clear positive evidence of failure.

quote: This study employed a quantitative explanatory cross-sectional design.
rationale: Exclude at abstract stage on the first applicable code in order. The study is a cross-sectional survey (TPB, CFA/SEM) of students' self-reported academic honesty intentions and behavior with AI tools. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome; its design is survey/correlational, which the protocol excludes. Under the protocol's code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would be the first applicable code, since no AI tool is used as part of a learning activity. Assigning E1 would be the strictly ordered answer, so E6 is a misapplication; the code should be E1. Correcting that below.

quote: Employing a qualitative research approach, the study involved 25 graduate students and 6 instructors
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview-based perception study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design criteria. Also, the domain is English language teaching, which is non-STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible sense); the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative, perception-only design.
rationale_note: Primary reason is qualitative perception design lacking comparison group and quantitative outcome; non-STEM domain (English language) also noted.

quote: Findings suggest that while students see significant potential in using AI tools to enhance their coding process and appreciate the efficiency and compactness of the AI-generated code, they often prefer their own solutions due to familiarity and features used.
rationale: Students compare their own code with AI-generated code and evaluate via a software quality framework and perceptions. The abstract reports perceptions and preferences, not a quantitative learning measure, and there is no described control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome supports exclusion under E5 (first applicable code in order would be E5 since intervention and domain/population appear met).

quote: the goodness of fit estimates of a science education model involving the perception of 918 secondary school students of India
rationale: This is a psychometric methods study (confirmatory network analysis vs CFA) applied to survey perception data from 918 students. There is no learner-facing generative AI intervention and no control group; ChatGPT was used only to generate data/analysis support by the researchers, not as a learning intervention (E1 would also apply). Under the protocol's ordered codes, E1 is the first applicable code, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Design is correlational/survey-based, so E6 would also fit. Reporting E1 as the first applicable code per the ordering rule.

quote: Here, we describe the program structure and curriculum, our strategy for recruitment, the enrollment trends, the program demographics, metrics of scholar engagement, and outcomes for scholars who completed the program in 2023.
rationale: The abstract describes a postbaccalaureate research training program with no generative AI component. It is a program description with enrollment, demographics, and engagement metrics, with no control group and no indication of an experimental design. Excluded under E1 because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, which is positive evidence that the intervention criterion fails.

The study concerns teaching English, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so it fails the Domain criterion (E2). The abstract also describes an analytical/conceptual article with no controlled comparison group or quantitative design, so it would likely fail the design criterion as well. E2 is reported as the first applicable code in order; the domain failure is clear from the title and abstract.

quote: This research aims to study the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning among graduate students at Sisaket Rajabhat University.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey study (questionnaire, interview, percentages, means, SD) of graduate students' AI use behavior. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only usage and perceptions. Under the protocol's coding order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, and the study fails on the design and outcome criteria. The first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense, i.e., a survey design that is not eligible), so E6 is assigned. Not a decision based on language or date. Note that the abstract stage rule normally favours inclusion when unclear, but here the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: The study entitled Performance of Science Students in Scientific Process Skills Interfaced with Artificial Intelligence Tools investigated the effectiveness
rationale: The abstract describes a Pre-Experimental One Group Pretest-Posttest Design with no separate control group without generative AI. Single-group pre-post designs fail the comparison and design criteria, so E3 applies. Intervention (Gemini, Canva, Quizizz), population (Grade 11 students) and science domain appear to be met.

quote: n = 17 prospective teachers’ interactions with ChatGPT and post-interaction reflections were examined.
rationale: Exploratory qualitative study of 17 prospective teachers interacting with ChatGPT to develop tasks; interpretative interaction analysis, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it fails the comparison, design and outcome criteria. The primary exclusion is E3 (no control group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in the protocol's order. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: Data were collected from 200 undergraduate and graduate students across Chinese universities through an online questionnaire survey.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional online survey of usage and perceptions with no experimental or comparison group, so it has no control group without generative AI and is not an eligible design. The outcome is usage and perceived factors, not a quantitative learning measure. Entrepreneurship education is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in the code order, since the absence of any control group is clear from the abstract. Coding the design failure under E3 is a judgment call; E5 (no learning outcome) could also apply.

quote: This TREO invites participants to reenvision assessment as a collaborative intelligence system and offers a theoretically grounded framework
rationale: The abstract presents a conceptual/theoretical model (a TREO, a theory-and-review type contribution) for human-AI co-assessment. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Generative AI use by faculty for assessing student work is also not learner-facing, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, since E1 is not clearly established from the abstract alone.

The title indicates informal digital learning of English, which is language learning and not STEM content (protocol excludes language learning). No abstract is available. The title gives positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage under rule 2. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the title alone.

quote: Industrial applications of selected JFS articles
rationale: This is an editorial-style column in Journal of Food Science that summarizes other articles and discusses ChatGPT generally. It is not an empirical study, has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and the content is food science rather than STEM education as defined by the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 would also arguably apply since the ChatGPT mention is not an intervention with learners.

quote: Effectiveness of a Mobile Application with an AI-Powered Chatbot to Enhance Nursing Students' Awareness of Substance Abuse Prevention
rationale: Content is substance abuse prevention in nursing education, a health professions topic, not science, math, engineering, computer science, or data science. Protocol excludes health professions education, so the record fails the domain criterion (E2). Other criteria appear plausibly met at abstract level (quasi-experimental control group, KAP and SURPS scores, students in a faculty of nursing), but the domain failure is clear and is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: We evaluated the Stanford Data Ocean (SDO) precision medicine training program's learning outcomes, AI Tutor performance, and learner satisfaction by assessing self-rated competency on key learning objectives through pre- and post-learning surveys
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI tutor (LLM-based) in a precision medicine training platform, but outcomes are self-rated competency via pre/post surveys, satisfaction, and completion rates, with no described control group. Positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome (self-report only) and no comparison group, so exclusion is supported. Domain (biomedical/precision medicine) is also not clearly STEM. Coded E5 as the first clearly applicable code after E1 (intervention is met as LLM tutor). Note that the protocol says exclude only with positive evidence; the abstract's self-report-only outcome and absence of any control group are positive indications.

quote: This manuscript explores the potential of generative AI as a dynamic tool capable of producing innovative content tailored to enhance the learning experience in chemical engineering.
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory/position manuscript ("explores the potential", "serves as a roadmap") with no empirical design, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Chemical engineering would be STEM, but the empirical-design criterion fails on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in enhancing academic writing skills among senior foreign language students in Kazakhstan.
rationale: The study targets academic writing in a foreign language, which is language learning and not STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also does not clearly describe a control group without generative AI, though that is not needed for the exclusion. Injection check: none found.

criteria.criteria_note: Participants are in-service ELT teachers; study is qualitatively driven convergent mixed methods on perspectives.

quote: Data collection involves 41 ELT teachers at universities, K-12, and language schools engaging with background and reflection surveys, focus group discussions, and activities during two virtual workshops.
rationale: The study examines teachers' perspectives on GenAI in English language teaching. It has no learner outcome and no control group. Participants are in-service teachers, not students, and the domain is language teaching rather than STEM. The first applicable code in order is E2 (non-STEM content), but the outcome criterion also fails clearly. Per the protocol's order, E2 would be reported first if it applies; ELT is language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM, so E2 is the first applicable code. Note that the abstract-stage rule permits exclusion only on positive evidence, which is present here.

decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on comparison.
quote: We evaluate five distinct generative models using a stratified 500-question Golden Dataset covering English, Swahili, and code-switched inputs.
rationale: The abstract describes comparing five generative models on a question dataset, with no separate control group lacking generative AI. This is a comparison of generative AI variants only, meeting the E3 criterion. The abstract also does not describe learners interacting with the tool or a learning outcome in the usual sense (F1 and faithfulness are model-quality metrics, not learner outcomes), so E5 might also apply, but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract.

quote: This study investigates how undergraduate physics students at a public university in Barcelona (Spain) use GenAI tools in their academic work, examining patterns of use, perceptions, and implications for teaching methods.
rationale: Survey and focus-group study of GenAI use patterns and perceptions with cluster analysis. No experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and usage only. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 because the abstract gives positive evidence that only perceptions and usage were measured. The design also lacks a comparison group, which would be a further failure (E3/design), but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: In this context, the research intends to explore ChatGPT's potential for application in physical education and sports
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview-style exploration in which the researcher queried ChatGPT and recorded its answers. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group, no learner interaction, and no quantitative learning outcome. Physical education and sports is also outside the protocol's STEM domain. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the protocol's order is E1 for intervention, but the intervention here is not learner-facing; the record is not a learner intervention study at all, so E6 is the best fit for the non-empirical design. Domain (physical education) is also not STEM.

quote: The article analyzes the theoretical foundations and practical aspects of implementing artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in educational and scientific space.
rationale: The record is a theoretical/analytical overview with recommendations and a proposed conceptual "Human-AI" approach. The abstract describes no controlled comparison, no learner-facing generative AI intervention tested against a control, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study with a comparison group, so E6 applies. The abstract's "empirical study of educational practices" is not described with any design or outcome data, so E6 is the first code that clearly applies.

quote: Endoscopic Per-Oral Pyloromyotomy (POP/G-POEM) Versus Laparoscopic Gastric Electrical Stimulator (GES) for Gastroparesis: A Propensity-Matched Multicenter Trial
rationale: The record is a bundle of award-listing blurbs from the Journal of the American College of Surgeons, not a single study. It describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention and no learning outcome. Each entry concerns clinical surgical research, and none involves generative AI in education. It fails the intervention criterion, and the other criteria cannot be assessed from this text. Exclusion is coded E1 as the first applicable code. Under the protocol's abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of failure on intervention, so exclude is appropriate.
decision_note: Record is an award-listing compilation, not a research article on generative AI in STEM education.

rationale: Abstract describes evaluating ChatGPT-4, Gemini and CoPilot's accuracy on proportional reasoning questions. The AI tools themselves are the objects being tested, not learners interacting with them in a learning activity, and there is no control group of learners. There is no learner-level quantitative learning outcome; accuracy is the chatbot's own performance. Exclusion on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the best fit given the abstract, though E1 or E3 could also apply at fulltext. Positive evidence of no comparison group and no learner outcome is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

criteria.criteria_note: placeholder

quote: A 12-week teaching experiment involving 42 senior computer science students in an HCI course examined the impact of structured engagement with an LLM on their accessibility knowledge and design skills
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM (multimodal) used by computer science students in an HCI course with quantitative outcomes (heuristic evaluation scores, knowledge, self-efficacy). Domain (UI accessibility in computing) is plausibly STEM/computer science, and population is higher education. The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists; it describes a single 12-week teaching experiment and pre/post improvements, which suggests a possible single-group design (E3). Because missing information is not evidence, but the single-group reading is a real possibility, the record is advanced to full text to verify the comparison and design.

quote: This activity was attended by all teachers at Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Mambaul Hidayah with a total of 12 teachers
rationale: The participants are in-service teachers receiving training to compile HOTS assessment instruments with ChatGPT, not K-12 or higher education students. The abstract states that the service does not involve students. It also reports a single-group pre-post design for teachers with no control group and no student learning outcome. Excluded under E4 as the first applicable code, with E3 and E5 also likely applicable.
rationale_note: Population is in-service teachers, so E4 applies.

quote: A descriptive–correlational quantitative research design was employed.
rationale: The study is descriptive-correlational with a survey questionnaire on AI use and correlates usage with GWA. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). Design is also non-experimental (correlational), which the protocol excludes. Under the protocol's ordering, E3 is the first applicable code. Population (Grade 11 students) is met. The abstract gives positive evidence of a correlational design with no comparison group, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This Spotlight will help readers learn more about workforce readiness after-school programs
rationale: The record is an Education Week editorial spotlight, a collection of news and opinion articles rather than an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison, no generative AI learner intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); publication type is also not a journal article, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for this non-empirical item.

quote: A total of 281 prompts from 122 submissions in four assignments were analyzed using qualitatively coded prompts and Co-Occurrence Network Analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative/network analysis of student prompts with no separate control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it is an observational analysis rather than a comparative experiment. Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists (no comparison group, no learning measure), so exclusion is warranted. The first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group without generative AI), though E5 would also apply; E3 is reported as the first failing criterion in the protocol's code order with the comparison absent.

quote: The models were compared using quantitative metrics such as execution time, generation success rate, test success rate, number of test cases, and textual similarity of generated exercises.
rationale: The abstract describes a workflow evaluated by comparing multiple LLMs against each other on system-level metrics (execution time, generation success, test success). There is no separate control group without generative AI, and no learner-level learning outcome is reported. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison group (two generative AI variants only), so E3 applies.

quote: The study is theoretical and design-oriented (design-based research).
rationale: The paper is a theoretical, design-oriented work that develops a classification system of didactic prompts. The abstract states that empirical validation is a future priority, so there is no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in the code order. The E1 check is not decisive because the abstract is silent on whether the prompts are learner-facing, and E6 is cleaner.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that no empirical study was conducted.

rationale: Survey and interview study of preservice teachers' use of ChatGPT for lesson planning. There is no control group and no experimental comparison, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. It also reports perceptions and usage patterns rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI). The abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group. The record is excluded at the abstract stage.

quote: This study explored the experiences of university students who participated in a generative AI supported, student-led drug prevention project
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study using semi-structured interviews and qualitative content analysis of eight students. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study meeting the design requirements. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., a qualitative case design that fails the Design criterion) is the first applicable code after checking E1 to E5; E1 does not apply because the AI is learner-facing, and E5 is also met but the design failure is the most fundamental issue. Drug prevention is health-related content, which also raises a domain question, but it is not needed for the decision.

The abstract describes a narrative/literature-based review ("A systematic search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar") about ChatGPT in digital health literacy and healthcare. It reports no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measured in learners. It is not an empirical intervention study and fails on design, comparison, and outcome. The content is health-related (health professions/health literacy), which also conflicts with the STEM domain requirement. Since the record is not an empirical study, the first applicable code in order is E6. Note that E1 through E5 are not cleanly resolvable from the abstract, but E6 is the clearest positive evidence of failure.

Abstract describes a system architecture and implementation of AutoPrep, a Gemini-powered self-learning platform. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome data. It reads as a system description rather than an empirical study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) on positive evidence from the abstract. Coding is STEM and the tool is generative, so those criteria are not the basis for exclusion.

Abstract describes a mixed-methods study of Communication students using self-perception, cybersecurity data, and technical performance on infographics, with qualitative reflection forums. There is no described control group or comparison condition, and the design is not an randomized or quasi-experimental comparison as far as the abstract shows. The outcomes are largely self-perception and qualitative. Positive evidence of failure: no comparison group is described, so the study does not appear to be an experiment with a control. Coding E5 is applied because the abstract reports no clear quantitative learning outcome; the design concern (no comparison group, E3) is also plausible, and the full text should be checked. Given the rule to exclude only on positive evidence, this may warrant a fulltext check instead of exclusion. Recommend reviewer verification.

quote: The experimental group used an AI chatbot that employed Socratic dialogue to support students in understanding course content and completing tasks, while the control group followed traditional instructional methods.
rationale: Abstract describes a learner-facing AI chatbot (Socratic dialogue) versus a traditional-instruction control group, with pre/post test achievement outcomes in an introductory programming course at a higher education institution, published 2025. The chatbot is not explicitly described as generative in the abstract, but an LLM-style chatbot is plausible; this is not positive evidence of failure, so it is included for full-text check. Effect size data, publication type, and the design's randomization are not visible in the abstract and need checking at full text. The title and abstract are in Mongolian/English; the English abstract does not exclude on language at this stage.

quote: In this section, the International Journal of Public Opinion Research features updates on past and upcoming activities of the World Association for Public Opinion Research (WAPOR)
rationale: This record is a society news column (WAPOR News 2025) summarizing conference, awards, webinars and membership updates. It is not an empirical study and reports no experiment, intervention, control group, or learning outcome. Under E6 (not an empirical study) it fails the protocol. Publication type also falls outside journal research articles, but the core reason is that it is not empirical. Nothing in the text suggests generative AI is used by learners in a controlled comparison.

quote: Columnist Jonathan E. Collins interviews his colleague, Professor Suresh Venkatasubramanian
rationale: The record is a magazine-style interview/column discussing ChatGPT and education policy.
