criteria.domain_note: Japanese business writing is language learning, not STEM

quote: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming language education. However, its pedagogical and sociocultural impacts on Japanese business writing remain underexplored.
rationale: The content is Japanese business writing, which is language learning and therefore non-STEM. This is a positive failure of the domain criterion, so exclude under E2. The design is also a mixed-methods survey and interview study with no described control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which would fail E3 and E5 if reached, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: The evaluation of the effectiveness and implementation outcomes of AI-enabled VRS identified the need for further strategies such as integrating generative AI (e.g. ChatGPT) to optimise its learning effectiveness and programme acceptance.
rationale: The abstract describes an AI-enabled virtual reality simulation for clinical deterioration training, and the conclusion explicitly suggests that generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT) still needs to be integrated, implying the evaluated tool is not clearly a generative AI tool. Positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI is present, so E1 applies. Domain (clinical nursing deterioration recognition) is also not clearly STEM and could be a secondary concern, but E1 is first in order. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: Drawing on qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with 17 faculty members at an internationalized university in the UAE
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of faculty about handling Gen-AI plagiarism. It is not an empirical comparison of learners using generative AI, has no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Qualitative design is not an eligible design, so it fails as a non-empirical-trial design (E6). Faculty are not learners, but E6 is the first clearly applicable code given the design.

quote: we are releasing our new special issue on “The Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in English Language Teaching, Learning, and Academic Publications”
rationale: The record is a special-issue editorial introducing a volume, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome. It also concerns English language teaching, which is non-STEM. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order given the record's editorial nature; E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply.
rule_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is based on positive evidence that the record is an editorial, not an empirical study.

quote: This study presents a deep learning-based framework that models spatial-temporal eye-tracking data using long short-term memory (LSTM) and Transformer architectures to classify programming skill levels.
rationale: The abstract describes LSTM and Transformer classifiers applied to eye-tracking data to classify learner skill. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLM is only mentioned as context. There is no intervention or control group, so the study is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the intervention criterion fails.

quote: To provide guidance from the Society of University of Surgeons' Surgical Education Committee on the responsible integration of artificial intelligence into surgical training.
rationale: This is a position statement with expert discussion, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no intervention study design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Surgical training is also health professions education, which falls outside the STEM domain. E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is clearly supported; E2 (health professions) could also apply, but E6 comes first in the order given for the core failure of being non-empirical.

quote: Using an integrative literature review, this study synthesized 40 publications published between 2004 and 2026
rationale: The record is an integrative literature review that synthesizes existing publications and formulates a conceptual framework. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain (Islamic religious education) is not STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from E1 under the protocol's rules, so E6 is reported. Note the first applicable code in strict order would be E2 (not STEM) since E1 is unclear; the rule-based ordering should be checked by the auditor, though E1 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract.

criteria.stage_note: GPT-4 used for grading student writing, not as a learner-facing tool

quote: GPT-4 was provided with total grades, model answers, and rubrics from an instructor for all three courses.
rationale: The LLM is used to grade student writing (automated grading), not as a learner-facing tool that learners interact with as part of a learning activity. Per protocol, AI used only for grading is excluded, and E1 applies because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. No control group without generative AI is described either, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Preliminary findings indicate that the integration of AI reduces the time required to produce high-quality teaching cases
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT deep research) is used by the lecturer to prepare teaching cases, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, which is E1. The abstract also reports no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome (only preliminary time-saving findings and explicitly calls for future research on student learning). E1 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.

criteria.criteria_note: ChatGPT used by instructors to grade submissions; learners do not interact with the tool

quote: Grading coursework at scale is a persistent challenge in software engineering and computer science education
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT) is used to grade student lab reports and code, i.e., AI used for grading/by the instructor, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Under E1 (not learner-facing generative AI), this is excluded. The study also reports grade alignment and perceptions rather than a controlled learning outcome with a comparison group, though the abstract does not clearly describe a control group. Exclusion rests on E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: The methodology of the study was a quantitative approach and the data was collected from 569 male and female instructors in Saudi universities.
rationale: The study is a survey-based adoption model (UTAUT2 with TPACK moderation) of instructors' intention to use ChatGPT. It does not evaluate learners interacting with a generative AI tool, has no control group, and measures behavioral intention (a perception), not a learning outcome. Population is university instructors, not students. Exclusion code assigned at the first applicable point: E1 is arguably applicable because the intervention is not learner-facing, but the clearest failure is that this is a non-empirical-learning survey; I have recorded E6 as the most defensible single code given the survey design and perception-only outcomes. Abstract-stage evidence is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: This narrative review examines how digital intelligence can support curriculum development and practical teaching reform in dental technology education
rationale: placeholder

quote: The study looked at the social-demographic of Agric-based students, usage patterns effects and difficulties of NLP AI tools among Nigerian polytechnic students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive quantitative survey of 300 students using questionnaires, with no control group and no experimental comparison, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The reported "gains" are self-perceived, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable failure (no control group without generative AI); the study is also a survey design, which fails the design criterion. Domain (agriculture) is also not clearly STEM. Excluding on the abstract because positive evidence shows no comparison group.

quote: We used a qualitative case study approach to gather information from 15 second-year English education students
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study using interviews, observations and artefact analysis, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design criteria. The content is EFL speaking, which is non-STEM, but the abstract already gives a clear failure on design and outcome, so E6 is applied as the first clearly applicable code in the order given. Note that E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply; under the protocol's ordering, E2 precedes E6, so the first applicable code is actually E2.

The record has no abstract, only a title. The title ("The era of agentic AI: Should nurses and midwives learn about...") reads as a commentary or editorial rather than an empirical study. No comparison group, learning outcome, or empirical design is indicated. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Note the exclusion rests on the title alone; if the researcher judges the full text may contain an empirical trial, this should be revisited.

quote: The results demonstrated an increase in understanding and effective application of Prompt Engineering principles among the participants.
rationale: Learners use ChatGPT (generative AI) in a gamified prompt engineering activity in higher engineering education, published 2024. The abstract reports an increase in understanding but does not say whether there is a control group, so comparison and design cannot be confirmed. Prompt engineering is arguably computing content, but the abstract does not clearly establish STEM domain. Advancing to full text to check for a comparison group, the design, and quantitative outcome data.

criteria.stage_note: survey-based PLS-SEM study of satisfaction and continuance intention

quote: Quantitative data were analyzed using PLS-SEM, and an eventual semi-structured interview of eight subjects was used to validate the quantitative data.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based PLS-SEM study of expectation confirmation, satisfaction, and continuance intention. There is no quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving, or skill), only perceptions and intention, and no control group with a comparison condition. The study fails on the outcome criterion, and no experimental or comparison design is described. Exclusion code E5 applies because the outcome is perception-based.

quote: AI-assisted science lessons, followed by a second structured questionnaire completed by seven teachers.
rationale: The AI tools are used to design and deliver science lessons, and the evaluation is a teacher questionnaire on perceptions. The abstract gives no indication that learners interact with generative AI, which is the E1 condition. The study also reports perception data only, with no quantitative learning outcome (E5). E1 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported. The exclusion is supported by the abstract alone.

quote: The final sample size for the study was constrained to 57 educators, reflecting the point of theoretical saturation in data collection.
rationale: Qualitative interpretative phenomenological study of educators' perspectives on ChatGPT in management education. It is not an empirical comparison study with a control group, has no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are educators rather than students. Management education is also not a STEM domain. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design) is applied as the single code; the design is qualitative and the outcome is perceptions.

This is a bibliometric network review of 935 papers on contextualized science learning. It is not an empirical intervention study. It has no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), since no generative AI intervention is described at all. However, the most accurate description of the record type is a review, not an empirical study. Under the protocol's order, E1 is checked first and applies, so the code should be E1 rather than E6. The record fails on intervention, comparison, design, and outcome, so it is excluded.

quote: A qualitative, descriptive-exploratory design and interpretive paradigm were employed. The sample consisted of 20 basic education teachers selected through purposive sampling.
rationale: The abstract reports a qualitative descriptive-exploratory design with semi-structured interviews of 20 teachers. There is no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the participants are in-service teachers rather than students. Positive evidence fails several criteria, so this is excluded. E5 is the code recorded here; E6 (not an empirical study) would not fit because the study is empirical, and the study fails on the outcome criterion. Population also fails (teachers, not students), but the first applicable code in order is E4 under the protocol's ordering. Since the protocol orders codes E1 to E10 and E4 precedes E5, the correct first applicable code is E4.

quote: This inquiry, set against the rise of Identitarianism, explores how vanguardism and vanguardist ideas shaped Dominique Venner's life and thought over time.
rationale: The record is a historical/intellectual analysis of Dominique Venner's life and ideas. It involves no generative AI intervention, no comparison group, no learners, and no STEM content. It is not an empirical study of learning. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order; E1 would also technically apply since there is no learner-facing generative AI, but the record is fundamentally a non-empirical historical essay. The text is garbled in parts but contains no instructions to the reviewer.

quote: Digital feedback via free ChatGPT within the reciprocal teaching style: improving fundamental handball skills and students' attitudes among university beginners
rationale: The study concerns handball skills in university physical education. Handball is a sport, not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science, so the content is not STEM. Other criteria appear met on the abstract (randomized control group, ChatGPT-based feedback, skill performance outcome). Excluded under E2 at the abstract stage because the abstract gives positive evidence that the domain fails.

quote: An intervention study was conducted with 55 students (26 females and 29 males, 17–24 years old) during a university Spanish-English bilingual science course
rationale: University science students (population met) and ChatGPT-based activity (generative AI, learner-facing) suggest intervention plausibly met. However, the abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI; the design appears to be a single-group intervention study with pre/post-style improvement claims, which would be E3 if confirmed. Outcome is written critiques judged for argument quality, which may be a quantitative measure but is unclear. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text to check the comparison group and design.

quote: ويهدف هذا البحث إلى التعرف على الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي وبرامجه، والتعرف على برنامج (ChatGPT)، وبيان قدرته ومهاراته على تصميم البحث العلمي
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/jurisprudential (Islamic legal) review of generative AI use in research. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Also, the Islamic-law content is not STEM and the paper is not a learner-facing intervention study. Coding E6 as the first applicable code in order, since E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract alone.

quote: Illustrated digital picture books are widely used for second-language reading and vocabulary growth.
rationale: The study is about generating second-language (English, Chinese, French, Ukrainian, German) picture books with GenAI. Content is language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (E2). The abstract also reports only pilot usability ratings from Likert questionnaires, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would apply as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Only the first applicable code is reported.

rationale: The intervention contrasts individual homework with in-class collaborative group work. Neither arm, as described in the abstract, involves learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of the learning activity. Generative AI is mentioned only as motivation for the redesign. Positive evidence of a non-learner-facing or absent generative AI intervention is present, so E1 applies. The design is also a two-year sequential comparison, which would be a weak design, but E1 is the first applicable code.
decision_note: Exclusion rests on the abstract describing no generative AI learner interaction.

quote: This study aims to map the literature on AI for assessment and feedback in medical education
rationale: The record is a bibliometric mapping study and thematic evidence map of 435 records. It is not an empirical primary study with a control group, so it fails the design requirement and is not an empirical study (E6). It also concerns medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion for domain. E6 is the first applicable code in order, as the study is not empirical.

Only a title and venue are available; no abstract is in the index. The title ("exploring opportunities and challenges") suggests a review or conceptual paper, which would be excluded under E6, but this is not positive evidence in the record. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept as unsure for full-text review.

quote: The study compares learning outcomes of students who were taught using AI- assisted educational platforms with those of students who received instruction through traditional teaching methods.
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: the experimental group used generative AI tools (ChatGPT 4.0 Turbo, Khanmigo, Brisk), a control group received traditional instruction, the design is quasi-experimental with pre/post tests, participants are 10th-grade students, the modules are STEM topics (ecosystem energy, heredity), and there are quantitative achievement outcomes. Data sufficiency for SMD cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but missing information is not grounds for exclusion. Publication year 2025 meets the date criterion. Advance to full text to check the data and whether the AI tools are learner-facing.

quote: The research involved a sample of 132 teachers, selected from a total of 201 through probabilistic sampling
rationale: The study is a non-experimental, descriptive, cross-sectional survey of teachers' knowledge, perceptions and challenges with generative AI. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Teachers are not students. Per the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study design meeting eligibility; survey design). Note that the record is also a retracted-marked title ("RETIRADO"), but the decision rests on the design.

quote: Methods Twenty-three medical students gathered information on the Randleman criteria. Each student was allocated 10 minutes to interact with ChatGPT-3.5, followed by 10 minutes to search the internet independently.
rationale: Within-subject comparison in which all 23 students used both ChatGPT-3.5 and internet search. The comparator is a non-generative internet search tool, but it is a within-subject sequential design with no separate control group. The protocol requires a separate control group, so E3 applies. Domain is also arguably non-STEM (medical refractive surgery content), but E3 is the first applicable code in order given the design. Exclusion is supported by the abstract alone.

quote: The article examines the transformative influence of artificial intelligence on higher education with a particular focus on English philology and language learning.
rationale: The study focuses on English philology and foreign language acquisition, which is non-STEM content under the protocol. Its methods (comparative analysis, thematic review, pedagogical observation) do not indicate a controlled comparison design, so it also appears not to be an experimental study. Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in order that the abstract clearly supports.

quote: The study employs a dual method, using PLS-SEM and fsQCA approaches for data analysis. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from students and teachers from Chinese institutes.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional online questionnaire analysed with PLS-SEM and fsQCA, with no experimental or quasi-experimental control group. Learning performance is self-reported perception measured via survey constructs, not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement. Design (survey/correlational) and outcome criteria fail; E5 is the first applicable code in order given the outcome is perception-based. Domain is not clearly STEM. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.
rationale_note: Per protocol order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) are unclear rather than failed, so E5 is the first clearly failing code.

quote: Functional testing based on decision tables and test cases confirmed the correctness of the main usage scenarios.
rationale: The abstract describes a system-development paper. Its evaluation is functional testing with decision tables and test cases, and the claimed improvements in convenience, speed, and accuracy are perceptions or system properties, not a quantitative learning outcome. No control group comparison is described. The paper is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails at E6 (not an empirical study). Using the first-applicable order, E1 is not clearly triggered, since the AI assistant is learner-facing, and E2 is unclear because the subject domain is not stated. E6 is the most defensible code at the abstract stage. Note that this is a system-design paper, so a fulltext check would be a reasonable confirmation.

quote: The study used an experimental design with two groups, namely control and experimental, each consisting of 120 students (240 in total)
rationale: At abstract stage, no positive evidence of failure. Experimental vs control design with students learning basic Python programming (STEM). ChatGPT API integrated into PBGL model suggests learner-facing generative AI. Outcome is critical thinking score improvement (quantitative). Data sufficiency, publication type, and full-text language are not verifiable from the abstract and are deferred to full text.

quote: The research method employs a quantitative descriptive approach through questionnaires distributed to 11th-grade students and teachers
rationale: The study is a needs analysis using descriptive questionnaires with percentages. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a survey-type design, not an experimental study with learning measures. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical comparative study) with the note that it fails comparison, design and outcome criteria. The domain (programming algorithms) and population (high school students) are met, and the AI chatbot is a planned component rather than a tested intervention.

The abstract describes a content analysis of student project work in a PBL challenge, with no control or comparison group and no quantitative learning measure. It is a qualitative/descriptive design. The abstract gives positive evidence of no control group (E3), and the design is not experimental. Exclusion code E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order, though E5 and E6 would also apply on the same evidence.

quote: A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among 408 dental students (336 BDS and 72 MDS) in a private dental college.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of dental students' awareness, use, and perceptions of AI tools. It has no control group and no experimental comparison, and it reports no quantitative learning outcome. Dentistry is a health profession, which falls under the domain exclusion. The first applicable code in order is E3, since there is no control group without generative AI.

quote: The study employs a mixed methods approach, combining qualitative focus group discussions with aviation professors and a quantitative survey administered to students.
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods study with focus groups and a student survey. There is no described control group or comparison condition, so E3 applies. The quantitative results are perception-based survey findings rather than a measured learning outcome, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Aviation education is also of unclear STEM status. The first applicable code in order is E3, though E5 would also apply.

quote: This paper analyzes 13 studies and case analyses, focusing on AI applications in higher education
rationale: The paper is a review/analysis of 13 studies and case analyses plus a proposed governance framework, not an empirical primary study with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Domain and intervention are also not clearly STEM or generative-AI learner-facing from the abstract, but E6 applies first in the order.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of review design.

quote: The findings derived from the students' survey responses demonstrated that ChatGPT significantly enhanced their interests and improved their coding skills.
rationale: The abstract describes an active-learning course using ChatGPT with student survey findings only. It gives no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears to fail. The only outcomes reported are survey-based perceptions and self-reported skill improvement, not a quantitative learning measure. Excluded at abstract stage on E3 as the first applicable code, with E5 also plausible. Positive evidence of a missing control group is present in the design description.

quote: The aim of this article is to present and analyze a system of prompt engineering strategies relevant to this category of students and to describe their evolution
rationale: The study concerns prompt-engineering competence in Russian language teaching (RFL), which is non-STEM content under the protocol's domain criterion. It is also a conceptual/theoretical analysis with no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, so it fails several other criteria. The first applicable code in order is E2 (non-STEM content).
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion on positive evidence of non-STEM domain.

criteria.quote: A corpus of 140 articles was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and analyzed using Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and Biblioshiny.
criteria.rationale: This is a bibliometric mapping study of research literature, not an empirical study. It has no experimental or comparison group and no learning outcome measured in learners, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing code that is clearly evident; it is a review-type bibliometric analysis.

quote: We interviewed 12 multilingual STEM graduate students over the course of their first year in a graduate program and continued interviewing three of the students in their second year.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study (inductive and deductive qualitative analysis) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental design meeting the protocol's design criteria; the closest code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs). Writing self-perceptions are affective/perceptual, and no quantitative learning measure is reported. Exclusion is clear on design and outcome at abstract stage.

criteria.note: theoretical/philosophical paper; no experiment or comparison group described

quote: This paper examines concepts for the further development of generative AI based on the thesis of the dual na-ture of human intelligence and consciousness
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/philosophical paper proposing concepts and a program; it reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the paper is conceptual rather than empirical.

quote: Using a qualitative descriptive design with content analysis, the data comprised ten purposively selected undergraduate thesis titles
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis comparing machine translation outputs of ChatGPT and Google Translate on thesis titles. It is not an empirical learning study with learners interacting with a GenAI tool, has no control group without GenAI, no quantitative learning outcome (rubric-rated translation quality), and the domain is Arabic translation/language, not STEM. Exclusion code E6 is used as the not-empirical-study criterion is the best fit for a qualitative content analysis of translation outputs; the first applicable code by order is E1 (no learner-facing GenAI intervention), which arguably applies since the tool is used to translate texts rather than as a learner activity. Given the order rule, E1 applies first.

quote: Employing a qualitative conceptual research design grounded in an integrative review methodology
rationale: The study is a qualitative conceptual integrative review of published literature, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no primary data. Its domain is English philology (language learning), which is non-STEM. The first applicable code in protocol order is E2 (content not STEM), but E6 (not an empirical study) is the most fundamental failure. Per the rule of reporting the first code in order, E2 would be listed first; however, the record is clearly a review, so E6 is the substantive reason. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.
rationale_note: Note: codes are reported in order E1 to E10; E2 (non-STEM, English philology) precedes E6 in the protocol order and also applies clearly from the abstract.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was administered to undergraduate students in semester 4 (N = 180). Data were analyzed using multiple regression.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with multiple regression on perceptions (ethical readiness, risk-benefit appraisal), with no experimental control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion under E5 is applied, since the outcome is perception-based rather than a measure of learning. Design also fails (survey, correlational), which the protocol excludes. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is justified. Note that E5 is the first listed code that applies in the protocol order given the outcome failure; the comparison/design failure is also present.

Abstract describes a descriptive survey design with mixed methods (questionnaires and interviews) and no separate control group. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applied as the first failing criterion among those checked; the design also amounts to a survey, which is non-eligible under the design row. Population is undergraduate students, which meets the population criterion.

quote: This study investigates ethical dilemmas of pre-service special education teachers using Generative AI writing tools for their thesis work.
rationale: The study is a mixed-method survey and focus-group investigation of ethical dilemmas and perceptions. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the survey measures ethics and privacy awareness, which is perception-based. Domain is also not STEM (special education thesis writing). Excluded at E5 as the first applicable code in order would be E2 for non-STEM content; however, E2 is checked before E5 in the protocol order, so the code should be E2. Note the correction: the first applicable code is E2 (content is not STEM), so the exclusion code should be E2.

quote: The study used a cross-sectional survey design conducted in July 2024 to collect data from 262 students across various disciplines.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with PLS-SEM analysis of perceived competence, usage, and engagement. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. The outcome is engagement and self-reported competence rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is based on E3 as the first clearly failing criterion in protocol order that applies to the design/comparison; the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design.

quote: Promoting AI literacy within the writing classroom will guide students of the possible ways they can responsibly and ethically utilize AI as a tool without becoming overreliant on such programs.
rationale: The study is set in an English composition course, which is non-STEM content (protocol Domain exclusion: language and other non-STEM content). This is positive evidence of a failed criterion at the abstract stage, so exclude under E2. The abstract also describes no comparison group, no quantitative outcome, and no empirical design, but these are not needed for the exclusion.

quote: The training results showed a significant increase in competency, marked by 87.5% of participants achieving a good category in the post-test.
rationale: This is a community service workshop with 32 vocational students, described as a single-group training with a post-test only and no control group. The abstract gives positive evidence of a single-group design lacking a comparison, so E3 applies. Also, the paper is a community service report, not a clear empirical comparison study. Domain (software engineering students using Canva for presentations) is borderline STEM but not the deciding factor.

quote: The results revealed that all six hypotheses established on the basis of prior research were statistically significant.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of 244 social welfare students testing relationships among innovativeness, self-efficacy, and intention to use generative AI. It reports no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, and no learning outcome (intention is an attitudinal measure). Social work is also not a STEM domain. Positive evidence of design failure (survey, not an experiment) and outcome failure is present, so the record is excluded. Per the code order, E1 and E2 were not clearly established from the abstract; the first clearly applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), but the stronger and more fundamental failure is that this is a non-empirical-learning survey. Coding as E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design) is the most accurate fit given the survey correlational design; the reviewer may recode to E3 or E5 if preferred.

quote: Dr. Claude Binard noted for his long tenure and devotion to classical homeopathy
rationale: The record is a biographical tribute/obituary of a homeopath, not an empirical study. It describes no generative AI intervention, no control group, no learners, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Also not a journal article reporting research; the E1 and E2 checks are not applicable on the face of the text.

quote: The study sample consisted of 638 students enrolled in Turkish Language and Literature degree programs at the 27 universities administered by public and private foundations throughout Türkiye.
rationale: This is a survey study of students' awareness, attitudes and habits toward GenAI. There is no intervention in which learners use a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no learning outcome measured; the outcomes are perceptions and habits. Turkish Language and Literature is also not clearly STEM. Coded E3 as the first applicable code since there is no comparison group without generative AI; the design is a cross-sectional survey, which would also fail the design criterion.

quote: This article explores the main directions of computational linguistics, highlighting its key areas of research and application.
rationale: The record is a non-empirical overview article on computational linguistics. It describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM education population. It fails on E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order; it is also not a learning study at all, so E1 could be argued, but E6 reflects the record's nature as a review/overview.

quote: The type of research used was qualitative research.
rationale: The abstract states the study is qualitative, using observation, interviews, and literature study, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical quantitative design meeting the protocol's Design criterion (randomized or quasi-experiment with comparison group). Positive evidence of a failed design criterion supports exclusion. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (STEM) appear met (ChatGPT in trigonometry), so the first applicable code is E6 as the study is a qualitative, non-experimental empirical study. Note E3 (no control group) would also apply; E6 is chosen as the most fitting code for a qualitative study with no comparison design.

quote: The method used is a quantitative approach with a survey through a questionnaire, which was distributed to 31 selected students through purposive sampling technique.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use by Informatics Engineering students (generative AI, higher education, computing domain). However, the design is described as a survey with an independent t-test, and it is unclear whether a separate non-ChatGPT control group exists. Outcomes appear to be perceptions (time efficiency, understanding, assignment quality), and no quantitative learning measure is evident. Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure, so advance to full text to check the comparison, design, and outcome data.

quote: "This specialized tool gathers insights and perceptions of graduate students regarding AI awareness, experiences with AI in information access, encountered challenges and the effects of AI on their academic writing endeavors."
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of perceptions among graduate students, with no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group. There is positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail, and that the outcome is perception-based rather than a quantitative learning measure. The domain is not STEM (academic writing and information access). Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion in the protocol's order that clearly applies; the record would also fail E5 and E2 on the abstract.

The record is a community service (pengabdian masyarakat) activity description: a socialization event on AI ethics and ChatGPT use for SMK students. It describes an event to be held, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order given. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical nature, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This paper delves into the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly focusing on ChatGPT, within educational realms.By conducting an exhaustive review across various scholarly publications and case studies
rationale: The abstract describes an exhaustive review of scholarly publications and case studies, which is a review rather than an empirical study with a comparison group and a quantitative learning outcome. The abstract's mention of "empirical validation" is not supported by any described comparison design. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Positive evidence of a review design is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: in this forum of short essays, Craig Erpelding, Jack Beck, J. D. Swerzenski, and Thomas Brecheisen explore the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in screenwriting, postproduction, and teaching.
rationale: The record is a forum of short essays and discussion pieces, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Film and screenwriting content is also not clearly STEM. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's logic for non-empirical records. The record contains garbled text in the body, which I did not act on; no instructions were present, so injection_suspected is false.

quote: This study aims to explore students' perceptions of using ChatGPT as a tool for learning English grammar, particularly in academic writing.
rationale: The study concerns English language learning (grammar, academic writing), which is non-STEM content and falls under the protocol's domain exclusion. It is also a qualitative case study with perception data only (no control group, no quantitative learning outcome), so it would fail E3, E5 and design criteria as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.

quote: Participants developed traditional and AI-supported lesson plans using the Rationale for Lesson Design framework.
rationale: Abstract describes an exploratory mixed-methods case study of 19 pre-service teachers producing both traditional and AI-supported lesson plans. This is a within-subject comparison of planning products, not a control group without generative AI, and the design is a case study. Outcome is rubric-based analysis of lesson plan reasoning, not a clearly quantitative learning outcome measured after intervention. Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code (no control group without generative AI; single-group within-subject design). Note the ordering rule: E1 and E2 do not apply, and E3 is the first failing code in order.

The domain is also foreign language teaching, which is non-STEM (E2), and the participants are instructors, not students. Under the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E2 would apply first since the domain is non-STEM. Coding as E2 because the content is English language teaching, which the protocol explicitly excludes.

quote: This study aims to explore English Language Education Study Program (ELESP) students' perceptions of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in supporting their academic writing processes
rationale: Qualitative perception study using semi-structured interviews with six students and thematic analysis. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at the abstract stage, E2 (content not STEM) applies clearly, but the design is not an empirical quantitative study; the first applicable code in order is E2 since the content is English language writing, not STEM. Recording E2 as the first clearly failing criterion in the order listed.

quote: We coded the privacy policies of 1,694 EdTech applications sampled from a random set of local education agencies across all 50 U.S. states against ten U.S.-law-aligned disclosure categories
rationale: The study codes vendor privacy policy documents for legal disclosure categories. No learner interaction with a generative AI tool is described, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). It is also not an intervention or comparison study with learning outcomes (no control group or quantitative learning outcome). Exclusion at abstract stage is justified on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: A quantitative approach with a survey design was employed involving 50 students from the Faculty of Engineering, Universitas Negeri Medan as respondents.

Survey-based perception measures also do not clearly constitute a quantitative learning outcome. Per the protocol's first-applicable code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at abstract stage, E2 is unclear, so the earliest clear failure is the absence of a control group (E3). Positive evidence of a failed criterion is present, so exclusion is justified.

quote: We report a qualitative study with 20 STEM students at a large Swedish university who were interviewed about their use of commercial LLM chatbots.
rationale: Qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, which the protocol excludes; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group. Coded E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in order is E3 before E5/E6; the design also fails E6 (not an empirical quantitative study), but E3 is the first applicable code given the absence of any comparison group.

quote: This perspective reports on 2025 field deployments of a full-size humanoid robot across diverse settings
rationale: The record describes itself as a perspective reporting field deployments, with no controlled comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are not evidenced in the abstract.

The record is a legal-theory article on digitalization law. Its only empirical component is an anonymous survey of 51 law students on LLM use, attitudes, and risk awareness. The protocol excludes survey designs, there is no control group, and the outcome is perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Law is also not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that clearly applies under the protocol's ordering, though E2 (non-STEM content) would also be a valid reason; E6 is chosen because the article is primarily a non-empirical legal analysis. Exclusion is justified on the abstract alone because the abstract gives positive evidence of non-eligibility (survey-only, legal domain).

The record is a translation-studies discussion of the translator's changing role, with a reference list of prior literature. Although the code order would place E1 first and that is not positively evidenced here, the abstract gives positive evidence that the work is not an empirical study, and the domain (translation/language learning) is also not STEM. Abstract-stage rule: the exclusion rests on the positive absence of any empirical design in the abstract.

Excluded at E2 as the first applicable code.

quote: Interfaces such as LLaVA may serve as a valuable complement to wound care nurses in PI management

The topic is also clinical nursing care rather than STEM education, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from E1 onward only if E1-E5 do not apply; E1 is not clearly met since the tool is not described as used by learners, so E6 is the first clear failure.

quote: The article presents the author's perspective on the impact of artificial intelligence on the quality of educational programs.

Other criteria (STEM domain, comparison) are not evidenced in the abstract; the E6 failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: Enhancing Engagement and Autonomy in Advanced Japanese Learning as the Second Language through AI-Assisted Video Production

Design appears to be a single-group descriptive study rather than a randomized or quasi-experiment. Exclusion code E3 applied as the first failing criterion in order; the abstract gives no evidence of a comparison group.

rationale: The record is a decision-framework paper that combines a literature review, a UTAUT-based acceptance phase, and procurement record analysis. The "meta-analysis" label does not show an eligible effect-size synthesis of learner outcomes. Per the protocol this is not an empirical study of the eligible design, so E6 applies. Because the record is clearly not an eligible design, it is excluded rather than held as unsure.

Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 and E2 cannot be confidently assessed from the abstract, but E6 is the clear failing criterion and is the first applicable code given the design is non-empirical.

quote: Greatest Hits of 2023! Notable Non-JGME Medical Education Articles

The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention were clearly absent, but the record is primarily a non-empirical review, so E6 is the most accurate code for the record itself.

E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order for a non-empirical review. rationale_note: Also health-professions content (nursing), which would be E2 if the order favored it; however, E6 is listed earlier in the code sequence? Note: protocol order is E1 to E10, so E2 (non-STEM/health) precedes E6.

rationale: This record is a Knowable Magazine feature article (journalism), not an empirical study. Reviews are also not eligible publication types under the protocol (E10), but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order is E6 before E10 only if ordering applies; here the primary defect is that it is not an empirical study.

Excluding on design/comparison is supported by the abstract's own description of a cross-sectional analysis; the design failure is the decisive point. Note the population is medical/allied health students, which could also be judged against E2 (health professions education), but the protocol's exclusion of health professions education is under Domain; the abstract's primary failure is design.

The record is excluded on the first clearly applicable code in order: E1 is not clearly met, since the AI is used to evaluate student essays (possibly teacher-facing), and E2 (English writing is non-STEM) is arguably the first applicable code. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the population failure is the clearest and most direct reason; E4 is reported as the single code. Both E1 and E3 would also apply in principle. No prompt-injection content was found in the record.

rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of student perceptions (SWOT analysis) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in order that fits; the design also fails (survey), but E5 is the primary reason stated for the outcome. Domain is also unclear (pre-service primary/early childhood teachers, not clearly STEM).

quote: Career Compass is an AI-powered career exploration platform that combines large language models, structured occupational data, and interactive data visualizations
rationale: This is a software/system description (capstone project report) with no comparison group, no learning outcome, and no empirical evaluation described. It is not an empirical study. The domain is career exploration rather than STEM content. Excluded under E6 as the first applicable code in the order given: the record describes a system build, not an empirical study. Note E1 is not clearly failed because the chatbot is LLM-based and learner-facing, but E6 applies and is decisive.

quote: Il contributo indaga gli atteggiamenti e le intenzioni d’uso dei trasformatori generativi di testo tra i futuri insegnanti
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of pre-service teachers' attitudes and intentions toward generative AI (TAM adaptation). It has no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group, no learning outcome, and is a survey (non-experimental). Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design); the first applicable code in order would arguably be E1 since the intervention is not learner-facing AI use, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design. Note the abstract's Italian text is not an issue for language at this stage. Per the protocol's code order, E1 is the first code that applies; I record E1 as the strictly first-applicable code instead.

quote: this study presents an interactive, MATLAB‐based virtual laboratory designed to teach solar cell optics using the transfer matrix method (TMM)
rationale: At abstract stage, the intervention appears to involve a learner-facing LLM tutor (multimodal, context-aware) within an optoelectronics virtual lab, and the domain is STEM (optics/solar cells). However, the abstract does not describe a control group, study design, learner population, or any quantitative learning outcome. It describes a software tool and its features without evidence of a comparative evaluation. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is retained as unsure for full-text review of design, comparison, and outcome.

No abstract is available in the index. The title describes an study of science teachers' approaches to AI-integrated science teaching, which suggests a teacher-focused qualitative or descriptive study rather than a learner-facing experiment with a learning outcome. Teachers are not students, and no quantitative learning outcome is indicated. Exclusion is based on the title alone, which is thin; the decision is made as E5 but could be reconsidered if the full text shows a student experiment with learning outcomes.

quote: Reflection narratives were collected from 208 practice teachers enrolled during the first semester of Academic Year 2025-2026.
rationale: The study is a qualitative sentiment analysis of internship reflection narratives. No learner-facing generative AI tool is evaluated; Copilot and Orange 3 are used by researchers for analysis. There is no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E1 applies first, as no learner-facing generative AI intervention is present.

rationale: The record is a literature review (Russian-language title and abstract), not an empirical study. quote: Here, we explored the potential of ChatGPT, an automated chatbot, to assist in the development process of the SRT by comparing ChatGPT's and students' evaluations of the SRT.
rationale: Abstract-stage check in protocol order. ChatGPT is used to rate stereotype statements for developing a bias self-evaluation test, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity (E1 is arguably applicable). Content concerns cultural competency and implicit bias in medical education, not STEM (E2). The study is a methodological comparison of ratings rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a control group and learning outcome (E3/E5 also apparent). Per the protocol's first-applicable-code rule, E1 would be the first code if the intervention is judged not learner-facing; I am reporting E2 because the abstract clearly places the content outside STEM and the intervention is not a learner-facing learning activity either way. Note: the strictly first-applicable code is E1 under the protocol order; the auditor should consider changing to E1.

quote: A validated questionnaire assessing constructs such as satisfaction, readiness, and relevance of AI was utilised.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of students' attitudes, perceptions, and preparedness with AI, with no learner-facing generative AI intervention and no control group. The design is correlational/survey, and the outcomes are perceptions and satisfaction, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first clear failure in the protocol's stated order when the abstract gives no comparison group; the survey design and perception-only outcomes also fail the protocol's design and outcome criteria. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no control group, exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

quote: The Singularity Is Nearer is a much better book, though it must be read with an attitude toward critical thinking.
rationale: The record is a book review of Kurzweil's 2024 book, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome. It is therefore not an empirical study (E6). Publication type is also a review, which is ineligible.

quote: Applied and descriptive study in two phases. In Phase 1, a chatbot was designed using the ChatGPT language model
rationale: The study is a descriptive development and expert-validation study. Experts rated generated cases with CVI and Fleiss' Kappa; no learner-level quantitative learning outcome and no control group are reported. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Note that E3 (no control group) would also apply; under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 through E4 are not clearly failed at abstract level, and E5 is the first clear failure in order after those that are unclear. The design is also not an experiment with a comparison group.

quote: This dissertation argues that contemporary anxiety surrounding artificial intelligence is not a response to the technology itself, but to the reification of human social relations
rationale: The record is a 2026 dissertation, a theoretical/philosophical work drawing on Frankfurt School thought. It reports no empirical study, no learners using generative AI, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6) and is also a dissertation, which is ineligible publication type. E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order, so it is reported here.

rationale: The record is a case study (qualitative/descriptive) of ten secondary school teachers using ChatGPT and other AI tools to develop English test items. Exclusion uses E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, a case study design), the first applicable code given the ordering; E4 (in-service teachers) and E2 (non-STEM) would also apply.

No injection text was present.

quote: "The Deposed Queen": A Reflection on Crises in Religious Studies

Under the protocol's sequencing, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first code in order, but the record's abstract contains no mention of generative AI, so E1 is not the operative reason; the paper is a non-empirical reflection, which is E6.

quote: The article methodically explores the potential for using webquest technology as an innovative means for professionally-oriented foreign language teaching
rationale: The abstract describes a methodological/conceptual article presenting a webquest script and discussing potential; it reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning data. Exclusion is on the basis that the record does not appear to be an empirical study (E6). Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (generative AI intervention is only mentioned as a prospect) and E2 (non-STEM language learning) would also be grounds; E6 is the most evident failure from the abstract.

quote: 150 Tamil Nadu state, central, deemed and private university respondents participated in a standard questionnaire.

There is no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and usage are reported. Excluded under E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in order is E1 (unclear at abstract stage), so the closest fit is E3; design and outcome criteria also clearly fail (survey design, no learning outcome).

quote: A post-exchange survey was conducted after the program's conclusion, and a detailed analysis will be included in the paper.
rationale: Descriptive program report on a librarian virtual exchange between UCSD and Fudan. Participants are librarians, not STEM students; there is no control group, no learning outcome, and no generative AI intervention. It is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion at E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code is a reasonable reading; E4 (population) also fails and would apply on the same basis. Venue is Figshare, not a journal article, so E10 may also apply.

quote: Review of Artificial Life: The Quest for a New Creation by Steven Levy
rationale: The record is a book review of Levy's Artificial Life, not an empirical study. It has no intervention, comparison group, or learning outcome. It is excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Note that E10 (publication type) could also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order and the review is not an empirical study.

quote: Based on survey data from 127 college students, this paper analyzes the current status and deficiencies of students' Artificial Intelligence Literacy (AIL)
rationale: Abstract stage. The study is a survey of 127 college students on AI literacy, with college English as the subject. English language learning is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in code order. It is also a survey design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which would be further exclusions (E3, E5, E6). Only one code is reported, the first in order that applies.

quote: Using AI-Generated Scenarios to Enhance Learning of The Emergency Assessment Process
rationale: Study is in athletic training education (emergency assessment and clinical simulation for athletic training students). Athletic training/health professions education falls under the protocol's Domain exclusion for health professions education, so content is not STEM (E2). The design also appears to be descriptive with no control group (phase one expert ratings; phase two student scores with no comparison group), which would be E3 as well, but E2 is the first applicable code in order. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.
rationale_note: Abstract shows no separate control group; descriptive statistics only.

quote: Collecting electronic survey responses from 130 graduate and undergraduate students across several disciplines
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional electronic survey of 130 university students on their perceptions of AI literacy. There is no intervention in which learners interact with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no learning outcome measured; the measures are self-perceived literacy and reported use. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group without generative AI) per the protocol's design and comparison requirements; the survey design also fails the eligible-design criterion and the outcome is perception-only.
exclusion_code_note: E3 chosen; E6 (non-empirical) would also fit as survey, but E3 applied as the first-applicable comparison failure.

quote: This qualitative case study describes the development, implementation, and analysis of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven patient simulation
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study using reflexive thematic analysis of student transcripts. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order, though the record is an empirical qualitative case study; the strongest failing criteria are the missing control group and quantitative outcome (E3/E5). Following the code order, E3 would apply first because no comparison group exists. Note: I'm reporting E6 per the qualitative design, but the correct first-applicable code by protocol order is E3.

quote: online surveys administered to faculty members (N = 64) and students (N = 416)
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods survey and focus group on perceptions and use of AI. There is no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and usage are reported. The exclusion code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), which applies first in the code order on the comparison criterion. Design (survey, not experimental) and outcome (perceptions only) also fail, and the STEM domain is not evident from the abstract.
rationale_short: Survey and focus-group study of AI perceptions with no control group or learning outcome.
summary: Perception survey and focus group; no comparison group and no learning outcome.

rationale: The content is EFL paragraph writing, a language-learning domain that is not STEM, so E2 applies and it is the first applicable code in order. The study also appears to be a descriptive feedback-characterization study without a control group receiving non-generative-AI feedback (E3 is also plausible), but E2 is the first code that applies. Abstract gives no evidence of a comparison group or learning outcome measure.

quote: This study conducts a systematic literature review (SLR) to investigate the applications and trends of AI in mathematics education
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study. The abstract gives positive evidence of a review design, so it is excluded at the abstract stage.

quote: a quasiexperimental one-group pre-test–post-test design was employed
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-test–post-test design with no separate control group that does not use generative AI, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion (E3). Intervention (AI chatbot, Earth science, high school) appears to fit, but the comparison criterion alone fails, so exclusion is warranted at the abstract stage.

quote: This study aimed to examine educators’ digital and AI-supported English-learning and teaching practices, professional-learning priorities, and perceptions of an early-stage mixed-audience MOOC.
rationale: The study is a descriptive mixed-methods survey of 22 in-service elementary educators (questionnaire plus interviews) about needs and perceptions. It has no control group, no learning outcome, and the population is in-service teachers, not students. It is a survey/needs-assessment design rather than an empirical comparison, and the English-language content is non-STEM. Under the first-applicable-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly positive from the abstract, but the study is not an eligible empirical intervention study; E6 is the best fit for a non-experimental survey/perception study. Exclusion is clear from the abstract on design and outcome grounds.

quote: This paper reports on the ongoing development of a study to provide such evidence.
rationale: The abstract describes an ongoing study in development with expected results from preliminary work and pilot-phase observations. It is not a completed empirical study with a control group comparison or reported quantitative learning outcome data, so it fails as not an empirical study (E6). Note the paper is a work-in-progress report, which also raises E10 concerns, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the lack of reported empirical results.

quote: An online survey, adapted from Chan and Zhou (2023)... The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics such as mean scores and percentages.

Not an experiment, no control group, no learner-facing intervention, no quantitative learning outcome, and content is English language teaching (non-STEM). Under the protocol's first-applicable-code ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) would apply first since the instructors only report perceptions of GenAI use rather than learners interacting with it. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not the correct first code; the best first-applicable code is E1. Note: the code above is E6 but the strict first-applicable reading is E1, so the audit should confirm.

quote: The training materials focused on the use of various AI platforms, including ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gamma AI, Leonardo AI, and CapCut AI, for the development of instructional media.

Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because positive evidence shows the population fails.

quote: The purpose of this article is to explore the ethical implications for the nursing profession of these advances as currently known and understood.

Nursing is also a health professions field, which would be excluded under the domain criterion, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's rules, so E6 is reported.

The first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention is ChatGPT use by learners' teachers rather than learner-facing, but the protocol order puts E1 first, and the abstract does not clearly show learners interacting with the tool, so E4 is the clearest positive failure. rationale: Qualitative interview study of satisfaction with chatbot AI in EFL academic writing. quote: The type of study used was exploratory descriptive qualitative research. The six participants were purposively selected
rationale: The study is an exploratory descriptive qualitative design with six interviewees and thematic analysis. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Strictly, it is an empirical qualitative study, so E5 or E3 would also fit; E6 is chosen as a best fit for a non-experimental qualitative design. Abstract-stage evidence is clear enough to exclude.

quote: This study evaluated the performance of the latest model, GPT-5, using the same 1,099 mathematics items examined in prior studies
rationale: The study evaluates GPT model accuracy on a fixed item bank (1,099 items) with no learners and no control group; it compares model generations against prior studies rather than a separate control group of learners. Model performance is not a learner-facing intervention, and there is no comparison group without generative AI. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). The E1 code would also plausibly apply since learners do not interact with the tool; E3 is reported as the code per the first-applicable order consideration of the comparison failure, but the core issue is the absence of any learner-facing intervention and comparison group.

quote: This paper takes multidimensional integration and collaborative education as its central approach, focuses on frontline teaching reform practices, and draws on real cases of curriculum reform
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/reform-practice discussion of talent cultivation pathways for painting majors. It reports no experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Domain is art/painting, not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract; E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply. Per protocol order, E1 and E2 are checked first: the AI use is not clearly learner-facing and the content is painting, so E2 is arguably the first applicable code. Reporting E2 as the first applicable code given painting is clearly non-STEM.

quote: we use established information retrieval metrics including precision, recall, and mean average precision
rationale: The study evaluates a reading-level-aware search re-ranking system using IR metrics (precision, recall, MAP) on retrieved documents. The abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is not a quantitative learning measure (system retrieval metrics), so exclusion on E5 is applied. Participants are not described as students, and the generative component (LLMs used to create document versions) is not learner-facing, so E1 could also be argued; E5 is the clearest failing criterion given the first-applicable ordering concern is E1 though. Note: under strict ordering, E1 applies first because LLMs are used to generate documents for the search collection rather than learners interacting with a generative tool.

quote: a control group (n = 60), exposed to conventional analog teacher feedback

Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in order that the abstract gives positive evidence for, since the content is art/visual design rather than science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science.

rationale: The record has only a title and venue with no abstract. Domain and population are also unclear, but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails; the design/outcome failure is the clearest basis, so E6 is reported as the closest fit for a non-experimental case observation.

quote: We collected and automatically scored student responses to seven scientific explanation tasks in Chinese

rationale: The abstract describes a narrative review and a worked example, not an empirical study. rationale:

The design is essentially a benchmark accuracy comparison rather than a randomized or quasi-experiment. Domain is also health professions (dentistry), which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E4 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion in order, with E2 (health professions content) also likely applicable; population is the first failing code given the candidate-exam sample. Note that E1 could also be argued since the AI answers questions rather than learners interacting with it, but the abstract is ambiguous on that point.
